Just a different style of cake. I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here. If I'm in the area and there's no other option for dessert then I'd probably eat at The Butterwood again.
Meh. Ice latte was good. The cake I got was kind of dry and it definitely wasn't very freshly baked because the butter cream kind of fell off it.

Stopped for a quick coffee and dessert on a whim. The place is charming, we immediately got a hello when we entered the door. We had a selection of desserts even on a late afternoon. They were fresh and filling. The coffee was fabulous and the tea was satisfying. Enjoy!

Walking in, I felt like I had been transported into one of those British bake shops where you can can hang out with your girlfriends for hours around cake and lattes. That's exactly what I did. I absolutely loved this quaint little place and they had plenty of comfortable seating. The only reason I'm giving this place 3 stars instead of 4 is the simple chocolate cake we ordered was a tad dry and the buttercream was hardened. It was as if the cake had been sitting out too long in the fridge and it was almost to the point of being stale. I've heard people rave about their delicious cakes so I'm going to assume we just got there on a day of a bad batch. The latte's we got were fine, nothing too special. I definitely loved the atmosphere and its a great little place to meet up with a few of your friends. Sure it was pricey for the subpar cake I had, but I want to come back and try it again to give this place a 2nd chance.

I walk by here (ironically to get to the gym!) and have been curious to check out the spot. It looks charming from the window. We were down that way for an errand with the pup, so hubs waited with pupster, while I went in. Hubs asked for something of his own or forewarned me that he would eat whatever I got. Noted. The cafe has an old world feel. Think a dark Viennese cafe. I made my way to the counter and saw so many beautiful cakes. Alas, cakes aren't practical for grab and go errand type. The brownies were huge and would fit the size criteria of a shared treat. Then I looked up and saw what I thought were whoopie pies (gobs for Western Pennsylvanians). I read closer and they're cookies with peanut buttercream filling. Done! We sat on the bench outside and shared the tasty treat. The buttercream was light and greatly paired well with the chocolate chip cookie. It was a bit messy to eat, but so good. Pupster enjoyed hanging on the bench, too!

This place is great. The atmosphere is amazing. Beautiful artwork with lovely couches. The tea, coffee, and baked goods are out of this world. I cannot believe that their vegan stuff tastes as good as it does. They are also always so helpful when it comes to asking questions. I even got my wedding cake from here and it was magnificent.

It's sometimes difficult to get tasty vegan desserts so I was looking forward to trying this place out! I love how unique and refined the flavors they offer are - of the things we ordered, my favorites were probably the matcha/rose cake or the blood orange loaf slice. The earl grey cake was quite dense however, and the raspberry buttercream was a bit too sweet and buttery tasting. Unfortunately, the lady that was working was not very friendly but I'd like to give her the benefit of the doubt; perhaps she was having a rough day. Overall: The vegan goodies can lean on the dense or dry side but the flavor options are lovely and the desserts are beautiful!

If you are looking for a quaint coffee shop with excellent baked goods this is the spot. With different options everyday this is a place that won't get dull. Staff is very helpful and knowledgeable of the items sold.

What a neat cozy and delicious place to grab some fantastic dessert with tea, coffee or hot cocoa! Visited on a Friday evening at 10 pm and enjoyed a slice of chocolate cake with pistachio creme filling accompanied by a lovely cup of Earl Gray tea. My husband opted for a blondie with chocolate chips accompanied by a cup of hot cocoa with creme on top. Everything was delicious and we look forward to returning to see what the next group of desserts is being offered.

I cannot believe this place has 4.5 stars overall- it actually blows my mind. I have been to hundreds of bakeries, including the amazing bakeries of NYC and have to say this is the worst bakery I have ever been to! First of all, my fiancÃ© and I ordered one coffee, and three very small pastries. We had an apple pie to eat at their cafe, and took home a chocolate matcha cupcake and a coconut cream pie. The apple pie had a decent flavor, but was mostly crust. The apple chunks were extremely small and there weren't nearly enough to make it a moist apple pie. My fiancÃ© did say that his coffee was good. The following day we tried our desserts that we choice to bring home and they were inedible! My chocolate matcha cupcake tasted like dirt/grass. We each tried a bite and then ended up throwing it away! My fiancÃ© said the coconut cream pie had next to no flavor, and that was partially wasted as well. I cannot believe that I wasted $22 on this place! So disappointing to say the least!

Our desserts for our wedding were made by Butterwood Bake Consortium, and weeks later our guests still cannot stop raving about how good everything was! We had a blood orange cake with vanilla mascarpone buttercream wedding cake, banana spice cake with mocha buttercream mini cakes, blondies, and brownies. Everything was AMAZING! I don't know how they do it, but their cakes are so dense and moist, and the brownies just melt in your mouth! Ally was amazing with answering our questions, and making sure everything was absolutely perfect. Butterwood is now my go-to bakery in the city. We'll be lifelong customers!
The pumpkin cake with maple buttercream frosting was delicious. Looking forward to having the gingerbread tomorrow.

My absolute favorite bakery. Used them for my wedding and got so many compliments!! The cakes are delicious, I love that they are a bit thicker and not overly sweet. Not to mention they are beautiful! So many unique flavors to choose from too!

If you've seen or heard anything about this place, you've seen their magical photo-worthy cakes. Their display looks like it comes out of the Secret Garden. Many items are vegan! Unfortunately, I've now had two less than great cakes from this place. And the bottom line for me is - your cakes can be Instagram fodder all day, but if you want repeat customers, they also have to taste good. To get specific, because I'm happy to go back if there are some changes: first, the cakes I've had are way too sweet. I asked for something light and not very sweet and was still served a pretty dense slice of cake with hard, ultra sweet buttercream. Call me strange, but I generally like my buttercream fluffy. The highlight of the cake I tried most recently was it's blueberry lemon compote - which was perfect, so I know there is someone there who sure can cook, the recipes just need some fine tuning IMHO. More good stuff - the coffee is strong, the wifi is free, and the ambiance is fantastic. If the recipes get a little fluffier, lighter and the cakes feel a little fresher, I'm happy to return and give this cute spot another shot.

Reasonable prices for very unique tastes! We were looking for a new dessert place to check out and this was the cutest little shop with a variety of different desserts to choose from. Definitely recommend if you got a palette for flavors you don't normally see around!

I first visited this place on the way home from doctoral classes because it seemed like a pretty great reward for having survived statistics. I have been here, oh, four or five times now and the only reason I'm not giving five stars is that, every once in a while, I get a cake that is a little too strange, even for me. However, most of them are fantastic. Sage with prickly pear? Awesome. Earl gray? Spectacular. And the hot chocolate is real CHOCOLATE. It will change your life, seriously. Also, the brownies are the richest you'll ever find. So, basically, come here. Do it now. It is open late. Have a complex cake like Vegan lavender honey cream with edible flowers. You will not regret it. This is real cake, not a mix. Bask in it and be happy!

This is the best cake I have ever had. The cake is so moist and the icing so light it melts in your mouth. I always get the mini cakes because they are just perfect. I haven't found anything that compares in Pittsburgh, but I will keep you posted.

Came here on a late Thursday afternoon and the place was completely empty. The decor is great. Was not sure what to expect about the cake options and was pleasantly surprised. They had a variety of unique cake flavors and vegan options. I ended up deciding on a lavender olive oil cake with pistachio buttercream and a latte. They do not have a coffee menu also fyi. My friends ordered and then we waited. The interior decor is beautiful so really didn't mind waiting for the coffee and cake. There was only one lady working so we understood it would take some time. Was so happy to see latte art on all three of our drinks. I had a latte and my friends had cappuccinos. I was so excited that they served the cake on cute china. The lavender olive oil cake was hands down the best cake I have ever had. The olive oil made the cake so dense and rich and the lavender was the perfect complement. It was not too overbearing. The pistachio buttercream was also perfect and not too sweet or rich. Surprisingly, after eating the slice of cake I was so full. Was hesitant, because for a piece of cake and latte it was $10.70, but I will definitley come back and try other cake flavors!

Very cute bakery! They have so many interesting flavors which change daily! I ordered the gingerbread cake with maple espresso cream - extremely decadent! (Definitely recommend splitting between two people - I'm still (hours later) in a food coma after eating it all) The store itself is quite quiet and not a bad study spot either! Excited to go back and to try something else !

In the wise words of Rhianna - cake cake cake cake cake cake! (And delicious coffee too!) This place is my dream. Their decor is fabulous, very Parisian Victorian with some modern etsy kitsch. Super comfortable. The staff is wonderfully friendly and welcoming...but really it's the CAKE! I can't believe I'm lucky enough to live in a neighborhood with this bakery! The desserts I've tried so far have been luxurious and decadent. Olive oil fig cake with pistachio buttercream icing...butterscotch pudding...chocolate peanut butter cake...like nothing I've ever tasted. I will happily continue to indulge in my new favorite Larryville spot.

Came here with my mom after dinner as the desserts at the restaurant did not appeal to us. There were about 6 different specialty cakes on display, and we went with lavender with strawberry buttercream (based on other reviews, I believe the flavors regulary change). We were given a generous slice and they also gave me a candle since it was her birthday. Cute coffeeshop/bakery with Victorian plating, decor and furniture. Would be a cozy place to spend an afternoon or have a date.

I ordered the 9 inch lemon almond cake with buttercream and lemon curd icing for my son's 42nd. birthday. The cake was probably the best cake that I have had in years maybe in my life. Also it was beautifully decorated with fresh leaves and tulips. There were six of us and we all had a generous slice and extra for them to take home. I love icing and it was to die for, thick and delicious. In the past I have also had the lavender cake (a slice) and it also stayed in my memory as incredibly good. BTW the bakery inside is decorated like a jewel box with gorgeous lighting and wallpaper.

I'm usually not a (cup)cake person, but Butterwood has changed my mind! The chocolate cupcake with raspberry was moist and delicious. The buttercream frosting was stiffer than I was expecting, but worked perfectly. We also got a brownie each, which were both large and super chocolatey. The dÃ©cor was unique and it had a great feel. I will absolutely be coming here again, plus they're open late!
Awesome KLVN coffee and scrumptious desserts. Serious coffee, no flavors but you can get your latte sweet if desired. French victorian decor meets shabby chic. My new favorite coffee shop.

I came for a get-together with a few friends and I enjoyed the quaint decor and presentation of the sweet treats. There is a surprising amount of seating for the size of the location. Street parking was readily available nearby. I did not have the best experience due to understaffing, there was only one individual working and she was having a difficult time keeping up with the orders. I was also not a fan of my hot chocolate, which as you can see in the photo was served in 3 containers. When I received it it was cold and the staff was unavailable for me to notify her. The icing on my cupcake was incredibly rich that it was difficult to eat the entire thing. The friends I was with had the same issue with the slices of cake that they ordered. I will be giving it another chance, hoping that my disappointment was just based on the understaffing.

I purchased a whole chocolate cake, which I had pre-ordered online. This was my first time buying baked goods at this shop today. My daughter selected the shop for her bday cake due to positive reviews online. I spent about $70 after tax etc. It looked nice but that's it. The cake was EXTREMELY dry and seemed old. The texture was awful for the money. We bake better cakes at home. Nobody at the bday party finished their slice and we all agreed Wal-Mart cake taste better and fresher. We ended up running out for replacement dessert tonight.

3.5 Stars I went to Butterwood with a friend after months of wanting to try it out. When we arrived, it was pretty quiet. There were not too many people in the store. However, that did change over time - a line started to form later on! I guess this place is pretty popular! The decor is Victorian-esque. The ambiance is very interesting- albeit a little dark and strange- but they make it work. The cakes are all very pretty, and I love the variety of flavors that they seem to have. There are also vegan friendly options. This is definitely not your typical cake shop. My friend and I ordered two cakes: one with espresso buttercream and the other with blueberries and lavender, I believe. First of all, the cakes are huge. One slice is definitely enough to share between two people. You pay $7.50 per slice, which is a bit expensive, but it was okay considering the size. Both cakes were extremely dense. The espresso buttercream was good, but a bit too sweet, and the lavender cake did not really taste of lavender. I prefer lighter cakes, so these were not my cup of tea as everything was very heavy. Overall, I don't regret checking this place out. The workers were very friendly, and the cakes and desserts are very beautiful. However, the cakes are just a different style to what I prefer- very rich and heavy. It was a good experience, but I do not think that I would go back regularly.

A very delicious bakery, but I do think it's suited best for people with a certain taste. I like my cakes and icing very sweet and soft, and I find the icing style here to be much more on the butter-y and thick side, less on the sweet side. They have classic flavors and more experimental flavors, but nothing too out of the box and I think everything works really well. The indoor space is beautiful (almost Victorian decorated?) and they have a small back patio you can sit at.

Found this place online after eating at SMOKE. So happy we decided to stop in. It was busy but not crazy. Easy to order and sit to wait for our espresso and cake. Ordered the Tumeric cake and some butterscotch pudding. Both excellent. Chill vibe. Great place to come for dessert or just a coffee. Staff friendly.

I stopped in early on a Wednesday night looking for a nice place for my mom and I to enjoy dessert and chat. The ambiance is remarkable. I ended up having the vegan lavender cake and was blown away! I usually cringe when thinking about vegan desserts but this was so light and elegant. My mom had the poppyseed cake and really enjoyed it. The lady working was extremely friendly and hospitable.

I love their cakes and the staff is so nice and accommodating! However I had to bump my review down after my 2nd visit because I realized that all the cakes taste the same... So I bring my friends here, hyping up this bakery as I normally do. We all got a poppy seed rose cake with chocolate buttercream and couldn't finish the slice (just like the last time). I thought that the taste was the same as the slice I had last time, I couldn't taste the rose at all. It just tasted like vanilla cake with chocolate buttercream - but I dismissed it. So then I got really excited when they brought out a newly made raspberry cake with ricotta cheese icing. So...naturally I bought both. You'd think they'd taste different right?? Wrong! They tasted exactly the same...I don't know how, but it tasted exactly like a vanilla cake with vanilla buttercream with no raspberry or ricotta. Disappointed by the wasted splurge, but enjoyed every bite of the cake!

Very cute store with a wide variety of treats. Gluten free and vegan selections are very nice options to have and not always easy to come by. Cappuccino was one of the best I've had in Pittsburg. The chocolate cake was just ok unfortunately. The frosting was a bit artificial for me, and dropped an otherwise 5/5 place to just a 4. But if your looking for a cute place to try some AMAZING coffee this is a MUST.

I live in the neighborhood and finally stopped in. It was worth it. They have items for everyone, vegan included. Though, I will say, 9/10 of the combination choices are "unique" -- which personally I love, but if you're looking for the plain Jane typical options, maybe go elsewhere. When we went I tried a pound cake with pistachio cream with fresh strawberries. I didn't really get too much pistachio, but it was decadent and very good. The same for the chocolate brownie. Amazing! The place itself has interesting decor and the originality alone is worth the trip if you're nearby!

Just picked up a cake I ordered for my girlfriends birthday. It was supposed to be a white cake with a toasted buttercream icing, but it was the most odd cake I've ever had. Let's start with the high points; the icing was AMAZING and it was decorated beautifully. Now the low...As soon as we took our first bite we both said it tastes like shrimp. Yes, shrimp. I have no idea what in the world would make a cake taste like that, but it does...it's inedible. It smells odd too and completely crumbles apart. I had such high hopes but was completely disappointed. I might try again in the future, but not anytime soon.
Everything we have had here is amazing. The atmosphere is great to have a date night or hang out with some friends. I am also pleasantly surprised by the creative options we find each time we go.
Had a blueberry basil with whiskey cream cake and brown butter blonde. Delicious and unique flavors in a comfortable and relaxing atmosphere. We'll be back!

Yuuuum!! This place is incredible. I went with the chocolate cake w/raspberry buttercream icing (it was vegan). Probably one of the best vegan desserts I've ever had. It was so tasty and rich w flavor, which is not the case in most vegan desserts. The service was great, and our waitress was very helpful. I heard about this place from social media so I decided to try it after dinner. It was the perfect end to the night! It also doesn't hurt that it's so freaking cute inside! Love it. I will be back.

I stopped by with two friends a couple of weeks ago on a Sat. evening. Given that we were looking to get together later in the evening for hot beverages or dessert, Butterwood fit the bill, so we headed over to L-ville to check it out. Because their specialty is clearly cake and there weren't many other desserts in the case, we each ordered a slice of cake ($6 + tax each). Going against my usual adventurous streak when it comes to edibles, I decided to play it safe and stick with the chocolate cake with chocolate buttercream icing. The cake was velvety in texture, but not quite as most as I was hoping, and it was rather stiff on the iced side. As for the icing, it was definitely the best part of the cake--it was decadently creamy and rich, as buttercream should be. My friends ordered the chocolate pistachio cake and the vanilla poppy seed cake, and I tried bites of both. The cake component of the chocolate pistachio seemed identical to my chocolate cake, but the icing was saltier than mine with a rather muted pistachio taste. The vanilla poppy seed was the most interesting of the bunch, consisting of yellow cake and tangy vanilla icing sprinkled generously with poppy seeds. As others have mentioned, the slices were rather large, such that neither of my friends entirely finished theirs (as usual, I unabashedly housed my entire slice, however). If you visit and don't see a cake that you'd enjoy, I'd recommend waiting a bit and checking back, given that the cakes seem to rotate. By the time that we left, all of the cakes that'd been available when we ordered had been replaced by different types of cakes (hello, Meyer lemon cake!). The atmosphere is quaint, making it an ideal setting in which to relax and catch up over dessert and/or hot beverages. If you're a night owl and/or a fan of dessert, I definitely recommend checking it out--your inner Martha Stewart will definitely be pleased!

This is the third time I come here and I love it. Tonight we got a lemon and pistachio cake! The cake is moist, the lemon flavor is very and I would say that the frosting adds anything to it: it is already delicious. The selection of cakes is always changing, so hurry up and go try it!

I loved this impromptu stop over the weekend. It's a super cute, tiny space with comfortable seating options and friendly service. I got tea and split a snickerdoodle blondie with a friend that was unique and delicious. We sat and talked and although we had planned to walk around a bit after we stayed long enough that we had to head straight out. It's a perfect place to sit for a spell and chat with friends or read a book and all their sweet treats looked amazing. There was also a flier on the counter for an evening knitting group that apparently meets there. Highly recommend and I am definitely getting my next birthday cake from them!

Fantastic little bakery/cafe in Lawrenceville. The cakes are delicious and dense, and the buttercream frosting is to die for. The chai latte was the perfect temperature and wasn't too sweet. Go with a few friends so you can sample all the treats!

Updating my review to include a custom cake order my office had placed for a co-worker's birthday. We placed an order for the cake on Tuesday and it was ready Friday morning. We ordered a vegan cake, chocolate base with pistachio buttercream. It was easily one of the best cakes I've ever had. We didn't ask for any decoration but it still came beautifully presented. Absolutely will be ordering cakes from here in the future!

We found the Butterwood on Yelp while searching for some desert to cap off dinner and a show at The Cabaret. Tucked away at the North end of Butler Street in Lawrenceville, this little place is a gem. The mashup of Victorian influence and bare brick walls adorned with interesting art just works. The case is filled with delicious deserts and there is an array of beverages to sip on. Give this comfortable and cozy desert cafe a try the next time you find yourself in L-ville. You'll be glad you did.

One of the coolest bakeries in Pittsburgh! I've gone a couple times and each has been extremely enjoyable. The inside is so welcoming and has a wonderful warm atmosphere. The baked goods are always different, and there are tons of vegan options! I got a the chocolate cake with almond butter cream icing and my girlfriend got the lavender bunt cake. Both were fantastic and they warmed our desserts up before serving them. The cake was very moist and the icing was light and not too sweet. I'm not one to always get chocolate cake as a dessert but I couldn't resist with this one. The lavender cake was so good. There was a hint of lemon that paired so perfectly with the cake. The flavors were all light and nothing clashed. The hot chocolate is an experience in itself. It's a sipping chocolate that they make in house. It's very unique and if you like rich chocolate flavors you'll love this! It's not really sweet, it's more on the bitter side but it's a perfect match with the sweet cakes. Heads up: there is pretty limited seating.

Whoo haaaa, finally stopped by this oddly named bakery in the far end of Lawrenceville area. They have lovely cupcakes, tea cakes, vegan and non. The tea was pretty good as well. I think the baked goods are yummy and of a good quality, however the prices are severely extravagant. Our bill came to 25 dollars and it was just for one blondie, one slice of rose tea cake and two teas. If you want to buy an actual cake from them it is literally 400 dollars, WTF? What has happened to this world that people can charge this much for food?

The space is absolutely fantastic, dark and gothic but also homey comfortable, I love it! We tried a few different cakes and pastries and all of them were exceptional, the focus on herbs was pleasant and played really well. I had a herbal tea and my friends had lattes, all were good. I'm definitely adding it to my lawrenceville agenda when I'm in the area!

This place is SO darling! So unique. Such a fun addition to Lawrenceville. A "dessert cafÃ©", I've only ever popped in and gotten stuff to go, but plan a visit to enjoy their fabulous desserts, coffee, and tea inside. The dÃ©cor is so fun, they have an array of eclectic chairs, velour couches, and tables for dining, drinking and relaxing, and a tiny little outside area with a few tables as well. Closed Monday & Tuesday, the rest of the weekdays they're open noon until 11 PM - open late, love it! Perfect for post-dinner dessert and tea. Weekend hours they open at 10 AM and close a little earlier. If you're in or around Lawrenceville, definitely add a visit here to the top of your list. Their desserts are truly SO decadent and delicious. They use only organic Daisy flour, Wholesome Sweeteners sugar, and local organic eggs. Their display case is always full of the most gorgeous cookies, cakes, cupcakes, bars, etc., always with vegan and non-vegan options, and sometimes gluten free as well. I mean....it can't get better than this! And you can truly tell they use quality ingredients because the look, taste and feel is topnotch. They do custom cake ordering as well. Two recent standout desserts include the vegan lavender cake with buttercream icing, and the vegan chocolate cupcake with peanut butter icing...wow. My boyfriend's go-to is the Blondie bar...so good. Treat yourself next time you're in the neighborhood, you will not regret it!

I have not actually been to this location, but had one of their amazing cakes! For my baby shower, my friend ordered a vegan carrot cake with the vegan buttercream icing. It was honestly one of the best baked vegan treats I have ever had! The icing was so decadent and the perfect balance of not being too sweet. The cake was soft, moist and so fresh! The cake was decorated with real, fresh and beautiful flowers. I look forward to making a trip to the storefront to try even more of their amazingly vegan treats!

Ohhhemmmmgeeeee! I'm seriously so in love with this place. The cake was so freakin good. Somehow she managed to serve it where the bread was slightly warm but the icing was still cold. Chefs kiss man. You can tell it was made with quality ingredients & a lot of thought was put into the flavors. The ambiance of this place is amazing. HIGHLY recommend. We visited Pittsburg for the first time this weekend & this was on my list of places to go- it surpassed all expectations.

I was visiting my hometown for my Dad's 70th birthday. This bakery was recommended to me because they have vegan options. The cake was fabulous! Vanilla with coconut buttercream. So yummy! Everyone loved it. Highly recommended.
Lovely cakes and the iced chai was so good! Cute interiors too - and I LOVE that they're open so late.

As I'm sure you've read from other reviews that this place is pricey, the ever changing selection of sweet, decadent baked goods make up for it. The toddler got a vegan noir chocolate cake, which he devoured, and the MIL and I got a buttercream blood orange cake, which we ate in an unladylike fashion by scarfing down. No shame because the cake was gooood!
Great little bakery/coffee shop in upper Lawrenceville. The desserts are beyond beautiful and taste amazing! The service and the wifi are a bit slow but otherwise well worth a visit!

After running by this place numerous times and wondering what a "bake consortium" was, we finally walked in and discovered a beautiful coffee and bake shop. The space is decorated like a traditional old-fashioned tea parlor with crystal cake stands, wrought iron seating and tables, and dramatic wallpaper. What my husband referred to as a"hipster interpretation of 1920s jazz music" played in the background. An impressive array of treats are on display, including vegan options (no gluten-free on this day, sadly). The barista was excellent and took great care with my americano and my husband's pour over, and they tasted lovely because of it. A quick trip this is not- plan on stopping by in their cozy space for a chat and a dessert. I do suggest better signage, since we weren't sure if we could go in at first! But do go, and enjoy a lovely afternoon brew and treat.

Open late! A pleasant surprise from what otherwise appeared to be a dead city during the week. Came with my mom looking for good dessert with vegan options, and this place more than satisfied. We shared a slice of their vegan chocolate strawberry cake, and an oatmeal cookie sandwich type thing with coffee filling. Both were fantastic, and moist. I could be biased, but neither appeared to lose any flavor or produce any weird aftertaste as a result of being vegan. Only complaint would be that they were just a bit too sweet. The frosting was very, very sugary. We also had tea along with the dessert, which was a good compliment to the food and the cold weather outside. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a place to hang out later at night in this city, or looking for good dessert in general.

To know me is to know that my favorite food is cake. That being said, my expectations are high. The best of the best in my opinion is...wait for it...Giant Eagle. Yep. I love the sugary sweet icing and the texture of their cakes. BUT, Butterwood is giving GE a run for their batter. I stopped in on Saturday with some family to complement our delicious and decadent dinner from Dive. Among our choices were a Cranberry [short] cake (literally - it was short), cinnamon/chocolate cake; vanilla/sunflower seed and chocolate/sweet potato. I split the sunflower seed and sweet potato options and DANG, these are GOOD cakes! They're so dense and flavorful I actually couldn't finish - which is VERY unlike me. Take a pic, because now that a bakery is open down the street from me until ELEVEN PM, I'll be twice my size in no time. At $6+ a pop, I might also be broke, but I'll also be happy - so bring on the Butterwood P.S. I got our cakes to go, but look forward to eating in next time. The dÃ©cor is straight out of a Victorian cakery! Love it!

The interior styling and decor of this cafe is incredible with usage of antiques and vintage items to create a cozy, artsy aesthetic. The Butterwood offers a variety of succulent gourmet pastries and cakes with surprising flavors to delight every taste bud. In addition, many coffees and teas are available to accompany your sweet treat. Service is always excellent and the baristas are extremely helpful answering any and all questions. If you want to stop somewhere for a great (and unique) baked good and hot beverage in an interesting setting, you must stop here!

Great hot chocolate, I would go there just for that. The cake choices are interesting and I give them props for having a cool atmosphere, great customer service, and vegan options but unfortunately, I never liked any of the cakes. The cakes are gritty and the frosting is oily tasting. Get the hot chocolate!

Super fun cute place to have something sweet and a coffee or tea. I wouldn't go here if you're in a rush, only 1 employee. The homemade cakes and icings are delicious AND beautiful! Fun place to go alone or with a friend to catch up!

Stopped in for a hot chocolate. It is so cute inside. The decor is very rich and beautiful. The cakes look amazing! I wasn't able to get a cake as I just bought a cake yesterday. They have a lot of vegan options which is very important. I was able to get a vegan hot chocolate which has been causing me a headache lately trying to get. I was happy they were able to accommodate. The cashier was very nice and fulfilled a special request I made for cinnamon on my hot chocolate which I appreciated. I will definitely return and maybe bring a book to read inside. It was very quiet which was nice.

I came here on a Sunday for a short cake break. I was pleasantly surprised to see how nice the bakery is designed and by the lovely atmosphere which is somewhat romantic/bohemian. There is a unique selection of delicious cakes including vegan options. They rotate their cake/frosting flavors frequently. I tried the chocolate cake with pistachio icing and my wife ordered the butternut squash cake with caramel icing. Both cakes were very well made, and delicious. They were rich in flavor and we left with our sweet tooth craving satisfied. There were several people who ordered coffee or tea, and had their laptops open doing work. I Overall, a very pleasant experience and will definitely come back to try their rotation selection of cakes.

The Butterwood Bake ambiance was soothing and cute. No strong lights makes it sort of romantic too. That is not why I ended up there. The reason was the cakes and they delivered - peach custard was almost naughty, so creamy and delicious. The pear cake was a pleasant surprise - I did not expect a burst of flavor that I got. I felt in love with it and I wanted the feeling to last longer but, all I got now is a nice memory so I will have to go back to get more of the same. A confirm a few previous reviews saying that "the girl at counter" was nice.
I've had this place on my must try list, it didn't disappoint. The lavender cake was appealing, the aroma was inviting, and the flavors, out of this world! This was the first of many future trips

This place has great tea, coffee and desserts. It is a bit expensive, but you definitely get what you pay for. They have very unique and unusual flavors and combinations, things you will not find anywhere else.

Stopped in here with a friend last weekend. It's welcoming and cute inside. We tried several different dessert items - blackberry cake, chocolate cake, chocolate tart and the pear cake. I liked the Fall flavors of the pear cake, but wasn't a big fan of the blackberry cake. It was just lacking in flavor overall. My favorite was the chocolate cake which had an espresso filling and what I think was a salted vanilla buttercream. Lots of flavor - awesome! There's comfortable seating on the couch, though it gave me the view of the dust underneath the old wood stove.It looked like no one had cleaned under there in a long time. My only other disappointment was that the only iced beverage option they had was the Hibiscus tea. Don't get me wrong, it was really good, but what I was craving was an iced coffee. I would return to check out other flavor options that have :-)

We stopped for dessert with friends and thought Butterwood was such a quaint little bakery with really unique flavor combinations. The atmosphere was super cozy and more like being a guest at someone's home than being in a bakery. The employee was friendly. The desserts were like nothing I had ever had before. Typical bakeries have chocolate and vanilla, but Butterwood uses unique flavors that were delicious. We tried the mini chocolate cake with Strawberry whipped cream, the olive oil orange cake with strawberry icing, the fig cake and apricot cake with pistachio icing. The cakes are definitely denser than what I was used to, more like pound cake. Everything was very flavorful. The cakes were moist and the icing wasn't too sweet. Such a nice little place to stop and loved that they are open late!
Best tea cake I've ever had. Great chai latte... right balance for spice (get it with oat milk.) Friendly and comfortable atmosphere.

We ventured out to The Butterwood Bake Consortium after dinner one night to try some of their pretty and delicious desserts. It was hard to choose given all of the variety that they have but I decided on the Blueberry Rose Cake with Fig Cream and hubby got the Frosted Brownie. The cake was light and the frosting now too sweet which is just the way I like it though I didn't really taste much rose or blueberry in there. The decor and ambiance are really relaxing and they have a cute patio in the back with a few seats.

I loved this little..."boutique" bakery. Loved the decor and the laid back vibe. Loved the options for vegan or healthy choices (none of which I selected, mind you). Loved the blondie I had over coffee late at night (they're open late...another thing I loved). It was huge and delicious. Pretty much my only complaint was the dent it left in myfitnesspal calorie budget. And...by dent...I mean it obliterated it. That said...I didn't go there for the healthy options. I'll be back.

Very cool! I picked up 2 of their little cakes to take back home. The vegan chocolate one was really good. The cake itself was delicious and not too dry as some vegan cake variations can sometimes be. I would definitely have their chocolate vegan cake again and would like to try more of their cakes! The other cake I got for my friend was their lavender cake with honey buttercream. My friend said it was delicious as well. The shop itself is very cute and has a vintage vibe to it. There is indoor and outdoor patio seating. They have coffee/espresso drinks too. I'd love to come back!
I'm lactose intolerant and this place has it all. You won't be disappointed by their attention to detail either as these sweets are almost too cool to nom on!

The decor inside this place is beautiful. One you step in you're greeted by comfy chairs, big spacious mirrors and cute little iron and glass tables. The big display case is set back in the space with plenty of selections with a majority of them being vegan friendly. A couple of sweet ladies were running the store making coffee and serving treats. I chose a non-vegan blondie which was served on a cute little (prob antique) pattern plates like grandma had. The blondie i had was rich and soft with that typical brownie crust on top. I didn't order coffee as it was later in the day and i wasnt in the mood for any joe. About halfway into the blondie i needed a drink and the server hooked me up with a small glass of tap water. All in all a nice little bakery, really nice atmosphere, tasty treats and good service. It would have been nice for them to have a water cooler for an alternative to coffee, but other than that very nice.

Well typically we are pleased with this place but today not so much. The girl that took our order was completely unfriendly and rude, and the two pieces of cake I got to go were dinky and crumbled into pieces. For about $5 each that sucks.

Great coffee, and coffee service with a signature touch. Awesome baked goods, tasteful, fun decor, and a super friendly staff. Great meeting spot or study spot. Kudos especially to the kind and knowledgeable baristas!

This place is heaven! The perfect spot for a cup of tea and a slice of delicious cake. Perfect for a craving as they serve by the slice and they are always making fresh, new cakes. They also make excellent full sized cakes per whatever you want, truly amazing.

Allow me to start out by expressing just how much I love this place. I happened to discover this quaint little bakery on a sunny Sunday after church. And I've returned several times with friends and sometimes even alone! Every cake I've tried thus far has been moist, not too sweet with just the right amount of icing! What makes the cakes even better is that they're vegan so they're constructed with all natural ingredients. For example, they use olive oil instead of butter. The fruit and flowers on the cakes are always fresh. The dining atmosphere is an absolute delight filled with old-fashioned charm. There is just one thing that bothers me about this place. Whenever slicing your cake and transferring it to the plate, the baristas use their ungloved hands to pick up and balance the cake slices. Today, I watched one of the baristas pick up a brownie and just hand it to a customer then mess with her hair bun. This screams unsanitary to me. Other than this, the place is amazing. I just hope one day they'll actually use gloves or serving utensils.

Is this place decadent? Yes. Is this place pricey? Yes. Is it worth it? Heck yeah it is! I'm not a penny pincher by any means. I'm an impulse buyer, therefor I look at prices as I'm being rung up. The place is expensive, but I'm totally fine with paying the price for delicious, well made pastries. The slices of cake are MASSIVE. They don't skimp on that. Plus, the ambiance alone is adorable. You feel like you've fallen down the rabbit hole and woken up in Wonderland at the Mad Hatter's tea party. Only less crazy people (probably... depends on the company). I tried the matcha cake, and it was fab... and I don't even like matcha! But the green tea was very faint, and the buttercream was very rich, so it all blended together in an excellent fashion. Plus, I LOVE that they're open late night. PERFECT spot for after dinner treats! This will definitely be a spot I will stop at regularly.

Just want to preface this review to say that the decor, atmosphere and employees are lovely here. This review is solely based on the bakery items. Such a disappointment! The Black Sesame cake honestly was so dense, thick and impossible to take more than 1 bite of. The frosting on top tasted like plain sugar. Chocolate tart - just not something even worth finishing, it tasted stale. Came here wIth really high hopes. I don't know if this is just a type of baking style that doesn't work for me or if this bakery was just having an off day but I don't see any reason to come here again.

Came here late on a Saturday night after dinner at another place on Butler. It's one of the only options for late night sweet treats. The dÃ©cor is cute and I'm sure could be better appreciated during the day. There is ample space to sit, chat and enjoy the baked goods. The selection is pretty small, but understandable for a small establishment. I got the carrot spice mini cakes that had sugary icing. The cake itself is pretty mild. I thought it was a bit expensive, especially compared to other bakeries ($4.28). The cashier is a bit reserved...my friend commented that she is "not too friendly."

Ally made our wedding cakes and they were SO DELICIOUS! Lemon buttermilk cake with vanilla mascarpone icing and lemon curd. Lots of guests said this was the best wedding cake they'd ever had. Not only were the cakes delicious and beautiful, she was really helpful throughout the whole process. We couldn't have been happier. Also a great spot to stop in for a slice!

Love! So excited for this adorable cake/bakery! That is open late! We got the chocolate cake and it was just amazing! The coffee was good too! I am taking my kids this Saturday! We love it! Such a cute place inside too! :)

This is my favorite bakery. The cakes are so original, and I always order something new every time I come and continue to be impressed. I love the coconut cakes and the lavender cakes. The cakes are not too sweet or creamy, just about right. The desserts are on the expensive side, but the portions are huge. The staff are super friendly, and I love the Victorian theme. This place is quiet, and even when lines form, I never get frustrated because I know that Butterwood is worth the wait.

The Butterwood Bake Consortium had me at cake. When my friend first told me about the place, I was so excited that there is a cake specialty bakery close to where I live. After stalking them on Yelp and Instagram, I finally went in. It was a Friday afternoon and there weren't too many customers so my friend and I got to chose the nice couch. I looked at the available cakes and they all looked so good that I had trouble picking out THE one that I wanted. Once I got my cake, it was gone before I could blink. It was THAT GOOD. I couldn't resist my temptation and got another cake to-go. The interior is very elegant yet not too aloof. The staff were very friendly and helpful, especially because my friend had a stomach ache. They brought her hot water and told her to lay down until she felt better to move. Their cake flavors vary day to day, so if you want a specific flavor, I'd say give them a call to ask. They will also bake a whole cake if you call a day or two ahead of time. I'm definitely going back again soon and get a whole cake for my party coming up!

Yum! This place is super vintage chic decor with nice seating area and even a little outdoor seating area in the back. They have some of the cutest, most instagram worthy cakes and pastries that I've ever seen and they're just as delicious as they look! I love the cake so much that I got a slice of Lemon Poppyseed to bring home and my husband (who doesn't like cake) love it!! I didn't get a drink this time but would want Excited to go back!

this quaint cake shop is perfect for everything from afternoon tea with friends to dessert after a night out in lawrenceville! tucked away and easy to miss, the Butterwood Bake Consortium offers deliciously succulent and thick slices of cake with an assortment of creative and fresh tasting flavors. the prices are high ($6+ for a slice) but you're getting a huge slice easily shared by two that is rich and decadent without weighing you down. they have other pastries if you're not a cake person and have a variety of vegan options too! having worked previously in pastry kitchens, i can attest this is some of the best cake i've ever had! the space is small, but even when it's busy, you can usually find a space to sit and chat and the atmosphere is pleasant without being too loud. wifi is available (cell service was spotty inside) but this is more of a hangout spot than a study spot. staff are friendly and helpful, though service can slow down a bit at peak times when the line gets long. when my friend was disappointed that someone in front of us got the last slice of chocolate cake we were eyeing, the staff made sure to go check if there was another similar one in the back even though it was late in the evening (thankfully there was an espresso chocolate cake!) it's a cute place with delicious treats, definitely not to be missed!

I visited butterwood yesterday for the first time and really enjoyed my experience. The ambience is of a quant Victorian/ European style cafe and the decor is lovely. I particularly liked the seating arrangements in that there were several Parisian style metal cafe tables and chairs and then couches with tables in other areas. My fiancÃ© and I ordered the Parisian style hot chocolate, pot de creme, and a piece of olive oil cake with raspberry filing and salted vanilla buttercream. Everything we had was delicious but insanely decadent and we definitely over ordered. We would have been fine sharing 1 item but good to know for the future. The items themselves were really very good but again it was a lot all at once. The hot chocolate was literally just like chocolate syrup and they give you steamed milk to add in. The pot de creme was so so dense and same with the cake. My fiancÃ© joked that we might leave with diabetes after eating everything. We paid ~$15 total which I think is a fair price considering the size of the items, how filling they were, and also because I believe they tend to use natural ingredients where they can. My only comment would be on the gal that took our order and brought us our items. She seemed to be a bit pretentious but I'll chalk that up as her individual personality and not a ding against the business.

I really wanted to love this place. The vibe and decorations are beautiful. However, the day that we went, they only had one person working and the service was ridiculously slow- about a half hour of waiting with only a couple people ahead of me in line. The barista ended up getting the order wrong and we were told that we had to go back in line to get it fixed (another 15 minutes of waiting). For all of the waiting, the drinks were pretty good and the two cakes we tried were fine, but dry. Not sure if I'll go back.

This place is so cute! It's the perfect little spot for a dessert! Fun decor, good music, friendly staff, and delicious treats! We parked in the small parking lot right next door. They have a sweet little outdoor area I can't wait to check out once it gets warmer. We ordered a cardamom cake (small with light frosting/whip cream) it was so good- like a spice cake. Chocolate cake with raspberry frosting, dense and large it was good, the raspberry flavoring could have been stronger but I was good.

I love the decor and antique finds! The cakes were great. I got the lavender strawberry and my mom got the spiced cake w/ maple frosting. We both got the drip coffee. I would recommend to someone who wants a quaint place to read while enjoying delicious coffee and something sweet!

A fantastic bakery that makes gourmet cupcakes and cake slices. Beautifully decorated. Overall cakes moist. Flavors are unique, some great combinations while others not so much. Overall would make great gifts to bring to large gatherings, but forewarned to get your blood sugars checked, and a safe place to nap for that post-sugar crash. vegan lavender cake with agave buttercream - bits of savory, floral, saltiness in one bite. Strong lavender flavor, one of my favorite! blood orange with priickly pear buttercream - tasty, couldn't quite taste the blood orange or prickly pear aspects. coconut cake with macha buttercream - definitely one of their most flavorful combinations. Mild, rich on the palate, light on the stomach. Would highly recommend this cake. earl grey with honey buttercream - cake was a bit dense and dry. Honey buttercream although aesthetcially appealing was not very flavorful. Tones of earl grey flavor stand out strongly. However, would not recommend this. poppy rose with fig cream - fantastic, incredibly moist cake. The rose flavor stands out strongly, very floral. I very much enjoyed this cake. chocolate can with maple sweet potato cream - rich, a bit heavy. Not for the faint of heart.

My girlfriend surprised me with a cake from here from my birthday and it was so delicious! I've been here before and picked up some little things but I've been dying to try their cakes. I love that they have vegan options especially vegan cakes are so hard to come by. The blueberry lavender cake was delicious and even my non vegan friends loved it and said they wanted it for their birthdays! If you need a vegan birthday cake (or any cake really) this is the place to come!

Finally was able to stop by, and I'm so happy I did!! They offer a wide variety of different baked goods and drinks. Everything was delicious! Although there's not much seating indoors, during the warmer season they have an outdoor garden in the back.

Butterwood is my go-to place for baked goods whenever I have a sugar craving. They have plenty of delicious vegan and non-vegan options, so there is something for everyone. I always enjoy how the cake flavors rotate, so I'm encouraged to try a new flavor every time. There is also an extensive coffee and tea menu, so you can have the perfect drink to go with your dessert.

I just recently found out about Butterwood Bake Consortium and had to check it! It's essential a cake shop. The interior is rich and inviting. I love the red velvet chairs and benches. It's a pretty small space but it feels very comfortable. I almost overwhelmed by the amount of sweets options in the display case. I was also surprised to see multiple vegan options. After looking at all my options I decided to try the lemon poppy seed cake with a black berry buttercream and a hot chocolate. My two friends and I sat down and waited for desserts. The staff person was friendly and quickly brought out our cakes and drinks. The hot chocolate was a tea cup filled half way with melted chocolate that you poured cream into. It was delicious and rich! Definitely would recommend it to anyone who goes. The cake on the other hand was just okay. It was just a little to dense for liking but still a quality cake. I can't wait to go back and try more of their wonderful selections!

It's okay, The atmosphere is nice, i thought the way it was set up was really cute, they have a very pretty tree with really pretty plates as the foliage. I thought that was neat. As for the food, I wasn't very impressed with the cake, it seemed too...doughy? it's just not what i expect in cake, and it's waaaayy too sweet. To be honest, the thing that i will come back for is the Chocolate pot de creme, it's like a dark chocolate creme, with whipped topping. It's amazingly delicious. The service was great, the girl there was very courteous and whenever we needed something, she definitely helped. I want to give this place a higher rating, but i just didn't like most of the stuff they had so i can't.
We went here for a late night dessert and cup of tea. The peanut butter chocolate cake was to die for. I loved the atmosphere and loungey feel. I will definitely be returning for a late night treat.
The atmosphere is awesome. Super cute decor. I purchased a classic chocolate brownie. In my opinion, the brownie was too chocolately and too salty. Box brownies are better.

I have been to Butterwood three times. The ambience is cozy and luxurious and I really appreciate that they are open late. The reason I give this place three stars is the lack of consistent quality of their desserts. The last cake I had (it was their standard chocolate) was very dry and crumbly like it was weeks past its prime. I was so disappointed! If I am going to splurge on something like this it must be perfection every time.

I had the strawberry cake which I immediately regretted... it didn't hit the spot... but the lemon cake with apricot buttercream was def one of the most delectable cakes I've ever eaten (am im a professional cake eater)!! It was dense but soft and extremely flavorful. I am going to order that exact cake for my birthday next month!!

My Dear Butterwood, I'm still in love with you and think you have the most delicious cakes on this planet and the most adorable space in which to enjoy them. And one of your charms is the fact that you are open late, making you a great post-date-night spot to grab dessert and coffee. But Butterwood....don't be open late if you keep running out of desserts before closing!! The last four (count 'em, FOUR) times I have been here after 9, your dessert case has been nearly wiped out (the last two times, in fact, it was literally *empty* save for one sad-looking piece of honey bread). What's the point of being open late if you consistently run out of desserts to offer your cake-loving customers?! I would think by now you should be able to have a better idea of your customer flow (I'm no business whiz, but it's painfully obvious to me as a frequent customer that you do not regularly keep sufficient quantities of desserts on hand to fulfill demand for an entire weekend day). Now Butterwood, I'll give you one more chance, both because I love you and because I think I might have a diagnosable cake addiction disorder. But if you expect me to continue to spend approximately 95% of my bi-weekly paycheck on your cakes, I'm going to need you to start keeping your case stocked during ALL of the times that you are open. Otherwise, you might as well just close early and save us the trouble of making the trek only to be continually disappointed. Still your biggest fan (for now), Tricia

I stopped here for the first time last night and I can't believe how rich the vegan chocolate cake is. The slices are very big and enough to share for two on a date. The vegan chocolate slice was more flavorful than most other "normal" cake I've had (the couch in the front corner is also very comfortable).

I had the brownie and something with elderflower in it and I couldn't have anticipated the explosion of flavor in my mouth. The waitress was nice on a next level and did all she could to make sure me and my friend were taken care of. My new favorite spot.

Came in around 9pm and the place was still busy, more of a quiet hipster crowd with a unique sense of style. We got a piece if chocolate cake to share which was very good, nothing to run back for but good. My wife got tea which ended up being tazo tea, I thought it would be something more non commercial but she said it was good. I on the other hand got a small french press coffee that tasted gross. It's a cool little place but I wouldn't tell my friend you have to try it.
Not bad. Was a little underwhelmed with their sweets selection. I expected to have more selections. The inside was really nice and unique.

Oh, Butterwood. Where to begin? First, the cakes. They are inventive, delicious, and beautiful. They usually offer at least 4-5 different buttercream cakes, in addition to some staples, like browned butter blondies (which are VERY good - it's hard for me to walk out of here without one) and vegan chocolate pudding. There are always at least a couple of vegan options, which I shied away from for awhile because I love butter and dairy. But damn was I missing out! Today I had a vegan almond chocolate raspberry cake, and it was basically the best vegan dessert I have ever had. Trust me - you will not miss the dairy! The buttercream cakes are beautifully crafted, often topped with decorative herbs and flowers. If you check out their Instagram, you'll see that I'm not joking about the beautiful part. The slices are large - I would recommend splitting one with a friend! Cake flavors are always rotating, but there is almost always something for chocolate lovers and almond lovers. Flavors like lemon, lavender, and matcha make frequent appearances. It is important to know that Butterwood's cakes are dense. If you are a fluffy/airy cake person, consider yourself warned. I love my cakes dense and moist, so the ones here are perfect for me. The buttercream tends to be a little sweet for my personal tastes, but it's certainly not overly sweet compared to almost every other bakery out there. For this reason, I usually get other desserts, like blondies and pound cakes. By the way, if you think you hate pound cake because you grew up eating those ones from the supermarket, you must try the ones here. One bite will lead you to revise your idea of what pound cake even is -- or can be, anyway. On top of all that, they serve up KLVN coffee, beans that are not only local but deliciously roasted. The decor is charmingly Victorian, which makes for a very unique ambiance - equally pleasant for enjoying cake with friends or hanging out and working on your laptop. And they are friendly to well behaved dogs... apparently even the vegan dog treats are amazing, because at this point my dog will NOT let me walk past the shopfront without going in!

Very cute and eclectic bakery with some awesome flavor combinations!! The food was good and looked delicious. A little pricey, but totally worth the experience. Loved the deconstructed hot chocolate you then prepare at your table!

This is an amazing bakery and late night dessert spot. We were visiting Pittsburgh from Orlando for a wedding and I found Butterwood via Yelp. It is located in Lawrenceville and has an adjacent public parking lot. The dessert case was full of great looking cakes, pies and bar cookies. We had the Chocolate Beet Fig Cake and the Blood Orange Honey Cream Cake. The genoise cake layers were super moist and the creams and soaks were flavorful and on point. Open sides cakes like these can sometime be dry. These were perfect. The cake styling reminds me of Christina Tosi of Momofuko Milk Bar. This is a beautiful space with a Victorian decor, people coming for coffee and tea with leashes dogs. I definitely will visit again if I am back in Pittsburgh.

I've been here multiple times, but this is the first time writing a review for The Butterwood Bake Consortium. Their desserts (mostly cakes, mini cakes, and brownies) are all incredibly delicious and unique, leaving you wanting more after each bite. Each time I've gone, they've had a different selection of desserts. There's usually 4-5 large cake selections and a few mini cake selections. What makes The Butterwood Bake Consortium so unique is the flavors of their cakes and buttercream frostings. They have always had a lavender cake as part of the selection, which is a personal favorite of mine. They also offer coffee and tea, although I have never ordered one when I've visited. This time around, I ordered the mini lavender cake with blackberry buttercream frosting. The lavender was very fragrant and pleasant while the blackberry buttercream was light and creamy. I also ordered the lemon basil cake with vanilla buttercream frosting. The cake, like the other cakes I've ordered in the past, is very dense but still moist and flavorful. The lemon curd on top of the cake balanced well with the sweetness of the cake and buttercream. The buttercream frosting they make here that surrounds the outside of the cake and layered between the two layers of the cake has always been my absolute favorite! Every one of their cake buttercreams is incredibly creamy and melts in your mouth. The decorations here are very cute and gives it a classy yet whimsical feel. There are old victorian-age looking couches and small cafe tables. This is the perfect place to grab a bite of dessert after having dinner out in Lawrenceville!

I love the decor of this place and they have lush, beautiful chairs. Seating is limited here but the cakes are good quality here. I enjoyed interacting with the employees too! Overall, this is a nice place to visit with friends or a significant other! Best time to go is during the summer or fall when it's nice to walk the streets of lawrenceville

Y'all, I don't even like cake like that but this place was delicious! I went with a friend, and we split slices of chocolate cake & lemon cake. EASILY best cake I've had in my life. The texture, the icing, it was all fantastic. This is really a must visit if you come to Pittsburgh or if you live here!

Butterwood is open late. That's awesome. The deserts are $6 and the coffee is $4. So for $10 per person, you've got an awesome after dinner dessert option. The cakes are fancy. We had a strawberry basil slice and an olive oil almond slice. Both were fantastic. The frosting to cake ratio was perfect. My only warning is the cakes are very heavy. If you're only looking for fluffy cake, this is not your place.

I've tried really hard to love this place but I just haven't been entirely swayed with any visit. Maybe it's my dessert selections. Most recently I ordered a slice of vegan chocolate cake with peanut butter buttercream and an earl grey cupcake with honey buttercream, sound amazing right? The cake was a little dry and the peanut butter flavor was such a kick to the mouth that it was too much. The cupcake was also dry but the flavor was very nice. With both selections the icing was hard, not like a smooth creamy icing I'm used to. It's a very unique spot though, it's certainly worth experiencing at least once. They gave very creative flavor pairings and options for any type of diet.

I have been here 3 times and each time was an unfriendly experience. The girl with dark hair and glasses is the rudest person I have ever been in contact with. Miserable, would describe her best, she should not work with the general public. Lawrenceville is a great community with some pretty awesome local businesses. Please don't support this bakery, they are not appreciative of your business, and will likely treat you like an inconvenience for even stepping foot into the Butterwood. Also, the cake is overpriced and really doesn't taste that good.

I was debating between a 3 or a 4 star rating, but I went with the 4 because this place was definitely better than a 3. The reason I don't feel that it is a solid 4 is because I felt the selection is very limited. That being said... I loved the decor, the cake I tried was delicious and moist, and the espresso was better than most coffee shops. I will definitely be back, but I hope there will be more options next time.

Butterwood did an amazing job with our wedding cake on October 28th! It looked and tasted fabulous! We opted for a pumpkin buttermilk cake with cream cheese frosting and it was delicious!! The fresh floral decorations were also beautifully done. We are saving a piece in the freezer for Christmas and we cannot wait to dig into it again! They were kind enough to deliver the cake to our venue on the day of the wedding, and their prices were very reasonable. I would highly recommend them to anyone who is looking for a beautiful and unique wedding cake - we received so many compliments on it!!

What an awesome place and a hidden gem in the upper Lawrenceville area. Looking for a place to have some cake or sweets after dinner in Pittsburgh is little hard, as most places close super early. Sifting through all the places finally came across this name and decided to give it a try. It was advertised to be open till 11 at night, which is uncommon. The place itself is beautifully decorated and staffed with very friendly person. It has both coffee and cakes of various kinds. I had espresso and pour over coffee along with slices of cakes. Both the espresso and the coffee tasted superb. The ambiance of the place is warm and inviting. One could spend hours there. Definitely recommend as an awesome place to hang out and enjoy some great java with sweets.

I absolutely adore the chocolate cake with strawberries and cream (buttercream that is). Yes, you've read that correctly, I adore it. The incredible flavours that hit the palette all at once is the stuff that dreams are made of. Couple that with the incredibly gorgeous environment, a quaint tearoom with an old time concept. It's like being transcended into the days of Little House on the Prairie and such. This place is a treat for the eyes, mouth and belly!
Their blondies are outrageously good. Love their cakes, they have unique flavors and they're open much, much later than most bakeries so it's better for the night owls.

Can a bakery be sexy? You bet your sweet buttercream it can! I ventured in here one night after a dinner date with my husband, and I fell in love. The Victorian style furniture, the soft candlelight, the decadent desserts...It's all quite romantic. We split a lovely pear tart and a huuuuge slice of chocolate cake with curry chocolate frosting. My husband also had an espresso that he quite enjoyed. I love that they are open late so I can appease both my sweet tooth and my inner night owl. Everything was great and I absolutely don't mind paying $6 for a large slice of delicious gourmet cake. We'll be back for sure!

First off the interior is adorable with its luxurious large couches and chairs and antique decor however the dessert particularly the vegan desserts are seriously lacking flavor and texture. We had the lemon cake with raspberry buttercream and blueberry scone both had very dense texture and almost no flavor.

My friend and I have been passing Butterwood for weeks, each time tempted to try it out. Yesterday evening we were both craving something sweet, and finally met up here for dessert. It's super cozy inside, furnished mostly in a Victorian style with plenty of seating options. It's a nice alternative to a lot of bakeries that have no option to dine in. There was a decent selection of desserts available, as well as drinks from the espresso bar. I chose the honey blackberry cake with vanilla buttercream. I don't like super sweet icing, so I was happy to find that the filling was just right. The blackberry sauce on top and in the filling was tart and flavorful, and there were some fresh berries on top as well. The cake itself wasn't bad, but seemed somewhat dried out. It was also nearly $7 which is a little steep--granted it was a large slice, and apparently they're careful to only use all-natural ingredients. Overall a nice spot to grab dessert and a coffee, and a good alternative to cocktails at the bar. Always nice to see new spots opening up in the neighborhood!
Another great place in the area. this time for desserts. Open late, quiet place good music.

A-freaking-mazing!!!! Vegan options galore. I can not recommend this bakery enough. Beautiful to the eye and oh so delicious. The whole family craves the offerings here. Adorable inside. Visit as soon as humanly possible, you will not be disappointed.

This place was so cute! The interior was nicely decorated and the layout was great. My friends and I got slices of cake to go and were very pleased with the taste and portion of the slice. I got the lavender vegan cake with blueberry buttercream. I personally liked this flavor the best out of all the flavors we tried (rosemary fig cake with salted almond butter cream, raspberry cake with chocolate butter cream, and chocolate cake with chocolate butter cream and brownie pieces). One slice was almost $7 but I thought it was worth it. My vegan cake was pretty dense but also very light. The flavored buttercreams were very light in general and was nice when paired with tea. I do recommend trying this place out if you're craving a good slice of cake! They also have espresso drinks!

I love the atmosphere here! It's so cozy and timeless. The cakes are always new and an inventive blend of flavors. I would definitely recommend coming here to sit down, have a coffee and some cake, and relax.

Butterwood is one of the cutest spaces I have ever seen! The dÃ©cor is fabulous and makes it so you never want to leave. I sat in here for hours working on my computer. And...the baked goods...wow! The cakes are phenomenal!!
What a gem! Such a cute little spot to indulge in a fancy treat. As soon as you walked in a good a cozy vintage feel. Decided on a slice of rose water cake with pistachio cream. Delicious!!

Very pretty decor and perfect to sit and sip with a book. Butter cream was so delish. Cute presentation when served to eat in. Not much variety and that's the reason for 4stars not 5 Parking lot adjacent but pay at kiosk and only $1/hr. So worth it.

Have came here twice now, great service, awesome drink selection and even better treats ! I'm not a fan of added colors, sugars and flavors and Butterwood makes a delicious delicacy without all the mumbo jumbo extras. Highly recommend

I've been here twice, both times around 10pm. Where else can you get cake at an adorable quirky location late at night in Pittsburgh!? I think the pictures here on Yelp can help to show off their decorations and the kind of feel this place has. After ordering and paying for the cakes at the counter, they'll bring it over to your seat with your drink or some water. All the cakes (total of 4) that I've tried here are more on the dense and sweet side. Although I'm usually more for the fluffy/light type (I grew up on Japanese-style cakes), I still really enjoy the cakes here. Rather than being like the cakes at a Japanese or French patisserie, the cakes here remind me of the cakes that the mother of my childhood friend made. Cakes that are like what I would imagine the best home-baker in town would make. Rich and flavorful, with delicious cream (NOT hardened frosting!). Except unlike a home-baker's offerings, at Butterwood you get to choose what you want out of an entire display case of drool-worthy, uniquely flavored goodies! For the price, size, and heaviness of a slice, I would say that you could probably share a slice between two people if you're not super hungry. I'll be back the next time I'm out and craving sweet things late at night. On my next visit, I'd love to try their hot chocolate!

I had an all-around exceptional visit. Not only was the food delicious, but the staff were very friendly and eager to talk. I had 2 vegan "mini cakes" and they were so delicious! I definitely recommend any type of espresso drink - I had a cappuccino with almond milk and it was by far the best I have ever had. I will definitely be going back!

Thumbs down. Highly overrated! Went there with my date and had a piece of cake. It took very long to be served and when we got our cake I was very disappointed. The cake was *very dry* like stale bread on the bottom, like it had been sitting out for a long time on the plate or something, despite being told it was freshly cut. And the overall quality of the cake was sub-par/ not a treat to enjoy. Also, because of the other reviews raving about this spot as a cake spot, I was very disappointed in the selection of cakes, only a handful (4 or 5) to choose from. One slice will set you back about $7-8 dollars (with a tip.. $6.50 each) which is fine if it tasted good. But no. Cake should not be dry flavorless bread. Don't serve stale stuff. It leaves a bad taste in your customer's mouth (literally -- no one likes to be ripped off). Underwhelming experience. Also, a suggestion for an actual menu either on paper or posted somewhere, so customers can get an idea of the types of beverages the place offers would help. Needs improvements in quality of service, selections, and quality of the products.
I been here several times and everything has been incredible. At least once the cake was dry but the taste was so good I didn't even mind. I always try to stop when I'm driving past.

Got a 6" honey lavender cake from here, and not only was it absolutely delicious but it was GORGEOUS. They went above and beyond by arranging fresh flowers on top. Our new go-to for cakes and cupcakes!

I really want to like it... Been there twice cause I want to give it a second chance... For someone who loves desserts it just wasn't there... Certain things were dry other things were lacking flavor both times ... Great Decour and really nice service but the food quality is just not there

Love Love Love this place! The vintage decor is so charming. It invites you right in. They had a nice selection of desserts. I ate the Chocolate Cake with Strawberries and Buttercream. The cake was dense and chocolaty. The strawberries were fresh and the buttercream was light. It was very delicious. I wanted to try a little of all their creations. The young lady that helped us was delightful. I'll be back with my friends.

Great quality and great concept! The Butterwood Bake Consortium has decorated the space nicely and would be the perfect venue for coffee, team, and sweets while catching up with a friend, holding a business meeting, or celebrating a success. It's a great (and cute) alternative to your typical coffee shop or happy hour. My friends and I tried the pumpkin bread mini loaf, chocolate cake with peanut butter frosting, and pour over coffee. We enjoyed everything, and I'm looking forward to my next visit! My one criticism (and the reason for four instead of five stars) is the lack of posted coffee menu paired with an employee's pretentious attitude. The baked goods are all labeled, but there is no posted menu of their coffee/tea/drink options that I saw. This led my friend to ask for a regular coffee, to which the employee responded that they only offer a "regular espresso menu". I wouldn't consider the definition of that to be common knowledge to the average customer. When my friend replied "drip coffee", the employee repeated that they only offer a regular espresso menu. My friend and I had to ask what the options were that would be similar to a drip coffee in order to be given some options. She never ran through the options and could have definitely handled our interaction in a less condescending manner. I'm sure employees get tired of running through the menu over and over, and think that a clear posting of the entire menu could easily avoid a repeat scenario!

Awesome little place for desserts. Been here 2 times and have tried different things each time. I've had the vegan cake as well as the regular cakes and they have both been amazing ! The vegan cinnamon cake with buttercream was absolutely the best piece of cake I've eaten in the city hands down. Also the olive oil chocolate almond cake with buttercream was very good as well. Great coffee as well. Cute setting to grab something sweet. It's Lawrenceville so the clientele are hipster so if that is an issue don't go there. I don't care about anything except when I can go back and have some more cake !!!!!!!

Oh my goodness!!! The best cupcakes I have ever tasted, the best in Pittsburgh by far!!! I live in Lawrenceville, and have to say I am not a healthy eater... I love my sweets. But I was driving by, and saw them. They were open and I stopped last week and got a lemon cupcake with raspberry icing! Oh my, dessert Heaven!!! I also got a brownie which was moist, and very good. I just stopped in now( Friday night), was impressed, I wanted to try it again!i got 4 cupcakes to go. I just ate a chocolate with cinnamon icing, oh so yummy! I also bought the chocolate with raspberry icing, cinnamon with vanilla icing, and cinnamon with raspberry icing! I could not tell these were vegan or gluten free! So delicious!!! Yes, they are expensive but in my opinion well worth it! Plus it is a healthier option than regular cupcakes, and supports our local business! The decor is beautiful, very relaxing! I love this place, and found my new go to bakery!

We stopped in here for a coffee during a rain storm while we were waiting for an appointment nearby. The mix and match furniture is so cozy, but the decor overall is just very inviting and funky all in one. We had pour over - it was delicious, but we were so relaxed we stuck around and had another and ordered a slice of cake. I can't say enough about the sweet service OR that incredible cake. This is one of my new favorites.

What an awesome addition to the neighborhood. Delicious desserts, great coffee, friendly staff, and open late. We've made our way to Butterwood a few times post-dinner and have been so pleased. Great selection even late into the night. Hope to try some savory quiche sometime soon.
One of my favorite places in Pittsburgh. The cake is rad, the coffee is bomb, and everyone who works there is the absolute sweetest.

This place is very picturesque with colonial (victorian) style and comfortable seatings. Per my experience, cakes and brownies were very rich and tasty. I been there just once with my husband and we are already in love their vegan bakery. No wonder if we turn into patrons. I loved the cake especially the carrot cake.
