Wow! Talk about falling off! I recently purchased a bunch of macarons, some tarts, some pastries, etc and ALL of them tasted exactly the same. Like old state desserts. Their macarons definitely do not taste like the flavor they're advertising. Big disappointment! I would not call this an authentic French bakery.

The sweet treats were absolutely decadent and delicious. There is a large dining room area that is decorated nicely. We enjoyed our mini pastries and macarons. I definitely recommend anything pecan that is being served.
Their pastries are alway fresh and flakey. The flavors and type are unique. Great for that special brunch or dessert to celebrate with

Anything you going to find is is superb. This is the only real French bakery I am aware of in the charlotte area. The only reason I am giving it 4 stars is that if you come in the evening they don't have much left to choose from.
Always great. I've even special ordered a cake from here and it was amazing and very affordable. You can never go wrong with an eclair or fruit tarts!

Summary: Food is great, coffee was delicious, the customer experience/wait time is atrocious. Went here with a few friends and we each got a coffee and a sandwich along with some pastries. The pastries were given to us as we ordered because they just came out of the case, which makes sense. The coffees we ordered were all tasty, but when the barista gave them to us (one at a time) she misspoke to 3 of them which was which. Meaning she stated "this is caramel, no milk" when it in fact did have milk in it, etc. Eventually after playing some coffee roulette we all figured out which was which. All the food we ordered were very tasty which included the roast beef sandwich, the sun-dried tomato chicken sandwich, a build your own sausage, egg, and cheese, and a piece of bacon quiche. However, we literally waited about 40 minutes for the food to be made. And its not a sit down place due to covid so there is only seating outside. If its obvious that people are piling up waiting for their food, there should be some type of buzzer or text confirmation where you can get notified that your food is ready. This is both reasonable for a better customer experience in general but with covid, it would help alleviate people standing in a small space waiting for their name to be called for 30+ minutes.
Delicious as always!!!! My favorite "go to" place for brunch and pastries! Love love love
A must do in Charlotte for baked goods and desserts, love the French patries. Inside decor is an experience in itself very eclectic, very artsy and cool.

I wish they only sold sweets and pastries so I could give them five stars. Their macarons are the best in Charlotte, and I've never had a bad chocolate croissant! Order anything that needs preparing from the kitchen, however, and you may be in for a hit-or-miss experience. We've waited multiple times for 20+ minutes on an order for a single hot sandwich, only for the sandwich to somehow come out cold. On more than one occasion, the order has been wrong or the side omitted. I've also had a chicken baguette that twice had salad greens that were brown and slimy from going bad. Sometimes the food is good, sometimes it ruins your Saturday. But stick to the pastry counter and you can't go wrong!

I go here every time that I got to Charlotte and Saturday was no different! I really like that the NODA location is open until 2 am, perfect for a late night stop after hitting uptown. The macaron selection is impressive and I've never had a macaron I don't like here. I had a pumpkin macaron and the pumpkin cake was the best dessert I've ever had there. The creaminess of the filling and the crunchiness of the bottom layer made it the perfect combo. My friend ordered the salted caramel and the pumpkin macaron and enjoyed them. Something unique about AmÃ©lie's is the decor there. It's very eclectic and there's many opportunities for Instagram backgrounds. I like that's it's not difficult to park, unlike other places in Charlotte. There was no line when we went, which was nice. The staff were very polite and enthusiastic to help with selection.

Excellent bakery, sandwiches, chai tea BUT I wish their outdoor seating included some area in the sun. Charlotte does indeed have 45-55 degree day time temperatures so if you have a dog with you, you must sit outside in the shade Mid-day Yoghurt Croissant sandwich too Chai tea

The pastries are delicious but not enough to make up for the awful service. While we were being helped the lady at the pastry case talked to me, a 23 year old, very condescending and was rude. My boyfriend was astonished the way that I was talked to. Will not be returning

Our go to for desserts! Especially the macaroons! Omgosh, to die for! Don't walk, yes run here! Gets pretty busy on the weekends depending on which location you go to, plus different locations have different desserts available. I frequent the noda location a lot due to their stock of my favorites. If you haven't been, it's a must! They also have sandwiches, soups, coffee, etc if you want to sit and have a nice lunch/brunch. I love this place!

It's not bad...but it can be a lot better. I was recommended to this place for some French bakery and small snacks. I don't think I will comeback...their service is really night though, but if i want true French snacks for this price, I can go somewhere else. Setup and staff are very friendly though

We waited in a hefty line on a Saturday night. It looks like there is seating during non-Covid times that is cute and cozy. The bakery could have benefitted from air flow and low volume music to create a lighter mood. Now for the food: 1) The chocolate ganache mousse cup was to die for 2) The mini key lime tart was okay-the crust is what killed it for me. I was most looking forward to this item. 3) I had a taste of the entremet. It was like a springtime meadow with hints of lemon. Next time I'm definitely trying an entire serving of this item.
Came for the internet and ended up with the caramelized onion and asparagus crustless quiche. this was very good and savory. Not pictured is the coconur matcha latte which is a hit!!

I really like Amelie's, don't get me wrong, but my last visit was not a great experience. I have been several times before and tried various pastries/desserts and you really can't go wrong. Everything is delicious. I also really like their build your own breakfast sandwich. I get It on a croissant every time. But this last time I went, the staff was not friendly at all. They actually seemed a bit annoyed with being there and having to help anyone. I get that people have bad days, but all 5 people behind the counter and in the coffee section? Secondly, I tried the 1/2 sandwich, 1/2 soup deal for lunch and It was good but not great. I tried the leak and asparagus soup and It didn't have much flavor and the half sandwich was so tiny... I was still hungry when I left. I will definitely go back because I really do love their desserts but I hope they step their game back up!

This pace is so pretty, gives European cafe vibes. When I reached a lot of things were already sold out, so that was a little disappointing. I ordered Chocolate Petite Gateaux - it was so rich, creamy and chocolaty. I could tell that the ingredients used were the highest quality. I also got a black coffee which was freshly brewed and it woke me up (just with the smell). Its quite spacious and I spent almost an hour here. I will recommend!

The French bakery of note in Charlotte, this place offered a robust selection of pastries, which I bought to share. They were very strong on nuts, which make for filling sugar bombs that at least have some nutrients in them. The person working there didn't quite get the pastries right that I pointed to, but with others waiting behind me in a socially distant line, the difference between chocolate and hazelnut wasn't something I wanted to make a hassle over. The place does offer curbside pickup; their current model is all takeout with no indoor or outdoor seating. The nutty pastry I took from the pack was certainly delicious enough to be worth the stop.

I love this little bakery! I visit the one in uptown quite often as I work close to it, but today I ventured over here! The staff was friendly and the treats were yummy! Would recommend the Salted Carmel Brownie it's the best! My kids love the Macaroons (cotton candy and the cookie butter ones are amazing) I can wait till they open their dining room again as I would love to take the kids there for a lunch soon!

Everything looks amazing the moment you walk into the store. Every item I have tried so far from pastries to breakfast sandwiches to their lunch soups and salad has been delicious. The atmosphere is very casual and perfect for a breakfast/lunch. Would highly recommend!

It's very unfortunate that I need to change my review but after my recent experience, I won't be returning. I was online about to order (like I've done so many times in the past year) when the lady behind the counter ( Sunday morning) started yelling at me telling me I had to change my mask to one the store provided or leave. She tried to humiliate me and embarrass herself in front a a dozen customers. I don't support businesses which treat the customers badly, so I left. What the lady assumed was that I was wearing a mesh mask when in fact the mask I was wearing had a cotton layer inside. The mesh was just on the outside. A little less aggression and a little more compassion and understanding towards humans at a time like this would've gone a long way. The lady was repeatedly yelling at me Telling me I needed to wear a cloth mask. She then told me to go to front door as they provided masks. Except the masks they provide are PAPER. She clearing doesn't know the difference between cloth and paper. From reading other reviews it seems that 8 employee have caught covid and the manager apparently plays back the store videos to monitor the employees- but this is no way to treat the very customers providing you a living. I will NEVER give this place my business again.

Allana was wonderful. My wife and I had our 7 year anniversary and her attitude made our evening. The quietness and quaintness in this place is so memorable. Thank you Allana. We would recommend this place to our friends.

The pastries here were delicious. They weren't too sweet which can sometimes be an issue. The customer service was also great. They had additional seating in the rear if you wanted to sit down and do some work. I also had the macaroons which I thought were also good and they had a variety you could choose.

Awesome! Wanna try some french style breakfast and pastry? This is it right here, love it, love it, LOVE IT! Honestly could go for a second visit (oh yes it's happening) because wow they really know how to make you hungry. Fully recommend.

I would give them five stars, but I've only eaten one thing from there, so I haven't really tried the rest of their menu items, however their Macarons are delicious. The aesthetics is nice and the customer service is very professional so I do recommend.
Have loved Amelies for a long long time and I absolutely love their new location for noda! Its bright and clean without a difference in the food quality. No complaints!!

Came in on my hour long lunch break. Ordered my food and waited in line for 30 minutes. I watched 6 people that ordered after me get there food. I asked for a refund and told them I had been waiting for over 20 minutes and they said "we are busy and orders are in front of you." I told them that if they would have at least acknowledged me that it would have been nice and the manager said, "well that won't work because they cook in the back" I hope that this doesn't happen often, but I will not be returning back here.

This place is so cute! French themed and they take many safe precautions so I felt good walking in here. My friend and I got basically a baked goodie box, we got the Smores and Pecan Macaroons, the salted caramel brownie (THE STAR) 2 different almond flour cakes (apple & smore again i think) and the pumpkin cheesecake. All of them met both of our different taste needs. I dont typically like macaroons but the ones here were not too sweet so I enjoyed it. Hands down, the STAR of the box was the salted caramel brownie! The bakery highly recommended it and they were right to!

Took MLB to the airport and figured I could use a meal before heading home and this was almost nearly on the way... Not much space between the doors and the pastry case which is great planning in my book; way convenient to get an orange macaron while deciding on snacks. According to legend this is ground zero, the home of the provencal trailer park motif seen and loved by all. Half a Croque Monsieur plus tomato fennel soup and icy water sounded about right. Usually not a fan of the red soup but it's got fennel...! which fixed everything up nicely thank you very much. Hot vermilion soup abounding with flavor, texture, and substance - not the feeble stuff of childhood. My sandwich was superb! a healthy smear of spicy dijon zip complementing the subtle dignity of gruyere on thin sliced hams nestled in a flakey buttery toasted croissant. Yea for a ham sammich!
All the desserts here look amazing. I ordered the mini pecan tart pie and vanilla macaron with an iced vanilla latte on the side. The best macaron I've tried so far!

I have never been more insulted. I used to love this little gem in Noda but after visiting tonight, I plan to never go back. The Young woman behind the pastry counter, with her hazard of a razor blade necklace, was ridiculously rude and publicly embarrassed me. I didn't hear her the first time, I thought she had said I couldn't be inside without a mask. So okie dokie, I grabbed a mask and re-entered. Completely understandable. Oh no, she yelled at me that I couldn't be inside the establishment because I have open wounds, well no, I do not have open wounds! I have poison ivy rash. It's not contagious. YOU HAVE TO GO OUTSIDE, it's a health concern, you aren't allowed inside, as she chases me out, while im exiting now that I realize it had nothing to do with not having a mask the first time! According to her, management doesn't allow people with poison ivy inside, im a health hazard. Now, I ask, had i said it was psoriasis or another skin condition, would she have treated me the same? Likely. This business should be ashamed. I could understand if I had Covid or another serious, CONTAGIOUS, sickness but wow.

Omg the tarts are amazing! They also have mini tarts so you can enjoy more flavors without getting too full! I brought some to several friends and they all love them!! Basically all favors of tarts are great and I cannot lick my fav!

What a beautiful gem right outside of downtown Charlotte. Located in a little business park, it doesn't look like much from the outside, but as soon as you walk through the front doors, you're welcomed by the smell of fresh baked French pastries and surrounded by quaint French decor. It's always busy, but that just speaks of the quality of everything AmÃ©lie's produces. I love their French macarons and mini tarts. I got an assortment of the macarons and a mini dark chocolate raspberry tart. All of it was utterly delightful! My mom had a strawberry, vanilla mousse cake (I can't remember the actual name of it) and it was melt-in-your-mouth perfection! The staff has always been friendly and the line can get a little lengthy, but come and relax. Enjoy the ambiance, French pastries and a cup of tea or coffee.

The ambience alone just screams France! We were visiting and had to check this location out. I'm so glad we did. The peanut butter bar thing was Devine and the selection of sweets and even a food menu was diverse. Such a corky kinda place to chill with that someone special and just enjoy a coffee and sweet(s). We left with a box of sweets and some awesome IG pics too

Really interesting vibes here, and quite like the artsy french theme. Service was quite friendly, albeit a bit slow, it took about 15 min of waiting to have my order delivered, and all I needed made was a breakfast sandwich (another customer next to me also remarked the same). In all I ordered a latte, chocolate and almond croissant and a breakfast sandwich. The sandwich, once it arrived, was quite fresh & tasty, well presented and a reasonable value at $8(I had sausage, spinach and cheddar on a baguette). The almond croissant was excellent, bursting with sweet almondy goodness and flavor; the chocolate croissant not so much. The choc croissant was a bit disappointing, and I should have known as it was the only item in the display case completely full and untouched. It was small, had too much air, and not enough chocolate; I wouldn't recommend. The latte was average, nothing amazing, bit not terrible either(although a little expensive for my tastes given how small and average it was) All in all, not a bad experience..I would return for a sandwich or almond croissant if nearby for sure! And some of the other baked items looked worthy of a try as well!

Yes the desserts are awesome! But THE COFFEE SUCKS. I always come back for desserts but never coffee. Tonight I gave the coffee a chance again at their new location. & they BURNED ALL OF MY INSIDES. Stay away from the lattes unless you enjoy burning coffee.

My first time here and it did not disappoint. I only came in for a coffee and left with a huge box of desserts. Their salted caramel brownie layer cake was divine, their brownie chocolate cookie was extraordinary and their mini mousse cakes were little explosions of flavor! I never thought to come here for a soda but their lavender honey soda was addicting. My friend ordered this and I wish I would have ordered a gallon to take home! I ordered the cafe Marcotter and it was super tasty but the big winner was the soda on a hot day. I'm grateful I don't live here as I would frequent this place everyday.
Tasty but need more gluten-free options. Staff is pleasant and all pastry looks amazing.
Pastries are delicious. Employees are very attentive and patient. The environment, even during COVID, feel free welcoming while at the sam time they take all the necessary precautions. Lovey place
Absolutely awesome place! Phenomenal macarons. Sandwiches, drinks and too too or off great courteous service!

This one is my favorite of the Amelie's. Maybe because it was my first but I think it's because of the quaintness of the place and the many places you can sit with friends or get some work done. Their bakery is endless. Never know what to get but typically select something that has raspberries. Bottom line... you can't go wrong. Located in Noda I love going to Amelies any time it's open. The smell Itself will wish you away. Enjoy
This place is absolutely Amazing and the food was incredible. We'll def be adding this to our routine.

Super cute French bakery in a really good location! It was just what I expected a French bakery to look like. Display cases full of pastries, macaroons, cakes, you name it! There is also a section of the restaurant that allows guests to view the baking magic in action! Super dope. When I visited downtown Charlotte, I tried the fig tartine. I didn't know this at first, but a tartine is a sandwich with just one breaded side. This tartine had perfectly toasted bread, sweet fig, crispy bacon, and delicious Brie cheese! I enjoyed every bite! The portions were smaller than what I am used to, but it was perfect because I didn't feel overly full after lunch.

Disappointingly Medicore This our second time to Amelie's for pastries after many insisted that this location was better and my opinion has not changed. It's not bad, but it's not great. We got a mini key lime tart, mini mirror tart, mini lemon raspberry tart, mini mouse cup, coconut cream macaron, coffee macaron, pistachio macaron, mixed berry macaron, palmier, and twice baked chocolate croissant. Our favorite was the palmier. The macarons have great texture, but lack a shiny top and real depth of flavor. The key lime and lemon tarts could be tangier. The chocolate croissant lacked a lot in texture. We also ordered an iced latte that was not made well and took forever to get. Would return in the morning to try a croissant again when they are fresh, but otherwise would probably skip the "pretty" items.

This is the go to spot for macarons and other French pastries. They have the best macarons I have ever tasted. Always fresh and flavorful. I also enjoy their coffee they have a small selection but it's a great selection. The flavor of their coffee is delicious . Their decorations are also a sight to be seen. I realized a chandelier can be made out of anything.
Perfect place to eat and study. Nice comfortable atmosphere and the pastries are bomb! I would definitely recommend this place

Amelie's is a great spot to catch up with friends, get work done, and satisfy your sweet tooth. We stop by Amelie's quite frequently to pick up a sweet treat or breakfast sandwiches. The interior is quite intriguing with the variety of colors and different design styles. It is spacious with a good amount of seating but it tends to get packed very quickly!! The lines wrap around since it's such a go to spot for many. Our favorites are their macarons (Pistachio and Salted Caramel) and their cinnamon sticks! As for breakfast sandwiches, we tend to do the build your own and customize it to our likings.
Damn I love this place. Good deserts, and coffee. I could visit every day! My wife and I love to skip deserts at restaurants, and pick up a little treat on our way home.

Amelies has a great atmosphere and delicious pastries. Only reason for 3 stars is there food is just okay. I tried their tomato soup which was probably the worst tomato soup I've had in some time- more so resembled a salsa then soup, which was disappointing. I recommend sticking to their sweet options!

I had the pleasure of attending this location for outing recently. Upon entrance, much of the place is lit up well with lots of abstract lighting. I have always enjoyed visiting each of these locations as no two are the same and follow an unorthodox decoration style. We visited late at night so the staff was ready to get us out of there but always stayed kind and efficient. The pastries and deserts were absolutely delicious and come at a fair price for the quality. They offered a fair bit of outdoor seating along with having plenty of indoor seating. I love this place as it is perfect for any social gathering or if you prefer to just keep to yourself and get some work done.

Where do I even start over there even words to describe how amazing this place. I got two boxes of treats and they were fairly priced I am still in how delicious everything was none of it was overly sweet and the macaroons were perfection! The decor was very unique and I love all the chandeliers that they have throughout the entire place if you go to this location continue walking around it looks like it stops but it really never does it wraps around two. And there's a lot of privacy and some of the back rooms even though there was a long line it didn't take us long to get through the line everyone is super helpful and nice I highly recommend this place!!!

I've been here numerous times. I've also visited the downtown location, but I prefer this one because I can always find a parking spot. You can usually find me here on Sunday for the quiche or the Provence BLT, which is my absolute favorite. Just the right amount of bacon without making you feel like a pig for eating bacon. I have tried several drinks. I have had the creme brulee french soda a few times, LOVE IT, and other coffee drinks. I haven't had one that I didn't like. Again, I like this location because there are several cozy little area where one can sit and be alone, yet in the middle of everything. Not to mention, you can easily share a table or couch with a stranger without it being uncomfortable.

God save my gainzzzz! This place is phenomenal for sweet tooth folks! Their bakery is all hand made and presented in an exquisite way while being so fresh and so delicious that you will only come back for more! Fantastic spot to hang out or go on a date or just have a quick bite mid day! Their variety of options is amazing and it is always clean and tidy and most friendly.

Honestly wasn't ready to be super impressed because I lived in France for a short period, but wow these pastries are good! I had a key lime tart, a salted caramel brownie (amazing!) And a twice baked chocolate croissant (or pain au chocolat ;) ). All three were wonderful! I'm only in Charlotte for a few days, but I'm considering going back for more.

A cute French bakery... the dÃ©cor is cute and reminds me of Paris. When you walk in the railing has some locks ..reminiscent of the 'lock bridge' tradition that is practiced on the bridges of the Seine River in Paris. I had the berry scone and latte. The scone was moist, and the berries were fresh. It was a very large scone. The latte was rich and creamy. Overall, a wonderful start of the day.
I've been coming here for years, and I will never not love it. Today I got a chocolate mousse cup and a salted caramel brownie torte-- both are fantastic! A must-go every time I'm in Charlotte.

So this place legit earns all of its amazing reviews! Really fun eclectic interior, from both the furniture to the chandeliers! But the main showpiece is obviously the treats! It was hard to pick only two things, but the almond tea cake and the raspberry lemon tart were both to die for. Hands-down everything you would expect and then some! With some good coffee you'll feel like you're in Paris, even if just for a few minutes.

Best Macarons! Got the Pumpkin Cheesecake & Vanilla & omgsh.. Best I've had! Coffee & atmosphere is always on point. The staff was super quick & helpful to a friend who hadn't been there before & unsure of what to order. I give 4 stars vs 5 because the Chicken & Broccoli soup was kinda disappointing & lack in flavor as well as one of the pastries tasted old.

Came back to Charlotte for a quick visit with my family from CT. Stopped by Amelies (as it's a known Charlotte staple), we got a breakfast sandwich on a light breakfast crescent and a iced cookie coffee that was to die for! So happy we stopped by on our way out of town. Everyone working behind the counter was also very nice and courteous.

This place came highly recommended to us, so we went. The place is super cute inside and has a great seating area outside. The menu has some exciting looking things on it, but since we just ate we decided to get a Chai Tea, coffee, and 4 tarts. The pumpkin tart was our favorite. We also had a fruit tart, pecan and peach tart. The other three tarts were ok, they had a weird glaze on it that we didn't particularly care for. The pumpkin was the only one that didn't have it. The crust wasn't as flaky as I'd like and was pretty thick. We also got the almond croissant to go. I ate it the next day and I found it to be very flaky and well done. So all in all I would say the pumpkin and croissant took home the prize.

I only came for the sweets but i thoroughly enjoyed it all! We had some small cakes and a chocolate croissant. Everything was clearly fresh and super tasty. Definitely interested to try their lunch and coffee another time. Despite being jam packed they moved through the crowd of people quickly and managed to still be sweet and helpful.

My all time favorite place to go in Charlotte!! Especially for a late night sweet tooth!! The delicate treats they have are so amazing. The macaroons are absolutely delicious. Great place to study and hangout.
Love their house soup! They ate doing a good job keeping everyone 6ft apart. They do have outside seating. Treat yourself and get some desserts for Thanksgiving!

Fair 3 stars for the food. Breads alittle chewy. I made my own sandwich. I would say decent. Soup was kinda cold. Not the worst and not the best. Nice atmosphere but I was it wasn't as open, I wish there was smaller nooks to read.

This place is definitely a treat! It's very whimsical and cute inside. The decor is mismatch and vintage but very tastefully done. It definitely fits into the NoDa neighborhood of Charlotte. When we came it was early afternoon on a Saturday and it was very busy! There was a long line but it went fairly quick, especially since we were busy taking in the atmosphere. When we got to the counter, we ordered a passion fruit mousse, vanilla macaroon, croissant, and a creme brÃ»lÃ©e. I LOVED the passionfruit mousse. The croissant wasn't my favorite. It wasn't buttery enough or light enough on the inside. The creme brÃ»lÃ©e was great except the top sugar coat was a bit too thin. I would definitely make a trip back just for the passionfruit mousse!

My BIL suggested Amelie for dessert after a lovely dinner at Cajun Queen. It's a lively, eclectic space with more seating than it might first appear. That's a good thing, as it seems they're always crowded. Overall, there were things I loved about Amelie but some significant shortfalls too. Menu: A French-inspired listing of sandwiches, salads and soups. There's a daily quiche too and really creative drinks like lavender honey soda. Five stars here. Service: Though its crowded, the line moves fast and the staff is nice. Five stars. Presentation: Just TRY and walk past that pasty case and not order a thing. It's not happening, friends. The devil's winning this round because the offerings are are beautiful. Four stars. Actual taste: Sad trombone noise. For all that the space is cool and the product is beautiful, if it doesn't taste great, well - we have an issue. Sadly, my raspberry rose eclair was the size of a long John and frankly, was overbaked and tasted of neither rose nor raspberry - just sugary sweet donut icing. Sad face. The dessert stuff is all about twice as big as it should be but half as tasty. One and a half stars. I like the 24/7 hours, the space, and the concept. I'll be back to try actual food since it sounded great but I'm a hard pass on the sweets for now.
By far my fav coffee shop that's open 247. Every time I'm in Charlotte I drink my body weight in their seasonal lattes and pig out in the pastries. 15/10

It's a staple of Charlotte and this is the original location. And it's open 24 hours. Being the original, this is the busiest location I've been to and it's for good reasons. From sandwiches to fresh salads to delicate desserts and my favorite coffee, Amelie's delivers on quality food and dessert. My most recent trip was on a Friday night. It was packed. On this trip, we were looking for a tasty treat. Between the two of us, we got a couple of macaroons (chocolate, lavender and lemon), a chocolate cake and a twice-baked almond croissant. Simply heavenly! I'm a sucker for plain chocolate and there's is a more dark chocolate, so it's not over the top sweet. I love the seasonal lavender lemon macaroon. A light flavor with a citrisy kick. I wish I had ordered tea with it. The cake was rich. The layers were light, but that chocolate ganache is to die for. The croissant was okay. It picks up an almost cake like texture, but this was hubby's choice. I highly recommend the chocolate croissant which is my usual go to. If you are ever craving soup or salad, they have excellent choices. This location does get a bit crowded. The line moves fast, though. And shout out to the girls working the dessert case who can help explain everything and share every macaroon flavor. We actually found a quiet table to sit and enjoyed ourselves.

I stopped by here 3 times while in the Charlotte area and so this will be a composite review of all 3. We discovered AmÃ©lie's because the house that we were staying at was about 1/4 mile away from it. AmÃ©lie's is open 24 hours a day and on the one Friday night that we visited fairly late, it was still hopping! The inside of this place is interesting with a large room where you can order your food which has giant menus as well as a number of display cases. Then they have a back room type area with a ton of seating. Their decorations are what I would consider eclectic with a ton of different and unique chandeliers and then some antique looking items. The display cases are what you really want to look at though as they have all sorts of fantastic looking French pastries. I believe that their salted caramel brownie is the most famous of these and that they have sold over 1 million of them! Across the days that I was there I was able to try an almond croissant, the meat quiche of the day and then the Cafe marcotter. On the day that I got the quiche of the day it was a chicken, onion and cheddar. The eggs were set perfectly and I really enjoyed both the chicken and cheddar while the onions were a nice addition too. As for the almond croissant that I had on another visit, it was flaky and crispy with a nice bit of almond flavor to it. If you don't know what a cafe marcotter is, it's a drink that is made with vanilla bean, milk, espresso, caramel sauce and a touch of sea salt. I watched them make it and let me tell you that they put quite a bit of caramel in it. Actually it covered up most of the flavor of the drink which I can't say that I minded much, but that does mean that I didn't get any sea salt flavor which I was interested in seeing how it paired with the coffee. The bottom line for me which you can probably tell from my 3 visits in the space of a week, I would come back here again in the future. Everything on the menu here seems to be both interesting and good and so I would recommend you sample some and see what you like!

We visited AmÃ©lie's on a #TasteCarolina food tour this AM. What a treasure this unique place is. Our tour included a fresh glass on lemonade, a bacon-cheese bread pudding and a creme-brÃ»lÃ©e macaroon that blew away every other macaroon I have ever eaten. The case of baked goods looked to offer hundreds of items I hope to taste some day. Our host baker was a fun, informative host. She added positively to our visit. Thank's Amelie, your staff are awesome!

Beautiful place to have breakfast or afternoon tea. Stand line first, order and get the number, they deliver to your table. Cappuccino was the best! Sandwich also. I don't think we can't find this level of bakery easily in any other city. A must visit place when you are in Charlotte.

This place has the best ambiance! The staff and manager are extremely nice and hardworking. I visit regularly now as time allows as the pastries and coffee is amazing. My favorite thing I've ordered over 10+ times would be the French Silk tart. It's perfect for chocolate lovers like me and it's not too sweet not too bitter it's just right. It compliments the other tarts in the case as well. A lot are sweet or based on fruit but this one I feel gives a full range of selection. The macaroons are the best ones I've had! The only other time ironically I've had such good ones were in France when I visited in 2017. I would highly recommend the Ukraine macaroon and the cotton candy one as well. The cafe Marcotter is my go to drink as its delicious and has a nice kick of caffeine but not too much. Overall 12/10, I would recommend this place to anyone and I already do.

This was the second time I have been here but first time reviewing. Amelie is a very cute and interesting place. With so many pastries to go and a few gluten free options, which makes me happy. The fact that they stay open 24/7 is great. They offer gluten free bread for breakfast sandwiches, so obviously I went with that. The bread was buttery and held it's own very well. On the sandwich I ordered egg, bacon, cheddar, spinach and tomatoes. Everything was good until I realized they forgot my bacon, by then we were on the road already. My husband had a croissant which he thought was perfect. Coffee was delicious and we took some pastries to go, including the famous gluten free salted caramel brownie.

Loved this spot! The pastries & desserts are perfect looking. The cappuccinos are very good. You're going to have a hard time deciding what to get! But the one of the best parts is the building itself. It's a very unique coffee shop that has a lot of little nooks to hang out in. It's super cute!

I absolutely adore Amelie's. The thing that sticks out to me most when I think about this place is quality. They truly put their passion behind their products to make the highest quality french pastries, cookies, pies and other confections. My favorite thing to do is to pop in and just buy one tiny treat for myself when I've hit a big goal or really need a little pick-me-up. Because the desserts are so well made, I know that every calorie is worth it. They also have coffee and tea and delicious made to order sandwiches and salads. As with the baked goods, these are also crafted with care with high quality ingredients. I have to stop writing this review now because just thinking about this place is making my mouth water and I don't want to drool all over my keyboard. So, don't take my word for it, go try Amelie's out for yourself!

I Love AmÃ©lie's!! A small taste of Paris in Charlotte! Tarts: I go for the fruit tarts which are Always AMAZING! I highly recommend. Chicken Salad: Good, The chicken pieces are larger than expected but the taste was just basic. Missing relish for the pop! The wait was not worth the taste. Strawberry Rose lemonade: My friend LOVED it! Me not so much... very acquired taste. Outdoor seating: picnic tables with umbrellas Once again I love AmÃ©lie's and if you have never been I highly recommend you give them a try! You'll love them too! 4/30/21

Literally my favorite bakery around. Large menu including lunch. Coffees always pair well with a sweet treat. Best macaroons Ive ever had. Multiple locations. Each has its own wacky decor that sets it apart. Employees are always nice and helpful. Gotta get there early to avoid long lines on Weekends but worth every bit of the wait.

I hadn't been in before and they graciously answered my questions about what is in the case. The salted Carmel brownie deserves an applause as well as the chocolate eclair. The atmosphere is nice and they keep the line moving. The bathrooms are clean and the art is nice. Headed back!
Beautiful choices, a favorite place to go with my grandkids! And the new location is very convenient.

Fabulous! Loved the mini lemon and key lime pies. Cute dining area. Very crowded on a Sunday afternoon. About 1/4 of the customers not masked. They ran out of bacon and most of the sandwiches have bacon as an ingredient, so not many options for lunch the day I went. But I got a turkey sandwich with brie on the flakiest, most delicious croissant I have ever eaten. If I lived in Charlotte, I would go there every week!

Okay, this place isn't all hype. Listen. The interior has super cute decor that is perfect for all your Instagram shots. There is plexiglass at the counter to protect the staff, and they all wear masks. They enforce somewhat of a social distancing with stickers on the floor but when we went there was only 1 other party so not sure how it is when its busy. They have a bunch of desserts and let me tell you. SO. GOOD. I'm not a fan of overly sweet things so I was hesitant to try their macarons and salted caramel brownie but everything was the perfect amount of sweetness with a good balance of salt. The brownie was fresh out of the cooler so the brownie felt like a cross of normal and crispy brownie with a soft and velvety caramel on top. Also their seasonal pumpkin cheese cake is TO DIE FOR. Souffle cheesecake consistency without the tart flavor of cream cheese, pumpkin puree in the center, coated with pumpkin maybe? If I could, I'd eat like 5. At once. Their almond flour cake bite things are 3rd rate compared to the other things. Everything about this place is amazing. Already recommending their pastries to all my friends!
Spoiled by traveling through most of France. I wish they had traditional French pastries, even a simple Cochon would have been nice. For that I give 3 stars.

Love it! I personally don't like sweet stuff so it is hard for me to find any patisserie that is not sweet but taste good. I was not expecting anything but chocolate petit gateaux got me! A good balance between cake and ganache, well balance of the sweetness. I regret I didn't take any pictures! Other tarts and tortes are good, not as impressive as chocolate cake.

Not only did they yell at everyone as they walked in to the store to wear a mask (when the sign on the door didn't read "mandatory") but also as I get up to the counter with my mask on and the lady asks if I ever have been crop dusted wearing my mask. Extremely rude and uncalled for. Very rude and inconsiderate staff. Pastries and desserts were okay at best. Nothing explains to you what these parties are and staff barely knows. Safe to say you lost a customer.
Awful service. Unclean environment. Rude arrogant employees. Overpriced and stale products.

We Stopped by for a little breakfast. Ordered their Baguettes as they were always good. Bit of a disappointment, something has changed. No longer crunchy crust and more doughy than french baguettes typically are with no real butter. That isn't to say the baguettes are bad just not real french style. Coffee was good.

Visiting from Texas and fell in LOVE with this cutie of a coffee shop. The decor alone would make me come back but the customer service and delicious pastries really sealed the deal. The funky French style had me taking pictures like a true tourist. They even have the bike lock wall outside! They have an area for working/studying that was spacious and set to the side out of the hustle and bustle. We had just about every pastry...the pecan sticky bun situation thing was truly next level. The coffee was yummy and I learned that a medium roast actually has more caffeine than a dark roast. The more ya know, right? This shop was definitely a bright spot in a very long work day. Can't recommend enough. Oh and the yogurt with fruit had the biggest blueberries I've ever seen.
Don't miss much about my country. But when I occasionally do, this the place I go. A great blend of french taste and American humour. Merci!

Of all the Amelie's locations, this one is probably my favorite. (The uptown spot is probably my 2nd favorite.) The pastries have always been a little hit or miss for me. Salted caramel brownie? Hit!! Eclairs? Miss. And, I'll never understand why macaroons are so freaking expensive. But, the menu items are always a big ol' hit in my book. I love their daily soup offerings paired with a sandwich, tartine or even just 1/2 a baguette with a spread or two. I also love the lavender lemonade. This spot can get packed! When it's crowded, service can be pretty slow. If you hit them at an off-time, it's easy to find a table and staff are fairly pleasant and efficient. Fun decor! Be sure to look around while you're there.
Chocolate Croissant is to die for! This place is such an amazing spot to grab coffee or a delicious dessert. Everyone is so nice!
Love Amelie's coffee & bacon, egg, & cheese croissant! I add spinach & it's wonderful!

i found the food to be ok nothing great. The pastries were better but very pricey They could work on cleanliness I couldn't find a clean table & had to wipe it down myself would return only for takeout dessert

My friend she have a gluten allergy. The sever made a mistake and gave her the wrong ones. Thank god someone caught it. That was one reason for the 3 stars. The crime brÃ»lÃ©e was not good. This was definitely not my best. It was very mediocre. I was very disappointed because my friend been here before. She spoke highly. And it was very busy and long line. So my anticipation was very high. However the macaroons were phenomenal. I also had a brownie that was very good. So that made me happy. I will come back for the macaroons. The salted caramel brownie was really good.

What a Gem we have in Amelie's! Sweet or Savory, its all here! I believe this is the closest I will come to sitting in a French Bistro in France, and I am 100% fine with that! The dÃ©cor, staff and all the goodies are consistently top notch! Definitely don't miss this place!

Was looking for a place to have a relaxing lunch with some girlfriends and this wasn't really it. This is a counter service restaurant and the line was really long. However, a long line is usually a sign of a good restaurant so we waited. There was an extensive case of pastries and macaroons to look at while in line and as someone who is gluten free I appreciate that they had gluten free pastry and bread options. I ordered a sandwich once I reached the register. Unfortunately, this did not end our wait. We were not given a number and allowed to find a table. We had to stand there and wait for our food which took a good 20 minutes. By the time I got my food the canned soda I had ordered was warm. I ordered the chicken, sun-dried tomato and goat cheese sandwich. Flavor was good, spinach was fresh but it was just a bad piece of chicken -- really tough and gristly. Not the relaxing lunch experience we were looking for. In addition, the amount of packaging this place uses is ridiculous. I would recommend them asking if the order is for here or to go so every orders not packed in plastic containers and paper bags.

I was looking for a place to eat before my flight out from CLT and this came up as a popular spot for breakfast/brunch/pastries. It took me a while to arrive but I'm so glad I did! The whole place has a very unique aesthetic with nooks and crannies to explore. I got a brown sugar Danish pastry and it was absolutely delicious. I also got an open face sandwich- also good though not super filling. I highly recommend this place for a fun and fairly affordable experience. They have an incredible looking pastry selection and I wish I could've tried them all.

Always an enjoyable experience. I do believe that putting all those delicious goodies in the cases just before the registers is an unfair business practice ;-). Set your expectations for sandwich's and the like properly. It is NOT a fast food restaurant so if you want your food fast, go to McDonalds and don't take it out on the counter folks. I believe the food is worth the wait.

When I got here there were two other customers in the store plus myself, I figured it would be quick to get a cold sandwich. After waiting 20 minutes after ordering I finally got my sandwich. When I got home I found that the one single alteration I made "no Mayo" was not done. So this Wednesday night I get to eat an overpriced sandwich that I waited 20 minutes on that tastes like a jar of Mayo. I would not recommend.

WOW! This is a baked goods haven! So much to choose from. Cookies to the most delicate pastries! I'm in love if only I lived closer... but when in Charlotte I definitely recommend these baked yummies! A few things to know, it is so popular that we waited about 25 minutes in line just to order. Though while you wait your turn you can visually explore the scene. It's like a museum of chandeliers, portraits and 1700'ish art touches. There is a dine in and dine out option! The cafe is small but with so much to offer!

Absolutely awful experience here recently. Came in and saw a line forming in front of a register near the entrance. Stood around until we realized no one was taking orders there and you're supposed to order at the dessert counter. Why have a register there? Why no signage to adequately direct people? ANYHOW, walked over to the dessert counter to check out what they had and someone came to ask if we needed help. Since we weren't ready yet, she walked away and started building boxes. Once we WERE prepared to order, there was no one around to help. Finally, someone appears and I ordered a lavender lemon macaron and my friend went with the pecan sticky bun. The person helping us grabs my macaron with parchment paper, puts it on top of the counter without saying anything and walks away to grab my friend's sticky bun. So, I assume I'm supposed to grab it from the counter and do just that (I grabbed it with the paper, by the way). When she comes back, she lowkey shades me for taking my macaron and doesn't let me put it on top of the counter again for her to box because "germs." Okay, weird that you're so concerned with germs when you're not wearing a mask? Anywho, we sit down and my friend and i decide the sticky bun needs to be warmed since it wasn't super fresh. When she asks the same person that had helped us earlier, they say that they can't take the sticky bun (that we hadn't even touched) to warm because of "germs" but can sell us another one? Hmmmm, why wouldn't you ASK patrons if they want certain pastries warmed before boxing them if you know that the germs are SO RAMPANT you won't be able to do so after the fact? And again, hilarious that germs are such a concern when not a single soul working there was wearing a mask or hairnet. On top of the terrible service, the pastries were also not worth the price. Save yourself the agony of this wreck and hit up The Batchmaker instead. Incredible, FRESH baked goods with way better service.

Came to AmÃ©lie's on a Sunday morning for breakfast. I enjoyed their croque monsieur, which is served on a croissant. I bought a box of macarons to try a bunch of different flavors (they rotate according to what's in season). Expensive, but that's fairly typical. Currently there is no indoor seating because of COVID, but the aesthetic of the bakery is whimsical and cute.

French cafe with vibrant and eclectic decors. The dark roast drip coffee was smooth and nutty. Although the spot is known for its caramel brownie, personally it did not impress me that much. it's too little brownie for too much money, and too sweet for my taste. Regardless it's a fun place to get coffee

When I first starting going to Amelie's the food was great and the service was great..... Over the past few months I would occasionally go there to get breakfast and coffee. Every single time I'd go I'd be waiting an hour for my food and almost every single time they would forget an item in my order. Today was the last straw... I ordered an egg sandwich with soup. Took them 30 minutes (not busy) to get my food and they Forgot my soup. And didn't put EGG on my egg sandwich..... I'm done throwing my money away.

I came here two days in a row: once in the evening and once in the morning. Definitely your selections are greater in the morning. Due to COVID-19, you cannot dine indoors, but there are plenty of outdoor patio seating near the road, and plenty of parking for this location. Follow the signs to place your order while physically distanced. Masks are required for entry. If you order a beverage, it should be ready pretty quick within 3 to 5 minutes. I ordered the spinach and asiago tartine and you get two pieces if you get the half size. I loved it. It was made fresh so it took a while for me to get my order from the kitchen in the morning when there was a line of people. Their macarons have great flavor, but it's not something extraordinary to not raise anyone's expectation. However, they're still a great choice. Also, if you sign up with them for your birthday, you'll get $5 to spend within a limited time frame. Go a treat yourself!

The staff is AWESOME! So helpful and great customer service. It's a very cute French boutique inspired cafe. You will not be bored here. They have a wide array of goodies to try. A little pricey but definitely worth it!

Absolutely 10/10 experience every time we come to Amelie's! Such a cool vibe that is 100% backed up by its delicious food and pastries, and wonderful staff! Allana (apologies if I spelled it wrong) helped us this time and was moving the large crowd through efficiently while also being so sweet and helpful!

I'm definitely biased because I'm from the area and have been a long time regular, but AmÃ©lie's is always the first place I take friends that are visiting. I can't speak to the macarons, as those aren't my thing and I know very popular from here, but I've never had any complaints about any of the baked goods. The breakfast sandwich always slaps, and definitely my favorite place to grab a quick and tasty iced coffee!

They have several locations The downtown was the cutest but shut down during covid. No longer have indoor seating but some locations w outdoor seating. All of their dessert pastries are delicious especially tarts, and macaroons but pricey Coffee solid.

It's the abeyance for me! As soon as you walk in you feel like you're in France. We sat for hours just talking and drinking coffee. The pastries were very tasty. I'd definitely recommend you check them out. Staff were friendly and knowledgeable about items on the menu.
There's just something about this place, A certain je ne sais quoi That brings out the best in ya The decor is never a snore
Absolutely a great sweet spot. Macaroons, napoleon, pecan pie minis, lavender honey soda... just the whole menu, and their cute British nod with their lock 'bridge' gate

Love this place! It is very cutesy with the French decor, such a perfect date spot or just hang out place. The bakery items and coffees are good and somewhat customizable. My weakness whenever I come is there Macarons which always come in beautiful colors and interesting flavors!

When I moved to Charlotte from Chicago. I never knew how much baked goods meant to me. Until I visited AmÃ©lie's... This is the third location I've visited. I love how the quality has remained the same through out. The first time I went was with a friend who raved about their macaroons. I had to try it. I'm now addicted. I try them everywhere I go. AmÃ©lie's has the best macaroons IMO. Their iced coffees are strong. On one of my visits with my friend we opted to have caramel added to our remade drinks because it was almost on the bitter side. Which leads me into customer service. They treat you real good here. They are willing to go through flavors and heating up your treats when needed. I see why people of all ages and walks of life can be found here. The relaxing atmosphere and the bomb treats. AmÃ©lie's is a must when you're in Charlotte. I haven't tried their other baked goods but my friends say their awesome. Please check them out if you're looking for a treat...or two!

Disgusting. These people have never been to Paris to know how a real pastry should taste. Everything I ordered was stale. Maybe they have less turnover. Bad and very slow service, the child behind the counter was rude and wouldn't answer my questions regarding food allergies. Would not come here again and really makes me question why people go to this place. Poorly managed and went even further down hill due to COVID. I question there cleanliness. There are plenty of better bakeries in CLT- this one isn't it.

I will always start my reviews by letting people know I'm a high talented Chef and Baker, so I know good food, which is why I made a choice to review restaurants. Amelie's is a completely overpriced bakery featuring French pastries. What irritates me most is the price of their macaroons in particular. Now,I am a pastry chef and know the cost to make them and even still they should NOT BE over $2.00 a piece. That is absurd. In addition, they have many flavors but very few of them taste like anything more than sugar,which to me means they're skimping on the extracts and flavor associated ingredients. With that being said, Their key lime tart is really good, one of the best I've ever tasted. I believe their cake pastries are pretty good also. Everything else is "okay".

*AmÃ©lie, AmÃ©lie, AmÃ©lie, AmÃ©lie, AmÃ©lie* (singing in Lil Wayne's voice to the beat of A-milli, hope you know it.) WOW. Three letters that describe our "having a hard time deciding what to get, grabbing-a-box-of-pastries-to-go, and eating them" experience at AmÃ©lie's. This was one of our bookmarks during our trip to Charlotte for my birthday, but it was one of those, "We may not make it, it wasn't high on our priorities" kind of thing. That would have been the BIGGEST mistake. I have seriously found the best French bakery I have EVER been to! There are a few in the area; this is their NoDa location. Inside - very shabby chic and eclectic. Colorful walls, old furniture, chandeliers, fun paintings and pictures, cool knick-knacks. They serve everything from breakfast, sandwiches, tartines (open faced sandwiches,) salads, seasonal beverages, and of course, variations and tons of options for coffee, and of course, EVERY pastry imaginable. The hardest part - deciding what to get. We went with - 2 macarons - Orange CrÃ¨me, and a Nutella one, a pecan tart, a lemon tart, a Chocolate croissant, two Palmiers (elephant ears,) and a Cinnamon twist.) Every single pastry was pure perfection. Crispy when it needed to be, fluffy, moist, delicate, and oh-so-flavorful. The box did not make it back to Virginia Beach. We tried, maybe if we got more, some would have, but these didn't stand a chance. It was a 5 hour drive, after all. The BEST part besides how amazing these pastries are?! This place is open 24/7. YES, 24/7!!! What the!?! Great and efficient service (you order, they box it, and you pay,) everyone was nice, the line was smooth and moved quickly, and you get amazing goodies for great prices. What's not to love about AmÃ©lie? When we return to Charlotte one day, this is definitely high on the priority of places we must return to. Keto-schmeto!!! Highly recommend! *Review #50 of 2019.
So I decided to get a late bite to eat and drink...I came across this awesome cafe. I have never had a tart or a macaroon until I visited Amelie's, and let me tell you, I wasn't let down.

Amazing to find a 24 hr cafe serving up sweets, coffees, and sandwiches! This is rare when I've only ever found Ihop and Walmart's to be 24 hr stores. 4 stars for hours and selection. The actual confectioneries though were unmemorable. Mini Peach Tart - best dessert of the lot, not too sweet yet satisfies. Napoleon - frozen cream, beautiful, delicate pastry Salted Caramel Brownie - incredibly dense, one bite is enough! Petit GÃ¢teau chocolate - thick frosting with unmemorable chocolate cake Ã‰clair - fine, if you're about eclairs Petit Fours - pistachio, chocolate peanut butter (x2), lemon, tasty if you're looking for a one bite dessert Mixed berry, strawberry, chocolate cinnamon macarons - only the mixed berry was fresh at the time, the strawberry and chocolate cinnamon were stale. Quick service, nice people, only fresh juice available is lemonade, the rest is store bought. Lovely indoor and outdoor seating. Plenty of parking.

Had breakfast and coffee here while in Charlotte. Cute decor - no inside dining at this point but they have tables outside. The staff was very helpful, friendly and pleasant- offered a lot of help in terms of choices. We had a few items to taste. We also ordered coffees... cute place - I'd definitely go back!

MANAGER TERRI SHOULD BE FIRED IMMEDIATELY' Sisters visiting from CA and love dessert. First thought was Amelies being they have a great selection on French bakery items. We waited in like for a good 6-8 minutes and as soon as I approached the counter to place my order I am screamed at by who I now found out is the MANAGER. There are plenty of coffee shops in the ' No Da' area, however you can not go wrong with hitting up this place !!! AmÃ©lie's is by far the BEST there is. And to the 'Emilys' ( Emily F and Emily E ) you 2 rock !!! To management, these two are stellar employees that represent your business with great personalities and are extremely friendly and make you feel as a friend and less like just a customer #EmilysRock #SuperStars #Amelie's
Didn't realize that this location is open 24/7! Came in super early for a breakfast sandwich. It was delicious, but a bit pricey.

Very Disney World kind of feel. Everything we had was excellent. Very popular with a line at 10 at night. But did a fairly good job moving people through. Only complaint was one worker was put chairs on top of tables at 10; a whole hour before closing. I must be old school; if you state you are open till 11; you don't start cleaning around people before then. Seemed rude and pushy. We ate vanilla eclairs, chocolate torte, cream brÃ»lÃ©e, and a variety of macarons. As stated earlier- all excellent!

One of my favorite treats! I save this place when I am in a good mood or need a pick me up (lol). The macrarons are delightful, and they always have fun flavors! The vibe is so fun inside. The only downside is the line can get long on weekends and they run out pretty quick -- just a testament to how delicous they are!

OMG! WOW WOW WOW! Have a customer sent us a few boxes of macaroons from here and I'm not even a macaroon fan but these were to die for! I mean every flavor was delicious! I had never heard of this place but apparently its pretty famous around here. I am for sure gonna go order some more macaroons!

There is no inside dining at this time. The desserts were AMAZING. Like even the ones that I got just to try out were pretty great! I highly recommend the vanilla macaroon, or the Lemon Entremet. I didn't really enjoy the iced coffee, but I'm pretty picky when it comes to coffee. Overall 9/10. I really enjoyed trying this place out. I will definitely come again. Side note: this didn't really affect my review but the parking lot and area outside of the establishment needs to be cleaned a little.
Amazing atmosphere with unique decor! Great desserts and small bites that are perfect for a quick brunch:)

I have been a fan of amelies for years, I usually never complain but I have to say....since covid it's not the same...the pastries are just "okay" tasting although they are still pretty and the attitude behind the counter is terrible...what a shame...plus they aren't open late anymore or abolle to sit inside.... I used to go weekly multiple times a day pre covid...now I've been 3 times since covid hit and the disappointment is just too great. Now I have to hunt for a new pastry and tea late night hide out spot.

What a disaster! Paid $56 for a dozen macarons and a couple danishes. No big deal if the experience warranted it. Pastries were stuffed in a box, despite saying we were eating in. Waited about 20 minutes for 2 cappuccinos and when we finally sat down we realized we didn't have any plates. This resulted in us clumsily trying to balance pastries and my wife dripping sticky danish in her hair, the napkins and sugars etc are tucked away on the far side of the place where the customers (see herd animals) are queueing for almost an hour to get mediocre pastries and coffees. The 2 baristas took turns preparing a single cup of coffee at a time making the whole ordeal unbearably drawn out. DO NOT RECOMMEND!
A great dessert spot that my husband found for us. Had several tarts and macaroon options. I would have loved to try everything!

Eeww! Very hot day and no indoor dining ( even limited due to current COVID guidance). Air conditioning? Outdoor area filthy with trash, birds, and flys. Waaay over priced for the quality of food and a limited selection of patisserie for mid-day - especially for a "French bakery". Rule of thumb in food service industry is that the last person in line should have the same choices as the first person in line. Go ahead and pass this one by. Again... eewww.

I used to love this place and I would spend 150 easy here we always came in after hours as a group well as they grew the quality change the soups got thinner the staff seemed to always change the drinks never tasted the same. How can you mess up a Chai tea it was brown water.

Amelie's is my go to for macaroons and fresh fruit tarts. After spending a Saturday brunching with my friends and cruising the Noda area on my way home I decided to stop by Amelie's. It was kind of busy in there so the wait was a little longer than usual but that was ok. Another cashier jumped on to help get the line down which I appreciated. I usually order the same thing majority of the time. I got a fresh fruit tart all strawberries, a lemon macaroon, a vanilla bean macaroon, 2 cotton candy macaroons, a birthday cake macaroon and a honey rose macaroon. Let me tell you delicious. Two of the macaroons didn't make it out of the parking lot. They're just amazing. It can be pricey if you think about it but worth it (6 macaroons for $13, 12 for $26 or $2.45 each). I also ordered the spinach, asparagus and leek soup. It's my favorite and delicious. If you don't like the outcome of eating asparagus then you may not like it but this soup I can order alone without the sweets. If you've never gone to Amelie's before please take the time and go. You won't disappoint. There is a wide variety of pastries, sandwiches, soups, etc.

The original location I believe, is part of a larger complex of creative , duvet business. AmÃ©lie's is decorated in a very French way. This particular location has the best music. The gluten free salted caramel brownie has become one of my new favorites, tastes just as good as the regular in my opinion . The team is also kind enough to change gloves when serving you gluten free items if you prefer. Other all-time favorites are the pecan tarts, baguettes with honey butter and jam, and iced lavender tea. I haven't tried them, but I've seen AmÃ©lie's pushing these macaroon ice cream sandwiches which look very interesting. Very French, very decadent desserts, very hipster atmosphere open 24 hours.

ECCENTRIC FRENCH There is a reason the line is out the door. This place is the place to be for great desserts, savory fillings and great beverages. The eccentric decor adds to the ambience and gives you things to look at while you are in line. The line is long, but goes quickly. Keep going in the back they have more seating than you think. My daughter enjoyed her eclair while I had the pot of chocolate. She had the turkey and bacon. I had roast beef and monchego. We brought home pastries for breakfast. Great value. Wonderful quality.

My children and I came for lunch. While I was a little disappointed there was no dining in options, guessing due to COVID, the food was amazing! We all had some type of croissant sandwich- ham or turkey. I had the Croque Monsier and I highly recommend!! Afterwards we had bakery... I only wish we could have sat and enjoyed the ambiance while sipping coffee after. Great service too!

This was the perfect stop after shopping and grabbing an early dinner. Initially, we were only going for coffee, but the beautiful sights and smells led us down a different path. As you can see, we loaded up on a few delights, and that was only my purchase. I was in a group of five! The pumpkin cream cheese entremet was so rich. If you like pumpkin and cream cheese together, you have met your ultimate treat. You can definitely share it since its so big, or go big while you're at it! Why not? I did not try the Key Lime, but the macarons were gone by morning and were perfect! Great place to kill some time, or just grab something on the run.

We closed an evening out with a stop at this open all night bakery. I couldn't believe how many people were waiting in line, but this had to be a good sign, right? The line moved very quickly just as the decisions on what to try had to be made fast. There were 4 of us and together we purchased two vanilla eclairs, two coconut macaroons, chocolate cream puff and raspberry chocolate tart along with fresh brewed coffee. I thought the prices were very reasonable considering the quality. I was told the salted caramel brownies are very popular. The French bohemian decor with mismatched tables, chairs, and odd assortment of pictures on the walls adds to the vibe. Definitely worth stopping in to give yourself a treat.
It's a good place to drink hot chocolate!. The eclairs are delicious! There's no seat area available inside, only take out.

Came here while I was in town for work and met up with friends for dessert. Location: it was late on a Monday evening (9pm) and the place was packed - mostly of college/high school kids getting school work or studying done - as long as you see what you want and order it - you get through the lines fairly quickly. It did take us a bit of time to find a table but we found a really small bistro table and were able to carry a conversation - albeit the place was a bit loud. Service: Not everything had labels/descriptions, so the staff patiently answered any questions anyone had which was great. Many of the tables could have used some busing/cleaning before being turned over - but the place was still very clean. Food: I am one of the odd balls who doesn't like sweets, and so, it must LOOK and taste great for it to be worth it. I selected the Strawberry Vanilla Petit Gateau and the Salted Caramel Layered Torte. These were not overly sweet - which was great, but it didn't pack the punch of a pastry that I was expecting.

AmÃ©lie's is a favorite all day and night. Don't be surprised to come and find a line 20 people deep and then wraps around the corner. But don't leave! The staff does a wonderful job and the line moves fast. I've had sandwiches, coffees, teas, and lots of macaroons and other desserts at all locations. Yet this location was the first and is by far my favorite because of the decor. The macaroons are soft and delicious as they should be, they have some flavors year round with seasonal flavors. Tonight I had the pumpkin and it was so good. I bit into it before I realized I needed to stop and take a picture. The pumpkin e-something dessert was amazing! With a nice surprise of caramel falling out much like a lava cake. Yum yum yum. My least favorite was the sweet potato torte with pecans that my friend ordered. But I'm a huge fan of pumpkin. So if you prefer sweet potato over pumpkin like my friend does, then you will love it. The best thing about this location colors to the other three locations is the parking lot. There is ample parking. I also forgot to mention the larger patio which is also nice to enjoy and look toward the uptown skyline.
Best bakery in Charlotte! Everything is 10/10 and the space is so unique and welcoming. Staff is excellent and helpful in decision making. Especially since they have a ton to offer.

Oh my God. This place is beautifully eclectic, but let me tell you what won me over the most - the HEART with which this place was designed: 1. Has a special handicap elevator for wheelchairs 2. Gender non-specific bathrooms And so much personality! While it's VERY French inspired, the ambiance is really a hodgepodge. Sort of Paris, sort of hipster, sort of a lot of things! It's a HUGE SPACE! Lots of seating throughout and different areas of the bakery have a different vibe. Never seen a bakery/coffee shop like it before. The bakers work behind glass screens so you can watch them pour batter in and out of huge pots, and it's super fun. I tried their spiced chai and it was really great! They have an assortment of drinks and desserts. I didn't try any of their desserts after a heavy brunch beforehand, but will DEFINITELY be back when Im in Charlotte again! We went Saturday mid-afternoon, and there was no line!
One of my favorites since I was young! Love the lavender Italian soda and a salted caramel brownie.
Amelie's is a staple! Try the pumpkin latte in the fall with some macaroons or a salted Carmel brownie. 10/10

This had the best little atmosphere, even during covid. I got a breakfast sandwich which was so fresh and warm and delicious, a cinnamon Cherie latte that was perfection, and a salted caramel brownie to go (divine). The staff was pleasant and helpful. Thank the lord it wasn't too close to my hotel cause I would have tried everything!

Amelie's in NoDa is "The O.G." or as I like to put it, 'My 3rd Shift Savior' (back in the day, when I rolled at night). Where else are you going to go to get a chocolate croissant at 2:30 in the morning? Wait, why do you want a croissant at that hour? None of my business, it's yours if you're in NoDa! Located at the corner of 28th and N. Davidson, Amelie's is everything you've ever wanted in a corner side cafe. They make premium coffee, tea, and desserts as well as many lunch offerings. My hands down favorite for lunch is the Chicken Salad croissant: chunky texture, very little filler (just for binding), buttery flaky pastry, excuse me for a moment I need to take a drive back there now! How about sweets? Mixed berry Macaron is a crowd-pleaser. Be sure to ask the counter staff about all of the macarons on display. The Salted Caramel Layered Torte is great, as long as I didn't have something too filling to eat before because this thing is as rich as it comes. If you're familiar with the Salted Caramel Brownie, add laters of mousse in between with more chocolate. WOW Mad respect where it is due, with this being the original location, but I'm a much more frequent patron of the uptown location. Not due to proximity, because I'm much, much closer to the NoDa site, but because of the typical crowdedness of the place. Forget about sitting anywhere near the service counter unless you want to be brushed up against by dozens of people you don't know! Even the back is iffy sometimes if they're really busy as the line can easily back up 50-60 deep. They're doing the best they can, trust me, it's just a really busy spot. Don't even think about going here after a N. Charlotte event or a NBA game, you're doomed. When it comes to crowd control, they're a victim of their tremendous success. Yes, logic would have you believe that the Uptown location would be busier, but it's almost always the exact opposite. Still, sometimes I'll pick a time I know it won't be too bad (think very, very early on a weekday, like 5am) just to enjoy the ambiance this location offers, knowing that I'm sitting in the middle of Charlotte history, and wondering where they'll pop up next (please be University, Mallard Creek even better!). To all the people who thought a 24/7 bakery in the middle of NoDa would close down within 3 months, look at them now. Break bread with your neighbors and join in the pride of watching this great QC brand continue to grow and wow you with enticing treats!

Everything! This is our favorite spot to grab breakfast sandwiches from. I am not typically a big fan of bread, but I will swallow these buttery, flaky Croissants like water. They are so good! And when you mix that with ham and melted Brie on a sandwich. Oh Lala!

10/10 bakery, vibes, food and service. I came here on a Monday during the day and it was very relaxing and not too busy. The service was amazing, I was stuck between what pastry to get and the woman patiently walked me through her favorites and helped me choose one. I ended up getting the espresso entrement (see pictures) which she recommended and it was delicious! It also looked so cool as a bubble kind of pastry and seemed too pretty to eat. The inside was huge, it had a lot of seating and the decor was nice to look at. I worked from here and it had a nice and relaxing vibe, definitely recommend checking it out!

Popular French bakery! Artwork displayed around is very interesting and will keep you entertained on their long but quick moving lines. They also have great COVID security measures to keep you safe while you wait. When you enter the series, you are hit with the best buttery scents. I love coming here for treats when I visit family and friends. My personal favorite are the pecan and "raspberry and lemon" tarts. Their macarons and chocolate croissants are also awesome. I highly recommend!

Obsessed with their tartines!! An open faced sandwhich on a delicious baguette. Make your own breakfast sandwiches, great coffee, new menu items seasonally and super cute Paris vibe inside. They also host events for groups or seems like an awesome place to catch up on emails or have a meeting. Overall impressed on my first visit, so glad I live right down the road from this place!
So charming and sweet! From the decor to authentic French treats and pastries, it always makes my day to pop in here when I am visiting Charlotte.

The first time I came here years ago I absolutely loved this place, but my most recent visit was lacking. It's a fun spot with a really interesting atmosphere and a beautiful display case of pastries. We got a myriad of treats to try and my husband also got a latte. I really wanted to try one of their lattes but can't have caffeinated coffee, unfortunately for me they don't have decaf espresso so I didn't get to try one. My husband really enjoyed his though. I tried a bite of nearly everything and it was all so sweet. I eat baked goods a lot so I expect them to be sweet, but these were so sugary I just couldn't stomach much of it. They were all good but far from the best I've had. The tables were littered with crumbs and hadn't been cleaned, which is a little off putting. The service behind the counter was helpful and prompt. I would say it's worth checking out if you're visiting and wanting to do something unique.

On Saturday 7th 2022, I stopped in about 1 - 2PM to get coffee with my sister and mother who are from out of town. The line was nearly out the door and we looked at each other questioning if waiting would be worth our time. I looked around at the fun dÃ©cor and told my family Amelie's is a Charlotte small business worth the experience. It took about twenty minutes to get to the counter which we understood given it was your opening weekend in my neighborhood. The person at the register was kind and helped us order our coffee. They explained if we want pastries, then we can pay at the end after we select them. People behind us had not ordered coffee so naturally they walked around us to order pastries. As we walked in their direction they apologized and said they weren't sure what to do. We said it was no matter and that they should go ahead. We both stood there for several minutes while no one helped or acknowledged us even though we had already paid, our drinks were getting cold, and we had waited in line nearly half an hour. Up until this point, everything was acceptable. Next, an employee directed guests from behind all of us to select pastries. I addressed her and inquired if we could go ahead and she dismissed us that someone would be right with us. I interposed and asked to be told what the categorical difference was between them and those already in line. Disneyland doesn't rush people through rides faster because they wait in line longer. That would be absurd and bad for business. Amelie's is the opposite of Disneyland. There is no magic there. There are so many other places in NoDa and Greater Charlotte that will treat me with respect. Rest assured, I'll never be back and I'll definitely be sharing this experience with those I care about.
