There's usually a decent sized line, but it moves somewhat fast. Whether you're in the mood for a macaron, baguette or coffee, Bouchon Bakery makes the wait worth it. I usually like to grab small bites since I'm always on the go, which is what this spot is pretty much known for. Don't expect a full on French meal here, but there is a Bouchon in the area that you can dine at. Either way, the service is dependable, quick and friendly. As with anything French, it is of great quality and comparatively pricey. It's only open until 2 PM, so get here early to enjoy and satisfy your patisserie cravings!

This is a good spot to go if you just want an affordable breakfast on the go instead of dining at a restaurant. Me and my group wanted to go eat at Grand Lux for breakfast originally but we were told the wait was 40 minutes so we cancelled and came across this bakery and we noticed that it has a long line which means it's probably really good. Don't let the long lines fool you, it goes by pretty quick. I ordered a cheese Danish and it was really good, the crust was crispy not stale and the cheese was sweet just the way I like. I'm glad I came across this place, it was worth the wait and I saved a couple bucks on breakfast.

You can taste the butter! Ordered croissants, amongst other items, and both were perfection. If you like a nice crispy, flaky, buttery, soft center this is for you. Their oat chai latte isn't too sweet and paired well with my almond croissant. Located inside the Venetian Hotel in the casino food court near escalators, you can't miss it.
Either here in Las Vegas or Yountville Ca no morning is complete without a shortbread cookie and a Bouchon.

Have been to Venetian over a dozen times, but this was the first time that I have spotted this Bouchon Bakery location. It is a tiny spot that is actually located outside the hotel (closer to the Clock Tower) and Casino so NO air conditioning! We were sweating as we chose which sweets to eat!! This is what we shared: Kouign Aman was the bomb!!! Such a simple and ordinary looking pastry. It is rare when I really enjoy a pastry that is not very sweet. After we shared one, we bought the last 3 to go! (5 stars) Better Nutter was tasty. It is a Peanut Butter cookie with peanut butter butter cream inside. Not quite what I expected, but would buy it again. (4 stars) Cheese danish was different than any I've tried anywhere. Looked more like a cupcake, but did not taste like one. This Cheese danish was dynamite! It is Top 5 in my list of all-time best cheese danishes ever! (4.5 stars) Bouchon Bakery has a couple of other locations inside the Venetian. You may want to try their goodies there where it is cooler. I will be looking out for these delicious treats whenever we spot a Bouchon Bakery.
Came here for coffee every morning as it was right below the elevators at the Venetian, and they can elevate even a simple americano. Huge fan of Bouchon!

The giant macarons are fantastic. We bought the 12 pack and it was expensive, but they were perfectly baked, which is hard to find, even in professional bakeries. The flavors were so delicious. The passion fruit and raspberry macarons were our favorite. We wanted to order raspberry macarons for our 12-pack but they were sold out. =(
The best I ever had! The Macarons are very fluffy and creamy. There are different flavors and they are individually all very good. This should be on the bucket list of what to eat in Las Vegas.

Picked up breakfast this morning and was pretty happy with the taste unlike the one from lavazza yesterday. The omelette had good smell of butter, chocolate almomd croissants were yummy and the parfait was pretty good along with coffee, hotchocolate and tea. Kinda of expensive but pretty good value! !

I have to give this a 3 star because the girl working had the worst customer service ever! She was more into her phone for her plans for that night then taking our order Didn't even put the phone down as she was getting the macaron out of the case. The macaron was big and yummy and fresh. yes we would get another one. Just hope for another person working there.

Asked for a hot Mocha and received a warm cup of dirty water. Do you know mocha is another word for chocolate? Blueberry muffins were good but I needed a cup of coffee. Did not go back again in our 6 night stay.

Value: ***** Macaroons: ***** Service: (we were indulging to even care) ***** I was introduced to Bouchon Bakery 7 years on a visit to Manhattan and fell in love with their macaroons. Every visit to Manhattan requires a stop at Bouchon. I was excited to see they have a location in Vegas so when we planned a trip to Vegas, we had to make sure we were close to Bouchon. We loved the fact it was in the Venitian where we were staying! I have visited many other bakeries and consumed many macaroons and none in my opinion even comes close to Bouchon Bakery. Now this may be a matter of opinion as I am not a pastry chef but the flavors of vanilla, caramel and pistachio (my favorites) are outstanding but not over the top sweet. The biscuit is soft and chewy and a slight hard coating. But it's the flavor of the macaroons that astounds me, and theirs are twice the size of other bakeries. And for $3.50 each, I feel it is an outstanding value. We stopped every day of our trip here to get macaroons. I look forward to visiting other locations such as Yountville! Macaroons and wine! For the sweet tooth, this is a must stop, must visit, must experience!

"You had me at Thomas Keller!" Every time I'm in Vegas, I always need to stop by Bouchon Bakery so I can bring some baked goods back home. Luckily, the Venetian Hotel has three locations for me to get my fill of delectable flaky morsels. With so much to choose from, you really can't go wrong with anything. On my recent trip, I got a box full of Beignets, Monkey Bread, Chocolate Almond Croissants, and Kouign Amanns. Everything was so delicious, but oh my goodness, the Monkey Bread was phenomenal! I've never had anything like it. The sweetness of the bread was so perfect, I didn't mind how sticky it was. Pair it with a coffee and you have a nice little snack. In addition to all the sweet baked goods, there's also a good mixture of savory items to choose from as well. The Ham and Cheese Croissant is usually a crowd favorite. However, I like the Turkey and Ham and Gruyere Baguette Sandwiches. They're perfect for a snack or quick lunch. If you have limited space in your carry on, might I suggest bringing back a Macaron Gift Box. These are some of the best macarons I've ever had. Each box comes with 6 macarons. The quality put into each macaron is worth the price of the $14.50 box. When it comes to the name Thomas Keller, you know it's of high quality. These little bakeries are no exceptions. If you're near the Venetian, definitely stop by one of these bakeries and grab a snack or a box of pastries. It's definitely worth it.

This place is hidden away inside the Venetian - not sure why they moved from their previous location near the front of the hotel. But their croissants are more than worth it. Their savory items are pretty good as well.
Their croissant was delish!! And their coffee was great too. Solid bakery for early morning bites when restaurants haven't opened yet.

What a really nice bakery right outside the Venetian and you don't have to go inside the casino as it is located right on the LV strip. We went here twice on our trip and both times they really had great pastry items I would go back to try for more. I tried the Kouign Amman and the fruit croissant. The Kouign Amman was flaky and was something I've never tried before, but was one of my favorites after I had it. The fruit croissant was fresh tasting and had very good flavor. The mochas we had were very good too and definitely had a good amount of caffeine. If coming to Vegas the next time I would surely come here again as they have a good variety to choose from and everything looks fresh and tasty. They do have seating, but it is only outside and in the mornings we came it was just too cold and windy.

I can't come to Vegas without visiting Bouchon. This is my absolute favorite brunch spot (sorry Hash House) and I Iove that Bouchon also has two bakeries for when you want some pastries without sit down service. Everything is reasonably priced for being a Thomas Keller establishment ($3-$5 for pastries, $3-6 for drinks) and they taste just as delicious as when you pay more for them inside Bouchon. My personal favorites are the macaroons and the classic croissant but many people love the TKO (Thomas Keller Oreo - tasted like a dry Oreo pie crust to me when I had it in NYC) and the other beautiful desserts. If you're looking for a quick Thomas Keller fix, stop by!

I eat here every time I am in Las Vegas! And, I am never disappointed! It's a little difficult to find. However, just consider that part of the adventure. Unfortunately, due to COVID, they currently are not open for breakfast or lunch. Very disappointing, since I think they have one of the best breakfast's in Las Vegas! I had the Steak Frites, medium rare, paired with a nice glass of Makers Mark 46 on a big rock... Excellent. In previous visits, I've always gone with the Poulet RÃ´ti. It is also an All Star choice. When they open back up for breakfast, BÃ©nÃ©dicte au Crabe is fantastic. Enjoy!

9/21/21 - CLARIFIED DIRECTIONS TO GRAB AND GO BAKERY: 1. Park in the Venetian Self Park Garage 2. Take Elevators to Food court /shops level 3. Take the escalators down and make a sharp right or left to join line for the shop counter (line window started right across JUICE FARM) Idk if they recently changed the location, but previous reviews mentioned near the palazzo theater, guest elevators etc, but If you don't know where those places are then you might get frustrated like i did. I done lost my mind looking for this counter right behind the escalators that take you up to coffee bean(food court) /parking garage. Pastries were just as good as I remember from the restaurant and the boxes flew home well on my flight home. Standouts- kouighamann : the closest texture I've tried in the states to the ones in France. Dense and buttery- should not be flaky or falling apart into crumbs. Almond croissant: so toasty (even when cold) with good buttery almond filling. Bouchon: a hybrid between a brownie bite and toasted cannele lol. Got a few chocolate chips on the bottom too.

Love that carb life! What I love getting: - Kouign-amann: So buttery, so flaky, so delicious - Ham and cheese croissant: Perfect morning snack on your drive home - Bouchon: Basically the best chocolate brownie bite ever - Macarons: I found that it's a cheaper deal overall to get 6 of the big ones then getting one of their premade boxes - Epi bread: As one of my all time favorite restaurant breads, I love taking this home with me. You can spritz it with some water and toast it up to warm perfection in your toaster oven at home - Chocolate chip cookie: I can't explain it, but this is the PERFECT chocolate chip cookie. It's crispy, but has this chewy center. It has plenty of good quality chocolate, but also balanced with hints of salt. Pros: - Basically, the entire bakery section. Like ALL of it. From their baked goods, to their sweets, to any of the sandwiches (I prefer the ones they can heat up for you). Carb life!!! - The line can be long sometimes, but they do a good job of moving things along and starting your order before you get to the cashier Cons: - Location is right by the guest elevators, so unless you're a guest at the Venetian, it can be a bit of a walk to get to this shop - Coffee was not great. At all. We got a latte and it just tasted so weak! We had the guy make it again, and it was the same thing. I'd rather get my coffee elsewhere from now on - Good quality baked goods are not cheap. But I don't care. Carb life! Would I come again? YES every time I stay at the Venetian/Palazzo. That carb life!

There is a reason for a line here everyday. Their Oreo Cookie pastry is so delicious, plus it's bigger and better than the original. Tried the macarons - melt in your mouth. Worth popping over to try at least one pastry if not several.

Tasty treats of great quality, and good coffee. It's a fast food version of what you'd get at the restaurant. The restaurant isn't open currently for breakfast on weekdays so this is your best bet for amazing pastries in the morning. Sometimes the early morning hours are dicey - Monday they weren't open till 8+ but the rest of the week they were on time.
A little hard to find through Google maps but worth the trip! The chocolate almond croissant was a bit hard, but the flavor was spot on. The fruit danish was also a hit and my mom loved the cream.

This new location (the 2nd outpost in the Venetian) is located facing the strip, in a walkway between the Venetian and Palazzo. It's new, it's small and it has the same goods as the one under the escalator. If you need a Bouchon Bakery fix, it has the main favorites... TKO, Butter Nutter, Oh Ohs, Large Macarons, Bouchons, but doesn't have a lot of the items the main Yountville bakery has (that place is 5 stars!). No scones, only a few pastries, no lemon tarts, no bread pudding, no raspberry danish, etc. It probably has about 50% of selection of the one in Napa Valley. In that sense it was a little disappointing when I asked if they had the Bacon Cheddar Scone that I was craving and was met with the puzzled look of, "What's a Bacon Cheddar Scone?" Well, Yountville has it, and it's to die for, that's all I can say. The service here is good and prompt. They do have coffees and some bottled juices. They are temporarily running a promotion where if you dined at Bouchon Bistro and show your receipt, you can receive 25% off your order at the bakery. The 25% off is ONLY good at the Clock Tower location. It will not work at the location under the escalator. I love Bouchon Bakery, I just wish there was more selection here.

I love the ham and cheese croissants, one of my favorite things anywhere. I tried a variety of macarons and the texture was spot on but the flavor was forgettable. The vanilla was the best one. I would try some other things here

Pastries are the best but check your order before leaving specially if you're ordering worth $100+, didn't get my order complete it was missing 4 items, unfortunately i was only able to check it when i got home. So disappointing!

Almond Croissant - It was hard and over baked. I had huge hopes but was very disappointed. This must be fluke, must be a one time mistake because I saw a picture of one of their half eaten croissants with airy hole pockets. But if they had messed up a batch, why not just throw it out? Where is the quality control? It really is not worth tainting their brand name.

Vegas is not Vegas without our Sunday brunch at Bouchon! We travel at least 3-4 times a year to Vegas and this place does not disappoint! It's our absolute favorite place for food! Everything is top notch and we always have great service!!! The chicken and waffles are like no other! Chef Keller does an amazing lemon brine with the roast chicken! The waffles are cooked with chives and bacon bits. My absolute favorite is the savory chasseur sauce!!! We always have fresh delicious oysters and several rounds of mimosas! Cant say enough great things about this place! if you haven't tried it, you are truly missing out!

An outpost of the Yountville original, Bouchon Bakery actually has at least three outlets here on the Venetian/Palazzo campus, as far as I can remember. As such, there are multiple Bouchon Bakery entries here on Yelp and I hope I'm writing a review for the specific outlet I actually checked into. (Additionally, there is also a Bouchon *restaurant* here which is different from the Bouchon *bakery.* I see folks have erroneously posted photos here that are actually of the restaurant.) This particular outlet is a small stand in a busy area right outside the elevators to the Venetian guest rooms and, if I remember correctly, underneath a bank of escalators. It has a compact but decent selection of cookies, macarons, pastries, baked goods, desserts, and sandwiches, plus it also serves espresso and coffee drinks. Things can sell out pretty quickly early in the day, but pretty much anything is good here, whether the macarons, nutter butter cookies, or espresso drinks that I tried. Service is simple and straightforward; there's one person at a counter manning everything. Because this is located right outside the Venetian guest elevators, it's a perfect venue to grab a snack or a small breakfast to go.

What a hidden treasure! This spot used to be another doughnut shop and closed down. I've tried the churro and original beignets. Omg they are like heaven! So good! Light and airy, it's the perfect amount of dough to sweetness on the outside. I had a chance to meet one of the owners, very very nice! The own staff was nice as well. I'm certain with the desserts they offer and fabulous coffee, they will be here to stay!

Ordered an almond croissant, two cheese danishes, and one small coffee in the morning we checked out of the Venetian. The almond croissant was like taking a bite into dry, two-week old cracker. Took one bite and trashed it. Did not taste fresh at all. Would not recommend. The cheese danishes were alright. At least there was cheese on top of the danish to combat the dryness of the bread. Was able to stomach these at least. Also had a coffee. Good coffee... but would be even better if they put it in a cup that didn't leak! See picture. Very disappointing. Not a great way to start of the long drive back to California...
i had been to bouchon before and loved it. this visit...not so much. almond croissant had very little filling and was just so-so. coffee also ho-hum.

We came here for a birthday lunch. The service was great, and the food was awesome. We had lobster rolls and crab Benedict. The drinks were good. The atmosphere was relaxed and they did not rush us. We definitely will return.

So much pastry deliciousness ... This is just a little shop near one of the entrances to the Venetian; it can be accessed from inside the hotel, or there's a little window if you prefer to stay outside. There are tables outside, but none inside. We got a big box of pretty much everything - buttery crumb coffee cakes with a ribbon of cinnamon in the center; crispy chocolate almond croissants; pull-apart monkey bread with, I think, apples; an amazingly crisp and lightly sweet Kouign Amann ... and while we were at it, a strawberry shortcake and a fruit pastry with a divine lemon custard filling. Every item was absurdly delicious. Even my simple iced coffee was the best cup of coffee I had in Vegas. Don't walk - run to Bouchon Bakery! Or, given you're in the desert, maybe do what we did and uber over from your hotel. It's worth the trip.

They have the BEST blueberry muffin I've ever had! Wow! You have to try one! It was so fresh and delicious. There cheese danish was also very good, if you like a lot of cream cheese filling. Still very tasty.

Cute little stall upstairs at the edge of the Venetian and the Grand Canal Shoppes. We came here to pick up some pastries and coffee before heading back home. Super friendly staff and very quick! Be sure to stop here for a delicious almond croissant!

I _think_ I've located the right spot to review. Three bakeries in the same place and two on top of one another... who do you think you are, Starbucks? I visited and purchased food from the Bouchon Bakery on the first floor of the Grand Canal Shoppes area. It's just off the Strip near B&B Burger and the outdoor gondola ride. We happened upon another Bouchon Bakery when we went upstairs afterward, and the original location is somewhere inside The Venetian. We found this one to be the most convenient, and it had a slightly wider selection than its overhead neighbor. I took two items to go and ate them within a few hours. The Croissant ($3.75) is a go-to pastry, and the version here is golden brown outside and chewy outside, with enough buttery flavor for anyone but diehard butter fans. Aside from how easily some of the outer layer flakes off, it's comparable to any other versions in town both on-Strip and off-Strip. The Kouign Amann ($4.50) is another classic, although it's tougher to find. It's both more difficult to make and less popular. This version does have a lot of the right crispy and chewy textures and the expected sugary flavors. I think this one cheats a little though; you can easily see a glassy sugar layer on the flat side of the kouign amann, and the dough just doesn't have enough layers. It's way too flat compared to other good versions that I've had. However, if I was blindfolded, I would likely have no issue. As long as parking stays free at the Palazzo and the Venetian, I'd consider making regular stops to this Bouchon Bakery for some pastries. My first taste was good enough (let's say 3.75 stars averaged between the two bites), so I'm optimistic about similar results if I venture into the cookies, macarons, or other baked goods (cinnamon rolls, monkey bread, and so on).

I come here for the macarons only. They are so yummy and bigger than anywhere else. Vanilla and lemon are the standard favorites and love when they add special ones like PBJ. My friend got the pistachio one and did say it was pretty stale. Booo.

Bought ~$70 worth of coffee and pastries. For Bouchon's brand and pricing of products, I would expect service to be with the brand. There was nothing special when it came to their service. Felt like fast food type - got your orders, pushed food products out. No smiles or warmth of service. Sad coz I was very excited about experiencing Bouchon. If first impressions last, sad that this was my first impression.
Food was delicious. Little pricey,but this is Las Vegas. Busy bakery. Had a little hard time finding this place, but it was all worth it. Loved the ham and cheese sandwich.

Wow this little bakery is definitely a must go to when you are at the Venetian! The macaroons are without a doubt the best we've had. I tried the pistachio, chocolate, and raspberry. These are not your normal macaroons. They are creamy and so flavorful. The texture is a perfect harmony between chewiness and filling. The pistachio was so creamy and the raspberry even had delicious white cream inside of it. The croissants were buttery and flaky- perfect with a coffee combo for only $5. A great way to start breakfast. The banana bread is great too and very moist. Sadly, I was only at the Venetian for two nights so I could not try every baked good here! I seriously would have if my stay was longer :)

Phenomenal as always! Also a long line always! Ha! You must get in line early although they do move along pretty quickly. I opted for the chocolate croissant and it was thick and flaky! They definitely don't skimp on the chocolate. Their coffee is delicious so much rich flavor in one single cup!

How could I give bouchon a 3? I've been to the location in Napa and something about this location in the Venetian doesn't cut it. Maybe it's the long lines, slow service, but something about the pastries wasn't 100% satisfying. We had the chocolate croissant, the bouchon (like a brownie) and we purchased a bunch of macaroons (every flavor). Again, it's bouchon so there is a standard here and I am sure you will enjoy it, but given the time tradeoff and plethora of options in Las Vegas I would pass on this location.

Located by the elevators in the Venetian hotel, this little bakery booth is a convenient stop for a quick on-the-go breakfast and/or cup of coffee. The coffee is good, but what a disappointment the pastries were! I had such high expectations but the two things we tried (coffee cake and I believe a chocolate almond croissant) were just so dry and mediocre. I usually hate wasting food but it was not even worth finishing. The next morning when we stopped there, we opted for just coffee and skipped the pastries. Perhaps other items are better, for example the macarons. Also - because of the location and convenience, the line was usually quite long in the mornings.

Walking on the Strip as I was passing by the Venetian hotel, I spot Bouchon Bakery. I walk in and ask if they have Kouign Amann- a puff pastry creation- there is one left! Wow today I'm having a streak of good luck!! There's a cute little patio area to enjoy your coffee and pastry. Delicious!

The Mrs. and I stopped by to grab a light breakfast. The coffee was ok and the pastries were good. We split a chocolate croissant and a breakfast sandwich. As others have noted the service wasn't the friendliest. There isn't any seating inside, but have a patio outside with 7-8 tables which was ok since it was a pleasant morning. The issue is there are pigeons lurking everywhere. They will walk right under your feet, occasionally bumping into you. It was incredibly annoying and l couldn't wait to finish up and get going. I know they cannot control nature, but it soured the experience. 3 stars for the food and service, and I'd highly recommend looking for a place inside the Venetian to sit.

Food: almond croissant. Since we went at 3pm, it was no longer fresh. Very dry and old tasting. They should have given it to us half price at that point - or better yet -- free! I didn't even finish mine. Time: Go first thing in the morning when items are fresh. We wanted a snack around 3pm and almost nothing was left. Ambiance: tiny with one glass case display. No indoor seating. You can get your food and then walk outside to their outdoor patio seating and watch the weirdos walk by on LV Blvd. Service: the gal helping us looked bored/tired. Location: Clock tower next door to Walgreens. Tip: get your drinks at Walgreens next door!

Since I can't make it to French Laundry and don't have time this trip to make it to the Bouchon restaurant, why not make a pit stop at the Bouchon Bakery. I was expecting a line 20 people deep like the Starbucks and other coffee/snack places in the Venetian hotel, but was pleasantly surprised when there were only five people in front of me. I was greeted quickly, which didn't even give me enough time to even check the pastry cases. I wanted something substantial to eat as it would be my lunch and breakfast, so I went for the ham and cheese sandwich on a baguette. I asked for it toasted and it came out perfectly warm with a little crunch. It also had great flavor. I'll be back for a pastry and coffee next time!

Got to come back to Bouchon finally! Last time I was here was 4 years ago and Bouchon is one of the main things I always remember about Vegas and couldn't wait to go back. I stayed at the Palazzo this time and was so excited that Bouchon was a short walk away from me! Bouchon for breakfast every day! I only managed to take a picture of my almond croissant because I would devour everything else I bought without thinking. Also, because I was hungry. On this trip I got almond croissants, a chocolate chip cookie and a breakfast sandwich. YES, everything was amazing. I've also tried their macarons in the past. Their macarons are huge. To me, their macarons are the next best ones after Laduree. That's saying a lot! Their breakfast sandwich is cheese, an egg and bacon in a croissant. They warm it up for you and the croissant becomes this soft flaky heaven. This sandwich is also huge by the way. I'm sad I couldn't finish it. Their chocolate chip cookie is wonderfully soft. So soft, it stayed almost it's natural state 3 days later in the bag in my hotel lol. I couldn't eat it all at once but still tasted great the third day. I got the almond croissant almost daily to have some sort of carb readily available in my room. So good. Still not as good as Nadege's almond croissants but these are probably the next best thing. Service at Bouchon is always so friendly and upbeat. Makes our mornings all the more pleasant.

Damn the cheese danish and croissants were both so good I'm laying here in bed thinking about it. It was crispy, flaky, buttery, and airy. They don't skimp on the cream cheese. Taste even better lightly toasted

Oh Bouchon, how I adore thee :) I love macaroons, but this place saved me. The chocolate and vanilla macaroons are amazing! My boyfriend and I stopped by for the 4 days we were in Vegas, and when I was back 3 weeks later, I purchased the minis to take home for my man, and some for my best friend. Long story short, I have a few more orders coming in from the NY bakery as well I also tried the actual bouchons and my my goodness! A sweet tooth paradise

Chocolate Croissant: I had it at room temp, wish it was warmed. It was large and filled with an adequate amount of chocolate. It was a little dry to my liking. Raspberry Cream Puff: BIG AF. It was delicious. The vanilla custard cream wasn't overtly sweet, just right! The puff was light and airy.

I had been wanting to try Bouchon Bakery for years, so when I went to Vegas recently I finally got the opportunity, and I was really impressed with the freshness and quality of the pastries. I got a chocolate chunk cookie, a plain croissant, and a peanut butter and jelly macaron. The cookie was huge, chewy, and loaded with chocolate chunks, exactly how I like my chocolate chip/chunk cookies. The macaron was awesome (and I'm particular when it comes to macarons!) - beautifully and perfectly made, chewy with a well-balanced filling of peanut butter to jelly. It wasn't too sweet either, which some macarons can be. The croissant was flaky and buttery with lovely lamination - simple but delicious. As many others have noted, it is not easy to find, but it's worth the search! Can't wait to visit again next time I'm in town!

Extremely un-impressed. I did the bakery side for a quick bite and coffee. There was one person in front of me and no one after me so I thought this would be a breeze, not. I ask for a warm croissant and an iced latte. I was given the croissant cold and waited for my latte. The staff was chatting away without making any drinks and there was no one else in there so I was confused as to why my lattes was taken so long. Although the staff could clearly see me waiting no one asked me about it. Finally I asked about my latte and turns out they didn't know anything about it. Although the person who rang me up was friendly everyone just seemed very inattentive. I can't imagine coming here during a busy time if it was this bad with no one else there. As far as the food goes, the display case really didn't seem so appetizing and just very common over all. Nothing about the croissant or coffee stood out. I expected more honestly.

If this is what you called service than I guess I should never have tipped! The service is definitely hit-and-miss at this location. I am a regular here when I stay at the Venetian. the cashier was taking my order and in the middle of my order taking she turned over to the two baristas asking/discussing about something - possibly about an order she took for the person in front of me. FINE! She continues to take my order. I asked "is your latte sweet?" She said no. So I said, "great, I will take a large iced latte. I will also have an iced tea, easy on the ice, please. And a double shots of espresso." Got my order. I was a bit confused why I got a hot latte opposed to an iced latte. So I told the barista (as seen in the photo) that I ordered an iced latte. OMG... here comes the condescending remark - "well, did you tell her that?" With her big eyes eyeballing at me. I responded, "yes I did." The barista turned around asking/telling the cashier. The cashier came toward me telling me, "you told me you wanted iced coffee, you said latte, you didn't say "iced" latte." I responded, "first, I asked you if the latte was sweet or not", you said unsweetened and that's when I said "I'd like an iced latte". I also said "iced tea, easy on the iced." (me: thinking to myself, how many times do I have to say "iced"???)... mine you, they are not even busy. After speaking with the cashier, she took away the hot latte and she told to the barista, "just make a new one". The barista took the hot latte and threw it right in the trash with FAT CHIP ON HER SHOULDER as if the world is coming to an end and that she needs to sacrifice her life to make me an iced latte! well, maybe I was exaggerating, but seriously, that was the attitude I got! I mean, gesh... She could just put the ice in a new cup and pour the hot latte over. I would have been fine.... but no, she wants to make it even harder on herself.

Big fat MEH. Would not visit again that's for sure. Service is unfriendly at best. Latte is well below average. The only thing saving this place from being 2 stars is the cheese Danish which was marginally better then a grocery store pastry. Line up at your own risk

They were out of macarons but I was able to score eight croissants that lasted well over a week. Very fluffy pastries and worth the stop. Staff were helpful even though they were out of stock. Located across from Grand Lux near elevators. About a 10-15 min walk from the LINQ

I had always wanted to stop by here and I'm so glad I was finally able to! Needed a morning coffee and little nosh before embarking on a day of Vegas, and this Bouchon was located right at the base of the Venetian elevators so I could pass it up. Coffee was good- strong! Ordered the chocolate croissant and cheese danish to share with my boyfriend. The chocolate croissant was fresh and flaky, but OH MAN that cheese danish was just somethin else! So buttery and flaky with a perfectly creamy and sweet cheese filling- I'm drooling just typing this!! Really worth trying and honestly the baked goods are EXTREMELY reasonably priced for such a famous Vegas bakery!

Thomas Keller has developed quite a name for himself and his restaurant groups. Most people will know him because of the French Laundry in Napa which led to a ton of other restaurants that he eventually opened in NYC. They're famous for a reason as his food is really second to none. Some of my fondest memories of my trip to the French Laundry was definitely the baked goods. Served hot in a basket, we were offered various types of bread multiple times throughout the night. We even got to take home some shortbread cookies at the end of the night! Thinking about all that great food had me nostalgic for some of Keller's cooking. Bouchon Bakery is part of his restaurant group and somehow we bumped into it. We are always looking for that perfect U.S. baguette and a good almond croissant. The fragrance of fresh baked goods drew us over so we had to check them out! Instead of a baguette today, we got an epi (small one) and an almond croissant. The epi was not bad but tough to eat. Had to really work my jaw muscles. Perhaps heating it up would have made a difference. The almond croissant looked perfect on the outside (in fact for those who did enjoy it, you can find a recipe online!) but it didn't hit the spot for me. I felt that the almond paste was not sweet or smooth enough. For me, the perfect almond croissant needs to be buttery to the point you almost lose all the flakiness of the croissant. Then the almond paste should be silky/buttery smooth with tons of sugar but not masking the incredibly rich notes of almond. This paste should fill the pastry so that every bite you got a mouthful. Unfortunately, we did not find what we were looking for here this time. Will always be willing to give a Keller restaurant another try. The baked goods today just didn't quite do it for me.

Good place for early morning pastries. Even though it's a Thomas Keller venture, the pastries were good but not French Laundry level. Their Almond Croissant was flavorful and flaky without being too buttery. Price is reasonable. Their coffee was nothing spectacular and something that will get you through the morning. Their macaroon was slightly bigger (about double the size) and their vanilla macaroon was good and light but the filling could've use a hint more vanilla extract.
Had the coffee n it was smooth n delicious Best coffee I've ever had. Will pick up bakery items tomorrow

Amazing bakery. I got the chocolate croissant and it was delicious. The chocolate bouchons were amazing. I came here two days in a row because of how much I liked it! They have sandwich options in a baguette or a croissant. The line goes by quick and the prices are very reasonable for the quality. Service is great and quick. Highly recommend this bakery!

Chef Thomas Keller has created little holes in the Venetian filled with sweet and savory items to pick up and take away. There are two bakeries, one across the Venetian Theatre underneath the escalators and another street side by the Strip. Like I said, little holes in the Venetian! I am a fan of Chef Thomas Keller and have been to 'French Laundry' in Napa as well as his Bouchon Restaurant several times and little bakeries in the Venetian. Like I said, I am a fan! I have never been disappointed with his food, baked items or service in any establishments. Everything in these little bakeries are baked in the restaurant and brought down daily. You really cannot go wrong with whatever you choose. I have chosen several over the years from cupcakes, cookies, croissants, sandwiches, macrons, etc. You name it, I have probably ingested it. For sweets the cupcakes are a favorite of mine because they change with the season. If you go during the holidays, you will find fun holiday themed pastries. Coffee is also served at Bouchon bakeries, so you can grab a coffee and pastry to go any time of the day. You may need to check the hours because Bouchon Bakery is not open 24/7 but they are open early in the morning. Enjoy your Bouchon!

Amazing!!! Wish I ordered more. Tried so many restaurants in Vegas on our visit but breakfast here was honestly my favorite meal we had. The toasted ham and cheese sandwich is something I dream about. It doesn't like like much different than an ordinary bakery but wow, just so so good. The flaky buttery taste of the cream cheese pastry and the sweet intense flavor of the cookie were just perfection. Can't rave enough. The stand is hard to find but worth it!!

Napa's finest in Vegas. This Bouchon location is more of a food stall close to the guest elevators. Next to Grand Lux. They have an actual location in Venetian but I do not think it was open. Busy right when they open. Pastries were fresh. Prices are reasonable for the being in Vegas. Chocolate Croissant - $4 - Flaky and good amount of chocolate inside. Cheese Danish - $4 - Thick and a bit to dense for me. Was not a fan of the cheese. Pistachio Macaron - $4 - Good crust and chewy body. Smaller then the napa one I had. Ton of pistachio flavor. Coffee, large - $4.25 - Basic and overpriced.

This Bouchon is located next to Grand Lux Cafe and close to the elevators for Venetian hotel guests. I came every day during my three day stay at the Venetian. Lines during each visit were super long. Understandable if due to popularity/demand; however, the people working there were not the most efficient. We saw some employees goofing off and ignoring customers despite a long line. I am all about having fun with your coworkers, but it's annoying when you've been waiting in line for a while. They also forgot to give my friend her macaron that she ordered at the same time as her latte. My latte was just alright - lacked great flavor and too much foam. Very small selection of items. Bakery items are the same quality that I've enjoyed over the years. Would go here as a matter of convenience, but would definitely go to the casino/strip location for a larger selection.

Looked at the reviews and it looked like it would be super yummy, but kind of a disappointment. Listen to the reviews that say that they run out of food early! We were only able to get a chocolate crossaint, and although it was yummy, I would've liked to try the other items too. The service was eh, probably won't come back unless I'm there as soon as they open.

After a hugely disappointing visit to another big name Bakery on my visit to Vegas I was delighted to find that Bouchon have some delicious baked items. This is more of a kiosk than a store as it is really small with nowhere to sit so expect to take your items and have a Picnic somewhere. Strawberry Cupcake (yelp.com/biz_photos/bouc¦) - $4. Beautiful decoration, it was a shame to ruin it. Also filled with the same smooth Strawberry Frosting that topped it. The cake was moist and fresh. Not too sweet. Raspberry Macaron (yelp.com/biz_photos/bouc¦) - $3.25. Not your regular sized Macarons, these are on steroids! Seriously, they are the size of the palm of my hand. This wasn't quite so fresh by the time I got around to eating it (completely my fault) but still tasted great. Crisp outside, chewy center. A little too light on flavor for my liking. Other items found here include Pastries, Cookies, Mini Cakes, Tarts and Pudding cups as well as Drinks. *TIP* Dine at Bouchon restaurant , bring your receipt here and you will get 25% off of your purchase.

Delicious almond croissants and lattes! The only detracting factor is that since it's located on the casino floor, there's second hand smoke everywhere (alas, Vegas). Take the deliciousness back to your room to enjoy in a smoke free environment.

Full disclosure: I haven't been there since the pandemic began but my husband and I have the fondest memories of breakfast at Bouchon Bakery on all my Las Vegas trips. I honestly still dream about the kouign amann, but I've never had a bad treat. It's one of the places I miss most in Las Vegas, and surely one of the first places I'll visit when it's safe to get back.

Came in earlier because they usually run out of the popular pastries starting at 12pm. No wait at all, and service is quick and friendly! The only disappointment is the seating. They do not have indoor seating area, kinda cold during winter season.

Love this bakery , a Las Vegas gem. Have to be careful because don't want to gain a 100 pounds, all their stuff is do good. Specially love the chocolate croissants. Our little grandbaby loved it too. No visit to Las Vegas is complete without visiting this bakery. Ps. Should have checked in when we were there.

So there are a few Bouchon locations around the Venetian. The restaurant is located next to guest registrations (where you check in)... There's a counter under the escalators coming from the parking garage to the casino floor, next to the elevators going to the hotel room... And little shops at street level in from of Venetian, and close to the the skybridge leading to TI. I visit the counter by the guest elevators (a few times). There's several employees behind the counter. Service was okay, but a bit rushed, even when there wasn't much of a line. Oatmeal cookie- large. Full of flavor. So so chewy. I bought it and ended up not eating it until 2 days later, still so fresh tasting. Granola bar- sweet and chewy. Also really good. Chocolate almond croissant- so crisp and flaky on the outside... But soft, moist, and buttery inside. Just enough chocolate bits and a nice amount of almond spread. Just a bit messy to eat! Macarons- I got one of each flavor. Again I didn't eat right away, instead, I took it home and stored it in the fridge. Next day, the macarons still tasted very fresh. Delicate cookie, soft, and chewy. The vanilla and chocolate ones were very sweet and rich. The flavors were kinda plain actually... The PB&J macaron tasted a bit like the chocolate one, but with jelly/jam in it.. The size of hockey pucks, just one is enough to satisfy any sweet craving you might be having. I'm hopeful that the pistachio one I have left at home has a flavor I'm more excited about.. Overall, I loved Bouchon and will definitely come back to try some of their other items next time I'm in town... Everything had a fresh taste and with quality ingredients.

Waited in a long line for latte on a cold Las Vegas day. Was it worth the wait? YES! Had this pastry called Kouign Amann. A croissant with a candied crunchy sugary crust. Beyond delicious!!! Latte was great and I also got a butter plain croissant. But the star is the Kouign Amann. Order that! Now my only complaint would be that in order to try to reduce the line and make it go faster. Staff asks for your order way far in ahead before you are actually able to see the glass refrigerated selection of sandwiches and the chalkboard menu. You are only able to see the display of non refrigerated pastries. People like myself who were going for the first time did not see offerings on the opposite side until it was time to pay. I would of order other things to try had I seen that.
It was morning delight. Chocolate almond croissant and cream cheese danish are Fresh, crunch and perfect sweetness.

Good latte and amazing macarons. Pretty good size, I was expecting it to be around $10, given other Venetian pricing, but at $3.50 for a good-sized macaron, it was practically a steal. The salted Carmel was delicious.

I am a super fan of Bouchon in Yountville....I like the NY location ...this is my least favorite of the 3. The pastries are delicious at all 3....no complaints there so i know that I will always come back again and again. Why is it my least favorite? it's tiny inside...like really tiny it's way too warm inside (when it's 100 plus degrees outside..would be nice to walk into a cold room) it doesn't feel super clean...i'm sure it is...and i think the filth of vegas itself just puts that in my head....but it just feels subpar to the quality of the desserts. service is blah...they do their job ...just not the extra love i get at the Yountville location. yum yum croissants and macaroons!!! and the coffee is yummy

Upon arrival at Venetian, you'll find multiple small Bouchon bakeries spotting the area. After so many alcohol and cold drinks, my sweet tooth hasn't been quite satisfied. The pastries were quite eye catching and line wasn't too bad as I spent time contemplating what to get. Some of the cakes looked dried out, and was dubious how fresh they were. I settled on "Oh Oh" which is a chocolate cake with cream roll, a fancier version of Swiss Rolls. Just not as sweet, but sugar flavor was still bit over powering. Chocolate did not have the depth of bitterness to combat this, and it ended up being unimpressive. Looks pretty, but that's the extent.
Excellent was to start your day! Coffee is a must too. Location is beneficial to hospital guests. 6-10-2020

What can I say but WOW! Great french Bakery. The Epi's are to fantastic and you can never go wrong with the Macarons. If you ever get a chance to make it to Napa Valley, your trio wouldn't be complete without a visit to the mother ship.

Highly recommended guys! If you need a custom cake made in Vegas, definitely go here! After doing research for my husband's birthday, we found this gem that didn't cost me an arm and leg. Not only did they get what the birthday boy wished for right on the money (chocolatest cake ever lol), it was super duper delicious and moist! The Private Dining Administrative Assistant, Jolene Bernabe, was very informative and had everything in order before my arrival. No problems what so ever! She is the Best! fyi...I ordered the devil's food Chocolate Cake with layers of Chocolate Mousse in between for less than $50. See photo below.

OMG!!!! I'm so glad I tried this place!! I purchased a cheese danish and chocolate almond croissant. Both items were crunchy, flaky, perfection!!! This is definitely a must try when in the Venetian!!!

Food: 4 stars Service: 3 stars... If you are staying at the Venetian, this is a great spot just steps away from the elevators. The quality does seem to be a bit lower than the Yountville location though. The prices are fair (4-5$ for a croissant, muffin, or kouign amann; 8-10$ for sandwiches). Considering this is what you would pay on the Strip for a low quality food court breakfast, I think it's worth it. The line is very very long at times, but it does move quickly. However, they seem to consistently stuff their bags and pancake your baked goods. I discovered my croissants had been squished into the same dimensions as the chocolate chip cookie two days in a row. The breakfast croissant is probably one of the best ways to start your morning for 8$. The chocolate chip cookie was definitely one of the best I've had. They seem to use small wafers of chocolate that bakes into little laminated layers of chocolate throughout the entire cookie so no bite is without.

Amazing coffee and pastries. Best chocolate croissant I've ever had in my life. Had to break keto to enjoy one! I did get an almond milk latte with an extra shot of espresso here that was out of this world, so good they beat out Starbucks. I'm glad we don't have one back home, or I would testing my willpower. Definitely a must if you're staying at the Venetian. They're only open mornings, which is a small disappointment.

Delicious chocolate Bouchon! It's very rich and a bit in the dark side on the chocolate scale. It's the perfect size for a $2 pick-me-up. The almond chocolate croissant was flaky and buttery. Just wish we got it warmed up! The coffee is good too, not watered down at all. There were 8 people in front of us but the staff is super efficient and the line went by quickly.

This was my second time at Bouchon for dinner. First time was with my husband and this last time was with my son. My husband had the steak and frites (my son ordered the same thing) and the first time I had pasta. This last time I had the chicken. The first time I went I wasn't familiar with chef Thomas Keller so I had no idea to order the chicken. Since going to his restaurant the first time I did some research and have made his roasted chicken a few times (highly recommend). So it was a real treat to get the chicken the second time around. And wow it's good! Best roasted chicken I have ever had. My son loved his steak and frites (just like his dad) he missed out on the truffle on his frites because he has the pallet of a 8 year but the appetite of a grown man. Don't miss out of the truffle fries. Our waiter was very helpful, I didn't catch his first name but his last name is HernÃ¡ndez. He did a great job taking care of us and helping my son with the menu. The only thing I've heard is better than dinner at Bouchon is brunch at Bouchon. We will be back to experience that menu next!

This place is simply delicious. While in Vegas my husband woke up early and was making line at 630 am and there was already a long line. He brought back cheese danishes, macaroons and an oatmeal Cookie. We ate them before we had a chance to take a photo. The oatmeal cookie is simply Devine. It's soft and smells amazing. The macaroons my Children gobbled up but I tasted them and they were delicious as well. They were vanilla and dulce de leche. So good. Now the cheese Danish. It was absolutely delicious and the cream cheese wasn't overly sweet and it was just too good. I wish I had bought more to bring back home to California. The coffee was a bit strong for me but then again my husband forgot to put sugar lol this place is a must when in Vegas.

Simple and quick stop to Bouchon bakery is a great way to start your day in Vegas. Tips: - Quality coffee. Dark roasted and rich! - Pastries are reasonably good. If I were not in the area, I wouldn't travel for it. - Single purchase macarons are larger than usual but we didn't try them. The boxed ones look like normal sized. - They do not accept casino credits. If you are staying at The Palazzo or The Venetian, check it out!

Macaron heaven!! Light and flakey with the perfect amount of chew. We only get the large sized macarons because you gotta go big or go home! Every flavor was wonderful but my favorite was the salted caramel. We had to take some home for the road only to shed a few tears once we finished the last bite.

Great quality and prices, friendly service. Best pastries I've ever had (recommend the danish, any or every croissant). Definitely need to stop in if you're in the area and buy some gifts to take home. Their macarons look the size of moon pies!
This place is legit...pastries are baller and eapresso drinks are solid. Will be back...easy access right on the strip

I've been to this Bouchon bakery before but I guess I never wrote a review for it. There's other locations around the Venetian too so it gets confusing. I've ordered a box of macarons here before and decided to come here for some more. They only had the big macarons left, so I got two instead of a box like I normally do. I got it with a caramel latte and asked for it iced, but got a hot one instead. They fixed their error, no questions asked. The following day, I got a croissant from here and it was flaky and delicious. Their chocolate croissant is really good too.

I woke up at 5:00am to get on the Bouchon Bakery line because I had been dreaming of their raspberry macaroons ever since I tasted one on our last visit to Vegas. At 6:00 am, the line was about 15 people deep and I happily waited. The macaroons were just as heavenly as I had remembered and the chocolate croissants were equally so! I only wish they shipped their full menu nationwide. I was thrilled to find out that they do ship the macaroons through the goldbelly website. I know what I'm asking for on my birthday, lol.

Cute small hidden bakery in the Venetian. It's behind the escalators. We didn't get to try the brunch at the Bouchon so we settled for a pick me up at the bakery inside the Venetian. My boyfriend had a chocolate croissant, it was flaky and delicious. I had the apple croissant and man it was good. It was soon heavy. Its topped with apples, and crumbles, it is pretty big. So enough for 2 maybe even 3 people to share. Unless you loves sweets, but its very dense. My sister had a large oatmeal raisin cookie which she enjoyed. The coffee was great too.

Really consistent pastries, and although some items seem to disappear they have a decent selection of baked goods. There used to be a chocolate peanut butter cookie that was really great but I have not seen it back on the menu since 2020. The covid situation hasn't slowed their operations and as there is still a line right at opening (with proper spacing between the guests, of course). The chocolate bouchon ($2) is really small but packed with great chocolate flavor and bits of chocolate chips. The macarons are about $4 and much bigger than your average macaron. Coffee is about $5 and a decent cup of joe, whether cold brew or fresh brewed. The croissants are also really great and always fully stocked, from plain croissants to chocolate almond croissants. Overall, it's a nice quick stop for a pastry and coffee while being conveniently located at the entrance of the first floor to access Venetian elevators to your room.
Love the atmosphere, the service was impeccable, and the bread was superb. Highly recommend them for their professionalism and food

Man, this place is good. I was in town for a conference at the Sands Expo, and I met a friend for a quick breakfast before the show started that day. I had a chocolate croissant ($4ish) and I bought a birthday cake macaron ($3.50) for later too. The macaron was HUGE and I wish I bought more. So good. I returned the next day, again for breakfast, and got a ham and brie croissant ($7ish) and that was amazing also - they warm it up for you too. Their croissants might even better than the ones at Paris Vegas. Definitely coming back here next time I'm in town! Quick and mostly inexpensive meals.

This place is small and hidden under the stairs on the way up to the rooms at the Venetian. The almond croissant was light flaky and had a lovely filling. I only wish the almond pieces were a tiny bit bigger as the filling felt a little too homogenous in texture. The chocolate almond croissant was also very good. The bouchon itself was a let down- it was like a brownie but the outside was a bit dry and hard rather than being nice and moist. Maybe that is what a bouchon is supposed to taste like, but it was not my favorite. The macarons were massive and looked amazing but I was too full to try. Coffee was very good.

Great bakery for the morning . Very small little cart located within the Venetian close to the guest elevators. Convenient for guest. Very tasty and fresh macaroons which I'd highly suggest. The blueberry muffin was also delightful as well as the bouchon brownie bites.

We got lost finding this place in our hotel. I almost gave up and turned around but we finally found it and let me say this..... sooooooo glad we did. We ordered a cheese danish and almond croissant. It was amazing! The pastries were so soft they melted in our mouths! Flavor was also on point. The location is somewhat hidden under the escalator so that's not convenient . However it was a fun adventure to find these yummy treats. It also opened earlier than most places in the hotel so that was a plus!

I love Bouchon and I like their bakery too! It's right downstairs from our room in Venetian. We always go downstairs to get some latte and pastry in the morning. Sometimes the line could be long but they move fast anyway. Quite a bit of choices with this little stand, they do run out of cold brew a lot and have to op for ice Americana couple times. Also the latte is on the lighter side, would suggest to go with an extra shot if you like your latte richer. Anyway, I enjoy coming here especially the Bouchon in Beverly Hills is closedown :-/ please come back

This coffee shop and bakery is the bomb. All the baked goods are top notch. You will not be disappointed with any of them. We really like the litte brownies. The coffee is also good. We stop by every morning to get the day started. In hear the restaurant is very nice also. It is on our list for next trip.
Absolutely delicious from the sandwiches to the macaroons and bouchon brownies And decadent croissants and beautiful coffee you can never go wrong with this wonderful patisserie

Delicious bake goods. I'm not a breakfast eater nor a sweet eater, but their pastries are so good. It's buttery, flaky, with the right amount of sweetness that made me go back again and again. Always long line no matter what time of the day and they close early

This review is for the cold brew and their macaroons. The cold brew was amazing. No bitter notes, very smooth! Their macaroons. Oh my god, I've never seen macaroons so large! They're about palm sized and they offer a variety of flavors. Got an box of Strawberry, chocolate, coffee, pistachio, and blueberry. I thought they were perfectly crafted while my girlfriend thought they were a bit too sweet. In her defense, I was having the macaroons with my cold brew black so maybe that was a nice complement. The line here can get a little long depending on when you arrive but the line moves fairly fast.

Delicious goodies and drinks at the Buchon bakery. The line is long to get a goodie from this place. We stood in line for about 40 minutes but it was worth the wait. The most buttery and pull apart croissant and the most heavenly blueberry muffin ever. There were so many flavors of macarons- we tried salted caramel and raspberry- both were SO good, the raspberry one even had fresh raspberry in the filling. Must visit for breakfast or a quick bite and coffee!!

This place was kinda hard to find but well worth the search. I wish there was good searing in the area but it's off the side of the casino floor, so not. My husband enjoyed the ham egg and cheese croissant and I enjoyed my cheese Danish. We both had coffee which was very good. The sandwich was warmed on request. We also had cookies. My husband had his chocolate cookie warm and I enjoyed my oatmeal raisin cookie room temperature. This was by far the BEST oatmeal raisin cookie I have ever had! Even better than my home made ones! I want another one.

Ok, I've been wanting to try these macarons forever! We tried getting them the night before but could not find the hidden bakery outpost! I must say I expected more offerings to make my mouth water but ended up getting macarons. Buy 5 get 1 free for about $19 with tax. These are giant size macarons, not the typical small ones so a good value. I wish there were more flavors. We ended up getting (2) vanilla, (1) raspberry, (1) pistachio, (2) salted caramel. The texture was on point. Except for pistachio. It cracked after a bite and was too crunchy, not the soft chewy texture we expected. Something was a miss on this one but the others were great. The counter person was not welcoming or friendly but I got what I wanted and macarons were pretty darn good, glad I've finally tried them.

My husband and I love the Bouchon restaurant. We always stop in for breakfast and order pastries to go. We were very happy they had a Bouchon Bakery inside the Venetian, especially because the days we were in Vegas, the restaurant was not open for breakfast. We stopped in two different days. The line moves very quickly. The blueberry muffins are so good here, as well as the chocolate bouchons. We also really enjoyed the macarons. They have two sizes here and the large ones are very big. Today we ordered two croissant sandwiches with ham, cheese and egg. This would have been a perfect sandwich BUT it was so cold. While we understand that they are trying to keep the line moving quickly, we would have gladly waited a minute or two longer for the staff to heat the sandwiches all the way through. The cold eggs made the sandwich not edible, had they been heated properly, this place would have been 5 stars.

Ok this is just a regular bakery at the Venetian right? Ummm this is one of the best bakeries I have ever been to in my life! The taste of all of their pastries is just mouth watering! - croissant: it is the flakiest buttery croissant I ever had! It's huge but will be gone in 3 seconds. There is a few different kinds of croissants and can't go wrong with any of them. But the best to me is the original one - macaroons: all huge! Usually macaroons are a bit chewy or dry. Their center filling is super creamy and light! Which was a shock for me. Can't go wrong with any of the flavors but my favorite is pistachio and earl grey! - muffins: honestly their muffin is great. It's super moist and chewy. Maybe I'm not a muffin fan. Wasn't that impressed - cookies: there is a few variations of cookies. All great but I still think I had better. All in all, great stop if your at the Venetian. They have sandwiches and coffee which I have yet to try. But if I wanted that then I would go to grand Lux next door and I feel like it would be a lot better. No you come here for bakeries. All are amazing and can't go wrong at all in any choice you make. The only down side is that the service is a bit slow, they aren't as organized, and under staffed where it is only one or two people working. Also, the price! It is Vegas after all but usually each baked goods will be about 5 bucks each. But the size does make up for it, still kind of pricey since I usually leave with a good box full. -

Worst experience ever. I ordered a dozen macaroons which was over $40 only to see the person behind the counter grab the display box and some sanitizer wipes from underneath the counter and go in the back room. When she came back out I asked her what she did with the wipes and the box that she put out macaroons in. She said that she wiped down the box and the plastic container because they ran out of boxes! As a customer that just spent over $70 on pastries the least I expect is a new box and not having to worry about whether or not I'm ingesting cleaning chemicals! This is an embarrassment! Tom Keller train your employees to have some common sense! On top of that when we asked for 3 cups of ice water the employee told us they are normally 50 cents each! Really, I just spent $70 on some pastries, you can't give me water? I'm surprised they didn't charge me for each napkin!

For us their bakery kiosk was conveniently located near our suite's elevators. Content that I got my macaron fix quelled due to its larger portion size. Their confection is bigger than the average macarons. No complaints from this carber -_0 Plus thanks for the hot water (brought my own oolong in the suite). Upon the initial chomp, the generous raspberry macaron was puffy, chewy, fruity, and creamy. The buttercream oozed out w/each bite - nothing wrong w/that. I actually prefer buttercream over ganache. But to each their own of course. Their espressos are espressos and cupcakes are...you get my point. Hubs just needed a quick shot of caffeine and he's into chocolates. That may be sufficed anywhere. Focus on their puffed pastries and fritters. Next time we're in LV I've gotta try their chocolate croissant. They ran out so that triggered my curiosity. Next time Bouchon...next time. Ã bientÃ´t ^_^

My first time here and we tried 3 pastries. A pistachio macaron, a kouign amann, and a chocolate almond croissant. We went in the early afternoon and did not feel like there was a huge selection to choose from. The kougin amann was my favorite out of the 3 pastries. It was dense, flakey, with that caramelized exterior I love. The chocolate almond croissant was more dense than any almond croissant I've had experience with but my boyfriend said this is how a proper almond croissant should be so be prepared for something a little different. There were 3 flavors available for the macarons. The pistachio had good flavor and a slightly chewy texture with a light crispy exterior. These macarons are on the large end but they were baked perfectly. The pastries here are certainly a step above your standard French bakery and if you love pastries this is a must eat while in Vegas!
Got a couple of TKOs. Tasty but like everything else in LV, a bit overpriced. Super busy when we were there so service a bit lagging. Not a bad spot to get some coffee and bakery treats.

My wife and I have previously visited the Yountville and New York City Bouchon Bakery locations and were pleased to discover this location on a recent stay at the Venetian in Las Vegas. The Macaroons are heavenly and a must try when visiting any Bouchon Bakery location. On this trip we tried the Mint Chocolate and Lemon Macaroons. The macaroons were flaky on the outside and soft on the inside with a nicely creamy filling. And yes the mint was perfectly minty and the lemon was perfectly lemony and tart. We also tried the Better Nutter and TKO (Thomas Keller Oreo) cookies. These cookies take some of your favorite sweets and make them even more addictive. The Better Nutter was crunchy and filled with plentiful rich peanut butter cream filling. The TKO was basically a fancy Oreo with crisp and crunchy cookies filled with sweet cream. We also stopped by for breakfast and had the Pain au Chocolat and Cheese Danish. The Pain au Chocolat was nicely flakey and lightly filled with flavorful chocolate and the Cheese Danish was flakey and filled with a rich cream cheese filling (similar to cheesecake).
Standard bouchon fare. Coffee was perfect as always and the Pastries were delicious.
The kouign-amann is to die for. Their iced tea was pretty good too, not bitter or sour. I would start my day with those two things from here every single day if I could.

This is the outside location, not the internal one. Once my friend got me hooked on the macarons, I had to have some more. The shop wasn't very busy and the folks on the inside were more than happy to help. I bought one box of six small macarons, one of each flavour and I bought 8 of the larger ones. When They brought out a tray of the pistachio, after they'd filled my box and I'd already paid for it, I have to admit I was disappointed. Seeing that, the gentleman helping me gave me one gratis. :) That's what I call customer Service. WAY TO GO! You'll have my business from now on!

Bouchon Bakery is located in the maze of what is known as the Venetian Hotel. For my brief stay, I came here 3 different times for a quick pastry and a coffee to jump start my day. I tried numerous pastries and was not expecting them to be as good as they were. I was able to try the Monkey bread, Chocolate au Pain, Chocolate almond croissant, cinnamon roll, and the small chocolate bouchon (Sounds like a lot but I reluctantly shared with my friends). The best pastries were the Chocolate almond croissant and the monkey bread. Both were extraordinarily done and required a 5-star yelp review. The chocolate au pain was very good as was the remainder of the pastries. Best $4 I spent in Vegas. Quick and easy if you are staying in the Venetian and have any sort of idea of how to navigate that maze.

Every time I am here, there's always a line! But it's worth it!!! With Vegas prices, you might as well get Buchon Baked Goods. They are a French bakery. My friend loves the Kouign amann. I never know how to pronoun it. I seriously butcher the name each time. The first time I got here, they sold out the Kouign amann. It was November 2017, Thanksgiving day. I visited Vegas a month later and called around 9 AM to reserve the pastries. They require it to be paid prior, so have your credit card ready when you order. 2 pastries come out to be $9.01. At the time of arrival, I noticed they didn't sell out and I didn't have to pre-order...I guess you never know.

Bouchon Bakery is a classic tourist trap in the Venetian on the Vegas Strip. I came to Bouchon Bakery one other time a year or two ago and the experience was so forgettable that I don't remember what I ordered or ate. This time, they won't be so lucky. I ordered a ham and cheese croissant ($6.94) and requested it warm. Their version of "warming up" a croissant sandwich is apparently putting it in the microwave without actually turning the microwave on. Whatever treatment they gave it resulted in a "smooshy" and sad-looking croissant, but one with a decidedly cold filling. The ham was of the normal sliced deli variety. Despite being billed as containing dijon mustard, I couldn't taste any mustard. My eagerly-anticipated croissant ended up being nothing more than an unfortunate waste of emmenthaler cheese, and a waste of $7. I would have had a more satisfying croissant sandwich at Dunkin' Donuts. I also ordered the kouign amann ($4.16), which was not as bad, but also no better than the kouign amanns I get at bakery-chain Paris Baguette in San Diego for half the price. Rather than being rich and buttery, with a cake-like consistency, Bouchon's kouign amann simply tastes and feels like a large croissant with a caramelized top (or bottom, depending on how you plate your kouign amanns). My pastries were accompanied by an iced latte ($5.32) that was poorly conceived and negligently put together, with my syrup of choice fully sinking to the bottom of the cup before I could even take my first sip. Middling chains from Starbuck's to Panera Bread to Coffee Bean have solved for this by using thinner, more soluble syrups, why can't Bouchon Bakery? Anyway. Shame on you, Chef Keller. Understand that when you put your name on an establishment that serves food, your customers reasonably expect that establishment to represent your culinary ideals and perspective, regardless of whether or not you're directly overseeing the operation or engineering the menu. Your name has value, and people are willing to pay extra for that given your well-earned reputation. I have to believe that if one of your pastry chefs ever tried to serve anything of the quality I've had at Bouchon Bakery to your customers at French Laundry or Per Se, you'd fire him or her immediately for gross incompetence. Do the right thing and put this abomination of a bakery out of its misery -- your reputation is at stake. Food/DÃ©cor/Service: 1.2/3.3/NA

They have the best macaroons in town but the virus is messing up my macaroon eating they were closed and open at 5. I always stop after attending the theater next door but they happen to be closed too. The bakery is at the entrance to the Grand Lux Restaurant

This was my first experience with Thomas Keller creations even though I've been in Northern California my whole life! Sad, because my drive to The French Laundry is basically half the time it takes to drive through rush hour...Anyways, I'm glad Bouchon Bakery was relatively close to me during my latest trip to Vegas. It's located on the side of The Venetian, actually tucked away in a small corner (on the left side of the The Venetian if you're facing it). There's only standing room to look at the display offerings and to purchase, but a few tables outside. Don't confuse this place with their bigger bistro restaurant inside Venezia Tower on the 10th floor. They offer a delicious-looking variety of French pastries, macaroons, and sandwiches. I only tried a few pastries, which included their most popular - kouign aman, cinnamon roll, almond croissant, and pain aux raisin. Normally, I really don't like to eat baked goods, as they're two things I dislike rolled into one - bread and sugar. These pastries were wonderful! They hit many notes - fantastic texture, delectably delicate, and subtle, buttery flavors. They had soo many crunchy, flaky, and light layers folded in the pastries, and I really couldn't pick out a favorite as I loved them all. The kouign aman was unique, buttery, and just a wonderful treat. The cinnamon roll was perfectly coated with a glaze that wasn't oversweet. The almond croissant was texture heaven with the thinly sliced and crunchy almonds. The pain aux raisin was filled with very plump and juicy raisins. This is one of the finest bakeries I have visited - the taste is very mature, as the pastries are more rich, delicate, and buttery than cloyingly sweet. I can taste the amount of thought and time that's gone into the pastries. Eat them fresh, when they're at their best!

Deeeeelish! Tried a smorgasbord of the pasties. A chocolate croissant, banana nut bread and cheese Danish. By far cheese Danish was the BEST, banana nmbread was a second and chocolate croissant was last. Cheese Danish had plenty of cream cheese filling, banana bread had a hint of banana and was pretty hefty, chocolate croissant was meh- not enough chocolate for my taste. Overall I would definitely go back for the cheese Danish. The coffee was good but super strong. Be ready for lots of cream and sugar. Staff is great; very friendly and all adhered to covid protocol and the line moved fast. If you stop by or stay at the venetian resort this is a must try.
We try to come here at least 1x a month for brunch and their chicken and waffles are amazing. Service is always very good. Highly recommend!!!

We had reservations for a party of 6. They sat us at a table too close to another table and they bumped my seat many times. The food was amazing but they could not get our drinks right. Maybe mishaps. Finally, we asked for separate checks but it was brought out together. Overall, food is worth it but bring your patience.

Kickass Pain Au Chocolat & Ice Latte. Most recently I have become a fan of croissants . Flaky kind and this bakery has the perfect one. Coffee was good as well Tip - get an extra espresso shot in your latte if you don't like ice. Bon Appetit!

The restaurant and the bakery are a must stop for me when I'm in town. There was a conference at the Venetian and the bakery that's inside had a line through the casino. I remembered this location and quickly ducked out of the conference to stop by to grab a coffee and breakfast pastry. I was so glad because this location was basically empty when I stopped in. Food: You cannot go wrong with anything you order from their bakeries. I've tried a number of things from them and my favorites are the oh-oh, chocolate croissant, mini brownie and toffee candy. I usually order an iced vanilla latte for my coffee choice too; it's better than the coffee chains nearby. Staff: Everyone is usually friendly and efficient with your order. I never have to wait too long even if the line is long. Location: this one is tucked away outside of the Venetian. It's upstairs from the Walgreens. Because it's kind of tucked away the line never gets that long.

Imaginably, one of the best decisions I made in Vegas. It took a hot minute to find this place. Close to the Burger & Beer joint, it's connected to an outdoor dining patio and the canal. So it borders the hotel on the first level. It's not deep inside the Venetian. (Note: The Bouchon restaurant is in the Tower and the other Bouchon bakery is in the Casino). As soon as I spotted this adorable patisserie some nimble sneak slid in front of me and bought six TKO Oreos. There was only one left after her so I snagged it and it was my favorite! ($3.50) Heavenly! Think bakers chocolate wafers broken down into magical unicorn cookies sandwiched between a satiny, delicate vanilla creme. Criminal. Even though I got here in the late afternoon, I was still able to pick up several world class items. Their peanut butter sandwich cookie ($4) was a divine choice. Soft and buttery cookie with a uniquely spiced peanut butter filling. Their Oh Oh ($6) is a high class mimic of a ho ho. Genius idea executed beyond expectation. The Oh Oh cake was light and decorated in a fanciful way. Not easy to pull off in a mini Swiss roll. Cute presentation. I also picked up a few almond and chocolate croissants ($4). Though I didn't taste these, the size was nice and kept well. Stellar coffee, too! I planned ahead to hit up Bouchon to bring home tasty "souvenirs" for my hubby and BFF. Worked out super well and was the ideal treat. Everything stayed fresh and brought the biggest smiles to their faces! Without a doubt, this is an absolute must while chillin at the Venetian. If you're not stopping at Bouchon for a treat you are totally missing out on life.

If you're in Las Vegas for even one day, you MUST stop here. And PLEASE do not be on a diet because you're going to want EVERYTHING. When you go, this is what you're going to get... 2 cream cheese muffin croissants, 2 Kouign Amann, 2 cinnamon rolls (DELICIOUS warmed in a microwave), 2 chocolate chip cookies, 2 pecan cookies and 2 oatmeal raisin cookies. You need 2 of everthing because once you eat the 1, you're going to want another and you won't have to walk all the way back to get it. It will cost you a "few" dollars, but Mmm... mm! it will be worth it and you'll thank me for it later. : ) Tip: If they don't have what you're looking for downstairs, there's another location upstairs.

I went to Vegas for a week and for the six days that I stayed there, this bakery was always closed! (I should've looked at their business hours) Luckily I was able to catch them when they were opened. I bought a box of macarons and they were delicious. Probably the best macarons I've had. They were big, crunchy, and chewy. I enjoyed every bite of it. They even have chocolate covered macarons! Of course I couldn't resist that, so I got a raspberry chocolate covered macaron. I highly recommend that when you come visit this bakery. There were other flavors like vanilla and caramel for the chocolate covered macarons. I wish I tried their other pastries though. I definitely recommend this place when you visit Vegas! It's a really small bakery though and could easily be missed.

Great little spot for a quick sweet treat or your caffeine fix while on the busy Vegas Strip! Very pleasant & helpful staff. Nice quaint little patio seating on the outside the perfect area to read a book or people watch all day long!
