No indoor seating or restrooms so don't expect to order a drink and enjoy your pastry in the cafe. Makes me miss hanging out with family enjoying a leisurely chat over some sweets and coffee.

Thought it was pretty crazy that there was a line to go in and then a line to pay. Line outside to go into the bakery was about a 3-5 minutes wait. When you enter you grab a tray with some tongs and grab whatever desert you wanted and when you were ready you had to go into the line to pay which wasn't too bad, it was about a 5 minute wait. I wasn't in any rush or anything so I was patient and was willing to wait 10 minutes if I had to. Had I not had too much time on my hands then it would've been a different story. Anyway... first thing my son and I tried were the chocolate chip cookies. Super delicious. What made me even love them more was that my son said he couldn't stop eating them and that next time we go we should order a lot of them. He said that it was the best cookies he's ever eaten. ( he's 6 btw) I have yet to come back and try everything especially their cakes. Although you have to wait, I don't mind it at all. It's fun for my kids and super delicious.

Pastries Galore! I've been waiting for 85c Bakery to open in Vegas for quite a while. This happens to be one of the bakery's other than Porto's that I visit when I go to California. This Las Vegas location is a good size. I would say that it is bigger than some California locations that I have gone to. When you enter the doors, you are quickly in front of many pastries. All of which are very good. This Bakery allows you to get any pastry you want and put it onto your tray and when your done gathering all your pastries take it to the counter and pay for it. Other than the fresh pastries, they do offer cakes that are in a refrigerated display and they even offer some coffee and smoothies too. Things I would suggest trying are: Coffee milk butter bread Marble Taro Berry tale All of the following are really good and have something stuffed inside. These are my go to pastries and I usually get more than one. Other than the pastries, I would suggest trying the sea salt caramel iced coffee. The sea salt really makes the drink. I will say when I tried it at this location they didn't have much salt in it and it tasted just like a regular iced coffee. But the location just opened so I won't hold it against them. Pastries do taste just like ones in California. As far as seating, although it looks like a big location, the seating is limited. I would recommend getting your pastries and enjoying them at home. But if you are lucky enough to get a seat. Enjoy the smell of fresh pastries and coffee. Parking here is ample. It is shared with other restaurants in the area. But I had no problem finding parking.
Very delicious baked good highly recommend ham and cheese was good the jalapeno bread was very good also good customer service

I'm so upset with this baking store. We're got here at 8:50pm, and the door was locked but still had some employees in the store. And the guy saw me knocking the door and ask him did they close, he was just pretending not seeing me. I can understand that if closing at 9:00pm, and lock the door whatever you want to,but at least you need to have somebody to answer me that you're closed,right? First time been this bakery store but never ever again.

Craving milk tea and some baked goods, yelped something in the area and this came up. We are here! Large and clean store. Not a lot of ppl so we were spaced out quite well. The prices seem to be a tad lower than California prices so that's appreciated. Cashier was nice and friendly. Tip: order drinks and pay from the machine so you do not wait for it after you pay for the baked goods. Did that right when I walked in, then walked thru the baked items and while in line to pay, my drink was done. Love their zebra milk tea.

I came here for coffee and was definitely satisfied with the coffee. I got the hazelnut latte. I came here around 930 am and there were plenty of pastries in stock and no line. This is definitely a good time to visit.

85 degrees falls under the "not as good as the one in California" category. Still, I'm glad it's made its way to Las Vegas. It's a well known brand for a reason. The recipes are consistent here and the bread is fresh. 85 degrees is no doubt better than the average bakery and has fair prices for their products. They've got a decent variety and you can see that there are fresh batches made and brought out throughout the day. The pastries and breads are packaged already, even before COVID, plus the tongs and tray you can use make it easy to make your selection and go quickly. There's about 30+ options you can choose from, not including the case desserts and drinks. The service isn't anything above and beyond, but they are friendly and can keep the line moving. It does take a while for tea and coffee to be make though, so if you plan on getting drinks, I recommend placing your order on the touch screen kiosk to save time so it's ready by the time you're done paying. (There's also plenty of drink places in the plaza that have better options, but I'll let you decide what you want to do with your money.) Because it's a grab and go place, there's not a lot to stop and appreciate, especially with the dine in area closed down. It's very true to it's brand, so there's not much novelty to it. 85 degrees is always worth passing by when I'm in the Shanghai plaza, but there's no denying that there are better bakeries in Las Vegas.

Always my go-to chinese bakery shop. They have a huge variety of buns both sweet and savory. We loved them in Dallas, and this place actually has an even bigger selection than the ones we've been to before. Very affordable as well.

This is one of my favorite bakery anywhere I go! When I found out they have one here in Las Vegas, I was excited to go! It didn't disappoint me! I had the brioche (this is the best) especially when it come right out from their kitchen, the matcha chocolate bun, choco bun and white macadamia cookies! They were all really good! If I had a bigger stomach, I would get more! You need to go early otherwise the bakery items are gone!

WOW! I found my new favorite bakery. I think I have been going for a week straight now and I still have not tried all of the different breads and pastries, the staff is super helpful and so friendly. Try the hibiscus lemonade tea iced it's the best

I was first introduce to 85 C by my father who lives in Los Angeles a few years ago. When I head to LA, he always has some baked goods ready for me! So I was super excited when they opened one in Las Vegas and am not disappointed! I came in during the Media Event during the soft opening and several times after the Grand Opening lines died down. This place is solid for the type of baked goods and cakes they offer. I tend to lean towards savories like their sausage rolls or ham and cheese. I love the lightness of the bread and how buttery it tastes. As for the sweet stuff their cake slices are delicious and the price point is very reasonable. The only small issue I have with this place is that the items are not consistent. Meaning that sometimes they will have an item and other times not. I love their ham and cheese but sometimes I see it and other times I do not. First world problems, I know, but still a problem! Other than that, this is one tasty place!

Stopped by on 1/21 as it was near a place I was at. I wanted some breakfast and decided to give it a try. The location was clean, with items being restocked and rotated throughout. There were plenty of items out at 9:30am, with the option to order your drink ahead via a kiosk before selecting all your pastries. I opted for a Matcha Bun that had chocolate in it. A Twist that had raisins and a sweet filling, and also a bacon cheese roll. All of the items were individually wrapped, with things still available to pick up things. I did like this but I do think it's quite wasteful with all the added plastic. As I was checking out, I added a Rose Milk tea (hot) to my order. My total was $10 which wasn't bad for 4 items. The tea came out fairly quickly so I didn't have to wait and the cashier was quick too in checking me out. The Matcha Choco Bun - normally I don't like filled buns (not into the creams inside) but this was actually quite good! Not overly sweet and good texture. The Coconut Twist - I was surprised to find raisins inside as I didn't expect that but it was good and the filling was good as well! Not too much of a coconut flavor, however, it paired perfect with a warm drink. Rose Milk Tea - this was ok, not the best I've ever had but good! The flavor wasn't too artificial (some rose flavored drinks tend to taste like bitter petals) but this drink was balanced well in flavor profile. I do wish they had more combinations as I like rose with match. Bacon and Cheese Bun - I ended up eating this the next day (right before typing this). I microwaved it for about 15 seconds in the plastic bag, and it's so soft and perfect! Very delicious and not stale at all considering I had it a day later. I would definitely buy this again next time! I recommend giving this bakery a try!

Been to a bunch of locations in Cali and finally got around to this delicious bakery. Located in the Shanghai Plaza with other greats like, Sul and Beans, Cruncheese, Somi Somi and Shanghai Taste, you could spend the whole day at this little strip mall. When you walk in, there is hand sanitizer so you can sanitize your hands before grabbing your tray for your goodies. They were fully stocked with our favorites: bacon and cheese roll, shoku pan, chocolate croissant, jalapeno cheese bread, egg tarts, coconut roll, and more. We love that these delicious pastries are incredibly light and fluffy. Nothing dense or heavy. Everything melts in your mouth.

My mom raves so highly about this place. Everytime she makes a visit to SoCal, she always stop by 85C Bakery just to get a full box of fresh bread and pastries to take home to Vegas. Now that we have one here in Shanghai Plaza, my friend and I decided to meet early on Sunday morning. For a moment I thought Yes! We are gonna beat traffic. No wait time and no line, right? Wrong! The line was already there and curving by 9 am. Initially I had no idea how this work. Then I saw a sign that says grab a tray and a tong. I was watching how the pros were doing this which helped alot! You find what you like, pop open the cover, it slides in, you grab the item with your tong, then place it on your glossy tray. It's also good they have clear labels that way you know exactly what you're getting. I got one or two of everything, sweet and savory, and when my tray was getting full they keep calling out "Fresh Bread!" Oh good! Get them while they're hot. They'll even add one on your tray. By the time we stood in line, the wait can take 20 minutes or so before you reach the register. They will ring up individual items and package each one in plastic. You can opt for a carry out bag or a box. I end up getting two full box and also purchased a big red bag for $2 to carry these box. Cakes and drinks are ordered using the kiosk or at the register. There's a few table seatings to dine in. I was able to enjoy a delicious sea salt caramel coffee and a yummy grapefruit green tea! Fresh bread and pastries are soft and fluffy. I love the tiramisu and black forest cake, it had the perfect amount of sweet. Nothing was dry, brittle, or underwhelming. Service staff are super nice and everything I had was perfect!

I'm so happy there is an 85 Degree Bakery in Vegas! We go to this franchise often in California when visiting. There's no tables or chairs to sit and enjoy your goodies as this is more of a to-go type location since it's during Covid. I'm sure that area may open up afterwards. They may run out of items if you go later in the evening so expect that. If you are there in the day, you can ask an employee for any items that have run out to see if there are more in the back. Fresh! They do offer teas here as well so that's great to have the option for a nice, refreshing drink! They also offer some fancy looking cakes/desserts in the display case, but I've never purchased those. I mostly go for baked goods like taro bread, ham&cheese croissant, hot dog baked item, coconut bread, etc. Great place to pick up individually packaged baked goodies for any occasion!

Have you ever went to a store and want everything from the store? Have you ever almost miss a flight because of shopping at a store? THIS.IS.THAT.STORE I had this in LA and was pleasantly surprised/excited they opened one up in Vegas. This is an Asian bakery and it appears they have FRESHLY baked bread throughout the night. The line was hectic but it was well worth it. All of these pastries + a large sea salt ice coffee only costed $21..it would have been $30+ in Chicago I love everything here and wish there is one in Chicago. Sorry tous le jour, you ain't got nothing on this.
Soft opening Extremely busy Everything looks delicious Friends had desserts and raved about it Unfortunately I didn't have time but will definitely be back

I'm Loving These "Grab N Go" Self-Served Bakeries! In Particular, 85°C Bakery Cafe. The Selection Is There... We're Talking Pastries Galore!!! What Better Way To Eat Your Baked Goods With A Tea or Smoothie. So Happy This Place Has My Favorite; Hot Rose Milk Tea! Yep, Even If It's 110° Outside, I Still Run To My Rose Milk Tea! The Service Was Fast... You Felt The Sense Of Urgency When Your Order Is Made. Not Like Some Other Places That Take Their Sweet Time! lol. Line Was Long But Moved With The Speed Of Light.

I love the stores in SoCal, particularly the one on Alton Pkwy. This store however, leaves a lot to be desired. I have been here many times over the past year. I keep telling myself to give them time with it being their first year and all. After that, I would say, oh it's just the pandemic impacting their operations. After today, I am done making excuses for this location's poor communication, poor product quality, and poor customer service. Arrived at a bit after 10 AM. No signs on door or modified hours listed for July 4th. I was advised to return at noon. I came back to discover only half the selection of SoCal locations. Plenty of workers moving slowly and not restocking the limited selection very efficiently. Despite all the visits to this location still no egg tarts. I can understand rotating product, but how on Earth do you not keep your core product available so frequently. I was excited to find some berry tales available only to be sabotaged upon looking inside--absolutely no filling! Ordered a couple of sea salt iced coffees only to discover it tasted watered down and contained about a third of the coffee jelly we receive at other locations. Only two sips worth of jelly. I still love the brand and the SoCal locations. However, this location should be renamed to a much lower temperature to reflect what they actually excel in--a universally sub-standard experience from product quality, product availability, and customer service.

Yum yum yummy!! I love desserts! They have pastries where you can grab your own. They are individually wrapped. I get other pastries to try but the one I love the most and always get is the Ube Marble. It's mashed sweet purple yam in sweet bread. Better when toasted. They do have cakes which I'm sure is sweet and good. I haven't really tried those. They have different variety of teas and coffee and boba. When we first walked in, we were not greeted nor asked if we needed help. But they did answer questions when asked and were nice. You can eat your dessert inside in a different room. That room was a bit messy with tables that weren't clean and few garbage laying around. We still enjoyed eating some of our treats there!
Everything we order here is yummy -Salted caramel coffee with add on jelly coffee -Mango peach smoothie And all kinds of pastry. And now they even offer the app were you can earn points.

Busy place with tons of space but more space than options. I picked up Coconut Snow Cubes (I LOVE COCONUT ); the cube was light and airy yet dense. I was hoping for a burst of flavor; sadly, I got a coconut taste, barely any taste of anything but water and air. Mixed Berry Tart is yummy! This tart packed a flavorful punch until I chewed on a stem. Next up is my hands down, the favorite cookie of all times White chocolate macadamia nut. Loads of flavor and an equal balance in each bite of yummy deliciousness. To drink strawberry milk tea. Sweet and creamy.
Support local business now and later. They reopen today- May 1. Very limited bread. Limiting 5 costumers at a time. Got something I haven't had before- milk tea boba lava cake. It's so good.
The bakery was good but most of the employees are suck last few times are always no tray and when you ask for it it took forever or never until you complain to cashier

First and not the only time! Great prices and amazing taste. The parking is crazy but that just means it's good. Had a boba and loads of different types of breads. None of them let me down. Staff was nice and it looked clean.

This place always gets me in trouble, as I come for one thing, then leave with a box full of everything lol. Their baked goods are so delicious, with such a variety that there's something for everyone! And the kicker is that all the pastries are not incredibly sweet, which I prefer. They offer a bunch of drink choices, which I suggest ordering in the kiosk before you start picking pastries, as they can have it ready by the time you are done in line. Believe me, the line is LONG, so I highly do NOT recommend going here on your lunch break. I'm talking average 30 min wait, unless you're lucky or if you go earlier in the day when it's less busy. The main reason why I didn't give 5 stars is that there is potential for problems with it being self-serve, as some people may tend to not follow the rules and might not use the tongs properly and contaminating food. It's not common, but I'll see people use tongs and then place them back in the with the unused ones when you are supposed to give it to the cashier at the end. And the line is another big problem, as it is so long, but it allows me to plan ahead and not go there when I know I'm not gonna have enough time.

Can't get enough of this place. Wish they had another location this place is always pack and very hard to find parking. This is located in a big plaza with dozen of other restaurants. Worth the wait just to have the salt bread. So very buttery and a hint of sea salt. Ham and cheese is a great snack for on the go. The custard bread is really good too if you need something sweet. The bite size cheese cakes are so cute and delicious. I tried their mango slush and that was really good too and not too overly sweet.

They lose 2 stars for forgetting my boba that I paid for!!!! The cashier was nice but I specifically asked for boba in my green milk tea. I took an Uber to this place so it's not like I could return easily. I opened up my cup and dug with a spoon only to find no boba!! I'm very upset as I paid for it! It even said boba on my receipt AND cup!! I have included a picture as well to show proof.

Located in the Shanghai plaza. Prepare to circle for parking. This place had great stuff but has a steady flow of chaos. The setup is a grab and go, which is simple enough. However the line to pay is always backed up and bleeds into the area where you select your items. The savory items are a must try, especially the potato and curry. Tried lots of different breads, so it's too many to name. The one that stands out is the taro bread, egg tarts, and milk bun
Good Asian style bakery with good taste. I thought a bit smaller in size of bread compared to other Asian bakery in Asian grocery shop.
All of their baked goods are delicious, you can't go wrong with anything. If you are going to buy some things, you should also pick up their Thai tea because it's very good.
I stopped by to buy bread but wtf this store doesn't have res room for customers. I hope next time they more care to customers

I got the Brioche, milk bun, espresso bun, hokkaido cheese tart, taro swirl, green mountain tea with sea salt cap, and mocha slush. Long wait line for bread, and the organization of breads and workers feels a bit messy overall. Maybe don't put sweet breads next to fresh savory garlic bread because then everything smells like garlic?? The fresh brioche was soft and chewy; however the the person bringing the breads out literally got scouted as he came out and everyone took the bread so he had to go back in. That's not bad, but also not so good to leave the bread space empty. Hokkaido cheese tart was great!!! Crunchy tart contrasts with the soft cheese. Would come back for it. Mocha slush tasted similar to a McDonald's drink(not bad just wouldn't get it again) , but sea cap tea was light and beautiful. Overall I think the bakery/ pastries standards are up to par with the other 85°'s, just need to work on organization.

Finally 85C has come to Vegas which is long overdue. If you're a fan of Asian-style desserts (lighter, fluffier, less sweet) and breads then this is the place for you. Expect lines for the immediate future since it is newly-opened. When we visited in the evening the line was probably about 20 minutes. Many of the bread displays were running low and/or empty though the cases with the cakes and cake slices were quite full. They were trying hard to be efficient and had a staff member mid-way through the line who was packaging everyone's bread items into individual plastic bags before they reached the register. Download their 85C app to earn rewards and receive a complimentary coffee just for signing up. We tried a few items, but the black forest cake really stood out. Excellent, delicious, moist, and not too sweet. They have a vast variety of breads and cakes to suit just about any taste, so by all means visit 85C if you want a less sweet dessert that's still plenty delicious! There are a few tables inside for seating, but given how busy it has been you should probably plan to take things to go for the time being.

One of my favorite place to grab pastries and dessert. Grab a few pastries and sea salt coffee with boba. Tried the aussie pot pie with impossible meat and that for sure was tasty. The bread compliments the meat flavor. The sea salt coffee with boba was made exactly how I want it. It's a straight up coffee no cream beside the foam on top so you can definitely taste the coffee. They always have new pastries to try.

They have to have a better update on their store hours on Yelp or website. Was there on Friday ( 4/29/2022 ) thinking to pick up some pastry and they decided to open at 9 by just sticking a sign up. Called the store, the lady just simply said "we are running behind and sorry about that". Which store does that. Ridiculous.

Checked out this spot as it's new to Vegas and it was my sons birthday so we came here for dessert!!! This place has a HUGE selection of pastries, cakes, coffee and tea drinks. We ended up choosing a variety of things. Lemon cakes, milk bread, cinnamon pastry were some of our favorite choices. Iced salted Carmel coffees and a boba milk tea rounded out our order. Definitely has to be tried the milk bread was unexpectedly different as it had custard inside, the cinnamon twist light and sweet. Nice spot if you're in Chinatown and want some varied dessert fare!!

First time coming here, since I live in the PNW. My parental in-laws eat here often. Came here on a Christmas evening, slim pickings, I did get to snag a ham and cheese sandwich thing, it was delicious. Also got Thai tea drink. Definitely will eat here again

I've been to 85 degrees in SoCal so I was shocked to see one in Vegas. I had to stop in to check things out. It was similar to the CA locations in that there are many sweet and savory baked goods and they are individually packaged. The location here was definitely busy and the line was quite long which kept me from staying here longer to browse through everything. Thankfully the line moved at a nice steady pace. I picked up some chocolate chip cookies and was disappointed to find out from tasting it that it was oatmeal chocolate chip cookies. I'm not a fan of oatmeal cookies so I didnt fully get to enjoy these cookies, I hope their labels will accurate reflect that their cookies have oatmeal in the future. Parking in the area was crowded and small unfortunately.
Overall a good establishment. I like the food, the drinks are good, but the reason this place sucks is because of the wait. The line will take forever because they keep their bakery understaffed.

Stingy cashier, they got a bad attitude. I ordered 20 pieces of bread and they shoved it in one small box and it all got crushed. If u want to go to 85 degrees I suggest going to a different location. The bread is only decent and it even worse that these poorly trained workers crush them into a box.

During our vacation in Vegas, my sis was adamant on checking out this Taiwanese bakery chain, and now I can see why. There were 20+ people in front of us when we arrived. We got the bacon & cheese roll (I'm a sucker for savory rolls like that) and signature egg tarts. OMG, both were hands down the best AJ and I've ever had! We also tried a the macchiato cheesecake, mango panna cotta, chocolate bread, which were all very delicious. They were just extra flavorful (perfect balance of sweetness) and the textures were all on point! I wish they would come to Hawaii, but for now I'll be on the look out for it whenever I'm traveling.
Great selection however Staffs needs to be more welcoming and friendly to their customers!!!!

We come here ALOT, maybe 2-3 times a week for lunch, and I even recommended and showed many of my friends this place. We usually have great experiences here but today (6/24/22 1220p), we encountered Emily who was probably the rudest employee we've ever encountered in this shop. We were standing in the isle, not busy at all. I'm holding a baby, my wife is holding a tray full of bread and treats, and Emily comes by loudly saying "EXCUSE ME" so we both stand out of the way. Then louder she goes "CAN I GET THROUGH" because apparently she wanted to refill the bread that we were standing by, but first of all how do we know you wanted to get through? Second of all, you could let us know you wanted to get there in the first place instead of the run around. We would've simply went out of the way. Third, it was not busy at all, so why rush us out of the way? Just a fyi, we spend $50 every visit here on goodies, and now I'm sort of regretting. How can you be so upset with us who didn't even say a word to you the whole time? Quite disappointed.. someone please talk to Emily about customer service. I've worked in the customer service industry as a manager for over 10 years and I would be upset if my employees treated customers this way.

Great bakery with fresh authentic Chinese bread. And there are so many choices. But too bad it's in the worst plaza ever where there's never enough parking. Driving there and finding parking is a nightmare. This entire plaza needs a better parking solution.

In France, by law, a bakery has to make all the bread it sells from scratch in order to have the right to be called a bakery. It's a good thing 85°C makes theirs! Dat bread doe. They got some thicc buns that'll make your buns thicc! Want something sweet? Get a Premium Milk Bun! Want something savory? The Pork Sung Bread is fire! They have so many amazing options that it's just impossible for anyone to walk away empty-handed. Is it worth waiting in line? I'm not too sure but if I find myself in the Shanghai Plaza, I would definitely stop by. In 2008, the first U.S. 85°C Bakery Cafe opened in Irvine, CA. The location quickly became an overnight sensation with over 5,000 Yelp reviews and lines out the door. 85°C is projected to have over 1000 locations worldwide. Very impressive!

Decided to stop here before leaving back home to bring pastries for family. I've gone to 85° in Dallas & Houston and the pastries itself never disappoint, those are always good. Well, with my visit here everything was fine until I got home and discovered my receipt left in my luggage and i saw that I was overcharged. I ended up getting charged for 2 extra pastries when I actually only had 1. So this is a warning to double and triple check your receipt before leaving like me. At least the worker was nice enough to bag my things so that I could put it in my luggage easily and the drinks I ordered also were made fast. But yeah.. don't get overcharged like I did.

I totally get the 3.5 stars at almost every location I've looked up across 2 states. The pastries are mediocre. The service and lines are super slow. Good choice for a novelty asian treat or an affordable fill, but that's about it.

The good: pastries are good. Fresh baked and well prepared. They have a lot of choices from savory to sweet and even the cake slices are well made. The mango creme brulee is a good choice; soft chiffon cake and slight notes of mango makes it a satisfying bite. Service is good, at least in how knowledgeable the staff is and how they expedite the baked goods to front of the house. I would go back for the pastry, which for a bakery is a good thing. The bad: i do want to point out that the bad is not really pointed to anybody in particular because as I understand it, the bakery is a popular chain in California (LA maybe) so I understand corporate marketing strategy and whatnot. But it honestly angers me that every pastry is individually wrapped in plastic. You enter the bakery, get a tray, stack on the pastries, and they will individually wrap the pastry on its own. Even if you ask for a bag or a box, the staff said that it is their policy to waste the plastic. This is done whether you dine in or not. The sustainability of it is ridiculous. Again, it's not the staff's fault but the establishment itself. This individually wrapping technique thing is wasteful and honestly contributes to the long lines that everyone is reviewing about. Taking the time to do that makes a two minute transaction into seven minutes. It just angers me that this idiotic policy is in place as if it keeps the integrity of the pastry by doing that. So yes, the hype is understandable and the pastry is worth a visit. But carbon footprint you leave and the waiting in line you have to suffer through are not.

YAY!!!! I am so happy this bakery is finally open in Las Vegas. It is about time! :) If you are craving asian pastries - this is the place to go. The bread is so fluffy it is like eating a cloud. My favorite bread is the milk tea. The pudding inside has great texture and it is not overly sweet. The prices are also phenomenal, costing about $1.00-$2.50 for a pastry. The set up for this bakery is very cool. You come in, grab your tray and tongs, and grab as much bread as you would like to purchase. An employee then bags your pastries for check out and you are good to go!! I was also impressed by their other small desserts. I purchased a cream puff and it was phenomenal! I cannot wait to try their cheesecake. They also sell full cakes. I purchased a tiramisu cake and it came out to $33!!!! That is an amazing price for a FULL cake from a bakery. My friends at the party loved it! Tip: Popular breads do sell out - come early!!

I have been here 2 times since it opened and lines are still moderately long. If you come around 6-7pm just know that most of the pastries breads might me limited and you need to wait for the refill. Tip! Mondays- buy one Sea salt tea get one!! Download the app so you can start earning points and rewards as well. I usually get my bakery fix when i go to cali but know they are here in Vegas!! Im sure to be a regular!!

Welcome to Las Vegas 85°C. Located in Shanghai Plaza (Spring mountain and Wynn Rd). Came in here two days ago and it's extremely busy. We stood in line for almost 25 minutes to get in, and waited more at the check out. This location is a bit smaller than the one's I always went to SD. I love how they have a kiosk to order your cakes and drinks to avoid the line. Breads and Pastries were always great at affordable prices, ranges $2-3. My favorites: Cheese bread, Choco bun, Taro marble bun, and milk tea bun. Egg tarts are sooo good, a must try!! They continually restocked fresh pastries, and you will probably hear them yelling "fresh bread" literally every few minutes. Fresh bread all day long. Cashier named Nancy was super nice. I'll come back here more often for my bread fix without long hours of drive.

A stingy cashier, with a really bad attitude. She shoved my fifteen items into one small box, and refused to give me another one. Also gave me a small bag which couldn't fit my box, so I could imagine buying a cake there. If you're planning to go to 85 degrees, I definitely recommend another location.

This bakery deserves 5 stars! Everything is so reasonably priced and such high qualitty!!! Amazing customer service too. They have savory and sweet pastries. You grab your own set of tongs and help yourself. Make sure you check out the refrigerated case too - the caramel pudding and strawberry cake is so good!

They believe 85 Celsius is the best temperature for brewing coffee. How interesting and scientific! I love this bakery! I visited one in Pasadena in the past. Their pastries are affordable, presentable, and flavorful. They offer nice variety of pastries as well as cake desserts. I also tried their house coffee which was light and smooth. Their house coffee comes with sugar and cream automatically so if you don't want sugar or cream make sure you tell them so. Customer service is also excellent here. They have sitting area available.

All of the baked goods are made fresh and individually wrapped to maintain freshness until you eat them. A large selection of flavors and different types of pastry's. A definite must try if you like breads and pastries.

I was very very very excited an 85(degrees)C was opening in Vegas but I HATE long lines so I decided to wait it out a bit before trying. I also decided to go on an off hour (430PM) to make even more sure I didn't have to get aggressive with an old lady and then have stare at her in line for an hour. Disappointed. It's not that what we got wasn't good. The egg tart was to die for. It was hot when I picked it up. Flaky and rich and just D@#N delicious. The taro bun? Very good. The berry bun? DELICIOUS! Everything I got? Really really good! What's the problem then? The selection. Each case was filled with the same thing. I basically got one of everything and didn't get any of the items (save for the egg tart) that I wanted. The items I was craving. And why? Because it's too late in the day. Yikes! Shouldn't you make the more popular items available all day? Also, the line. Geeeeez. There were only about 15 people in the store and about 5 in front of me in line and I swear to you I waited half an hour. That's crazy. A line of five people took half an hour! And their trays weren't full. They didn't order drinks. So if I want to try the stuff I want and come at peak times... then I'll have to spend 3 hours here? Not worth it. I'll just have to come and get what I can in the off times.
Absolutely perfect. I could eat the toro alll day. The texture is irresistible. Can't wait to tell all my friends about this unique dessert. Not too sweet either.

This bakery is to die for. Delicious bake treats. They have a traditional items like egg tart and sweet breads, but with a modern twist. Delicious items like taro mochi bun, espresso bun, cheesy sausage bun, matcha coco bun and many others. I didn't try any of their cakes or coffee drinks, but it all look delicious. Next time you're in Las Vegas, take a quick detour to Chinatown.

I love coming here once in awhile. They always have different bakery items, so it's never the same every time you come in. Before COVID-19 happened, the bakery items were just out on its own in the display cabinets. They then would package up the bakery items once you paid for them. Due to the pandemic, they have everything already packaged up in the cabinets which is something I actually prefer. They had a milk tea bun with actual boba inside that was SO GOOD! They ended up discontinuing it, but then bringing it back with a different recipe. There's a different kind of filling inside, rather than the actual boba. I wish they didn't change it because the first ones were amazing. My mom loves the brioche bread. It's always nice and fresh whenever we get it. Other favorites include the espresso bun, marble taro, red bean bread, and cinnamon twist. Their boba is actually pretty good too. I had ordered a green tea drink with boba and was pleasantly surprised at how delicious it was.

Nice addition to the pastry shops in Vegas Just two days shy from their grand opening day last year on Dec 6, 2019 this bakery and cafe is its first in NV. This popular bakery is sprinkled all over California and glad to see it finally made its way to Nevada. 85°C is a Taiwanese international chain. Many of the items they offer are coffee, tea, and cakes, as well as desserts, smoothies, milk teas and baked products. Located at the Shanghai Plaza in Las Vegas, we stopped by to pick up some treats. Usually, the process is you grab a tray, place a wax sheet over it and use a tong to choose your pastries. Now they are individually wrapped already so no need for tongs. I can never remember what's good so I just chose a few pastries that looked good. LoL! Got the premium milk, cinnamon twist and cheese bread. They had indoor seating and a handful of seats outside but they took all that down during Covid. Now the open space is set up to channel the long line to the cashier... 6' feet spacing for social distancing. I also ordered the strawberry/banana smoothie w/ boba but wasn't happy with that drink. I better stick with the Jamba Juice version of that smoothie. That's it! Review #2033

Highly recommend if you have a sweet tooth like me. Its not fair to compare different franchises locations in other states to each other because of course they will be different. There are specific buns I prefer to this location verses the LA location and there are certain breads I prefer at the LA location over this location. One item I enjoyed more than anything was their caramel coffee with a salted cream top... pure delicious-ness.

I know I'm a little late to the party, but WOW -- I love this bakery! A couple weeks back, someone presented me with a variety box. They all looked tempting, but I finally decided on the matcha bread. I could only taste a hint of matcha, but it was still delicious. The bread was freshly baked, soft, filled with matcha cream, and dusted lightly with powdered sugar. I immediately opened my Yelp app and bookmarked it. On my way home from work, I stopped in to pick up a box for my family. The parking situation is great - plenty to choose from and a couple of 90 min spots up front. They have a large variety of sweet & savory selections. I chose the following: taro filled, strawberry, guava, chocolate/Oreo, egg tarts, garlic bread, cheese, hot dog, and the impossible meat with cheese and jalapeÃ±os. I also got a milk tea, half sweet with boba. I can't say we loved everything, but my favorites were the egg tarts, strawberry, and taro. I put the leftovers in the fridge and they were still good the following day. I used my toaster oven to heat up the savory breads for my kids the next day, and that seemed to work well. Looks like I found another awesome place to pick up some treats! :)
Worst boba I had. The bread really aren't anything special except it's Taiwanese style. You can tell that they don't use real egg nor real butter. Super affordable place and that's about it for me

Picture said it all. It seems to me cream was not properly mixed so when I took off the cover icing came off with side cover with it. And as far as taste. They used to have really soft tasting cake but not recommendable anymore.

Tasty not too sweet Asian inspired pastries and cookies. They also offer custom cakes and other cream based treats. The place is always crowded and the staff is super busy. If you want the best selection, come early in the morning and avoid the weekends. Most of the treats can be frozen for longer term enjoyment so we usually stock up! Definitely worth your time to o visit this bakery. High quality goods

Come here: If you like this style of desserts and pastries If you need to pile your tray high for the 'gram Don't come here: If you frequent spots like Rosalie, Breizh, Suzuya, and Bouchon Bakery that sells a higher quality product. Seriously... Items purchased: Taro Bread Milk Tea Bread Oreo Bread Cream Cheese Brioche Cream Puffs Ham and Cheese Bread Finished half of the TARO bread...took one bite of the milk tea bread, oreo bread, and cream cheese brioche(all dry) and that was it. Took a bite of the Cream Puff...soggy and filled with cheap cream. Took one bite of the ham and cheese, spit out the artificial butter tasting bread. Being in the Baking and Pastry industry for 25 years and working with some of the best pastry chefs in the industry, I know quality when I taste it. These items sadly lacked it. Items here look better than they taste. This review is definitely in the minority, but it is a true, unbiased experience. People like what they like, and will continue to go here, but if you're still curious about coming here, you have been warned. ALOHA!!! SHAKA METER: ZERO

UPDATE: Thank you to the shop owner for clarifying... their dairy free creamer is not Vegan. I'm curious to know how that works. Looks like I have some research to do. If there's no dairy in it, shouldn't it be vegan? Hmmm. This place is wonderful! I can't wait to come back! This was my first time in, I arrived later in the afternoon on a Saturday, and they were fully stocked! And it was NOT due to lack of sales. People were buying the pastries by the dozens and the employees were restocking crazy fast! The lobby is super clean, employees were walking around cleaning as we chose our breads, AND THEY HAVE BOBA TEAS!!! :-) Prices of the pastries are very reasonable and the boba tea prices/sized are comparable to most boba shops. I picked up a caramel boba tea and a hot dog bun. Hot dog bun was so good it didn't last the walk to the car, haha! The caramel boba tea was delicious as well. All their milk teas are made dairy free so drink up my vegan and lactose intolerant friends!

I love 85 degree bakery, however this location is at a very unfortunate spot : in the midst of a shopping center that is mostly restaurants with too little parking. The last 2 times we came there was no parking spot to be found even after 20 minutes of slow circling (with 10 other cars). We ended up leaving empty handed.if you want to purchase something do not come between 11-1 or after 5. Wish they had spots for 15 min parking only for shoppers or were in a center that had more parking (ie across the street).
Came two more times around 7pm and they didn't have many items. Keep in mind to come earlier :-(to

I came here for the grand opening on 12/6/19. I saw an ad on Facebook saying the first 100 customers will receive a free yardcup, so I knew I had to come here! My friends and I were about number 77, so I'm glad we arrived at a good time. When we went inside, it was a madhouse! Customers trying to get their pastries and employees rushing to refill the pastries, but at least they were doing it really fast! They had a good amount of different pastries out and were super fresh too! Checkout was actually fast and the cashiers were so friendly. I received my yardcup filled with tea :) and purchased my treats. I am just so happy there's an 85 degree bakery here in Vegas! I will definitely be back for more.

"Fresh bread" "FRESH BREAD".... This is what you keep hearing when you seat there for a while having your coffee and more. One guy comes out the kitchen saying "fresh bread" and all the staff answers (I should say screams) "FRESH BREAD" ! This is kind of funny at the beginning but after seating there for half an hour it gets on your nerves!!! Besides that, I got a latte and didn't think that was the best one I've ever had. In fact it was served in a to go cup and it felt not full, like only 3/4. Anyway, nothing special. We got the chocolate truffle cake that we shared. It tasted "fridgy" meaning not made that day but probably refrigerated for 1 night or so. Chocolate used to bake it was not high quality. This bakery is located on Spring Mountain right in the middle of Chinatown in a new plaza. The design of the place is nice, staff very busy. I understood it's a chain coming from California. When you come in either you line up to get coffee and pastries or you take a tray and you help yourself with different kind of breads. Nice concept but to me they should improve the quality ! This place could be a nice spot to hang out with friends if it was better.

Everything is delicious! Coming from Denver I was so excited to get a box of goods to take back to the hotel. Top things we enjoyed- Taro bun, egg tart, and Passionfruit tea. This is a must-stop for us when in Vegas.

Yeah, still 5 stars and I just grabbed another big box of 85C goodies. They're limiting the number of people entering which helps the lines a little bit but it's still goes way slower than those experts in CA but hey, they're working as fast as they can. New recommendations: try the caramel pudding in the refrigerator case. It's so good! Also, the almond half moon cakes are excellent. They're light, fluffy, a little bit of cream and crunchy sliced almonds. Yummy.

This cafe has items that are Asian and Europeans inspired! This store is available in china town. The store is filled with savory and sweet items. Once you walk in, you will see Tongs and trays right away. All you have to do is pick up a tray and set of tongs, and utilize the tongs to pick up whatever items you want, and there are soo many to choose from!!! Then, you get in line, where someone is standing at the end to individually bag up each item before you check out. They also offer teas, coffee, smoothies, and cakes which you can order at the check out. Will definitely be back

If you love mango like I do then you really need to go here! They have this mango custard muffin that is so freaking good!!! Of course all their food is delicious. It is a hit and miss though because sometimes they have a full shelf of multiple things to pick and choose from. But sometimes I find myself not being able to get my usual Hawaiian Chicken Buns along with my other favorites. Which is why it's a four star...but it's a strong four since it's worth to come here!

Today is 12/24 .. I understand every bakery is busy but this is not acceptable when people lie to you.. cake is being sold out quickly .. this female bump my cake into the door so it got damaged and she says " I'll bring a new one from the back " and she goes to back kitchen and fix this damage cake ( not a good job fixing it because I could see the side swap dent ) and she try to hurry up and put it in the box .. I said " no no I don't want this " and I ended up getting some other cake .. smh

I wanted to try out this place as it looks great. Yup it LOOKS great but it is not that great. Nice variety of items. You take a plateau and pick out what you would like to buy. Then wait in line. Seven people working (of what I see) yet the wait is pretty long and the line moves slow. I got 2 pastries that I heated up in the oven. They were very bland: mushroom one and the hot dog one. There's better spots I'd say...

Service is fast, friendly staff and just a great bakery cafe place. I always buy their taro bread and their loaf. They're really good! My only complain is that 2 hours before closing, their bread stocks are almost empty. So make sure you go before 7pm, otherwise, you'd be wasting your gas going there and then finding out that there's nothing left on the shelf because they're sold out.

You can buy jugs of house made milk tea AND they sell the elusive and glorious Hokkaido Cheese Tart! The prices are fantastic and they are taking all precautions very seriously during the pandemic. Social distancing, special packaging and display. Terrific!! My new go-to japanese bakery.

I stand corrected after writing my Tous Les Jours Bakery (Garden Grove, CA) review last week. As I indicated in that review, my wife said that 85 Degrees Bakery is even better than Tous Les Jours. While I still stand by my assessment of Tous Les Jours with a 5-star rating, I have to say that 85 Degrees Bakery here in Las Vegas comes in even higher with a 5.5-star rating; if I could give such a rating. I insisted on going by this bakery late this morning, so we made the trip to Spring Mountain Road (thank goodness for GPS) and found 85 Degrees tucked away in a small Chinatown shopping complex. From the start, I couldn't believe it would be any better than Tous Les Jours. Upon arrival, we found a line literally out the door, which piqued my interest right away. The line snaked back and forth around the display tables and cabinets, and the 85 Degree staff were having trouble stocking the empty spaces. My wife picked out a handful of items that I had no clue about, but they looked good. Other people had their trays piled high with 15-20 and even more things, while ours looked pitiful with a half dozen. All the while, I took pictures and didn't notice what my wife was purchasing. At checkout, I asked the girl a little history about 85 Degrees, and she was pleasant and charming in offering the information she had. When we left, the line had gotten even longer, to my amazement. When we got into the car, my wife immediately passed over a packaged, oddly shaped pastry. Hesitant, I pulled a piece off and found that it was chocolate bread. I took a bite, and it melted in my mouth with just the right texture, sweetness, and flavor. I took another bite and found the prize inside; the best-tasting chocolate gnash I have ever had. It was a perfect combination of bread and a gnash filling. I ate the entire thing, and five hours later, I was still talking about how it was the best pastry (or was it bread) I've ever had at any bakery. With well over 300 reviews, I know I'm not saying anything different than others, but I can't understand how this bakery is only rated three and a half stars. I can only assume some people don't like the prices, which are on the high side, but that's no reason in my mind to disparage this incredible bakery. All I know is this place is awesome. And I have to watch out that I don't get hooked on this bakery, or I'll end up as big as a house. STAR VARIANCE: 5.5 RECOMMENDED: Highly SERVICE: Excellent PRICE: $$$ as bakeries go. COVID: Practices pandemic regulations. PARKING: Convenient but very crowded. REASON/INTENT: Pick up some bakery items.

So... I tried 85° C Bakery back home in Oregon, and I loved it! Vegas being our other home, we had to try it out while we were here! They're in Chinatown, in a newer shopping center. This place is clean, organized, and decorated nicely! I love that they were able to put all of their food in little bags, so that you're still able to get the experience of walking through and grabbing what you want! COVID-19 has caused many changes in the world so it's nice to find things that feel "normal". I got a box full of things and a coffee and loved everything! Both times I've visited, I've been very happy all the stuff I've eaten from here. My favorite is the brioche, the jalapeÃ±o and cream cheese bread, and the Hawaiian bread. Their coffee is good too and recommend you get it with your food! I brought my mother-in-law for the first time and she loved it! I also took some to my parents for the first time, and they loved it as well. I recommend everyone to try this spot at least once and see what you think! Prices are pretty fair considering how fresh and delicious their food is!

An array of freshly baked cookies, bread, pastry & othes that will surely excite you. You go through the selection using an empty tray and by the end of it you will be surprised to see how much you got. Price is reasonable. they s add lso have a great selection of cakes by the slice or whole and drinks too. There is a seating area. Paying for your pastries could be more organized. Having several lines instead of one line may be better. My fave are their cookies, egg tarts and muffins

I'm pretty stoked that Vegas finally has an 85c bakery here. I no longer have to drive all the way to SoCal for "fresh bread". This bakery is a lot smaller than the ones I've been to. The quality of the bread and iced sea salt coffee is equivalent to the other bakeries. Please keep that up! I'm rating this a 3-star because of their inefficiency on inventory and line control, plus their "no ice" policy on their drinks. Inventory: The shelves would have one or two bread left or it'd be empty. But you'd see a fully loaded bakery rack chilling in the corner. I'd suggest assigning an additional person to deliver those bread. Line control: This shop has been opened for 2-3 months now, there's still a long line, most of the time it's even out the door. I get it. Everyone in vegas wants their bread. I once came on a Tuesday night around 8pm, thinking I'd bypass the long line. Well, I kind of did. I bypassed the line to grab bread. But the line to pay was long, and it took forever. They only had 2 cashiers when there were 20+ people in line. They definitely need more help; assign an additional cashier or a person to bag up the bread to expedite the process upon check out.

Best egg tarts I've tasted! I've tried all The bakeries in Chinatown, Vegas . I also tried a few in San Fran! The crust is flaky and buttery and the egg tart it's self is delicious! I also got some chocolate strawberries and cream puff pastry. All of the pastries look yummy the establishment is very clean I think they've been here for a little bit over two years maybe but I love this little place and I went early because this parking lot gets very busy

I'm not new to 85 degrees, but wanted to share a review on to yelp! Once they've opened one in Vegas, a good majority of my money went here buying bread for my family, boba runs, and cakes for parties. -- Covid-19 review: Rules and regulations have changed since before Covid. Now that LV is in its second wave of reopening things, I've noticed that they don't regulate the amount of people who are inside the store with someone monitoring the entrance. -- Arrival: They practice social distancing with X's telling you where to stand. Each of the bread is individually wrapped and masks (just like everywhere else) are mandatory prior to entering the store. Sitting areas are closed. -- Staff: Everyone is wearing a mask and gloves. There is glass in front of the cashier to ensure social distancing rules. They're all so hardworking and make sure that the bread remains stocked. It's extremely busy with every customer grabbing more than at least 5+ items per visit. -- Menu: Their drink menu stays the same with new seasonal drinks being promoted here and there. The bread is kind of like a game of chance, you never know what's on display and there's no way to ensure you'll get a certain type of bread since it's in a first come first serve basis. -- Price: Extremely reasonable! For the amount they make everyday and the popularity of the location, I'm surprised they keep it at such a low price. Such a good reason to come back and try new items. -- FOOD: - Every food and drink is really top notch/consistent. Any location I visit, whether it's Vegas or Cali, the pastries all taste the same and rarely really misses the mark. -- Bonus: The times when you go and the bread you want is actually there, it's all worth it. -- Recommend? Go if you have the TIME to get all the delicious pastries. Don't go with an expectation to get a certain bakery item, it's most likely run out.

A really good bakery in Shanghai plaza and in Chinatown. Tried a variety of treats and hands down the best pineapple cake I've ever had and I always eat pineapple cake for Chinese New Year, so worth $2 each. The pastries are delicious and I love that they have drinks too. I wish the inside was open for seating but the treats travel well and are good even the next day. I have to say the cheesecake was perfect. I will be back when in the plaza since I enjoy bakery items with some milk tea.

No breads - just drinks We got the iced taro lavender latte with boba and mango strawberry smoothie with lychee jelly which were both wayyyy too sweet. For the taro lavender latte, I tasted absolutely no hints of lavender - just taro and sugar from the boba which I was pretty disappointed with. The mango strawberry smoothie had no reminiscent of mango and the lychee jelly just made it way too sweet. Although the toppings did make the drinks overly sweet, the drink itself did not match the description and I would not get again.

I feel like 85° could have went for a more spacious store. The layout seemed a bit odd and with the amount of people trying to grab pastries at once, it becomes a little too uncomfortable. I came in 7 pm on a Thursday and most of the displays were empty. There were also mostly repeats at this point, but I did snag the last Guava Cheese Strudel. It was just alright. The saving grace of my tray would be the Strawberry White Chocolate Bun though. I know I popped in on a whim, but all the egg tarts were already gone. Lesson learned. If you want something specific, set a plan and come in way earlier. The only things that were fully stocked were the cake displays where the cash registers are at. Even the line to pay snaked around to where customers were picking up pastries. I cannot imagine the utter insanity grand opening day was. I don't dig long lines and the craze for this place has not cooled down yet. It was nice to give it a go, but I'll hold out for a little while until all the minor issues get resolved.

The variety of bakery goods found in this store is like a Gold-mine. Them pastries are so delicious. You come in and on your right there is a tray you use to gather up some supplies of goodies. Mix of Croissants, croquettes, cheese dogs, curry buns, cheesy buns. They also have cakes and plenty of beverages to choose from such as their Mango slush and Passion Green tea. I bought so many since its a drive to get here. I was able to purchase two-boxed of goodies. The place can become packed so I'd suggest coming early morning to when they open. Some of the pastries are warm and I love them warm! I am definitely coming back here, probably my go-to bakery despite its location. The drive will be worth it.

I finally visited this world-famous Taiwanese pastry & coffee shop! Now I can't resist on shopping here on a bi-weekly basis, albeit it's a 20-minute drive from my house. Thus far, I am enamored with the vanilla cake roll; Black Forest cake; red velvet cake; blueberry cheesecake, and pineapple milk cream bread. The hubby, and me loved everything we've tried - not overly sweet, FRESH, with creamy & rich frosting! I look forward to sampling coffee & smoothies on my next visit. I also LOVE how clean, modern, and SPACIOUS the bakery is. Added bonus is that all the staffs from my three visits were friendly & efficient!

I love this place!!! I went and loaded my tray so high I couldn't see over my pastries. The milk pudding is amazing and a customer recommended the salted caramel iced coffee, and OMG it was the best iced coffee I've ever had! My suggestion is to try everything, it's all excellent. The only problem is once you go you become an addict;)

Welcome to Las Vegas 85C Bakery Cafe, we've been waiting for our Brioche Loaf, Berry Tale, Iced Sea Salt Coffee and all your delicious bread, cakes and pastries for a long time in the greater Las Vegas metropolitan area for years! For those who are not aware what the Hype is about. This particular brand of Bakery has been setting up shop throughout the United States in the past years and have been a huge success because of its price point and delicious items which combines the flavors of Europe and Asia. There is so much to choose from and the shelves are replenish throughout the day. From flavored bread/loaf to pastries like buns filled with berries or mango to ham and cheese croissant. They also sale cake slices and round cakes of various flavors from Tiramisu, Red Velvet, Strawberries and Mango. I've been a fan since visiting their locations throughout the Southern California region for years. How does it work? Upon entering you get a tray and add a paper liner and set of tongs to picked your items that are enclosed in cubicles of plastics stack against the wall and windows. Then you stand in land to get them package with plastic or in a paper box depending your preference. FYI, they have an automatic machine where you can place drink(s) or cake orders for pick up so you don't need to wait in line. Is something I recommend. However, your able to place your drink order when your at the cashier. For the many one star reviews listed, many of the posted reviews deals with the frustrations from the recent soft opening and crazy grand opening weekend. Those folks choose to visit and vent their frustrations which I completely understand but I would advise others that they have been super duper busy these past weeks and according to the staff that I've spoken too, it's been non-stop. So do plan ahead and be patient with the staff. This is the very first location in Las Vegas and the state of Nevada. They have a lot to improve on but honestly they've been doing a good job. FYI: -85C Bakery started in Taiwan and entered the United States market in 2008 with their very first location in Irvine, CA. and it continues to grow with more locations. -Affordable, it's one of the main draw as to why this Bakery have gained a huge following from the public and its common to see customers hoarde or haul like my FamBam, LoL. -It's Known as the, "Starbucks of Taiwan!" 2019 Yelp Review #16

Was excited to find 85 C in Vegas ! Got all my bakery for myself and family to bring back to AZ . Only complaint was they lacked a lot of selection the other Los Angelos stores usually have but at least we got what we wanted most. Service was good as they went to the back looking for a few items for me.

Reminds me of home! Very delicious and business was expected. If you don't like lines or waiting - don't come. Simple as that. People know how good it is here and that's why it's always busy. I love how they shout "fresh bread" when they bring new trays out. I don't know it was fun to me haha. They have all my favorites. And some new stuff. Of course every other day they will have different breads, it's not always guaranteed and that's fine. Try something new. It's a bakery. And if an item is more popular one day over the other, they might run out. Good for them! There's a lot of folks still in training, but really nice. Be patient. It's a new location with new workers. I had a great experience. My partner fell in love with the place :) Thank you for being in Las Vegas!

I have been complaining for years that 85c has been missing a huge market opportunity here in Las Vegas. They are to this day unaware of the demographics in the west and southwest areas of Las Vegas. It is evident that they will need to open another location because the demand is going to overwhelm this one small location. You guys need to open something along Rainbow Blvd south of the 215. China Town is old news now and Asian families are spread far and wide now in Las Vegas, especially in the Southwest part of the city. That area is filled to the brim with the target demographic for 85c. I look forward to the grand opening on Friday with the later hours and I hope that senior management wake up and realize they need another location and quickly. Update 12/7/2019 - I will reiterate that they need to open another location. This is like the Irvine store 5 years ago all over again. Today it is COMPLETELY mobbed and they are running out of pastries. Vegas has a massive Asian population who all love 85c. One store is not nearly enough!!!! Do you roll Into a new market and open just 1 Starbucks??? I think not! Do your Market research 85c!!! I for one will avoid this place like the plague. I'm not waiting in line for over an hour. Ridiculous

Came here at the Las Vegas store expecting to have the same great pastry after visited multiple stores in San Francisco. When I finally came home and opened it, upon peeling off the baking paper at bottom of the taro bread I immediately saw the long hair sitting at the bottom. Disgusting and felt sick to the stomach after seeing that. This shows how bad the baking environment is behind the scene and who knows what else is going on back there... Also whenever employees yell "fresh bread" and took out the trays, please do not speak out while your mouth is on top of the pastry... bad hygiene standard by all means, at least wear a mask as if you're baking from the inside.

Came here on 02/17 with my mom for the first time. Upon walking in you grab a tray, liner & tongs & pick whatever bread you would like. We only grabbed the Brioche & Berrytale. The line was pretty long that they had to stop people from coming in until they were able to clear the line. They also had a lot of different choices on cakes & boy they all looked so delish!! But being our first time we didn't want to get too crazy so we paid for our breads & also ordered a slice of the mango creme brulee & a med iced tiger boba latte. My mom couldn't wait til we got home to try the mango creme brulee cake so she ended up sitting down & ate it while I was waiting for my drink. The tiger latte was a little too sweet for my liking but it was still good. Went home tried the Brioche & it was soo good. At that moment it was instant regret for not grabbing more than we did because it is such a far drive from Henderson. The next day I came home from work looking forward to having some Brioche but I was a little too late. My 3 year old had eaten both Brioche & the Berrytale. :( For a picky eater I sure was shocked she ate it all. Looks like we'll be making another trip this weekend & make sure to grab more than 3. :)

A friend recommended this place for pastries. Located on the east side of Chinatown and is a very easy commute. My wife and I selected multiple buns to try and red velvet cake. The buns were all delicious and stayed soft for a few days. The red velvet cake was dry and far from moist. The taste was a little bland. Staff was friendly and processed the multiple customers quickly. They offer several hot and iced coffees to enjoy. My wife and I both have different taste's for coffee and I enjoyed my selection and the wife was very happy with her coffee. overall a good experience. Would repeat business.

The first time I came here happened to be the grand opening. I had no idea, just thought it was ordinary day, so I decided to stand in the hour long line (which went pretty quick) to get inside to another line snaking around the bins of bakery goodies. I'm not a real big Taiwanese pastry person and found I only liked one item, the Berry Tale. It's a light, sweet bread filled with blueberry cream cheese and a dallop of blueberry jelly on top. My two favorite drinks are the Sea Salt Caramel Iced Coffee and the Sea Salt Iced Jasmine Green Tea. Both on it's own with no boba etc. Three days later (Monday), I'm craving the coffee so I get here at 8:10am. NO LINE!!!! I took my time looking at all the breads and took my time deciding on the drink menu. I bought a bunch of bread pastries for my friends and family and the Iced Sea Salt Caramel Coffee...i'm addicted. The reason why i'm giving it a 3 Star is because of the excessive use of plastic. Each one of the breads had their own plastic bag and I bought about 8 items! On grand opening day, I bought at least a dozen items! Imagine 100 customers each buying 10 items??? After bagging my pastries individually, the cashier asked if i wanted a box or put it all in another bag. I asked could we have put it all in the box BEFORE it was all packaged?She looked at me a little confused. So unless i'm here to eat it here, I can't frequent a place that use that much plastic. That's just me. I hope they can do something about the over use of plastic in the very near future.

I was very excited to go buy a cake for my brother in law. And boy was I wrong !!! No one greeted me, lines were long, no ambient music. A female employee saw me put down the tray full of bread that I carefully selected while I looked at the cakes and she swiftly took it away. I was about to buy a $35 cake and this was so rude that I just walked out. She clearly saw me set it down and look at the cakes, she should have at least asked me if I didn't want the bread. For a business who has been vehemently "strict" due to covid it's obscene that the female employee just put the bread back on the shelf for other customers to purchase. Also BEWARE with the "specials" they have it's usually bread that is due to expire the same day. Needless to say they have lost a loyal employee. Moving forward I will shop at local bakeries not at chain company bakeries.
Wonderful selections, delicious yummies. Great hours, line moves fast. Reasonable prices. Busy area so be prepared for crazy weekend visit.

We've tried many different boba milks in Vegas. This place is by far our favorite. Great Boba Milk, great desserts, easy to find location, very clean and great customer service. If you like tiramisu and boba milk then this is your spot!
we came twice yesterday for snacks. halfmoon cake was my favorite. i never heard this bakery chain before, but they are good, they almost sold out everything at closing time.

85 degrees is always a good spot to curb any of your doughy sweet bun cravings. This location is hard to beat, situated in the heart of Spring Mountain is a newly developed plaza. Inside is clean, organized and spacious...I could only wish the full establishment was open to experience. Of course, because of our friend COVID, all the buns are individually packaged which is not the same experience we are normally used to. For going towards the closing minutes, there was still plenty of buns to choose from. And with that said let me tell you which ones I picked... Strawberry Cream Tart (3.5/5) - The tart was a good size, just that perfect mouthful. Simple enough to curb your fruit tart craving, but not enough wow to give the full 5 star review. The crust was tasty and had a good crunch, maybe a little too much if I were to be picky. Strawberries were perfect rip with the perfect amount of glaze. Wish I had a couple more strawberries to compliment the abundantly cold cream. I did appreciate the nice little box they used to package the individual tart. Sugar Cream Cheese Brioche Bun (4/5) - this bun is soft, airy yet doughy. The cream cheese is the perfect compliment with the hard sugar sprinkles. Probably something I imagine pairing with coffee/tea, not so much a dessert bun. Coffee Milk Butter Bun (4.5/5) - nice airy, soft, chewy texture. The flavors hits you on all side. Sweet, savory, with a espresso follow up. Good amount of filling and the chocolate chips are always fun. Ideal treat for the coffee lover. Strawberry White Chocolate (5/5) - if you like that old school strawberry shortcake flavor, this is it. Barely has a white chocolate taste. Bun it's soft, fluffy and buttery. Definitely would be my first pick of buns. Taro Swirl Bun (4.5/5) - If you ever imagined a perfectly baked bun, this is it. The bun has a nice crisp top layer married to a nice fluffy body encompassing a sweet taro custard. If you're a taro lover, you will love this. And if you're not a taro lover, this will make you a believer. Chocolate Croissant (3.5/5) - just your standard chocolate croissant. No eventful "wow" presence. The dough is a solid buttery croissant but I'd only call it a step above the ones from Starbucks. Would I get it again? Probably, but not any of my top 5 choices. Overall a 4.9 so I'm rounding up to an easy 5-stars. I'm happy and so is my stomach.

Delicious pastries at an affordable price. I love that there's an 85 degree bakery in Las Vegas as I've been going to the OC location since forever. Each pastry is individually wrapped and you use tongs to grab your choices which I think is a great way to prevent germs. My favorite is the choco bun and egg tarts. Most the items are relatively cheap and I believe are under $3. They have whole or sliced cakes for sale but I feel they look better than they taste. The sea salt ice coffee is a must. I recommend coming in, ordering a drink first at the kiosk and then pick and pay for your desserts because it takes a while for them to make drinks. Line can get long here but unless you order drinks the line moves very fast.
Omg this place was amazing! Everything was light, fluffy and fresh. I will definitely go back.
U gotta be kidding right we have 20 people on line n only one cashier where is the manager Cmonnnnnn today may 27 at 7:15pm .

Just went in for coffee and really enjoyed it! Wait wasn't too long (for waiting to get inside and getting the drink) The coffee was smooth and not bitter at all. I'm a big fan of sea salt anything so I was very eager to try this.

Welp; I'm embarrassed to say this was my first time hearing about or going to this bakery even though I was born and raised in California :-( but as they say better late than never, right!! So we definitely went twice in the 3 days we were here and I definitely took home 3 boxes so I could bring pastries for everyone and know what it feels like to be Opera. You get a pastry and you get a pastry! Haha No but in all honestly I think for like the 3 boxes and a coffee it was like maybe $50! There is such variety here and everything was so stinking good! The spicy sausage bread, the egg tart, the chocolate chip bread, there were so many pastries that were so amazingly delicious. They were fresh, and squishy, and airy, and light... I wish there was one in denver because I would go there all the time. Guess I'll have to wait until next time I go back to LV or CA!!

There are a variety of pastries that you can choose from. They bake it there at their bakery. All pastries are individually wrapped. You take a tray and grab whatever you want and place it on the tray. Then, you stand in line to pay for it. They also have drinks and whole cakes that you could buy as well. I got a marble taro bun, guava strudel, and a Hokkaido custard. All where amazing! The marble taro bun was very soft and chewy! On the inside there's a thick taro filling that tasted so comforting! It went so well with the bread! The guava strudel was very tasty! The guava filling was strong and the breading on the outside was very flaky, crunchy and not too sweet. I wish there was more guava filling! But, it was yummy! The Hokkaido custard was delicious! It tasted like a milk cheesecake! It was soft and creamy and the crust was baked to perfection. Soft and crunchy at the same time. I definitely would get these items again. I will be back here to try the other pastries!

Mood - pastries Upon entering it began. The race to get the pastries. Some shelves were empty, as you walk thru in a semi nice orderly fashion and go to the next station, then an employee calls out fresh bread, everyone scrambles to that area, and takes goodies. The idea of nice orderly fashion out the door, and survival of the fittest sets in. Honestly I was confused, I didn't know I needed a game plan to get all the goodies. We opted for the premium milk, Taro swirl, egg tarts, and cookies, plus beverages. Can I say wow, and I can almost understand why people behaved that way. Interior is of course, the shelves full of goodies, roped area as you wait to pay, a small sitting area in the main room, and a larger seating area in the 2nd room. The tables weren't that clean, however it does seem that most people grab their items and leave. Would def recommend- pricing was reasonable, and can def add up when your getting alot. Be prepared for a line, either outside, or when you've entered and are getting ready to pay. Location is Spring Mountain/ Arville ( Shanghai Plaza) ample parking, can get very congested though

After hearing good things about this bakery from several different people, I was excited to finally get to try it! When you walk in, it is every savory/sweet lovers heaven. Something in there for everyone. It was so hard to choose, but I was leaving the next day. I wanted to see how they'd hold up, so I just got a few. Went with the milk tea bun, matcha bun, croquet, taro bun, curry bun & one that had bacon on it. The croquet hit the spot for that savory craving, full of flavor & just the amount of filling. Curry was also good, however I do wish there was some spice to it. The taro bun was so soft & the filling wasn't too sweet. The remaining ones I took home, threw it in the fridge & didn't eat till the next day to which at that point they were 2 days old. I gave a few away, but don't worry, I ate one first to see if it was okay. I decided on the milk tea, zapped it the microwave , good as new. The bun was soft & to my surprise there was actual boba in the filling, of course it was a bit melted but it was still really good like milk tea, & not overly sweet. Since that was safe, I gave the matcha bun to my coworker, who enjoyed it & also commented how she liked it because it wasn't too sweet. Also gave away the bacon & croquet, both of which got positive feedback. I also have to mention that the croquet wasn't consumed till 3 days old & was still good. Everything is individually wrapped, so it's an easy pick up & go. I just had to put some tape on them before packing it in my carry on. This might be my new thing to take home whenever one is nearby. Everything was good & held up well. Can't wait to go back & try more! Yumm, my mouth is watering just thinking about it.

First time here and here's my first impression. The space is pretty big if you're wanting to hangout here or eat your bakery stuffs.. they have a wide selection of breads that it looks big and puffy but as soon as u bite into the bread it deflates.. so I'm thinking they just used a lot yeast to make it rise (I don't know. I don't bake) and the stuffing inside is not a lot either. They have cookies and pan bread... it's not that good either... they have teas and coffee to go with their bakery goods . So it's ok but I would suggest to just get your tea to the store next door called share tea. It's pretty good there... so the most disappointing part here is the waiting and the cleanliness part... when u get their bakery stuffs you have to get a tray and put ur own breads etc, they provide you with your own tongs. The price and the name of the bread are displayed!
