While holding the breads, bakery goods on ur tray you go to this long line to wait and pay while having your food exposed to cough, sneeze, air etc..there is no protection because they don't put plastic wraps until You get to the register where the money and all kinds of germs your food can get exposed to.. thee waiting in line to pay takes about 45 mins so if you're carrying your big tray with your goods depending on how heavy it could be it's really annoying... so when you get to the register the cashiers have to no conversation because they looked pretty beat up, taking payments, bagging the goods one by one and arranging them In a box. It's not very efficient.. and they are tired.the cashier I had said she hates it.. lol! I understand that they make their breads, goodies fresh but packing them already before putting them in the shelves is much more safer, cleaner and efficient if people loves their baked good they will buy them anyways, I'm sure they still make it fresh everyday because it will run out, some of the baked goods are gone and I can see them refilling them... so to save time, to save the food from Dirt packed them, and provide the clients a box so they can get in and get out.... and they also have to make sure the breads are filled and not just air inside... if it's gets better I might give it another chance but if not... I'm good. And I will not recommend it...

My favorite pastry here is the milk pudding buns. I didn't see any around when I first looked around and ended up with other items. I asked the worker putting the items out if they had any and she said not today. I finish paying and while waiting for my drink decided to walk around once more and guess what! MILK PUDDING BUNS!! I was upset at first, but quickly grabbed 6 buns and headed over to check out again. The guy at the cashier noticed I had an 85C bag in my hand already and welcomed me back while he was ringing up the people in front of me. The store smelled quite off today, not fresh baked goods, but smelled like sewer today. I can smell it through my 3 layer cotton mask . Hopefully they get that fixed and due to covid they removed the tongs. I rather they offer tongs cuz there were multiple people touching pastries and putting them back. Hand sanitizer is only available checkout where you pick up drinks. I think having one available as people enter the store would be a great idea. As for the worker who I asked if they had any milk buns, she asked what kind and named a long list of buns until I recognized a name just to tell me they didn't have any. Which was inaccurate, at least check before answering me if you're unsure but she answered back with a quick solid No. Shoutout to the Gambit, the cashier today you attention to detail actual made up for the somewhat poor experience I had earlier.

If you want some good Chinese pastries, I recommend 85° Degrees! This place here has many pastries like: - Pork Sung Bun - Giant Pork Sung Bun - Coconut Buns - Sponge Cake - Garlic Bread - Black Forest Cake - Mango Cake - Almond Cake - Chocolate Cookies And much more! Everytime when me and my cousin go visit this bakery after dinner during the weekend, there's always a long line! We always buy a whole lot of pastries to eat for our family to share. Their pastries are very soft and they don't hardened for a few days, Yay! If you are looking for a special treat for a special someone or wanting to get some pastries, visit here! But I recommend to come during the day time because if you go during night time, their items are gone quick! From my recent visit, I actually got the last sponge cake! Oh, I felt lucky!

I went to the 85C Bakery in SD in 2017 and one of the workers told me that a LV location was in the works. Two years later, it's FINALLY HERE! I waited a couple days after the grand opening to visit and you could tell that some things needed improvement. It was 1pm and most of the shelves were empty. They would yell, "FRESH BREAD," but they were only cranking out 3 different kind - BerryTale, Choco Bun, and Egg Tarts. Ended up grabbing a few, just because there wasn't much to choose from. The line was about a 30 minute wait to get to the register. It was Monday and the had BOGO sea salt drinks advertised on their app, but when I go to order and ask the cashier if it's BOGO she says that they don't do promotions since they're a new store. I came a second time, this time, at 9am. The lines are better, the selection was plentiful (not just cases of BerryTale), and the FRESH BREAD that was coming out was more of the good stuff. Ended up with 2 trays full because I didn't want to pass up trying everything. I asked the cashier if they're still not doing promotions because I wanted to do the "buy a $20 gift card and get a free mug" deal, but the last time I visited they said they weren't doing it. She gave me a confused look and said they should've wrong me up for the promotion and apologized for the misinformation. I ended up eating dinner at Shanghai Plaza and took a peek at the selection and saw they still had some premium items (I could see someone picking up a pink bun which had to be the Strawberry Chocolate one). There was still a line outside, but at least I could see the shelves were still full of pastries. I have high hopes for 85C and think they're still working out the kinks because everyone and their mamas are coming to visit and wait out the lines. *Pro-tip: there's a kiosk in front to order drinks and cakes only! A girl behind me didn't grab a tray and said she only wanted a drink. One of the ladies next to me said, "you're going to wait in this line for a drink?!" I let her know about the kiosk and she was in and out quickly.

Very bad experience here! The store does not even reach its capacity, it was barely half of its. Unfortunately, they let people wait outside for nothing in the cold rain! A prudent people will let the same numbers of people in vs out, unfortunately the young lady guarding at the door didn't know how to handle the situation. We asked her why? She simply answered she was afraid of long lines, but looked in the picture ! This is not even defined as a regular "long " line that you should imagine. My gosh! Sorry Even in bigger city, things like that Never happened with other 85 locations which are even smaller in square feet. This store manager better know how to prepare for holiday seasons.

Here we go this 85 B is finally OPENED and it's banging it. There was a line up but it was worth the wait All the goodies was hot and fresh. When new stuff came out the Team yelled " FREASH BREAD " so funny but cool tho. Five thumbs up from me I'm going back again n again

Really good salted cream coffee. Easy to use kiosks to order cake or drinks. The line was too long to try the baked good, but after they are open for a while I'd like to try the hotdog buns. The prices on the bakery items was very reasonable.

"FRESH BREAD!!" I think it's so funny that they say that. I love it. They literally say it every few minutes.. so that means they have fresh bread coming out often! I believe it opened last week, so it's fairly new. I think it's also smaller than the usual 85's in Cali, but maybe I'm trippin, it's been awhile for me. I came in on a Saturday afternoon(yesterday). They did have a line out the door, but it wasn't a bad wait. I feel like they had a good system going on, so the employees aren't too overwhelmed with customers. When you do get to enter, you pick up a tray and Tongs, please don't pick up the pastry with your hands .. COMMON SENSE. most of the pastry shelves(windows? I don't know..) were occupied with delectable items, And if it didn't have anything, I feel like within minutes it gets filled back up. My mom was with me, she grabbed every taro flavored pastry she could find. I'm all about that milk bun. I went overboard with pastries, it'll definitely last me.... a couple days LOL. Their pastries are so yummy, not too sweet, and even their savory items Are delicious! I also had a sea salt caramel drink with boba. So good, it reminds me of a caramel macchiato. I'll probably wait til it calms down a little.. or maybe when I'm craving it again, who knows!
Awesome bakery. It was busy, but they were fast and efficient. Parking was hard to find, but it's in a very busy shopping center.

While I'm used to going to 85° in SoCal, it is an absolute madhouse here in Vegas. Store is weirdly laid out and there is usually a line out the door. I've noticed that even when they open at 7 AM they'll have multiple trays of the same product in their cases, rather than having a variety. If you like taro buns and chocolate chip bowls you're in luck - everything else, it may be there today and then who knows when it will be back in stock. Multiple times I've left because it's way too busy to bother buying anything. It's totally inefficient to have cashiers also grabbing stuff out of the cake case, building and filling cake boxes, along with ringing up and bagging orders. This inefficiency has lead to ridiculous wait times just to pay. Also, for a place that sells jellies, puddings and mousse, it's weird that they don't stock spoons, only forks, but that's a company wide policy. Odd.
A little pricy, but everything I've got here has always been good. Can be busy at times, but the line moves quickly. Staff have always been friendly. I'll keep going back.

This place did great managing things during covid! There were lots of people while I was in the store but the workers were fast and edgy in getting people in and out. I went during the last hour, and they were still stocking the shelves with buns! I grabbed about a half dozen and all were good!

I give 5 star for their bread, always a big fan. A cashier named Kaitlin was rude to me. I will attached my receipt for the proof. We were at the store around 8:22pm of 1/5/2022. I bought almost $100 worth of pastries with drinks. 35 pastries to be exact, she gave me only 2 boxes and a bag. She stuffed 14 pastries on each box and 7 loose in a bag. I asked for another box, she refused she said minimum 9 for boxes and I only have 7. I asked her to move some from the other boxes since they have 14 each. I told her I'll pay for it if it cost something. She said she still can't do it. I asked another cashier to give me a box and he gave it to me with no questions asked. This kind of employee is bad for business who work for customer service field. I don't want her to lose her job but this need to be addressed.

I felt like a kid in a candy store coming to this bakery! I kept giggling the whole time while adding bun after bun to the cafeteria style tray they provided for you. Everything tasted as delicious as they looked. I got to try over ten of their products. My definite favorites were the chocolate mousse cake (dark and rich), the milky pudding bun (soft and creamy), the cheese tart (almost tastes like a cheesecake in tart form!), and the guava pastry (super flaky and fruity). Dreaming of coming back here and feeling like a kid again

Coming from LA, particularly the 626 area, I am a frequent visitor at this store. I was visiting Vegas for a family birthday and decided to order the cake slices rather than a whole cake and settled for 85 since it was a familiar name. We placed our order an hour before the given pickup time and arrived around that time. When we arrived inside the first thing I noticed was a sewer stench and I thought I would get used to it but the 15+ mins we were there I did not (or does the plaza sell durian and I don't know about it..?). We went up to the pickup window and someone eventually helped us because it was so busy and the line was pretty long but that's ok. The thing that led me to write this review was that they did not have the order ready when we arrived so it took a much longer wait while they prepared it. We came in at the same time as someone else and I noticed they left way after us, so what was the point of having an online order function..? So we get dibs on the items? After we got our order and left for home we realized that the order was incorrect and they mixed up 2 items. It was our fault for not checking too but could our experience get any worse.. I don't blame the guy that put our order together but management should well.. manage better in terms of work flow and get on that online ordering issue. For all the folks that bother to read this, maybe skip out on online orders for now because you might have a better experience going into order. Would still probably go back in the future just to see if I have better experience but in the mean time disappointed.

I wish they opened another 85 bakery here in Vegas. They don't always have every bread out. Some breads don't get cooked all the way. When I order my coffee a certain way they do it wrong. U ask for boba and they hardly put any boba on ur drink. The fact also that this location gets really packed badlyyy and hardly ever find parking. I have a handicap placard due to my disability & people who are not disabled & no handicap placard on their cars park on handicap spots. This just makes me sooo mad.... They need to put signs also to be a 15-20min parking ONLYYYY for people who are just buying something fast & leave. I love 85 degrees but I wish they opened another location here in Vegas.

The "Starbucks of Taiwan". I'm happy that they finally opened one here in LV, no longer have to travel to CA. If you like Asian style bread and cakes(light and fluffy), this is the place you would love! They all reminds me of Japanese bakeries. Great prices and NO TAX. Not much of a seating area since it's so busy, don't expect this place to be a hangout :)

Yet another great restaurant in Chinatown -- a Taiwanese bakery with a great selection of baked goods and good drinks, in a shopping center full of many amazing and diverse restaurants. My personal favorites are the Hokkaido cheese tart, cheese bread, and the seasonal specials. A change they have made for covid: everything is individually wrapped in plastic.

I first tried 85* Cafe in Irvine many moons ago. I grab some goodies whenever I visit California. The hype is still alive in Vegas even after being open for a few months. There's still long lines, chaos, panic, hoarding, and bread shortage. The choices are limited and lots of empty trays and shelves especially at night and weekends. There are more empty shelves than there is bread/ pastries. Everybody's grabbing whatever's being put before they even hit the shelves like it was going out of style. The pastries are delicious. My favorites are the green tea tale, mango tale, cheese dog, garlic cheese bread, bacon, ham and cheese, milk pudding bread, and iced lemon black tea. What I don't like: choco bun, mocha bread, sugar cream cheese brioche, and their cakes including the boba tea cake. They're dry and flavorless.

I went in for the memories. I used to love their bakery while I was studying in China. The one in Las Vegas was impressive. I could find the familiarity in taste. Wide selection of buns and rolls and pastries. I enjoyed their rose cheese bun best.

Life looks wonderful and beautiful through another's eyes! Know that YOU have meaning, life should be lived one happy moment at a time. Discover what makes your life happy! For me, please, coffee; is how to begin anew and renewed each and every day. The staff here makes a mean cup of your have to go try caffeinated beverage. If your not a caffeine addict, they sell the milk teas with an extra amazing assortment of boba flavors. This review is post COVID, so many changes have taken place in our world. Health is paramount, now that 85 degrees is open it's time to support our favorite bakery. To keep you "the customer health," everything is pre packaged now. Rest assured everything is baked in house with proper safety procedures followed. The store is always clean beyond what is called for. Did you see that speck of dirt anywhere? Nope, neither did I ! Thank you crew and staff of 85 Degrees for making my health happiness great. The joy of life should be especially importantly enough-right! When we think long and hard on it! What about when life throws those unexpectedly off? That curve ball out of right field. How about that birthday that you need a cake for with one hours notice? Can you possibly make a deadline like that; and it still turn out "golden!" Indeed it can. Make epic parties and be the talk of your little circle. The 85 degree bakery sells cakes that are made with no notice. They are delicious too! They even provide the knife to cut it with. As an added touch purchase a chocolate happy birthday marker moment too! The variety and flavors will honestly surprise and surpass your cake needs expectations; especially on short notice. How do I know about cakes in an hour? Or on the fly! Between the life that I pull off, it's always busy busy! This for work, a dog, a twin, then work calls again; you get the idea. My bestie needed her cake and I was going to make it and all it home. Then I fell asleep! I remembered that 85 degrees does some of the best cakes I've seen. You need no notice they are positioned behind glass ready to be taken to your function. The pricing is no issues either. A larger cake will run under $50. The adornments are so beautiful and appealing to the eye. When you taste that first bite of your fabulous cake that price will just melt away with the icing under your tongue. The strawberries tiramisu is so smooth and decadent. You will be taking seconds and thirds wondering where the cake went; it's so damn delicious. Now if it's just the bakery needs of breads and pastries it's all here awaiting your selection. So many versions of sweet breads and cakes. There are still many to choose from, but not like prior to COVID. You are still able to shop for your own purchase of bread and pastries. They are again all individually wrapped with perfect care and joy. As you shop employees of the bakery are restocking what customers are buying. Usually, a line is always gathered outside. With the COVID restrictions relaxed for now up to about fifteen individuals can be in the store. Remember the mask you cannot shop in the store without it, regardless of vaccine status. Now we have the place to cake. Dessert should be taken very seriously. Trust the crew of 85 degrees to make that special moment super. Have epic moments all the time. It does not take a special occasion to have a slice of cake. Sure, maybe you should share your favorite dessert! Maybe not! No judgement here. Let's dessert together in harmony. Get that strawberries boba drink with extra whip to go for a limited time I've heard. I have dessert waiting and it needs extra special attention. Remember your incredible and unique because you are YOU! Now have cake and make it all better! I've heard pie can change life moments too!

If you love pastries, you MUST try this place! It's located in Chinatown near spring mountain and Wynn road. All day long pastries are baked and coming out hot straight from the oven! I tried few pastries and our favorite are the little flan or egg tarts, the garlic and cheese bread, the brioche and the mushroom bread! They offer to bag each pastry individually or in a box. The missing star to make it a 5 is for the below. If you are in the rush, it won't be the place to go. Pastries comes and goes right away lol (they sell it quick) The line to pay is long long long... so be patient. The sitting area is alright, something is missing to make it cozy. The staff at the cashier always look stressed and overwhelmed by the constant crowd waiting to pay. If they close at 10pm, they stop baking at 8pm so most of the pastries won't be hot. Great concept! And love the pastries

When I discovered they had an 85C here, I was OVER.THE. MOON. We walked in to a full bakery with a TON of savory options (always prefer savory to sweet) and I was so happy! Here is everything we had - Elote bun - VERY delicious, highly recommend getting Mushroom and Cheese bun - Okay-ish, I think they used a multi grain dough for the bun that I wasnt a fan of. Spinach and Kale Danish - SO much nostalgia from the Orange County days, lol. This was my absolute fav and I highly recommend it Lemon cupcakes - Ragz loved them, they were very light and fluffy, not very lemony. French Garlic Cheese - Very mild flavored, but tasty. Garlic Cheese Bread - VERY garlicky, but so delicious I cannot recommend this spot enough - I think I may make a trip back so I can lug some carby goodness back with me to DC!

BECAREFUL WITH THIS PLACE. The customer service is zero. The price is pricey but the cake quality is poor. I bought the birthday cake for my husband ( coffee cream brÃ»lÃ©e) the coffee cream taste like medicine, very strong bitter taste. I drinks coffee & I know how coffee taste. This is not the taste of coffee. I called & speak with the manager ( her name is Edna) & she not try to accommodate me with anything. She said nothing she can't do that is just the way the cake tastes. Becareful with this business. This is my first time & it's going to be my last time order cake from this 85 degree bakery shit. We only eat the strawberry & try the cream & we throw almost the whole cake away.

As soon as I heard that an 85c Bakery would be opening in Vegas I was stoked!! However unlike the 85c in California which always has what you need in stock until it sells out, this one unfortunately is hit or miss. I'm a very big fan of their egg tarts and green tea bun with chocolate filling, but the Vegas location is very hit or miss with the menu. Some days they'll have the pastries you want, some day's they don't. Overall the California location is much better when it comes to consistency, but taste-wise, both locations are on par. As of now I believe this place is a solid 3 star solely due to the fact that the pastries are inconsistent and the service isn't the greatest.
I bought mango and strawberry cake with some others . I love them all . I wish we live closer so I can come here often .
Great pastries but they need more baker or staff or something always have to wait for the things I want

What a surprise drive to Chinatown with the family! Whoohoo, great galore of pastries and drinks! Pick your own selections and order your drink. Then your all set and ready to go! Their milk donut is the best! We've gotta come back again for sure!

Hailing from Southern California, I'm well versed in 85 bakery since their first one opened in Irvine more than ten years ago. Came by before I realized they even had their grand opening so I realize they're still ironing things out. However, the Hawaiian chicken that I got lacked toppings. Their cakes, however, are on point. I didn't give them five stars due to the poor customer service. I understand that they're still in soft opening phase but the drink I received was wrong from the one I ordered/reflected on my receipt. When I pointed it out, the man serving drinks tried to lie and say that they only charged me for the regular mountain green tea when I was clearly charged 3.45 for the sea salt mountain green tea. Additionally, it listed "SSALT MT" instead of apologizing, he took my drink and just added sea salt on top despite it being already cold so the consistency won't be right. It's supposed to be milk tea-esque and mix when it's hot so I was very disappointed. I saw that they were very busy so I didn't push the issue further but it's something they can work on- apologizing to the customer when they've made a mistake!

Went to the grand opening today on Friday, 12/6/19. Headed there by 815am and there was a line about 50 people. Luckily it wasn't too cold that 45 minutes waiting did feel bad. I got the ticket for the free yard tea which I choose was jasmine tea. When 9am hit, the unlv cheerleaders did a small performance, ribbon cutting, and red good luck streamers came down. By 9am the line was all the way down to the bbq place. Line went quick to get in and it was pretty organized. The main items were there, however not full menu they had. Only gripe was it was crowded getting thru with the fresh bread getting refilled. Make sure you look at every item so you don't have to fight the crowd going back. Because I got the tea, I didn't get my usual boba definitely will going back. Now I don't have to drive to So Cal !
Jasmine Milk Tea was warm milk with a hint of tea, so if that is how "hot" their drinks are, I will pass on them in the future. However, the breads & pastries are the definite star here.

Love this place Only problem this place has that they have to bag each items one by one when you get to the counter that's why the line goes so long Suggesting .. cashier needs to have some assistant bagger when its busy idk .. so it can go quick as possible.. Just the line sucks that's all everything is good ..

I would have given it 4 stars.... this is why I am giving it 3. ZERO control over social distancing, the line to pay was stacked up and there was no social distancing (6 feet is the standard) they were 2 feet apart WTF....... They need to control how many people are in there at a time, not hard.... just limit 10 customers in the business at a time. There isn't any excuse for that. Also, the they are slow as hell ringing people up and the guy over charged us. Simple math too, how many items price per item.... The wait in line is unacceptable for the amount of staff, get people moving, be more efficient getting the drinks out.

My daughter & I stopped by on a Sunday during their soft opening. It was our first time. Even though it was busy things went smoothly and lines went fairly quick. The only thing that ruined it were inconsiderate customers. They would constantly block the way of staff trying to bring out fresh bread & pastries or would get out of line (instead of waiting until they reached that area) to get bread & pastries making it difficult and squishy for everyone. There were also those who would start grabbing from staff trays as they walked by. So rude! Despite all of that, staff remained professional, friendly and helpful. Everything that we ordered was delicious! Breads & pastries were nice & soft. Milk tea was nice and mild with just the right amount of sweetness. Definitely a place we will visit often :) Overall a great asian bakery that lives up to the hype.

Haven't been to this bakery for 2 years since I moved out from San Diego. We don't have that bakery where I currently live. All type of cakes you can think of, plus tea/milk tea or coffee. It was very busy when we went in. Shortly after that, there was one worker had to standby at the door to make sure not so many people in the bakery due to social distancing. Asian style bakery, quite similar to what I usually buy when I was in my home country too.Wish I could bring home more cakes and bread.

I absolutely loved 85 degree bakery whenever I went to California to get baked goods. I was really excited when they built one here in Las Vegas last year. I went to the opening and a few times after that, and everything was great. Today was the first time I decided to order a cake for my brother's birthday. Very disappointed. I ordered a cake along with a caramel pudding, lemon mini cakes, and large pudding milk tea with boba last night for a pick up this morning. My mother went to go pick it up today. When my mother went there this morning, the person at the counter said they don't have the order. She explained we ordered online and showed the picture. Then, they came back and said they can't find it. They went back to check 3 times and finally said that they would prepare the order. The guy asked if we wanted the drink with boba and the guy said they would have to charge for the boba. My mother asked "how do you know she didn't pay for the boba?" The guy said "because I saw in the order she didn't pay for it." My mother then pulled out the screenshot I had sent her that showed I paid for the boba. It literally says everything there in the email receipt that I did pay for the boba. The guy didn't bother double checking and assumed we didn't pay for it. He was about to charge us extra even though they first said they couldn't see the order and then was about to charge us for the boba because apparently "we didn't pay for the boba." I find that absolutely ridiculous. How are you going to say that we didn't pay for something when you couldn't even find the order in the first place? I loved the baked good, but the customer service needs a lot of work. Also what is the point of ordering in advance when they can't bother to have it ready for you? Isn't the point of ordering in advance to be able to walk in and have it picked up instead of having to wait for the order to be made once you are there? If they don't bother checking the online orders, then don't accept it through online! Or you know, if you are going to set up a system to order in advance, then check it! Very frustrating experience.

We've been on the search for a good bakery that offers good, fresh baked goods. We stumbled upon this place after our adventure from the hot dogs. They just opened not too long ago but still had a pretty decent sized line outside. We didn't know what to expect but a line out the door to get in we thought was a good sign right? When you get in, you immediately smell the freshness of baked goods. They have multiple casings with different baked options and also have similar options in multiple casings. So if it's out in one casing it could be in another. There were sooo many options I don't know where to begin or say. Everything was fresh and you can get things from fresh baked bread to tarts to taro flavored small loads and cranberry cream cheese roll. Our favorite was the chocolate mocha loaf and taro loaf! We only got 6 items and are sad we only got 6. We found out they're also in California which we will be there soon so we're going to be stocking up. People are 50/50 about the pricing but we think it's definitely worth it!!
Coffee is great. Addicted to sea salt coffee. Service is fast and location isn't bad. Parking lot is crowded but I always find parking close by.

This was such a cute and convenient place to pick up treats and drinks! We stopped by this morning and grabbed some pastries (milk pudding bun, coffee-flavored cake and more). We also ordered a smoothie, americano and salted caramel coffee. We ate inside; everything was clean, staff were super friendly and the atmosphere was really great.

Located in Shanghai Plaza with a lot of other Asian businesses and eateries. If you like carbs, you'll like this place. I had to summon all my restraint and willpower to not try one of everything. Everything looks delicious behind those glass display containers (and it is as I write this review and eat em!) they serve coffee, tea, and boba, so it's a convenient 1-stop shop for snacking.

I'm so happy to see that there's finally an 85C Bakery here in LV! My fiancÃ© and I had our first taste of their baked goods whenever we travelled to SoCal. The pastries were so tasty that we always made sure to bring some back home with us. We tried to stop in one night when they first opened and there was a huge line that was nearly out the door. So after that, we decided to wait till the crowds died down. We finally stopped in this morning and the bakery wasn't crowded at all. I definitely recommend stopping by in the morning when it's not super packed. This bakery is arranged as a grab and go. Once you walk in, simply grab a tray, liner, and tongs and start grabbing any of the baked goods you want. When you're done, just pay in the front with one of the cashiers and they'll bag it for you. It's super easy and quick! They have a large selection of sweet and savory items to choose from. Some of our favorites were the sausage roll, milk custard bun, and mango custard bun. We even picked up a package of coconut snow cubes in the refrigerated section of the bakery, which was pretty good. In addition, they have a display of other sweet treats (such as cakes, tarts, cookies, etc) and milk tea/coffee. We haven't tried any of their drinks yet but it's definitely on our list to try next time. This place is a wonderful addition to LV. With the friendly service and delicious pastries, we will be sure to come back again and again.

So happy to have ran into this location while visiting Vegas. We have this bakery back home in San Diego so I was so glad to have found one . I called my order ahead of time and picked it up the same day .

85C Coffee was so sweet, I took two sip and threw it away. There was no mention that this coffee would be so sweet. I was assuming it a high end regular coffee. Cake that I ate was not my favorite type of whip cream. It was too much buttery. I like pure whip cream cake which I'm still searching for good bakery.

After my stop at O.Onigiri next door, I had to try this bakery. I remember the long lines when it first opened so I stayed away. It was breeze yesterday. When you enter you take a tray. I didn't and I wondered why so many others were doing so. I soon found out why. People load their trays with Asian style buns and other bakery treats. I got two buns--a mangotale and a berrytale. I picked up a guava cheese danish like pastry and I got a chocolate cookie crumble from the refrigerator case. The buns are large in diameter and are very soft with only a small amount of sweetener. The guava cheese and the chocolate crumble were the best of what I got. While the items were good, they didn't give me a reason to go back and I couldn't understand the long lines when there are other bakeries with better fare. It was worth a try but I see no reason to return.

Finally 85c bakery in Las Vegas! :D This place was one of my favorite places to go when I lived in Cali, so many asian style bread and sea salt cream drinks. Bread and drinks here are above average taste (at least to me) and also price is reasonable. This time I bought 4 bread and a fresh strawberry milk tea and it was like 12 bucks, which I think it's reasonable in the price wise. The store is also clean, spacious, and modernly decorated! Be aware that there might be a huge line when you come around lunch time in weekends.

85 degrees is a Taiwanese bakery/cafe chain with stores all over the country. This location has a decent selection of baked goods, both sweet and savoury. My favourites are the boroh cream danish (kinda like a soboro bun with milk butter/custardy filling), marble taro bread, and egg tarts. I also tried the drinks at the recommendation of my boyfriend, and so far, I've liked everything. The sea salt caramel coffee is sweet and creamy, and something I'd drink even though I hate the taste of coffee. The sea salt chocolate milk tea is my favourite though -- it's a milk tea with chocolate chips (which are supposed to melt and give off the chocolate flavour I'm assuming?) with the sea salt cream topping. Service is friendly and it seems clean and well kept-up. Overall, a great spot to pick up coffee/snacks!

The customer service sucks. They overcharged my food when I only bought 4 items and not 6. When I went to get a refund, they charged me again instead of refunding the money they owe me back. I once again, have to go back in the store to ask for a refund and finally this time I ask them to refund it with dollar bills instead of doing it through a card which they did. If you do indeed go here and buy their food, make sure to check your receipt so you don't get overcharged.

Bought a cake for my sister's birthday 3 days ago. We always buy cakes and bread from them but I think I'd stop buying from them. We found a fingernail in the cake we bought and because of that we had to throw away the cake. We ate a slice before we found it, and was totally grossed out.

This is bread heaven. All the bread flavors are good- Taro, milk pudding, coffee, choco, matcha, strawberry, cheese, red bean, mango, blueberry, EVERYTHING. The only flavor I witnessed someone disliking was the Milk tea flavor since it had chewy tapioca inside. I thought it was good and interesting, but the texture weirded her out. Because of covid, the bread in the display cases are already individually packaged instead of being packaged at the register. I'm praying to god they continue doing so because it makes the process of paying so much faster. I think that's one of the main reasons the line sometimes extends out the door.

This has become my favorite cafe since they opened one close to where I live. If you haven't been there I would really recommend you to just go and try it out. Their bakery items are soooo good! They are fresh out of the oven! They have so many vegetarian options (without egg) like the jalapeÃ±o bread, choco bread, cookie bun, garlic bread, etc. I really like the milk tea and coffee over there. I didn't even realize it was made with soy milk . I never knew I liked soy milk. But definitely give it a try if you are like me who doesn't like soy milk.

You must try this place! I'm glad I did and can't wait to try more goodies from this place. My first try was an egg tart from here--heavenly custard!! It was so tasty and smooth with a perfect flaky crust. Oh. My. God. And, it's size? Perfect! A great treat to cap off a busy day. I'm definitely going to be back to try their coffee and other bakery items. A++++ all around!

I was super excited when I heard they were opening a location in Vegas. My first time was in California and I fell in love with it. Since then, I've been to their locations in Seattle and Hong Kong. Today was their soft opening and it did not disappoint. I loaded up my tray with all the delicious goodies from egg tarts, puff pastries and various buns. I felt like I was in a candy store all over again lol. You can see the staff members just restocking the fresh goods as it comes out from the oven. Everything tasted so good and freshly made. I didn't get a chance to order any drinks but next time for sure! I'll definitely be doing frequent stops here for coffee and delicious goods. If you never been or heard of this place, then you are missing out on some good eaten.

I didn't know about this place until a bunch of my friends were excited to go. I went about a week after opening around 7pm. There was an outside line and then an inside line to pay. Together it took about 2 hours. It was insane but it's not really their fault. I seriously hope that the line gets better because I really want to go back The thing that shocked me the most is that I actually don't like sweet bread. Honestly I would say that I extremely dislike sweet breads. My mom buys conchas and pastries a lot and I just don't enjoy sweet things. I just got a few things from here because it was so popular and I wanted to try them. But I was completely shocked that I didn't just like everything but I ate all of it. I'm not really sure what is in their bread because they all just tasted so good. They must do something different than any other bakery I have gone to. But I got a few different to try and I liked every single one. They are also not that pricey. I was definitely expecting it to be more around $1-$3 each. I got the taro bread that is very popular. It was very good. I also got the mushroom bread because I wanted to taste the savory breads as well. Funny enough it ended up being my least favorite (still good though) but I've never picked something sweet over something savory. My favorite so far was the mangotale. It has cream cheese that tastes like mango inside. That was probably my favorite sweet bread I have had in my entire life. I really want to go taste some more. I wanted to try the hot dog and curry bread but they were out. I'll wait a bit more to go and I hope I can taste them all.

When I went on Thursday night (around 5:30pm-ish) to ask if I could preorder the breads because I was bringing some pastries back to my hometown, there was a fairly short line. Unfortunately, I was told by one of the workers that I could not pre-order the breads. So, I had to go early in the morning on Friday and I was like the second person in-line waiting for the doors to open at 7am. I was there until 10am bc I had to wait for some breads to be done baking. However, while I was waiting there was a good amount of people coming in and out and the line to check out was pretty long but there was a worker bagging all the pastries to make the process go faster. Overall, the customer service was awesome. The workers were kind enough to help me get my big order together. Definitely will be back! P.S. I was told that they'll be expanding one of their stores in Henderson. Then, they'll be planning to put 3 more of their stores up

Every time I've passed this restaurant, there has been a line outside of at least 10 people. So I had high expectations going in. Overall, the prices are very fair but the actual product is just okay and definitely not worth the long wait. When you walk in, you grab a tray and tongs, line your tray with paper, then grab what you want from the little cube displays. There were people with trays overflowing with buns, breads, everything in the store. I'm talking 20 things on one tray! I only got a garlic cheese bread, milk pudding and a choco bun. My total was $5, so very reasonable. I liked everything I got, but it wasn't phenomenal and I was expecting phenomenal. After you fill up your tray, you stand in line to check out. Luckily I only had 3 items so my tray wasn't that heavy, but it was still a pain to hold it for the 15 minutes I was in line. The line moved slowly. There were 2 cashiers but during the checkout process, they individually bag every item. If you have 3-4 items, it's not too bad, but when they're having to bag 15-20 items per customer, it takes forever! Price: 4 stars Experience: 2 stars Food: 3 stars

So glad their issues were resolved and we can come back and get some of their very missed baked goods! We got a little bit of everything this time and tried the new boba roll (its very unique and delicious). We also saw their new holiday cakes and can't wait to preorder them for Christmas time! Also, there are a few people complaining about there only being a few items left near the end of the day. Not sure how you think a bakery works but, stop with entitlement and get there early if you want the good stuff.

85° keep doing this, why open for business only to have a few dozens bread items available at 5pm on a Saturday? This happens too often, management need to step up. And today Sea Salt for their teas were also out, ordered one anyways and I wished I hadnt. I live far from Chinatown and my kids look forward to eat their eggtarts and blueberry muffins, only to be disappointed.

We got the strawberry cream square ($3.20), coconut twist pastry ($2.05) and the bag of 3 chocolate chip cookies ($3.30). The strawberry cream square was just ok, but it's expensive for such a small square of cake. The coconut twist pastry was just ok too, better can be found at Sunville Bakery. I had the biggest complaint with the chocolate chip cookies, which was horrible with the large cinnamon flavor in the cookies! The cookies didn't have any buttery flavor with the chocolate chips and the cookies were hard and crispy, where I prefer crispy outside and chewy inside.

I have tried a variety of breads here as well as in California and wasn't really a huge fan and would say it's a hit or miss depending on what you get. The price point is amazing, and the bread is fresh. I feel the variety is limited compared to the Cali locations and they tend to have a repeat of the same breads on the other side of the bakery. The cakes or a no-go for me. The cream cheese filled breads I like, but I'm also a huge cream cheese fan. Lines go by quickly.
They have a chocolate bun that is too good. My mom even liked this bakery and she's a hard sell.

My little family stopped here after dinner for some dessert. It is in a plaza area and is super busy and crowded. This location is a lot smaller than the other ones I have been to when in California. I was looking for coconut butter bread (I think that is what it is called) or anything close to it and this location didn't have any. Tried a Boba drink for the first time....and it was pretty good. I would recommend the Iced Bobba Latte.

Visited here today to get a gift card and see what kind of pastries were in stock. I've experienced this bakery in SoCal and San Francisco. Fell in love with the super soft breads. This location was very packed when it first opened and pastries were flying off the shelves. We already know our favorites and we weren't sure if it they had them here because we didn't se them. That was a little disappointing. Today's visit tbough, was much better. We were able to get our faves, white choco strawberry, taro puff pastry, chocolate cream and berrytale. Those are just a few...I did not see the Hokkaido cheese tart. I think that's what its called...they had the regular egg tart, the Hokkaido is a little more fluffy and flaky. They also have another cheese filled bun but it was not there, I'm not sure if some of these are seasonal, but we got enough for now. I usually don't get the drinks or cakes here. But my daughter tried the sea salt oolong milk tea with lychee boba. She really enjoyed it. They have a rewards program also. Just have to download the app. All the workers also announce when fresh patries are being brought out.

This bakery is amazing!!!!! their Deluxe Strawberry Cream is amazing, the whip cream is light and soft. The strawberry is a little bit tart and with the whip cream sweet taste, matches well just right! I love this bakery! If you haven't tried the bakery, go try it. Definitely recommend!

If you are carbphobic, stay away! More for me! =D Along with their variety of baked items, they also make cakes and coffee. The kids working at 85 haul ass making sure items are stocked and no one leave hangry. Tip appropriately. The line may get long but moves efficiently. People, use a tray if you must hoard delicious baked goods.
The pastries at this place are diverse and tasty if I were being honest. I believe this is great spot! In a very popular shopping center as well! So it feels full all the time!

FINALLY went & checked out 85's Las Vegas location! And I am so glad I went. We went on a Sunday, right around 5:30pm and it was PACKED! But they have a simple system in place to keep the lines moving in an organized fashion. One of the items I specifically went in for (the Marble Taro) was out on the shelves & I was soooo bummed. Then I spotted it at the front, FRESH, straight outta the oven goodness & asked one of the workers if I could snag a couple and she was quick to help me out. They are managed so well with such orchestrated precision to make your experience well worth your time. The quality of products, the excellent customer service & the affordability is just fire !!

FINALLY, a decent Asian bakery in Vegas. I've been to multiple 85C bakeries in SoCal and this is one of the bigger ones in my own personal experience. The variety in the evening is pretty subpar, but this place is legitimately so busy that it wasn't a surprise. By the time I got there, they were probably running low on everything. The fact they probably are still adjusting, as they have only been open for roughly half a year, didn't help on that front. Taste-wise is consistent with other bakeries in the chain, which is good! I thought that the service was fairly fast for the number of people waiting. Despite the baked goods being low in variety, I'm so happy to have a place to go get goods and SALTED CREAM COFFEE. A Happy Lemon opened down the road, but didn't have coffee options I've seen at other locations, so I'm especially happy for the drink options. 4/5 only because I didn't get to experience the variety available at other locations, but I'm sure they will eventually adjust and be able to provide more options or more of some of the more popular options and less repeats of less popular options. This bakery, along with the whole plaza, is nice and clean. Employees are friendly and work hard. Definitely going to return. :)

freaking love this place!!!! All their breads are so delicious and fresh. My favorites are the garlic cheese bread and the mango custard bread. Their drinks are delish too! I would recommend the peach green tea or jasmine green tea or salted caramel coffee. All my favorites! I haven't had any of their desserts but I'm sure they are just as good. The employees are always so sweet too!

This place is amazing. I have never been disappointed in any aspect, from products to service. The marble taro loaf is incredible! So many different items to choose from that are absolute delicious. Love, love, love the egg tarts! And the prices are incredibly reasonable. I usually stuff a box full of different breads and never spend more than $23. I really wish this franchise came further east than the CA/NV area. At certain times of day, be prepared for a line out the door. It's best to get there early before 9am. Otherwise the place gets so packed it's hard to move around inside with your tray and tongs. Enjoy the "FRESH BREAD!" and get out of their way when you hear it, because they're comin' in hot!

I love 85C before I even had them. I think it's because all my Cali friends brag about having them. Well thank you for opening one in Vegas. It sure live up to the reputation. Pastry and bread are so good and cost is very low compared to other bakery around town. I got the strawberry dipped in chocolate for V-day holiday and a cranberry cheese bread!! So yummy. This is like the 12th time me and my hubs have been here. Service is average but the food speaks volumes. The line system can be better tho.

I was so excited to finally see 85 coming to Vegas! Unfortunately my last visit left me missing the california locations. Most of the staff is new so they are really slow in packaging the items and checking out customers. I noticed one cashier had to constantly stop and ask what code was for each item. I understand it's a newly open shop but it was almost ridiculous how much time they'd spent chatting or doing other things before taking the next customer. The lines were out the door and there were only 2 cashiers servicing the entire night. As for the food, it's 85! It was tasty but not worth standing in a line for. I'm glad they're open but there's a lot of room for improvement.

Really excited they are open in Vegas!!! I love, love this place. They are still in thier soft opening so they are still ironing out all the kinks. When we went it was lets just say a rough experience. The pastry shelves were mostly empty but they were bringing out pastries just slowly. They ladies bringing them out were also bringing out the samethings so they had to keep going back. Not sure if they dont know whats on the shelves already or not but maybe an idea to figure out so they dont bring "fresh bread" out just to turn around and bring it back to the kitchen. The line to check out was extremely slow but you could tell the cashiers didnt really know what they were doing. We stood in line for almost 30 min just to check out. I will still be back, just might wait till the grand opening Dec 6!

So the long wait is finally over--85c Bakery Cafe has opened up shop in Las Vegas and we were thrilled to see that they had a soft opening today until 5 pm (Grand Opening on Dec. 6th). Me and my wife immediately grabbed a tray and selected a few of our favorite freshly made breads and pastries. Of course, the 85c experience isn't complete without their famous sea salt iced coffee (which you can order unsweetened). The soft launch staff is adequately prepared and the bakery is abundantly stocked and continuously churning out fresh bread just like the well-oiled 85c machine we've grown accustomed to in California. So far there's no long lines, probably because people aren't aware that the cafe-bakeshop is open. It's a glorious day for Vegas foodies indeed and we'll definitely be visiting regularly.

This was my first time here at the new location located at the new Shanghai plaza in China town Las Vegas NV. I came here around 2:30 pm to 3:00 pm and WOW the parking lot throughout the plaza was packed and was hard to find parking. Luckily I was able to find parking within less than 10 mins. This 85 Bakery it's somewhat smaller than others i've been to but bigger it's not better. When I came in the store it was packed and they had all ready people in line outside waiting to come in. So I got a few things for my hotel and all I can say it's way better than the ones at San Jose CA. I didn't take any pictures for this trip because most asians that comes here they know what 85 Bakery specialize in. 85 Bakery got very good baked goods & drinks but their customer service and policies not too much. First of all if customers wants to buy a stupid box let them buy a stupid box and just set it to a fair price for them how hard is that. 2nd note to some customers nothing in life is free so you gotta remember that too even though you spend a lot. I just hope some rules would be change or made to service customers better in the future. Also just short note all of my breads I bought today tasted so fresh and so good especially the Berrytale. Thanks 85 Bakery for the delicious breads and i'm super glad that you're near the strip in Las Vegas NV and please remember Quality not over Quantity. See you guys next time Happy Holidays and be safe everyone.

Decided to stop by and check it out because I'm craving for the chocolate creme cheese bread. Since it's still soft opening they have very limited items. No mocha bread, no taro bread, all my faves were out. Stopped by 11.27 and got a couple of breads and a chocolate hot tea. At that time there was a long line inside and out and they were only letting a couple of people in. It was utterly sweet! There was curds of chocolate, I ended up having to toss it out. I know they are on training but come on, when you stir it you can see the curds of chocolate. I cant understand why they would serve it. Hopefully with this review they'll take it to account and make their items the correct way. I love 85 degrees and I cant wait for it to fully be operational and be up to the same consistency as the ones in Cali.

The line was long, but the bakery's were yummy!!! I would give 5/5. The drinks were good. I would give 4/5 If only the line was not long, I would rate this just a little higher than 3. I would have given it a 4.

So amazing! When you walk in you grab a tray and pick any pastry you want. You can order cake or drinks at the touch screen stand or when you check out with your pastries. Will definitely be going back!

Early Bird gets the Worm!!! Planned on meeting up with my friend at 85 degree's at 8:30 am this Sunday morning however, the crowd beat us no fear we got our Fresh breads and pastries from sweet to savory! Hearing and reading all about 85 degrees bakery on how amazing it is and folks the information is true and it blew me away. Upon entering, immediately to your right you grab a Tray and Tong, Pick your bread of sweet and savory of your choice and line up with items to pay at the cashier. Also, you will see a kiosk which you can order slices of desserts or a whole cake also you can just order once your at the cashier. Every time the staff says " Fresh Bread" my eyes go immediately to one of the staff that is carrying fresh items from the back which makes it harder to leave the selection area because you want the "Fresh Bread" coming out of the oven. So far, I tried the Berrytale and it was love at first bite! OMG! Light and Fluffy and as you get deeper you will hit the bottom of a surprise and delight of a texture like cheesecake. Second Favorite it the Curry Bun. The bun was very light with a subtle of crisp and gets soft as you bit into it and you hit the curry filling. Loving Every bite!! I cant wait to try the desserts and other sweet and savory breads that 85C degrees has to offer.

01/16/2021....went around 1230pm. Started off with a line outside. Covid precautions in place with masks and social distancing. Got in and not much of a selection as before. A little disappointing but their sea salt ice coffee was good. Not much to say but they kept the store clean, staff are friendly, and pastries was good. Nothing to WOW about now! Happy eats yelpers!!

Check your receipt!Check your receipt!Check your receipt! Different price when you check out! And cashier will add some products you didn't buy. If you don't check the receipt, you will unconsciously overcharge. I've been cheated twice by them with this trick. The first time I found it after I got home. The second time I found it after I checked out. It can be seen that they always using this trick.

TAIPEI BAKERY EMPIRE 85° C BAKERY is mastering the bake industry like a monster typhoon. Huge dominance in So-Cal and now has moved north on I-95 anchoring itself as a foodie hot spot in Chinatown's Shanghai Plaza Las Vegas. Its actually a big bakery shop, but dine-in section is closed for good reasons. The area where you personally select your pasteries is a free for all zone without any observance for social distancing. Sorta like a mob after a storm when all the fish are washed a shore. It was a scene from a Charlie Chaplin fire drill. Then you get in a queue to pay, and it's stand apart with four feet spacing. The cashiers are spaced even closer. Thank goodness everyone is respectfully masked. I choose five pasteries and three I would buy again and again. But I'm not going to compromise my health with their current methodology of social spacing. I cannot say I didn't try this 85°C.

Smaller than the 85 C I'm used to but honestly had a very great selection! There were actually a couple items that I hadn't seen before. Line can be kinda long depending on when you go and I wish they could somehow space the bread display things more effectively so everyone isn't back to back. One of the people I was with had never had it before so we obviously had to get some of my favorites like the Boroh Bun (aka Pineapple Bun) aka a sweet fluffy normal bun topped a cookie like crust that's shaped like a pineapple with the criss crosses. The one filled with cream is also very good. I also like the milk custard bun with the heart on it! The egg tarts are also very good here.

Jason was so welcoming! I had a good experience here. He was the only one at register, which was a bit concerning especially since there was a line, but he was trying his best and it made my day. He was connecting w other customers and made sure each one was taken cared for.

All my favorite Cali places are finally in Vegas; 85°C being one of them. It's only a 25 minute drive from my place; much better than the 4 hours. Yay!! Now for the pros and cons list to make things easier for me and for anyone reading this. Pros: 1. Of course all the delicious, soft and fluffy baked goods. My favorites are the brioche, boroh danish, taro swirl bun, Hokkaido cheese tart and coconut twist. And the bf likes all the savory ones; jalapeÃ±o and cream cheese, hot dog buns, spicy sausage and ham and cheese. 2. Due to COVID-19, all the pastries are already wrapped individually. I find this a lot easier than the old way. With things already wrapped, you're not waiting forever at the register for the cashier with their dirty hands to wrap all your pastries one by one. 3. I loooove their coffee with sea salt foam!! It's so good and gives you a nice boost for your day. Cons: 1. It's located in Chinatown. I hate Chinatown. People can't drive and Spring Mountain is terrible. It's located in a new busy plaza so good luck finding a parking spot during the weekend. 2. Why is this place soooo tiny?!? All the other locations I've been to in Cali have been much bigger and spacious. With all the money they make, you'd think they could afford bigger real estate. 3. Speaking of small spaces, forget about social distancing. With customers constantly moving around looking at all the bread, you're literally standing next to someone all the time. And of course there's that one customer who has no sense of their surroundings and takes 19 years to move out of the way. 4. The line gets long really quick, and of course, the not-so-smart customer doesn't know where to go and cuts in front of everyone. Why are people so clueless?!?! *sighs in exasperation Of course I'll make the drive to the dreaded Chinatown for this place. And if you're not a fan of 85°, that's fine by me. Less people in my way. Thanks bye!

I can't wait for this place is opened in Vegas & they made it. It is one of my favorite place in California with so many location. They are always busy. They have so many bakeries which are hot & fresh made. I came here for birthday cake & bakeries. Everything is so tasty! I always get a good experience with the birthday cake from this bakery. Highly recommend !

I absolutely love this bakery! I love it so much, I've gone twice this week. Let me say this bakery is a little far from where I'm staying but so worth the commute!! There are so many pastries to choose from, from sweet to savory! There is a kiosk to order from to make things go faster because this Place is always jammed packed with a long line! I am impressed with how decadent the desserts cakes are! They aren't too sweet and you get the full effect of whatever flavor the cake is supposed to be! I've had the deluxe strawberry cake twice this week and I'll have it more if I lived here! Delicious! Two thumbs up!!
The bread was okay . But the drink it's so nasty . Try twice and it's so dissapointed . I will be back for the bread but not for the drink !
My second time visiting. Loved the berry bun thing the best. The cake portion of the mango cake seemed a little dry. But it was not too sweet which was great.

This place is so cute! Not only is the ambience great, but everything I tried here was so yummy! There were mixed reviews that I read before coming here, but I still wanted to give this place a try. My roommate and I came here around 9pm and they still had a bunch of pastries out; both sweet and savory! Everything was so fluffy and fresh. I couldn't finish all the pastries we purchased, but they were still soft after a few days. Check this place out!
The business hour says they are open till 10 pm. I went there 9 pm and 8:30 pm in two nights. Both of times, they had nothing. Change your biz hours then !!!!

OMG! I love 85C!! This place is always busy and there is a reason for that! Every single item I have gotten here was outstanding! Be ready to stand in a line at any time of day here. It's worth the wait!

Location: Spring Mountain Rd / Wynn Rd (Shanghai Plaza) The new location is still in their soft opening, so it is a MESS! Instead of spacing out their pastries throughout the store displays against the wall, they choose to put them in the front display cases ONLY. Food options: all of the usual items weren't readily available, but I'd definitely come back after a month or so. Hopefully they'll work out the kinks by then.

They technically close at 10pm today. It is currently 7:30 now. The picture is no exaggeration. I asked if they are still baking some pastries to make this visit worth it & we will wait. Unfortunately, they are not refilling the shelves anymore. Not sure if the opening last friday was a "soft opening" but this is just very disappointing. They hyped this place soo much and they should have prepared even better.

I cannot put in words how excited I was to find out that 85'C was opening in my city. I checked frequently and even had people notify me when it was officially opened. I would have wanted to attend the grand opening but was able to get in soon after. It was a bit hectic everyone wanted to be there. But overall managed to get almost everything I wanted excited milk pudding (which is a swirl bread with vanilla custard inside) and I usually get multiples of those to go. Service was efficient despite how busy it was and I look forward to going back. I'm glad now that a trip to 85'C doesn't involve trekking all the way to LA. The bread side is a little smaller than what I remember but would love to see more options as the bakery continues to grow. I have high hopes as 85'C rarely disappoints

85°C is a regular stop for me when visiting SoCal. I'm so happy that they made their way to Vegas! I attended the grand opening several weeks ago and have been back a few times since then. During my first couple of visits, the selection was not too great because the bakery was very busy, but the staff are getting their routine down and everything was well-stocked during my last visit. The employees are friendly and helpful. I haven't tried anything that I didn't like. It's a win for me!
Love this place !!! Love the cake bread Drink !! Especially the cake!! Tastes so good

Awful. Dining experiences are more than food. It's the overall; treatment, wait, friendliness, etc. 1) Why would you only leave two cashiers up front when there's a line 20 people deep? (From earlier review) 2) Why did the kid making my vanilla latte have a problem making me a half-caf? 3) Why is the back room so ice-cold? 4) Why is the service so sub-average? 5) Why did I come back? - A) Inexpensive pastries - B) decent product. ... But I stand firm on

I am so happy that they finally brought 85° into the Las Vegas area. The pastries and cakes here are so delicious and bring a hint of Asia to our little tourist town. From their jalapeno cream cheese bread to the taro bread to the milk buns and egg tarts, You can't really go wrong when you come here. If you like salt then maybe you want to try the sea salt coffee but I normally go with an iced Americano. What's even better is that they box everything up and put them in individual little bags which allow them to stay fresher and keeps the taste! If you have a birthday coming up they have some pretty sweet cakes too and delicious tiramisu! It's kind of loud and packed here normally because it's so good so I would caution you that you might find all the tables occupied if you're looking to sit down. If you haven't been here you probably should and it's in the new Shanghai plaza with some cool little restaurants nearby. Obviously with what's going on now everything is pretty much take out and you'll still be happy leaving this delicious establishment.
This place smells so bad for a bakery. You'd think as soon as you walk in you'll smell fresh pastry but no, it smells like gutter! Unacceptable

I was hoping 85 bakery to open in Las Vegas for a long time, and it's finally here! I have been here five times since it was opened. I will probably coming here everyday If it's closer to my home. My favorites are taro marble, salted butter, taro danish, and lemon cupcakes. They tasted the best when you consume within one day. Their drinks are also good and prices are very reasonable. I wish they could open another location in the other side of the town.

This is the 1st time I have been to this bakery. I believe it is Taiwanese owned. They make a fresh bread every day. They have smoothie options, boba iced teas, and coffee. I was bot happy with the strawberry milk tea that was one of their bew options but they ended up making me something else. I ender up with the peach jasmine green tea and i was pleased with that. I love oolong tea so i was disappointed when I found out they did not have oolong. However taro bread made up for it. The breads are not too sweet. The price is great. I will definitely return. Below I have posted some pictures of the bakery. They also offer different types of cakes.

I don't recommend this specific location. I'm from Seattle and so far I only like that location unfortunately. One of the employees was so disrespectful, I don't like writing negative reviews but it was uncalled for and each time I come here it's always negative. I genuinely hope they get better because I love 85 and due to me not being in Seattle this is the only location I can get to

I've been going here since the soft opening and all I can say it's ok. The bakery is a hit or miss depending on the day you visit. It is limited with the breads they have and every time I come here and most things run out very fast. I'm a big fan of fruit tarts and the berry one they have here is ok. The last time I came here, I was impressed with the Fresh Strawberry Milk Tea because whenever I see this at other places I am hesitant to try it. I'm afraid it might taste like Nesquik! LOL. Surprisingly, this drink hit the taste buds on the right spot. It included strawberry bits which is a bonus. The rest of their milk teas honestly just taste like half and half milk, which I am not a fan of. Also, a drink I usually get and love is their iced sea salt coffee! I would recommend this for any coffee lovers, it's not too strong-- it's just the perfect everyday iced coffee with a kick of sea salt creme. If it's a hot day, I recommend to try the iced grapefruit green tea! This place deserves a 3 star.

I mean i understand why people are frustrated because of the long wait times and the poor use of the spacing of tables. But the truth is, you can't beat the price on its pastries and for the stuff you get I it's better than most pastry places. I typically get 3-5 pastries (I don't know the exact names but stuff like Taro bun, the green tea cake slice, the Mushroom bun, and bacon onion bun), and 1-2 drinks (like Tiger Boba, I recently tried the Zebra boba because it was buy 1 get 2nd 50 percent off) and all of that adds up to less than 20. They even help you package the pastries afterwards. I mean yes the wait sucks. But you won't be disappointed knowing you grabbed some great snacks for the next few days. Just remember, don't let small things get in the way of great things like that bite from your pastry!

Wow! Talk about heavenly baked goodness! I love tje smell of baked goods... i couldn't resist! The smell just draws you in... From outside the shop you can smell the yumminess but when you walk in you just get overwhelmed by not only the smell but the shop is full of all the bake goods... I wanted ot all... We walked around at least twice before started to pick out our goodies to take home... The shop itself was very retro and clean... the set up was very easy to follow and well set up... all the staff was busy hustling around stocking, cleaning, or helping customers... For a weekday in the middle of the day was pretty busy but the shelves were constantly being refilled... i had the bacon buns which was really good the bread was so soft and the bacon made it so much more tasty... i also had the strawberry shortcake it was so light and dreamy with the fresh strawberries... yummy! My daughter got the milk bun which is her favourite... oh and the pork bun that was onolishous too... we have to go back for more...
Ordered several pastries, breads, sliced and whole cakes. Never disappointed . I am returning on Saturday for a family dinner party and yes dessert time! They want a Choco mousse cake. Yummy

I love this bakery, my favorite is the milk bun and the drinks. I can't get enough of them. They have so many cute breads and pastries, sometimes I just wanna get so many things but I can't get out of hand. Their dessert selections is awesome too, and they have beautiful cakes. I haven't had them yet but one day I wanna try their cakes.

Had a chance to come in and try 85 degrees. Thank goodness the line wasn't too long but still waited for a decent amount of time. I totally understand why the wait is so long and what else do you expect from a business that's so well known to finally open a location here in Vegas ? Of course it's going to be hectic for about a month or two so it seems unfair to give them a low rating due to "long wait" and "being crowded". It was around 3pm when we arrived and a lot of the pastries were out already. I definitely recommend coming in earlier to score on some of their delicious baked goods. Even though we didn't get to try a whole bunch, what we got was super good ! We also ordered drinks and I have to say that the 85 degrees iced coffee is delicious! Will be back for more. My girlfriend got the iced hazelnut latte and it was a little too sweet. *** If you come in and only want a drink, you can order from the kiosk up front so you don't have to wait in a longer line ! *** Inside is pretty big but the seating area is a bit small. I don't think it will be a good place for a study session but more of a quick casual kind of thing. Overall we did enjoy the pastries and drinks but will probably be back when they start to settle down a bit. Or maybe right when they open !
It's clean and beautiful atmosphere. Pastries are scrumptious and deliciously fresh and yummy.

Been a huge fan of 85c bakery and being from California I was so happy to finally have a location in Las Vegas! The location is overall great! Its very clean and easy to find! Parking was not difficult to find at all! There was a long line, however it was the grand opening so that is bound to happen! Once you are in you are able to order drinks and cake from the kiosk and pay there! Once you pay you get your order number and are able to pick up your drinks! I highly recommend ordering from here ! FYI they do not take credit cards such as American express and discover! They take visa! I highly recommend getting the sea salt caramel with iced! So good! I will definitely come to this location more and hope they causes more 85 degrees in the Las Vegas Area!

If you want to get the best varieties possible go there by 10AM. And I mean by entering the store by 10AM. Because we left the store by 11 and some of the popular items are starting to sold out. since it's grand opening time and they are still new so I'd expect that trend will happen for a while. Their box of egg tarts are pretty good.

From the current soft opening I can say I am IMPRESSED. It blows the other bakeries out of the water. The stuff comes out fresh and it isn't left overnight. All the items and individually wrapped as you are checking out. That way you are taking home pastries that will last and not go stale. Tons of variety of pastries I believe they have a few types of egg tarts lots of buns with filling inside. Green tea buns, cheese cake tarts, plenty of fruit cakes, chocolate moose cake. To many to name as I don't even remember what I ate. BE FOR WARNED they are busy especially as the open up and so far even if you come mid afternoon they can run out of stuff quickly.
Good customer service. Everything smells delicious. We went early so there was lots to choose from. We will be back

Our third visit and the baked goods are still knockouts! This place is always busy, shoulder to shoulder crowds filling their trays with delicious baked goods, cookies, buns and custard tarts...they ran out of the purple yam taro.... Gotta try this place..several times!
We got there at around 9:30 am just as they were bringing out freshly baked goods. We've tried several of their pastries and they were all good, we especially love the guava pastry.

Natalie is phenomenal!!! She helped us pick out pastries based off of our taste preferences. We had been to 85 before, but no one has ever really taken the time to make recommendations and/or give advice. She is the fastest bagger in town. We will definitely be back tomorrow and every day after that!!

I loooovvee this place. I'm so glad they finally made it to Las Vegas! The team is still trying to figure out their groove so the lines are a little long but they have the same long lines in California, too so I'm used to it. They do have a quick check out station at the entrance, so maybe use that. My favourites are the egg custard, taro marble, fruit tart, and the berry tales. Honestly, anything you choose here is going to be scrumptious. If you need a jolt to wake up, I highly recommend the sea salt Carmel coffee. It is beyond words, and cheaper than Starbucks!
I love this place.the pastries and cakes all have natural flavors and awesome textures. I frequent here often :)
The line is sooooooo slow!! Don't come here, service is terrible! 15 mins on line and only let 3 more people inside. They make everyone wait outside while the inside is empty.

Bread is amazing, along with their cold deserts. If I could I'd buy every single one. We tried their drinks and were very delicious. Social distancing and masks were required. Great service. Will be coming back for their tiramisu.
I love this bakery! It's possibly the only bakery I'll ever go to in Vegas, the pastries are delicious and the staff is super nice and welcoming!
I love 85°C! Their baked goods aren't overly sweet and have just the right amount of savory behind them. Their Zebra Oolong Milk Tea is amazing as well and NO DAIRY!

The Taro bread and pastry is sooo delicious! Real taro in the center!! Carmel milk tea was perfect as well, not too sweet. The brioche bread was mouth watering as well! It was light and buttery. We are definitely coming back. Plenty of room to sit, prices are good, quick service, and everything is fresh!!
Long line during grand opening weekend. Continually being restocked with fresh pastries. Would definitely be back. All breads were delicious . Diet just went out the door.

This place was packed!!!! There was a line all the way out to the front door and beyond. It took us about 10 minutes to get to the front of the door. Once inside you get your tray and your utensils to pick up the bread. I got the small bread with the custard and also the frozen angel food cake with strawberry. I wanted their chocolate cream cheese bun which was amazing but they ran out at 1 pm. So I called the next day and they held 6 buns for me. I would recommend the earlier in the morning the better for a good selection.

Got the coffee cake and it has good coffee flavor. Tried my friend's mango cake and it's very refreshing. We didn't get any bread bc that line was too long. But I'm excited that we have one now. Don't have to stop by the ones in SoCal anymore.

We're very excited for this Bakery to be available here in Vegas... Bought few goodies to take home but seems that the filling inside the bread are getting less :( ... My husband ate all my leftover and he seem to like them. He said less sweet and filling is better with his coffee like having regular bread lol!!! But no matter what, we still find ourselves coming back for more bread every other week :) Just wishing someone can monitor guests coming in and have a better well organized place. As you walk in and grab tray, another guest from behind does the same thing and walk in front of you and then another guest and another till you hardly move to pick :(

I was there at the grand opening at 9. got there around 8:00am and was one of the first 25 people . They had UNLV cheerleaders to cheer and had a great opening. The bread was nice and fresh. Respect for the managers to have crowd control and not let it look like a Hong Kong protest inside with people grabbing bread off the trays before they hit the shelf. They handled that pretty well. I got everything I could on my tray. two mugs and the yardstick for the first 100 customers. The above review is 5 stars worthy for the morning. the reason why I put a one star is for people who are curious and for the managers to look at how they did cause they care about the business and need customer feedback. I went back there at night because I gave most of the bread pastries away to my coworkers since we had a birthday celebration.
