Their sorbets are also delicious - I love the lavender strawberry when they have it! Today I got the green tea, which was new to me but probably one of the best flavors I've had there. You can get your scoop in a cute Chinese takeout box complete with a fortune cookie, or on a come (sometimes they can even shape it into a flower!) They have other toppings as well. They also have candies and other snacks so be sure to bring your sweet tooth and your appetite when you stop by!

This place was super cute. The staff was ok, it was my first time there so wish they would of explained the ice cream flavors instead of just staring at me as I tried to figure out which one I wanted. They did allow me to get some samples. Tried the trix that was good just a little on the sweet side. The Cap'n Crunch caught my eye, decided to get that one and so F****** happy I did. It was litteraly like have a bowl of cereal, just instantly bought me back to the couch watching Recess on a Saturday morning lol. The serve the ice cream in a Chinese food container topped with a fortune cookie. Super cool! They were sold out of the waffle sandwiches so next time I go that's what I'm getting... Counting down till my next visit
This went from a storefront to a corner ice cream stand in front of JoBot. Good ice cream and service with a smile!
To the tall guy with long hair and glasses, wearing a red shirt; how could you take something sweet and make it so sour?

Honestly overpriced for taste and presentation. Serving in a take out box with a fortune cookie is hella cute but so VERY inconvenient to eat out of. The paper box disintegrates (duh). Forget abt saving leftovers if you have any- sticky mess. Tastes like straight sugar if thats your thing. On the stringy/ chewy side.

This place won my heart instantly just based on the crazy flavors they had available! Thankfully the staff were super friendly and helpful and allowed us to sample basically everything. Hubby took the last of the Lucky Charms and got it in milkshake form. Honestly, this ended up being my choice. The ice cream on its own was incredible. And somehow the milkshake retained that magical flavor and didn't taste watered down at all. I ended up with two generous scoops - one of coco puffs and one of birthday cake. They were both awesome, for sure. But that Lucky Charms is what really got me!

Absolutely amazing ice cream. Nice location to enjoy sitting out front at the picnic tables during our great spring weather. The staff was friendly and more than willing to let us taste any flavors prior to purchasing. We had the lemon custard, which was creamy and had the right balance of tart and sweet, the pistachio, which had a nice amount of chopped pistachios in it, the hibiscus sorbet, which was amazingly fresh and not too sweet, the banana chocolate crunch, which had delightful little crunchy chocolate bits and the right balance of banana and chocolate ribbon in a sweet cream base, and the black forest, which had a deep chocolate flavor, bits of cherries, and chocolate crunch. We will definitely return. Go with a group so you have an excuse for trying the ice cream flight.

Great spot for some good ice cream. Came here cause I liked the to-go containers and was not disappointed by the ice cream. Honestly, I do not remember what flavors I got. But everything I taste-tested was pretty good and they have a decent variety of flavors, so you can't go wrong!

Come early in the day if you want more flavor options. We came around 9pm and most of flavors were sold out. Obviously I came for the cute ass Chinese food takeaway box and bomb ice cream! but the girl working the register was in a terrible mood and killed my ice cream buzz

Melt is a great place to go for decent ice cream and unique flavors! They got rid of their six flavor sampler, but you really can't go wrong here. Their horchata flavor was amazing and I haven't had a bad cereal flavor yet. With that said, the comments about there being pieces of ice crystals in the ice cream are accurate. Sure, it doesn't compromise the flavor, but it does show it's not the best made ice cream in town. Also, I don't really get the novelty of the ice cream coming in Chinese take-out boxes, but some people really get a kick out of it. Lastly, street parking can be rough to find some nights (but hey, it is downtown Phoenix so what do you expect). This place is definitely worth checking out because of the unique flavors and convenience, but Melt and Mary Coles are close to downtown too and they might be better!

One of the best places for ice cream! They always have some really good and interesting flavors. I definitely love how unique they are. It's very small and during the summer they at times can get a line out the door! Super hip ice cream shop. The employees are friendly, but not very talkative? They somewhat lack in customer service it would be great to be able to have a somewhat of a conversation, I guess. Overall really good place for ice cream. And if you cannot make up your mind on what flavor to get just order a flight you won't regret it!

I love this place... it's my hidden gem! I like going here because it's in the cut( not busy) and I like their different flavors and pairings they make. Plus I like the concept of using a fried rice box to put the ice cream in and putting a fortune cookie on top.... PURE GENIUS!!! I like that they ask you if you would like to sample options and the workers are always friendly and kind! Only knock I have which isn't a big one, but still a knock lol is that I usually go late at night(open until 12am) and they either ran out of ice cream options or don't have what I would like! Other than that it's a cool spot to take family, friends, and a date to. I have tried a few different types of their ice creams.. "Reese Puffs".. "Fruity Pebbles".. "Cake Batter"... "Butterfinger".. BOMB.. SUPER BOMB!! So if you have a chance check it out!

We stopped in here on our walk home, there was a bit of a wait, but it was worth it. I had wanted to try them for a while, but had to watch my sugar intake. I am now able to occasionally cheat, and glad I did on this! They have a ton of flavors that frequently change. It was so hard to decide on which one to get. My husband and I decided to share a double. We got hot fudge brownie and bourbon toffee! They were both delicious and worth every calorie ;) I will definitely go back the next time I am in search of a sweet fix. They also have waffle ice cream sandwiches, which sound amazing. Also, the service was great. We came in when there was a bit of a rush and only one girl was working. She handled it well and efficiently, with a smile.
Everything was great. Just a small sorbet and ice cream shop with amazing variety. The pear and cucumber sorbet is delightful. Price is a steal. And they are open until midnight.

Their ice cream is wonderfully distinct without being pretentious. They work out of a humble converted house; divided in two and selling their sweet creations out of the left half. Parking is plentiful because there are streets all around. The outdoor seating was a perfect view of the blood moon tonight. I really couldn't ask for a better ice cream experience. I love the brandy/toffee ice cream which was one one of the five flavors I tried in my flight. I think their fudge brownie ice cream has the highest brownie to ice cream ratio I've ever had. I really like the chocolate rose pistachio, it was such a strange mix but it worked. I'm very glad I stopped in for a bite.

It was starting to feel like all ice cream shops were the same with the difference being just the location, atmosphere, and service. Typically you don't get truly unique flavors but this place has really changed that. With flavors like fruity pebbles (made with real fruity pebble cereal) and horchata (it really did taste like homemade horchata) this place went beyond what I expected.

Friendly and sweet service. We tried the pomegranate sorbet, the banana ice cream and the butter finger. It was good, wasnt spectacular. I sampled the coconut milk and strawberry and it just tasted funny. The service was sweeter than the ice cream. Minimal shade in the seating area. Napkins werent readily available, but I asked and she happily gave me them and even got them wet for me. Packaging is super cute and they give you whatever samples you ask for w a smile. Ice cream gets 3 stars, & for $4 a pop, that wasnt the business, but service gets 5.

Once a quaint little house. Now a cart. Owners mixed it up from buying the restraint where it sits outside. A little disappointed they were still selling ice cream worh the freezing machine broken down. It meant melted icecream. Was still good but killed the experience.
Oh my what a great selection of flavors!!! It is a little bit on the more spending your side of things but it's homemade and it's wonderful!!!!

It's good, more A-OK, than "great!" I wouldn't drive out of my way for it. Yeah!: nice selection of flavors of ice cream, sorbet... But : some of the "ice creams" tasted really "thin" (not rich, creamy) Yeah!: she let us sample a good number of flavors But: having sampled a good number, there aren't many that I was keen on Yeah!: the one I did enjoy and order...I was tired of by the end of the single scoop (too sweet) - I'm speaking of the salted caramel. The other flavor that stuck out was the cucumber sorbet and it is just a huge burst of cucumber. But: Overload of flavor for me. (except for the white chocolate chip raspberry seemed done right) Yeah!: locally made (Superstition Farms) But: flavors will vary so if you loved it last time, try a sample before ordering again Yeah!: cute to-go Chinese food containers with fortune cookie But: large spoon relative to container size; also note there's up charge for a cone Yeah!: kind of a cute front porch, but this the block itself is a bit hit and miss on appearance. I get it that it's "converted homes" and "artsy" and such; I just may not be this cool. But: once inside, it feels unfinished. I don't know if this was because I could see into back rooms (supply room? or something) it just didn't cut it for me. Yeah!: clean patio area But: would be really cramped (we were only ones out there) The Yeah! Buts stick me on the fence.
I've always wanted to try the place out, the ice was good. Next time we wanna try the places food out.

WARNING!! This place must no longer be what the pictures and other reviews are saying!! Melt is now just a rolling cart stand at this address. The ice cream flavors were super limited. They didn't offer any toppings other than their signature fortune cookie. I have to say the ice cream wasn't horrible just far off from what I was expecting based on the other reviews and pictures.

These flavors are INCREDIBLE!!! So happy I found this ice cream spot! I got peanut butter and jelly flavor, but they also have a bunch of different types of cereal flavors (lucky charms? Cap'n crunch?) and other unique options! I wanted to try them all! The ice cream itself was super creamy, and it came in the cutest container with a fortune cookie. Highly recommend Melt!! :)

I scream for ice cream! After a night out, my pal and gal pals weren't quite ready to go out yet so we yelped up a dessert joint the was close by and still open that we could hit up. Thankfully we found Melt! Melt is such a cute little place, but it does its job. They sell drinks, candy, mangonadas and serves extra delicious ice cream. The packaging is so cute too, it comes in little Chinese take out boxes and includes a fortune cookie. My sister and I each got a single scoop, Cookie Monster and a Cute-cumber. Our total came out to $9.00 even. Single scoops are $4.50, double scoops are $6.00 and triple scoops are $7.50. Cookie Monster was the perfect amount of sweet and chewy from the cookie and cookie dough. Cute-cumber was a refreshing, very light, less sweet option. We both enjoyed our ice creams very much. I really like that they have a lot of different and seasonal flavors, some like zombie brains, pumpkin pie and churro. They do have a roomy outside area to sit and enjoy, none inside. They have tea lights and benches that create such a cozy ambiance. I like it here, and I can't wait to come back to try new/changing/seasonal flavors! Also: Parking is a little hard to find on busy nights, and meters are available.
Super delicious icecream! Pretty grumpy service, no matter how hard I tried to be friendly. * Don't make any jokes. Just order. Pay. Leave. Enjoy.

This place has a few vegan options and unique flavors for their dairy ice cream options. It's located in an open, trendy space that's shared with a bar and coffee shop. I like the large space and ample seating. It's a little loud, so I would not use this as a study spot unless you like noisy areas. The only downside is the location might be hard to find because it's inside a larger area.
Very unique ice cream and the cutest stickers! I'm sad the original place closed down; regardless, the ice cream is very yummy!

Incredible ice cream, gelato, sorbet, and other frozen treats. I can't say enough good things about this spot. Located inside of Jobot, Melt always has a fresh lineup of delicious desserts. The menu changes regularly, so you can always try something new. Ice cream is served in one of two sizes of Chinese food take out boxes. You can also choose to order a flight, which includes 5 scoops each places in their own hole in a muffin baking sheet. You'll also be happy to know that they'll throw in a small handful of fortune cookies as well.

I loved this place but they've moved to being a pop up shop out front of Jobot Coffee right down the street Friday-Sunday only... the sign out front of their original location right now is a little misleading. I watched three other groups of customers walk into Jobot and ask where melt went tonight, hopefully the actual store comes back soon -- not sure if it's closed or just under construction?

Melt is super cute. Little old house in the Roosevelt neighborhood turned into a quaint ice cream shop. If you read the reviews you know that the ice cream is served in a Chinese Food to-go box with a fortune cookie topper. They have a sampler tray which gives you the chance to try 5 flavors ($7). Probably the best bargain they have. Melt has a lot of interesting flavor combinations. I highly recommend you ask for a sample first. Don't commit to an untasted flavor or you may find yourself throwing out the rest once the flavor profile sets in in your mouth. There's a lot right with Melt, but there's a lot wrong as well so I'm not sure how anyone could give it a 5 star review. The flavors I tried however were spot on, creamy, cold and yummy. Right: building has a cool vibe, lots and lots of interesting fruit flavors, sorbets, sherbets and sweet flavors like chocolate mint, chocolate, etc... plus Superfarm; Hazelnut Chocolate with Nutella. Good stuff. They give fairly good sized scoops, the staff is very nice, great patio for eating your ice cream as well as people watching, they offer the 5 scoop sample tray, and they're open noon to midnight. Wrong: Inside is too small, no inside seating, outside seating is not misted or cooled, street parking is horrible, they don't put a malted milk ball, melted chocolate or something into the bottom of the waffle cones to keep them from dripping, lines can be long and slow to move leaving you standing around in the Arizona heat (depending on the month). As I said above, the Ice cream is NOT made on-site, or home made, it's locally made by Superstition Farm. If you live in the east valley you can always just visit Udder Delights (which I like as well). I'm not knocking this, just pointing out a fact. Cool vibe, great selection of flavors, nice staff, lousy parking, patio not Arizona proof, long lines at times. 4 Stars.

I had ear-marked this place for a while and was excited when I saw them at First Friday in Phoenix. Their packaging with the Chinese take-out box definitely looked creative from the pictures and the reviews were convincing. However, when I got to their stand, I was a little disappointed in the inability to sample the flavors. They had about six unique ones and I just felt like I had a hard time choosing without trying them first. Plus I feel like part of the fun in eating ice cream is sample the options! Nonetheless, I went with the coffee and my friend went with the churro flavor. We enjoyed breaking open our fortunes cookies together and reading our fortunes to each other. The ice cream itself wasn't bad but I wasn't entirely impressed. It tasted like something from cold stone- a little on the richer and sweeter end, but the flavor wasn't quite there. I would probably have enjoyed the churro a little more if the pieces were also more crispy fresh. Not a bad option though if you're looking for something cool on a hot summer day!

Great ice cream shop. They let you try as many flavors as you want. The ice cream is rich, creamy and delicious. Outdoor seating na cool little part of town. The staff was fantastic. Great place, we will definitely be back.

First off finding parking is a mission, but what do you expect for a downtown location. The store itself is NOT wheel chair accessible. I had my 3 month old with me who's in a stroller so we had to leave that outside. Which was not a problem because the store is so tiny we would of taken over the whole space. It was also rather hot inside as well. This of course is part of the reason they lost a star. The staff was amazing super friendly, and with it being our first time there, they weren't bothered by us or anyone wanting to try their variety of flavors. They had many interesting flavor that not many big chain ice cream stores carry such as Nutella, banana nut, & white chocolate macadamia. Their prices are too much for what you actually get and the ice cream melted fast. That could of been why it's called melt or the 106 degree weather we were experiencing that day.

I feel bad, but man, 5:30 on a Saturday night and you have 4 flavors? 4?? And the vanilla only had enough for 1 scoop. Bummer cause the vanilla was good - but not what we would have ordered if we had more choices.
Love this place. I had mango and watermelon sorbet WOW! Perfect for a hot spring day. I love the presentation and it was cute getting a fortune cookie with my ice cream.
How creative is this place with their presentation and selection in flavors ! Definitely my spot to chill and enjoy a delicious ice cream while exploring downtown Phx

It gets 3 stars because the bar it is in is pretty cool and the service was friendly. The ice cream itself left much to be desired. The strawberry and cafe de leche were tasteless. Every flavor was crunchy due to ice crystal formation, which shows that the ice cream has been partially melted and refrozen. I'll stick to Scooptacular and Novel I guess.

Very good homemade ice cream in funky little part of town. When we drove into this area it was hard for me to keep my eyes on the road because there was so much graffiti art on all the buildings. In fact, the whole block is covered in graffiti and it is something to see. Melt is tucked away in a little old house that was converted into retail spaces and is very cool. They serve all homemade ice cream and condiments. I got the salted caramel ice cream with homemade whipped cream and it was excellent! There are also other establishments on this (what was once a residential block) street including: vintage clothing shop, coffee shop, a bar, and some more I can't really remember right now. If you have not been down to Melt you should check it out. I would go in the colder months so you can sit outside and take in all the atmosphere.

Sometimes getting lost is the best way to find amazing treasures hidden in a city. I'm still new here so finding cute little ice cream shops like Melt is fantastic. Though it was $3 for a miniscoop, the ice cream I tried was really creamy & tasted fresh. Which is a lot to say considering most ice cream shops tend to keep theirs frozen for a minute. I recommend the Chop Suey. It had walnuts & berries in vanilla cream. I'm not a sweet tooth type of person so this was a perfect blend for me. They come in these cute little fortune cups!

High prices, lame flavors, skip. I was expecting some more unique flavors from the reviews but was sooo disappointed in the small selection of plain Jane flavors that I ended up not even ordering. My husband had a peanut butter chocolate sundae which I tasted, it was very rich but nothing I couldn't have gotten in a tub of grocery store ice cream. My sister got a small brownie (looked old) with scoop of vanilla and hot fudge. Our order for those two small-standard regular joe desserts totaled $17!! Not worth it.

Now this is what I would call good ice cream that is unique and stands out about the rest! The shop is located around the Roosevelt Row artsy section of downtown Phoenix. The store front is small and nothing fancy, but they have a nice outdoor seating area. My husband had the PB and J and I had the Cookie Monster (blue colored vanilla ice cream with Oreo and chocolate chip cookie chunks). They offer many other unique and delicious looking flavors such as honey lavender and fruity pebbles. They also feature more traditional flavors as well and rotate them out regularly so the selection doesn't get old. I highly recommend trying this place out if you are in the area. This is hands down THE best ice cream I have tried since moving to the Phoenix area.

Melt isn't the same as it used to be. I was a regularly customer for several years until they and sister-business Jobot were forced to move two streets over to "gentrification central" under Roosevelt Point from their original location on 5th street. In the past 2-3 years, I've seen a great decline in taste and quality of their ice cream and overall customer service. They have gutted many products and taken away several "classic" flavors from their arsenal. I am not sure what has been happening but I hope it changes soon because the Melt that I had come to know and love just isn't the same anymore.

Yummy ice cream. I got the Cookies N Cream. It was so creamy! I liked the presentation in the Chinese takeout box with the fortune cookie. It did take me a while to find the place, I circled the building, but I found it inside the corner store/coffee shop.

All I have so stay is that the blueberry muffin ice cream is glorious! It tasted exactly like a freshly baked buttery blueberry muffin. It's the perfect amount of sweet with a non-artifical blueberry flavor. I paired it this time with the cookie doh because I had to compromise with someone else since we were sharing. Next time, I will be pairing it with the oatmeal cookie. The oatmeal cookie sample I had was really good, not as good as the blueberry muffin but still good. It was a mild oatmeal cookie flavor it would have gone nicely with the blueberry muffin. The cookie doh one that I did get was aight. It was kinda boring in comparison to the blueberry and I don't know if I honestly would have liked it any better alone. In it's defense, I'm not a huge cookie dough fan. I also sampled the pumpkin ice cream. It's not the best I've had but it was decent. I thought the bluemoon flavor they had was beer flavored it was not lol my friend never told me what was smashed up inside it but it was not beer haha The ice cream comes in a stereotypical Chinese food container and is topped with a fortune cookie (I love it when places have a special signature). I didn't get a chance to ask why. They also sell Mexican tostilocos that I never tried before but plan to try at some point (here or somewhere else). Not sure what the theme is here.. The outdoor seating is super cute especially at night. I would say that this place would make a nice little date spot for sure.

If you're just driving by this place might be hard to see at first, but on a walk through Roosevelt Row the cool front door caught my eye. This ice cream shop not only has friendly employees it's ice cream is phenomenal! The milk is bought from a local dairy and it is yummy! Cool flavors that you can sample, and they put the ice cream in Chinese take out containers topped with a fortune cookie. Cones are also an option. If your looking for unique, flavorful, and friendly this place is for you.
Ordered the cappuccino splatter at their Pemberton phx location. Horrible. Had no cappuccino or coffee flavor at all and cost $8 for one cup. Complete rip-off.

We kept driving in circles trying to find the place- there wasn't a sign that we could see on the outside. We parked and asked someone walking by about it and they confirmed we had the place. The ice cream was delicious and the atmosphere very fun- a great place to come for food, ice cream, coffees and teas- we loved it!

I enjoy Melt, they always have at least one or two dairy free options but occasionally they have an employee or two who you can tell, just wants to go home & rushes thru the entire interaction. I live near melt, it's walking distance from my house, but I still seek out Novel over Melt most days of the week. When novel is closed, I'll go to melt. They have excellent flavor options but again, the service always leaves me feeling blah. Last night the service was appalling. I get it, it's Sunday night but every single employee was either rude, rushing us, or just generally unhappy to be there. The vibe was off. The employee gave my boyfriend a very small double scoop portion, only to give me almost twice as much when we ordered the same double scoop box. No "iconic" fortune cookies for either of us & again, the service was just terrible this time. They basically threw the change down on the counter & basically then they ran to take out all the trash before we finished our ice cream, thus leaving the trash cans with no trash liners in them, so I took our trash HOME to throw away because I'm not a jerk....... but they acted like they were closing up shop at 9pm, literally sweeping us out of the place. It was weird. Prices are ok, but with service being so off, it makes it almost not worth it. I wish they would also bring back the CBD option. I bragged so much about them having this option only for it to disappear every time I want to try it. This place is so inconsistent, but they do have great flavor combos.

This is my favorite gelato place in phx! The flavors taste so real and there's so many to choose from and they constantly rotate. It tastes like high quality gelato for sure. The gelato comes in a Chinese takeout box with a fortune cookie on top - like I need MORE dessert. But yes. The answer to that question is always yes!
Yummy! Pretty small place and seemed like it stayed busy. I visited at like 10pm on a Sunday night and it was still buzzing
The ice cream was so delicious. Strawberry banana was amazing. Salted caramel is so yummy

This was such a cute little ice cream place, although it was a little difficult to get to because there was construction on the nearby roads! I really liked the swirly mural on the exterior of the building. The interior isn't anything special and very tiny -- no places to sit inside (there were several outdoor tables though), which was disappointing because it was 110 degrees outside. The ice cream: The flavor selection was definitely varied and featured several unusual flavors, like Thai tea, fruity pebbles, and ricanelas. I got the fruity pebbles and red, white, and blue sky (I visited on July 5th -- it consisted of strawberry, blueberry, and lemon) flavors and both were awesome! I especially liked the fruity pebbles one because it reminded me of eating cereal as a kid. The red, white, and blue sky was also delicious and not overpoweringly fruity, which was nice. My mom said that the ricanelas and Thai tea flavors were good, although she was miffed because the female cashier gave her less ice cream than the male one did! Side note: The male server was very friendly! My dad got the blueberry muffin flavor, which wasn't anything special, and my brother got the chocolate and cherry flavors, which he said were good! Presentation: I thought it was cute how they serve ice cream in Chinese takeout containers with fortune cookies instead of the standard cup! I found it kept the ice cream from spilling as much as it does when it's in a cup and the servers can be more generous in portion sizes. Price: For a double scoop, it was $5.25, which isn't too bad for such cool flavors! I would definitely come back!

The variety of choices makes for some interesting combinations. Tonight, I liked "bitter orange in olive oil" combined with "froot loops". It was good! Like I let the smartest foodie I know and a small child decide my flavors. It was great and paired well. My date picked strawberry-jalapeÃ±o and sweet potato. Next time, I'll get one of their chocolate or caramel things...

There is a line constantly out the door for melt and for a good reason. The icecream and sherbet let's not forget that for the lactose free individuals is divine. The whole style is great also. From the little Chinese take out boxes, to the fortune cookie, Melt has a style all of its own. Also, for any avid sticker collectors they have some pretty cute stickers to decorate that Mac or hydro that are constantly used for stickers. Again, Melt has a great product, fast, and delicious.

Went in at lunch time on a little date with my daughter. The guys there were so nice! I was glad the flavors were anything but ordinary. I got the strawberry jalapeÃ±o one which I was a little afraid of but it was perfect!!! My daughter got pink lemonade and didn't share cause it was that good! ;) will definitely be back!

Good ice cream, but the rest of the experience is such a hassle. I definitely applaud them for their creativity and execution in making such odd ice cream flavors very enjoyable. The pricing was cheap IMO ($7.50 for the flight), and the establishment was crappy so i didnt want to come back, so i made sure to get the Ice Cream Flight. (FYI even though there are 6 cupcake slots, you only get 5 scoops of ice cream since the 6th slot is for garbage fortune cookies). Unfortunately, they didnt properly prepare for their day of business and ran out of their Cucumber Sorbet. So i had the Lemon Grass, Pear, Oatmeal Cookie, Fruit Pebbles, and Melon flavors. Pear was a bland let down, and the Lemon Grass stole the show by being creamy and subtle. As for the rest of the experience, their store is built to handle only 1 or 2 customers at a time, having 6 people in there is like an awkward and hot elevator ride. You're forced to take your order to go or eat it outside in the heat. Their product is very good and worth a higher price. Hopefully they work out their kinks and provide a better experience for their customers.

Came here twice during our stay in Phoenix. For those unfamiliar with the area like me, you should expect to pull up to a neighborhood looking area with a bunch of houses. Well Melt is located in a house, and it has a tiny sign in the window. Outside of the house are a couple of tables with lights strung above for a cute, hip vibe. They have a bunch of interesting, cool flavors. Their honey lavender was light but I got all the notes from it. I got the nutella flavor, which was rich and flavorful. The next time I tried their Horchata flavor which tasted exactly like it.. so good! My one wish is that their ice cream was a bit more thick so it wouldn't melt as quickly.. but maybe that's why they named the place..? Or it's just ridiculously hot in phx? The service was awesome. We ended up having a full conversation with the guy at the cash register as we were remarking how incredibly hot it was in Phoenix. Even though a line was starting to form to pay, the guy at the register still talked to us, took his time, and was so genuine. This was such a breath of fresh air, as this would never happen in LA...

There are problems only ice cream can fix. Melt is located in a artsy and quirky part of downtown Phoenix, that is refered to as Roosevelt Row. The area is filled with art galleries, vintage shops, and book stores, it's worth a stop just to look around if you're in the area. As we walked into Melt we were greeted, asked if it was our first visit, and given as many samples as we wanted. Melt has a display case which is stocked with 18 flavors of ice cream, which are all made locally at Superstition Farmin Mesa. Melt has all the standard flavors and lots of creative flavors, like fruity pebbles. The flavor selection at Melt is always rotating so there is always something new. On my first visit I had the super farm, chocolate, hazelnuts, with nutella swirled in. The ice cream was delicious and perfecy sweet. And the scoop.size is large. At Melt you can choose to have your ice cream served in Chinese takeout boxes and topped with a fortune cookie, between two cookies, or in a house-made waffle cone. The prices are reasonable, the customer service is great, and most importantly the ice cream is delicious. If your in the mood for really good ice cream give Melt a try you won't be dissapointed.

Their ice cream is a must! I love banana ice cream from cold stone (which only locations serve) so when I saw that they had banana nut ice cream I knew I had to try. Once I tried it was delicious. Had to get a scoop of it. They were out of waffle cones though :( sad. My BF loves horchata, everywhere we go that has horchata to drink that's what he is ordering. So I immediately saw it and he couldn't believe it he thought I was playing with him lol so he ordered it. He loved it! He thought my banana ice cream was too sweet. But I thought it was just perfect:) Their line was too long. And hard to find parking. But it was worth it

Even if the chinese takeout box and fortune cookie are gimmicky, I still eat it up! A small, cooky shop that offers some interesting flavors. I wouldnt say the flavors are wacky, but they are not conventional. The captain crunch won my heart! It tasted EXACTLY like the cereal. Not every flavor they have is as mindblowing, but there's a good amount that are damn good. The white chocolate raspberry chocolate stood out to me as well. Check it out!

Had the white chocolate raspberry ice cream and pomegranate sorbet in a waffle cone. Was really good, but I think the price was a little too high in my opinion. It was $6 for 2 scoops in a waffle cone. The service was ok, but the guy working seemed like he had the most annoying job in the world. Maybe the person before me left a bad taste, but this guy make me feel like I was a total inconvenience. I like quality service and products, so I'll check out another place next time.

We went at 9:30 on a Friday night. The ice cream is good, but flavors are limited-especially for chocolate lovers. There were a lot of cereal flavors, which I found odd. I got a double scoop, which was $5.25. I like the uniqueness of the Chinese takeout box with the fortune cookie.

I actually enjoyed this place the Cookie Monster Ice cream was delicious and the chocolate wasn't bad. It is a bit expensive 4.50 for a single scoop and 8 for a double. But at least they weren't tiny scoops and they tasted good and they put them in a Chinese takeout container with a fortune cookie which is cute. So if u want ice cream and don't mind spending a bit more id say try it out it's outside of the building.

Small ice cream cart on Roosevelt - delicious and unique ice cream flavors!! Service was fast and friendly and ice cream came in small take out containers with a fortune cookie on top. We had honey lavender (my favorite), blueberry muffin, chocolate, and mango sorbet. Would recommend all flavors

Independent stores are cool, and I always want to support them, but it's hard to do that when they aren't on par with the large chain places. First off, the service here was great! The guy at the counter was friendly and cool. Now for the icecream - it was regular, nothing special. Looking at the display case, nothing unusual or particularly tempting called out to me, so I ordered a half scoop of cookies and cream with a half scoop of dark chocolate. It was yummy, but icecream is always yummy. I wanted that something more that would make this place worth returning to, and I didn't find it. Ways this place could improve - offer more toppings. Most of the toppings they offered were chocolate covered in a hard candy shell (M&Ms and Reese pieces) or gummy bears, which I hate in icecream bc they get extremely hard. I would like to see offered as toppings: fudge, caramel syrup, crushed oreos, crushed reese's, cookie dough, brownie, cake... Or if you're not going to offer more toppings, then at least put more chunks of "stuff" into your icecream, and not just have the straight up plain flavors with nothing in there to add texture and interest.

I hadn't been to Melt in awhile and I swung by on the way home from work a few weeks ago. It seems like it's gone downhill quite a bit. They were out of almost every flavor and only had about 5 left. The shop seemed kind of dirty, and service wasn't the best. I had to wait a minute for an employee to come from the back to help me, and he seemed put out that he did. I got a basil sorbet for myself and some kind of chocolate flavor for my husband. My basil sorbet was really refreshing and the flavor was fantastic. My husband said his was just alright. I originally liked Melt because of their service and unique flavors. However, it seems like both are now lacking. If I was downtown and wanting ice cream, I'd choose Novel over Melt.

I'm a huge Melt fan! I remember when it opened & I've been coming here ever since. It's not your typical ice cream spot. True to the downtown vibe, it's inside what used to be a house. The decor is fun & playful. The ice cream is phenomenal! They described it as "artisan-crafted" & they use local high quality ingredients as much as possible. The flavor selection is always extremely unique. Things like Fruity Pebbles & Blueberry Muffin. Tonight, I got Peach & it was so flavorful & full of peach chunks! Oh, & it's served in a take out box, garnished with a fortune cookie!

Stumbled across this spot walking through downtown Phoenix one evening. The staff there was very helpful with answering questions about flavors and let you have samples. And o boy! This ice cream is very good. Probably jumped straight to top of my favorite phoenix spot above other power houses.

I've been following the Insta for so long, I randomly ended up parking near it while I was volunteering downtown, and had to try! It was tinier than I expected, but I thought it was cute! Loved all the retro candies they had on display and such. Also like that it's in an old house, and all of the shops and places surrounding it, very colorful! Being from the Midwest and hearing that they had blue moon, I had to ask because I wasn't sure. They call it smurf's blood there which I think is kinda funny haha. But it definitely brings back memories eating blue moon, which was great. They served it in little takeout containers with fortune cookies which is unique and cool. I liked the free stickers they had too haha. My friend got a watermelon sorbet, and she did not like it very much. I also tried it and wasn't a fan. The ice cream had a wonderful creamy whipped texture, and that texture just didn't work with the sorbet. I think we would have preferred if the sorbet was more dense. Overall it was a good experience, glad I went!

Yummm! This was great! Definitely get the Flight. You get to taste 5 flavors for 8 dollars! Such a good deal. The ice cream was phenomenal. Super creamy. I loved the chocolate kiss, pumpkin praline, lemon sorbet, and blueberry. The green tea was good but it tasted JUST like green tea. The atmosphere is so fun. I will definitely go back!

I loved this place! So many unique flavors I wanted to try, but ended up getting the honey lavender and my date got the mint chocolate chip one. Bit were phenomenal!!! We walked from an apartment downtown; not sure if it's a good thing or bad thing to be so close! I may frequent this place too much!!! The staff was really friendly. Super cute little shop, can't wait to go back!

I've been wanting to try Melt and after seeing that they did ice cream flights, I made it a mission to come here. We had the pistachio almond (my favorite), churro (second favorite), s'mores, butter pecan, and nutty professor (chocolate peanut butter). An ice cream flight consists of 5 scoops of ice cream for about $7, not a bad price at all. All seating is outdoors so make sure you go when the weather is tolerable.
I am loving the fruity pebbles and captain crunch ice cream tonight. They taste just like the cereal! Very friendly service too

This place is so cute and love that they use chinese take containers for bowls. Cute idea and the fortune cookie just sells the cutie concept. Order the plain jane vanilla. The staff explained that all the ingredients are local and made in house. I could not wait to try it. It was good, but way too sweet for my taste buds. I heart local businesses so I need to come back to try another flavor.
We stopped in after my daughter's dance recital for a celebratory ice cream. The only two flavors available- cucumber sorbet and chocolate. Really? No thanks, we'll take our celebration elsewhere.

I'm ashamed that I have yet to review this place. Really. The amount of times I've been in late at night and needing my fix of crazy delicious flavors can't be counted on two hands at this point. I first came here last year as I heard they were magicians of dairy goodness, and I'm convinced this is the best ice cream in the valley. My personal favorites, even though they seem to change, are the coconut and the salted caramel. I've tried the lavender (which was amazing) and also this blueberry icecream that was mind blowing and only lasted a few days I think. They're always rotating flavors which is exciting. The fruit loop one? Try it. Its like leftover fruit loop milk. I do think some of them are bit...interesting (I forgive you melt, for the one time I tried some weird spicy pineapple sorbet that tasted like buffalo sauce on a pineapple) but all in all you have to try this place. The patio is a perfect spot to eat your icecream on, great for a date, or by your lonesome fatty self, like me.

It always makes me sad when I come here and my favorite flavor is out of rotation. I miss Strawberry Balsamic more than I've missed any ex-girlfriend but I love late night trips here because there's always something new to discover and love. Lemon Olive Oil previously and Cucumber Mojito Sorbet tonight. Those flavors may not be your style but I don't like sweets and this place gets me excited for bold creative flavors beyond their delicious fudge, coffee, Cap'n Crunch, Fruity Pebbles, and other standard fruit flavors. Staff is awesome and the patio is nice, comfortable and full of friendly people. The neighborhood is the South Roosevelt Arts District with great stores, bars and restaurants to enjoy before and after. Plus there's often a great and friendly jazz/blues guitarist on the corner or a concert at the bar next door to enjoy. I've also been there when a DJ will spin records on the front porch. I love this place and unlike some other places downtown it's not pretentious or catering to a narrow, young and hip crowd. This is a very family friendly, date night, guilt eating and all purpose hangout spot. Check it out for the creative flavors and delicious homemade standards.

Went here tonight to get some ice cream. We were excited to try a new place. It's located in a cute bungalow on 5th St by Roosevelt. We walked in and looked at the case: a variety of homemade ice creams all half MELTED!!! We asked the guy behind the counter what the story was. His response: "uhhhhhh yeah it's kinda hot." Really?! Apparently this place is called melt for a reason. And at $4.50 for a small you can keep your half melted ice cream. We went to Safeway and bought a carton of frozen Ben and Jerry's for $4.

I've been going to this place since it opened and I can honestly say it is the best ice cream place I have ever been to! The people are nice, great atmosphere, and the ice cream is delicious. Whenever someone asks me for an ice cream place to go to, 10/10 times I recommend Melt.

I'm an ice cream lover and after hearing all my friends rave about how hip and great the ice cream is I decided to give it a try today. The ice cream itself was no different than any other store bought ice cream. The flavors were bland, and the ice cream I got was super melty. Other than their attraction having ice cream in a to go box with a fortune cookie. This place has a nice urban feel but the ice cream was like any other average place. Customer service on the other hand was nice because they were patient with customers trying different flavors and were very courteous.
Sssoooooooo! Vegan Ice Cream is the shit! If you love yourself you'll cop that banana vegan option next time you walk by this ice cream pop up

We walked over at 4:45 only to realize the store was closed and it's now a janky little ice cream cart inside of Jobot which no one was attending to and all the ice cream had freezer burn. Woof! Why can't good things stay the same?

Disclaimer: I want to try this place at the right time and redo this review! Came in on a Saturday night and there were literally only 6 flavors in the ice cream freezer (all of which were near empty) and a lot of other products were sold out. My friends sucked it up and got a Peanut Butter & Jealous shake mixed with other flavors I can't remember and the other got two HEAPING scoops of a berry ice cream for himself. I must say, they looked good. So 1 measly star for having so much out-of-stock, but I will visit again and I will have ice cream! Hopefully.

Melt was an extraordinary little shop with exotic and close to heart flavors. With the please aesthetics of the to-go containers or the lovely art and stickers they have available for purchase, you would definitely fall in love with this place.
Had the strawberry and it wasn't good. It tasted old and like the carton it comes in. I'm an ice cream lover and I eat all ice cream but this one I just couldn't finish.

We're happy to have found this little place that's in the middle of downtown Phoenix! We were walking around and happened to see a small street sign that pointed us to Melt. It wasn't too late yet so there was no wait when we walked into the small establishment. The staff promptly greeted us and offered us samples. We had never been here before so we gave a couple a try! Each flavor was unique and really delicious. I decided to get the mango sorbet which was really fluffy and just melted in my mouth. Also really unique is that they serve ice-cream in little Chinese take-out containers and also give a fortune cookie! There's some seating outside but not much. Like I said previously, it wasn't too crowded when we got there so we were able to find a seat, however it got much busier by the time we were done enjoying our ice-cream. I definitely recommend giving this place a try!

Very cute little spot just off of Roosevelt. I love the presentation of the ice cream in Chinese take out boxes, complete with fortune cookies. Love the flights, a sampling of five flavors plus fortune cookies presented in a muffin pan ($7.50). Love the dog friendly outdoor seating. And, most importantly, love the ice cream. My favorite ice cream flavor this visit? Peanut butter & jelly. Not the most juvenile flavor we ordered believe it or not. Those were Captain Crunch-berry and Lucky Charm based flavors ordered by the kids. Fear not. There are numerous choices for the adult palate as well.

Cute ice cream shop on the same street as MADE. I went by at 3:40pm and realized they don't open until 4:00pm (yikes!) so I walked around (and stumbled upon the gem that is MADE Boutique on the corner) and then came back to Melt. There was a girl working inside. She wasn't too happy when I asked permission to sample some of their flavors but she still let me. There wasnt a single one I didn't like. I decided on a "Double"; 1 scoop of the Chai and 1 scoop of the Chocolate Wasted. What I wanted was a milkshake ($7) but they didnt have any coffee ice cream and that is what I was craving. I'm glad they didnt have it because my ice cream combo was the bomb. The Double is $6 and is served in a Chinese take-out box, topped with a fortune cookie.

Items Selected: Samples - Drunk'n Nut, Arizona Sunrise, Wine n' Cheese Single Churro Single White Chocolate Raazz with Sprinkles Triple - Cap'n Crunch, Drunk'n Nut, Twisted Delight No doubt playing the Instagram-era plating game by way of Chinese take-out containers complete with Cookie, Central City's Melt takes Phoenicians on a flavor-trip by way of housemade Ice Cream with a texture somewhere between hand-dipped and soft serve presented by clerks who try entirely too hard to be funny. Located in a converted former-home on 5th Street, this odd style of makeshift dining space familiar to locals but a bit disconcerting to visitors given signage posted along a low fence, those entering Melt are immediately bombarded by high decibels of Punk and bad puns paired to samples, a limit of three almost a point of pride even when the shop was otherwise uncrowded. Trying to make conversation about the product, flavors like "Arizona Sunrise" that are not especially obvious described with a snarky response before finally yielding "like a Creamsicle" it was with small tastes of savory Wine n' Cheese plus a riff on Humphry Slocombe's "Secret Breakfast" that decisions were made, though not before the young man chastised one in the party for adding Sprinkles that "taste like chalk." Getting past the service, or lack thereof, including an unwillingness to sell a friend less than a full pound of Chamoy Gummy Bears, further tastes of Melt confirmed a semi-soft texture quite unlike most modern-day Artisans while flavors trended sweet yet not "sugary," the Churro essentially just Vanilla with a bit of Cinnamon while White Chocolate Razz was even milder, and thus quite different from the yeasty Cereal Milk flavored Cap'n Crunch or "Twisted Delight" of Strawberries and Balsamic.

The Melt was so cute! My friend and I were looking for an ice cream shop to get a sweet treat after dinner and couldn't resist when we saw how the Melt served their ice cream: in little Chinese to go boxes. It was so unique. They had unique flavors I'd never seen before. I can't quite remember them, but each had a Latin or Mexican influence on it. The prices were reasonable and the person who served us was welcoming and allowed us to try the flavors. Vibes in the Melt were relaxed and low key.

Very interesting flavors! I got the Cap'n Crunch (tried fruity pebbles and birthday cake), my friend got chocolate chip-mostly chocolate, and my bf got sweet and salty brownie. They come in little Chinese food take out boxes which I don't really like because I feel like it's gonna leak out when it Melts. The parking is atrocious but I found a decent spot after circling the block once. And the building is a renovated house that fits maybe 6 thin customers at once. Lots of outside seating though. I will say this place is insanely popular though for adult and kids.

One night after a big dinner, friends and I stopped by this place and gave them a try. The hardest part is finding a parking spot, since the downtown area can be quite hard to navigate. Melt was quite small and overall quite clean. Unfortunately no public loo for me to try. And I was ready!!! The dairy products helped too....Jk We got a scope of cute-cumber which was very refreshing, even the neighborhood kitty thought so. And a scope of Cookie Monster which my friends thought was the perfect amount of sweetness and chewiness from the cookie and stuff. And the blue colour was amazing. Overall a great and fantastic little place, and we highly recommend you come here today. And the cat does too, she's hangry!!

We recently made a stop here since seeing the pictures posted by friends. I got the fruity pebbles ice cream and my hubby got the caption crunch. It was okay wasn't what we thought. The caption crunch ice cream taste blah the cereal tasted old and didn't have flavor in it. Would we came back again I think not...

A little annoyed that I drove 30mins to try this place out and all they had was 5 flavors to choose from!? For the people that have to make a drive maybe you should call ahead, and see if they're serving more than 5 flavors or have waffles in stock. It was a waste of my time...

I wanted to love this place, as we love local, love ice cream, and love creative. Ice cream: delicious Location: cute area Shop: not the cutest inside. Super dark and blah. Space has way more potential. Service: blah Wish they had kid or mini scoops, any type of toppings or cones (sold out?), maybe a slightly enthused employee, and seriously the dark/dingy interior was really a bummer. That said, ice cream was on point but not sure we will return.

So with all the hype we decided to try Melt. Tiny ice cream shop, went on a Friday night, the guy and girl working it weren't very enthusiastic , looked like they didn't want to be there. Ice cream was okay, $6 for a double. Started to melt quickly, we wont be going back. Should have gone to Sweet Republic!

It's nice to take a break from your typical run of the mill flavors and what I loved was how natural the blueberry icecream I got tasted. The little Chinese takeout box was definitely a fun way of changing things up, the fortune cookie was also a cool little thing to add. I would love to go back and try out the other different flavors sometime.

Melttttttttttttttttt my heart :)))) I love it here, cute hole in the wall. I got the mint chocolate chip in a Chinese to go box :) with a fortune cookie. we sat outside, people watching. I like it here.

This place was pretty darn awesome. They put your ice cream in a Chinese to go box type deal with a fortune cookie on top. The flavors are different. I got ether pb and j or peanut butter. I don't remember but for some reason I didn't realize there was going to be jelly in there and I didn't like that. I'm not a big fan of jelly though so don't go off of that. Outside of me not liking jelly, it was really good. There store is small and cute. Definitely a different vibe than I'm used to. Everyone should try this place at least once! I tried it while at first Friday in February. It's definitely buzzing during that time!
Stopped in here late Monday afternoon. Awesome coconut ice cream.

This little shop stole my heart. I love the chinese take out containers and the fortune cookie. Never in my life have I seen anything like it. And so much ice cream fits into such a little container. If it sounds weird just give it a try and you'll know what I mean.

I asked for two scoops and I got one scoop to equal two and they charged for two scoops. The scoops keep getting smaller and smaller. Although the ice cream is good, the portion sizes need to equal the amount you pay for.

My kids love when I get on Yelp and we are in a different city. This time we find ourselves in Phoenix AZ. They know that I always find a great experience for them. Melt is a great little shop that is located in the middle of a neighborhood. The concept is great the ice cream is incredible. My favorite flavor is the cucumber and mint. I know it sound weird but trust me it's WONDERFUL! Forget about the big chain ice cream shops support local shop. Thanks Melt for the great experience.

This place is great!!! The flavors they offer are unique and have strong flavors that leave your mouth watering. Beware this place is very popular and you may find yourself in a long line down the street! That only means one thing...this place is on fire!!

Melt did not disappoint. I looks like a cute little beach house. Inside the most adorable decor and amazing ice cream flavors. I got the mangonada and my friend got the captain crunch one I think. Simply delicious and served in cute Chinese takeout containers with a fortune cookie. I totally regret not getting the chamoy gummy pack. I will be back soon to get it.

Cute little independent ice cream shop in the middle of an artsy row of houses. Being from out of town, we just used yelp to find a dessert place around Pizzeria Bianco. In a winter afternoon in November, it was a nice stroll from the Pizzeria to Melt. The flavors are very seasonal as I was able to get sweet potato pecan and pumpkin pie. How inventive! Generous scoop sizes were also a plus. Easy street parking around the area.

Melt Ice Cream Shop is a hidden gem located in the heart of Downtown Phoenix! They have a wide variety of different flavors + toppings and they specialize in "unusual" ice cream creations instead of the basic chocolate, Vanilla & Strawberry! They have Cookie Monster, Fruit Loops, Fruity Pebbles, Matcha Green-Tea, Churro, etc. They also top each ice cream with a fortune cookie + puts the ice cream in Chinese "to go" containers! I love doing their ice cream flights which comes in a cupcake tin so you get to have 6 different flavors and you get to try a little bit of everything! Definitely a must stop if you're exploring Downtown Phoenix and you have a sweet tooth craving!
Took a while to find the stand but on a late night on Sunday we were able to find it!! Martin and Arianna were amazing they deserve a raise and heater!

For a place that says "open until midnight" i expected that the store would actually have a full line of products and someone to greet you upon arrival.... this was at 10:30pm. Ummmm, that was not the case during my visit. No one was there to even say, "hello," and when looking at the flavors available there were only two to choose from (chocolate and cucumber something). One of my biggest pet peeves is an "open" store that's not really open... might as well be closed right?! I went to this location with my wife with hopes to have my sweet tooth satisfied, but was disappointed due to this experience. I would give it one star, but that's just not fair because I didn't even try their goodies. Hopefully next time I'll have a better experience and arrive 5 hours before the stated closing time so I can actually see what their 4 star review is all about.

I definitely miss the old Melt location but I'm happy I was able to experience the new set up. Cookie Monster was just as delicious as I remember a year ago. They also have CBD infused ice cream, it's about $8 a scoop.

Such a great little spot to enjoy ice cream out on their lit up patio. I wanted to show my mom and brother how Phoenix does ice cream and glad I brought them here. Ended up enjoying our Lemongrass Poppyseed and Fruity Pebbles ice cream out front at 11pm in the warm, Phoenix night. The place served up quick ice cream scoops and amused my family with their Chinese take-out boxes and fortune cookie garnish. The ice cream was creamy, had spot on flavors and Melt's patio is lovely. They serve up candies and other kinds of snacks here as well. Street parking is easy and there's a couple of great places nearby like Jobot and Songbird Cafe.

Phoenix is so hot!!!! Omg lol We were exploring downtown Phoenix and craved an ice cream, we found this place (on yelp of course) and decided to check it out. The shop is in a street with houses turned into businesses and has a really cute little patio out front. Walking in we were greeted and the ice cream looked so delicious. They have flavors I've never seen or heard of before and customers are allowed 3 samples of their choice. I ordered cucumber which I definitely recommend, but you have to try the mangonada flavor!!!! it was so delicious and satisfying and it cooled me off! The ice cream is scooped into a little Chinese take out box and a fortune cookie. I thought it was the cutest thing ever! Next time I'm in Phoenix and craving ice cream I will definitely be visiting this place again. The only thing I didn't like is that we had to sit outside because there is no space or table to sit inside, but the ice cream was good enough to overlook that.

After a hot, long hike in the red mountains, ice cream is the perfect pick-me-up. I tried the Fruity Pebble, and it came in a cute little Chinese take-out container with a fortune cookie. No reason, just because it can. I LOVE the unique flavors Melt has to offer. Will certainly return to see what they will come up with next!

Probably one of my favorite ice cream spots in Phoenix. From the delicious flavors to the nostalgic candy that they also sell. Snuggled right in downtown Phoenix in the Roosevelt Row, it's a perfect location and brings in all types of crowds. It's open until midnight which is perfect. We went last night (Saturday) around 10pm, and had to wait for about 20 minutes. Unfortunately, this last visit, I had probably the worst customer service. I hadn't been in a long time, so maybe it's the norm to have such a bad attitude when serving ice cream, and everyone is ok with it because they just want to eat the delicious ice cream? Who knows? I didn't know the difference between a mini and a single, and the girl that served me talked to me like I was some idiot. So sad. She had such an annoyed look on her face with me and everyone that she was serving. It's sad to experience this type of service in a local business. Nonetheless, I'll be back! Just let me know when the grumpy ice cream girl is not working.

"Greek yogurt tastes like the ice cream they'd make in a town where dancing is illegal" • John Oliver Here on Roosevelt Row sits a cute ice cream shop. It's small inside with no public restrooms but there is a large outdoor patio area for you to chill. There seems to be a lot of stray cats on Roosevelt Row but try not to feed them your icy treats. Cats aren't able to digest dairy after kittenhood. You'll give them an upset stomach! So cute-cumber sorbet? Yes! It's refreshing, light, and oh so sweet. I love how Melt had some seasonal offerings of pumpkin pie and more ghoulish themed names for Halloween. All ice cream are served in Chinese takeout containers and are topped with a fortune cookie. Blueberry mascarpone and cherry pistachio are some of the other flavors that caught my eye. They get an extra star for their flavor combinations alone. All in all, Melt is a cozy lil business on Roosevelt Row that you should stop by if you're in the area!

Saturday. Hot. NEED ICE CREAM! Melt. is THE PERFECT place to go.... They have an amazing selection of delicious flavors (ice cream, yogurts, and sorbets), everything is locally made. The people running the place are super cool, let you sample a bunch of the flavors, and are very patient while you make up your mind. And you get a fortune cookie! (Plus the 5th St neighborhood is really cool for wandering around, checking out the street art, grabbing a coffee/beer, etc. Best area in Phoenix.) Go. Get there! Take your friends!

Great shop. Sweet treats to beat the heat. Very cool vibe and establishment. Unique presentation, great flavors. Holy hell the ice cream is good and I love how it comes in a Chinese food to go box with fortune cookie. Try the Thai ice cream.

When we first got there I noticed 2 cats on the roof and I thought it was cute. I saw the little window and I thought they live in that lil attic. The place was easy to find and we are lucky we parked at the street right in front of the shop. When got inside and the guy ask us if it was our first time and we said yes. He ask us if we wanted samples and so we tried the cucumber sorbet and superfarm. The only downside was when we purchased the cucumber sorbet the guy didn't give us a full scoop, he probably got distracted because he was talking on the phone and did not realize the scoop was not full. Oh and they're open till midnight which is cool.

This place is cute, small, and at the heart of downtown phoenix! The staff is friendly, the ice cream is good, and they support local artists. It's quite random. I ordered two scoops of grasshopper mint. DELISH! Jets the random part: they put it in a Chinese food takeout box and garnish with a fortune cookie. HAHA! You go Melt!
Thank u for existing Very good spot Believe they have more chains of this But this is my favorite that I've been to for sure .

There seems to be a curse on whichever establishment opens up in this old house, but Melt is a parlor that needs to stay. I have my booze, coffee, and food options already taken care of on this road, so an ice cream shoppe is refreshing! Tried the watermelon and cucumber sorbets. None of that fake crap like high fructose corn syrup or artificial flavor...it was all so fresh, you'd think they farmed the fruit that day. The price is reasonable, the quality outstanding, and you get to snack on a fortune cookie at the end. I have no regrets.

This place is so cute and the ice cream is amazing!!! Not only does it offer a nice range of creative favors but it comes in a super cute Chinese take out box! If you're in the downtown area definitely check this little place out!

When I travel to Phoenix for work, I always make it a point to stop by and get some ice cream. First, the weather here is usually never cold enough to stop me and second, they always seem to have some creative flavors like fruity pebbles or coffee & donuts. Best part is they'll serve you ice cream in an old school Chinese food takeout box with a fortune cookie on top. Can't beat that!
So bummed but this place is definitely not open. It is surrounded by caution tape and it's boarded up!

I was too excited to try this place! A little hard to find at night. Not much parking available. As I arrived I was immediately disappointed that there is no wheelchair accessibility! I was unable to go inside & check out all the flavors. I ended up sending in my mother to order a sampler plate. 5 different flavors of Icecream & fortune cookies are served in a cupcake baking pan. I love the atmosphere & ambiance they have achieved. Would love to come back if they build a ramp to get in.

This place was awesome! From the ice cream to the service. My sister and I had the flight (5 scoops of ice cream, served in a cupcake pan which was cool). We had the scoop of Captain Crunch, Coco Puffs and Fruity Pebbles which were so good! And the Strawberry Banana and Lemon with berries sorbet which were great flavors to cleanse the palate. Overall great place!
Best icecream ever! Would definitely recommend this to everyone. They got tons of unique ice cream flavors. My favorite is their grasshopper mint!

Hipster ice cream place. Overpriced and inefficient. Line was long because the employees were hoodlums more interested in listening to their rap music than scooping ice cream. Pretty unprofessional. The ice cream was fine but nothing special.

What an adorable little ice cream house. The girl working last night was just lovely- great customer service. She was very patient with us as my friends and I proceeded to get samples of almost all the flavors before we would commit to our pick. Lots of benches out front with bistro lights. Their ice cream comes from a local mom&pop creamery called Kristin's Creamery so everything they do is made to order and local which is just great! There are some other cool spots around here too so stop in!

Nomnomnom!!! Ice cream inside a house shack. Now that's character! Tried the cantaloupe, cookies&cream, and strawberry ice cream in their hilarious chinese cartons. The customer service is sweet too. We had great conversation about the vibe of Arizona too. Best plan of attack is goto Matt's Big Breakfast in the morn, then grab yourself a chock full of homemade ice cream here. You'll be a happy camper when all's said and done!

I miss the on location when it was attach to the RoPo apartments. It's still pretty delicious! I ordered fruity pebbles and my husband ordered brownie swirl ice cream. They had two flavors of ice cream with CBD which was creamy and vegan! There's loud music and Melt is new attached to Jobot coffee- that was interesting to experience as well. Idk I don't know if I will return anytime soon but it is a nice little sweet treat and super convenient for people who live above there!

Im appalled by the fact that during a pandemic people wouldn't be more mindful of cleanliness. This was my favorite unique ice cream spot but I am disgusted by the fact that I ate the whole thing and noticed there was hair at the bottom. Melt get it together.

Amazing ice cream! The fruity pebbles actually taste like fruity pebbles! Great flavor and presentation, with a cute spot in the art district of downtown Phoenix. The decor and upkeep inside could use some work, which is the only thing holding me back from giving 5 stars. It seems a bit shady walking into this place, seeing just a single case of ice cream, but don't let that stop you!

Although they do not have a particularly large selection of ice cream flavors, the options they do have are delicious! We were impressed by a few of the flavors we sampled, and ended up getting the cookie monster ice cream. They also have very good sorbet!

melt is my favorite ice cream spot ever. the people whom work here are very friendly. the flavors are very unique. if you use your credit/debit card you get points toward a free ice cream. the presentation of the ice cream is very unique the serve it to you in a chinese food togo box it's very different and fun if your in phoenix and want something different try melt.

Located near ASU downtown campus, Melt. is a perfect addition to the Arts' District. I mean, why didn't we have a local ice cream parlor in PHOENIX yet? The small shop is ran by a nice youthful and friendly couple and the ice cream is made with local ingredients. You can grab ice cream and take it next door to Lost Leaf and make a beer float, take it across the street to the bookstore and watch the open mic, or just sit on Melt.s incredible front patio. At first I was a little scared of their 7 dollar milkshake until I was reminded that it was made using local dairy products (and it was the most delicious shake I have ever put in my face). Melt. It's a First Friday must stop venue too!

I've been here twice already and I love it! Best ice cream hands down and on top of that it's a local business. They have a variety of flavors so you'll never get bored. I recommend to anyone who likes cereal! Never had ice cream like Melts.

Woohoo for a locally grown ice cream shoppe! I haven't had some locally made ice cream since I lived in our small college town in Northern California. After doing some shopping in the vintage shops around Roosevelt Row and sweating like crazy, my friend and I stopped by Melt. We had quite a few samples of their sorbets and ice creams including chips and salsa (with Tapatio on top). The cucumber sorbet was seriously refreshing. But I ended up with a mini-scoop of Peanut Butter. My friend also tried their Mexican Hot Chocolate and did say it was too overly spicy. Mmmmm, mmmmm, mmmmm creamy! This was seriously dreamy. Their ice cream, cultivated by Superstition Farms is incredibly creamy, smooth, and perfectly sweet without being too over the top. All the flavors I tried were very natural and that's a definite plus. You've got to love their scoops come in Chinese take-out boxes topped with a fortune cookie. Better yet, if you don't like your fortune, they have a jar full of them you can switch yours out with. Ha! We spotted their junk food cookies in their case on the way out and were very curious. But we asked the girl working that day (who was a bit of an awkward person who didn't listen to us very well) what was in it, but she couldn't even tell us. Ummmmm, okay? The cookie was HUGE and looked like it may have been some sort of peanut butter oatmeal concoction with potato chips and pretzels piled on top of it. I wish I would have grabbed one up to check it out. Maybe next time! My friend and I thoroughly enjoyed sitting out on their large patio area. It was a nice quiet Sunday and Roosevelt Row makes for a nice relaxing spot to sit in and admire.

I had seen countless of pictures of this place and its near my home so I always wanted to try it. I mentioned it to my brother and he said it was not worth it but I still wanted to try it. I finally went there and first off the outside is cute but once your inside to get your ice cream its nothing fancy. I got the mangoniada sherbert and it was just ok, nothing to rave about. I think the price was just a little to much for the taste and what you get. My friend got a different flavor don't recall the name but I do know she was not happy with it. Not a place I will be going back to.

Fantastic ice cream. I go to First Friday at least every other month, and every time there's a line that goes way out the door of this small ice cream joint. Since it's gotten colder, the line was a little shorter yesterday and I'm extremely glad we finally experienced Melt. First off, dude! They were playing 80's dance pop and people were dancing. As soon as you go past the threshold, it's almost impossible not to shake your leg to the fun retro vibes going on. The decor is pretty cool too. I don't like the description 'hipster,' but that's what this place is. A hipster ice cream joint. And it totally nails it man. So, let's get to the ice cream. There were flavors like grasshoper lemongrass, key-lime pie, and other weird flavors. The most normal one was vanilla bean, and they even spelled it a different way so that the level of normalcy was kept at a minimum. I went for 1 scoop of fruity pebbles, and 1 scoop of cookie monster. The fruity pebbles tastes exactly like the cereal. Imagine mixing milk, fruity pebble cereal, and maybe oreo icing together and chilling it-- that's what it tastes like. Then there's the cookie monster... DUDE, I'm in love with the cookie monster flavor. It tastes like oreo mixed with some kind of delicious batter-flavored ice cream that is just difficult to describe. It's seriously tasty though. I'm already craving it, and now Baskin Robbins is basic. Thanks Melt, for ruining other ice cream for me. You raised the bar way high!

Quaint little ice cream place on Roosevelt. Line was a little long, but it went by fast. We went late at night, so some things (like the waffle bowl) weren't available, but none the less still a lot of unique flavors to choose from. Good presentation, excellent taste, and great pricing for the amount they serve. The two guys working that night also had excellent customer service. Will return soon!

I LOVE THIS PLACE! Everyone i see that works here is so friendly! Ive met the owner once and hes such a cool guy. My Favorite Flavors are FRUITY PEBBLES & TARO! So amazing! I hate seeing the reviews of people saying that they dont explain things but ITS ICE CREAM PEOPLE! They have the names on there for you to see and give you samples. The place is a bit quiet and i wish they had music playing but i heard someone complained about that which is dumb. Anyways LOVE THIS PLACE! Definitely recommend!

I give them a good rating for flavor creativity but the establishment was too small for my liking and it was so hot. I tried the chop suey and butter toffee crunch. It would've been nice to have a small description of each flavor. The butter toffee crunch was melted and super soft, I'm assuming because it was really hot inside, but it was good nonetheless.

Tried the snicker doodle once scoop icecream. It was so good. Had little crunchy pieces of cookies. I loved the little Chinese takeout box they came in. They always have free stickers. Want to go back to taste more flavors. Nice customer service.
Good locally sourced ice cream and delicious homemade cones. Why don't they have malt to make shakes better? I'm not entirely sure. Even still, it's a pretty awesome little funky ice cream shop.

Whoever thought about this place is a genius! Love their ice cream!!!!! The location, ambience and everything were just perfect. Perfect for Arizona heat. Staff were chill and very friendly too. Will definitely come back to this ice cream shop.

Melt was such a great find! My sister brought me here a while ago, it was a small cute place with some very interesting flavors. The ice cream comes in cute little takeout boxes, or you can choose a cone. There were plenty of unique flavors, many that you wouldn't typically see at any other ice cream place. Theyre also open on First Friday of every month for the art walk, it's always a lot of fun to go to the art museum, walk around Phoenix, and stop by to get some ice cream with your friends (expect a long line though, because this place is loved by many).

I'm not a local, so trying this spot out was fun! A it was easy to find (through GPS of coarse) B they had some amazing flavors and C the staff was patient with our big group order. I ordered the coconut pineapple sherbet and it was refreshing, my cousin ordered the pomegranate sherbet which was also yummy! It's a very tiny place but worth seeing. The outside patio was the perfect spot to hangout. xoxo

I just went to Melt & the guy did not use gloves or use a TISSUE at least when he got the donut for my friend. That's gross. He had a cold sore on his lip, and those are very contagious. Me and my friends even think he didn't wash his hands, from how fast he got back with the donut. Not sorry for writing this review, just watching out for future customers.

This quintessential Roosevelt stoner dream hut is a welcomed, unique addition to the surprisingly limited Phoenix ice cream scene. First things first: the ice cream here IS unusually soft; however, it doesn't actually melt faster, so it's okay if you're feeling a little... zoned out. With a variety of flavors paying homage to the munchies (our favorites being Cocoa Puffs, caramel popcorn, chocolate brownie, and mint chocolate cookie), be forewarned: shit is intense. Oh, and despite being visually off-putting, the un-waffled (crepe?) cone is top-notch. Plus, there's a wee 'shmallow stuck in the bottom. The folks inside cheerily slung samples, had helpful opinions, and even complimented the local competition. I stifled laughter as an elderly gentleman ordered "a couple Molly waters," and lost count of the "Fuck Trump" stickers while waiting in line. The vibe at Melt isn't for everyone (i.e. those voting for Trump, or those who just associate 4:20 with getting to leave the 9-5 early), but I doubt there's a soul out there that wouldn't benefit from some Molly water and sugar cereal ice cream on a hot summer/spring/fall/winter day/night.

Went to see what all the hype was about. Only a few flavors available. Got a two scoop of chocolate and "get figgy with it". Cost close to $9.00 for two scoops no toppings. I'm all about supporting local businesses but feel this place is a little over priced for what you get. Quality was okay as was customer service.

Came here with some friends due to the awesome pictures we saw Instagram. We where up for a cool and different experience. What we got was completely different than what was advertised on Instagram. The ice cream actually tasted good but did not really look that appetizing. The gentleman just put a scoop of ice cream inside a Chinese box and we had to go get in line and wait for coffee from the bar that was put in a separate cup. Experience was poor, Was not aesthetically pleasing but did taste pretty good. And we didn't get any Fortune cookies either :(
