Been to this location and the east side locations many times. It's always great! My only complaint is that they need to be a little more experimental with the vegan flavors. They usually have the same two all the time. That said, they do make a great vegan ice cream. When I ate dairy, their GLBC collaborations were on point.
Excellent ice cream and yogurt. Can actually see the factory behind the counter. Service was great. Fantastic!

Their ice cream is SO. GOOD. I had a waffle cone with Black Cherry Chocolate Chip and Hazelnut and it was the perfect combo. The Hazelnut was so smooth and creamy, I didn't want my cone to end! They're more than happy to offer you samples, but sometimes that just makes it more difficult to choose because they're all so good. The space is also really great because you can see inside their "factory" and watch them make all the different varieties of ice cream. Love Mitchell's, definitely worth a stop.

I will be dreaming of this ice cream when I'm back at home! Incredibly delicious but also awesome was the whole setup at this location - located in an old movie theater, we loved the opportunity to watch the fresh ice cream being made!

My husband and I came here after going out for dinner cuz we were craving something sweet. I have to start by saying that the staff were all kind and very polite. They asked us if there were any flavors we wanted to try and didn't seem to mind when we tried more than one. My husband got the taster's trio of pralines and cream, cookies dough, and caramel sea salt (about the same as two heaping scoops in size). I found all three of his flavors very delicious. The caramel sea salt was delicious but very sweet so after a few bites you needed something to switch to or it got to be too much. I got a taster's duo (about a scoop and a half in size) of black raspberry chocolate chunk and fresh mint chocolate chunk. Both flavors were very fresh and didn't leave that "too sweet" flavor in my mouth. The chocolate chunks were nothing to write home about but complemented the flavors nicely. I also brought a brownie to eat with my ice-cream which was ok but I think next time I would just eat the ice-cream. They actually have two locations to this restaurant and this one has their factory in it. You can actually watch through the glass as they make different batches of icecream. I think watching them make the different icecreams is what set this icecream shop apart from others. I would definitely come back again to try more flavors.

Really cool. Ice cream shoppe and ice cream factory in one. I had the lemon, raspberry yogurt in a bowl. Right downtown in Ohio City. They have a Marquee for the entrance. Many flavors to choose from. Very kid friendly. Parking is a challenge though.

If I could have given 6 stars I would have! First of all, if you are unable or unwilling to consume dairy products they have Vegan ice cream, made with coconut milk instead of cow's milk and it is FANTASTIC!!! You can go upstairs (its an old re-purposed theater) and watch them make the icecream. Everything is fresh and hand made. It is fantastic. They make their own waffle cones and you can smell them baking the second you walk in the door. Very clean and very attractive inside. I can't say enough about my visit.
Such fun unique flavors and a true "local" ice cream vibe with outstanding decor and service. Try the coffee with chocolate chips! To die for...

pleasure of ice cream a treasure on the two five respite of flavor A new feather in the Ohio City neighborhood's cap. Mitchell's Ice Cream opened yesterday in the creepy old Moda space that, previous to that debacle, was a movie theater. The ice cream parlor area in the front starts with a cafeteria style line of ice creams, followed by a freezer full of ice cream cakes and pies, half gallons, and pints. Pints being "convenient single serve containers" in my book. There is a cute train that runs the perimeter of the ceiling. You can get a view of the production area through the glass partition walls. The old building's ceilings and rafters are exposed. And the re-hab of the space was done in a green and environmentally conscious way. With all of the designer ice creams out there, each ostensibly richer and sometimes weirder than the last, this stuff is not that at all. Yes, they focus on using local dairy and fruit products, but the ice cream itself is not soooo rich and fatty that your cholesterol spikes. It does not leave your mouth all slimy with butterfat. It. Is. Perfect. I had the "trio of tastes" in a cup. Banana Cream Pie, GLBC Stout with chocolate, and Rum Bobka, that was made to coincide with the shops Dyngus Day opening. Lord have mercy. I've eaten Mitchell's before, but the Rum Bobka was out of this world. The stout/chocolate had a rich coffee like flavor, and the banana cream pie had some salty bits of shortbread crust through it. Oh man... ...no words... And take note of this. After obviously throwing down hard to revamp the space, and having a live 3 piece trio playing to boot, ALL sales from the opening day are donated to two Ohio City charities, Providence House, and Malachi's. Mitchell's is a class act, and a tremendous addition to the area. Oh yeah. WAFFLE CONES!!! Carry on...

I am not really a dude with a sweet tooth. Ice cream, even during the hot summer months, doesn't hold that much attraction to me. But, you know, friends are in from out of town, and we wanted to get dessert after getting drunk at Nano Brew right up the street. (Beer and ice cream apparently make up the new Saturday afternoon food pyramid.) So we hit this place. And, man, I am glad we went. The sheer selection of delectable ice cream here is crazy pants. I got a turtle sundae while my pals got some of their other delights. It's pretty cool -- you can go upstairs to their second floor to (drunkenly or not) stare at ice cream being made in their in-house factory. A really great way to end a summer day.

Mitchell's is great. After always seeing the place packed with lines out the doors, I finally stopped by for a treat after lunch, to see what it was all about. Now I get why there are lines out the door. This ice cream is delicious. The staff are very patient and attentive to your sampling needs. The strawberry ice cream tastes so fresh and isn't cloyingly sweet. I went with the chocolate yogurt, and it was better than any chocolate ice cream I have ever had. Tangy and rich with the perfect sweetness. i can't wait to go back.

Saw the reviews of this place on Yelp so decided to try it. It is well deserved 4-5 star. The ice cream was terrific and well worth going to. If you are planning to go to Westside Market this place is right up street. Parking is only negative - on street only.
One of the best ice cream shops I've ever had! Really clean and spacious spot for natural ice cream flavor!

Go! The Ice Cream is AMAZING. My boyfriend introduced me to this place this year. Boy we are hooked and go twice a month. The seasonal Strawberry Rubarb and Coffee Ice Cream is amazing. Even a good old fashion Float is awesome. It's a must when traveling through Cleveland.

Made a quick stop on a Saturday, mid-afternoon. There were a few spaces for street parking during the summer in front of the bakery, and although the line was long, if was pretty fast. We tried cannolis, an apple tart-like pastry, and something akin to a cinnamon roll. All delicious! We will be back! Note: There is a Catholic church across the street. This seems like a great place to stop by after church!

This place was busy for a Monday dinner hour. Tip: Take a number for service! I missed it when I entered and thought I was going to miss my chance at a cannoli. Luckily, I was able to snatch one and a creme brÃ»lÃ©e. The cannoli was overly sweet and felt dry eating through it. The creme brÃ»lÃ©e surprised me at how not sweet it was (which is a good thing!) The let down of the creme brÃ»lÃ©e is that that I know it's been sitting there for some time because the top doesn't crack as smoothly when it gets torched. It was meh, I would pass for another Bakery. Another tip: $5 minimum for credit card use.

I really love the food here. The flavors are amazing. There is a large variety of choices deli style from entrees to deserts. The staff makes me laugh. They are not necessarily the friendliest but they remind me of Seinfeld with the various characters and so I actually enjoy the personalities. Just don't take their rush personally. There is always a line to the door and it's not easy trying to take care of the customers as fast as they come for the food here. Normally I would give this a 5 stars. The only reason I can't is that for some reason, my gut is sensitive to something that is being used in the food. If it was a one time thing thenbi wouldn't say anything but it happened nthreeb try imes over a month and I cannot go back no matter how much I love the food. Sometimes the best tasting food does this to my gut. There are a few other restaurants that I have had the same reaction to multiple times and it's disappointing not to be able to go back without personal repercussions.

One of my favorite Italian bakeries! We stopped in on our way to NY and bought two pounds of cookies to share with family. Coffee is strong and flavorful. There is a lot of character here because locals gather for meetings, Case kids come up the street for their yummy and inexpensive lunches and in general it's a pleasant place to hang out. We love the Napoleon cake and cream puffs!

If you ever visit Little Italy you know how challenging it is to find parking in this area! Somehow I managed to be at the right place at the right time and get street parking just as someone was leaving on a late Friday afternoon. So, I decided this was the day I'd finally try Presti's Bakery! When you enter, be sure to get a paper ticket number because they only place orders as your number is called. The treats look distracting, but don't run to them first without getting a number. I made that mistake and ended up waiting even longer because I didn't get a ticket. Its always busy and with just 2-3 people working expect long waits. They sell everything from gelato to cakes to pastries, pizza, bread, and some deli items like salads, sandwiches, and pastas. Very good selection of items! They also sell coffee, water, and other cold drinks. There is no price listing for most items, which can be annoying since the staff is only focused on helping whichever number they've called up. I found out the desserts are $20 per pound. My small box of mixed kolachi, biscotti, and nut rolls came to $10. I have to say my favorite item was the 'date nut roll.' Excellent!! After I took a bite, I wished I could walk back in and get more! Sadly that would have been a very long process to get another number and wait again. All of the other items were very good. Seating inside is ample with tables and booths. Lots of families come in. Overall, great treats! Parking will always be a problem in the area and a bit of patience is needed with the whole pick a number and wait. So, this is not a quick grab and go place (depending on when you go). Free wifi. Didn't see a restroom.

So glad we stopped here. It was a little crowded but the staff was amazing. They worked quickly to fill all of the orders of the customers in line. Everyone moved quickly; staff and customers. When you walk in, take a number. They have a great system here so no one has to wait too long. Baked goods: lots of excellent choices! We purchased a variety of cookies which went well with the fresh espressos we ordered. Loved the walnut ganache cookies! Other cookies super good too, but liked those the best. The espressos are great either hot or iced!

There are two popular bakeries across the street from each other here in Little Italy, each with pros and cons. Presti's, on the north side of the street, has a wider range of offerings and plenty of seating, while another bakery on the south side of the street has better pastries and baked goods, but no indoor seating. As for Presti's, they have all the goodies that you'd expect of an Italian bakery, including cannoli and tiramisu. I tried a piece of the cannoli and found it satisfying, although not necessarily ultra-fresh since it wasn't filled to order. A piece of stromboli was filling enough; here, note that a lot of notionally hot items, like pizze, were made much earlier in the day and were reheated. On this note, if you want a sandwich, deli item, or hot item, it's probably better to stop by during lunchtime when things are fresher or possibly made to order. Still, as a bakery that does not only baked goods but also a wide-reaching menu, this is a dependable place where you're spoiled for choice. Not to mention one that's been around for decades and has a good local following. There are plenty of tables inside, plus outside during the warmer months.

Delicious bakery in little Italy! You come in and take a number like the deli counter in a grocery store. Then you get served when your number is called. They have a variety of food including sandwiches, gelato, many pasties, cookies, and more! The cannoli and cookies we got were great!

Pastries were fine. It doesn't' even matter because of the god awful service we received. At first, I thought maybe the guy behind the counter was trying to be funny because he was being such an obnoxious di@#. He was not funny, he was just an ass. Everything he said, other than " would you like a coffee" was rude. He swung the bag with my pastry on it as he gleefully skipped to the register. He insulted How I ordered, he insulted how I inserted my credit card, and he got my order wrong. Is this guy family? Because he shouldn't be working anywhere near the public.

I have been going to Prestis since the late 70's when I lived on 126th. Normally I enjoy the experience but not on the morning of 7/26. I tried to use the restroom but the door was looked. After waiting a few minutes I tried again thinking that maybe the door was locked but not in use. I knocked but got no response. An employee walked by and I asked her to try the door. She did but again no response. A kitchen employee finally came out. I said "it's about time" his response was " you're a effin ahole " a debatable take. I asked him to repeat but he declined as he shoved his way into the kitchen. I asked the young lady, who was very kind, if there was a manager there and she called the gentleman over, I believe his name is Tom. I explained the situation, his response was " did you say anything thru the door?" I told him I knocked and asked if anyone was in there and told him that an employee had done the same. He repeated the question I repeated my answer. His response was a halfhearted apology and " everyone has to go to the bathroom " no debate there. I will probably be back to see Isaac but I will spend more time at Corbos and some of the numerous options in the area.

while traveling in italy i discovered my favorite italian pastry...sfogliatella...a clamshell shaped delight with layers of crispy pastry dough filled with ricotta and semolina and a hint of orange (...and maybe cinnamon?). i have not been able to find a truly good sfogliatella since...until my visit to presti's. frank (one of the bakers) makes a superior sfogliatella just like the ones i loved in florence...kudos, frank! now that's italian !!

Not sure what the fuck is wrong with the staff here. Don't go into the service industry if you can't communicate with customers. Was scoffed at, treated like a burden, and ignored particularly by a taller young lady with a bob haircut and a beret. Treated us like trash the entire time and laughed at us while we left the establishment. I've worked in 4 different restaurants so I understand how chaotic it can be, however this was just egregious. Enjoyed this place the first two times but will not be returning.

What a great selection of baked goods. Some simple, some unusual, some high end. All good. I love that they open until 9pm, so you can stop by for a small bit of desert after dinner. Wonderful sweets! Must stop by there if you are in the neighborhood.

Back around Thanksgiving 2019 I called around for a carrot cake and this place popped up on my radar. What I didn't ask and assumed was that they had carrot cakes available the day of. When i arrived, i was told it's a weekend item and available on weekdays if you call ahead. One of the team members did me a solid and whipped one up for me. Instructed me to come back later. I was more than happy. The carrot cake was well received by the birthday person and everyone loved it. There's a white chocolate sheet that runs through the middle of the cake and gives it a crunch. That was amazing in texture and flavor. I would say the lobster tail pastry was just a tad stale but nothing to stop me from buying more in the future. A few days later we stopped in for coffee and dessert. All the desserts were on par to the quality of the carrot cake. It was unanimous the coffees were not exactly the best. I'll keep coming back for their dessert but probably get my coffee fix elsewhere. It's street parking.

Went in at a non-busy time. Two gentlemen working the counter completely ignored my family and we couldn't place an order. A family walked in behind us and was immediately served by calling the number system which clearly said was for busy times only and there was no one there else waiting to be served. Ok we grabbed a number and as soon as we approached the counter the other guy just left and went to talk to the other worker servicing the family behind us. We left without placing an order. The only conclusion I can reach is that they are racists that work at this store as my family is a mixed race family and the people behind the counter were white and seemed to be eager to help the white family who came in after us. Please be aware of this if you are thinking about trying out this bakery.

Stopped in to make a quick purchase of a bottle of milk. They were in the process of closing and had one person working the counter and three people cleaning up in the restaurant. Literally stood at the cash register for four minutes with a bottle of milk no one else in the place except one person mine something at the counter. Finally asked one of the people closing the restaurant down/bakery hey do you sell this milk or not? Oh I only clean up he only cleans up she's the only person that can help you keep your milk keep your crappy cookies next.

Wow this was a hidden gem. We had dinner across the street & came here for dessert & it was really good. There were four of us. One had the Creme BrÃ»lÃ©e & she loved it. One had the strawberry eclair & he made sounds of utter satisfaction (lol). One had the raspberry mouse it was very light & yummy. I had the lemon blueberry cheesecake & it was delicious. I highly recommend stopping in for a treat.

I drove by a couple of times but didn't go in; looks like a great place for when we're able to gather more and walk up and down around here. Then a couple of friends picked some up and shared, and, I want to go even more. I had a sticky bun: pecans on top, doughy sweet bun, big, tasty, sticky, yum. Not the best one I've ever had, but pretty darn good. There were other options in the box that looked just as tasty, but I had been jonesing for a pecan roll and this worked nicely. There were also bagels that looked good. I'll be back someday to go in and try not to buy one of each thing in the case.

Some bakeries are just another inconsequential stop along a railroad of blandness; but Presti's has long been the final destination for top quality Italian pastries and baked goods. This Little Italy gem has been serving fresh baked goodness since 1903 and continues to set the gold standard for quality. Of the countless occasions on which I have patronized this place, never once have I been disappointed. One word of advice however, be mindful of the weekday lunchtime rush as it can get flooded with patrons from UH and other University Circle institutions. From fresh baked bread to cassata cakes, Presti's has a large assortment of authentic Italian specialties and classic baked goods That will surely satisfy even the most selective tastes. Just a few selections include cannollis, tiramisu, cream puffs, custard puffs, creme brule, cookies, cinnamon rolls, croissants, and many others! My personal favorites here are the cassata cake, canollis and the tiramisu, all of which are simply the best in Cleveland. However, you can't go wrong with any of the selections. If you're seeking the best and don't want to settle for less, Presti's takes the cake!

It absolutely doesn't get any better than Presti's Bakery. It's a must visit if you are in Little Italy. It will take you forever to make a selection because they have so many wonderful options. They have a nice little seating area to sit and enjoy your coffee/pastries. Staff is always very friendly. Nice place to visit after dinner in Little Italy for dessert or to find something to take home.
Anything I have ever eaten from here has been delicious. The cavatelli & meatballs, pizza, ALL of the bakery!!! You really can't go wrong here.

Stopped in this Sunday morning to pick up breakfast to go. Despite what other reviews suggest, the line was quite short and my food was served promptly. The pastry options were beautiful and extensive, but I chose to go with a croissant egg and cheese breakfast sandwich and a cappuccino. Let me tell you. I think I made the right choice. The sandwich was buttery, flaky, and hearty without being greasy, which is truly an art. A simple delight. And the cappuccino was fabulous, and topped with cinnamon and cocoa. Next time, I'll definitely have the cappuccino at the restaurant, as I think it would have been even better piping hot. It's Little Italy in Cleveland, so parking is a challenge, but Presti's is well worth a few drives around the block.
Wonderful! Nice staff. The food is perfect. A little pricey. I never leave without spending over $35 on just a few items. Lower those prices! Always busy, especially on the weekend.

A great bakery in the heart of Little Italy. It was the only place open semi-late (9pm) on a weeknight in the area where we could grab dessert. I ended up with the cappuccino brownie and it was fantastic. Some of the staples like cassata cake were already sold out but they had quite the selection of desserts still available. Staff was very friendly and made each customer feel like they were at home.
I should have known how good this bakery was by how busy it was on a Friday night. Delicious variety of Italian pastries and desserts. You won't be disappointed!

Give me one of everything! Every time I come here I end up going home with way too many baked goods and everything is stellar. I haven't tried one thing that I wouldn't buy again. I've custom ordered birthday cakes here as well as just picked out things from the bakery shelves. This place will not disappoint either way!

Their baked goods and pastries are to die for!!! The cake with strawberries is my go to and their lattes are refreshing as well. Don't really enjoy the food to be honest,but I frequent this bakery for its breads, cakes, and cookies!! Such a pleasant cafe in Little Italy to go with friends, for a date, and even by yourself to get some work done.

I've come here for years and years, and their bakery section is amazing. Their Stromboli and pre-made foods are absolutely delicious. The customer service is usually friendly as well... but recently (11/18) I had an experience that left me a bit shaken and sad. I was with my husband and 2 friends and couldn't wait to show them Little Italy. We decided to go in and get food to go and eat it in the park. The moment we walked in, the staff behind the counter treated us like we were not welcome. Especially the dude with the glasses and the grey mouth covering. He was rude, impatient, never thanked us for stopping in. We ordered Stromboli to go and he didn't offer to warm it for us and left out the marinara sauce completely (something we didn't realize until we were at the park). I asked him a couple of questions and he pretended not to hear me. It was very, very obvious what was happening. My friends and husband were all very upset with how they were treated and it really put a damper on the entire day. I have a large feeling it's because I was holding my husbands hand when we walked into the building (because we are gay). It was very obvious that we were being treated differently than the rest of the people around us. I even told him (mr. glasses) that he needed to work on his manners and he didn't bat an eyelash. Just kept staring at me like he couldn't wait for us to leave. Needless to say. I've gone here for years but won't be back any time soon.

I went here with my family to get some desserts for my birthday. Their selection is amazing and everything we got was fantastic. I especially loved the strawberry eclair I got and the cheesecake I tried was amazing to. My sister enjoyed her cookies and my parents liked the cakes they tried as well. The desserts were delicious while not being to heavy and we all really enjoyed what we got. I will definitely return in the future to try more of what they have to offer

only have one picture because i just can't wait to take the picture before devouring the food presti's have one of the best iced latte i've had in the area. love the baked goods as well - so far i've had their tiramisu, carrot cake, custard puff and coconut bar. I love how they're all perfectly balanced and not overly sweet like most desserts here in the US. The carrot cake i had to go back multiple times because they don't always have them. The coconut bar is by far my favorite - it's similar to lamington: chocolate sponge cake in the middle, coated in chocolate icing with shredded coconuts on top. my complaints: - prices are relatively high and they're not clearly marked so you have to ask - the place gets BUSY and the line moves SLOW. Sometimes you may have to wait for half an hr before getting served - the staff isn't super clear on the ingredients. I wanted to see if the date nut bar is vegan and two of the staff just said, you can reasonably assume there's butter inside
The best bakery in Little Italy! Hands-down. The variety of authentic treats isn't going to be matched anywhere else. The taste? Chef's kiss perfect!!!

This is seriously one of the best bakeries in Cleveland. I am in love with the cappuccino brownie and think they have one of the best cappuccinos in the world. I kid you not, I made a special trip here when I was in town for a business trip. When I used to live here I loved doing work at the cafe seating!

Let's just get this out of the way: is it safe to walk in and order at the counter? YES. Everyone is masked and they enforce social distancing. Now, the good stuff! Hands down the best Italian bakery in NE Ohio, and honestly, probably all of Ohio! I've been coming here since my teenage years and this place has gone from a Naples, Italy-style (I know, because I was just there last year) small storefront bakery to a brick and mortar cafe and bakery with dine-in options on the same street, on the same block! Why? Because they bake consistently delicious pastries that keeps customers coming back with lines outside the door. You want cassata cake? No problem. How about 5 different flavored cannolis? Sure thing. Tiramisu? Of course! Cheesecake? Italian or NY style? They have both! Sfogliatelle? Hells yes! Macarons and macaroons? Both, in about 20 different flavors, plus many, many more delectable traditional Italian and New World pastries. Can I get a side of cavatelli to go with my dessert? Defnitely! It's made from scratch. So are the meatballs, sausage, peppers, and marinara sauce! Mama Mia!

This place is a must try when in little italy, cleveland. They have a huge selection of cookies, pastries and cakes. It's mesmerising. They also have hot foods, anything from pizza, strombolies, sandwiches and pastas. We stopped in around lunch time and it was jammed. You must take a ticket and wait, but it is definitely worth it, plus it gives you time to decide what you would like. We ordered the blueberry cheesecake, cannoli, lobster tail and a piece of cassata cake. Everything was delicious. The cannoli was one of the best I have ever had. Cheesecake was nice and creamy and not overly sweet. Lobster tail had nice buttery layers with the soft marzipan filled center. The only disappointment was the cassata cake. It seemed old. The cake was dry, the strawberries were mushy and did not have a great flavor. It could have been because it was during the "Feast of the Assumption" and they made a ton of them. Even with that we would still return next time we are in little italy.

If you desire being treated rudely, this is the place to go. I went from being so excited to patronize them to wishing I never set foot in there. I can assure you I wont ever again. I don't think it's necessary to treat a kind customer like dirt on your shoes...shameful! By the way...this was a geeky dude with glasses and known for his nasty attitude. If he is so incapable of being kind, helpful or humble as he takes your money which goes toward his paycheck he should be fired!

Where else is there an eat-in bakery where you can find great Italian pastries AND Italian food? Nice atmosphere and good seating. Anything in Little Italy I support, because those people don't "buy into" the narrative and they don't collect stimulus checks to close down their businesses! We NEED people like this Everywhere!!!

I've only ever visited Presti's Bakery for breakfast, which I think is why my opinion is in conflict with so many other reviews. They specialize in sweet pastry items and haven't mastered the other options on their menu quite yet. -- Food -- I ordered the Sausage Breakfast Sandwich, which is a croissant with egg, American cheese, and sausage. I honestly wouldn't have been surprised if everything other than the croissant was from the Jimmy Dean freezer section. The cheese wasn't melted, the egg was burning hot in some places and freezing cold in others, and the sausage was noticeably dry. This dish was clearly microwaved, despite the fact that I ordered just 20 minutes after the store opened. It was a little over $5, which just doesn't seem right for something reheated. My friends ordered a breakfast sandwich and French toast and had a similar opinion of the food. This is the first time I've ever seen my friend not finish a meal. The French toast had sesame seeds in it, which leads me to believe it was just bread they weren't able to sell the day before. -- Drinks -- The restaurant boasts a large espresso and coffee menu. However, their customization options are abysmal. For example, the only milk options are whole milk or soy. I ordered the mocha and couldn't finish it. It was unnaturally sweet and served with sticky canned whipped cream running down the side of the cup. -- Service -- No table service. Service is typical of a bakery, you order at the front, wait for your order to be filled, then you can take a seat if you're eating in. When I arrived, my three friends and I were the only patrons in the bakery and they had already ordered. There were two people working the counter, but they were handling orders separately and not working together. The man who took my order took nearly 10 minutes to make a mocha and microwave the breakfast sandwich I mentioned previously. He seemed to be annoyed to be at work and was very short with me and uninviting. Not impressed. -- Stars -- Service: (0/1 Stars) Food: (0/2 Stars) Drinks: (0/2 Stars)

Presti's. We've been coming here for for over 25 years. Kathy has been coming here even longer than that (I think add at least another 20 years, shh). I think they do a very good job with lunch items and their prices are reasonable. Coffee is decent and the baked goods are worth the calories and the price point is fair. I have other places in the area that I like more for baked goods, deli food, and coffee. However, no one has a combination of quality in all three off those categories, plus price, and pretty fast friendly service. And the clincher for Presti's is atmosphere. There's an ambiance I can only describe as a little worn, a little chic, a little hint of Cleveland attitude (in a good "it is what it is" kind of way), along with a dash of theatre. Or maybe that's the espresso kickin' in.

I would have given it a higher score, but two things stopped me. First, let me say, I loved the area and the atmosphere. With COVID, it's a bit challenging, but the area has a great vibe! I needed a cannoli. I was excited to try this place on a Saturday night, after an Italian dinner (the Italian restaurant I went to didn't have desert). Being a New Yorker, growing up with some great Italian food, the best cannoli are the ones that are filled when you order, not pre-filled and sitting there. That said, it still had a bit of crunch with the shell. That said, the one thing I didn't like, the cannoli had a hint of lemon flavor, which for me was really different. Perhaps that's their twist on the standard cannoli, but I'm more old fashioned and traditional. To me, it would have been better without the flavor. Still, great vibe, lots of deserts to try! I'll go back!!
Can't say enough great things about this place. It's all great eating !!! It is a perfect fit in little Italy.

I gotta admit this place has grown on me. Now that I know to avoid the cold food items (all entirely unremarkable and lacking in hearty flavor e.g. caprese salad just hard small tomatoes, bland mozzarella balls, and small shreds of basil which may as well not exist thus leading to a spectacularly bland caprese salad), I've come to appreciate the deliciousness of their tender rum soaked Rum Baba cake ball thing and their tiramisu and absolutely chocolatey decadent mousse. Basically order from the case on the far left with the top shelf bakery items and skip the other stuff and you'll come away satisfied! Also the employees are always upbeat and never rude despite having multiple very busy jam packed times throughout the day where people must take numbers with standing room only to wait.
We stopped here when we were in town for a visit to the Cleveland Clinic. The choices were overwhelming! So much deliciousness in one place!
The lemon bars and napoleons never disappoint. Efficient service. It's tough to leave here with fewer than four goodies in your box. A must stop whenever I'm in or near Little Italy.

Items Selected: Sausage and Pepperoni Pizza Amaretto Lobster Tail Sfogliatelle Cannoli Lemon Biscotti, Slivered Almond Cookie, Pignoli, Nut Horn, Turtle Cookie, Helen's Date Nut Bar, Raspberry Thumbprint Located at 12101 Mayfield Road, just a few hundred yards from Corbo's and the rest of Cleveland's Little Italy, Presti's Bakery has long been a favorite of neighbors, tourists and Case Western Reserve University students, the family-run space originally founded in 1903 most certainly having withstood tough times, yet still doing great business. Sizable in its selections as well as its seating options, a lack of the latter admittedly a problem at its nearby competitor, entry to Presti's sees diners confronted by nearly one hundred selections both sweet and savory, everything from Pizza and Pasta served as early as 6am with Pastries rolling out all day to replete diminishing favorites. Using an old-school ticketing system, many diners unaware and thus delayed in placing their order at the counter as they are redirected to the red device on a poll, it was after a bit of perusal that most composed an order by way of ever-patient servers, a total of eleven pieces comprised mostly of cookies delivered in boxes and paper trays at the end of a $16 tip and tax inclusive assortment. Approaching 10:30am, essentially lunch hour taking the day's plan as a whole, dining began with a flimsy slice of square Pizza that strongly resembled something from a Highschool cafeteria, even after rewarming, all but a few bites discarded before progressing quickly to the pre-filled Cannoli, the Mascarpone filling smooth and sweet, but the shell already besieged by sogginess. Happy to again see Sfogliatelle, small bits of Fruit giving this iteration a leg up on Corbo's despite a shell that was not quite as springy and shattering, best bites of the meal were found in the lightly Almond scented Lobster Tail piped full of Cream filling, the Date Bar and Pine Nut Pignoli also highly praiseworthy while the Nut Horn and Slivered Almond Cookie each begged for something more than water to combat a texture that was more dry and stale than nutty and crumbly.
Tiramisu is great, Napoleon is so so. This place is always busy! Be prepared for some noise, not necessarily the best place for business meeting
The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. The food was quick, very reasonably priced, and delicious! The pastries, even better! Definitely try a cannoli!!

I tried the gelato at Presti's and loved it! I got chocolate and appreciated the rich dark flavor. I would definitely go back to get a few sweet bites of this awesome bakery's gelato. Also, the selection of other pastries and drinks was very large. Parking is hard to find so try coming here on a less crowded day.

If you unfortunately must have lunch at this establishment...get Tiramisu for dessert. I'm not going to tell you what to get for lunch. They're not worth mentioning. Tiramisu should offer subtle, warm sweetness from the Mascarpone cheese and egg cream batch, balancing with the right amount of bitterness from espresso in the lady fingers and cocoa powder layer. If the cheese layer does not have a tint of yellow, that means the recipe removes the egg yolks. If using only egg white, yes it enables an airy body, but it's not worth it to lose that warmth that only the yolk renders. It should NOT carry any sour taste, not even a hint - that means cream cheese is used. Cream cheese does not belong in Tiramisu. We're not making cheese cake here. Whipped cream also should NOT be used. That's just lazy cooks attempt to create the illusion that the body is airy. I make Tiramisu at home. Whenever there is a potluck occasion, the only dish I bring is Tiramisu. Hence you can say Tiramisu is the signature dish of my kitchen. When I go to Italian restaurants, I used to always order tiramisu, just so that I can critique it. This includes restaurants IN Italy. Presti's tiramisu is one of the rare few that reminds me of my own. There may be a little variation: I don't have electric mixer at home, AND I steam bain-marie the raw eggs in case of salmonella, so my Mascarpone cheese batch is denser. I usually make mine into 2 layers, whereas Presti's is one layer. For $5 worth of cost, mine is six times bigger than Presti's. But since I can't feed the whole CLE yelper community with my masterpiece, get your fill at Presti's.

After a great dinner nothing is like a freshly baked pastry and a hot cappuccino with whipped cream. They have so many freshly baked pastries it is hard to pick, I recommend the chocolate-covered cannolis.

Overall, this is an amazing bakery in a must visit part of Cleveland. The lines can get long at times, and I have waited as long as 30 minutes before, but the food is worth it. Excellent assortment of pastries and larger desserts. I think the lemon bar is among their best desserts. Their canolis are good but not the best I've had. If you're in the Little Italy area definitely go visit.
It was fine, not busy and the pastry was good. I got a latte and a cinnamon apple muffin

I love their date and nut bars... But something in the process of making these former favorited delights must've changed, as I experienced biting into hard bits of shell on two different occasions. I sent them a message on FB but perhaps the didn't read it, as I didn't get a reply. Oh what to do. I still recommend the chocolate dipped cannolis, but as November is upon us, I have to remind everyone that Presti's personal sized pumpkin pies are precisely the splurge for the self-loving needed to DEAL with the upset of seasonal climate change. Winter is coming, but so are these limited-time-only pies. If you're lucky to have one (all for yourself), buy an extra one to-go. Take one now, and another in the evening, before bed... With every bite, pause to think about what you love about being you. Once the last morsel is gone, think about what you love about living in Cleveland. Remember these things when you're shoveling snow. If you come in a day too late, all that will be left is some pouting about, waiting for a whole 'nother year until it's time for November pie again. Come get this pie. Sadly, I am in Oklahoma and Florida for all of November. You are not me. You are better than me. I am (hopefully) receiving mine in the mail. Presti's pumpkin pie, AKA November pie.. Not to be confused with Patterson's Fruit Farm pies.. which are also wonderful pies, available year round... read about it on Yelp ;)

On my road trip to Cleveland, my friend took me to this bakery in Little Italy for breakfast. I had a chocolate croissant and 2 raspberry thumbprints. The pastries were both very good and for the price of $3.5, I would definitely come here again if I visit the area again.

Cute place! Their tiramisu is delectable, we had it for a friend's birthday and its consistency is so creamy and thick, it's ice cream like. The sides are aligned with light and fluffy lady fingers and it was a joy of a cake! A cake shared between about 6 people came to $30 so more expensive than other small cakes for not a huge party but it was surely a treat. I also always get their cafe au lait and sometimes there is too much milk added and not enough coffee but for $2, it is still a good drink! The outdoor seating is super nice overlooking mayfield and Murray hill. The way the bakery is placed allows plenty of sunlight and I can see myself on a less busy day coming here to read or just sit and enjoy the sun! Try their discounted bakery goods as well! You can get muffins or croissants for just $1 if they are a day old and they have other discounted goods like crostata and Turkey sandwiches.

My family has been patronizing Presti's since shortly after they opened in 1903. (I live in Seattle now, but a stop at Presti's is a must when I'm in town). This is a neighborhood institution. Their pastry displays are jaw-dropping, and they've probably got the best gelato selection in the state. The chocolate cannolis are amazing, and their Americano is the best I've ever had, (Starbucks can take a flying leap). Great variety of pastas and pizza by the slice, and a great neighborhood vibe.

Holy cannoli!!! If you're in Little Italy, you need to end the night at Presti's. Even if it's to-go. The casada cake is delicious. I buy the lemon biscotti in increments of 10. And they have gelato! You can also get food (not just dessert) there. The Stromboli will hit the spot. When you walk in, don't forget to take a number, or else you'll be waiting a long while!

If you are in Cleveland, Ohio and looking for sweet goods, I strongly recommend Presti's, an Italian bakery located in the Little Italy neighborhood || Pictured is their Silvered Almonds, which I thought I would love since I pretty much anything Almond, but this wasn't my fave. I think the soft texture turned me off || However, their Cassata Cake, Carrot Cake, Red Velvet Cake, Lemon Coconut Cake, German Chocolate Cake New York Cheesecake were incredibly delicious! || I have to say the Cheesecake wss by far thee best I've ever had, it literally melted in my mouth || Now hold on now, I didn't have full slices of each and every cake mentioned but did get an opportunity to taste throughout my several visits to CLE

People think that the slogan "Cleveland Rocks" revolves around the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame? King James' Cavaliers? Nope. It's Presti's. Throughout C-town's roller coaster existence, the boom and bust from Mistake on the Lake to the Birthplace of Rock and Roll, one neighborhood has enjoyed prosperity: Little Italy, with great restaurants and monster good bakeries. The queen of the leavened, and now, I think, the only big one left, is Presti's. They've added sandwiches and remodeled a couple of times, but they've left the character of the place in-tact. More important, the baked goods are still AMAZING. Over three decades, they have been the saving grace of a bad trip to Cleveland Clinic; the point of discovery for my kids' college hunt summer trip a few years back; and a place of celebration for the youngest who capped off his discovery of how great Case Western Reserve University is with a macaroon and the most light delicious cloud-like tiramisu on the planet, over perfect espresso drinks. To locals, who probably think that such places are the norm, don't take it for granted! They should tag the building with an endangered species tag. Gone are the greats in New York, a few remain in Chicago, and a handful here and there. For the tourist, whether you came to see Elton John's outrageous outfits, a basketball or baseball championship run, or just enjoy watching your NFL team bash the bumbling Browns, you MUST ditch the diet for a day and make Presti's a destination.

We come every Sunday after Church! Every pastry is delicious. There is something for everyone! A must is their cappuccino - they sprinkle cinnamon on top and is heaven in a cup. Try buying a loaf of bread! It is fresh every day - comes out around 10:30am and is only $2! Pro Tip: grab a number ticket at the front! They don't do lines. Numbers are needed!!!

Loved long ago by my parents who used to go to Presti's early in the morning after late night parties at CWRU. Back then, they knew it as a "hole in the wall donut shop." Now this bakery is posh, far from a hole in the wall. Glass cases with all sorts of treats and delicious food. Loved the chicken Marsala, roasted potatoes, and brussel sprouts! Can take items to go as well. ***Note: don't forget to take a number when you come in! Only complaint is that employees are not in a rush - expect to wait for a little bit even if there is a small line. Always love prestis

Definitely one of my favorite spots in Cleveland. I pass by Presti's almost everyday and it's so hard to not go in and get something. Presti's is a bustling bakery in the heart of Little Italy that offers a wide variety of pastries, desserts, bread, coffee, gelato, as well as hot food (mainly Italian). There's ample indoor and outdoor seating, making it a great place to hang-out or study. Unless there's no line there, make sure to first take a number by the door and wait until it's called. Then someone from behind the counter will take your order. It can get pretty busy so I would avoid coming in during the lunch rush if possible. Now onto the food. The pastries and desserts are BOMB and definitely their best . My favorites are the tiramisu (perhaps one of best I've had), chocolate mousse cake, and the cannolis. I'm warning you now: it's going to be hard not to overindulge. They also make a darn good mocha (my gf thinks it's the best she's ever had) and have a selection of hot food, such as pastas, sandwiches, and pizza slices, that hit the spot. Also, sometimes they provide you utensils but sometimes you have to get it yourself from the concession stand so make sure to double check. The prices are on the more expensive side but I think it's worth it for how good the pastries and food are! Overall, Presti's is an established and reputable place that has never disappointed. It'll always be worth stopping by and picking up some tasty treats from here!
Staff were very rude and made us feel very unwelcome, but the drinks were good and the area is very cool!

A quintessential Italian bakery with a very tasty (albeit limited) lunch menu. Everything in the bakery cases is delicious, so just go hog-wild. Everytime I come here, I buy an entire box of baked items because they're just that good. The staff are friendly, although not admittedly speedy as has been mentioned before (the person preparing your stuff kind of does everything themselves, so heated orders or complex orders slow down the line). And parking is Little Italy, so mentally prepare for that. That said, any time I have a free afternoon, I find any reason that I can to come by this place. Thanks, Presti's!

everything about prestis bakery is absolutely amazing. the bakery itself is adorable inside and incredibly clean. the food is FANTASTIC and reasonably priced. staff is very kind and attentive. my absolute favorite place in the world to eat. the finest bakery I've ever been to by far.

Great hours for a bakery - skip dessert wherever you have dinner or have a sweet breakfast at Presti's! Cannolis and all pastries are excellent. Cookies are average so skip those for the good stuff. A Cleveland MUST!
Cafe mocha and coconut lemon cake. Nothing like a sweet snack before supper. And,cookies to go.

Presti's can be really hit or miss. It's definitely the most popular bakery in little Italy but it's a little overpriced and I haven't enjoyed all of the bakery items I've tried. I would definitely suggest sticking to the cassata cake, cannolis or their assortment of Italian cookies, which seem to be pretty consistent in quality. They do have a wide range of food items including baked sweets, gelato, hot drinks and hot prepared food and they are a convenient dessert stop if you are grabbing dinner in little Italy.

We visited Presti's while visiting Cleveland for personal business. The place was busy but efficient and it was very clean. The cannolis were delicious and all pastries looks appetizing. The reason for the average rating was the service, which was horrible. The individual that waited on us acted like it was a bother for us to be there. His demeanor was so dismissive. We are tourist so maybe our expectations were too high but usually when you are offing people money for food, they act somewhat nice. Not here. Good food isn't enough for us to return to Presti's because I'm sure we can find great cannolis with good service in the Italian portion of Cleveland.

This bakery is really excellent. I last came with my family for a mid-afternoon snack. We ordered a meat Stromboli and an assortment of desserts- a slice of sorrentina cake, a classic cannoli, and a creme brÃ»lÃ©e. I have always loved the cannolis and creme brÃ»lÃ©e here, so those were fantastic as always! The sorrentina was tasty, but there was a layer in it that I didn't really enjoy, so I probably wouldn't order that again. The stromboli was pretty solid as well. Also, even when this place is super busy, everyone behind the counter is always super nice and helpful, and their ticket system for getting through orders is really efficient. Overall, a great little gem in little Italy that I'll definitely come back to whenever I'm in Cleveland!

I came in for a cannoli but when I saw all of the choices, I opted for raspberry mousse. So light and airy. I also bought an iced coffee. It's a busy place. Make sure you grab a number as soon as you walk in and start making your decision so you can keep things moving.

I visited with a friend and ordered Pepperoni bread and a few pastries. The bread was a good savory quick bite. I really enjoyed the bread --even though simple, it was fluffy but also chewy. Remember to ask for the dipping sauce on the side. The mini fruit cheesecake was okay but nothing spectacular. The cannoli was also fine because I really like chocolate, but it was kind of difficult to bite into. The cream puff was the tastiest even though it was slightly messy to eat. I think I'm general my expectations were very high because a lot of people hyped it up for me.

Long wait on a Saturday afternoon, and there was no way to social distance. But, the wait was worth it, and everyone had masks on. I really enjoyed the cannolis. Unfortunately the only ones they had, had chocolate chips in them. Of course, some people would find this to be a great enhancement! The thumbprints we're delicious and had a strong almond flavor. They also had coconut bars that tasted like a chocolate pudding cake.

When in Little Italy, Presti's is a MUST! The meatballs are handmade and yummy. The sides are delish. And there are so many fresh baked goods to mention. You may have to take a number due to the crowds but it is truly worth the wait. Try their coffees and cocoas also!
Best bakery in Little Italy. Been coming here over 20 years, cookies are awesome, half off specials, pasta salads, gelatos

Always delicious pastries and cookies. Never a disappointment. The best coconut bars around! Very clean. Friendly staff. We love going to Presti's Bakery!

On this most recent trip I ordered a chocolate dipped coconut macaroon, a handful of Pignoli cookies (my absolute favorite cookie), a cinnamon bun and a handful of thumbprint raspberry cookies. This place seems yo have it all! They have savory items that you can eat for lunch and dinner and they have all the delicious pastries/cookies you can think of as well as a well sized selection of gelatos and even an espresso machine to make your favorite coffee drinks.

Service bad. Disappointed with the cold shoulder and dismissal of the staff. Especially the man with the glasses and grey bandana. I have been there many times before, greeted with great staff, but this time was different. I am not sure if it was because it was loud, cold, or just a bad day, but he was very rude. When I asked if it was good to take the food he waved at me with the dismal like a dog and shortly said "Bye." At first, I was not sure to take this personally, but by the way he called out numbers and spoke to other customers, it seemed that is just who he is. I think other customers felt similarly. I got a lunch special from the counter (my first time) and it was just okay. I am not sure if I will be back. This store is a really mixed bag between good and bad service, food quality is decent. Really just disappoint me, the first time a waiter/employee has ever treated me this way in general.
Italian cookies, coffee, and savory options are great! A great place to relax and chat with a friend or people watch outside.

We stopped in at Presti's for the first time. Great selection and we looked forward to a great dessert. After taking a number we began the wait. There were approximately 8 customers in front of us so I expected a bit of a wait. After 35 minutes I was on the verge of walking out, as others had done. Although there were 4 employees there only 1 was helping customers. After ten minutes he left, went to the deli area, waited on 2 customers, chatted with them awhile and left the bakery customers waiting. One employee at the bakery counter was wrapping loaves of bread into bags for future sale, never thought to ask the group of customers if they needed help, just kept wrapping and ignored the group. Finally, made my selection, and walked out. The products were great but I would not go again. Amateurs all.

This place is no joke. Came on a Saturday night around 10:30 PM and this place was jamming. They have such an amazing selection of Italian pastries and gelato as well. You can tell that there is a lot of respect because there was definitely no shortage of people who were wanting some yummy treats. Very well organized as I have you take a number and then one person helps you and then rings you up. Even though there was a little bit of a wait we ended up with some delicious tasty treats such as cannolis, blueberry cheesecake and chocolate chip cookies.

I've been coming here since I was in high school and it's like time doesn't change. I love their cases of cookies, both large and small in size. My favorites are the small, tea cookies- chocolate ganache and raspberry and apricot lindzers. The tiramisu and other pastries do not disappoint- I'm just usually too full for them after a large meal at one of the nearby restaurants. It's also a great spot to grab some prepared food too. Don't forget to grab a number upon entering! And if you can snag a table outside with a coffee, then you'll feel like you've stepped into an Italian sidewalk cafe.

I used to work in Cleveland and every Wednesday was Doughnut Day... the company would spring for doughnuts for all the employees, and would buy the doughnuts ONLY from Presti's. Let me tell you that I have never had a doughnut so delicious... I have become utterly spoiled and cannot possibly eat a doughnut from Dunkin or Krispy Kreme, they are just awful when compared! I haven't tried anything of their's other than the doughnuts, but if the doughnuts are this damn good, the rest must be great as well!

A classic example of a great Italian bakery that happens to serve very good food too. We stopped by for lunch and it was busy - always a good sign! I got the Italian sandwich which was terrific. Super fresh roll made it delicious. Came with a tremendous homemade coleslaw. Other members of our party had chicken parm sandwich ("good not great"), meatball sandwich, chicken salad and pesto tortalini. Chocolate cannoli was also really good. Very reasonably priced, with drinks came to around $34.

Love this place! They really do have the best Chocolate Cannolis in Little Italy. They also offer a wide variety of Italian baked goods as well as other food such as pizza, sandwiches, and salads. I have also seen people doing work on their laptops here as well but I don't know how productive that you would be since this place is usually very busy. Parking is a bit hard to find since it is street parking and personally I've only ever walked to this place from my apartment. This place is perfect for an afternoon catch up with a friend or a coffee date. Check out this place if you're ever in Little Italy!

The cassata cake is really delicious & wonderful--and worth the trip alone. There are lots of other treat options, coffee, and a great seating area to hang out w/friends or read, etc. A delightful spot to stop by in Little Italy!
So busy but the pastries are worth it. I had a cannoli and the tiramisu and both were excellent and traveled well back to my hotel.

I can only speak to the dessert section of Presti's as it's our go to bakery when in little Italy. The cannolis are always on point and never overly sweet which is exactly what I look for. The gelato is flavorful and a great texture, so don't be afraid to grab a few flavors and split among your group. There is a large selection of Italian baked goods where there is something for everyone. Each time we've been there the baked goods are always fresh and what you would expect from an Italian cookie or cake. The line moves quickly and is ticketed so you can move around to explore before you are called. If you are in the area, I would definitely suggest stopping by for a dessert.

I had Presti's cater an event for my residency program. For the dinner, we ordered 2 vegetarian stromboli, 1 sausage strombolo, 1/2 pan of meat lasagna, 1/2 pan of vegetarian lasagna, and 1 pan of salad. Overall, our experience with the staff was phenomenal. Our order was done on time, and the staff helped me carry the order out to the car. They also had receipts ready as I left. Ordering over the phone was easy, and every person I interacted with on the way was wonderful. As far as the food goes, overall, we were wowed. Lasagna: Excellent. Both the vegetarian and meat lasagna were a hit, and definitely fed more people than we thought they would. There was a great amount of cheese, and everything was perfectly cooked and seasoned. Stromboli: The meat stromboli was a hit, but the vegetarian strombolo was not the greatest. Don't get me wrong: it was good, but I probably would order something else off the menu; the inside was a bit bland, though it was well cooked. Salad: Pretty standard salad overall: Lettuce, tomato, olives, cucumber. Fantastic balsamic dressing that everyone loved. I will absolutely have Presti's cater another event, and I am excited to eat more of their delicious food!

Kill me! I want everything when I walk in. The food, the desserts, the cookies , the gelato.... I honestly don't know how to control myself. It's always super busy. You pick a number. It's like being in NYC. LOVE!

The food is great, this low review is because I am extremely disappointed by their lack of recycling. The amount of cups, cans, bottles that this place goes through on a daily basis goes to rot in a landfill- for any profitable business this is unacceptable. Do better for the world that allows you to run a profitable business. Great deserts tho.

Visited after lunch on Fri 11/17. Very crowded so we grabbed our number and waited while peering at the tremendous selection of cookies, pastries, pies, and cakes. There really is something for everyone. Our party of 7 each had something different including creme brÃ»lÃ©e, cheesecake, assorted cookies, chocolate croissant, and brownies. Also had espresso and cappuccino. Everything that passed my lips was delicious. Parking was tight in the area, and the wait was long, but we ultimately enjoyed the experience.

This place has some amazing pastries! The seating areas is decent and it's easy to find since it's on the main strip of Little Italy. The cannoli and lobster tails are really good and worth getting. The cookies are also authentic Italian cookies! The parking isn't great though. A lot of the street parking is very narrow there's a bunch of construction in the area. There was somewhat of a wait since it seemed they were understaffed and the employees seemed flustered. They have an old ticket system that you have to grab a number in the front.
Wow, I understand why there is always a big line to get there bakery. Best crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e ever and there mocha was awesome.

Holy pastries Batman! Oh my goodness! Talk about some amazing mouth goodies, I'm so grateful that as a newbie to the area, a colleague recommended Presti's to me today. I had no idea what to expect and was blown away. I'm gonna start by saying that the pecan roll was truly one of the most delicious things I've eaten in my life. Truly. I am already daydreaming of getting back and ordering it again. I'm ashamed that I don't remember the names of the other things that I ordered as I'm not very familiar with Italian desserts. The pine nut cookies (pagnoli?) we're also frickin' delicious. I could've easily devoured 10 of them. The other pastry (flaky puff pastry layers with lemony, maybe clove and orange? Filling) was also really tasty and unlike anything I've ever eaten before. I also brought home a loaf of warm Italian white bread that I will be toasting and eating with my eggs for breakfast. The vibe in Presti's is high energy and quick paced. Don't forget to grab a number when you walk in the door.

Presti's Bakery in Cleveland's Little Italy began as a humble shop in what was definitely a not very trendy working class neighborhood at the turn of the century ... not this one, but the one before. While the demographics may have changed, they appear to have remained consistent and keep on thriving. I already knew how I'd be rating them and I'm right in there with the pack. I look at the rare 1 and 2 star reviews and wonder what they're all about. Then, even 4 and 5 star places have valid 1 and 2 star experiences by the rare few. Fortunately, these are outliers and, if that's what someone actually experienced, then that was unfortunate. While it's in Cleveland, where the Great Lakes Midwest meets the Northeast, Presti's looks like it could be in New England. It looks homey and beckons you to come in. And, should you go in, you will be greeted by a line and you will have to take a number ... and be patient. Presti's is mostly about being a bakery, with the left two thirds of the lengthy front counter being dedicated to desserts, cookies, and breads, with some of them being fairly elaborate. There is also lunch fare such as pizzas, hefty sandwiches, focaccias, salads, and even some pastas. Those looked good, but nowhere near as tantalizing as the desserts. And their baked goods are what they are known for. You should not go here every day though, on one visit, I made back to back trips to Presti's! I've tried about four desserts, but two have been committed to memory. The first is their cannoli with the chocolate shells. The second, and my favorite, is their Italian cheesecake. I am not a fan of the sometimes bland taste of ricotta but, given how it is blended and metered into the mix, the cheesecake was excellent. The service ranged from being perfunctory and polite to being enthusiastic and friendly, and they are always crowded. The pricing is a little higher than what you might expect for some items, but you get what you pay for. The interior is both old school and modern. There are floor to ceiling windows in front, but the rest of it has older wooden tables, chairs and booth type seating against the wall, and one of those old school (copper) ceilings. The crowd is eclectic, considering that this is both a touristic area and that it's a few blocks east of the city's main train line, while Case Western Reserve University is a few blocks to the west of it. Wrapping it up, the sum total of the parts here is quite good. And, when they had run out of Italian cheesecake, the young lady helping me summoned an Italian looking guy who told me that some was being made and asked me if I could wait. I did. And he even brought it out to the table. For those complaining about parking, I have to laugh. Presti's is neither in Boston's North End nor in San Francisco's North Beach. The parking is doable and, if this vexes you, take the train to the rapid station only 1 or 2 blocks away. Lastly, when I ordered a chocolate cannolo and a slice of Italian cheesecake, I ordered the exact same items to be put into a box so I could give them to a friend since it was coincidentally close enough to her birthday. If my friend, whose parents ran an Italian restaurant, got a (by then) stale cannolo and slice of Italian cheesecake and sang the praises for Presti's for several weeks after that, then that really says something. Presti's is in a league with the sorts of Italian bakeries you'd find in New York, Boston, or Chicago, though probably not in any points west of those.

Being from the Cleveland area, I was long overdue to try Presti's. I have lived in Columbus for over 10 years, but every time I'd go back to the CLE area and we'd head to dinner in Little Italy, it was typically a Sunday and Presti's would be closed by then. Luckily, I scheduled a date night with my boyfriend on a Saturday in Little Italy. We went to Mass, dinner at Mia Bella and then over to Presti's! I was so excited! However, when we walked in the door, the first thing we saw right away was a serious cluster. There were people at almost every table, however none of them with food. And then there were about 20-30 people hovering around the cases with no clear line in sight. We walked around for a bit trying to find the beginning and end of the line, but there was none. We also saw signage to "take a number" but we couldn't see anything pointing where you were supposed to take a number. Luckily, I spotted a woman with a paper number in her hand and asked where she got it from. It was hanging on the first post to your left when you walk in. We got our number only to see there were ~30 numbers in front of us. We grabbed a table inside and waited it out. It did take quite a long time, but they have signage up front so you can see what number they are on. We walked up to the glass case a few times to see what we wanted. Honestly, everything here looks fantastic! You can spend so much time just looking at everything (hence why there was a huge blob of people up front the entire time we were there). I'd say overall it took about 30 mins from the time we walked in to the time we were taken care of. A tad too long in my opinion. At one point, we counted that they only had one associate working for that many customers. Luckily, he was eventually joined by a few others. I couldn't decide between the cheesecake and the gelato, so I ended up getting both! I got the cherry cheesecake (the round one, not the New York slice cheesecake) and the stracciatella gelato. My boyfriend got the chocolate cheesecake, a very sweet option for him. I was kind of annoyed though because my boyfriend asked if they had any cassata cake left as we had just seen another customer take the final slice. My boyfriend said that if they didn't have that, he'd order the chocolate cheesecake. The associate said he'd go back and check and he was gone for a bit, came back out, put a slice of chocolate cheesecake on the tray and told us our total. I thought it was kind of rude that he didn't even say "Sorry we are out" or anything. Overall, I found the staff there to be kind of short, overworked and not really pleasant. We wanted a seat outside, but the tables were packed....all with people who had no food. It was frustrating because some of the people out there had been sitting out there since we got there. So I don't know if they had food and just finished it and were chillin out there for 30+ minutes or if they were loitering or what. So we took one of the only empty tables inside and sat down there. Overall, I enjoyed the gelato. I wish it had more chocolate in it though. Tasted a tad too vanilla. Also, I didn't love the cheesecake. It was just okay. I felt like it was the type of cheesecake with that "lemony" flavor to it, even though it was cherry cheesecake. I guess I could expect that from an Italian bake shop. Next time, I'd like to try the NY style cherry cheesecake. I had a bite of my boyfriend's cheesecake and again wasn't overly impressed. Tasted like it came out of a box. Overall, I'd definitely go back because there were a lot of different things I'd like to try. However, I think they need to get a better system in place because there are just way too many people standing around and/or sitting down with no food. Also, the sweets I had were just okay. Looking forward to hopefully updating my review in the future.

Good for lunch. The food was very tasty. Homemade everything. The sub sandwiches are huge. It is a popular place, so allow some time to get served. Don't forget to take a number when you walk in the door or you'll be waiting extra long.

This amazing little shop rivals any pastry place I've been. Huge selection of sweets and savory. Lots of seating. Great for people watching on Mayfield. Charming atmosphere in a great location. Perfect for grabbing a little after dinner treat or sitting with a cup of coffee and chatting with friends.

Waited 25 minutes here to grab 1 cannoli to go! No regrets! Very family friendly and date friendly establishment for a yummy treat in Little Italy. Most guests enjoyed a pastry/cake with coffee at tea. Adorable!

The bakery is awesome all the bakeries around in Little Italy this is far the best there baked goods have flavor and they actually taste like baked goods. There Canola Cake is the bomb and it rocks so if you want good homemade baked pastries and cakes I strongly recommend Presti's bakery in Little Italy. 5 stars all the way

If you love fresh made Italian pastries, I know who doesn't, then you MUST take the time to check this place out. AH-MA-ZING Cheesecake is to die for. Chocolate custard puff was perfection. The cannoli was better than anything I have tried in New York Worth the trip to Little Italy Cleveland just to eat at Pesti's

Every time we're in Little Italy, we make a trip to Prestis. We love the antipasti and the pre-made hot items. Particularly the breads and Stromboli. But the real star: the sauce and the cookies! They have a huge selection of baked goods and Italian cookies. My Italian boyfriend was like a kid in a candy store. We ordered cookies for his family and they loved every single one! If you're ever in little Italy, Prestis is a must visit!

Located in Little Italy, Presti's Bakery has lots of options as far as treats, lunch (pizza & sandwiches) & ice cream. There's some traditional Italian snacks as well as Americanized sweets. Inside & outside seating available. There's a restroom inside as well. I had the Italian sandwich & espresso - both were OK. Nothing spectacular, but not bad. With the sandwich, you get the option to add chips or coleslaw as a side.

Food and bakerys great, but this place has gotten to be so slow, takes 15 to 20 min just to get your number taken even when its not overly crowded, which doesnt make a lot of sense when all of the food is pre made.

Love, love, love this place! I live in Seattle, but whenever I'm in the Cleve, I always make a point of coming here and ordering tons of cookies. Last week was no exception. I bought 4 dozen assorted Christmas cookies and they're almost gone. Sadly, they don't ship, and there isn't an Italian bakery in Seattle that is even close!

What a horrible experience when they decide to LOCK the doors at 8:52 and they close at 9:00! I was horrified when the staff chose to LOCK the doors early at 8:52 when they close at 9:00 and 2 customers were waiting to enter. I'm Italian and I'm shocked at the behavior of the employees that felt the need to lock the doors 8 minutes before it was officially closed. I don't understand why this "unacceptable" behavior is now commonplace in our society today. I really feel like they should be ashamed of themselves for their selfish behavior.

I have been lived in Cleveland for more than my year but have not been to Presti until yesterday. It was awesome. No wonder so many of friends highly recommended it to me. I and my friends orders something to go. It was a nice brunch at home. Having the cheesecake and the coffee together makes me so relaxed and happy. The Italian cheesecake is perfect. it is not expensive at all. The cannoli is not as amazing as the cheesecake but it is ok too. I was so amazed by the food itself that I even forgot to take some pictures. I am so glad I finally try Presti's bakery before I leave Cleveland. Highly recommend it.

I hadn't been to Presti's in years, and now I remember why. The days of the pride that bakeries like Corbo's and Presti's use to have is long since over. All it takes is a few generations, and a lack of wanting to preserve something of value, and just general laziness, to ultimately lead to a businesses downfall. I ordered a breakfast sandwich and asked them to toast it in the toaster oven to heat it up. The outside seemed warm enough, but when I bit into it, the egg was luke-warm, and the sausage was cold. I asked if they could put it back in because it was still cold; the reply was "not after it has crossed the other side of the counter." Seriously? She said, oh well you can use the microwave... Sure I could, if I want to have a soggy mess!!! If you are going to sell pre-made breakfast sandwiches, expect your customers to ask to have them heated up. Or better yet, take some PRIDE in your work, and make them fresh!!!! I should have demanded my money back. I will NOT be going back. Customer service is LAST on their list
Just came in from Long Island, decided to stop by for a quick bite. From the coffee to the sandwiches to the pastries you can tell everything was made fresh and with love. Can't wait to visit again.

Been here a bunch of times over the years and was never that impressed by its offerings, but figured I would give it another shot since it had been awhile. If I'm being honest the baked goods look much better than they taste. The chocolate chip cookies were rather average, and hard, which I prefer soft to. The Napoleon was bland and didn't even come close to comparing to Farka's in Ohio City. Oh well.

Asked the guy for 2 cappucino and 1 macchiattoooo!!! All served in cappuccino cups!!! He started heating the milk and got it to the point to burning the milk/foam as it was whistling continuosly. Then he started filling the cups with a spoon. Woot!!! Please!!! U are italian bar not MCcaffe!!! Staff was unorganized and scattered everywhere. Its used to be great place but 90% empty tables at and a crowded line at the cash register is not good.Dissapointed!!!

When I first went to Presti's years ago, they just made donuts. It was a tiny little shop tucked away in Little Italy. Since then, they have expanded to lots of Italian pastry, and delicious meals. The chicken Parmesan with a little nest of angel hair pasta is delicious. Their Italian sausage is sweet but has a little spice to it and it's my favorite in town. The prices are reasonable. Their pizza is traditional and sold by the slice ...take a couple home for later!

Meh! Crazy busy at 730 pm on a Sat night. Very noisy. Tried a cannoli and a chocolate torte with cannoli filling. The torte was mediocre at best. Cannoli was ok but I've had better. Very overrated on my opinion!

The atmosphere and friendly service create a sincere atmosphere. As delicious as the many cookies appear in the well lit cases, they are tasteless. I am a baker and am consistently disappointed in the cute little nuggets of dough.

Oh My Goodness BEST Cannolis EVER!! WOW this place is the real deal and a must try!! This Bakery is in Little Italy of Cleveland there is street parking but not a lot we got lucky and got a place right in front of Presti`s!! There is outside seating and also indoor seating, the service is excellent. We went try there Cannolis I had heard the were very good, there was not any in the show case so we asked and she checked in the back she came back and said it would be 10 minutes we said that fine we ordered some pastries and two double espressos, and by the time we were done she came out with are Cannolis. We ordered a Lobster Tail which was so delicious and my husband had the blueberry Cheesecake also very good. We brought are Cannolis home and had them the next morning and WOW I swear they are the BEST Cannolis EVER!! Very nice Bakery very clean place with nice seating area, they also sell gelato and cookies and a cafe menu for lunch I really can`t wait to go back for another visit. The waitstaff that helped us was so friendly and was saying how sorry for the wait for the cannolis I said it was really no problem we were not in a hurry and enjoyed have some pastries and espresso

We came to Presti's and were overwhelmed by the sheer amount of people in here! It almost looked like a madhouse - but Presti's has a method to their madness. People can grab a number by the entrance and wait inside/look around until they hear their number being called. Once the Presti's employee shouts out their number, customers can go to the front to place their orders. Presti's employees will loudly shout the number twice before moving on to the next number. We ordered some strombolis but they were adequate! Definitely did the job for some Italian food, but I wished there was something that wowed me more.

If you are anywhere near Presti's Bakery, you must stop in and get something. Not only do they have THE BEST cannolis, cookies and cakes but they have sandwiches and all kinds of salads. Really delicious food, sweets and breads. YUMMY!
Best Stromboli and cannoli. Excellent customer service and don't miss the gelato. Parking may be little struggle but you will definitely find a spot. Their cookies is delicious

Amazing! What a cute little bakery. During my too short stay in Cleveland I kept hearing about competing bakeries, and I'm glad I checked out Presti's.
