No matter what generation you are from, Milk & Cookies are NEVER going away!  ------------How the cookie crumbled------------ During a recent trip to Las Vegas, I tested the 80's theory that Milk does a body good and went to the Milk Bar located inside the beautiful Cosmopolitan Resort.  Im gonna be honest... not to detour you,  not to shape your opinion, not even to make you think twice... But my family and I were just not fans.  True story...  You know the saying, "Don't cry over spilled milk?" Well, crying we did not. (Read more for why)  We ordered a cup of their Cereal Milk soft serve with sprinkles and a prepackaged confetti cookie.  The cereal milk soft serve looked pretty, but was way too sweet and just was not our thing.  The cookie although fresh, tasted a bit chemically/processed and we landed up tossing it after a few bites.  About 100 feet from Milk, our 3 year old dropped the soft serve on the floor after each of us just having a bite or two.  Normally, I would cry after dropping 14 bucks on a dessert that I only got 1 spoonful of, but because 1 spoonful was all I needed to form my opinion of whether milk truly does a body good, I think next time I will just order a bottle of Elmer's glue and call it a day.

Not sure what the hype is about? I'm a diehard ice cream and sweets lover, but I just couldn't put my finger on anything that wow'ed me. - Compost cookie: almost *too* sweet. Texture was not my cup of tea. Have had better cookies. - Soft serve with the corn flakes: you could recreate this at home with some softened vanilla ice cream and cereal. - Birthday cake balls: probably the best thing I tried. At least it was moist? But have also had better cake pops. It left me wondering why there was a line at opening, but perhaps we just didn't try the right thing.

Came back to Milk Bar with a few coworkers & LOVED the soft serve cereal milk along with the milk bar (aka crack) pie slice! I was disappointed with the cake balls & the cookie - simply because they were prepackaged & didn't taste fresh AT ALL! Only go for their fresh baked / crafted goods! Get their pre-made at a grocer back home!
Cake was great! Employee was very nice! Prices are almost what you would expect, but the serving could have been slightly larger for the price. Either way, now I can say I've tried Milk!

Going to milk bar in person has been on my bucket list for several years. I've gotten the milk bar pie and cookies delivered once and became hooked. We got the milk bar pie and ice cream and I was blown away. I'm so obsessed with the cereal milk flavor in the ice cream that I couldn't get enough of it! We also tried a White Russian which was also so good if you're wanting a sweet-milkshake-style drink with some alcohol. It was all I wanted and expected!

Some of my friends are OBSESSED with Milk bar, going as far as to order an entire cake for special occasions, so I knew I had to try this when in Vegas. I ordered a slice of the classic birthday cake and it was good but not "best thing I ever ate" good. And certainly not worth the $15 for one slice of cake. The cake was a little dry and crumbly and the icing was good but, again, not anything to write home about.

A little pricey for the portions but worth it if you're looking for a one of a kind dessert. Everything is expensive in Vegas so no real surprises there but the flavors were worth every penny. If its your first time I highly suggest you try the Milk bar pie or the Cereal Milk soft serve.

For me, it's the story behind Christina Tosiand her legacy she has made the food world. Yes, it's expensive af for a slice and is very questionable for non-foodies. However, highly recommend Chef's Table on Netflix (Season 4, Ep 1) before getting something from here. The original store is in NYC so this one does not have the same magic, but is good when you are craving some of her classic desserts and you happen to be in Las Vegas. We were celebrating my mom's birthday so I got a slice and surprised her in the hotel room. The Birthday Cake definitely hit the spot!!

Looks pretty, but tastes pretty bad. We got the cereal milk ice cream with birthday cake and sprinkles. The first bite was extremely unsatisfying and honestly pretty disappointing considering we paid $19 for a pint of it. The birthday cake crumbles are super dry and have a distinct salty taste which is so off-putting in ice cream. The sprinkles are giving everything they've got to save the entire experience but unfortunately it's not enough. If I were you, I'd seriously consider going to one of the extremely overpriced convenience stores in the hotel and getting an overpriced ice cream as it'll be better than this and you'll still come away spending less money. You've been warned!!

I've tried Milk's cookies and other treats in LA and was not a fan.. Decided to give them another try but their soft serve this time. I got the Cereal Milk soft serve with corn flakes and omg... somehow the soft serve tasted SOUR?? Like the milk in the soft serve has gone bad. I couldn't get past 2 bites.

Atmosphere: Milk is a small stand inside the Cosmopolitan. We thought the fluorescent sign in the front was cute and great for pictures! Service: The service was solid. The line to get the treat was a bit on the longer side, but other than that, we do not have much to complain about. Food: We ordered a cup of the cereal milk soft serve with toppings of sprinkles and cornflake crunch. This was such an aesthetic cup of soft serve that looked really tasty and refreshing; however, our mouths would say otherwise. The soft serve had very little taste and tasted vaguely of plain milk with a hint of old cheerios in it. It definitely wasn't the sweet or rich milky ice cream we were expecting. Additionally, the sprinkles and cornflake crunch were alright additions but did not elevate the dessert except for looks. Overall: While Milk had such a cute aesthetic both in terms of the stand and the dessert, our cereal milk soft serve was perhaps some of the most underwhelming soft serves we've ever had. The only reason we would come back is to try other desserts or to take a picture of the soft serve and then melt it to use as overpriced milk.

Disgusting ice cream. It was the worst I've ever had. Peanut butter ice cream tasted like salt. The cereal milk was slightly better. We didn't finish our cup. It was way too soft serve. The next day we got Ben and Jerry's and it was phenomenal. Don't waste your time at the milk bar it was awful.

Just as amazing as I remembered! They had gluten free birthday cake, it was delicious and the slices are huge so more than enough to share. It's located on the second floor in The Cosmopolitan, very easy to find walking in from the strip.
Every time I'm at Milk Bar, I gotta grab the chocolate bday cake truffles! They're a cute little treat for myself but are a great addition to a birthday gift for anyone who has a sweet tooth!

Get Momofukos next store and come out and get a little dessert. First impression...too small for price. Then I ate it. Well...inhaled it. Ate it too fast for a pic! Milk bar pie...aka crack pie. In the age of sensitivity we don't call it crack anymore. But my body tells me otherwise. I'm a "crack" junky. Step aside bitches the crack is mine! Christina Tosi...I love you! (Shhh...don't tell my wife! You supply the crack pie and I'm yours!)

If you're not yet deeply acquainted with the Milk Bar birthday cake, that should be your next priority. Best. Cake. Ever. And the slice from their Vegas outpost didn't disappoint. Chocolate was also delicious. Cereal milk soft serve is great, but the cake is where it's at. Cookies are also amazing, but sticking with my cake for now. Service was friendly enough. Busy. Crowded. But fine. All totally worth it.

This place is basically just living off its hype. In my opinion it's way overpriced, but for some reason my wife loves it, so we still get something every time we're at the Cosmo. Don't get me wrong, the desserts are pretty good, but just be prepared to pay a premium. We usually get some form of the cereal milk ice cream and the pie. The cookies come packaged and in my opinion don't taste fresh, so I wouldn't recommend them. Service has been great every time we come.

I've heard a lot about Christina Tosi's milk bar and even seen the chef's table episode. I was not disappointed when I tried it. My favorite thing on the menu was a crack pie. It's this gooey butter Cookie bar that's absolutely delicious. I'm originally from St. Louis so I've had many of those St. Louis gooey butter cookies and this is exactly like it. The birthday truffles were good but, not as amazing as I expected them to be. The texture is a little bit off I'm not your usual cookie dough. It's a little bit more powdery and chalky. Overall, a great dessert option and with the try!

milk bar pie : 10/10 perfect texture on the outside while having a nice chew in the middle. very rich flavor and so good while warm cereal milk soft serve: 9/10 had a nice crunch from the cornflakes, and the ice cream had just the right balance of salty and sweet

I had to try this place after seeing Milk Bar all over social media. The Cereal Milkshake was definitely different and I loved it. It tasted exactly how you'd think. My only complaint would be the cereal chunks were hard to chew from being so cold and almost stale. Their cookies were also good, but a little dry. I would recommend it to everyone once, but I don't need a return visit.

I watched Christina Tosi as a master chef judge and was curious to try her desserts. Although the hype for this place is good, the prices are outrageous, however the quality is better than other dessert places I been to. And for the size of the dessert, it's a no go for the price. I got the bite sized cookie dough flavored confetti and it was really good, it was one of their truffles. The others were the cookies and they tasted kind of like any other cookie but with a different flavor than your typical cookie. The three cookies ran for $11 and the flavors were confetti, marshmallow and blueberry. The cookie truffle was 7$ and you get three small balls. It was definitely an experience that will be remembered. Was it worth the price tag? Hell No! But was it worth the experience. Yes! I would say give it a one time try and call it quits. I wouldn't go back, but the dessert is very good. Service was nonchalant. The employee that served me was kind of boring and annoyed about the pandemic, but pretty much everyone is. They wore gloves as well as having a clear shield in front so you don't come in contact with the employee. It's a mess but it is part of history for us folks.

I've had Milk Bad before but really wasn't a fan. I don't get the hype and popularity. The only thing I like are there cookies. Specifically the blueberry cookie. The chocolate bday slice of cake was ridiculously expensive and not really worth it. The cream was tart and.could do without it. The line moves along .

I wanna like this place so bad. I have been three times. I have now tried the cookie, cake, and cereal milk ice cream. The cookie was average, but still pretty good. If I return I will stick to the cookie. The slice of cake was extremely expensive. While is was aesthetically pleasing, the taste of the icing was not my favorite. The cereal milk ice cream with corn flakes was honestly the nastiest thing I have ever eaten. It tastes like spoiled milk, and the combined taste corn flakes with it grossed me out. I just have to worn people before they spend the money. If you do buy this, get the insta photo- then immediately throw it in the garbage. Also note the cornflakes are not included with the ice cream.

Iconic is Milk Bar's "Cereal Milk Soft Serve". As with my love at first lick of it many moons ago in NYC, elated I was of this fab treat at Milk Bar Las Vegas. Including the lick off the top, mmm, yum, was each of the wicked wooden spoonful of sweet and savory creaminess along with bits of crunchy corn flakes. Along with the friendly and efficient service, rejuvenated I was after a tough day. Must admit also, 100 times better Milk Bars are vs their trucks. CHEERS!

Honestly... I ordered the b-day cake because the cashier said it was the most popular item on their menu. Walmart b-day cake tastes better! Their cake was dry and the butter cream was extremely sweet. Also ordered a cereal milk shake and threw that out after a sip. Wasted $45 including tip. I did it so you don't have to.

An update is overdue for this place for a couple of reasons. For one, I didn't review the birthday confetti cake which is quite legit. Sad to say that most cakes in America are t that great to me, but the chocolate birthday cake was a pleasant surprise. The chocolate was not too sweet and was rich with the perfect amount of cream cheese frosting to balance it all out. There's been some new investors, hence, the famous "crack pie" has a new name now and they've gotten rid of the cereal milk soft serve with crack pie pieces. Or maybe that was an insider menu item but they offer you to buy them separately and make your own soft serve with the "crack pie" pieces. Bring it back, though, because it's a unique masterpiece. If you're a chocolate lover, the chocolate birthday cake gets a solid 5 stars, and I'd pick it over the white confetti.

overhyped, poor customer service, and wayyy too sweet. i had heard milk bar was overrated but i still wanted to try it for myself. turns out it's just one of those gimmicky instagrammable dessert places
We HAD to get a slide of the birthday cake. Was it an amazing slice of cake? 100%. Was it worth $15? Nahhh

If I could give this zero stars, I would. This was some of the worst desserts I have ever had. My boyfriend and I bought the chocolate birthday cake, chocolate shake, and cereal soft serve, and all of it tasted horrible. You will have better spent your money going to eat dessert at McDonalds after chowing down on one of their forever burgers, because while that food might be incredibly bad for you and difficult for your body to digest, at least it is a pleasant experience eating it. This place, these desserts, will not be a pleasant experience. Horribly gross. If disappointment was a food, this would be that. I for the life of me do not understand why this place is called, "Milk". The food had hardly any milk if any. It only consisted of sugar. The chocolate cake: It was very dense and served cold. Not a huge problem except that there was no chocolate flavor. It was just sugar. Each bite contained lumps of cake/sugar that when bit into, my mouth could only comprehend the acidic taste of straight sugar. Any chocolate or wheat or anything else about the cake was immediately lost to this overpowering sensation. The consistency of this cake was also atrocious. It was dry, crumbly, lumpy, and gummy. The frosting was basically solid and only sugar. It was like they took a block of sugar, watered it down just a little, and slapped between the solid blocks of cake. Not to mention, the slice of cake was about 40% frosting, leaving almost nothing to show for a $13 slice of cake. The chocolate shake: As with the cake, there was absolutely no flavor to this shake. It was just plain sugar, with the addition of being suspended in what I thought was milk but who knows? I couldn't taste it so it may have been the ejaculate of Pillsbury doughboy for all I know. They literally took the chocolate cake and blended it up with this mystery liquid and put in a cup. It was so hard to drink, because the solid clumps of cake were clogging the straw and eating them was even less satisfying because they had no flavor, only sugar. The cereal soft serve: This mysterious concoction must've been made by an elementary school student who thinks that "fun dip" is the pinnacle of high quality desserts/snacks/candy. Again, there was zero flavor, but there was the overwhelming sensation of thick, sugary, nothingness. Imagine that white fun dip stick that you would dip into the fun dip as a kid. Now forget about the fun dip itself, and imagine that fun dip stick flavor. Now imagine that fun dip stick but in the form of very thick "soft serve ice cream". That was probably the closest description of the so-called flavor of this "soft serve", and even this description is generous. I got some strawberry jam topping, which improved this concoction only slightly. It was still bad, but there was at least something that resembled some form of flavor that was distinct and not just plain sugar. Overall, I wish I could go back in time and just go to McDonalds instead, because going to McDonalds would have been a far less disappointing experience and actually enjoyable.

I first tried Milk in New York and was a fan, so was excited when they opened up a Milk in Las Vegas at the Cosmopolitan some years back. I order their Soft Serve in a cup ($6.00) and added the Cornflake topping for an additional $1.25. Their soft serve is good, but it's nothing extraordinary. It definitely needed the cornflake topping; the cornflakes added that extra crunch and touch of sweetness. It honestly wouldn't be milk 'n' cereal without it! The only drawback was the $7.25 price tag for some soft serve. Definitely on the pricier end for what you get!

mmmmm Yummy in my tummy!! This was a late night snack at like 12 am so we walked down from our hotel room and walked to this place. The cereal milk soft serve is featured here and it tasted like what milk would taste like in your cereal bowl LOL! It was tasty(but a really light taste) and just something to satisfy the cravings. Yea the price is a little high so hopefully there's a price reduction?

Christina Tosi is my favorite baker. The treats and desserts you get at Milk Bar are unlike anything you have ever had before. The success of Milk Bar can be summed up by saying it's the perfect combination of science and creativity. Cookies (4-5 stars) All are at least 4 stars but the sure winners are the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow Cookie (which tastes like Frosted Flakes had a baby with a chocolate chip cookie) and the Compost Cookie (which incorporates salty treats to the sweet cookie to create a flavor explosion). Crack Pie (4.5 stars) - Don't think of this as pie. If you compare it to traditional pie, you may find it odd. Think of it more as if a butter cookie was fused with pie crust. It's unlike any dessert on the planet. It's equally as buttery as it is sweet and very satisfying. Cereal Milk Milkshake (3 stars) - The first few sips are incredible. It really does taste like cereal milk blended with ice cream. BUT it's incredibly sweet. So sweet that my husband and I couldn't even finish TOGETHER their smallest sized shake. If you can handle a ton of sugar, go for it! But if you're a weakling like me... maybe pass or just be OK with throwing some away. Birthday Cake (4.5 stars) - It's visually stunning! The cake is very spongy and light. And there are funfetti cookie dough crumbles throughout. This would be the world's perfect cake if it wasn't for... CHOCOLATE Birthday Cake (5 stars) - I normally don't like chocolate cake that much. I almost always prefer vanilla. But this one, WOW! The cake tastes like an Oreo Cookie in cake form. And the frosting tastes very similar to Oreo Cream. Also... We bought this cake and I totally forgot about it (because I normally don't want Chocolate cake). I ate it a whole WEEK after we bought it and the cake was still soft, spongy, and fresh as if it was just made that day.

Sign me up buttercup for this trendy dessert bar! My favorites include the cornflake cookie and sprinkle cookie, but I never leave without the scrumptious Sprinkle/confetti cake in tow. The cake is fluffy; the icing is smooth, light and sweet. And the rainbow chips give a nice sweet crunch. But buyer beware, expect 4x Vegas prices at this joint. Worth every penny though!
The milk bar was tasty to satisfy a sweet tooth. I enjoyed my small dessert and pie. Hip and fun, great for some good desserts.

I had heard a lot of hype- the birthday cake was overpriced and completely dry. After letting it thaw, it was even worse. I also tried the French toast flavored ice cream. The cashier pointed to the French toast ice cream picture, I paid, and what came out had no toppings on it. That was frustrating, but worse was the taste. It was like salted butter ice cream. I ended up taking 2 bites, and literally throwing it away at the pink counter. You'd be better going to ANY other dessert place around.

Came here for dessert after dinner one night. I've heard so much about this place but never had a chance to visit. We got a slice of birthday cake and a chocolate birthday milkshake. Everything was so good! Can't wait to come back soon and check out the rest of the menu.

I'm not a fan of cereal but had to try the soft serve here . We just had dinner next door but saved room for dessert here at Mill Bar . The girl working the cashier was so friendly and helpful (5 stars to her ). She gave me a sample of the cereal milk soft serve to try before purchase ). It's about $6 and another $1.50 for toppings . I loved the crunchy corn flakes topping but thought the soft serve was oddly salty . The consistency was nicely thick though. I'd return to try other items though :)

This place unfortunately did not impress me as much as I was hoping it would. We tried a variety of things: crack pie latte, Birthday latte, one whole crack pie, cereal milk ice cream, and birthday truffles. Needless to say, we spent a pretty penny. The ice cream did initially taste like vanilla but then shifted into a cereal milk aftertaste which I found unique. This is probably what I was most impressed with. The crack pie latte is, as you can imagine, extremely sugary. It is without a doubt the most sugary lattes I've ever had and we were not able to finish either latte because of how sweet it was. Unfortunately, the problem was that all I can taste is sweetness and there was no unique or even coffee flavor. If you're wondering what the crack pie tastes like, just imagine pecan pie. It basically tastes exactly the same and I honestly don't think it was worth the money. I'd rather go to Cosco and get a big, thick pecan pie. The slice was so tiny and so thin with not that much filling in it, I don't think it was worth it. One slice is around seven dollars and one whole pie is $52, not worth it. The birthday truffles were really good, they tasted like cake pops with sprinkles but once again, I don't think it was worth the price.

Located inside the cosmopolitan casino. No dine area but their is a separate seating area a walk away. We got 2 birthday cake shakes and coffee shake. The coffee shake was about $11. Wished they either filled the cup more or added whip. They have some shakes with alcohol too.
You need to go here early, they run out of items very easily. Enjoyed the chocolate birthday shake.

I haven't tried their baked goods, but I came for the soft serve. It was cereal milk flavored. The actual flavor was OK, but I didn't like the texture of the soft serve. I'll be back to try the some cookies.
Excellent! The birthday cake is the best cake ever! Also yummy is the crack pie. It's open till 11am so it's the perfect place to get your dessert after that fancy meal.
I got the vanilla soft serve with fudge topping. it was very good but significantly overpriced for what it was. Now I can say I tried it but we wont be getting it again.

An awesome pick me up for anyone looking for a quick dessert option on the strip! So many creative flavors, but our favorite is the cereal milk soft serve by far! Just a fun easy ice cream spot with a little something for everybody!

Honestly came here cause I really wanted to try the birthday cake at least once in my life. I wouldn't say it's worth $14 for one slice but when in Vegas, ya know. It tasted like a normal funfetti cake but I actually quite liked it. A little to sweet for my liking but super flavorful! Probably wouldn't get it again though for the price.

The cookies are definitely not worth it. (Maybe the ice cream and shakes are). We stopped here for a visit bc i was interested in trying some of the treats that Christina Tosi is known for. This was particularly true since I've considered signing up for her online baking class and love to watch her judge MasterChef Junior. Imagine my surprise when, after paying $4 per cookie, we were handed two shrink-wrapped pre-packaged items, the Confetti and the Compost. Don't get me wrong, they were tasty, but at that price point we are expecting fresh-baked, preservative-free cookies at a minimum. The cookies didn't particularly WOW either of our taste buds and I'd say they were probably on-par with other cookies I've had from Panera that are larger AND cheaper. I will say that I was surprised at how the pretzels retained their crunch. But my husband's stomach ended up being unhappy for the rest of the evening which typically only happens when he consumes a preservative that disagrees with it. Would not recommend, go to Bouchon Bakery instead for your fix.

Cute place to grab a quick coffee and dessert while walking around the strip. I opted for the compost cookie and would get it again in a heartbeat. Only thing I wish this place had was a place to sit down and enjoy your drinks & desserts.

Like a lot of other peeps on Yelp, I heard about Milk Bar from Netflix. I saw the owner tell her story on some cooking program sometime back. I was intrigued since back then and knew I had to try Milk sometime. I'm so glad I had the opportunity to do so! We liked their baked goods! The only thing I regret is not having one of their ice cream cups that so many on here rave about. We considered going back but unfortunately ran out of time. I had one of their boozy corn flake milkshakes. It was delish! It gave me a good buzz since it included Vodka and Kahlua in it. I wonder if the ice cream's taste is similar? Minus the booze of course! My bf had a chocolate boozy shake and it was also really good. We bought a few of their cookies, their confetti and compost. The compost was sweet and salty. It was interesting...My favorite was the chocolate confetti. The white confetti was just OK. They sell some of their baked goods online. I'm considering ordering some more. They are a bit pricey but not too too bad. The lady who was helping us was very nice and helpful. We explained that it was our first time there. She explained their baked goodies in detail to us. I still need to try their ice cream! I will come back whenever I'm in town again. We hope to go back to Vegas in a few months. For now, I'll just settle on buying some more cookies online. Milk Bar is located inside of Cosmopolitan on The Strip.

They only had one soft serve flavor as an option. Soft serve was good. But with the lack of variety only one of my kids consumed and I was running around looking for an alternative option for my other son.

We came here while walking along the Vegas strip and then craved it the rest of the week. I ordered the legendairy cereal ice cream which was so unique, creamy, and had a slightly nutty/rich flavor. My kids and husband loved it too. Small servings and high prices, but it's worth it. We also tried the Compost cookies which tried to stuff every possible ingredient inside with the end result of delicious chewy crunchiness: oats, potato chips, toffee candy, pretzels, graham cracker crust, chocolate chunks.

I love this place. Christina Tossi is a genius. I have not been here in a while and they have made a few changes. Still the same quality and flavors. The newest one I tried is chi late birthday cake. Yum. Today I asked them if I could have the cup in the 3 flavors. Chocolate birthday cake, crack pie, and cereal milk. Mixed in a few sprinkles and you have a winner. Definitely stop in and try some of their cookies. The compost and the chocolate cornflake marshmallow are the best!

I was always eying this shop every time I went to the cosmopolitan to eat, but I really don't know what I was thinking. I hate the taste of cereal milk. 75% of the menu cannot really be enjoyed to it's full potential for me, because of my wheat allergy. And it was all so overpriced. I assumed it would taste good but the reviews were not bad, and the store had visual appeal. I ordered a regular coffee shake without the alcohol because actually wanted a pick me up before we left Vegas. But I couldn't even finish. I mean, if cereal milk is your jam, go for it. But if you are like me, you never even bother to drink the milk as a kid after eating your Cap's crunch or Lucky Charms, you're not going to like where this is going. It is completely down to personal preference, but I can't say that I understand the hype at all.
I got the chocolate confetti. Wasn't all that. I prefer the boxed one I get at Whole Foods.

I really wanted to try a slice of cake or a cookie because I'd heard great things about Christina Tosi's desserts. But, we were merely passing through, so we shared a soft serve ($6) with cornflakes ($1.50 extra). The person behind the counter seemed a bit disinterested in being present as he told us that the soft serve is a very popular item with cornflakes being the most popular choice of topping. Overall, I thought the flavor was ok - nothing life-altering and the "cereal" flavor was quite subtle. For $7.50 an order, I expected something special.

I always drop by this place after grabbing Momofuku. Not gonna lie, their cookies could be cheaper but I enjoy the compost and cornflake-chocolate-marshamallow cookies the best! The compost is pretty much like the kitchen sink types of cookies... it has everything in it! Both have good flavor combo and texture! Another plus is the crack pie. It looks small and simple, but really is addicting like crack! Top it off with some cereal milk soft serve and you're golden! Trust me!

Ordered a $135 cake from here for a big event on Monday and was expecting it to get to the event on Saturday, then got an email saying it wouldnt get there until the following day. I would expect a big and famous chain bakery to be competant enough to have my cake the day I ordered it for. Highly disappointed and now I dont know what to do because the I ordered the cake to arrive where the event was held, and wont be able to get it when it arrives. Beware and do NOT order from this bakery. ZERO stars!! Update: The cake didnt get arrive until 3 days after it was expected

Paid $18 for 2 tiny sandwich cookies. I was expecting to get a warm cookie ice cream sandwich at least the size of the palm of my hand (the cookie ice cream sandwiches were advertised as big). Cookie ice cream sandwiches turned out to be tiny, practically frozen, and hard to eat.

I was so excited to finally try this place out. They don't have one where we live so when my husband and I were in Vegas for a weekend, we figured why not? Unfortunately the experience left much to be desired. The compost cookie was far too salty and the b'day shake tasted like nothing but straight up sugar. I love sweets as much as the next person but too much sugar is a very real thing. This in itself caused them to miss the mark on what could of been some really yummy treats. Also, the price, I get that we're in Vegas and everything is overpriced but I'm a strong believer in getting what you pay for and that was not the case here. The idea is cute but just not well executed. I honestly can't recommend it.

Milk in NYC was a lot cheaper, Vegas overpriced! Located on the second floor food area of Cosmo. Walk up shop. Service was friendly. You can sample the ice cream flavors. Compost Cookie Soft Serve w/ Cornflake Crunch - $6 + $1.50 - Thick and milky soft serve. Had the milk and cookie flavor. Cornflake Crunch was a good topping but you only get a few pieces on top and it falls off easy. I wish they would have layered it in the actual cup with the soft serve. Good but so overpriced for what you get. Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmellow Cookie - $4 - Comes prepackaged now. Back when they were small time in NY, they were baked fresh everyday. Not sure how fresh these were.

Do you like mush? This was the most disgusting ice cream I've ever had. It could be in part because there was minimal to no ice cream added to the ice cream pint, despite that supposedly being the main ingredient. I would not recommend this item to anyone. It looked like poop. See photo.

I was a skeptic because I thought this was gonna be mr softee with Kellogg's. But it was the creamiest most delicious ice cream I have ever tasted in my life. I would definitely recommend this to anyone in the area or Manhattan!

Split review from 2 separate visits. First time here tried the bdsy cake and it was yummy crack pie was a sliver of stale tasting diabetes lol, and the cookie wasn't fresh. I was a little disappointed since I actually own their cookbook and have made items. It was overpriced for that experience. Now that I think about it I went during the beginning of the week which may have gotten me the previous weekends batch. Went there 2 days ago and it was delish! The fall apple cake was moist and packed with flavor. The cereal milk ice cream with the cornflake typing was delish and perfect for sharing because on its own a small cup is too sweet for 1 person. The funnel cake ice-cream was gross we had a sample. Yuck. Lol

10/10. I didn't know they have a milk in Vegas and I'm so happy I got to try it hear. I got the build it yourself pint and wow! Not like any icecream ive ever tasted. I'm trying to understand how you get a burst of extreme sweetness and it literally settles in one second and it's not that sweet anymore. Soooo different. Bizarre experience - I love it

I had never heard of Milk Bar until it was suggested to me on social media. I'm apparently easily influenced when it comes to food ads, because I started thinking about their cake often! I considered ordering it to be shipped from New York, but I'm actually glad I didn't spend the money because what I tried at the Vegas location wasn't the greatest. I got a slice of birthday cake, which was straight out of the fridge. Do people like cold cake? I really dislike it. I debated letting it sit out for a while, but decided to just go for it. It tasted like week old refrigerated cake, heavy and overly moist. I did appreciate the icing though, it melted in my mouth! I wasn't able to eat more than 1/4 of the cake slice, but I did eat a bunch of icing because it was pretty good. I'd love to try a fresh slice of their birthday cake! For $14, I just expected so much more. I left feeling pretty disappointed.

This experience was not great. We paid $18 for a miniature affogato and a 16 ounce shake- for $11 bucks it should be at least 20 ounces. I got the birthday shake and my dad got the affogato, I chose the b'day flavor for my shake. The shake was below mediocre and tasted like watered down cake batter. The affogato was okay and an okay price but the shake should have wowed me for $11 dollars. It's not somewhere I'd like to go back to and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone else.
The cereal lattes were super overly sweet, didnt have the greatest experience. The service was cool but damn that latte was not good at all.

Milk Bar never disappoints when it comes to the tastiness of its treats. I tried the strawberry shortcake slice, which I think is new or seasonal, and it was unsurprisingly DELICIOUS. The drawback to me is the $14 price however. I would not rate the taste of the soft serve as high, definitely good still but not as exceptional, and again a little pricey. I would say Milk Bar is a place you go to try once or a few times a year but it isn't my go-to, and I'm okay with that because I'll most definitely still partake when I'm near one of their locations again :)
Not a fan. Wanted some ice cream and we were excited Milk was just a few steps away. Service was good but the ice cream was yuck (in my opinion. ) Needed to get a redemption dessert.

I had the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes, and it was different. Was it like a bowl of cereal with even some flakes at the bottom to end the experience with a bang? Yes. Was it something I am longing to go back for? No, not at all. Maybe there is something else on the menu that would hit it on the head for someone who enjoys a truly wonderful ice cream from time to time, but this is too far off the mark to make that happen. Too sweet and a flavor, at least for this reviewer, that should still remain at the bottom of a cereal bowl.

I really like Milk Bar. I visited the Vegas location for the first time recently (previously I had only been in New York), and it's a cute little counter spot located in The Cosmopolitan. For those that don't know, Milk was created by Christina Tosi, who founded the dessert programs at the Momofuku restaurants. This makes Milk a huge draw for a lot of people (including me), so don't be surprised if you visit and it's packed. We lucked out and it was completely empty when we stopped by early on a weekday, so we had no wait and we were able to order quickly. On this visit I opted for a Cereal Milk Latte, as I had just had breakfast and didn't have room for much more, but Milk offers so much more! They're slinging some standard desserts including truffles, pie, milkshakes, cake, and cookies; BUT, they offer them up in flavors you're not going to find anywhere else. First, their Birthday Cake flavor is unlike any other. Why? I don't know. It just is. And it's delicious! Try the Birthday Cake or the B'Day Truffles. They also have Cereal Milk (like my latte) and the Milk Bar Pie (a.k.a. Crack Pie) is bomb! If you're in the mood to opt for a cookie, try The Compost Cookie, it's got a hodgepodge of mix-ins, and it's delicious! And this Vegas location has tons of alcoholic drink options as well. Milk is a bit pricey, and depending on when you visit there may be a line, but I honestly think the desserts are worth it. It's not fancy, so please don't expect that, but if you're looking for a delicious cake, cookie, or pie, then Milk Bar is your spot.

Overall the impression of the place is good. I wanted to try everything so I ordered the pie, cereal milk ice cream, compost cookie, birthday cake, and birthday truffles for $40+ dollars. I'm a HUGE fan of Sprinkes cupcakes and I was looking for a replacement. The cereal milk ice cream with corn flakes is really good. They put some corn flakes at the bottom so they never run out. YUM! The truffles and cookies come pre-packaged so the dont have the "homemade" feel. They were okay. Nothing special and nothing I'd pay that much for. The pie looked homemade. It was pretty good but I wouldn't re-order as I'm more of a chocolate fan. However the BEST was the birthday cake. It doesn't look the prettiest but ITS SOOO GOOD! The outside is a little almost crunchy (in a good way) and it's soooo flavorful. The balance of frosting to cake is perfect. The two compliment each other nicely. The cake isn't too sweet but has a good flavor, you can taste the butter. I highly recommend it and will definitely purchase again once in town.

One of my favorite Netflix original series is Chef's Table. When they showed an episode featuring Christina Tosi I was hooked even though I'm not a cereal guy. Just had to bide my time for the opportunity to be in Vegas and head out to the Cosmopolitan, 2nd floor next to Momofuku, another one I had to get too. The line can get long here but it goes down quickly. The menu board could get intimidating offering cookies including gluten and sugar free, cakes by the slice or whole, crack pie, breads, milksquakes and milkshakes, soft serve and fancy drinks. It took us a long time to decide what to get but we finally made our choices. Staff is super friendly and knowledgeable. They will give you a little more information to assist your decision making. To start, we had cereal milk soft serve with flakes and another one with fudge. The soft serve tasted exactly how I remembered eating my Kellogg's Frosted Flakes getting to the bottom of the sugary milk. Ah those memories. This is just the first trip here. And I can't wait to come back to try more.

Having been to the original NYC location I knew what to expect when I joined the late night crowd at Milk Bar. I've had the cereal milk soft serve, the pie formerly known as "crack pie", and some of their baked goods. Wanting to try something different, I got a chocolate birthday cake shake, which had pieces of chocolate cake in it and sprinkles. It was actually quite good, probably the best thing that I've tried at Milk Bar. It was rich and thick enough to satisfy a milkshake craving but thin enough to sip easily, sans the cake pieces that got stuck in the straw. When I finished the shake, I wanted more, which is always a good thing. But, after paying $7 for the baby shake, I'm just not sure that I could justify paying more for a larger one.

A long time ago, we had $15 credit and decided to get some milkshakes. They were horrible. Very chalky and the chocolate did not have a good flavor and texture. So I read that the cookies were the specialty. So I use my $15 credit to get four flavors of cookies. There were also not appealing in the least. The flavors, the textures, the combinations. I have never turned down a cookie in my life and my husband never turns down ice cream. We both didn't enjoy either. Our family owned an ice cream shop and bakery at one point. I watch a lot of food network, so was excited to try this place. Disappointed
My fave dessert spot in the Cosmo. I usually stop by for a cookie or truffles. Some of their desserts can be a little pricey but your on the strip, and in the Cosmo. What do you expect?
I have been here a dozen times to share with friends while they are visiting and the majority of their reactions are amazing. The crack pie is also one of my favorite items to get.

Poor customer service and the ice cream was salty! Not sure if it was a bad batch. The young lady that fixed my order was very condensing when I asked for a water (that I orderes). When I discovered the ice cream was "off" I just throw it in the trash and didn't take it back. I gave them one star because my husband liked the cookies he ordered.
Ice cream was good and there was a generous amount of crunchies added overtop and underneath the ice cream

I've been wanting to try the Milk Bar for a while now, and I was so let down. I was not feeling the cake at all. It's definitely cute, I'll give it that, but the flavor was displeasing. I did taste my sister's cereal milk ice cream and it was not bad. Definitely something (the ice cream) that would have to grow on me.

Oh man so disappointed. I have followed this store for 3 years since seeing it in New York and not being able to stop. I got the greatest combo with ice cream, cookie, truffles and cake. It was so so so disappointing. The ice cream is sour with corn flakes on top, the cookie has a bad after taste and the cake was raw. I did not even try the truffles. Literally we paid 30.00 took three bites and ended up throwing it all away. So sad.

We went here after hearing about it on Social Media. It's not something I'd want to go back to. Workers weren't very friendly and I think it was pretty overpriced for toppings. The ice cream was too sweet for me, not the greatest experience.

LOVE THIS PLACE. Before I moved to Vegas, I would come here EVERY single time I visited Vegas. I love their cereal milk soft serve. I have also tried all their cookies and love gifting them. The price point is a little high, but hey you're in Vegas in a hotel, it's expected. Before they had other flavors like red velvet and their crack pie but because of COVID they are only serving cereal milk which I'm fine with cause that's all I get. I subtracted one star due to inconsistency. Sometimes the employees are nice and sometimes the person who is working is rude and not in the mood. The consistency of the soft serve is also hit or miss. The one I posted pictures of this visit had a melty consistency so it wasn't very good. But I recommend trying it, it's crazy how cereal milk tasting soft serve would be so good! Love love love milk bar and love cosmo!

My sister in law and I are fans of Christina Tosi after watching her on Netflix, so we were both excited to stop by while we were in Vegas. The Milk Bar pie and cereal milk ice cream were just as delicious as we dreamed, and the birthday cake was to die for! The cookies were a bit disappointing, as they are all prepackaged and you can even buy some of the varieties just like that at some grocery stores, but the Fried Apple Caramel Crisp cookie was something different, so that one was worth a try! The Birthday Cake Truffles were pretty good too. We definitely are planning our next trip back!

Ordered a pint, the soft serve lacks flavor, the toppings taste stale. For $18, they were too cheap to give us the clean milk bar container like the one on the menu, we got the unbranded paper cup instead. Totally not worth it, not even IG worthy

Milk bar is a little expensive for what it is but I expect most places on the strip will charge more. We wanted dessert ASAP and decided to swing by this place. There was a line but it moved quickly even with only one person working. We both decided on shakes, I got the chocolate cake shake and my husband got the birthday cake shake. There's sprinkles all over the top and chunks of cake mixed in with the ice cream. It was really a perfect amount and didn't feel as heavy as your typical ice cream shake. They were so yummy. The straws were nice and fat so you could suck up all those cake chunks. I recommend this place if you want something sweet and cool and you want it fast.

Wanted a sweet cheat treat while at Cosmo. Found milkbar. Menu overwhelming but fun. I ordered the pint $18 and birthday milkshake. The pint was swirl ice cream with cornflakes and sprinkles. This thing was waaaaaay too sweet. And it was messy, spilling on the sides. Why bother to put the cap on when it's going to melt. The cap just wasn't functional. The birthday milkshake was super small for $10 and I wouldn't order that again. It cost way too much, not worth the value and the pint was super messy. If I came back here, it would be for the cakes or cookies.
Managed to take a pretty idiot proof idea and make everything taste like sour milk. Pass.

Staying at the Cosmopolitan in Vegas we stopped by for a treat. The staff was very helpful and kind, that's why I'm giving it a two. The funnel cake flavored soft serve was just horrible. It went in the trash after the 2nd taste. The three little cake balls we like someone rolled up some cake into a ball and iced it. Clearly the cake items were made elsewhere as they were presented in sealed plastic. I was really expecting more from this place. But it just didn't deliver or compare to the level of the other restaurants we ate in the Cosmopolitan.
The icecream, cookies, and pie were all soooooo good!!! I recommend trying multiple items and sharing within your group!

Really enjoyed the cereal milk soft serve and cookies in New York a few years back so I was excited to find out there was a location in Las Vegas - second floor of the Cosmopolitan. Ordered the single size cereal milk with cornflakes ($7.25). The soft serve is super rich and creamy with the leftover cereal taste lingering behind. Definitely need to add the cornflakes to make the soft serve complete! In addition, I also purchased 6 individually wrapped cookies for $22. Two compost, two cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow (one of my favs; not sure how they are able to keep that crunch in the cornflake), and two blueberry & cream. The cookies are best eaten within 4 days of purchase.

As huge fan of Momofuku/David Chang, this place is a must whenever I visit Vegas. On my most recent trip, I came on a mission to try the famous Crack Pie after watching the Chef's Table episode on Christina Tossi and the Milk Bar. They have everything from birthday cake milkshakes to soft serve ice cream here. The crack pie was fantastic and absolutely lives up to all the hype! The oat cookie pie crust and buttery, sugar filling merge together for the perfect, gooey bite. The pie is actually served chilled, which was a pleasant surprise. I'm usually not a sweets/desserts-type of person, and the sweetness level was perfectly balanced. I've tried a couple other things on the menu, including their famed cereal-milk shake, but this one takes the cake (literally)! Definitely recommend checking this place out if you're feeling your sweet tooth.

Man alive, that cereal milk soft serve is incredible. Plus, did you know that you can get a swirl of cereal milk and fruity pebbles? It's the perfect combination. I had heard so much about Milk bar, first through momofuku and then learning more about Christina Tosi. The cereal milk was for sure the item I most wanted to try from milk bar, since I had already tried the compost cookie (albeit onboard Jetblue). I wanted to try the crack pie, but since we had not quite had dinner yet, we decided against it. We will probably try it the next time we are in NYC.

I'm only giving this place 4 stars because I'm in love with their crack pie. It is everything I want dessert to be...rich, sweet and decadent. Maybe it's me or my tastes have changed, but the cookies just don't hit the spot like they used to. Tried the crack pie soft serve this time around, but I dont think I'd order it again.

I first tried Milk in NY and loved it, so I was so excited when they opened one in LA. But since I hate LA traffic, I make it a point to go to the one in Cosmo when I'm in Vegas. You can NOT go wrong with getting the birthday cake truffles - if you get one thing from here, get that. Everything else - cookies, crack pie, soft serve, cereal milk latte - are really good too. I do like the cake truffles much better than the cake slice though. This trip I did decide to mix it up and also try the cereal milk white russian, and I wasn't really a fan of that. I thought it was just me but a couple of my friends tasted it and also said it wasn't good. For $12, I would steer clear of this one.

Does not live up to its hype to be honest. I get the cool names etc and the founder is a cool lady. I would love to do a dessert bake off with her. One I would learn and two it would be fun. I am just really under impressed with the offerings here.

This dessert place is not 4 star worthy and everything was overly sugary. The cereal milk ice cream was too sugary, and my friend and I were not able to finish the ice cream because of the amount of sugar that was in the ice cream. We shared the compost cookie and it tasted ridiculous. It was by far the worst cookie I had ever tasted, but the marshmallow cookie was alright. It was not an enjoyable place, and seems like a place that only drunks enjoy. Save your money because everything is overpriced and not worth a dime.

Nobody will believe me but I purposely stay at the cosmopolitan only, so I can have the milkbar softserve cereal milk as many times I want. I went there 7 times in a day one time and the lady at the counter started saying "welcome back" lol. I wish I can have their softserve instead of the breakfast, lunch, and dinner. There's something special about their softserve and the cereal topping.. I dont know how to describe the difference but it certainly is not the same softserve you would get from the mcdonals. Also the cereal topping is not as flaky as Kellogg's and also saltier. Stay away from this shop because you will be cursed like me who cannot stop thinking about their softserve cereal milk. I crave for it everyday!! ( By the way, I dont know her name but an Asian girl with glasses who works there is super super sweet. )

Well you would sure think that for $28 for a scoop of ice cream and a piece of cake it would be fantastic. NOT. Dry and hard birthday cake and the funnel cake soft serve ice cream was not something you want to finish let alone ever try again. Will never ever go nor recommend. Yuck yucky yuk.

Heard that I had to check this place out from a friend. I tried the much raved about cereal milk ice cream. They may use cereal to make it, but it is very bitter. Not sweet in the least bit. And what cereal are they using? Frosted Mini Wheats? Not the best choice out there

Bruh this my favorite ice cream place. Hot take but I don't think the west coast (yes consider Vegas west coast) has good non-Asian ice cream, but this was a shining beacon of hope for us picky ice cream eaters. Salt & Straw is shaking. I recommend the milk flavor and birthday cake swirl (not sure if I got the verbiage right) with fudge topping and sprinkles. Milk Bar is located in the Cosmopolitan hotel, near the entrance to Marquee, so it's perfect for when you just finished getting yurnt at the dayclub and want something to hold you over until dinner, before you hit the nightclub. The only thing is that the portion is pretty big, so you'll probably want to split with someone. The ice cream was $8 and I had to throw half of it away since I couldn't finish it, and I'll regret this moment for the rest of my life. All I want right now is to go back to the Cosmo for this one lick of frozen heaven.

I feel bad. But I honestly didn't love it... I had the Cereal Milk ice cream with corn flakes for the topping and took the Cornflake Marshmallow Chocolate Chip Cookie. Everything was pretty expensive for me, $4 for a cookie and $6 for a small soft serve ice cream...damn. I love how trendy it is. I love how friendly the staff are but I was just eh. Cereal Milk ice cream was soft and thick- nice texture- but also very salty to me. I felt like I didn't taste much but salt. I was unsure if it was salty because of the corn flakes or what. The cookie was not bad. Also tasted saltier than I would have liked but I did like the added sweetness and chewiness of the marshmallow. I liked the different textures in the cookie. My friend has a swirl soft serve of the cereal milk and something else that he couldn't remember. Whatever it was- that one was good! Because of this I won't totally write off that this place is terrible and I'll give it another try to taste another flavored soft serve or dessert. I will say price is pretty steep for me...but also...I get it. It's in the cosmo and it's Vegas. I just feel the price is high for the amount you're getting. I was assuming it would be a little pricey. I'm just not sure if it's worth it to me. Until next time!

By Cristina Tosi, whose claim to fame was creating the entire dessert menu for David Chang's Momofuku in NY. It's fitting they are next to each other at the Cosmopolitan. Her desserts are not traditional, unashamedly inspired by American junk foods and breakfast cereals. There's something nostalgic and familiar for those who grew up eating frosted flakes, reeses peanut butter cups, and fruit loops. They are reimagined and combined in interesting ways in their cookies instead of just being thrown on top like trendy donut and ice cream places. My wife skipped breakfast just to get the cookies, they come pre-packaged in sealed clear bags and make for great gifts to friends and relatives instead of the typical Vegas magnets or gambling themed gifts. The one common feature is the cookies are soft yet have an interesting crunch. Below are some standouts: -Compost cookie, the name is trademarked and seems like something you would eat if you lost a bet: potato chips, pretzels, butterscotch, and coffee are combined into a delicious sweet and salty cookie. -Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow Cookie, a less sweet combination that feels a bit like a rice crispie treat mixed with a cookie, soft from the marshmallows and crunchy from the cornflakes.

I was so excited to see this since I always see it on tiktok and boy was I disappointed! I ordered the cake and shake combo and soft serve. The line was long and they had celebrities that came plastered on the fridge. I got the birthday cake and crunchy cereal shake. The taste... was so strange to me? Like sour in a way? Like sour cream and I was so weirded out by the flavor of the ice cream and shake! The shake had crunchy bits of cereal but didn't mask that sour note. The cake was frozen and moist, but the icing was too much and very sweet. I was expecting it to be light a bit? But really it taste like those cheap birthday cakes you get at the grocery store.... The over sweet icing really killed it for me. For their price point? That is nuts! Prob not gonna give in on hype next time.

Unfortunately, I don't understand the hype here. Got the soft serve and it wasn't great at all. Overpriced watered down tasting soft serve was how I can describe it. I wish I saved my money to get gelato or Ben and Jerry's on the strip instead!!! I wouldn't recommend this place. I'm a sweets person so I absolutely love dessert and this won't be one of my go to places in Vegas. For the record I'm in Vegas probably twice a year for the last 12 years.

I've never been to the OG location in NYC, so I had to try in Vegas! It's conveniently located in the Cosmopolitan next to Momofuku (you have to try this place too, it's incredible) so I had to get dessert here. Get ready for prices that seem pretty high for a cookie or cake or whatever you decide to get, but also recognize that it's Vegas so . They accept cash or card and are open relatively late which one can always appreciate in Vegas. I got a slice of the Milk Bar pie and the Bday Truffles. Both were incredibly decadent so if you've got a sweet tooth, get ready to be in heaven!

I've been to Milk Bar Las Vegas multiple times, and each time it's always been a nice treat, but never the best dessert I've had. This store is located next to Momofuku in the Cosmopolitan, so it's a perfect dessert after a meal at Momofuku. Items I Would Recommend: Cereal Milk Soft Serve: 4/5; I always order this whenever I come here because while it's a simple soft serve, I love the taste of the cereal milk and I always add the cornflake clusters. It's not too sweet and perfect for two people to share if you get an additional item on the menu which I would always recommend. Milk Bar Pie: 4/5; Before trying the real thing at Milk Bar, I tried making this at home and really enjoyed it. I love the oatmeal crust, and the custard is really flavorful with the sugar and butter standing out, and while it's sweet, it's not too sweet. Items I Would Not Recommend: Chocolate B'Day Cake Slice: 2/5; I think it's far too sweet and bitter at the same time and was not able to eat much of the slice.

Have always heard this name being thrown around, but being from the Midwest, I can't really get to it easily. I've had cookies sent to be before and those were all spectacular, but I've ALWAYS wanted to try their signature soft serve ice cream and milk bar pie. I know that this is a trendy place, but ~$8 for vanilla soft serve and flakes? I don't think so. I only ate the parts with the flakes, but the soft serve didn't taste any special than what I can get at DQ. The flakes gave it a nice crunch but was a tad salty? It balanced out with ice cream, but interesting at first. Their milk bar pie was 6.50 for a very very small slice. I was shocked when I opened to see how big it was, BUT it did taste very good. It had a crumbly cookie crust and the filling tasted a bit like custard. It was INCREDIBLY sweet, so make sure you also grab water or coffee to wash down the sugar, but I did enjoy this item. I would order the pie and cookies to be sent to me if I ever crave, but would probably not seek out their ice cream anytime soon.

Don't waste your time or money coming here..cookies are pre packaged, the slice of cake I got was dry, and the milkshake lacked flavor..honestly a milkshake from McDonald's or Jack in the box would of been better Wasted over $40

Sugar high!!! These treats taste as good as they look. Seriously! Let's begin with my very favorite item, the crack pie! Also known as the Milk Bar Pie. I took one bite and was hooked! It's so buttery, sticky, gooey, sweet, and simply perfect. I learned it was made by mistake. Sometimes mistakes can lead to the very best results! My second favorite item is a slice of their birthday cake. Friendly reminder, you don't have to wait until your birthday to enjoy an amazing slice of birthday cake! Treat yourself! It tastes like a store bought cake from your childhood birthday parties when life was grand and simple. Each bite is worth the calories... My man also enjoys their cookies although I'm not a fan. When we find ourselves at the Cosmo we can't seem to skip grabbing something sweet to-go.

Not worth the hype!!! The cereal milk soft serve tasted odd (they were also cheap on the fudge) and the cake offerings were over the line sweet, making them not enjoyable. You're better off somewhere else for dessert!

Milk Bar goodies are my go-to gift for birthday celebrations and sometimes a special treat for myself. I love their gluten free b-day cake truffles and cornflake cookies. Bomb treats, awesome service! Recently I bought a birthday cake for a friend's birthday and being the space cadet I am-- I didn't think to refridgerate it so it melted before the actual birthday. I called Milk Bar and the manager Michelle was understanding enough to help replace it in time before the event free of charge. I am truly blown away by her customer service and she didn't make me feel like an idiot -- which honestly lol, yeah totally a ditz move on my part. People put your cake in the fridge!

If you haven't gotten the soft serve with cornflake crunch you need to! It tastes exactly like cereal milk. Was so tasty. The cake slice was pretty good the crack pie was a little too sweet for my taste. Definitely should stop here if you're in the cosmo.

Get the "crunchy cereal shake". My guess is that the negative reviews are for other things. "Cake" as a flavor sounds awful anyway. So the crunchy cereal shake. It's modest-looking, unassuming. I don't know why it's so good. I can talk about individual aspects of it but the combination is bigger than the sum of its parts. It's one of those things that you can eat a lot of. Not too sweet, just the right amount of saltiness to punch up the sweetness, and just really gratifying for something that is in the realm of a dessert. I think the consistency is perfect, too - thick but easy to drink with the fat straw. And the crunchy cereal is like the genius part of it. It's got the texture and crunchiness of Honey Bunches of Oats (with almonds) that has been sitting in 2% milk (lactose free) for the duration of time it takes to eat about 40% of a bowl. Sometimes I get impatient and just want to drink the rest of the bowl because I can't spoon it into my mouth fast enough. Maybe that's why this shake speaks to me. Anyway just get the crunchy cereal shake and you probably won't go wrong. It's a bit pricey at around 10 bucks but I think it's worth it.

ordered three crunchy cereal milkshakes and they're all weird tasting. i've had this same milkshake at the milkbar in new york and it definitely did not taste like this. the milkshake tastes so salty. saltier than salt & vinegar chips. just read the recipe online and it says it's supposed to be milk, cornflakes, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt. pretty sure they replaced the brown sugar with salt and this drink is just milk, salt, and cornflakes... the soft serve with crunchy cereal was also a little salty. the milkbar pie was 10/10.

The consistency of the ice cream is pretty great, it's thick enough to not be runny but still thin enough to be soft serve. I got the Crack Pie and the Cereal Milk as a twist. Both flavors are good in my opinion but I wouldn't say anything special. Same with the Cornflake Crunch, I think it complements the ice cream very well but it's nothing too outstanding. Overall, a little overpriced for what it is ($6-7 for a small cup). I think a part of it is that you're just there for the name because it's a famous place that started in New York (?)

The Milk Bar has delicious and unique treats. The cookies are delicious but the Crack Pie is the star of the show. They changed the name of the Crack Pie,but I will always call it Crack Pie. It's so good that it's like crack. This time I had the Fancy Birthday Shake. It's very rich and so yummy for your tummy. If you like sweet treats you must come to the Cosmopolitan and get some goodies from The Milk Bar.

I never got the chance to try the original location in California so I am happy I did since we got to stay at the Cosmopolitan. Since COVID, the hours and days are different for when they are open but if they are when you come you should definitely come try out their menu items. I went with their famous MILK butter pie. Rich buttery and great for a snack. If you feel adventurous you can try out their crazy concoctions of ice cream but I wanted something simple.

Milk Bar is located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan next door to Momofuku. I ordered two crack pies and the b'day truffles. I would say, the crack pies were good and unique, even though it looks super basic. I was surprised how small they were for $6 each, but I'm glad they were at least good. The bday truffles were disappointing so don't get them. Next time I'd like to try the crack pie at Momofuku where you can get it a la mode with the corn flakes.

My friend kept hyping up milk bar so I had high expectations before coming here. It did look good don't get me wrong, but I was not amazed. I would've shared with my friend but since he kept saying how good it was I thought i'd be better if we had our own cup of soft serve to ourselves than sharing. I got the soft serve with chocolate syrup and it was just OK. I've honestly had better soft serve elsewhere and this was pretty basic. It was also expensive as well! At least my friend still enjoyed it but I probably won't be going out of my way to get it.

Milk Bar looked delicious- but the taste was absolutely DISGUSTING. We ordered the funnel cake soft serve (absolutely gross- didn't taste like it at all- or anything good) and we immediately threw it away. The gluten free birthday cake truffles (these were prepackaged in groups of 3 so no mix/match) and they were slightly better than the soft serve. But overall it was a waste of $16.
I can only speak on the birthday cake but I'd make sweet, sweet love to that thing. Actually, I'd let it make love to me if it so desired.

Vegas has a reputation for being up all night but try to grab a snack after 11 PM and you will be out of luck - EXCEPT for MILK which I walked for a mile down the Strip to try and was completely satisfied with the sweet treats I got for my me and my sweetheart. I was so focused on making sure my lover had her sweet-tooth satisfied that I walked away with the moonpies, shakes and cookies and forgot my change - the super honest cashiers hollered for me to come get it - hey it was change for a hundred, we are talking big Vegas bucks here. Honesty like that should net MILK six stars here but you will not go wrong snacking here.

I'm a fan of Christina Tosi and her fun and eccentric creations, so it was exciting to visit Milk Bar in Vegas for the Cereal Milk Soft Serve as I had previously visited the NY location for only cookies. Located conveniently inside of the Cosmo located right next to Momofuku. The glowy, pink Milk sign will beckon you to indulge your sweet tooth. Cereal Milk Soft Serve - perfect soft-serve texture, Vanilla-ed milk base coated in crunchy, brown sugared corn flakes with a bit of saltiness to balance out all the sweet. Texturally contrasting and very reminiscent of eating a bowl of Frosted Flakes as a kid. Fun! They do serve other sweet treats here from their famous Milk Bar Pie, slices of cake, cookies to even truffles. Great place for a quick sweet treat, if you're walking through Cosmo.

I always order their cereal and milk soft serve. That's all I come here for. The only downside was that The Cosmopolitan was limiting their entry to hotel guests and guests with restaurant reservations only. However, once we informed the guard that we wanted to stop by the Milk Bar, he let us in. The line wasn't super long. My husband and I very much enjoyed our cereal and milk soft serve. We will be back!

If you're trying to decide what to get here, opt for the CRACK PIE!!! yes, I'm addicted, I want more!!!! You can't have just one bite. The cookies are amazing as well but my favorite is the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow. Can't wait to go back and get more!

I was sadly disappointed by Milk Bar. We ended up not finishing any of the items we got. We got the cereal milk ice cream, and it tasted like cornflakes that barely touched milk, I honestly would've preferred plain vanilla over this. The milk bar pie was also disappointing and we got two cookies that tasted stale. We both agreed we wish we would've stopped elsewhere for our late night dessert :/. I wish we would've tried out their cake instead of the ice cream, pie, and cookies, not sure if it's worth trying again after our disappointment. I will say the customer service was great and the employees did a great job turning orders quickly. I think the product flavors were sadly just not for us.

WOW, these cookies are so fire!!! why is this my first time trying them? I was too full the past few times I was at the cosmo but I made sure to visit them this time with a lighter meal to have them for dessert. These cereal cookies do not disappoint! They make them fresh and they are portionally sized and taste so good! I wanted to go eat them again and my friend told me they have them packaged at Target so I had to get my fix on.... not the same. The actually physical location cookies are twice the size and are the real deal! Can't wait to come make another visit to this location or the one in LA. the cookies are so bomb! keep them coming and keep up the great tasting cookies! I want to try and catch them for their seasonal flavors too. Come and check out MILK bar!

Not worth the hype unless your getting something Made to order like the milk ice cream. The cookies and milk bar are pre made and packaged. For the price you would expect a warm cookie and something tasting freshly made instead your getting a cold cookie and milk bar slice. Disappointed especially for price.

I recently just saw the Chef show on Netflix with the episode about this place so I was so excited to see it in Vegas! Located on the 2nd floor at the Cosmopolitan, it's located next to Momofuku. On Wednesday night, there was already a long line. My friends and I decided to get the birthday cake slice and the cereal soft serve with corn flakes to share. The birthday cake slice was huge and enough for 4 people to share. It was super sweet and decadent! The soft serve was my favorite as the cereal was a sweet flavor but the saltiness of the corn flakes balanced it out. I've never had soft serve like this before. Prices were a little on the higher side, but I guess that's what you pay for a big brand! I wanted to try the cookies because the flavors looked interesting, but we never had a chance to go back during our trip. So I guess next time!

Dessert here is the best! Though mostly what I get is the cereal shake and it's an accustomed taste but when you like it, you really like it! Always something I pick up when I come to Las Vegas for a vacation! I do wish they had more available but it's best to come earlier than late haha

Their milk bar pie did not live up to the hype. Tiny, boring, and expensive for literally 2 bites of boring buttered corn flakes. Not sure why it's so popular; makes sense because a lot of people these days have no common sense.

I've always wanted to try Milk Bar, at least the one in NY whenever I make my way there, but when I found out there was one in Vegas I had to stop by. I've tried their cookies when they've been mailed to me as a gift but I honestly should've tried the same cookies there to compare if it tasted even better from the source, next time I will! But I ended up ordering their Milk Bar Pie slice (i believe it was formerly known as their crack pie). I was sorta disappointed with how much smaller the slice was in what looked like a big enough container that definitely could've fit a much larger slice of pie, but ya know, it is Vegas. Therefore prices will be much higher for what you actually get. It was like close to $8 for the slice I got! However despite the price, their Milk Bar Pie was SO good. It had this flavor combo of sweetness and saltiness that I wished I had more of it. So I was at least impressed with what I got. My mom really wanted to try their red velvet soft serve but their soft serve machines were not working that day so that was another disappointment. But I'm sure next time we visit Vegas, I'd still give this location of Milk Bar another try.

Eh it's tooooo sweet and pretty pricey! Good thing I sampled the cereal milk and crack pie ice cream. Crack tasted like butterscotch while the cereal tasted like frosted flake blended in w ice cream. Milk ice cream was ok. Tried the crack pie which costed $6.50 and it's pretty small for the price you pay! Rich and sweet mixed with gooey and sugary all in one is what I described this pie.

The French Toast ice cream was EXTREMELY salty to the point where a few bites in could give you hypertension. We also tried the Birthday Cake Milkshake that was also bad. It seemed like the milk or cream had gone bad. On top of that it's odd that an ice cream place in a casino wouldn't offer tap or iced water.

Pricey but pretty good treats. I've been to the LA location a few times and I probably prefer this location better. I am usually a fan of their cookies and ice cream. The last time I came here was when I stayed at the Cosmo. I do not drink dairy and asked them to make a Milk and Cereal Latte for me with something non dairy. So I guess they couldn't with that option so I went with their regular size Birthday Cake Latte with almond milk instead ($6.50). I didn't think it was anything super special but it was good and I was glad I got it. I also got their Gluten Free Birthday Cake Truffle which I highly recommend ($6). It comes pre-packaged with three truffles inside. The packaging is cute and they were SO GOOD! I definitely recommend them. I do appreciate that they have non-dairy options and gluten free options available when not many dessert places do. I also like that most of their sweets are pretty good but just pretty pricey.

Came here due to the hype, but left disappointed. I got the Greatest Hits sampler ($22), which had crack pie, cereal milk soft serve, birthday cake truffles, and compost cookie. All the baked goods were cloyingly sweet, so no other subtly of flavor could come through. The cereal milk soft serve had a strong malt flavor, but didn't blow me away. On top of nothing being that fantastic, this place is pretty expensive and the desserts are quite small. I guess hype can be a double-edged sword because it was the reason I came here, but I also think if I had lower/no expectations, I would have enjoyed it more, but still not enough to recommend it or return.

It's a tradition of mine to stop by every time I'm in Vegas! If you don't want to try the expensive food next door, you can come here to and also grab a slice of pizza at Secret Pizza or eat at Eggslut! My go-to is the Cereal Milk Soft Serve! The mild saltiness in it was perfect, and I love the smooth texture of the soft serve! Get the crack pie too if you want something sweet!

The milk bar pie aka crack pie was highly recommended so we dropped in after having lunch at Wicked Spoon to pick up a couple of slices. The pie was dense and the taste just didn't blow me away. Sweet and buttery but not in a yummy way. Certainly not worth the 7 bucks a pop. And I told the person that recommended the pie to me just that. No hard feelings lol. Perhaps the other desserts such as the cereal milk would've been a better choice. I would stop by again to try something else when I come back to The Cosmopolitan to try Momofuku next door. Otherwise it's a pass for me.

I waited till the end of my trip to try Milk Bar and I really should have tried it the first day I was in Las Vegas. The cereal milk soft serve with pie crumbs tasted amazing. It was sweet, salty, creamy, and cold. It became the perfect snack that evening. I'm the kind the person that doesn't like toppings in or on my ice cream but those pie crumbs were yummy. I only wish I knew the "crack pie" got renamed to the "milk bar pie" so I could have ordered a slice of that too. I kept trying to find "crack pie" on the menu board but it wasn't there. I didn't want to be the newbie asking a bunch of questions and holding up the long line. They're located inside The Cosmopolitan on the 2nd level. There's an escalator by the giant chandelier that can take you up from the casino level. If you pass those escalators, you'll find yourself walking for another 10 minutes to find the next set of escalators. Anyways, I'll be making another trip back to the Milk Bar one of these days because I want to try that "milk bar pie!"

I have heard a lot of hype regarding Milk Bar, so I decided to try it while in Vegas. For reference, Milk Bar is located in the Cosmopolitan. I ordered a few items to try and some were good, while others were just disappointing. What I liked: I ordered the cereal milk soft serve. It tastes true to what it is. It felt like I was literally eating a bowl of cereal in ice cream form. It was so surreal and Christina Tosi did a great job perfecting this. What I didn't like: obviously I had to try the crack pie. It sounded good and I read reviews to get it, but it lacked everything. First of all, it's a tiny piece of pie. I thought maybe the flavor would redeem the size, but it did not. It was bland and did not taste as if it had been made that day. Honestly, it was pretty stale and overall disappointing. I also bought a cookie that was not good either. It was blah in both flavor and texture. Overall, not a good cookie. I definitely think it's over hyped and with so many options on the strip, I won't be returning to Milk Bar when I'm back in Vegas.

On and off Milk get's busy. Seeing the Cereal Milk Soft Serve as the most popular I order one and will say it is alright. Just the ice cream with nothing is $6, it wasn't a lot, and it a bit better than a typical soft serve having this sweet and creamy taste. The people are working hard but as a straight up dessert place, I wonder if the cakes and drinks will be better.

Gosh, where to even start. This place is just a walk up bar area with the only seating being a small bench. The service was very quick - other than that it was nothing that went above and beyond. But the quality of the dish - amazing! We shared a piece of birthday cake and also the cup of cereal milk soft serve. I am a big sucker for dessert, and if you are too - go here!

This is situated right next to Momofuku and has a cute storefront. There is a queue but it moves quickly. I didn't know what soft serve ice cream to order so I asked the server what the most popular flavor was and she said Cereal Milk Soft Serve. I didn't want something too sweet so she gave me a sample and she was right - it wasn't that sweet and had a sweet/savory taste to it. I've seen people eat this for breakfast....because why not?! I ordered it with corn flake crunchies and brownie bites and it was a great way to get my sweet tooth fix. I liked that this wasn't as sweet as other desserts.
