I was too full to try other items but the next time I stay at the hotel I'll be sure to try their Confetti Cake.
Came here when I was staying at the cosmo The prices are very fair. The ice cream is pretty good Does really taste like milky flavor I'll be back soon

We were so excited to go for our first time. Unfortunately, the entire menu was sold out with the exception of the soft serve ice cream. So, we got that. It DID taste like the milk at the bottom of a cereal bowl, but it wasn't that great, and far too sweet for our liking. We thought it was way over priced, s as well. It seemed like a gimmick. We ate half and threw the rest away. Bummer!

Every time I step inside Cosmopolitan, I always gaze upon the delicious menu at Milk Bar. This store hails from New York City and the cakes really are THAT GOOD. While you may find a select few items at your local Target, they have a much wider variety of cake pops, ice cream, and other delectable goods at this storefront. We weren't looking to gorge on the items so we simply left with a few cake pops with us. If you happen to have an Identity account, make sure to provide it so you can get points for your purchase. I appreciate the fact that this place is also open relatively late so you can satisfy that late night craving! (35/100--2022)

Located inside The Cosmopolitan; Milk Bar is located close to all the food places like Egg Slut and next to Marukfuku Ramen. Admittedly, I did not know about this place until a friend asked me to get them something from here when I was in town. So I figured since I'm here, might as well get myself something as well. So I got myself a variety of the cookies and a slice of that bday cake. The cookies, are just okay in my opinion. But the bday cake is fireeeeee!!!! I went back another time and tried their chocolate bday cake and I feel like that was even better than the regular one. The chocolate is super decadent and just kinds of amazing. Their stuff is pricey, but I don't know if it's because it's a Vegas thing or if all the other ones in other locations are the same, but I figured "when in Vegas, right?" Super side note: if you're planning to buy a cake here and take it back to your home destination to share with friends and family, the cake which normally needs to be refrigerated, can be out and about for four hours before it goes bad. I asked the staff and they told me that.

Was so excited to stay at Cosmo and try a slice of the birthday cake. The girl at the counter definitely did NOT want to be at work today and was not even the tiniest little bit friendly. They were sold out of the cake I've heard so much about so I opted for a cookie and some of the birthday truffle balls. Both were too sweet and underwhelming. I don't think I'll try to come back in hopes they have any cake. Way too many other delicious dessert options in Vegas with great customer service. I just don't get the hype.

This was most expensive ice cream I've ever had. I got a soft serve pint with cereal toppings for $14. It was really good and tastes exactly how it is described- like milk at the end of the cereal. I liked how they put topping on top of the ice cream and on the bottom of the cup so you can get equal topping to soft serve ratio. It was delicious and probably a one time treat for me because at $14 that is super pricey!

I have passed by this place a few times and have seen others post about it but I have never had anything from Milk Bar. For my birthday, my cousin said for us to get a slice of Crack Pie and I agreed. It was super bomb BUT I have no idea how to describe the taste lol. I would just recommend for you to try it and see for yourself. Apparently, they are changing the name "Crack" pie soon to just Milk Bar Pie or something like that due to the negative connotation (seriously people?!?).

We were excited to try Milk Bar after hearing so much about it. Unfortunately, it didn't live up to the hype for us. We tried the milk bar pie, which was ok, but very greasy and heavy without much flavor. We also tried the cereal milk soft serve ice cream, which neither of us liked at all - terrible flavor with a very strange buttery cornflake topping that clashed with the ice cream - ended up throwing it away, which was a shame for how much it cost!

Walking around different malls on the strip and remembered Cosmopolitan had a Milk bar! I've always regretted not going when in NYC but finally got to go now. I was recommended either the compost or cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie and went with the latter. They warmed it up for me and it tasted amazing. It was a bit pricey but I don't blame them.

During COVID-19: Visiting the food scene here on the strip, I was happily surprised my birthday guilty pleasure was right next door to AZ-- Milk Bar Las Vegas! I'm all about chef Christina Tosi (and all things related to David Chang), so I wanted a taste of home after months away from New York. The feels were still real. First off: located in the dark but modern Cosmopolitan, Milk Bar LV has the same setup as the other NYC shops do in which it's a takeout shop. There are packaged cookies out on display with their signature bright "Milk" light logo flashing about. What I loved here was the social distance markers on the floor, allowing customers to do their part. The barista also wore a mask and gloves while handling our order. We ordered our regulars: birthday cake truffles (for celebrations) and the infamous crack pie slice (renamed). We didn't attempt to get a big pie due to the hot heat and storage we had at the time. Everything survived being in a parked car in Vegas back to Arizona thankfully! They have everything a regular Milk Bar in NYC has plus... alcoholic concoctions! How cool is that? Mind blown. That is where it stands a part from NYC owned ones minus the giant flagship (see flagship review/photos in Midtown). Unfortunately I wasn't going for midday drinking so I wasn't able to try the delightfulness. ;( Overall, if you haven't tried Milk Bar in your life- order up! They also have full cakes here, so it's a good way to order something special for someone or yourself. They also carry the famous cereal milk which one should try once. The soft serves are delicious if you're craving something not so extravagant but familiar. Price range is nothing crazy if you have been to the ones in NYC. Very typical price range. Accepts cash and card. Open decently late. A taste of NYC in LV. Bon appetit!
The cake was excellent, moist, and rich. The line was long but moved very quickly. Well worth the wait!

While I'd like to think I'm pretty good at bringing back souvenirs and snacks from my travels, that's definitely not the case when it comes to my trips to Vegas. Perhaps it's because I seem to be there so often, but it never crosses my mind to bring stuff back. Not that there are a ton of good choices anyways - a Fat Tuesday yard stick/cup? Some cheesy t-shirt? A WIFE?! HA. Thank goodness for Milk Bar and all of their cookies! As you could imagine for obvious reasons, this Milk Bar is just SLIGHTLY different than the original one in NY; the second floor of Cosmo versus a tiny shop in the East Village? Yeah, that's different. However, despite being set in very different places, they're essentially the same in the most important way of all - their goodies! Whether it's their cookies, shakes (both regular and boozy), cakes, soft serve, or their famed Crack Pies, you're bound to find something for your sweet tooth! The first time I stopped by Milk Bar, it was strictly to pick up some of their cookies that I found oh so tasty when I had them in NY. The range of choices seemed to be about the same (Confetti, Blueberry & Cream, Corn, Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow, Chocolate-Chocolate, and their famous Compost cookie), but, more importantly, they tasted just as good. Of the bunch, the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow and Compost cookies were my favorites - SO DELICIOUS! Along with getting more of their cookies, I also decided to try their GRASSHOPPER MILKSHAKE the last time I stopped by here. It had never been high on my list of things to get here, but my friend couldn't stop raving about the one he tried (which says something). While I can't say how mine compared to his, I thought my shake was pretty solid. The flavor could've been a little richer, but I liked the texture (not super thick or thin), how great the minty chocolate flavor was, and that it wasn't overly sweet. Even though it lacks the coziness and charm of their original NY spot, I can't say that there's really anything bad about this particular location. In fact, with how well their cookies keep, stopping off here before flying out of Vegas is practically a must! Which hopefully leads to getting a slice of their Crack Pie...or finally trying their Cereal Milk soft serve! Such a fail on my part for still not trying them yet...

A great place to get your sugar fix after a nice dinner. No place to sit. No place to even put your food down for a second. Yes, the corn flakes in the vanilla ice cream was really good. Of course, the helpings look small, but it was plenty for two of us. Speed was good considering there was a line. Great place to try once if you are tourist.

Heard about this place through Instagram. We had family in town, so during our once-a-year-sort-of-forced-trip-to-the-strip, we went to the Cosmopolitan for dinner. Ended up walking by Milk Bar after our meal and decided to give it a try. I ended up buying 6 cookies for $22.00 - confetti, fruity marshmallow, cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow, chocolate chocolate, compost, and blueberry & cream. The texture of these cookies were odd. They were chewy but tasted like they were losing their freshness. The chocolate chocolate was the worst because it tasted like nothing! The fruity marshmallow was the best one, even though it was a little too sweet. Maybe they would have tasted better with some of their ice cream, but I don't see myself going back there anytime soon. On a side note, customer service was excellent and friendly. The cashier who helped us gave us an overview of their menu and pointed out the cookies that were the most popular. Again, unless I am at the Cosmopolitan again (chances of that being slim to none), I most likely will not be back.
Not a fan. I don't understand the menu and I won't respond to it. I ended up getting a piece of cake that was meh.

The birthday cake here is life-changing. Wow. Located on the 2nd floor right next to Momofuku and down the hall from Eggslut, the hype around Milk Bar is real and I'm so glad there's a location in LA now. I got to try their cookies when their pop-up came to my work one day so I knew how good their cookies were. The price is a bit hefty but it's probably one of the best slices of cake I've ever had! I love when cakes have good texture, and you can taste all of the toppings inside the cake. The cake comes out a little icy which makes for a delicious slice! If you're looking for a bomb dessert, I wouldn't hesitate to come here!
THE ULTIMATE BEST! I've been to the NYC, LA and DC locations and they never disappoint! Theres not much more I can say to sing their praises! So convenient that its located in Cosmo!

I had to try this place after seeing it everywhere.... TRASHED it after 2 bites. The reviews are mixed so I wanted to play it safe, I got the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes, sour tasting soft serve and regular ass corn flakes on top... I don't understand how this place is still in business with sooo many other choices that actually taste GOOD in Las Vegas. Save your money, you WILL BE DISAPPOINTED. McDonald's soft serve is better than Milk bar.

Always been a fan of Milk ever since my 1st time in NYC. I made efforts to pay a visit located inside the Cosmopolitan hotel. I wanted to bring home some Crack pie and try out their soft serve. Choices of soft serve were Milk cereal and Compost cookie serve. You can choose toppings such as cornflakes and sprinkles. Outcome: Kathy V. I approved.

Anybody familiar with Milk Bar's origins shouldn't be surprised to see their Las Vegas location next door to Momofuku, just like in NYC. I've been a big fan of both founders for some time and couldn't wait to try both, even if it was one of their outposts. Inadequate planning kept me out of Momofuku on my recent trip to Sin City, but I was able to try Milk Bar for the first time. It was split decision. We managed to hop into a relatively short line knowing right away what we were going to try. I have been hearing about the famous Milk Bar Pie, aka Crack Pie, for ages. I even almost ordered one on Goldbelly for mail order deliver awhile back, but couldn't talk myself into the expensive FedEx fee on top of a $51 pie (btw, they don't do mail order w/ Goldbelly now, they have their own website). She wanted to try the Cereal Milk soft serve. We were also going to grab some cookies to go for later as well, but seeing how the cookies were packaged and handled we decided against them. In fact, the whole packaging and presentation was a bit unexpected. Everything was packaged like something you would get when the goods were not made on-site. I could totally picture this stuff in a high-end grocery store. We were expecting fresh made stuff. So we passed on the cookies and took a slice of the pie and the ice cream for $12.50 plus tax and tip. We found a seat nearby (they don't have their own seating), and dug in. The pie slice was very small, but considering the ingredients and the 300 calories quoted on the label, this was probably an adequate single serving. The pie was in a little box, like a McDonald's Apple Pie. Removing it I found the slice to be extremely cold, possibly over chilled, like not quite Sara Lee frozen pie cold, but headed in that direction. The taste was disappointing. My senses wanted to fire, but something was off. She took a bite and gave her unsolicited appraisal, "the butter is stale." Yeah, it had that taste. When I made it to the back edge, there was a little more of the oat cookie crust, some of it not so compressed. That tasted pretty good. I'm not sure if I got a bad piece or I just have bad taste, but I don't get it. This was a disappointment. 1/10. I took a few bites of her Cereal Milk Ice Cream and it was fantastic. It was appropriately named. The malty flavor with the creamy sweetness tasted just like the milk in the bottom of a bowl of Corn Flakes or Rice Krispies. This stuff is so simple it's brilliant. 9/10. I'll get the ice cream again if given the chance. I'm glad I didn't order a whole pie mail-order. Still not sure about the cookies.
I got the s'mores cookie pie. Marshmallow was toasted but melted, with the hint of chocolate. Would recommend anyone staying at the Cosmo! Amazing!

After a wonderful dinner with my boyfriend and his cousin, we searched yelp for a fantastic dessert place! Although it was a bit cold, especially for dessert --- we thought what the heck-- let's do this especially since they had such high ratings on yelp. We ordered and shared: * Crack pie - Small which was an excellent size. However, not too special or amazing. * Milk icecream - Have you drank the leftover milk from your cereal? (This is less sweet) - Have you tried condensed milk icecream ) (This is less sweet) - Texture was creamy. * Birthday cake balls - Why are they only available in sets of three and why are they pre-packaged in plastic ???? It's horrible for the environment and makes them seem much less fresh. - They are delicious but taste just like cake pops without the chocolate on the outside. Maybe my expectations were too high.... Overall, I probably wouldn't return. Meh maybe to try their cookies lol.

***3.5 Stars*** The ice cream whore strikes again!!! Well, what did you expect??? Mm hmm... you knew it was coming. You know how I do! My next victim: Milk Bar Las Vegas! Because, it's just so damn... mmm mmmm milky!!! When I found out that there was a soft serve ice cream bar within walking distance of where I was on the strip, I nearly flipped. I started running over to it in pure excitement. Okay fine... I didn't really "run". You can't really run anywhere in Vegas. There's too many damn people in the way taking their sweet time to do that. But anyways, I rushed over to get in line. The first thing I saw was their bright neon pink signage. So stinkin' cuuuute! Milk Bar is located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan Hotel, across from the Chandelier Bar. You can sample some of the goods before you buy. People have been goin' cray over their cereal milk soft serve, so of course I had to try it. Honestly, I wasn't really all that impressed. It tasted a little bland in my opinion and wasn't sweet enough for me. I can't really remember the other flavor that I sampled, but that too was just alright. But that birthday cake soft serve... oh yeah. Now, THAT was the bidness. It seriously tasted just like delicious birthday cake. You know your girl had to add some sprinkles to make things official. It was the perfect "icing on the cake" if you will. HA! But really, the birthday cake soft serve is really where it's at. I didn't get anything else, but this place is also notorious for carrying all kinds of baked goods. The crack pie and cookies seemed to be very popular with the crowd. I would def come back to try one of their baked goodies on a future Vegas trip. Although I enjoyed the soft serve, it wasn't anything that really blew my mind. Just your basic soft serve with a twist I guess. The convenience factor is what keeps this place poppin'. Plus, Vegas is HAWT and people catch the ice cream cravings all the time. If this place wasn't conveniently located off of the strip, I don't think it would be this popular. It's worth a stop but I wouldn't wait in a ridiculously long line for it. If you do decide to go, give their birthday cake soft serve a try. It's deeelicious.

The only reason this place is getting a one star is because the cake pop was pretty good. Other than that, the cereal ice cream was BLAH! The chocolate cookie was Eeehhhhhh, i mean it's a cookie, it was whatever. Coffee was no Dutch Bros. These 4 items came in strong at almost $50!!!!! I know you go to Vegas to spend money, but common! Do yourself a favor and skip this place.

A great spot to grab something sweet and unique. The cookies are fantastic, the soft serve is orgasmic. However the thing that I crave on a weekly basis and fills my dreams is the "Milk Bar Pie" (Although I discovered it when it was originally called "Crack Pie" & so it will hold this title forever and always in my heart.) This pie is addictive, fair warning, once you try it there is no turning back and you will compare all other desserts against it. If you're really in need of a major sugar rush and feeling frisky.... order the pie with a side of the cereal milk soft serve... you are most welcome.

Crack pie was seriously amazing! Milk cereal ice cream was legit and the cookies were very very good! I would say my top 2 are the cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookies and blueberries and cream cookie. So good!

Finally got a chance to try out the ever so popular Milk Bar at the Cosmopolitan. Tucked away on the second floor of the fancy food court/shopping area, lies the uniquely decorated storefront. Reminiscence of a mom and pop bake shop with a colorful hand written menu proudly displayed up top. The goodies are in full presentation behind glass as well as shiny soft serve machines in the back. For my first experience I opted for; 1. Compost Cookie: My favorite of the bunch! The perfect amount of chew with a mixture of salty and sweet flavors from pretzels, potato chips, graham crackers, coffee, oats, and butterscotch. I can totally tell why this is their best selling cookie, even at 4 dollars a pop. Will definitely revisit; 2. Milk Bar/Crack Pie: Not knowing what to expect, I was greeted with a thin pie/cookie concoction which was scrumptious, but overly sweet for my liking. Slightly gooey and nicely chewy with sweet and salty finish. My favorite part has to be the oat cookie crust; 3. Birthday Cake Truffles: Sadly, I can not say I enjoyed this truffle ball much at all. Ultimately, a super sweet and dense cake pop. Just not my thing. Will I return? Probably after a winning run at the craps table so I can try a slice of $14.00 birthday cake that everyone seems to rave about. I have really high expectations when paying 14 bucks for a slice a cake, and would hate to be disappointed.

Uhg so bad we literally had to throw more then half of it away. Literally it just takes like a blob of shit. Salty and bland as the same time To make this clear my Sugar fanatic child thought it was gross and was the one to throw it away We got the chocolate chip with marshmallow and corn chip cookies with the soft serve and sprinkles and cornflakes Ended up Adding fudge to help - it didn't work $17 for a sundae funday What a waste of money and calories Service was okay not bad but nothing special they did the job they're there for however if milk products are so significantly unique and unlike any other and takes a special Tongue to enjoy employees may want to ask questions and engage a little bit with customers Examples of questions to ask knowing the product again is so rare to taste 1. Have you tried any of our products before? 2. What kind of flavors do you normally enjoy? 3. Would you like to sample perhaps? I am aware of the pandemic however many other places are currently again offering samples And if you can operate a business By putting Product in a big cup you can try putting it in a very small cup or a spoon as well

I had high expectations for this place. I was thinking it's like high end milkshakes, cakes, and unique deserts. Instead it was like diabetes. Sugar overloaded menu of colorful confetti sprinkled cakes, shakes and cookies. It just didn't look appealing to me. I ordered a slice of their $15 Chocolate BDAY cake and it was dry, hard, sweet. Skip this place in Vegas and better off trying the Hello Kitty Cafe.

Was so excited to try Christina Tosi's milk bar soft serve after seeing her on master chef... but ew. Tasted like sour spoiled milk... just nasty. I once got a shake from somewhere else that tasted similar and they told me they accidentally served me from the side that needed to be cleaned... This was supposed to be funnel cake flavored but was more like raw funnel cake (?). The gal at the counter overheard my son say he didn't like it and said, "the trash can is behind you." I stammered a response in shock to that comment... another employee came over and they offered him a sticker or cookie, but he had wanted ice cream. So in the trash can it went  should have asked for a taste first I guess. My other kid liked his chocolate shake but I thought it was gross and sour milk tasting too. oh well. We went next door and paid more for an edible shake.

We tried the cereal milk soft soft serve. I threw it away after a taste. It tasted like rotten milk to me. The nastiest ice cream I've ever had. We also had the confetti cake slice it was okay. Tasted like it had been stored in the fridge for weeks.

Dear Milk Bar, My daughter was so excited to get a Milk Bar cookie. She loves Chef Christina Tolsi from Master Chef Junior. She inspired my daughter to bake. Now, the person behind the counter had a terrible attitude and really ruined a happy experience. My girl just ate all her veggies at dinner so this was a real treat and it's been a tradition to get a Milk Bar cookie after dinner at the Cosmo. So we are very familiar except they don't display the cookies anymore. I told the young lady if we may know what cookies they had this evening as we can't see them anymore and don't know what they had at the moment. She just gave us a stare. I asked again what cookies they had. She just what do you want? I again asked what do you have? She asked what do you like? I asked again what do you have? Then she mentions two cookies. At this point my daughter is confused. I then asked if we can see? She then shows us two cookies. I asked if that's all they had. She said no their are more. At this point, REALLY? We ended up getting getting a couple of cookies but it wasn't pleasant. I could not believe since we had great experiences in the past. And for some reason because the customer service was awful, the cookies didn't taste that great?!?! It didn't have a happy taste this evening. A good attitude goes a long way!

My wife saw Milk Bar all over social media and had to try. Overall the presentation was nice and it is in Cosmopolitan, so don't expect decent pricing. We ordered the soft serve with and without the corn flake topping, 4 cookies, and the birthday cake balls. We were disappointed, all I can say is that it tastes like super salty dessert. Just overloaded with salt. We weren't expecting great things, but few things are more frustrating than paying a lot of money for bad food. The cookies and cake balls were ok, but again, too much salt and you can get better desserts else where in Las Vegas, like Crumbl or try one of the many bakeries in China Town. I'm giving two stars because the soft serve with the corn flake topping was good, but it was horrible without the topping. We ended up throwing away half of what we ordered, it was not good and waayyyyy too salty. If you like salty desserts, then by all means, but it wasn't for me. There are so many better places in Vegas for desserts, I will never go back to Milk Bar.

I've been wanting to try this place for so long since I missed out last time I was in New York. But I was very disappointed.. maybe it's just how I tasted it but it was not appealing to me at all. Located right next to Momofuku, they have a lot of different things on their menu board. So much that I could not see where the soft serve flavors were. There was too much going on. We were able to try some samples and I'm glad we did. The cereal milk flavor was very surprising to me. It tasted like soggy cereal milk without tasting the cereal bits. The first taste is also a bit salty...? I was really taken aback with this taste and disappointed because I thought it would taste really good. We also tried their crack pie flavor which is a brown sugar custard. That was slightly better but I just expected a bit more taste and more flavors. Sad to say I won't be coming back but it was worth a try! Definitely get some samples before you purchase though!

I wanted to try Milk Bar and was so excited it was next to momofuku. We ordered three cookies and two tastes old and dry. We threw them away after two bites (cornflakes cookie) they were that bad . The third was compose cookies and it was ok. Just ok for $3 cookie is unacceptable. I loved watching her on masterchef and wanted to try her stuff.

For as much hype as this place had, I did not enjoy my ice cream like I thought I would have. I think it was because of that, that I was so disappointed. There wasn't much of a selection and it made me want to get another dessert elsewhere. I know my husband enjoyed his, but it tasted like old cereal. I'm glad I didn't pick it. Maybe I need to try something else. It also took awhile to get and the portion was small. I'll give it one more shot and update my review accordingly.
i've been trying to get their soft serve but the machine has been broken for 3 days. i go almost everyday to see if they have it and i just waste my time

Had milk for the first time and my expectations were a lot higher. I don't understand what all the hype was about. It just tasted like ordinary ice cream to me. To be honest I think McDonald's soft serve is way better. Sure milk might be a healthier alternative but it was pretty tasteless. Service was nice and friendly. They also helped us go through the menu so we appreciated that ! I got the pie dough crumble soft serve and my girlfriend got the corn flakes soft serve. We both agreed that it didn't really have anything special to it and she didn't even finish hers !?Have you ever seen your girlfriend not finish her ice cream ? That says something... Overall the place is cute and service is nice but for average ice cream it's a bit over priced. Would prefer Honeymee over this place 100%

Place This place was an order and go kind of deal. The aesthetics of the place was really nice with the neon lights and all. Service The service was pretty good and was patient with my indecisiveness. Food/price $ The ice cream was pretty good! I got the chocolate birthday cake. I heard from my friend that this place was better than blank slate back in Ann Arbor and I have to say I still like blank slate as my number 1 ice cream store! Milk has good quantity and definitely fills you up. Audience Great for everyone! I went with friends. Recommendation/tips? I would get a water cup because it's hard to find water in that hotel. Plus water bottles are $7

Very overpriced for what it is. No doubt that this is indeed good dessert. The compost cookie has the flavor of my dreams. But after getting two bestseller combos I feel like a fool. Such a tiny small bag with tiny portion of goodies for $50. I know it is Vegas and all but this is just a bit too much. I am sure I can find place just as good for a portion of the price.

Got to love delicious treats and milk bar does a great job of making out of the box desserts. This location is right next to momfuku in the Cosmo on the strip. Great place to get a treat after a nice meal When I went here I was very inspired to try out chef Christina's delicious treats after seeing her on chef table. I heard alot about the corn cookie, all her soft serve and the crack pie, so I needed to try them all! First I started with the soft serve and I tried the cereal milk, crack pie and the fruity pebbles ice cream. All very good in their own way. The basis of the ice cream is the cereal milk ice cream which tasted exactly like corn flakes. Pretty good but definitely not my favorite. The crack pie was awesome tasting like a Carmel butterscotch flavor. Now my favorite was the fruity pebble flavor. Fruity pebbles taste great to eat and the milk is even better which is exactly what this tastes like. So good! I got a slice of crack pie which I don't even know how to explain the taste. All I can say is it is delicious! It's like a oat buttery crust with a custard with brown sugar. It's just flat out delicious! Get this! The corn cookie was nice, soft and delicious. It kind of reminds me of the cereal milk soft serve in a cookie. It's almost tastes like dunking a cookie in milk. Awesome cookie! All around a good place for treats. Fun thing is you can try out the soft serve before you purchase it. Good place to grab some delicious treats!

I've ordered from Milk Bar quite a bit, they are becoming my mainstay for cakes, cookies & sweet things! I will continue to order from you, everything has arrived on time, on ice & packed amazing. Though you ship out of California for Las Vegas it's been amazing quality each & every time!
Cereal milk shake! I was surprised that it actually tasted like real cereal milk ! Delicious! Must try

After drooling over while watching Netflix's show Chefs table, I definitely wanted to try Christina Tosi's milk bar. Milk bar is located on the 2nd floor at the Cosmopolitan. It's right next to Momofuku. We went around 11am and it wasn't that busy. We got the cereal soft serve with the cornflakes topping. I wanted to try the crack pie but it was already so pricey that I skipped it. The soft serve was delicious, I loved the crunchy flavor of the cereal, it was not too sweet but had a slight salty flavor to it. I really liked the texture it was dense and rich. The taste made me all nostalgic of my childhood. The milk bar is definitely worth the try and I would recommend it. I would want to try the crack pie in future, saving this place for my future visit.

I love their dessert. I came here every time I go to Cosmo. I have gotten their Milk Bar pie (crack pie) and their cereal milk soft serve. The first time I got their cereal milk soft serve we didn't know it comes with the actual cereal on it. Just got one with my boyfriend and friend, we all got cereal milk soft serve and this time they all came with cereal topping. DELICIOUS! Their crack pie was good too. I usually get a slice and share. For some people it can be little bit too rich, but if you handle sweet like me. I think it's actually good. Crack pie reminded me of ginger snap chewy cookie. There are so many other goodies that I want to try. Will definitely try other things next time. Stay tunes.

February 24, 2019 Sunday - 9:30 PM for dessert 5 Adults Atmosphere - 4 stars Food - 2 stars Service - 4 stars Background - As were walking into the Cosmopolitan we saw ladies with ice cream. They told us we had to get some on the second floor. Atmosphere - Come off the escalator and you can see that it is just a walk up window. There is not much to the place. Food Drink - I had the fancy birthday cake, fancy means boozy. I think the hype in my head to have an adult beverage milk shake was going off in my head. But the hype died when using an extra wide straw and having issues getting any shake. I had to pull my straw out multiple times to eat the birthday cake that was clogging the straw. The other issue was with the vodka, it was not mixed within the shake very well. Some sips was okay that was a good milkshake, next sip you go wow that was some high octane fuel. Service - My wife is gluten free and he warned us the drink I ordered for us would not be gluten free, because of the cake. Afterwards I thinking what kind of vodka they use. By definition vodka should be potato and gluten free but many distillers use wheat in their vodka. Future - I will pass.

After watching award winning Chef and Owner Christina's Tosi's feature on "The Mind of a Chef" and watching her concoct unique cookies with names like compost, confetti, corn, etc. I knew I had to have it in my life. The huge hot pink M I L K sign calls out to hungry patrons ready to indulge in their sweet tooth cravings as if saying, "come into the light. You will find peace, comfort, & happiness here" in the form of cookies, cakes, fancy shmancy drinks, & soft serves. This is definitely my happy place; my kind of heaven on Earth. The line was minimal on an early Monday afternoon. The Cereal Milk soft serve w/ cornflake crunch topping was at the top of my list to try. Made with milk, cornflakes, brown sugar and a pinch of salt, holy moly it did taste just like the milk at the bottom of a bowl of cereal. The cornflakes on top and lining the bottom gave it the perfect crunch and boost of flavor. It wasn't too sweet either and pretty much amazing. So nice, I had to get it twice just a few days later when I was in Washington D.C. I also got myself the bday cake truffes and the corn cookie which my sister in-law raves about. The truffles were good, but nothing to write home about and I wouldn't pay that much for them a second time around. Really pricey. The corn cookie was also good, but not as good as I had expected. It did also get pretty crumbled in my bag, so there's that. Overall, I really enjoyed the soft serve and would get it again next time I am near a location. Also need to try more of their fun cookie flavors!
Ordered a cake for Thanksgiving to be delivered 3 DAYS PRIOR to our event and it still has not arrived (2 days AFTER said event). Thanks. Horrible customer service.
I am gluten free so my options were limited, but I was happy there were options at all! The gluten free birthday cake truffles were AMAZING!!!

I have seen the Netflix show, I have made the crack pie (from when Target used to carry the mix) - I got the cookbook last year for Xmas. I wanted to expertise it "live". The crack pie was good - but expensive for a small piece. The highlight for me was the soft serve - I swirled it with cereal milk and crack pie flavor (preferred the cereal milk flavor).

Really good custard ice cream and shake. It's not too sweet and the flavor was light..not too overwhelming. I got the blended version with cereal. Definitely going to get it again and will try their mini shakes.

Never thought you could make bad ice cream but the people at this place managed it. It has to be, by FAR, the worst ice cream/soft serve I've had in my life. The cheapest, generic ice cream sandwich at a gas station is much much better. Maybe I had a bad batch but based on the other reviews I think it's just bad all the time. If you enjoy flavorless, not sweet , but extremely salty "ice cream" this is the place for you. And then they go the other way and use ONLY sugar as an ingredient in everything else. I have no idea why there is a line here.

Celebrating my birthday in Vegas and stopped for a slice of cake in the late afternoon. No cake visible from counter (maybe due to Covid) but the girl helping us said they had yellow birthday cake and chocolate birthday cake. I ordered a slice of the chocolate. It was $16, so my hopes were high. Not good. The cake was dry. The frosting was overly sweet, if it was supposed to be buttercream, you could not taste butter, not even shortening. Just sugar. The top had something that looked like cookie dough, but again tasted of pure sugar. I was really disappointed in this place.

It was a treat to finally try one of Christina Tosi's dessert creations. The Milk Bar menu had a wide selection of interesting ingredients which one would never thought of using in desserts but apparently Christina Tosi was able to concoct interesting texture and flavors using ordinary pantry items like corn, cereal, malt, etc. Ingenious! After asking for the least sugary cookies that they have, I was referred to the corn cookie which consists of both corn and corn flour - surprise! And to my delight, the cookie was chewy, buttery and more than satisfied my craving for that bit of sweetness.

In terms of price, selection, portion and taste -- Milk Bar is a flat 2.5 out of 5. The concept has so much potential, but the execution falls short. My boyfriend and I came by last night for a pre-Marquee treat. We noticed the "Fancy Shakes" -- classic milkshakes with alcohol included -- and decided to try a couple. He went with the Cereal Milk White Russian, and I went with the Chocolate Malt. Both were $12 each, both had vodka and kahlua. Maybe we should've gone with something else, but these were pretty lackluster. They were extremely sweet, even for milkshakes, and the alcohol didn't seem to complement the taste at all. Hard to finish, and they were tiny to begin with! Rounding up because they have a delicious variety of cookies and other drinks. Plus, they're open late. Wish they had more than 4 flavors of shakes, though. We will not be back.

Crack pie. It keeps you coming back for more. Very aptly named. I really have met very few pies that I disliked so of course this was a hit with my (taste) buds. Unfortunately, I had to share with my husband. FYI there does exist online a recipe for this dish although it does taste better if you a) spend 0 time slaving over making your own pie and b) spend a lot of $$$ purchasing it. Their soft serve I thought was overrated. Then again, I've never been a fan of the residual cereal milk, always tossing it down the drain. This is a little bar-ish setup in the Cosmo food court. So many new places here now! A glutton's paradise

The milk ice cream with the cereal crisp and chocolate syrup was such a good choice. My friend got an alcoholic milkshake that he really liked. There was a short line but it went by quickly. The service was pretty alright. They knew was they were talking about. Seemed a little impatient though which is why I'm taking out a star. Other than that loved this place and would come back again!

Usually a fan of ice cream, I was very much disappointed in the tastelessness of this soft-serve. I was expecting some type of flavor dimension but it simply came flat. The ice cream tasted like plain 2% milk not even a hint of vanilla or anything--so if you enjoy some type of flavor/sugar in your ice cream this is not for you. Next, the cost of the cornflake topping was just outlandishly expensive!! Literally, the cost of the cereal topping on two ice creams would make up the cost of the whole box at local grocery store. Definitely one of the most overpriced spots for super bland ice cream. I do not recommend but if you're curious about the hype just like me, then try it for yourself but don't have too high expectations.

Wasn't expecting this famous bakery to be selling prepackaged cookies and truffles that are no better than your local super market. We were expecting fresh desserts and were given food in wrappers. Not cool...

So I want to give this place 3 1/2 Not that it was bad, but we went back 2 days in a row and both days they were out of the birthday cake soft serve. So I went with the birthday cake shake on the second night. The shake was super sweet, it had a bunch of sprinkles on top so when you got to the end of the shake your mouth is just filled with sprinkles so neither myself or my husband could finish it. There were chunks of cake in the shake too that I thought was pretty good. I just wish I could've had the ice cream. They are a tad pricey, we got a small and it was over $10. They have cakes and pie, but again a little pricey.
After a day of walking the strip, what better way to cool down and indulge! It's also located in my most favorite hotel in Vegas!

I came here because they are so instagram famous, and unfortunately fell for the hype. They are located in Cosmo, next to eggslut ( another overrated place which I do not like). They had already run out of many items because we didn't get there till around 8pm at night. I got the birthday cake, cereal milk soft serve, crack cake, and compost cookie. The cereal milk soft serve tasted exactly like leftover cereal milk, which is my favorite part of eating cereal. The crack pie was delicious, super sweet, and rich. Crack pie is almost exactly the same as chess pie, I think it only got so popular because of the name "crack". I am not completely convinced that this was a brand new recipe because I have been to plenty of bakeries in the south that have a chess pie that taste exactly the same. This cake is very easy to make and super affordable, so paying so much for such a small slice felt so unsavory. The birthday cake and compost cookie fell through though, the birthday cake tasted like any regular birthday cake out of the box. It was not worth the $14, the compost cookie was really dry and not that great tasting at all. In fact all of the cookies looked really dry and gross. I took a chance and bought the cookie but I regretted it. So save yourself a trip unless you really really want to try the soft serve.

5 stars for customer service... 1 star for cake...Terrible! Bought a whole birthday cake. Thought I was doing something special for a special person, instead I ended up being embarrassed to serve such a disgusting cake! Cake was drryyy and tasted stale. Had the texture of a scone, but with Less moisture! Was I given a display cake? Looked great, was just inedible. $60 in the trash.

I had never been to Milk Bar, so when I was in Vegas I knew I had to give it a try. Milk Bar is located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan. Service was very friendly and they let me try all their soft serve since it was my first time. I ended up going with the Cereal Milk soft serve with Cornflake Crunch. Overall, it was just okay. I found myself wondering what the big hype was- to me just tasted like any other plain ice cream I've ever had. I couldn't really taste the cereal flavor. Overall, it's worth a try if you've never been. But I don't think I'll be back next time I'm in Vegas.

I'm updating this because I got to try the cereal milk ice cream and it's not too sweet and works really well if you get corn flakes on top (which they also mix into the bottom as a pleasant surprise). Ask for a sample of it because some of our group loved it and some didn't really enjoy having ice cream that tasted like semi-sweet milk. The service I received was great as well for a walk up counter. I wouldn't recommend the crack pie, but it seems like there is an option here for everyone's taste which is good.

My friends took me to this place for the first time. I was not disappointed. Although pricey, the cereal milk flavor really tastes like the milk after eating cereal It was delicious and I will come back when I come to Vegas again!

Was very much looking forward to trying out Christina Tosi's Milk Bar! Social media has really bowed down to this place - it really is the best kind of advertisement for people who love sweets. It's right next to Momofuku, so you already have dessert next door when you walk out:). We got the milk and cereal soft serve (cornflake based) - I wanted to get that iconic cereal topping on top, but it was already so pricey that I opted out. The soft serve on its own was delicious, my husband had no idea what it was and then upon first bite he was transported back to childhood. It was unique, but the texture was fluffier than I anticipated - I was expecting a consistency that was more dense and rich. Maybe I'm just a custard gal. I would love to try her crack pie one day - it's all so pricey that I just couldn't bring myself to buy both the soft serve and pie during the same time. Will save it for a future visit!

Never had I've been so jazzed to try a place in Vegas in a while as I've been to try Milk Bar. So much so that I made that I came to Cosmopolitan just to try it. For those who don't know Cosmopolitan is the best hotel to go to eat if your a foodie. There are so many options as great options for fast casual options. Let's get to Milk Bar which is a truly unique option of bakery items (cookies, cakes, truffles ext) & soft ice cream. The uniqueness of the treats you can only get here are worth a try. Friendly staff and cool decor also make for a good experience. Initially I was going to get there sampler that gives you four treats for 23 dollars. I really wanted to get a milk and cereal shake instead of soft serve so I ended up getting milk and cereal shake and chocolate to truffles. Now you if your looking to get some soft serve let me make a suggestion, the crack pie soft serve and chocolate pretzel are simply amazing. I've never tried such a unique tasting frozen yogurt. The crack pie by far my favorite and the good thing is you can sample the soft serve (which is what I recommend doing) in order to see for yourself. As for the milk and cereal shake it was kind of god is what I would say. In just being uniqueness of trying something completely new it is great. I think the highlight was the sweet corn flakes that gave it an added touch m. Other than that it taste most like the taste of milk after it is been sweetness by cereal. Better than the shake was the chocolate truffles. A lot of people do the birthday cake ones, but you can't go wrong with the chocolate ones especially if you like chocolate. Value wise is where this place falls short. Even as a foodie whose use to paying much more for superb eats, this place is pricy for what you get. A regular shake is 10 dollars for a 12 once shake. The shake and truffles ran me almost 19 bucks. I think the best value is the sampler I mentioned early. If you are expecting out of this world taste for what you pay or rate this place based on what you pay you may feel disappointed. Despite value I would definitely come back and try more goodies. I hear there is a Milk Bar opening up in LA soon, so I will probably check out that location before returning.

Cereal milk soft serve + corn flakes and a slice of crack pie. This is my recommendation for first-timers. I've had the pleasure of enjoying most items on the menu. Haven't had a single thing I didn't like, but the cereal milk ss and crack pie are where it's at. Pricey? Yes. It's the strip. It's a celebrity baker. But there's an elevator to the parking garage right by Milk Bar, so if you're a local it's quite easy to park and have a treat and head home under the 1hr mark which = free parking!
The cornflake soft serve was soooo good! Also bought some cookies with the cute MILK tin!

I'm disappointed at this Milk Bar. And my sister was too after having a good experience at their LA location. So I was actually in New York when Milk Bar was getting popular. I watched that Chef's Table episode, and realized I missed out on trying her cereal milk soft serve. After watching the episode, I knew I had to go to their Las Vegas location during my weekend getaway there. I got the twist of cereal milk and crack pie soft serves. Unfortunately I didn't know which side was which because they're both white! It all kind of tastes the same, and after 5 mins, I threw it all away. I tried to finish it, especially after paying $6 for it, but my stomach started hurting. I also wanted to try a slice of birthday cake, but it was $14. I know Vegas prices are high, as the rent at the Cosmopolitan is high, but $14 for a slice of cake? I don't care how large it is, it's still steep, especially when the prices are more reasonable in LA. If you're wanting to try Milk Bar, I say go for it just so you can say you've done it. But if you're from LA, just try it there. And if you're from NYC, go to the original location if you haven't been there already. And if you do plan on eating there, the lines can be long. Though, when I was there around 9pm on a Friday, there was no line. Tables are between Milk Bar and Eggslut, and scarce, so just be aware of that.
Yum!!! You have to try their boozy shakes! If you tell them it's your bday you get a free cookie (have to prove w/ ID). Fun place in the beautiful set cosmopolitan!

I've had milk bar shipped to Washington and the cakes are delicious. I thought they would be even better fresh from the bakery, so I bought one during my trip to Las Vegas. It was terrible, nothing like the Milk Bar I've had before. The cake was very dry and the truffles on top were hard as a rock. So disappointed, since I have been such a fan.

I don't get the hype over this place. Maybe the flagship store is better? We went twice in one week, hoping that maybe we just didn't get the right thing, but the experience wasn't great each time. The birthday cake is a big piece (recommend sharing), pretty tasty, but it's definitely not fresh. Cold, crunchy, and a little dry. $14 for a slice of cake and it's just famous because of the branding - its not actually good. We tried the cereal milk soft serve with rainbow sprinkles and even that was sour and salty - not very good. 2 stars because they have an amazing brand and excellent cold brew. The coffee is the only good thing. Even the service was bad.

Ice cream treats with sprinkles, confetti birthday cake, and the ultimate for us die hard coffee connoisseurs birthday cake lattes. Now that you are tuned in: this business is located inside the Cosmopolitan on the second floor. It is a small little stand with a red lit up neon sign that makes some of the biggest and baddest ice cream treats in Las Vegas! My first visit to Milk was overwhelming, since at first I did not understand their menu. After the friendly cashier explained how to order all was great again. The menu is above the cashier and is clear, once you know what your doing. On this visit I had the pleasure of spending the day with my twins. Who is not up for ice cream? We were. Realizing that some of what they offer is alcoholic, it was a no extra added happiness for mom today. Confetti birthday cake and ice cream cups, it does not get better than that. Except if you add coffee. The twins had small cups of ice cream confetti style. Needing some extra help I had the birthday cake latte. That latte was just what I needed extra caffeine and if I closed my eyes I can envision a slice of birthday cake instead espresso! The quality of the ingredients that Milk uses to make their treats is of the highest standards. With that being said, the ice cream that I ordered for the twins was what seemed to be a vanilla base. Then that vanilla ice cream was mixed with chunks of birthday cake. What ever their secret it is a safe one? I won't tell! Then it is topped off with whip and rainbow sprinkles. They handed both of the cups to me. Before handing the cups to the twins I had to try a bite from both so it does not injure them. I took one for the team, both of the cups of ice cream were safe. As I explained these safety standards to the twins the ice cream chef giggled. The staff of Milk are highly trained and professional. They are willing to help their novice customers that are trying to order for the first time. Whom are not drunk either! They have some talented employees that only serve the best to the customer. They realize that the products that they sell are of high quality and evoke a certain arrogance about their product. They are confident in their positions as employees representing their company and customer service. Thanks to company of Milk for hiring such amazing employees that care about their position in the company, customer service, and the confidence in their product. Milk is an amazing place for some of the highest quality gourmet ice cream I have enjoyed in awhile. Located in my favorite hotel the Cosmopolitan it is worth that trip to find some tremendous delicious ice cream with or without alcohol. Their coffee is so good! I recommend the birthday cake latte! Trust it is worth the trip; braving traffic to try! The employees are friendly and competent that provide a wonderful place for your ice cream needs!

Milk Bar is a hit for a reason. I was skeptical, but all that skepticism went away upon trying the treats here. First of all, I will say this place is quite pricey for the small quantity you get. But man, is it amazing. The Cereal Milk soft serve is amazing, which has a slight sweetness but is accentuated by notes of saltiness, like actual corn flake cereal! We like to have this with the corn flake topping, as the crunch offsets the smooth ice cream. Another go to for us is the Crack Pie. It is called Crack Pie for a reason. Though it might be on the sweeter side, it is delicious. Similar to the Cereal Milk soft serve, it is a very sweet pie that is accompanied with notes of saltiness and bite to it from the rolled oats that are within. I hope you guys enjoy this place as much as I do!

Horrible customer service by Ingrid. Ordered some milkshakes, 1 cookie and 1 slice of cake. She was acting as if we were ordering the most complicated stuff in the menu! Rolling her eyes and giving us attitude. The milkshakes and cake were good.
Not worth it. Shake flavors aren't great and the cookies are like a store bought packaged cookie.

This is a great place inside the cosmopolitan hotel- we love to stop in for a sweet treat! We just picked up a birthday cake here, and it was fabulous, beautiful and had a rich vanilla taste. I had sprinkles in the dough and was soooo pretty and festive!

Oh myyy... the Milk Bar Pie (aka Crack Pie) is to die for... buttery, creaming, and no calories at all (kidding on the last piece) and a great after dinner treat after eating at Momofuku which is right next door. Also got a chocolate cookie which was okay but not great but would happily go again and again just to get the Milk Bar Pie.

I've been to this location twice- once in March and once in July and both times I've had a 5 star experience. Location by the 16 Block inside the cosmo Milk Bar is the PERFECT treat any time of day and night! On weekends they have late hours which is a plus when working tradeshows late and having client dinners. There can be a line at times but when I've been the workers behind the counter have been pretty efficient with moving through it. Don't be sticker-shocked. These prices seem similar as they were in NYC and I happily will pay $6 for my favorite cereal milk ice cream. I usually end up buying the 6 cookie deal ($22) to take home to family or friends (they travel really well! Cookie tins are available too) The seasonal cake flavor in July was Elvis cake- Peanut butter, chocolate , peanut brittle, and banana- and my goodness was it tasty- super rich but most of the Milk Bar cakes are. I brought it to my hotel and stuck it in refrigerator to share later and it kept well which is another bonus. Christina Tosi keeps coming out with more and more flavors but you can tell she puts so much thought into the development of her treats along with the quality!

Heard this place is good so I checked it out. First, the cashier was rude, not the greatest customer service. The milk shake was birthday cake and it taste gross, like cake batter basically. The birthday cake was pretty good, pretty moist. If you go, get the cake, the shake wasn't good! I gave it 3 stars because of their customer service!

Normally I'm not a sweets kind of guy, I like my salt and savory items, HOWEVER, Milk Bar is probably my absolutely guiltiest of all guilty pleasures so it makes sense that I stopped here multiple times while in Sin City. Located in the Cosmo, this little shop its the perfect place for a sweet treat after some time spent gambling or whatever you do while in Vegas (I'm not here to judge). Let's first talk cookies: compost, corn, and blueberry and cream cookies were what I tried. The compost is that mix of sweet and salty. It's got pretzels, potato chips, coffee, oats, graham cracker, butterscotch and chocolate chips- what more do you want guys? The blueberry and cream has bits of milk crumbs and dried blueberries- amazing. And the corn is like this sweet, buttery cornbread like cookie which I never knew I needed in my life. They also have soft-serve and shakes guys and they are perfect. The cereal milk soft-serve was my first swing. They say it's supposed to taste like the bottom of your cereal bowl, which is the best thing ever, right? And they nail it on the head. Milk, cornflakes, brown sugar, and with a small amount of salt. Oh em gee... A perfect ten. They've also got chocolate soft-serve and you can make this chocolate covered pretzel thing. I mean, you guys. It's heaven. It's amazing. It's so sweet and lovely. I'll be back. I'll be back a lot more. I can't wait to waste all of my calories on this because it's worth every penny and calorie.

Terrible customer service. I don't want to fault her too much because I'm sure serving drunk tourists for a living is not fun, but the cashier had a really negative vibe and attitude. Lots of eye rolling, curt and terse dialogue, and she even threw down our order on the counter. I had the slice of crack pie which I'd say is overrated. It was good but not $7.00 good for an 1/8 slice of a maybe-6 inch pie. The store itself and the pie had a whimsical presentation. Glad I tried it but it's not something I'd crave.

Been there a couple times now. Have tried the cereal milk with the crunchy topping, slice of birthday cake, and the crack pie. All are incredibly delicious. I usually hate birthday cake but their version is so unique. Perfect amount of sweetness which makes you wanting more without feeling like diabetes is right around the corner. Probably still has the same high amount of sugar as other cakes but the taste and mouthfeel makes it a much better experience. Most items are pretty pricey but it's a nice indulgent treat.

I got the cake and shake combo for 22$. This should be considered robbery, charging people 10$ for what tasted like a Wendy's frosty with chunks of cake and sprinkles. Because of the sugar rush, from my Shake, i have yet to try my 14$ slice of frosting packed cake. ($2 saving for getting the combo, more like 22$ in the toilet). Fear of a diabetic coma wins this review.

So I went to the Milk Bar after accidentally stumbling upon it on my way to Secret Pizza after the club but Milk Bar was already closed. Thankfully about a year ago I had seen their episode on Netflix that the baker got so I knew I had to make the trek back! I walked 30mins round trip for some pastries TWICE and they didn't disappoint! The team was so accommodating! They allowed me to make edits to my greatest hit box (I can't do ice cream because of my gastric bypass surgery.) The cornflake-chocolate-chip-marshmallow was warmed for me by them and it was exquisite! It also came with the B'd cake truffle and it was life changing! The staff also helped answer a ton of my questions in regards to the cakes, sizes, & prices and even got me a frozen cake to far better on the flight home. The staff at Milk Bar LV are extremely kind and welcoming and the food is everything your middle school heart imagined adulthood would taste like. Do yourself a favor and don't go to Sprinkles or any of the other pasty dessert bars. Go to Milk Bar and order EVERYTHING!

I tried the normal cereal milk one. I wanted the birthday cake one but it had eggs and I am allergic. So the cashier let me have the plain one (no idea if that meant it didn't have eggs, it was a weird transaction). Anyway, as for the hype...I don't get it. Taste literally just like milk. No other flavor...kind of salty. I had the crunch flakes on it too. Kind of expensive after all that so I ate it all even though i wasn't in love. They were also offering free samples of cookies or the ice cream to some people in line but I didn't get in on that :( But, I have a friend who went here multiple times was on their trip and tried all types of stuff and loved it. So I guess if you like that salty sweet combo this is for you.

After watching Christina Tosi's episode on Chef's Table and trying the cereal milk in New York, I wanted to get my hands on some crack pie or the compost cookie. The compost cookie stole my heart. Location: inside the Cosmopolitan hotel, next to Momofuku I tried: -Soft serve in milk and crack pie flavors. They were nice to offer us samples so we could decide between the two. Milk tasted better than crack pie. -Compost cookie: a packaged cookie for $4 Overall, the soft serve ($6) topped with corn flakes was just okay. Nothing mind blowing. The compost cookie however is probably the best (and most expensive) cookie I've ever tasted. I just finished the whole 80g, 340 calorie cookie. I regret not buying more. Inside of it is: coffee, butterscotch and chocolate chips, pretzels and potato chips. What a salty sweet combo! I'll make sure to try more cookies next time.

Long lines. Not sure what the buzz about this place was. Tried it. Not my thing. My wife liked what she had. But she also didn't think it was worth the time or money. Perhaps it was the night we were there.

Sugar rush? CHECK! Should you share a cookie? YES, if you don't want to feel your heart racing for a couple of hours. I've tried the cookies and those round desserts here. They're alright. THE BIRTHDAY CAKE is where it is at for this place! I've heard nothing but good things about it and this year for my birthday, THAT was the dessert I wanted. A small slice will do you just right. I'm pretty healthy and that cake made my heart race and every single bite was worth it!

Visited Milk Bar after stumbling upon it at the Cosmopolitan. We've seen documentaries on the story behind this bakery so we figured we had to try it out. We tried: -Crack Pie- super dense and tasted a lot like toffee / heath flavor. Not bad but overpriced and too sweet for us. You could only have a few bites and definitely need a glass of water or milk nearby. -Compost cookie- very dense and lots of textures. Not bad but nothing special in our opinion. -Frozen cereal milk ice cream- the star of this visit. It really tastes like cereal milk! It was creamy and delicious and worth the $6 they charge per cup. Staff was friendly and there wasn't any wait. Overall, the place is cute and there's a lot of cool concepts. Some of the flavors are just a tad bit too sweet and prices were on the higher side for what the portions and taste actually delivered. Worth a visit maybe if you have a sweet tooth or if you are a big fan of cereal milk!

They now sell slices of cake. CAKE!! Fall fast for the fall season Pumpkin Dulce de Leche or indulge in a classic birthday cake. Tried some cookies this time around. Nothing corny about a classic sweet Corn, the Blueberry & Cream is like a solid cheesecake without the cheese, and the Compost is all sorts of sugar, salt, savor, and crunch. We got half a Milkbar pie to go as well. It's the same thing as the crack pie with a family-friendly name because "family-friendly" is the first thing that comes to mind when I think about Vegas... They make it in ice cream too, and it's the best kind of sugar rush. I'll never get tired of the desserts at Milk Bar - they're quickly becoming a classic, and no matter how long they've been around, they'll never get old.

Favorite thing at Milk Bar is hands down their corn cookie - sounds weird but don't knock it until you try it! The cook is soft and buttery, the perfect texture and right amount of sweet. I like the cereal milk ice cream but a sample of it is plenty for me. The fruity pebbles flavor is uncanny - literally liquid cereal. If you're looking to try the infamous Milk Bar and haven't made it to NYC, I love how accessible this location is. Also I've visited numerous times and there has never been a line!

I had honestly never head of Milk Bar before but my sister wanted to go here when we were in Vegas a few weeks ago. She said that it was popular in NY. We had dinner at Momofuku next door which is also the same company as Milk Bar. Milk Bar is located inside the Cosmopolitan Hotel in Las Vegas. They are known for their Cereal Milk Soft Serve and Crack Pie. I got to try their cereal soft serve and it was just okay. It's pretty much just vanilla soft serve with corn flakes. I wouldn't go out of my way to get it. My sister ordered the crack pie and compost cookie. I didn't get feedback from her on her opinion. Since we were full she saved her treats for later. We had just come from dinner so I wasn't that hungry but they do look like they have a pretty unique dessert menu. Maybe grab a treat if you're already in the hotel but I would make a trek out here just to get dessert.

I visited Milk Bar one morning and although a bagel bomb sounded good, I had been wanting to try their soft serve for some time now so I opted for that instead. Hey, its cereal milk flavored so it counts as breakfast. There was no line at 10am on a weekday, but I've seen the place get busy at times. They are counter-service with no seating, but they're located inside the Cosmopolitan so there are places you can sit nearby. To be honest, their signature Cereal Milk Soft Serve ($6) had an off-putting taste at first. The first bite tasted almost like milk that had gone bad. But as I kept eating and mixed it with the corn flake topping, it got better. The corn flake topping ($1.25) is overpriced but provided a must needed buttery crunch to the ice cream. Milk Bar has a cool vibe and it's great that they use local and organic ingredients, but I still think they're overpriced and a bit overhyped. The soft serve is something unique to try once, but I wouldn't get it again. I would want to give their compost and corn cookies a try next time.
Get a combo to try all the goodies. The Milk Bar Pie is the best pie I've ever had. Everything is perfectly balanced and not overly sweet.

The experience might not be the OG NYC location but, when you have the hankering for some delicious Crack pie and wanna get your sweet tooth fix I enjoy Milk Bar. When your abilities to bake is absolutely horrendous, I appreciate the consistency of a good bake. They might not be the best bakery but it's like Mc Donald's, not the best hamburgers but due to that consistent taste you grew up with, I crave that comfort! Milk Bar satisfies my once in awhile hankering for some fun cookies and that buttery simple but oh so delicious Crack pie. When we have a reason to go to Vegas we get a nice haul to enjoy back at home. Enjoy a nice cup of coffee or a cold glass of milk with that Crack pie :)

I feel like the hype is a little too much for this place. Don't get me wrong, I thought what I ordered was delicious, but the dessert doesn't seem to reflect the price for me. Pros: -The Cereal Milk ice cream with the Cereal topping add on is delicious! (The milk does taste like how it would after you eat all the cereal. AND the crunchiness from the cereal pieces on the bottom and top were a good bite!) -the cookies are laid out In their wrapping so you can see what they look like before buying them. -the cashiers are quite nice and helpful when it's your first time! -the crack pie was good -cute and picturesque packaging Cons: -To get here, you have to go to the Cosmopolitan on the strip. (I'm a local and not a fan or trying to just get dessert but having to get on the strip. Good for tourists though. Stay for less than an hour and parking is FREE!) -the portions of the Cereal Milk ice cream and the crack pie were fairly small. (Think the "like it" from Cold Stone if you know what I mean) -the price for each was a bit ridiculous for the amount and taste you got (in my opinion) Cereal Milk ice cream: $6 but extra $1.25 for cornflake crunch. Crack pie is $6.50 per slice and fairly small. I'm glad I gave it a try, especially since I didn't get to in NY, but I think I'll stay away for now. If I do go back, I hope to try their cake truffles and their cookies! My cousin and her friend bought 12!
Just ok...don't believe the hype because it's pretty much all hype..we pretty much ordered one of everything and weren't impressed by any of it

Milk Bar can be found on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, adjacent to its big brother, the legendary Momofuku. Been wanting to try Milk Bar ever since I first laid eyes on the NY store five years ago. Christina Tosi's idea of simple rustic baking intrigued me. Behind the flashy neon signs, you'll find some of the plainest looking baked goods you'll ever see. No fancy presentation nor crazy decorations. Just chocolate sprinkles! Birthday cake milkquake: basically a McFlurry/Blizzard with cookie chunks in it. Enjoyed the mildly grainy texture with the buried cookie surprises. However, sweet indulgence only lasts for so long, in the case of milkquake, the first five minutes. As with most desserts and pastries in the US, the excessive sugar dump kills all enjoyable aspects of sweets shortly after the start of consumption. The cookies were sweet, perhaps a little too sweet... Will be trying their extensive cookie selections next time!

Service was fine, food was underwhelming/ disappointing. We tried two of their signature items: Cereal Milk soft serve- had a sort of sharp taste almost like off milk; and Milk Bar Pie- very small serving, but still didn't want to finish it, served cold from fridge so it was hard and tasted of nothing except butter and sugar. Haven't even tried the cookies yet- they don't look particularly fresh since each individually sealed in plastic. Not worth the price or calories.

On the 2nd Floor of The Cosmopolitan is Milk Bar by Christina Tosi. It's the sister bakery to Momofuku Restaurant by David Chang, who Tosi used to work for as pastry chef! Her specialty was turning toasted cornflakes steeped in milk into the base for her ice cream, panna cotta, and ice cream pies. In 2008, she opened up her first Milk Bar in NYC. And now there's a storefront here in Las Vegas! We stared at the menu and truly had no idea what to order, so the nice young man behind the counter offered samples to try. First we tried the Crack Pie and then the Cereal Milk soft serve. Sold! We decided to order a slice of the Crack Pie to-go, a pint size Soft Serve of Cereal Milk topped with crack pie to share, and a single size Soft Serve with corn flake crunch. The Cereal Milk flavored soft serve tasted just like the bottom of your bowl cereal milk with a tinge of corn flake flavor, except in frozen form. Pretty cool! It was light and frothy-like, not too sweet. My kind of dessert. But, the addition of the bite-sized crack pie toppings made the dessert a little overbearing. The pint size for two of us was actually a generous serving and we couldn't finish it. The single size for half the price would've been perfect. On the other hand, the corn flake toppings on the single size serving was a lighter dessert with a nice crunchy texture. Probably will order that next time! The Crack Pie itself is very rich. It is a chilled slice of buttery, brown sugar custard on a toasted oat crunch. It's like a cross between baklava and a granola bar. Very filling yet satisfying in just a few bites. Probably better with a cup of coffee. So much more to try and I'm sure I'll be back with friends and family so we can share! Cookies, cakes, breads, milkshakes, fancy shakes - a whole lot of sweetness right there!

"Gimme three fingers of milk, Ma." • Bart Simpson We had just eaten dinner and wanted to walk off our food babies. It was later in the night but way too early to sleep by Vegas-standards. So the compromise? A $12 Fancy Cold Brew, served with Frangelico. The coffee was so good that we drank it black [like my soul]. I enjoyed the shot of Frangelico since it gave it a hint of hazelnut without being too overwhelming but let's cut to the chase: $12 for a small cup of coffee. Eeks! I love you Christina Tosi but really? The storefront itself is right next to Momofuku on the second level inside The Cosmopolitan. You order at the counter and take your drink and desserts to go. I do like how they open later to accommodate all the zombies and clubrats around the area. The Cosmo is killing it with their food and beverage game. "Milk is for babies. When you grow up, you have to drink beer." • Arnold Schwarzenegger

This was my first time trying the soft serve ice cream and the shake. Both tasted sour and spoiled and made me sick. I wasn't sure if it was supposed to taste like that or not. Super unfortunate for how much I've heard good reviews from this place.

Tried the bday cake Milkquake (similar to a blizzard from DQ). Texture is nice, a bit softer than you'd get elsewhere. The Bday flavor is basically their cereal milk flavor with sprinkles and their bday cake truffles mixed in. Pretty good. I wish it had more of the truffles (i had to go digging for them... Pun intended). Overall not a bad spot for a quick dessert, but the menu is pretty limited. Stay Cheerful ;)

The hype from the "Milk" in LA was what drew me to try Milk bar in the first place, so when I saw it here at Cosmopolitan hotel in Vegas, it made me excited; however, they didn't carry the ice cream macarons which was the reason why I liked the Milk in LA. Oops! My mistake...because the Milk is not the same as the Milk Bar, Duh! lol I did a little research (trusting the yelp reviewers) with their trusty recommendations, so I tried a slice of the birthday cake and a chocolate cookie. Talk about sugar rush...I guess I'm not into the super sweet, super rich and dense type of cake and both the cake and the cookie didn't taste fresh either.

Crack pie $7 Worth every bite . Caramel sweet thinly sliced pie. Texture, somewhat chewy and soft. Delicious pie crust. A tad bit of powder sugar. Very good and delectable after a meal. Would buy again. Small but good.

Prices for cookies are steep at $4/cookie but I always come back for their blueberry and cream cookies to take back home. Their cereal milk flavored soft serve is creamy, light, and slightly salty. Cornflakes as a topping is a perfect pairing! Their can be a line at times but the service is quick and my wait for my order wasn't long at all.

This is a great place to buy treats for friends and family at home. I bought a bunch of their cookies. They recommended their compost cookies which is a mixture of many different things (pretzels, chocolate chips), their corn cookie (made with corn flakes) and their confetti cookie (funfetti like cookie). Their cookies are pricey ($4 per cookie). The confetti cake was pretty good! I actually liked their confetti cake more than their popcorn cake. The popcorn cake was on the sweeter side for me. It was my first time trying crack pie too. It was nice and buttery. I really enjoyed it...especially with the ice cream. I always like to get their milk and cereal ice cream too. It's on the plainer side, but sweet and savory. This place can have a long line, so if the line is somewhat short, I would give it a try! At least try a cookie!

We stopped by late one night and grabbed the "favorites pack" which came with Milk Bar Pie, a compost cookie, birthday cake bites and a small thing of their cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes on top. The cake bites were great, but the milk bar pie stole the show. The cookie was not our cup of tea, but I enjoyed the soft serve. It was a little less sweet and the corn flakes were a nice contrast.

I honestly ate this in about 2 minutes. The taste of the ice cream was a bit unique and tasted like the milk from a big bowl of Frosted Flakes. I added some sprinkles and Frosted Flakes and when I got near the bottom I was surprised with even more toppings which I think was the best part. Was a pretty good late night snack.

I was here over a month ago on a Monday right when Milk Bar opened at 2pm. I came to Vegas for the weekend for my birthday and was leaving on that Monday, which was also the day of my birthday. I was so excited to get a slice of the popular birthday cake and I was even more excited to be the very first customer! I placed my order, "A slice of the birthday cake, please." Employee, "We are sold out... Come back in 45-60 minutes and it should be thawed." Um..... what?! How could I be the first customer for the day and you're "sold out" of a product already?! The employee was definitely lacking customer service. I used to work in the food industry and would have to come in a hour before open to setup, prep, etc. How does Milk Bar not have someone come in an hour earlier to thaw their famous frozen cakes to be ready at open at 2pm in the afternoon. This was a very disappointing experience.

I really don't understand the hype about this place... My boyfriend suggested we try Milk Bar to try their infamous Birthday Cake dessert treats since we were both in Vegas for the weekend celebrating our joint Birthdays. But after reading the mixed reviews, we decided we couldn't stomach paying $14 for a single slice of cake, and instead opted for the Birthday Trio of Truffles which were still $2 a pop. The Birthday Truffles were really underwhelming, so I'm glad we didn't buy the cake. A truffle is toughly the size of a donut hole, and it tasted like cookie dough with some sprinkles in it. It was really sweet and I definitely needed some milk to wash it down.Overall, I'm not a huge fan of overly sweet American desserts so Milk Bar didn't strike my fancy. Prices are too expensive for dessert and there's really nothing special with the desserts to write home about.

The service was incredible! Quick and friendly! You can get many kinds of treats here. The milkshakes were where it's at for me. Malik helped me figure out which was the best for my taste. I'm glad he helped me out as there are many options. The fancy milkshakes have alcohol and boy are they good! Sip slowly was the tip I got and they are totally right. It is packed with a punch and it sure will get you. Great team there and I'll definitely have to stop by another time when I'm in town.

Not worth the hype. We waited in line for a solid 25 minutes just to be presented with a surprisingly non-diverse menu.
