The shake was pretty much one underwhelming flavor of ice cream that made me feel worse about myself for mindlessly consuming it and overpaying. The packaged cookies are actually really good, but not worth the wait for the price of everything else.

About a year ago I tried their famous cereal milk ice cream and it totally didn't do it for me. The texture of the ice cream is more on the icy than the creamy side - not my favorite. But on my most recent visit I got to try their compost cookie ice cream and it had a completely creamy and satisfying texture! I will also mention that it really does have a strong kick of salt. But I thought it was delicious with the sweet cookie flavor. I think I'll have to return for more.....!
We gave this a try on our Vegas trip. Had the bday cake and strawberry shortcake soft serve. It was good but not anything exceptional. Staff was friendly and helpful.

Had to try this spot before I left. After we checked out, on the way back to the car, I stopped for some "breakfast". I went with a regular Crack Pie Soft Serve. I was going to get myself a slice of "crack pie", but they were sold out. Crack Pie Soft Serve- This was pretty darn delicious. It was a decent sized portion. It is softer than most "soft serve" I have had before, but it was ice cold, and the texture was great. It was almost like frozen whipped cream texture? It was delicious. I just wish I had a piece of their "crack pie" to compare tastes/flavors to the soft serve. The crack pie soft serve was very similar tasting to a salted caramel flavor. It was just salty enough, and not overpoweringly sweet. I went to town on my serving, and could have ate another one. It was good stuff!

Can't go wrong with the cereal milk soft serve! It is absolutely delicious and I'm salivating as I'm typing this review. The cookies are really good too! I got a dozen of them as gifts and while it is kinda pricey, it is also worth it, imo.
Cute little place that's tucked between Momofuko and a Juice Bar. Always a go to spot because we always bring back a ton of cookies. If you can, try to go for every flavor. They're all great!!

I'm not quite understanding the hype. I got the cereal milk shake and it was very off. It was really salty and didn't had any sweetness to it at all. The ice cream part just tasted like as if I threw milk in the freezer and made it into ice cream. Then, I added corn flakes and blended it all up. It really wasn't anything special. The price is ridiculous as well. I got a regular size, which turned out to be $10 for a 12oz cup. Considering the how much I disliked the product and price, I don't think they deserve more than 1 star. I might come back once more to try their soft serve and update my review if that goes well.

Best birthday cake, EVER! First of all, I'm a lover of all things sprinkles and white cake! Now, tell me you're gonna add sugar cookie bites inside of my already favorite type of cake? Hells to the yeah you are now my new favorite person! My friends surprised me with this birthday cake during our dinner at Momofuku LV next door and this was definitely the highlight of our entire meal! Getchu some cake from Milk Bar and I know everything else on their menu is legit because who else gets an entire episode about their success on Netflix?!

After watching the Christina Tosi episode on Chefs Table, I knew I had to try that crack pie and birthday cake. I was already planning my trip here the next time I'd be in Vegas. We drove all the way from San Diego for the Super Bowl weekend, and this was our first stop on the strip. I love walking around the pretty Cosmopolitan hotel lobby already, and so it was a bonus that this place is here. My husband wanted to try the cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes, and I got a slice of crack pie and a slice of birthday cake. 1. Birthday cake: it was OK - not something extraordinary or out of this world, it it tasted just like a boxed funfetti cake mix, but elevated to culinary pastry chef standards (which was what she was going for). I'm just not a fan of that particular flavor of cake, but my favorite part about it was the cream cheese frosting in between layers 2. Crack pie: good, but in my opinion WAYYYY too sweet! It would be a good pairing with some strong black coffee to cut the sweetness a little bit. I was looking forward to trying this the most, but sadly it was way underwhelming. 3. Soft serve: The surprise of the day. I didn't think I would like it, but this was my favorite thing I tried. The cornflake-flavored milk in the ice cream really did take me back to my childhood and it was just the right amount of sweetness If I ever come back again I'd get the soft serve and maybe try the birthday cake truffles.

I was excited to try this place out after seeing all the photos and hearing about all the hype. Many years ago my dad had brought home a compost cookie from NY after a business trip and I remember it tasting sooo good. I was excited to be able to try it again. My husband and I shared a cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes topping and a compost cookie. Maybe it's the hype but I don't really understand how the cereal milk is so popular. The cereal milk flavor is pretty subtle and the cornflakes completely overpower the taste. I personally thought the cornflakes were much too salty and I didn't really care too much for it. Also, it's quite expensive too--an extra $1 just for some cornflakes!! The compost cookie was pretty good but not as good as my memory makes me believe. It didn't taste that fresh and was also a bit too sweet. I like it but I'll probably pass in the future...$3 is a bit too much for a cookie that didn't blow me away. Overall, this place is definitely hyped up. Prices are high and it's not really worth it. If I ever come back again I'll probably try the Crack Pie that everyone is talking about.

I visited one of their NYC locations so I was very excited for another experience at their location inside the Cosmopolitan. Situated next to Momofuku and across from Eggslut, I was shamelessly excited. At the time, they offered 3 flavors of soft serve which the staff graciously let me sample. I was surprised that I didn't care for the cereal milk flavor - to me it tasted like old milk. But I did really enjoy the fruity cereal milk flavor. I ordered a small ($6 - toppings extra) and topped it off with sprinkles and cornflake crunch - which is a real winner. Also on the menu are cookies, cakes, cake truffles, pies, and shakes. Staff was super friendly and there were no long lines both times we passed by. Super cute store. Great place to satisfy the sweet tooth.

I came. I saw. I conquered. So the last time I went to Milk Bar was in the NYC location and although I got to try their Milk and Cereal soft serve, I was saddened that they weren't selling their famous Birthday Cake by the slice. Well, lo and behold, did the dessert gods decide to bless me during this Vegas trip! I was actually kind of torn over whether to buy this because while I've paid plenty of money for dessert, I've never spent $14 for a slice of cake...but I caved. Now the question begs, was their Birthday Cake slice actually worth $14? It was your basic vanilla cake with vanilla frosting and stuffed with cake crumbs. But so much more than that. Call me a sucker for pretty desserts but the rainbow funfetti sprinkles seemed to make this all the more fun to eat! The cake was moist and sweet and the little cake crumbs sandwiched between its 4 layers gave it a nice crunchy texture between bites. For its price, at least it was quite a large slice of cake. Also shared a Milk and Cereal soft serve with friends and grabbed some cookies for their 3 cookies for $8 deal: CORNFLAKE-CHOCOLATE-CHIP-MARSHMALLOW COOKIE, BLUEBERRY & CREAM COOKIE and CONFETTI COOKIE. All 3 were delicious but I'd say the Confetti Cookie would be the winner. The Blueberry and Cream Cookie was also very yummy and tasted just like a blueberry muffin!
This was my first time here. It was super busy, but the cashier happily told me popular items and picked out an item for me based on my preferences. Cute little spot for a cute little dessert!

This is a must stop whenever I'm in Vegas! You can't beat the soft serve with cereal crunch. It's exactly the same every time; a perfect blend of creamy and crunchy with a bit of salt and sweetness. I could eat this every day!!!

After watching the Netflix special, I've been really looking forward to trying the place, so we had to make a detour prior to seeing Bruno Mars. The location is more of a bar, not a cafe, so not as spacious as a traditional location. I got a slice on their signature cake, which came at a pretty price of $14. While I understand that all prices in Vegas are inflated, I was not blown away - it was good, but nothing to give it that extra wow factor that would warrant the price. We also tried the cookies, while good - were all individual wrapped in plastic. I could understand the packaging option for people wanting to take some baked goods to bring home, but for enjoying in the moment - the plastic was annoying because I was wanting something fresh from the counter. Overall fun experience, nice presentation - but not worth a detour.

Came to check out this dessert place and it hit the spot! My group ordered everything on the menu...a chocolate cookie, milkshake, bites, and frozen yogurt & it was all delicious!! Everything was so fresh and worth the cost. Definitely recommend the chocolate cookie!

Omg. I wanted to like this place so much, but I just couldn't. I first saw this famous cereal milk soft serve on every foodies Instagram page in NYC. It looked so delish I wanted to try it ever since. Low and behold, MomoFuku Milk Bar is located on the second floor of the cosmopolitan hotel. Right next to Eggslut! I decided to give this place a try after dinner. I was soooo excited!!!! Finally trying this cereal milk place? YASSSSS GIRL YASSSSSS. The employees were just sooooo friendly. She explained the entire menu to me and what they're known for. So I trusted her and got the cereal milk soft serve, with corn flakes on top. She said this is what they're most popular dessert. Oh no....... the soft serve was just milk....it was milk in ice cream formation. Ummmm. I mean I should have expected that, right? The consistency of the soft serve was so creamy, which is the only way I kept eating that thing. I'm sad I didn't try their crack pie which I've heard good things about. But maybe next time!! But for now, not impressed with the cereal milk soft serve. :(

It was our departure day and the wife and I were on a Friday night "red eye". As a result, we had a full day to kill before leaving for the airport. We decided to cap off our trip with a stop at Milk Bar. The wife wanted to try it for her first time and have one of their cookies to see if it would be worth the effort trying to bake it at home. I was down since I wanted to give Milk Bar another try to see if my previous so-so experience was a one-off. I had the Cereal Milk White Russian ($12). It was boozy and possessed the advertised cereal milk flavor. From its taste, it could've been something memorable. Instead, it was memorable for the wrong reasons. What I received could hardly be called a milk shake, but rather cold cereal milk-flavored soup with booze in it. The shake was so lacking in thickness, my plastic straw was unable to stand up on its own in the cup. I drank it right away in the air-conditioned comfort of the Cosmo not in the afternoon Vegas heat so I couldn't attribute its immediate soup-like quality to the temperature of my surroundings. I'm not sure if it was due to not enough cereal milk soft serve being used in the mix or using room temperature alcohol instead of it being chilled. Regardless, it was a failure of execution especially for the price. Dairy Queen has nothing to worry about.

I love ice cream! While in Vegas I had to try this place out. I wanted to try the soft serve and I am happy they offer samples. I wasn't crazy over the cereal milk, but I really liked fruity cereal milk. It taste just like Fruity Pebbles and had to try it with flakes. My soft serve was offered in a cup and decorated very nicely with the topping. I really like how they put toppings on the exterior and on the inside of the ice cream. After all, I am paying $1 extra and I didn't feel jipped. The ice cream was good, but a bit on the creamier side. I'd love to try the other items.

Yuuuuum is all I can say . Stop by this place in the cosmopolitan hotel for all kinds of goodies . Milkshakes , cookies , coffee and some pastries ! The coffee was perfect and the cookie selection is very unique .. I got the "compost cookie " which literally has everything in it !! Soooo good . The cookies get blended up into the shakes too . This is a win/win

Clearly, my relationship with Milk Bar would fall in the complicated category. But I really, truly, genuinely feel like this four-star review will be where we land. I've been back. I keep going back because the OG milk quake was just.so.good. I still crave it, so I go back hoping that I won't be let down repeatedly. I can happily report that the last three times I've been (in probably about as many months and in locations across the US), I did not experience the soupy disaster of three-star reviews past. The ice cream is still not quiiiiiite what I remember, but the consistency of the quake has been...consistent - good, thick, and chunky. I hated writing that whole sentence as much as you hated reading it. For what it's worth, I asked someone at their East Village location why the heck I had such inconsistent experiences in the past and she said it had something to do with heating up the cake balls which then melt the ice cream but that should never happen so if it does, I should take it back and ask them to fix it. Obviously not verbatim, but you get the gist. Long, very long story short...if you love something, don't give up on it. Maybe consider giving up on it if it consistently disappoints you, but do your research and do it throughly first. You might be pleased with the outcome. My work here is done.

I have been wanting to try Milk Bar for a few years now and honestly I was a little let down. Do no get me wrong, I definitely think you need to try it at least once but besides that, it is not a place I will be killing to go back to. If you get the cereal milk soft serve, it is a must to get at least the corn flakes on top. If you don't it really won't do the ice cream justice. My favorite was the compost cookie. I tried a few of the other flavors and wasn't too impressed. I also tried the Milk Bar pie and bday truffles; I did not like the pie at all and truffles were so-so.

when you're hungover and you need some sugar clap your hands *clap clap* I've had the pleasure of trying MILK Bar in NYC when they first opened up and I was hooked. It was my go-to must thing every time I went for a visit. And then we ended up in Vegas and I was like I can fly over for $39 and get myself some crack pie and shakes. Mmmhhmm yes you can girl. We ended up getting Egg Slut for breakfast and having MB for dessert and 'tis is what I call a good morning. There wasn't a wait which was great cause I saw it the day before and it was wrapped around the corner like say what. I also got their birthday cake bites which are super dense and packed with flavor. And you can't go to MB and not get a milkshake so I got coffee shot added in mine (birthday cake + coffee). Nailed it!

I love Christina Tosi, and I love cereal milk just as much, so I knew I just HAD to go here. For $8 (a pretty steep price!) I got a small cereal milk soft serve with their signature cereal crunch. Overall, I thought it was just a-ok. The concept is pretty cool, and I will admit it does taste just like cereal milk, it's just not as desirable as you would expect. I don't think I would ever go out of my way to eat here again, but it was decent. My fiancÃ© HATED it. After one bite he begged me for a stick of gum and kept making faces. Overall, worth a try to say you've been here, but know that's it's probably one and done. :)

Located next to Momofuku in The Cosmopolitan, this is the place to try all the ridiculous desserts made famous by Christina Tossi. You order from a counter and if you can find a place to sit (around the Cosmopolitan) you could maybe eat there, but there are no actual tables. The cakes are tall and one slice will set you back $14. I went for the Crack Pie, which has been renamed and is now called Milk Bar Pie. For $6.50, I got a small slice. They gave it to me straight out of the refrigerator, to go. I ate it cold in my hotel room and it was sweet and awesome. This is serious dessert.

I love the goodies at this place and I'm so glad they have a store in Las Vegas!! Their cake pops are delicious!! You're supposed to keep them refrigerated but they can stay out for 5 hours. I have bought them in the morning and flown out and kept them unrefrigerated for about 7 hours and thrown them in the fridge, and they were still fine! I love the chocolate flavor and the other seasonal ones are good too. I also LOVE the cookies!!! The compost cookie is amazing, and the blueberries and cream is delicious! The double chocolate one too! They don't always have every flavor, but they usually at least have the compost, corn flakes, and blueberries. This is located in the Cosmo where all the food is so it's also easy to find.

I first knew about Milk Bar because of watching Masterchef and Masterchef Junior because of Christina Tosi. She's one of the judges on those shows and she owns Milk Bar. Considering how fantastic of a baker she is, I just knew Milk Bar was going to be deliciously amazing, but I never had the time or opportunity to visit Milk Bar in Las Vegas. And then my friends visited here and we happened to walk to the Cosmopolitan where we happened to come upon Milk Bar. I was super excited because, see above. While my friends decided to go with ice cream, I went with cookies. They loved their ice cream flavors, by the way. I purchased 6 cookies for $22 and got 2 of each flavor: cornflake-chocolate chip marshmallow, chocolate chocolate, and corn cookie. Let me just say, even after keeping the cookies chilling in the fridge for a couple of days, the flavor was amazing and the cookies were chewy. My favorite was cornflake-chocolate chip marshmallow, hands down. I'm disappointed that I only purchased 6 cookies, but that was all my wallet could afford. Totally worth it though. I want to come back here one day and purchase more than just cookies. I doubt I'll be disappointed no matter what I get here!

Cookies are good and it kinda taste like rice crispy. It's $4 each for cookies and it's not even big. Chocolate truffle my favorite, chocolatey inside and the outer cover taste soo good but I don't know what it is. It just super good. Crack pie is small, pricey and tastes okay. The crack pie soft serve is good too. No need for toppings. I had a hard time deciding and reading their menu. The two ladies was like rushing me.

Milk Bar is Located in the Cosmopolitan on the Las Vegas Strip. This is a small counter that serves some sort of soft serve, cakes and cookies. The thing that is popular are the Milk Quakes. The Milk Quake has added broken dessert added to it. Desserts are very EXPENSIVE$$$$$$$$$$$ A 6in Malted Milk Chocolate Cake will set you back $56.00! The Milk Cake cost $10.00 (2017 pricing). We love watching Master Chef and we like Pastry Chef Christina Tosi so we thought we wanted to try something from Milk Bar while we were here. The person at the counter seemed helpful and we tried the Strawberry Corn Milk Quake. It might not be Milk Quake's Fault but when we were there they don't provide a counter or any seats for you to enjoy your treat. I note I have only been here once and have only tried the Strawberry Corn Milk Quake ($10.00). The frozen confection was served to me very melted and tasted sour like yogurt. It didn't take like strawberries. The milk quake also had lumps of broken corn bread in it. Both of us thought this Milk Quake tasted HORRIBLE! Two taste and the Milk Quake was in the trash. The Milk Quake was high in price but turned out to be very low in Calories. :(

I have been wanting to try this place for quite awhile, especially with the Christina Tosi's showcase on Chef's Table. Now, I have never been to the original but if the food tastes like it did here, I would be disappointed after having heard such good things. Overall, this place gets a 2.5 stars from me. When approaching the counter, I always thought it was weird that the cookies were individually packaged. Perhaps that's better for this type of establishment or maybe it's an excuse to jack up the price a bit more but it made everything seem premade and not fresh. My date and I got three cookies (chocolate chocolate, compost, and cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow) and some chocolate soft-serve. We also sampled two other types of soft-serve. Regardless of which flavor we tried, they all had a sour taste to them which to me was off-putting. The three cookies all had a very nice texture, firm but soft, essentially the perfect cookie texture. I have a hard time picking which was my favorite because honestly they all tasted very similar. They too had that slightly sour flavor profile that was present in the soft-serve. It must be the cereal milk...Anyway, the cookies were good and I did enjoy them but were nowhere near the best I've had; they were just different. The chocolate chocolate honestly did not even taste like chocolate which seemed really odd to me. I would normally think that I came on an off day but seeing as how they are all pre-packaged, this must be how they all are. It's a very weird feeling for me. I'm disappointed but I also want future cookies I eat to have the same texture as these.

Located in Cosmopolitan, their lively stand will catch your eye. Desserts galore! Compost Cookie: Like a kitchen sink, this has everything you could think of in it. I recommend asking for it hot! Crack Pie: I believe they said this is a brown sugar like pie. This was good but incredibly sweet! So have a jug of milk close by. Cereal Milk Soft Serve: The soft serve was heavy & I do not know how to describe it but I just was not a fan... Ask for a sample before choosing which soft serve you want.

3.5 stars. Good place for snacks or dessert after a meal. My SO and I actually had a milkshake (chocolate cereal milk) and a soft serve ice cream (crack pie) and we thought it was interesting. The chocolate cereal milk does indeed had some trace of cereal scent in it and not just plain chocolate taste that you'd expect. We both tried the crack pie ice cream but honestly I couldn't really figure out what was in it...maybe a lil bit of caramel and vanilla ice cream..but prolly something else in it, too. I'm generally a dairy treat enthusiast but I thought the treats there were a bit too rich and sweet. Nevertheless, it's a good place to try something that tastes different than regular dairy flavors you can get elsewhere. Price wise they are slightly expensive..but given it's affiliation with Christina Tosi's name and it's location in Cosmopolitan Law Vegas..that's to be expected. Good place to have a quick treat/dessert..especially after finishing a meal at Eggslut or a Momofuku store nearby!

I had high expectations for milk bar but it was just OK. It reminded me of Honeymee but not even as good. Good to try once. I did hope they would have the blueberry cake but unfortunately not this time around.

Overrated soft serves, shakes, and cookies. Their marketing team definitely deserves some recognition though. Everything from installing those ig worthy neon lights/ signage to choosing the prime location inside Cosmo. Great work to those guys. At the end of the day, save yourself the $ and head over to McDonalds instead!

We almost didn't come here because the reviews seemed pretty hit or miss. But it was my birthday and I wanted to try the birthday cake. Yes it's expensive, but you know that. Overall I thought it was great. Perfect ratio of frosting to cake and I liked the truffles on top. The employee was friendly and efficient. I obviously wouldn't get this cake frequently at the price point but I might order it again next year.

Best cookies ever! I first tried them when my friend brought them back for me from NYC. When I found out there was a location in Vegas inside the Cosmopolitan hotel, I knew I had to make a detour and get more. All of the cookies are excellent, but my favorite is the compost cookie. Aside from the cookies, I've also tried the birthday cake, which tastes exactly how you'd imagine - like the nostalgic boxed funfetti cake, but better. I've also had the milk-flavored soft serve they're famous for, which isn't my favorite. It tastes exactly like milk, with minimal sweetness. I'd recommend the crack pie soft serve with cornflake topping - the saltiness of the cornflakes works well with the ultra-sweet soft serve.
I stopped by around 11 pm they only had one flavor available . The soft serve was terrible and expensive! . Mc Donald's ice scream tasted better than this !

No longer so impressive. Has Tosi released herself from active management of the LV place? From the last two visits, I feel that the quality of the cookies have really taken a fall-- like off the cliff of deliciousness. For the price of the desserts charged, I would expect better offerings.... not dry, bad QC wrapped desserts for take home. Even the soft serve thing I tried, meh. At best!

CRACK PIE. There's a reason why it's called crack pie. It's just filled with butter and sugar, but its addicting. A little pricey, ~$6 a slice or $56 a whole pie, but totally worth trying... over and over again... LOL. I love their cookies too, it's more expensive in Las Vegas than New York, but you can't blame them. I really enjoy the blueberry & cream cookie. I like it when it's warm, so microwave it for ten seconds. I also enjoy their soft serve. They do split flavors too. I got the regular cereal milk and the crack pie soft serve served with some salty topping. It's delicious, although the salty topping gets tiring after a while. It is so hard not to spend a lot of money here. I always end up walking away with more than $75 worth of goodies. I just wish it was cheaper. Hurts my health and my wallet every time I buy cookies and crack pies from here, but worth trying at least once!

After a very poor experience at Milk Bar Las Vegas, I was ready to completely write it off but my last trip made me definitely rethink my negative review from the last time. Adding on the corn flakes to your soft serve is a must! My previous experience without any topping was just any ordinary ice cream. The corn flakes topping not only adds that extra texture and crunch, but also an extra saltiness that matches well with the sweetness of the ice cream. In addition to my lackluster selection, the Milk Bar suffered major issues in terms of figuring out how to get the food out to people in a timely manner. This time around it appeared that there was more awareness of numbers of customers and trying to get the product as soon as possible. Overall, the Milk Bar has made it on my list of go-to places in Vegas especially with their improvement in customer service that was lacking from my first visit.

What a sweet surprise, found a Milk Bar in Vegas :D It was nice to get a taste of this NY treat in NV. They have creative desserts which are on the pricier side, but quality ingredients are used. The employees were very friendly and had a good sense of humor. Their cookies and truffles are excellent, very unique and full of flavor.

The staff was so great and friendly. Super fast also and will get your order out ASAP. With that said, Milk Bar is located at the second floor of Cosmopolitan Hotel so you will have other options should you choose not to drink sweet milky shakes. The milkshakes and quakeshakes were good. A bit too sweet for my taste. The portion is not very big for the price. Selections of flavors are also limited. Often a particular flavor will be sold out when you get there late night. This place doesn't have a seating area for the customers so it's also a bit hard to eat the pie that we got. We had to find seats near the hotel lobby and to eat the pies since we didn't want to stand and eat our desserts.

I was definitely expecting more from this place based off of the photos. The reviews were accurate, everything was subpar at best. Which is unfortunate, I tried the Red Velvet Milkshake, B-Day Cake slice, B-Day Cake Truffles, and Milk Pie. The only thing that was above average was the Milk Pie. The Cake slice was hard and not moist at all, and everything else was just...regular. I definitely will not be visiting this place again.

I tried the Compost Cookie and slice of Birthday Cake. Both were wayyy to sweet and cloying. I could not eat more than 2 bites of each. I was so disappointed as I was looking forward to Christina Tosi's creations. I honestly don't get what the hype is about. You can get better baked goods at any other bakery. :(

7.25 for a 6oz froyo with cornflakes crunch is a high price tag BUT it is soooo darn good!! It really tastes like cereal milk but the best part is their cornflakes!!! It's not just any corn flakes, it's sweet and salty and has that perfect crunch!!! I've had this 3 times in NY with sprinkles and found out I've been doing it all wrong when this came to vegas and my sister ordered it with the cornflakes! I couldnt stop eating it and I didnt even feel like ice cream which is absurd! Too bad cosmo charges for parking and I dont think Milk bar validates...

Oh Milk Bar, how I love thee. Your cracked pie changed my life and I literally crave it every time I have a sweet tooth. Located in the Cosmopolitan, the line surprisingly wasn't bad. The pink aesthetic is perfect for Instagram, but the desserts will keep you coming back. A must stop on every visit to Las Vegas.

I really went back and forth with this review on 3 or 4 stars, so I'll say this: for the novelty, it's definitely 4 stars. For the product, 3 is more accurate. This place was on my girlfriends radar so we stopped by a couple of times during our stay at the Cosmo to try what they had to offer. It's basically a stand on the second floor as there's no seating or interior, so if you don't want to eat and walk you better hope there's open seating across the way. The people working the counter were friendly and quick to get your order. First visit we tried the crack pie and the bday cake, which cost us around $20. Definitely pricey for what we received. The cake was super sweet (duh) and the crack pie reminds me of a pecan pie just without any pecans. We enjoyed our selections but wouldn't necessarily get them again. So we tried a second time. Second round: assorted cookies, chocolate cake truffles, and cereal milk ice cream. I will say, the truffles were amazing as they tasted almost like a really gooey brownie to me. Definitely my favorite. The compost cookie wasn't bad but for something with so many flavors in it, it tasted almost bland. Finally, the cereal milk ice cream tasted exactly like it sounds, but we were only able to eat a few bites. Overall: you're paying for something different but not necessarily something you'll ever want again. The treats are totally instagram worthy but maybe not as worthy to your tastebuds. I'm glad I tried it but am I craving any of it? Not particularly.

On the day of my birthday I was alone in the room at Cosmo. I met up with my 2 girlfriends and they decided to get some dessert at Milk Bar to throw a little birthday thing and sang me a birthday song. We ordered the birthday Combo with a slice of a birthday cake, and provided a candle to go with it. Crack Pie- this was really a slice of pie on crack, very potent and caramelized filling. Birthday Truffle- donut hole size, tasted like the birthday cake almost, and truffle-like, I guess that what they called it the birthday truffle. Birthday Cake- wish there was a cupcake like this. The cake was fluffy and deliciously sweet. Cereal Milk Ice Cream- best ice cream ever, wasn't sweet at all, paired nicely with the birthday cake, and it was pretty addicting. Compost Cookie- tasted like a macadamia nut cookie and oatmeal cookie in one. Minus a star- I wish they had a better plate or something for the setup, we just used the cardboard box and looked very messy. I wouldn't take anyone here for their birthday in the future. Everything else was delicious.

I realized cereal drowns in milk therefor milk is a cereal killer. At Milk Bar, I love being a cereal killer. Milk and cereal, the perfect combination. Fact: you don't need to be a kid to eat cereal. At Milk Bar they serve ice cream that taste just like milk and cereal. Milky vanilla ice cream with cornflakes. It doesn't sound like it would taste so good, but somehow it's the perfect combination. I'm not big on ice cream so this was a surprise. I've had their ice cream before at their New York location and it was yummy too. Along with their ice cream they serve an item called Crack Pie. I had never tried the Crack Pie before but I decide to go all out and took some home. The Crack Pie wasn't bad but it wasn't mine blowing. It might have tasted better if I had warmed it up but it was still good. However, it just didn't quite live up to its name. I tried the Crack Pie soft serve ice cream and I wasn't a fan. I suggest sticking to what they're known for. Get the cereal and milk soft served because you're at a Milk Bar of course.

I love having a Milk Bar outpost in Vegas. So much easier coming to this location than flying to NYC! It's pricey, but for something as unique as cereal milk soft serve, I don't really mind. On my most recent visit, I got the cornflake topping with my soft serve, and it added the perfect crunch. Plus, they add cereal to the bottom of the cup too so every bite had that crunch. We always stock up on cookies to thank my mom for dog sitting. They're individually wrapped and sealed so they travel well. The compost cookie is my first choice, and my mom loves it even though she's not a coffee drinker. If you like boozy shakes, this is a great place to check out. They had a couple specials featuring St. Germain and another that had Glenlivet 12 year.

Stopped by the Milk Bar located in the Cosmopolitan during a night out with friends. My friend really wanted to get the cereal milk soft serve because she had It back in New York. They do offer milkshakes, "special" milkshakes with alcohol in them, pies, cookies, and ice cream. I believe they also have some snack foods like bagels and what not. We ordered the compost cookie and the cereal milk soft serve with sprinkles. I was shocked that It actually tasted like cereal milk. It actually tasted a lot like the Kellogg's mini wheat cereal. It was okay. The compost cookie I would definitely get again. It has everything in It!! What It reminded me of was the Kona Coffee cookie from the Honolulu Cookie Company which is my favorite cookie from there. I don't know if the ice cream is worth the price, but the cookie did make up for It. I need to buy a box of them next time!

Crack Pie - $6 per small slice but gelatinous, delicious, and flavorful. It resembled what sweeter, thinner layer of moon cake. Cereal milk soft serve ice cream with flakes - Delicious, sweet, like sweet milk leftover after consuming a bowl of cereal and the sugar had been lingering. Sweet cereal milk soft serve - Too sweet. Crack Pie soft serve - Not as good as the Crack Pie. Perfect 10 - Vegan cookie was thick and crunchy. Put in a microwave for 15 seconds and it was hot cookie heaven.

I was so hyped to visit this spot after watching the Milk Bar episode on Netflix. The cake truffles definitely lived up to my expectations, but I was the only one in my group that seemed to really love them. They gave them to my sister for free since it was her birthday. I thought that was a nice touch. The soft serve itself...I did not love. I have to add that I don't actually love the milk left after you've devoured a bowl of cereal, so that may give you some perspective on my opinion. The soft serve just didn't live up to my sweet expectations of ice cream. Think soft serve but with mild sweetness.

There are some desserts that look amazing on Instagram, but fall short on flavor and fails to elicit late night cravings. Milk has become that to me. Having tried the bday cake, cereal soft serve with crunch topping, crack pie, cake truffles and cookies, the overly sweet and decadent crack pie is the only thing that would drive me to revisit. This is so wrong of me to admit but, I tried giving away the birthday cake slice I didn't finish to a homeless person and... I guess beggers CAN be choosey. Maybe I need to go on a diet as well.

I was told ... when I'm Vegas make sure you stop here so of course I had to check it out! They're located right inside the cosmopolitan next to an Asian fusion restaurant. I asked them to give me there best recommended cookie and that's what I got! I got a warmed up cornflake chocolate marshmallow cookie - I've definitely had better cookies but I imagine if I were drunk and gambling, this cookie would've been mind blowing. I left a little disappointed but I would definitely give it another try.

I get it. There are some restaurants out there where people love or hate it. Milk Bar is one of those places and it just resonated with me a ton since the first time I had their desserts. Most people who are coming to this Milk Bar will probably have had this at some point and this won't be your first time. However being that this closer to the west coast than most other locations (isn't there one about to open up in Los Angeles?), it may very well be the first time you lay eyes on a crack pie or cereal milk ice cream. I won't go into a lot of detail about Christina Tossi (mostly because you can watch an entire Netflix Chef's Table about her or read any other review here), but as the inventor and owner of Milk Bar, she is a sweet tooth genius. I guess it takes one to know one right (a sweet tooth that is... I am definitely not a sweet tooth genius). Although the menu may seem simple, there are a few things you'll want to try from the get go: crack pie (it's all about the buttery goodness, textures and sweetness) and cereal milk ice cream with cornflake crunch. You'd think it's simple and you'll ask why didn't someone think of it before, but it's so distinctively Milk Bar and Christina Tossi. I was surprised to find that they have a fruity cereal milk which I blended together. What a great combo! Try it out if you haven't before. The next stage is to give into their cookies. Oh so many. All oh, so good. I get a tin of assorted to take home that I can then think about sharing with others but in reality eat them all by myself. I've ordered her cakes through Goldbely before which was a great birthday surprise. Love the unfrosted sides and really allows you to enjoy the cake instead of a mouth full of ice cream. Can't wait to go back but will have to find a location nearby. Perhaps I'll just move next door to a store. That may not be good for my waist!
Unique and absolutely delicious! The cornflake ice cream has a perfect balance of sweet with a hint of saltiness that I LOVED!

I was expecting much more from this place. I've heard so much about it and from all the posts I've seen from Milk Bar in NYC, I knew I had to give this place a try. I got to sample the flavors - crack pie and cereal milk. They were both decent in flavor. I ended up with cereal milk and the worker convinced me to get corn flakes on top ($1 extra) by saying that it was really good with the corn flakes. Honestly, unpopular opinion but... it wasn't good. They were WAY too salty and didn't really add much to the soft serve. Also, the soft serve was too soft - bordering on watery. My friends got the cookies - they tasted burnt to me - and the crack pie - really good, but really expensive. Overall, this place was not for me. Super basic and overpriced soft serve, I would most definitely choose McDonald's soft serve over this place.
Because this location did not have any soft serve or shakes available....and it's 108 degrees outside.

I mean, it's a Christina Tosi storefront! In the Cosmopolitan in LV for goodness sake. I love her and her appearances on Master Chef have always made me happy...but come on Christina. This is not the best effort. Cookies are available for $4 each. I was thrilled to receive a large tin of cookies from Milk Bar for Christmas this year from a co-worker so was excited to go to an actual storefront location. The birthday cake shake was absolutely brilliant and I couldn't force it down my gullet fast enough. Get it! The cookies were disappointing. The blueberry creme cookie tasted artificial and had a sort of chemical aftertaste. The compost cookie at this location was far drier than the same that I received in the tin for Christmas. The corn cookie was quite good though. Overall, Meh... the milkshake was far and away the best thing. The rest isn't worth the impending diabetes.

I was super excited to finally be able to try Milk Bar when I was in Vegas. I got the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch and the fruity cereal milk soft serve. My first thought when I got a taste was that it was way too sweet. I actually struggled to finish it and I have a major sweet tooth. The cereal milk tasted just like milk and the fruit cereal milk reminded me of Fruity Pebbles. Even though it costs extra, I recommend getting the cornflake crunch. The saltiness of the cornflake crunch is a good contrast against the sweet soft serve. Even though the soft serve looks small in pictures, you can easily share one with another person and it'll be enough. This is a pricey place for soft serve and my expectations fell short.

A "Have to" visit location every time we visit the Vegas Strip. It is easily located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan! Just curious though about one thing: When did they change the name of the famous "Crack Pie" to "Milk Bar Pie?"

Maybe I'll have to give it another go. Was so excited to finally try this place after all the talk and the hype and such. Maybe because it was later in the night we went, maybe it was an off night but the whole experience left me confused. What was all the hype about? The cookies come prepackaged which left me thinking.. soooooo they're not made fresh? Should've taken that as a warning. Took a bite and all I can taste was sugar. You could've given me a store bought cookie, put it in the same wrap and I would've never tasted the difference. The truffles were okay, have you tasted Godiva's birthday cake truffles? you should. it's better.

Cookies were NOT good! Was so looking forward to trying this place that litters my Instagram adds and was so disappoint. Maybe the cake is better but we tried every cookie flavor they had and they all tasted bad.

Nothing was bad. It just wasn't great for whose name is behind this. My expectations were set much higher. I had just finished dining next door at Momofuku (5*) and was very excited that they had a dessert bar. I had the birthday cake truffles and a crack pie. Personally, they were good. I just anticipated a much more of a WOW factor instead of "oh that's ok." The crack pie tasted like a dish my aunt makes (much better); an old southern classic called ooey gooey cake. I thought for the price $$$ that it was going to blow my socks off. I wasn't dissapointed, but definitely no real reason to go back a second time. Service was excellent, very professional, friendly, & knowledgeable about the product!

I have been wanting to try Milk Bar for so long because I heard great things about it. Finally got the chance to try it and I am sadly not in love with it as I want to be. First the service was not the best and the person ringing us up seemed annoyed. I got the birthday cake soft serve and I thought it was okay. Flavor of birthday cake was there but it was overly sweet for me. Also without toppings it was already $6.50. I get that we are on the strip so prices tend be higher. My husband got the chocolate cake milkshake that had cake chunks in it. He enjoyed it. I plan to give this place another chance for a better experience and try something different. It's definitely worth a try if you're in the area.

Delicious ice cream, perfect for those hot summer days. Unfortunately, a single scoop is kind of pricey so it's definitely a "treat yourself" kind of dessert. The cereal milk ice cream will taste exactly like that leftover milk you had in your cereal bowl. A nice milky taste, not overly sweet. Get the cornflake crunch as a topping too. That was my favorite part of every bite! Don't be afraid to ask for samples too! I tried the Compost soft serve and found it too sweet for my liking. Cereal milk is perfect if you can't enjoy sweet things.

If I was basing my review on Milk's notorious cake I'd give them a four or five. Overall, the goodies I tried were pretty good, but not showstoppers. Older reviews noted that the Milk cake could not be purchased by the slice, but on my recent visit it was available for purchase by the slice. A win! The cake was really good and for me nearly lived up to the hype. The cake was moist and delicious. The frosting was also delicious and there was just the right amount. The slice was large and enough for two or three to share. The chocolate malt truffles were rich and decadent with a fudge consistency inside. These were also great. Milk offers three truffle flavors and they are sold as three packs. I'd love to see them offer a variety pack with one of each flavor. Since I can only eat so many sweets in one sitting I also purchased three cookies to enjoy at home. The Compost Cookie was pretty good and not an overly sweet cookie. The Confetti Cookie was my favorite of the three with delicious crunchy sprinkles. The Corn Cookie tasted exactly as listed. It was an interesting cookie and I couldn't decide if I liked it or not. The corn offered a slight sweetness, but kept it from being too sweet. I had to think about how I felt about Milk after my visit and one thing stuck out to me that kept this from being a high rating. Many of the items offered are pre-packaged. I can't get past the fact that they are selling most of their items already packaged and not fresh from the oven. Especially bakery items at top price points. The cake and truffles were worth it, but I'd pass on the cookies next time.

Not as good as other people raved about. The wreak milk ice cream tasted like something from Dairy Queen with salty Kristi rice nuggets in it. I also ordered the crack pie which is a tiny little piece of thin pie with a chewy texture. Again kind of generic in flavor. Vanilla-ish. Not sure I'd come back again.

Went to this location last month and to be completely honest I was not a huge fan. I've eaten at the Milk Bar in LA multiple times but unfortunately the birthday cake here tasted too dry, not fresh and overly sweet. Hoping they make some changes to their recipes in the future.

Staff was super friendly and answered all our questions/gave us samples of the soft serve. But I was a little disappointed with the cookies I bought... CORN COOKIE - was super excited to try this because I love corn. but sorely disappointed, not the texture or taste I was expecting. it just tasted like a cornbread cookie. my friend's mom loved it though, so I guess just depending on your preference. COMPOST COOKIE - I'm not a huge fan of crunchy cookies and this one was also overly sweet. Soft serve was really good with the cereal, but a little pricey for what it is.

I've been to the one in Los Angeles I wanted to give this one a try. I got the cookie that had marshmallow, chocolate, and cereal pieces. It was chewy and very tasty. It was a five dollar cookie which is very expensive to me.

It has been a dream of mine for years to have my birthday cake from Milk Bar! I am so happy I finally got mine from here! The texture of the cake was so fluffy and the flavor was out of this world. My guy graciously made the trek inside The Cosmo to get my dream cake. All of the party guests said it was the best cake they've ever had. We got the smaller version of the birthday cake and it was enough for 14 people! I do wish we had leftovers though because it truly was decadent. I also recommend trying their cereal milk. Makes you feel like a kid agai

Its really disappointing how bad they have gotten. They changed their menu items and cant answer questions about them - and they got my order wrong. I hate being in las vegas, and i just wanted some comfort food that i like - and they just butchered it. Super bummed out. Edit - i got to my room and i'm looking at the pie slice and it's not what I had asked for - which is tough to do when the menu items change and the people behind the counter just say "yes" to whatever you ask. Also - I just didn't have time to wait for you to remake make my iced coffee - you gave me a hot coffee when i ordered iced - because i was running late for a meeting. I ordered 2 items and you got them both wrong - I walked 6 miles there and back - have I earned the right to ask for a refund? I feel like i have. Could I please have my money back? You can have the cookie thing back - it's not what I wanted.

Vegas...a place where a lot of people get addicted to certain vices. Sure we've all heard of folks addicted to gambling but how about being addicted to crack pie?!? Crack pie is the famed pie of Milk Bar and it's so good, that folks get addicted. Awhile back crack pie was only available in NYC but Milk Bar started slowly opening up in various cities and the latest spot is in Sin City! Located at the Cosmopolitan is the home of the addicting pie. It's also the place to get compost cookies, cornflake-chocolate-chip-marshmallow cookies, corn cookies, blueberry and cream cookies and chocolate cookies. Ooh how can I forget, that this place also offers soft serve, truffles and shakes (oh hey this is Vegas so they do have fancy shakes with alcohol in it)! Who cares about gambling, when you can be addicted to something that will please your tastebuds! Your tastebuds are sure to be pleased with the sweet treats of Milk Bar. I got a nice selection of treats here; cookies, truffles, soft serve and of course their crack pie. Each of the cookie I tried was delicious. Their cookies are so soft! Equal in softness and goodness is their truffles. From the soft serve, my favorite is their crack pie soft serve....hmm back to that crack pie again (maybe I'm addicted ;). Last but not least is their crack pie. I've had it before in DC and it still remains to be one of my favorite pies ever. It really is just that good and a bit addicting. It's nice to see Milk Bar finally in Vegas. It gives a little more sweetness to Sin City and alright maybe another vice fir folks...a sweet one ;).

LOVE it. DIG it. Cant get enough of it... I have so many things I like that Milk Bar makes, it's insane. I have been wanting to try Milk Bar's creations ever since I read about that famous cereal milk soft serve. It really conjured up the image of the perfect taste rooted in childhood. We all know the milk at the bottom of the cereal bowl is one of the best things in life. HA! Milk Bar is great and is open really late. I tend to stay at or near the Cosmopolitan so the walk over for some sweets is never too bad. Even if I stayed in another part of The Strip I would make my way there. I have something from Milk Bar every day of my stay. Oh yes... I do. Crack pie - DAMN YOU. You are so good and indeed made of crack. It's so good and so sweet and everything great in life. Yes. I am now a crack pie fiend. It's very sweet. Perfect to share. Cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes - YUM. Very good but not as sweet as I imagined. I guess my cereal bowls are sugar runneth over. Still tasty and yes, try it and share. Crack pie soft serve with cornflakes - SO GOOD. I actually liked this better than the cereal milk. It's sweeter. It's made from crack and crack is killin it. Get it. Thank me immediately after. You're welcome. Compost cookie - In the running for best cookie ever. So many different flavors and textures that combine to form Voltron. So delicious. It has chocolate chips, butterscotch chips, brown rice syrup, graham crackers, potato chips, flaxseed, salt, coffee, vanilla, etc... The ingredients are a long paragraph resembling a dissertation. Read it. Cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookies - Very good. It is a very sweet cookie. This one is not playing around. It is best shared. Corn cookie - I like it. It has great flavor and sweetness. And yes it tastes like the sweetest corn made by the Children of the Corn. Blueberry & cream cookie - What a tasty combination. I really like this cookie. My daily dose of fruit in Las Vegas. It's so good. It's perfect balance of flavors. Chocolate chocolate cookie - All the dark chocolate flavors possible on earth in one cookie. It's a little too bitter and dark chocolatey for me but you may dig it. B'day truffles - THIS is the real MVP. Dammit these 3-pack of birthday cake batter goodness in truffle form should be illegal. And yes, we took some home on the plane. Refrigeration needed. SO GOOD. Momofuku Milk Bar. Believe the hype. It did for me. Cant wait to have it again on our next trip to LV. And yes, I will have it every day. Customer service was great especially the young man from Manchester, England. It was great talking to him. Our friends & I all thought he was great... TIP THEM!

MILK is good BUT sometimes its hard to justify the prices of the items. Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow Cookie: 4/5. My favorite cookie they offer. Too bad only the name is a mouth full. Their cookies are too small for the price IMO. But this one is yummy with a good balance of salty (cornflake) and sweet (everything else). Compost cookie: 2/5. Im not a fan of pretzels or potato chips in my cookies so its a hard pass for me. But it also has a "hodgepodge" of other ingredients such as chocolate chips, toffee chips, graham crackers and rolled oats. I usually purchase 6/$22 - which equals out to about $3.70 per cookie. Birthday Cake truffles: 3/5. Super duper sweet and prices at about ~$7 for a pack of three or four, cant remember. Crack pie: 3/5. Also super sweet and priced at about $7 for a slice.

After a loung concert, perhaps a night of penny slots and cigarettes, or even if you're just being bougie at the chandelier bar, you should stop at Milk Bar for a late night treat before you hit the road. The cereal milk ice cream is to die for. Not your average vanilla. Topped with fruity pebbles is probably the best thing in life right now. I'm actually lactose intolerant but totally willing to remain uncomfortable for life if I could just live off this ice cream. The crack pie, wtf why is it so good? And that cornflake cookie?! Don't get me started.

I am so sorry Christina Tosi, your dessert bar is just . . .not that great! Christina is one of my favorite celebrity chefs and I love seeing her on tv as well as watching her cooking, her style, pastries, etc just her being a chef! I really wanted to try her place and we came by after lunch for something light for dessert. I saw all the cookie flavors and wanted to try a few but then my eyes caught the spiked milkshakes! So, I opted for the cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie and the White-Russian-Cereal-Milk Shake. The cookie was nothing special . . .and actually, nothing making me want to order it again or try another type of cookie. It was chewy but not a good chewy, and it seems over baked as it was pretty tough. The cornflakes have a very subtle crispness and saltiness, the marshmallow just seems to add sweetness, and the chocolate chips are almost nonexistent. It was just not a great cookie and I expected so much more. As for the milkshake, this was pretty good. The cereal milk flavor is interesting, unique, and pretty tasty! Spiked with the alcohol it becomes a great blend of sweet and . . . umami? Is that the best way to describe a boozy milkshake? I don't know, but it was good! I won't mind trying Milk Bar again, but definitely not the cookies next time.

Love their cookies!! So glad they opened in Vegas so I don't have to fly to NYC to get my fix. Great to eat and great as gifts for friends once I get home. Note: the cookies get pretty hard after the package is opened so eat it all in one sitting, mkay?!!

Space: This dessert spot is grab and go, there is a line and you order what you want and eat It in the nearby lobby by there is not an open seating. Service: The staff here is super friendly and allow you to taste test items. They always have a bright smile on their faces and answer all your questions. Price: The items are here very pricy. Cookies: $3 Crack Pie: $6.50 Bday Cake Truffle: $6.75 Milkshakes: $9-$10 Food: The items are pretty sweet, they have soft serve, pies, cookies, milkshakes and other sweets. The portions aren't huge but because of how sweet everything is, It is hard to finish. I personally LOVE the birthday cake truffle, It has confetti cake in the center but the outside is a crumble that melts in your mouth. The crack pie is pretty good as well but again, It is sweet and It is hard to finish on your own. Notes: I have never encountered a line here but the cookies can be frozen up to a month or you can let It sit for 5-7 days and they'll still be good!
Let's just say this- start buying larger clothes cuz this here is damn good. I got the truffle balls! Omg so yummy! I'll be back later for a box to go! Yum yum lick um up

The cereal milk ice cream truly tastes like cereal milk. Glad I came here to try out what the hype is all about. The ice cream isn't life changing, but it's worth a try. Apparently they changed the "crack pie" name to "milk bar pie." People need to stop getting offended over everything.

I've heard a lot about Milk Bar, which is a thought of David Chang of Momofuku fame. The interpretation is of the last milk from your favorite cereal in an ice cream format. We tried a sample, but had no room after a big dinner. I did buy an egg and cheddar with bacon breakfast muffin and a bagel bomb in a croissant like finish. The next day, the breakfast sandwiches only required a slight microwaving to get it deliciously hot. The menu was overwhelming, and I've seen lines all the way to the escalator. I have to admit I'm a David Chang fan, so just had to try this place out!

I wasn't sure what to expect with all of the mixed reviews but the birthday cake was actually really good. The frosting was smooth and not overly sweet. The milk bar pie was good but is better if you let it get to room temperature. It is not anything to get excited over though, basic cream and sugar flavor. My friend got a blueberry cream cookie and it was good. There is a cute seating area right near the entrance also.

We came for what everyone was talking about, the Crack Pie. Small slice for $6.50, it was simply too sweet. After taking a first bite, I was immediate hit w sugar. It makes enjoying the entire pie, which is damn small, very hard. Would not get it again. Also got a blueberry & cream cookie. Not as sweet but quite good. And the Compost Cookie, which is essentially everything. I tasted hints of coffee and salt. It was a nice balance of flavors and textures. Would get this again. Each for $3. Prices here are high, probably because rent is high and that's what they need to charge to stay in business. In my opinion, it's not worth it. But hey, it's Vegas and chances are, you're on vacation. So splurge a little and try it out.

not the BEST cookies I've had, but for a packaged cookie. YES. really really good and the employee that helped us out was so nice! ( sorry i didn't catch the name), but it was more towards closing time. I know they are famous for the compost cookie, which I wasn't a fan of. it had a very weird acquired taste and I can see why people would like it, but not my type of cookie. I think my favorite had to be the blueberries & cream and confetti. the chocolate on chocolate was good, hint of salt, but too much 'cocoa' for my liking. the marshmallow one was pretty good too! but, it would have to come in 3rd. overall, they were pretty decently fresh tasting for a packaged cookie and to satisfy a craving, or a few. I'm not the one to judge. I also wanted to try the soft serve, the employee gave me a legit sample. wasn't just a small serving, it was pretttty much a large heaping sample. he said 'oops sorry, accidentally overdid it'. hahaha. i'm not complaining. i love samples that aren't on the stingy side. thank you :)

My five stars are specifically for the crack pie...which I enjoyed everyday for breakfast... 3 days in a row! So awesome with a hot cup of coffee. It's gooey and buttery and reminds me of a cross between a pecan pie without nuts and a chess pie. I also fell in love with the birthday cake truffles. My kids loved the softserve quakes but I could not get past the sickening cereal milk taste. Make sure to get a sample of the soft serve before you commit. We also tried the birthday cake one day which I found to be dry and nowhere near as good as the birthday cake truffles. Located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan. Near the restaurants, and right after you enter from the sky bridge.

This place has pretty good cookies! They are $4 each but you can get a slight discount if you buy more than 6. I've tried the birthday cake confetti one and it's very soft despite being in a package all day (I thought it would be hard but it wasn't. It's quite a large cookie too. I liked the cornflake chocolate chip and marshmallow one too. There's a slight crunch that makes it taste good. Their cake slices look good too although it's $14 for a slice which seems absurd!

The most unique ice cream I've ever tasted. It's ADDICTING! I always order the soft serve with the cookie crunches they add. Their milk bar is delicious, pretty much everything is amazing. It is a bit expensive but worth it!

as i type this review, basically across the country ,from my first milk bar experience, I'm dreaming of being able to eat their cereal milk soft serve right now. and having a slice of their life changing ( yea i said it) birthday cake. so many choices, so many fomo opportunities on that board, I seriously wanted one of each. and i'm usually a salty/savory kinda girl but this joint could put me on the diabetic train with their ridiculously good delectable treats. inside the cosmo, second floor next to momofuku and eggslut, by the chandalier bar, youre able to see all the thots taking their bumble/tinder/ig/hinge pics. you gotta at least come and get a piece of the cake, bday or not, a bit pricey for a slice but no fomo, get it !

Simply had the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes and it was so interesting! A bit expensive for over $7 for quite a small cup, but 1) we're in Vegas where EVERYTHING is expensive, and 2) I don't need a gallon of ice cream to satisfy my sweet tooth anyway. But bravo on the flavor--quite literally the closest thing to the bottom of a cereal bowl besides the ACTUAL bottom of a cereal bowl! I like the added corn flakes at the bottom to really bring the theme home! The soft serve tasted buttery too--in a very good way!

Everything sounded so good and delicious, but after paying close to $13.xx for ONE cookie and ONE milkshake...it was SO not worth it!!! I ordered a chocolate cereal milk milkshake for my kids and a cookie (I forgot which one I got). The $8.50 milkshake tasted like a typical chocolate milkshake! Nothing special at all!! I could've went to In-n-out and got a cheaper one that tasted the same. And the cookie was no better than the frozen dough you can bake yourself at home! I will definitely not recommend wasting your time and money here.

I've eaten a lot of desserts in my day, and Milk Bar was nothing special. For all the hype they receive, it did not have me craving anything more after a couple bites of several of their cookie flavors. The demand seems high, as the lines were long and this inflates the prices as well. They've done a good job with branding and marketing, but the flavors fall short of expectation. Best, Charlie

I was disappointed with Milk Bar and just thought that this place is very hyped. The milkbar pie is super small and it din't taste all that great. It was pricey at $7 and the taste was not to our liking. We were planning to come back for ice cream after the dinner but hubby was not too keen on it after having the pie. Oh,well! Will try something new the next time but thumbs down to the milk bar pie from my end!

I've always wanted to try their birthday cake, so when I saw they had a birthday cake shake, I saw my opportunity to try it without spending $50+ on a small cake. $10 on a 12 oz shake that I think they used pre-packaged birthday cake truffles (do they even make the truffles fresh in house?!). It was okay. I got a flour-y taste, which was kind of weird/unexpected. For $10? Can't say this was totally worth it...
Not tasty at all and very overpriced. I really wanted to like this place but unfortunately it did not hit the spot.:(

I CAN GET CORN COOKIES ON THIS SIDE OF THE COUNTRY NOW!! Milk Bar, the famed bakery by the makers of Momofuku used to only be on the eastern side of the continent (NYC, DC, and Toronto) but now they have a location in Vegas. And inside the Cosmo, which is the perfect casino/hotel for it - a trendy match! Much like the one in the East Village, it's essentially a booth and offers the same stuff, cereal milk soft serve, crack pie, and COOKIES! After a weekend of overeating and overindulging, I sadly did not have room for soft serve (even though it was hot enough to have some). I ended up buying my favorite cookies to go - CORN COOKIE and the compost cookie. They have baskets full of them on the counter. Next time, I will come here first and get soft serve. And maybe some pie. And more cookies.

I came here recently on a trip to Vegas and stopped by to check out the hype. I picked up a tin of 6 cookies as gifts ($17... $18 and change after tax) and also tried the fruity cereal milk soft serve topped with crushed corn flakes. The cereal milk soft serve tastes exactly like how you would expect it to. It was almost salty and not sweet at all. The salty taste probably came from the crushed corn flakes. Not a bad dessert, but definitely on the heavier side. I could go without this in the future. As for the cookies- tried 3: 1. Compost cookie- this cookie is a bit hard texturally and has a lot of interesting elements to it. Overall, tasted a lot like a toffee cookie to me with bits of pretzel. I give it 2-1/2 out of 5 stars. 2. Chocolate chip marshmallow cookie- 4/5- softer cookie and you definitely taste the corn flakes. I liked this one more than the compost. 3. Corn cookie- my fave and I can see why it's a cult classic. Would love to replicate this at home! 5/5! Tried a nibble of the crack pie and thought it was good but way too buttery and heavy!

Indulgent and not cheap, but it's Vegas, so what do you expect? The cereal milk soft serve with corn flake topping was my favorite. So simple and such a distinctive flavor. And just when I thought I got played for adding on the corn flake topping, I realized that they sprinkled some at the bottom, like buried treasure. The crack pie was good too, but I will come back for that cereal milk soft serve.

But sure, let's just say 3.5 stars because it's a fun concept! Our girl gang enjoyed a concert at Planet Hollywood and walked to the Cosmo on a mission to find the cereal soft serve and crack pie. The line was insane, even at 10pm. We ordered exactly what we wanted plus one compost cookie to share. For the cereal soft serve, I've never been and still am not a huge fan of corn flakes; but I get the contrast and whatnot. I do think nostalgia is worth the hype and the pricing is probably more about aesthetics. Who doesn't love the good 'ol simple times? Overall, everything tasted like a straight up spoonful of sugar in every bite. I couldn't finish any single order by myself, my sweetness tolerance is definitely dwindling with age.

Their Crack Pie Milkquake is the best thing I have eaten in a long time, so five stars just for that! I've had their soft serve and crack pie separately - to me they taste better together than separately. (That's pretty much what their Crack Pie Milkquake is btw, soft serve with chunks of crack pie.) It's very, very sweet, toothachingly sweet, but I'll deal with it because my tastebuds find it so, so delicious! One serving can easily be split between two people, if you're willing to share :p You get to eat it with a wooden spoon too - how fun is that?! Brings me back to my childhood :) I've tasted a few other Milk Bar treats as well, like their cookies and Bday Cake Truffles. I can pass on their cookies, but their Bday Cake Truffles were also just some sweet, sweet goodness! FYI there was no line the times I went in the afternoon. As for seating, there is a bench in front, but you can find more comfortable seating if you go up the escalators to the floor with all the restaurants. But back to the treats :p I can't wait to have a Crack Pie Milkquake (Milkquake = Las Vegas exclusive) and some Bday Cake Truffles again!
Overall the milk cereal soft serve was tasty. Not too sweet and very creamy. Only downside is there no other options for flavor and the cookies taste pretty mediocre.

Located right by the escalator on the second (?) floor and next to the Momofuku restaurant is Milk Bar! I haven't been able to make my way to NY to try these treats so I wanted to try them while I was in Vegas. I got the Greatest Hits Combo ($19) and three cookies ($8). The Greatest Hits came with a cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes, a slice of crack pie, a compost cookie and a 3-pack of birthday cake truffles. I also got another compost cookie, cornflake chocolate chip cookie, and a blueberry & cream cookie. The soft serve was tiny but soooo good! You can actually taste the cereal flavor in the soft serve, like the milk when you finish all your Frosted Flakes. The cornflakes on the side of the soft serve were lightly salted and served as a good crunch and contrast to the soft serve. The crack pie was this ooey-gooey buttery pie that was sweet and delicious. The compost cookie and cornflake chocolate chip cookie to me were just okay, but the blueberry & cream cookie was amazing - it tasted just like the top of a blueberry muffin! The best thing I got however were the birthday cake truffles! They tasted just like funfetti and weren't dry at all despite their appearance.

I think I got rather "Milked" at the Milk Bar. A bit of play on words but c'mon. Let me put this on the table or rather no table sice Milk Bar is standing room only, but I am not fearful to pay top dollar for the food or drink experience. So when I slid my Credit card through the reader for a $12 Crack Pie Milk Quake, I was expecting a bit more than a plastic cup with a wooden spoon and a milk quake that was not even filled to the top of such said plastic cup. The group stood around in front taking pics and looking at what was placed upon us. We waited and waited because the order of one of our Sin City Foodie group members got forgotten. We located seats within the Chandeliers, ate and discussed... Oh and waited for our friend with his forgotten order. I would give this a Two Star but I gave it that extra shiny star because the Crack Pie was really good. Just the Crack Pie. The ice cream in my milk quake was average at best and the presentation was not the least bit sexy. Honestly, I would rather pay a few more dollars for an enormous sexy sundae at another on The Strip location, which will remain nameless. Although most Sin City Foodies will know where it is. Okay starts with an "S" and ends with a "3". I'm all about the full food experience from beginning to end using all the senses I have. If I compare with other on The Strip ice cream experiences, this falls short... To me.

The staff here is very friendly and patient. They will give you samples (even after you've made your purchase and you're just curious), and they will take their time giving recommendations. I saw some customers order the Chocolate Pretzel and the girl at the counter even asked them if they wanted to try it before buying it because she said a lot of people find it too salty! Even though I think the desserts here are 3 stars, I'm bumping them up for the good service! SOFT SERVE $6|$12 * Chocolate pretzel - 3 stars This is pretty savory, just enough in a sample cup, but it would have been too much in a cup of soft serve for me. * Cereal milk - 3.5 stars This by itself is plain, just like milk. With the Cornflake crunch topping ($1.25) a nice contrast is added, and it's pretty savory! FANCY SHAKES * Fruity cereal milk w/ triple sec ($12) - 3.5 stars A good thick shake, a bit strong for me with the triple sec! PIE * Crack Pie - 4 stars Tasty but I couldn't finish this! This was crazy filling and really was all butter.

I think I would have liked this place a little more if I hadn't gone at such a weird time. It was later on in the evening and I didn't know what to expect, so I was a little underwhelmed by the storefront and the people at the bar who seemed to take quite a while to notice me. Most people were heading out for cocktails and what not and I was roaming the Cosmopolitan looking for a cookie. Shrugs. Anyway, I got the cookie with the cornflakes and the marshmallow. It was pretty good! I would even say excellent. I should have gone back under different conditions.

This place is overrated. I tried some of almost everything. Most of it was soo sweet, and I know I'm a sucker for sweet things. How to find this place: go to the Cosmopolitan on the strip, go upstairs next to Eggslut. Here are the more popular ones: Milk & cereal soft serve: the soft serve tastes like milk, and I hate milk. Adding the corn flakes made it better, but I still couldn't enjoy it thoroughly. The corn flakes are a tad salty, so I liked that part. Chocolate soft serve: eh, actually the milk one was better. Birthday cake truffle: suuuper sweet stuff right here. I just can't. Peanut butter cookie: this one is really average. Compost cookie: the cookie is hard. I've had this numerous times. I'm not a fan of the oatmeal inside, but the potato chips are cool. Crack Pie: it's a sticky-ish dessert. On my last visit, I could feel my arteries getting clogged as I ate this. 3-stars because free samples.

I am not much of a fan for glorified ice cream, but this place is pretty decent. Their cookies are pretty good. They have a lot of flavors and cater to different tastes. My favorites are the chocolate ones. I think they have one called triple chocolate, and for chocolate lovers out there, this is definitely one to try. The ice cream is really good too. I tried the milk cream with cornflake crunch and I was blown away. Before trying the ice cream, I thought it was just vanilla covered in the Corn Flakes cereal. I was sure wrong. The ice cream was very delicious and not too creamy. The flakes are what make the ice cream, and they give you a healthy amount. Each bite you take is filled with bunches of flakes and they even give you a good serving on the bottom of the cup, so you aren't stuck with just the toppings on top. The flakes are very savory and each bite is filled with bits of joy. I would definitely come back here again for a nice cup of ice cream.

Delicious cereal milk soft serve; single cup for just 6 bucks. It was not overly sweet and had an underlying malt milk flavor in the ice cream. I don't know....i could be wrong about the malt milk flavor but that's what my taste buds told me and my husband had agreed to it, too! Anyways, I loved the cereal milk soft serve and so did my 2-year-old picky eater!

I wanted to love it so bad but I left disappointed. The shopfront is cute and everything looks and sounds soooo delicious!! We decided to try 3 cookies and a slice of the birthday cake. (3 cookies for $11 and $14 Bday slice) I was excited to try the cake... who doesn't love confetti birthday cake?!?! Unfortunately the cake was dry, crumbly and the frosting was not what I expected. It had a different taste/texture than most frosting and was not very sweet. We got 3 cookies: compost, confetti and cornflake/chocolate chip per the employee recommendation. Surprisingly the cornflake/choc chip/marshmallow was the best. However I still have a hard time recommending this place considering the price. I can think of several cookie/cake options that are way better for less $$. Maybe the ice cream is better...

tl;dr: reduce your expectation before you buy. ------ After dreaming about this place for years from all the food shows I've seen, the whole experience was a slight disappointment. We got the infamous cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes topping and the crack pie. The portions were small and total came out to be $15. #steep but I guess that's the Vegas price baby. The soft serve honestly just tasted like a regular soft serve and actually more on the bland side. It wasn't creamy or flavorful as I imagined. The cornflake didn't add much to the texture either. The pie was supper buttery and delicious but it was nothing special. Between my friend and I, we only got 2 bites worth each... All n all, I'd check this place out for the hype but definitely lower your expectation before you go in.
I got the soft serve, it was delicious but it wasn't the best thing I've ever had. It was sweet and salty which I did enjoy!!

You know, I feel this isn't their fault. When it comes to food, there is nothing more overrated than New York. San Francisco tries to be as overrated and it's getting close, but every time I hear about amazing stuff from some small, shop with huge prices, I'm skeptical. Here's the thing -- there is some REALLY delicious stuff in this world, but sometimes I just don't get what people are freaking out about. Take Milk Bar and their famed birthday cake. I brought my 6 and 8 year old daughters into town for Valentine's Day and to spend their mid-winter break and part of all that was sampling the food. Dessert on our first day was the birthday cake at Milk Bar and well....I admit, it tastes exactly like birthday cake. But it's also $14 for a slice, which does not offend me. What offends me is that given what people say about this thing, I was expecting to have the greatest slice of birthday cake ever -- and it just wasn't. I mean, yes, it tasted like cheap birthday cake (Christina Tosi proudly uses McCormick imitation vanilla extract to get that cheap birthday cake flavor!), but it wasn't even the best slice of cheap birthday cake I've ever had. Plus, when you refrigerate a cake like that, you cause it to forcibly stale and the cake gets hard. When Tosi talked about the cake, she discussed how it's drenched in milk so that it stays moist forever. This just wasn't moist and it could never be moist when it's served in that fashion. And again, it's not the price that bothers me. It's that I just don't think it was worth the calories, the effort, or the mental buildup that accompanied it. There is some really great stuff to eat in Las Vegas (or New York for that matter). If you're going to risk getting diabetes, do it eating something else.
