We needed something sweet so we decided to give Milk Bar a try. We tried the cereal ice cream and the crunchy bits on top made it. They added a nice salty sweet touch. I wasn't the biggest fan of the cake balls but that might just be me. The cookie with toffee and chocolate chips blew me away and I found myself continuously eating it and forgot to share with my husband. Oops!!

Milk Bar has been hyped up on tv and social media so of course I was excited to try it while visiting Vegas. Well, it was underwhelming to say the least. I ordered the single cereal milk soft serve with cornflake topping. It tasted like straight up milk with no cereal taste at all. The cornflake topping helped the taste, but without it the soft serve was very bland. My bf got the single crack pie soft serve with cornflake topping and it was a million times better than the cereal milk. It was so buttery and sweet. This place needs to do more advertising for their crack pie soft serve and less of the cereal milk.
Giving 3 stars . Cake was kinda dry . But the ice cream was rich and delicious. Hours are convenient!

We ordered the greatest hits which was perfect it came with a compost cookie, 3 pack birthday truffles, a crack pie slice and the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch! We also ordered a chocolate birthday truffle shake not pictured because we drank that so quick because it was SO good!! Along with being really good omg the soft serve defiantly tasted like cereal milk lol. And is it bad to say that we're addicted to the crack pie

Who pays $4 for an above average cookie? THIS GIRL. The compost cookie was highly recommended. They warmed it up so it was soft and gooey on the inside while maintaining a crispy outer edge. Overall, it was delicious but just OK. The price made it kind of not worth it. If I was to return, I'd probably try the all time best set so you can try a bit of everything. Also, they open late so if you have any sweet tooth cravings skip the bars and check out the Milk Bar.

If you don't mind paying $15 for a small-ish sized shake, then this place may be for you and your sweet tooth. The birthday cake shake was outstanding! Chunkiest cake shake I've ever had and much more smooth and creamy than expected. I'd have to say that given the size and price of the ever-shrinking Holstein's milkshakes next-door, this shake has a leg up.

I'll admit I goofed, there are not enough pictures below to display the beauty of all the things I've tried at Milk Bar (in Vegas and NYC). Honestly I just got too excited to eat and missed the photo-op. Here's to hoping I can describe it better! Cookies: Unpopular opinion, I think the cookies are underwhelming. I've tried the compost, the corn flake chocolate chip marshmallow, and the blueberry and cream. None of them were memorable. Honestly recommend skipping all cookies and saving as much room for cakes and pies as possible. Pie: What is crack pie? I don't even know, it's got a crispy oat crust and a not overly sweet but perfectly balanced buttery filling. It's ooey and gooey, I don't know how it's made, I'm not sure what's in it other then butter, but I ate it and I loved it, I urge you to do the same. Cake balls: I always thought cake balls were a little basic, I've tried them a few times and was never wowed. I WAS WOWED here y'all. The chocolate malt cake ball tastes like a soft, very rich and indulgent creamy fudge brownie. I don't know how they got it so perfect. It's a revelation. Cakes: Dear lord sweet baby Jesus, these cakes are BOMB. I've tried the bday cake and the pumpkin pie cake. The bday one I actually made in a Milk Bar class in NYC, so I got to see how they assemble them. The level of detail they put in to making each layer perfect is incredible. Cake, soak, icing, crunchy element. They hit every note. Definitely recommend the seasonal pumpkin cake while it lasts, the pumpkin ganache layer mixed with the graham cracker cheesecake layer- I died. I don't care where you live, order a cake for your birthday. Just do it.

Honestly the first time I tried milk bar in DC, it was awful. The cereal ice cream is so bland and underwhelming...I'm still not sure what the hype is about for this place I decided to give milk bar another try when I saw it at the cosmopolitan in Vegas. This time I went for the birthday quake. A quake is apparently like a blizzard? It was better than the cereal soft serve but still had the same salty and bitter taste...it's just not what I would imagine for ice cream. Doesn't satisfy the craving. The birthday truffles on the other hand are actually pretty delicious!! They're overpriced for what they are but probably the best dessert choice at milk bar.

A good (albeit slightly overpriced) place for dessert. After hearing the hype about this place, I decided to come and get a Milk Bar Pie babyshake ($7). What I enjoyed was that every sip of the milkshake was packed with flavor...it tasted rich and creamy, with a little bit of salt to round out the sweetness. (I have not tried the namesake pie, but it did have that feel that it tasted like a delicious pie in milkshake form.) However, for the price, I did wish it would have been a little larger. I would like to revisit this place to try some of their other items.

Holy Tosi-do, Milk Bar! This was my first time visiting Milk Bar since I bought Christina's recent book, All About Cake. I was planning a visit for a while but in the mean time I ended up in Vegas with my best friends and had the chance to come to this location. CEREAL MILK ICE CREAM: This definitely exceeded all of my expectations and I never thought it would be the taste that I got. I was a bit skeptical but I knew I was going to love it. My husband wasn't too excited to try it, but once he had it, he was hooked. We ended up sharing and I can't wait until I can go to another Milk bar for more! BIRTHDAY CAKE TRUFFLES: You know. I've had this concept before. I've eaten cake balls. I've eaten cake pops. I've eaten any form that's similar to Milk Bar's cake truffles, and yet, I enjoyed this the most. You would think because they're packaged, they would've sacrificed or lost some quality. But you would not have that experience with these at ALL! The truffles were SO rich, and I ended up sharing those with the group I was with. The price made me a bit wary but now I'm enlightened. Would probably still pick the soft serve over these. Overall, would come back for soft serve and maybe trying the cake and crack pie slices! Thanks for the experience, Milk Bar Vegas!

Why should you visit? 1) first and only west coast location 2) besides Toronto (which I regret not visiting while there) they have the fruity pebble flavor soft serve So I've been here twice: once last year and once this year for many visit to Las Vegas. I've had the all the cookies, crack pie, and obviously the cereal milk ice cream (which you'd think is vanilla but with the corn flakes it literally tastes like cereal and milk). If you've never been, there's an option that's around $22 something that lets you try all of their "well known" products. I personally recommend the crack pie and I come here just to buy the corn powder since shipping is terribly expensive and when you're just far away it's hard to find a place to grind your own dehydrated corn, let alone purchase it. Of course momofuku las vegas is right next door so I suggest visiting both. What to expect? Yes, its expensive, but honestly compared to the line in NYC, everyone who's visiting this location should count their freaking blessings how chill this store is. Would you rather wait in the NYC cold, or a casino building warm. I think it's well worth it just because you just won't get desserts that taste like this due to the corn base of everything. Also, hello? You're in a casino on the strip, ya ain't finding cheap eats yo. Also parking is downright terrible now on the strip since they effing charge for everything now :( Gone are the good ol' days. If you can uber, car pool or are willing to pay for parking then do it. I'd rather just walk depending on where you are or uber.

I don't know why anyone would give place anything less than five stars!! The soft serve is so delicious!! Pair it with the crunchy cornflake topping and you've got a delicious dessert treat to share after dinner! It's always too much for me so I like to share it! Definitely on the pricier side ($7 for a single serving of soft serve with one topping) but would you expect anything less from a Vegas dessert spot??

Yes, I'm a fan of Milk Bar! I didn't know too much about the desserts here when Milk Bar creator Christina Tosi opened up the first West coast location in the Cosmo. Then we got to meet her at a Yelp event prior to opening and try the birthday cake and truffles that are signature items as well as a few of the cookies. That's the first time I tried the birthday cake and from then, I've been a fan. Yes, the cake is on the pricey side, but it's great for a special occasion when you want to treat yourself. My friends and I ordered one for our July birthdays and shared it with a group of other pals because sharing is caring. The item that I've had multiple times is the cereal milk soft serve. My favorite flavor is the Fruity Cereal Milk soft serve because it really does taste like the milk at the bottom of a bowl of Fruity Pebbles. Apparently, this flavor is only available at the Vegas and Toronto locations so lucky us! The soft serve melts very quickly so have napkins ready. The cake truffles are tasty little nuggets of goodness and I've bought them as gifts for friends. I'm glad that we have this location here in town and look forward to another birthday occasion (mine or someone else's) for more cake. Yelp Review #800

I wish they could replace the blood in my body with that cereal milk ice cream. Bury me with that compost cookie. This place is so bomb! All the people there are super friendly and helpful. They have some pretty good deals on combos too if you want a little of everything too.

I just ate a bowl of cereal in the form of ice cream. I was very curious about Milk Bar especially because their ice creams look pretty good in pictures. I'm glad I tried it but probably won't eat it again especially with the $6 price tag!

When you have been waiting to try something for a long time and then you are let down. This is the feeling I got after finally making my way to the Cosmopolitan. Totally disappointed in 4 out of the 4 cookies I bought. They were just not good. I had the Blueberry and Cream, Compost, Chocolate Chocolate, and the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow. Every cookie was dry and tasted old. I'm not sure where these are baked and how long they sit in the baskets but it would seem to be a long time. If I were Christina Tosi, I would be embarrassed. She really can't criticize anyone's baking on MasterChef while serving these cookies. A waste of my money and calories.

Milk Bar was one of my favorite destinations when traveling in New York so I was ecstatic when I heard that they opened one up in the Cosmopolitan. It's a walk up dessert shop right next to the Momofuku restaurant. And yes, they are both owned by the same guy. They have a lot of different offerings from pie to cookies and even soft serve ice cream. I absolutely love their crack pie and compost cookies! They are a must try here and honestly my favorite things on their menu. I'm not toooooo big on sweets so a slice of pie and a cookie was good enough for me to share with my friend. For $17, you can bring home a tin of 6 cookies to share with your friends! And their Cereal Milk Ice Cream is delicious as well. It's kind of sweet and salty like salted caramel ice cream would be. Very creamy and served coated with corn flakes! If you're in the Cosmo and looking for something to satisfy your sweet tooth, give Milk Bar a try!

I was so looking forward to this place. After eating at Momofuku next door, my sweet tooth was calling me out. Sadly to say, Milk was more than disappointing for me. 3 stars for the Birthday cake truffles alone. They were soft, buttery, doughey and sweet. The cereal milk soft serve didn't do a thing for me and I love ice cream. Sadly, it tasted bland and wasn't sweet at all-- even with a generous heaping of corn flakes on top to give it texture. I sampled all of the soft serve flavors as well and nothing stood out. Sorry Milk, but all the hype is just that- hype.

3.5. I'm super torn because some was great and some was not. First off the Crack Pie is amazing. I mean amazing. I savored every bite. But after that things just kind of went downhill .... slightly all be it... but still down. The cereal milk with corn flakes was ok but I really wanted the fruity pebbles, and they don't do that anymore. It does honestly taste like cereal milk. My husband had the shake version and I had the sundae. His was better. The cookies were ok tasting but very hard. Maybe we got a bad batch? The truffles were not good in my opinion. I didn't get the slice of cake and I really wanted to so I may be back to try that out next time I'm in town.

If you want something different, come to the Milk Bar! You are literally eating cereal flavored ice cream. It is really different and quite delicious if you like milk and cereal! Crack pie is what we got and it was really, really yummy and totally wow'd us! I highly recommend!

I've been dying to go to Milk Bar for months considering I wasn't able to go when I was in New York a few months ago. Thankfully there was one that was close and walking distance on the Strip! It's located in the Cosmopolitan on the second floor, next to Momofuku and Allsaints. It's a very tiny stand where you can order things from cookies to soft serve ice cream. I got the cereal milk soft serve which is popular so I thought I'd give it a try. It tastes exactly like cereal milk, which was delicious.

I'm all over that crack pie. I've tried their cookies and while they are tasty, nothing beats the crack pie when I need a sugar rush in Vegas. It's one of those addicting flavors that I have to have when ever I visit. Oh, that's why it's called crack pie! I get it now. Anyway, if you go, get me some ok? Please? Pretty please?

Located right next to momofuku is the Milk Bar. The cookies are something of a must try for those cookie connoisseur. They are priced at $4 a piece or 6 for $22. The cornflake chocolate chip marshmellow cookie was superb! They also have some delicious soft serve - get the swirl of cereal milk with the crack pie. It does the trick for the hot weather.

I'm confused by a lot of the reviews on here, especially the three stars that say the desserts are delicious. I don't know. Milk Bar is pure five stars if you like desserts and if you don't like desserts, don't go here. We went to Milk Bar all three days in Vegas and each time it was excellent. I suggest trying all of the ice cream flavors and then getting a swirl of your two favorites. I'll always be a fan of their cookies, especially the cornflake marshmallow. Too good. I also got a piece of the Birthday Cake and daaaaang. The cream cheese frosting made it so the birthday flavoring wasn't too sweet. But if you want sweet, go with the Birthday Cake Shake. Or the truffles. The prices are high but these things aren't easy to make. How else do you get that perfect marshmallow pull in the cookies? Plus, it's Vegas so... Every employee was extremely nice and fine with me taking minutes to make a decision every day I visited.

After constant drooling over other people Instagram pics of milk soft serves, I FINALLY got the chances to try. It was pretty much my only goal this trip. So, MISSION ACCOMPLISH~!! Overall tho, was not fully satisfied, I love the texture of the soft serve, really felt like I was eating cereal with milk. But for some reason in my head, I was seriously expecting it to be so much MORE amazing. Failed. The person who helped me was very generous, gave me a BIG one, I couldn't even finish, there wasn't enough cereal to go with the milk! I def will go back and try something else next time. Price: $6 for the milk soft serve, $1 for the Cornflakes + tax Staff: very nice and friendly

The crack pie has been on my radar since this place opened. My sister was in town recently and was staying at Cosmo, so I met her there and we went to Milk Bar. It's located on the 2nd floor with the other restaurants. This is a walk-up place with no seating, just grab and go! There are places to sit nearby, but it might be nice to add some tables and chairs, especially for those who are eating cake or ice cream. I got the crack pie and she got the cereal milk soft serve. First things first, the piece of pie is tiny! The pies at mickey dees are bigger. I thought for the price of almost $8 it would be a decent size. It was good, but nothing special. It tasted very buttery and the filling was a bit gelatinous, like pecan pie. I am glad I got to try it, but it was nothing special. The cereal milk was very reminiscent of cinnamon toast crunch. Again I am glad I got to try it, but nothing special. I want to try the birthday cake, which they only previously had sold as whole cakes, but now they sell slices. Too bad it's almost $20 a slice. I love cake, but no way I am paying that much ever. Sorry Milk Bar but you are a one and done for me. Pro tip - Target sells Milk Bar baking mixes so you can make these goodies at home. Crack pie, and compost cookies to name a few.

I walked past the original location in NYC almost 8 years ago and have always regretted not trying their milk cereal soft serve. When I saw this location in cos I just had to try it. Milk cereal soft serve with fruity pebbles 2/5- flavor is light, but I can definitely taste the sweetness and slight saltiness as if I was finishing a bowl of cereal. The texture itself wasn't very creamy and a bit on the icy side. chocolate chip marshmallow cookie 3/5 Love the chewiness of the cookie. Tastes like a cross between a cookie and rice crispy treat. Not too sweet, crispy chunks of corn flakes Pricey- Overall spent 12 dollars on a tiny soft serve and a cookie.

The service here is great. The guy who helped me greeted me with a smile, and was very pleasant and helpful. This isn't a walk in restaurant. You walk up to the counter and place your order from their selection of desserts that include cookies and whole cakes. The birthday cake is their most famous cake and the only one the sell by the slice. The birthday cake costs a hefty $16. I got it, and I regret it. It did not live up to the hype. It was a decent cake. It wasn't bad, but for the price I expect more. The milk they soak it with makes it similar to a tres leche (but not quite as wet). It's on par with a grocery store cake at best. I'm a cake connoisseur and i've had far better for far less. Maybe the cookies are better. But don't waste your time or money on the birthday cake. Just go for the cute appearance and nice service.

The Cereal Milk Soft Serve was alright. It tastes just like the milk that remains in a bowl of frosted flake cereal. I think most people have more fun taking pics & posting it to social media than actually enjoying the darn thing. I am guilty of that. I'm a bit depressed about the thought of having paid $7.50 for just okay ice cream. The soft serve is $6 for a tiny cup plus a dollar more to add the Cornflake Crunch topping so with tax it came out to $7.58. For that price I am okay with not having it ever again. If it was mind blowing good I would not mind paying that price again. I also thought the pre-packaged cookies might make good gifts to bring home for future trips but, nope. There are much better things out there for that. Maybe you need to eat Milk Bars cookies as soon as you buy them? I was too full to 'sample' right away so I didn't get to try them until after I returned home so this review is not exactly thorough or precise. The Compost Cookie has a coffee flavor so avoid if you don't like coffee. The Corn Cookie is like a sweet, chewy cornbread in cookie form that was quite interesting. This was my favorite of the three I chose. The Chocolate Chocolate was just okay. Milk Bar is located on the 2nd Floor of The Cosmopolitan near Eggslut & Momofuku. Go if you must. I'm not rushing back anytime soon. Overall rating 2.5 Stars rating up.

There is nothing in the world quite like their cereal milk soft serve. My 5-star review is based solely on that one item! Every day that I'm in Vegas I stop here for a fix of it and sometimes I stop in twice! I've gotten multiple others addicted as well- it usually takes the first try to process the flavor/texture (you have to get the cereal crunch on it) and then after that you can't stop coming back for more. Everything else I've tried here has been amazing as well. Crack pie (which I think was recently renamed) and the cookies and the sprinkle cake- all so delicious!! But truly nothing compares to my favorite soft serve in the world. Try it!

Being a fan of David Chang & the Momofuku empire, its a pleasure to see Milk Bar stand out as another entity. David Chang recognized excellence and created a new branch of the business with Christina Torsi called Milk Bar. Milk Bar sells cookies, pies and crazy ice cream with cereal flavors. Man, I love cereal! To see a Milk Bar in Las Vegas, in the 110 degree weather no less, Milk Bar ice cream is an oasis in the desert. I walked up to the counter and ordered a cereal ice cream. I was asked if I would like the cereal cornflake crunch topping for an extra charge. Yes please :) The cereal crunch mix is amazing and different. To have this outpost in Las Vegas is a welcomed treat. I ordered a Cereal Milk Soft Serve with cornflake crumble topping. The ice cream itself is made with milk, cornflakes and brown sugar. It tastes just like the milk at the bottom of a bowl of cornflakes! I highly recommend Milk Bar Las Vegas, its one of my guilty pleasures :)

My husband and I got shut out of trying one of the boozy shakes at Holsteins next door because the bar was so crowded so we decided to give Milk Bar a try instead. Their boozy shakes did not compare. In fact, the alcohol to chocolate ratio was a bit too strong to be enjoyable. We also ordered a chocolate chip cookie, corn cookie, and a slice of crack pie (because apparently that's the thing to get here). The cookies were yummy but not mind blowing. The crack pie was pretty disappointing. It was a cold, chewy pie slice of sugar. I would go back to try their ice cream or for a quick cookie fix, but everything else here was pretty average or underwhelming.

I loooove coming here every time I'm at Cosmo! There was a good period of time where I was obsessed with the Birthday Cake truffles, but they're not the best to travel with since they need to be refrigerated. The soft serve is delicious, but really sweet and rich, so you have to be in the right mood to eat all of that (or bring a friend and share). Definitely get the cornflake topping! The cookies are to die for. I love having a little of everything when I eat and combining different flavors/textures. The compost cookie, birthday cake cookie, and chocolate chip cornflake marshmallow cookie are my go-to (3 cookies for $8! Or 1 cookie for $3). Very sweet though. I can only eat 1/2 of one in a sitting. I will always come back!

Milk Bar is just such an iconic spot for any hardcore foodie or Christina Tosi fan. The aesthetic is spot on and a millennials dream. The prices are a little steep, but I had to try something. I got the blueberry and cream cookie and the chocolate birthday truffle. It was solid. I was a little disappointed about how they came prepackaged instead of fresh out of the oven; but it is what it is. The desserts were still yummy and chewy and decadent and hit the spot, but I'm assuming it wasn't the best of the best as it wasn't the OG or another flagship store. Regardless, it's worth it to try at least once to say that you did. For any person with a sweet tooth, you won't be disappointed.

Milk- It does a body good. Now when it's combined with flour, sugar and eggs... I still count it as good! If you happen to be in or around the Cosmopolitan Hotel, stop in Milk Bar for a tasty treat we all deserve. Their infamous Bday Cake is now being served by the slice. There seems to be a slight citrus flavor which I couldn't quite nail down but really gave it a unique flavor. The cake itself was moist even for a slice. We were there when they opened up for the day so that might play a factor in how moist the slices will be. It was the perfect treat for us to share. Milk Bar is located on the second floor near their other restaurants. The staff were friendly and quick to serve. Thank you for the treat and I hope to return soon.

I appreciated that they let me try samples. I ended up with the small cereal milk and chocolate pretzel soft serve with corn flakes. Perfect blend of sweet, salty and creamy and crunchy. Expensive, but worth it for a splurge. I will say my hubby got cookies and I didn't like those at all, but he did. I updated to five stars because it was so good I wanted to come back the next day...and I did!

My friend recommended this place and told me their soft serve ice cream are good. So I came with high expectations. We ordered cereal milk with extra corn flakes topping and a crake pie soft serve. The ice cream was very creamy, especially the crake pie flavor. But i think it is lacking some in depth flavor in the ice cream. The first few bit was good but you can get board easily. Maybe I was expecting too much to when we finally got it it was a little disappointing.

I don't get the greatness that Milk Bar is trying to push. The ice cream tastes like it's 30 minutes away from being legit spoiled, the corn flake topping lets me imagine what toasted gravel is like, and I am so immune to the Crack Pie addiction that I left half of it in my fridge only to throw it out a week later. But the one thing that gives my sweet tooth a raging fucking hard-on is that damn Birthday Cake!!!!! I blame the truffle version as my gateway drug into this fat kid's dream come true, and moving forward for the rest of my life, it's either going to be this $60 cake or nothing at all from there. There's just something about that mix of sugar, butter, unbelievable frosting, and all crazy artificial flavor from the insane amount of rainbow sprinkles in this thing that makes me feel like I'm on a diet version of cocaine after a couple of slices. The only way to describe how I brought this from counter to parking garage was like if I worked for the bomb squad and was carrying live sticks of dynamite in a bag. I literally waddled my way out, made sure no one bumped into me, and even waited to use an empty elevator. Next time, I'll bring a snug doggie bed to put it in for the ride home.
We got the combination to try everything. Honestly didn't think it was anything great. I wish they said beforehand that the ice cream was salty and had corn flakes on it.

I was soooooo excited to try this place after hearing rave reviews about it but boy was I disappointed. My bestie and I shared the cereal milk soft serve with Frosted Flakes b/c hello?? You can't go wrong with anything cereal-milk because cereal milk is bomb! Well apparently you can. The soft serve wasn't smooth, and it was incredibly salty. Somehow, the Frosted Flakes made it even saltier! I thought we had a bad batch but after reading some of these reviews, I realize that's the norm! We literally tossed it after one bite and it was $7. We pretty much paid $7 for a cute Snapchat/IG story. Thanks I guess.

I tried Milk Bar because it's famous (Christina Tosi creation) and I love desserts. For me personally, the ice cream is too sweet. I tried almost all the cookies but not all of them super delicious. You should get the famous cereal milk ice cream. It tastes like a combination of cereal and milk which makes it so sweet. The ice cream is not the best but worth a try. I really want to come back to try the famous crack pie. The place is right beside Momofuku (The owner of Momofuku and Milk Bar did a collaboration). I think you should at least try it once because this place is quite famous.

I have had the birthday cake, the crack pie and a few different cookies- all were super yummy. Keep in mind that it's dessert, it's going to be sweet! (There seem to be a lot of complaints on here about it being too sweet.) So get a cup of coffee to help wash down the sweetness and to give yourself the PG version of the Fear & Loathing experience, fueled by sugar and caffeine! I had a mild issue on one of my visits and the customer service was outstanding- that and the yummy cake is a sure 5 star experience in my eyes.
Really cool spot for sweets! Highly recommend checking this place out, super nice staff and good snacks.

I was fan girling so hard and I had planned to stop here after we ate at Momofuku's but I was so incredibly full! We decided to comeback the next day when they opened and it was sooooo worth it! We got the crack pie, compost cookie, Birthday cake truffles, cereal milk soft serve with fruity pebbles, and the sky lark boozy shake (i may have the wrong name of the shake? It was a long week in Vegas lol). Since we were flying out we packed everything up but the ice cream treats into our carry on bag for our flight back up to Seattle. Everything made it! I would not recommend doing that for longer flights though as the crack pie and the truffles should be kept cold. The staff were super friendly! Thank you for the traveling tips with the food. For the treats - oh heck yes! That was a wonderful experience and I am going tell my husband to buy us some more cookies and truffles as xmas gifts for the family. The compost cookie was a hit with the guys because there is a slight hint of coffee in there. The crack pie was a hit for those who are not big sweet fans because it wasn't overwhelming. The birthday cake truffles were hands down my favorite. They tasted so fresh and not processed.

This was our first visit to Milk bar and overall we had a good experience. We ordered the greatest hits so we could try all of the most popular items and we also got a special knights milkshake. I was shocked (in a good way) at how good the cereal milk soft serve was. My boyfriend adored the knights shake but the taste of the scotch was a little too strong for me. The reason we gave it 4 stars was due to the fact that the space is really small and crowded which made us feel awkward and rushed. The line even on a Sunday evening was really long. Although it did move fairly quickly.

Milk Bar was on my bucket list for a long time, but unfortunately, I just haven't made the trip to NY just yet. When I found out there was a location opening up in Vegas, I was EXCITED (understatement). Luckily, I happened to be in Vegas shortly after the grand opening. My first time there, I tried the cereal milk soft serve and crack pie. I enjoyed both, although, admittedly, it was $$$. Regardless, every time I returned to Vegas (which is about 2-3 times a year), I always found myself squeezing in a trip to Milk Bar. When I tried out Momofuku for the first time a year ago, I made sure to try the Birthday Cake and I WAS IN LOVE. It's delicious without being too sweet IMO. So since then, instead of getting soft serve, I get a slice of cake at Milk Bar. I never can finish the slice in one sitting, and even though it tastes best fresh (when it's still frozen), it still tastes good the next day. Cookies are good and my fiance really enjoys them. We both love the corn and compost cookie, and it's especially delicious when you heat them up. :) I'm a fan of Christina Tosi, and I have so much respect for her and what she's accomplished. I recently watched her episode of Chef's Table on Netflix, and it's incredible seeing her journey. Not going to lie -- watching that episode made me crave Crack Pie and Birthday Cake SOOO MUCH. I'm excited for the LA location to open later this year. Yes it is expensive and maybe not something you should be getting all the time, but I'm a sucker for dessert. I also own the Glossier Birthday Cake Bomb Dot Com because of the Milk Bar collaboration, and it smells intoxicating. :)

Mehhh, I've seriously experienced better. Maybe I've been spoiled by all the good ice cream in LA already. There wasn't much variety as I was hoping for for an ice cream spot..in Vegas. I had the Cereal Milk with sprinkles added and got bored of the flavors real quick. That rarely happens with ice cream for me. Overall, overhyped and overpriced :(

I really was looking forward to Milk and i was hoping the reviews i read were just one-off instances,but they are right. There's all this hype and Milk falls short of its expectations. I ordered the greatest hits: compost cookie, birthday cake truffles, crack pie and the cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes. The compost cookie was ok...it seemed a little too salty. The coffee grounds in there seemed to overpower parts of my cookie..almost tasted peppery at times. The crack pie was disappointing. The slice seemed small and when i bit into it, it just seemed like buttery mush. The birthday cake truffles..are not worth it. Do yourself a favor and Pinterest a recipe for Oreo cake balls and make it yourself- literally Oreo, cream cheese and almond bark. That stuff tastes better than the birthday cake truffles. The only salvation is the cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes. The only strange thing is that it has a hint of sourness but i still liked it enough to finish it. This is my first visit to Milk. Maybe this location is just not the same as the Brooklyn one. I'll just have to visit the original to find out!

There was a moment walking down the strip with my wife where her eyes lit up when she saw Milk Bar advertised on the Cosmopolitan sign. As big fans of Christina Tosi, it was a bucket list item to visit her place. Little did we know one was located right here in Vegas. The birthday truffles were the culmination of a decadent dessert, shrank down into a convenient bite-sized form. These things could have only come from the mind of a dessert wizard. The hardest part is walking away from the counter without buying one of everything on the menu.

The Cereal Milk Ice Cream Was Cerealously Amazing. I was just a smidge hesitant before I ordered this flavor, but boy was I impressed. It legit tastes like sugary cornflake cereal milk turned into delicious, creamy ice cream. With the cornflake topping around the sides [and surprise in the bottom too!] it was reminiscent of eating the most delicious bowl of cereal ever. My only regret was not getting this my first night in Vegas. Because I wish I had it EVERY night.

We went here before going home after eating at another restaurant. My friends ordered milkshakes which they really liked but were very sweet. I did not get the hype behind these milkshakes at all. I did order some cookies including blueberries and cream and another which was corn flake chocolate chips with marshmallows. Neither impressed. They were OK. This place knows how to charge a lot of money just because of one name: Christina Tossi. Still, I must say that I am gravely disappointed and that I was not at all blown away by anything that I've eaten there and tried a few things at other friends ordered as well and none were all that impressive. It is expensive and I just don't get it. It's not terrible, but it's far from great.

Three stars only because it's highly overpriced and for a place that's probably on every dessert foodie's bucket list, I know they can do better. I bet there was hard work involved in making this cereal milk-flavored soft serve, but it is not worth $7. You can buy yourself a more wholesome meal with $7... But anyways, about the cereal milk soft serve that I got: it seriously tastes great. I did not realize that I enjoyed the milk that comes with having Frosted Flakes soaked in soggy the bowl for a while - the idea of that sounds kind of gross, but Milk's genius in this soft serve is marketing this into something that sounds totally palatable. However, the texture is kind of weird - very light, grainy, but also borderline melting. It didn't really hold its shape and soon after I got mine, I had to scoop up puddles of cereal milk from the cup with the inconvenient wooden popsicle sticks they give you for a spoon lol. The extra sprinkles were kind of expensive too, but I've never had anything like them - they were super crunchy and I loved them. It really added the much needed texture to the soupy soft serve. So, basically, I think the only reason why Milk Bar's cereal milk soft serve is so expensive is because of the unique flavor, but nothing else. So, if you have an ice cream maker and can concoct your own cereal milk flavor, then save money and make your own :)
My daughter liked it. Pricey, small portion. Located at the Cosmopolitan Check it out.

This is a lot of hype...but does not hit its mark in my view...there are many talented pastry chefs...and clearly she is one but her ideas are not that creative in this place. She has them but choose not to execute them, to bad for all of us. But, kinda cool place, average food , but a very great chef without question.
This place is a hit or miss. My favorite is the cornflake cookies and crack pie. Everything else is either too salty or overwhelmingly sweet.

Hustle and bustle at this NY chain in Vegas. These people were workin hard on a busy day. They were quick, kind and acknowledged everyone in line. Great work! Soft serve cereal milk and those birthday cake truffles. Not too bad. The crack pie wasn't bad either just a bit too sweet. The desserts were all pretty sweet, actually, for me but that's me and my opinion doesn't change that this place is good on what they do. So, don't knock it 'til you try it. :D

The froyo/ice cream here was delicious. Very good, and paired it with some of the cookies. The cookies are unique and delicious. I got one of every cookie. The staff also let me try the different yogurt flavors and some of the toppings before deciding what I wanted for my order. The place gets a long line, so be prepared to wait a bit.

I've seen a lot of hype about this place and I know there's a location in Los Angeles. I hate waiting in long lines so Vegas it is since I'm on the area! I've seen plenty of rave reviews about this place and had high HIGH expectations. But unfortunately I wasn't too pleased at all. This is just based on the ice cream I had and not for the cookies or cakes since I had neither of those. I ordered the milk and cereal ice cream with corn flakes. Price point is a tad bit high for what you get. As for the ice cream itself... it REALLY is MILK ice cream. I mean I have to give it to milk to get the flavor on point. Many ice cream places claim its milk (of course I know ice cream is made of milk but not all tastes like milk) but does not taste anything like milk. So THIS milk ice cream really does taste like milk.The reason for my low rating is the corn flakes. I mean.. i grew up eating corn flakes and frosted flakes and know what they taste like. My corn flakes on my ice cream was extremely salty. I'm not sure if it was meant to be salty to balance out the flavor of the milk. But because it was so salty, the topping I paid extra for (which by the way was a rip off) I ended up scooping off because it was PACKED WITH SALT. Not pleased with this and nor was it worth the hype. Yelp Review 2018 Challenge 82/100

Oh man! Crack pie and birthday cake is a must here! My husband came here a few weeks before with a piece of crack pie after his dinner with his friends at Momofuku. I took one bite out of it and it was like....what is this?!?! We had to come back together. I can't wait to try their soft serve next time. Service is slow....it's the only downfall. It took them over 15 minutes to slice the birthday cake and put it in the box and call it out. We'll still be back!

After watching David Chang on Munchies and Buzzfeed's Worth It series, I've been hyped to try Momofuku and Milk Bar ever since. Much respect to the chef! To be honest though, I didn't enjoy the samples I had of birthday cake and crack pie soft serve. Those flavors were overbearingly sweet in my opinion. But the cereal milk with Frosted Flakes definitely brought me back to my childhood days - scarfing down the last few bites from a cereal bowl while watching cartoons. :") Aside from the soft serve, Milk Bar's cookies aren't bad either. I have yet to try the crack pie but if it's as sweet as the soft serve I'm going to have to pass on that one. But this place is worth the visit overall, especially if you're in Vegas for vacation and want to treat yourself to something sweet!

I'm a fan of David so I really was looking forward to trying the Milk bar. Based on the reviews, I decided to try the crack pie and the cereal milk soft serve. Crack pie? Whack pie. It was gushy and felt like I was biting into something made with a cup of powdered sugar. If you have a super super sweet tooth, then I can see why it's good but if you're looking for flavor and not just plain sugar, pass on this. Cereal milk soft serve? Worth it. Creamy, nostalgic, and great on a hot day! :)

Finally, a frozen yogurt place that doesn't feel like I ate all the calories. Their cereal milk is awesome with the mixture of the chocolate (forgot the title), it was pretty light and creamy at the same time. The lady at the counter was very helpful as it was our first time trying everything. She gave as a descent sized free taste for a couple of flavors. She also explained well, the different types of cookies they offered which we tried as well. The compost cookie was good but so was the corn! Yup corn in cookies ;) Hope the LA location opens soon!

This place is awesome. The soft serve machine wasn't working so the staff stayed late to make it work so we could get our treats. Then they gave us extra truffles, Milk Bar Pie and a cookie because we had to wait! Such awesome service! I was so surprised by how delicious this was. Milk Quake was to die for! Like everything Tosi creates it's different, epic and delicious. What a crazy fun night!!!

So we've been coming back to try something sweet and I have to say that the birthday truffles are absolutely fabulous!! I totally recommend this! Last visit, we got the truffle box, which had 4 (3 truffle) bags. I choose 2 double chocolate, strawberry shortcake, and birthday flavor. The cost for the truffle box was $27. We will also grab a few cookies. The price is a little high but we figure, hey we're on vacation :)

This review is for 4.5 stars. Expensive all around but tasty and novel. Come here and just go fill out. Try the milkshakes the pie and the soft serve. Each will run you about $6-15 but well worth it. This will be the best version of whatever you order. We tried the crack pie and the cereal milk soft serve for $6.50 each and an additional $1.50 for the cereal crunch topping (necessary). The soft serves wee large enough for a nice after dinner dessert and they even give you samples of you ask before choosing the soft serve. Line can get log during peak but pretty fast service once ordered. The cereal milk is just so unique of an idea and deserves its infamy. Tastes as it sounds and if you let it melt drinks as it sounds. The crack pie is super buttery and just a very smooth and rich vanilla. Terrific flavors.

The lines and prices are outrageous and honestly i never understood the hype of cereal milk which is the grossest cloying sweet concoction of sour spoiled milk dredged in fruity pebbles overnight the Crack pie is an all butter mess too. I like masterchef but rather have joe bastianich than the utterly joyless christina tosi. How do you make desserts for a living and look like you just sucked on a bag of lemons all day? Anyway dont waste your time here unless you love bs hype trendy hipster nonsense long lines spending tons of money on subpar ingredients and disgustingly sweet over the top confections likely to benefit no-one but my family dentist

I expected so much better from here. I've heard a lot about this place for years now. Was not able to try it in New York since it was closed the day I was there. Very excited to see that it opened in Vegas. Got the chocolate cookie and cereal milk ice cream. The cookie was dry and stale. Not fresh at all. Wasn't that sweet either. Very gross. The cereal milk tasted salty, not sweet, and just very weird overall. Thank goodness I just got a sample as I ended up tossing it away after a few bites. I can't remember the last time I didn't finish ice-cream, which shows how bad it was. They have other stuff here, but these are the famous ones and it was disgusting! No line. Won't return.

I honestly cannot get enough of Milk!! Seriously the crack pie and bday truffles are my go to whenever i visit! This is a small location but the service is pretty quick and always friendly. The items are pricey but definitely worth for a once and a while expense.

This is my favorite dessert spot in the world (well, it's a tie between After You in Bangkok)! Christina Tosi is a genius. Everything is exceptional! I have baked through both cookbooks and tried every single menu item.. you can say I'm obsessed. Every time I visit Las Vegas or NYC I have to buy some cake truffles and cookies to take back to LA and store in my freezer until my next trip to Milk Bar! My must haves are: - birthday cake ($14): tastes like my childhood all grown up. Pricey, but so worth it! - cereal milk soft serve ($6): the best part of cereal! And the crunchy cornflake topping pairs perfectly with the milky soft serve - corn cookie ($3): I love the unique corn flavor in the soft chewy texture of the cookie - fruity pebble soft serve ($6): this is a newer flavor and is completely ingenious. The best cereal in ice cream form! The Vegas location has affogatos, which are a great deal! For $5 you get a shot of espresso and almost a full size cup of the cereal soft serve of your choice! And cereal in your coffee - need I say more? I'm counting down the days until Milk Bar opens in Los Angeles!

As of late, a lot of East Coast staples have been gracing Sin City with their presence. Starting with White Castle, Shake Shack, Halal Guys and most recently Christina Tosi's Milk Bar. People can now enjoy this cult classic at the Cosmopolitan Hotel, their very first store opened in the west coast. Like the ones that have come before, this too have been plagued with cheers and jeers. So how good is this place really? It's up for debate. Personally for me, I give it 3 solid stars. I decided to get the Greatest hits combo $19 to have that variety: 3 birthday truffle, a cookie of your choice (opted for the compost), a slice of Crack pie and a cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes. On a couple of subsequent visits I've tried their passion fruit and chocolate truffles, cornflake marshmallow cookie and chocolate chocolate cookie. None of which blew my mind. They were all fairly good but nothing stood out and not something I would go out of my way for.

The last time we were in Vegas and I noticed Milk Bar, I almost lost it. I read about them in multiple magazines and couldn't wait to try their treats out for myself. Being that we were there to celebrate my husband's birthday, I figured it was the perfect excuse to buy the birthday cake truffles. You can purchase them either in store (3 truffles to a pack) or online. Make sure that you have somewhere cold to store them if you aren't planning to eat them right away though as they require refrigeration. Because I bought them the day before as a surprise, I also got myself cereal milk soft serve to enjoy then and there with a corn flake crunch topping. It was not at all what I was expecting. Their soft serve is sweet, but not in the way vanilla ice cream is. It's more subtle and was almost tart alongside the crunchy cereal. The combination was so addictive, I couldn't put it down long enough to snap a picture. And those truffles? Worth every freaking penny. Here is a description taken from their webpage; 'vanilla rainbow cake mixed with vanilla infused milk, coated with white chocolate and rolled in rainbow cake crumbs'. Yes to all those things please! Unfortunately the lady working the night I went was annoyed with the world and practically rolled her eyes while taking my order. Nevertheless, the guy who actually gave me the items was very nice. It's more than I'm used to spending for dessert, but when in Vegas I suppose. Their cookies also looked ridiculously good, and I saw lots of people ordering the 'crack pie'. Having now tried the truffles from the store, I'm curious to see how well they hold up when ordered online. The next time a birthday rolls around I just might give it a try. Definitely a good option when your sweet tooth craving strikes and you're in the mood for something a little different.

Tried the milk soft serve with the corn flakes topping and some cookies. The milk soft serve for $6-7 is very expensive especially for the portion and you have to pay extra for any toppings. The customer service was the best part of my experience. The cookies i tried were the compost cookie, their most popular and the corn cookie. Corn cookie was weird. The compost cookie was okay. i thought the coffee flavor was too strong. Overall pricey desserts that were just okay to me.

Tried their cookies in New York before and thought it was average. Some were too mealy. This is the first location in the west coast so decided to try their other desserts and I'm glad I did! Crack pie - recommend. Don't be fool by the size, it's very dense. Fruity milk ice cream - recommend. Not quite fruity pebbles tasting but similar. Love that it's sweet and milky but not overwhelming. I got it with corn flakes topping. I like that they layer the toppings so you get it with every bite. I would definitely stop by again if I'm ever back at Cosmo!

Tried this and was a bit disappointed as everything was mass produced. The cookies were packaged in bags and were not fresh. The cereal milk soft serve was okay nothing too special. The one thing I did like was the crack pie! It's supposed to be served cold, but I recommend getting it down to room temperature and enjoying it that way. You can't really heat it up because it's a custard pie. Overall, service was good, but wouldn't really go back for their cookies. I would for their crack pie.

Perks of being in Vegas is everything opens hella late. Who would think that I'd be able to satisfy my sweet tooth at 12am on a Thursday night with options that expand from the standard Mcflurry. I mean, we knew I was going to stop here for ice cream during this Vegas trip right? Regular hours are 9am to 1am, extended to 2am on Friday and Saturday. So on this rowdy thursday as we sat on a bench watching people getting boozy, we were getting hyped on sugar from Milk. More of a novelty stop if anything, to have the privileged right to declare that I've tried David Chang's infamous Milk Bar. Did it live up to expectations? Yes and no. Taste wise 100% tasty, soft serve was velvety smooth and the option to add cereal flakes on top of my Crack pie makes me feel like a kid again. Cereal milk was equally delicious, not as sweet as Crack Pie but more subtle. Prices are on the higher side, but it's the name that brings them in, cute Milk cups make up for the price right? Couldn't justify a milkshake at this hour but I'll be keeping my eyes wide open the next time I'm in the same Zip Code as another Milk Bar. Cereal milk $6 Crack pie $6 corn flake crunch $1

Had the milk slice of cake with sprinkles. You can really taste the milk the lather into the cake. Was the slice of cake worth $14? I don't think so. The cake is really sweet. So if you like something super sweet this is for you.

Do yourself a huge favor and get the Cereal Milk Soft Serve with Cereal toppings (the cereal topping is a MUSTTT). I love that Milk Bar puts the toppings on top AND on bottom, way to think things through and perfectly execute the soft serve. I always love the ice cream toppings and get so sad when I reach the bottom and all that's left is ice cream with no crunchies, but no fear, Milk Bar gives you the perfect solution to this! Sober, drunk, morning, night, afternoon.. no matter what time or what condition you're in, Milk Bar is delicious!

Sadly, the hype did not live up to the expectation. I had Milk Bar in NYC before, but having it again in LV reminded me why I don't crave for these expensive sweets that are mediocre. Ordered: 1) Crack Pie: 2/5 Good but SO SMALL for the price! 2) Compost Cookie: 3.5/5 probably my favorite item on this list 3) Corn Cookie, 2.5/5 eh, just okay 4) Confetti Cookie: 2.5/5 a bit too sweet for me 5) Cereal Milk Soft Serve: 3/5 again, if it weren't for the price, I would've given it a much higher rating. Overpriced--bottomline.

If you're at the Cosmopolitan hotel and youre looking for a sweet treat, you need to stop by Milk. Their soft serve is incredibly delicious- not too sweet. They are a little pricey for such a small portion, but that's to be expected. I didn't get a chance to try out their other items on the menu... at one point, I was tempted to buy their cookies to bring home since I was only in Vegas for vacation. But if I do return to Vegas in the near future, I'll definitely be back.

True Rating: 3.5 Sweet and Savory My friends have hyped up this place for a while now, so I decided to check this place out the past MDW. I ordered the cereal milk ice cream with corn flakes and hot fudge. The ice cream base in my opinion was just ok. I am usually into creamy ice creams, but this my friends was not. However, I did enjoy the toppings. The corn flakes were sprinkled with salt and super crunchy as for the hot fudge it was not too overwhelming and loved the fact that they used dark chocolate. Final Verdict: It's okay.

I have always wanted to try this place and thought it only existed in New York! So excited to see it at the Cosmo! I got 4 cookies to take home and they were all good and had some unique flavors. I heard their strawberry quake is good and it definitely was super thick and creamy and not overly sweet. I love the sweet and slightly salty bite with the corn cookie crumbs in there.. this is a very filling dessert so it can definitely be shared. I tried a sample of their cereal milk soft serve and want to try it with cornflakes next time I'm in Vegas!

If you're looking for a good dessert, I don't recommend this place. It was super pricey for what you get. I don't mind spending money on good food but this place missed the mark. I had the Fruity Pebble ice cream, it tasted nothing like them. I was expecting sweet fruity flavors but it was super bland. My husband got the Golden Knight Shake, for $15 I was expecting it to at least be topped with whipped cream. I really should have looked at reviews and the lack of line here. Should have been a dead giveaway.

I am giving my experience a five star and the actual food I had a three. I ordered the pie because it was very popular in reviews unfortunately it was so sweet that I could only take a few bites before I recognized I needed to not eat anymore. The birthday cake was twice as expensive, totally recognizing we are in Las Vegas and things are going to be expensive but nearly $15 for a slice of cake is a little extreme. The staff was nice and on my next visit maybe I will try the ice cream. But the pie was way too sweet for me.

I only tried cookies and crack pie, and I was in heaven. They used milk powder in their cookies. That will be the first thing you taste when you bite the cookies. It goes so well with tea or black coffee. Corn flake chocolate chip marshmallow cookies: five stars! Cookie was moist, but not too soft, and it has some crunchy parts. Blue berry cookies: not so impressed, three stars. There is not enough blue berry in a cookie. Blueberry is moist and a tad tangy, which is great. However, I don't think it goes with this cookie with strong flavor of milk powder. Crack pie: five stars. Crust is made of oatmeal cookies. The filling tastes buttery with a hint of butterscotch and milk powder. When I first looked at the crack pie slide, I thought it was too small for the price. Half way through the slide, I knew why the slide was so small and thin. It's sweet and dense. A slide was a perfect serving portion.

MILK BAR is next door to Momofuku at the Cosmo hotel. Come here for unique treats such as their famous "crack pie!" It's a buttery shortbread crust with a dense chewy butter cake that is out of this world! If you get one thing there, get that! But of course they sell individual cookies from chocolate chip cornflake cookies, confetti cookies to their "compost cookie" which I bought as souvenirs!

I believe this showed up as a Yelp recommendation for me because I was in Vegas for a conference. I had never heard of it before but the concept of a cereal milk-flavored ice cream was very appealing and I couldn't resist trying it. It was exactly how you would imagine it would taste and the corn flakes took it to the next level. I even bought a box of the different flavored cookies for my kids. The compost cookie was everyone's fave but as the kid who helped me said, the corn cookie is super slept on! Not cheap but a nice treat.

Milk Bar wasn't as good as I thought it would be. I missed out on the NYC location and was looking forward to trying it here in Vegas. Not knowing what to try, I settled on the "Greatest Hits" ($19), which came with: slice of crack pie, cereal milk soft serve, bday truffles (3), and a compost cookie. I also purchased the corn cookie and the corn flake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie. My least favorite was the cereal milk soft serve with crunch. It didn't really taste like much and was small! The crack pie was also small. What a rip off. The crack pie was good, not amazing. Bday truffles had a strange mouth feel, like too doughy, undercooked, or flour-y. It wasn't that enjoyable. I really wanted to try the birthday cake, but they don't sell it by the slice, only whole ($56). I did like the cookies! I would try them all again, but I liked the corn cookie the best! One big flaw they have is no where to sit or even high top tables to enjoy your treats. Customer service was excellent though. If I am ever in the area and want to throw away some money, I might be back for these overpriced goodies.

It was really dang good. The corn flakes on the soft serve was such an amazing combination - i'm not really sure why it tasted so good, but damn was it great! Next, we got a slice of the birthday cake - it was freaking amazing!! The cream, the cake was so soft and delush. The only thing I can see why people would complain about is the cost, its like 12$ for a slice of cake or something like that - but hey, your in vegas! it was great!

Man alive this place was gross! I might have built it up big in my mind, but not good!! I am so glad they give out free samples because I would have been upset Getting totally over priced not good ice cream. We tried the plain cereal milk, fruity pebbles milk ice cream and crack pie ice cream and all of them were not good at all! The service was great, no line, just not good at all. Glad I tried it and glad I didn't spend any money.
MOST delicious milkshake I think I have ever had. I loved the shake with Glenlivet in it. I loved it so much I had it every day I was in Las Vegas. Be sure to try at least one cookie.

I stumbled upon Milk after eating Secret Pizza upstairs. Their original location in New York so I was excited to see Milk in Vegas. I felt bad for asking for samples so I ended up ordering something even though I wasn't a huge fan. I ordered the cereal milk with corn flakes, the corn flakes was sweet and savory. Initially I thought the soft serve was too sweet but the corn flakes balanced it out. They put corn flakes around the side of the soft serve and when you get to the end, you'll find some more gold! Seating: They have a bench right next to the cashier and addition sofa across the hall.

Exterior = 4/5 This place is located next to Momofuku on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan. It is almost like a stand so there is no seating area for it specifically - though there is seating near by or you could grab a slot machine (play and eat). The line was small when we got there so no major wait. It was nicely decorated, and definitely eye catching with the neon "Milk" sign. Interior = 3/5 Not much of an interior, since it is a stand alone stall almost. They have a cart in front of the cashier where you can get napkins and the utensils. Along the cashier, they have their cookies. Their menu is located on the wall directly behind the cashier. Service = 5/5 The ladies working the cashier and the food items were quick to move and get the items as you ordered. So there was basically no lag time between ordering and receiving your items. Their quickness almost had me struggling to pay and hold my items. Order = 3/5 Crack pie: 3/5 We felt this was a little hyped up, and it didn't really specify a flavor type. It was a kind of tiny triangle of pie, not very thick either. When I bit into it, it reminded me of butterscotch. It was also pretty chewy. Cereal Milk with cornflakes: 3/5 The ice cream didn't really have a flavor that I found I could nail down. The cornflakes itself seemed like they were sweetened, but not in the way Frosted Flakes are. I felt they were more crunchy than your usual corn flakes. I was thrown off as the combination seemed almost salty somehow. Fruity Milk with cornflakes: 3/5 Light fruity flavor. Boyfriend found there to be a slight chalky after taste. The cornflakes, added a nice crunch, but also had an interesting flavor. For me, I preferred this over the Cereal Milk since it didn't seem to have a salty flavor (which I think is attributed to the cornflakes). Overall = 3/5 It was good to try, but I'm okay with not running back next time I am in Vegas. If you like cookies, they also have a selection of cookies to choose from that are pre-packaged. The price was a bit much for the quantity of the items and ice served. Did find the saltiness/after taste of the ice cream a bit weird. Hint = Grab a cookie for on the go munching. They have a deal if you buy three!

My husband and I were excited to take the pilgrimage to Las Vegas to visit Milk Bar. We'd heard multiple outstanding reviews and couldn't wait to try out their unique creations. I left disappointed. While my husband enjoyed his Fruity Cereal Milk shake, I wasn't overly impressed with my Cereal Milk soft serve with flakes as my topping. The soft serve itself wasn't overly flavorful, which made the overwhelming saltiness of the flakes unpalatable. I ate a couple bites and couldn't stomach any more. It wasn't sweet/savory; it was bland/salty. Funny enough, a more significant part of what made our experience lackluster was the disinterested staff. They weren't excited about their product, they weren't happy to be there, and their lack of enthusiasm shone through. I won't be returning to Milk Bar in the future.

We stopped for dessert one afternoon at the Cosmo. My sister had requested cookies from MilkBar, so I brought her a selection of corn and compost cookies. I bought my kids a selection of all the non-chocolate cookies. They seemed to enjoy the confetti cookie the most. We tried the cereal milk soft serve with the cornflake crunch. I had had this in NYC before and I felt the Vegas location's version didn't have enough cereal milk flavor...it was more pronounced in NYC. We also tried the birthday cake milkshake per Food Talk Central suggestion. It was delightful, but really really sweet.

I feel like Milk Bar is the backup plan for people unwilling to wait in line for an hour for eggslut. I'm so glad we are those people. Milk bar has these little bagel pops that is just a bunch of cream cheese stuffed into a bagel roll. They also have drunky milk shakes and coffee (hair of the dog) that are surprisingly strong and can get a good morning buzz going. Don't judge, it's Vegas! We went back twice because they get people through the line quickly, and their drinks and treats are tasty. The staff was really friendly too, which is something that is not always easy to find in this city.

It's soft serve, and there's a limited amount of flavors; however, the flavors they did have were delicious! It was extremely pricey for what we got and the toppings were a lot extra. This review is more for the value, because even though the taste was unique, regular soft serve flavors would honestly be very similar with the added toppings. Also it's impossible to walk outside in Vegas in the summer with this because it melts in like 2 seconds as expected, but just kind of a bummer because it's extra melt-y being soft serve vs the real deal ice cream.

What the hell did I just eat?!? In a good way! Only tried the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake topping but everything looked so good! It is seriously the best sweet treat I've had in a long long long time!!

Just a heads-up, I only tried the Cereal Milk soft serve with the cornflake crunch. I enjoyed it thoroughly. The intentionally less-sweet milky soft serve paired with the delicately, sweet homemade cornflakes was a perfect combination. It truly tasted like the end of a bowl of cereal, without the sogginess. I was also happy to hear that they make their own cornflakes in-house. Obviously, after tasting them, it is apparent. Although the ice cream was delicious, it seemed a bit expensive. I would definitely go back and try more of their menu items and adjust my star rating accordingly. But for now, 3 stars for the hodge-podge, almost thrown together store front and the prices. Maybe, after being in their location for a while, it will get cleaner and more organized. Perhaps the hype built up my expectations a bit more, so I was slightly let down. But they just opened, give them a chance. I believe in you Milk Bar.

I've been to Milk Bar in NYC and I like their cookies and cake truffles. This time I tried their milkshake (Chocolate Malt)...while it was very good, it doesn't warrant the hefty price tag ($9.50) for a medium sized treat. It was definitely creamy and chocolatey, but at that price point, it's not worth it. It was a very good shake, but I probably wouldn't go back...unless someone else was paying ;-)

I've been meaning to come by for the last few Vegas trips and finally had some time! We grabbed a compost cookie, milk cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie, birthday cake soft serve, cereal milk soft serve, and a slice of birthday cake. YES it finally comes in (super expensive) slices which I was hyped about because part of me was considering buying an entire cake if they had it just because I wanted to try. The cookies were just okay, they're all pre-packaged and def taste a day or two old. Not sure if that's the case but they didn't have the right chew/fresh cookie taste to them. The soft serve is AWESOME, especially the birthday cake. Beautifully cream-cheesy and none of the food colouring taste a lot of "birthday cake" products tend to have. I also enjoyed the cereal milk that comes with crunch, sweet cornflake bits. A more subtle flavour but still really good. Now, the famed birthday cake, unfortunately is overhyped. I really wanted to love it, but it was overly crumbly(maybe too long in the fridge?) and just kind of average tasting. It did have some delightful crunchy bits in between the icing layers, but I def wouldn't pay $14 for another slice. 3 stars just because the only thing I feel is worthwhile is the soft serve, and I'll def go back for it!

You're at Momofuku and they serve Milk Bar for you. WHY NOT? Milk Bar is "one of the most exciting bakeries in the country" by bon appÃ©tit magazine. Okay, since they say it like that, it's a sin if I don't right? We ordered the Milk Cereal with crunch and the Birthday Cake ice cream. Milk Cereal: 3/5 Milk Cereal WITH crunch: 3.5/5 Birthday Cake: 4/5 I'm into that sweet life and the Milk Cereal was definitely not sweet enough for me. However, the crunch was a great addition because of the sweet and savory taste. For my preference, I enjoyed the Birthday Cake more because it was sweeter. Even though I enjoyed it more, I actually thought it was too sweet. If there was a sweetness level in between the two it would be the winner. I enjoyed them, but it was just alright. Yes, it was tasty, but I had higher expectations. Creamy but not creamy enough. I feel so bad for giving it such a low rating, but perhaps the cookie route is the safer route. We'll see how it compares when I visit the NYC location.
Milk Bar serves up some really tasty and Instagram friendly treats! My favourites are the cookies (egg-free), soft serve, and crack pie. Bring friends, get one of everything. You won't regret it!

If you enjoy milk and cereal from Afters in California, you'll enjoy this place as well. They have their own version with cornflakes on top of milk ice cream and it's a really nice treat to have while in Vegas! What I liked was that the ice cream wasn't too sweet, and the saltiness of the cornflakes went well with it. I tried all their cookies (besides the confetti) and my final verdict is that the BLUEBERRY AND CREME is THE BEST ONE. The others tasted just like regular chocolate chip cookies to me. Blueberry and creme really stood out! Also perfect balance of sweetness. Really does tastes like a blueberry milk ice cream. If I ever visit Milk in Vegas again, it'll most likely be for the cookie.

I wanted to love this place sooo bad! Being very accessible in the cosmo, my hopes were pretty crushed. Being gluten sensitive, I was very excited to try their GF option cookie but for some reason I felt like there line of, well, everything was TOO salty for my palette. My fiancÃ© agreed as well. We were lucky to be helped by the nice staff and tried every soft serve flavor, but every flavor was salty still. So we decided on cookies to go back to our room since we were only upstairs. Ate only 1/4 of the cookie and had a major headache and salty taste in my mouth. So sad!
Birthday cake truffles!!! Delicious!!!!! So soft, sweet and perfect bite size. I want to try the crack Pie next....can't wait to go back!

Five words to insure happiness...Iced Mocha with Cereal Milk! I also tried the Compost Cookie, which was very good. My only disappointment was when I tried to get one more Caffeine fix before leaving Vegas and they weren't open at 7:30 am. Milk Bar...if you are going to serve such great coffee, you need to be open earlier! It's an order at the counter kind of place, which can sometimes feel a little rushed, but the staff is very friendly and accommodating. We will definitely be back. Best Coffee this Vegas trip.

Some of this review is based off of my friend who bought the desert, in which she only ate. I was just there. This place is located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, by the escalators. This place is just a desert place and has absolutely no seating areas. The prices were in the $12-$30 range just for pieces of desert (cookies and cake). The presentation of the desserts looked good. My friend advised that the cake was amazing. She gives it a 4 out of 5 stars.

Wonderful customer service from Precious and the cashier. They helped me choose the right Milk shake flavour. I fell in love you other the chocolate cake milk shake a must have for all chocolate lovers. It has just the right amount of sweet and goodness. I love that at the bottom of the cup you get to chew the yummy pieces of chocolate cake. I also got a confetti cookie ask them to warm it up they taste delicious when warmed up. The place was busy given the holiday but that did not stop them, they were really fast at serving. Overall I enjoyed my shake and cookie, even my husband that doesn't have a sweet tooth loved it.
I order a slice of birthday cake. Kind of expensive for one slice of cake but it is Vegas. The cake was good but some people might find it to sweet

First and foremost, the staff was very friendly and accommodating at Milk Bar. Overall the store has cool and colorful decor with a modern appeal. I expected to pay more than the usual since this place is on the strip and located in a very popular resort and casino. I decided on getting the, Greatest Combo. Which was a good idea since it was my first time and wanted to try a bit of everything. The combo included a slice of crack pie, cookie, birthday cake truffles (3 pieces) and soft serve ice cream cone w/cornflake pieces. Crack Pie- Clever name, was ok and it was a bit bland in flavor. Cookie- This was my favorite of the items, consistent, chewy and full of flavor. I got the compost cookie. Will have to go back and try the other flavors of cookies Birthday Cake Truffles- Looks pretty but overall it was good and a little on the sweeter side. Soft Serve- I was expecting more of a creamy and tasty flavor but it more of like, "I could've gone to DQ, reaction." I wouldn't waste my time just to grab something sweet in the future. However, if I'm ever in the area with family and friends visiting is probably the only time I would come back or if I'm at one of the many restaurants or events at Cosmo. FYI: This place has no tables or chairs, it's more of a grab and go. There is lounge area that is part of the popular chandelier bar across the way that has decent amount of sofas and side tables. 2017 Yelp Review #10

Milk Bar.. Its located in the Cosmpolitan.. They have different choices of ice-cream that you can choose.. But I got the cereal milk soft serve ice-cream, and I think it's too sweet and also overpriced of the amount of what you're paying for just to eat this. ... And also this was hyped up..however, I don't regret eating this, but this willbe the first and last time that I will eat that cereal ice-cream.

The Milk Bar has finally arrived in Las Vegas, with all the hype surrounding Christina Tosi, the Crack Pie, Birthday Cake and the cereal milk. I was thrilled with anticipation, in fact I even watched dessert clips to get pumped up. When the moment arrived, I was met with disbelief and confusion. The experience factor took a dive similar to how Wile E. Coyote falls off the cliff as he's chasing road runner. I felt the portions were small for the exorbitant prices they were asking for the products. $7 for a kiddie size soft serve and $6.50 for a mini slice crack pie is ridiculous. I thought they both tasted great but not at that price point. What's worse was it was presented in paper cups and cardboard envelopes, for a minute I thought I was at Mcdonalds. I wish I could've tried the birthday cake but they did not offer slices only in a whole. Also, no adequate seating I noticed a few lounge sofas across from me. It was crowded, people were sitting having cocktails, I felt awkward eating ice cream around them. I can't imagine this being Christina's vision as having that nostalgic ice cream experience, this is far from it fortunately, there are other options in Cosmopolitan that I do enjoy.

I had a cold brew coffee with cereal milk. It was good! Similar to Starbucks sweet cream Cold brew as far as Sweetness is concerned. I also tried an everything bagel bomb. Tasty! Good for when your tummy can't handle a full breakfast or the line at Eggslut (next door) is too long.

Two words. CRACK PIE! OH MY GOSH!!!! I had heard about Christina Tosi and watched her on Master Chef Junior so I was pretty excited to check this place out. The crack pie did not disappoint! It was a buttery, sweet piece of heaven. In addition to pie form you can also enjoy crack pie as a milkshake, quake or soft serve. I also ordered her signature compost cookie which has pretzels, potato chips, coffee, oats, graham cracker, butterscotch and chocolate chips. I asked for it warmed up and it was just okay to me. I bet it's delicious fresh out of the oven so if you can figure out when they're baking and get a fresh one do it. My boyfriend ordered a fancy chocolate malt cake milkshake with vodka and kahlua. You definitely won't miss the alcohol in this adult beverage! It was very potent! Given my experience with the crack pie I will definitely come back to try more!

Ask to sample the soft serve flavors and choose your poison. My group and I came back to this place 2-3 times during our trip to Vegas because it was that amazing. DON'T SLEEP ON THE CRACK PIE. It's one of the best $7 you'll ever spend (second to that $7 ice cream you're about to buy hehehe)

My friend and I both ordered the cereal milk soft serve with the cornflake crunch. The soft serve was good but nothing remarkable. The cornflake crunch was very salty. It might have been an off-batch but we found ourselves eating around it... I wouldn't find myself venturing here again.

There was no wait. My friends and I all got the single cereal milk soft serve.The portion is way bigger than the New York location. It was like a meal in itself. I like how they layered the bottom with corn flakes. It was a pleasant surprise. It tastes just as good as the New York location. I would definitely recommend sharing. Recommendation: cereal milk soft serve

For all the hype about milk bar and their cereal ice cream, I'm just not a great fan. I ordered the cereal milk ice cream with cornflake topping and my boyfriend ordered the birthday cake ice cream with sprinkles. Both were not satisfying at all. I got some cookies to take home which were okay but definitely did not meet my expectations. The cereal milk ice cream was not sweet which I'm fine with but the cornflakes on it made it kinda salty which was not what I expected. My boyfriends' birthday cake soft was so sweet and disappointing he didn't even want to finish it. I ended up mixing our two flavors because I didn't want to waste my money but it surprisingly tasted a little better when I combined the flavors but I wouldn't recommend trying the ice cream maybe just their baked goods. Lastly, the workers at this location are not friendly at all. Maybe it was a bad day but they were just not having it when It was my turn to order.

Cookies were on the sweeter side. Compost cookies was yummy and a good mix of sweet & savory but too heavy for my taste. I also tried the corn cookies. It's like cornflake cookies. Tasted much better than the compost cookie. I ordered a small size soft serve. Tasted like cereal milk with cornflake topping. It's yummy if you like drinking your cereal milk after eating all the cereals.

The worst! We purchased two cookies that tasted extremely stale so we went down the next morning to ask if we can return them or exchange them for something else. The cashier called the manager Katie who I explained the situation to and she very rudely and quickly snatched the cookies and receipt out of my hands and handed me two of the same cookies. I was just dumbfounded by the interaction and how snippy and poor-mannered she was. We are from NYC and we know what the cookies usually taste like, I did not want the same ones and didn't appreciate the entire interaction. I can see why this spot has poor reviews. 1 star for the poor tasting cookies, Zero stars for service.

It was my birthday and my husband bought me a birthday cake milk shake with booze in it. I am not a huge cake fan, so this was perfect for my birthday cake substitution. The flavor was really good, but the vodka was so strong because the shake consistency was so liquidity. It needed to be thicker to be considered a shake. It just seemed like a milky cocktail. Other than that, this drink was cute with the sprinkles on top and just what I wanted.
