I waited years to try momofuku milk bar. I've been copying Christina Tosi's cookie and dessert recipes since 2010 but never made it to any of the NYC locations. When the Las Vegas milk bar was announced, I thought about working there. So when the long anticipated opening finally came during a bit of free time in my day, I drove right over to the Strip. I quickly located milk bar just a few steps from the parking garage elevators, east side second floor. Not having to walk through a casino was appreciated. What I found was a simple walk up counter and friendly cashiers ready to take my order. I would have preferred a store to browse while deciding on my selections, but this was my first peek at the full menu and I felt indecisive. The pie selection was limited to crack when I was hoping for candy bar or other varieties. Milk quakes are a Vegas exclusive and the strawberry and corn flavor was an easy choice after being recommended by two staff members. The workers are so welcoming and friendly! As soon as I paid for my order and stepped towards the pick up window, I was offered a crack pie soft serve to try because it was "extra." I wasn't too impressed by its subtle flavor but I enjoyed the crunchy cornflake coating. The milk quake, underwhelming in presentation, was a tasty treat. As I dug in with my wooden stick I uncovered surprises like soft pieces of strawberry jelly and large chunks of corn cookies. I've never tasted anything quite like it. It did remind me of my experiences eating halo-halo, minus the shaved ice, beans, and overall flavor profile. I'm sure the wooden sticks are trying to be nostalgic rather than remind you of the doctors office, but at least halo-halo is served with a real spoon. The only other item I purchased was a corn cookie. The texture was soft and chewy but the flavor was similar to dense cornbread. Target sells milk bar cookie mixes and they taste so much better warm out of the oven, making it even less appealing to spend $3 for a packaged cookie. I have no complaints about price point because it's inside the Cosmopolitan and matches its neighboring $12 carrot juice and $5 biscuit snack bars.

What a freaking ripoff! I didn't try Momofuku Milk Bar the last time I was in New York, so I was excited to hear they opened one on the West Coast several months ago. I've seen photos of their soft serve all over Instagram for years now, and I wanted to see why it was so special. There were mixed reviews of the Vegas and New York locations across Yelp, but I still decided to give it a try for the experience. Location/Ambiance (5/5): Milk Bar is a cute ice cream stand with a pink-and-white theme that fits nicely with the vibe of The Cosmopolitan. It's located on the second floor of the hotel next to its Asian fusion restaurant counterpart, Momofuku. Service (5/5): Came at midnight on a Sunday night, and there was no line. The cashier warmly greeted us and offered generous samples without us having to ask. We tried three of their soft serve offerings: Cereal Milk w/ Corn Flakes, Crack Pie, and Cinnaswirl. Soft Serve & Prices (2/5): The texture was nice and smooth; it wasn't too runny or frozen. They also give you a decent amount. However, I really did not like any of the soft serve flavors... They were also each priced at a hefty $6.50 (with tax) for a single serving. Yikes! 1. Cereal Milk w/ Corn Flakes (1/5) - The soft serve tasted like rotten milk. I was trying to hide my disgusted expression while tasting it in front of the worker.. The Corn Flakes did the dessert no justice, as it made everything weirdly salty and just not appetizing. 2. Crack Pie (?/5) - I honestly do not remember much of what this tasted like or how it differed from the Cereal Milk. I just remember that I was not a fan. 3. Cinnaswirl (3/5) - The best of the bunch in my opinion, as it resembled Cinnamon Toast Crunch. I wasn't in love with the flavor after sampling this, but I still ended up ordering it because I felt bad for spending so much time sampling. I later wished I had just tipped the guy and walked away, since the flavor became way too sweet after several bites. I couldn't even finish it because my teeth felt coated with sugar, and I'm normally one to lick my bowls clean... Try this place at your own discretion or for the experience, but there's a reason for all of the Milk Bar locations' averaged 3 - 3.5 star ratings.

How do I start I love this place for their soft serve cereal milk Ice cream. I go out of my way at times just to go here for dessert. I live in Vegas so it's one of my go to places. I don't like the other flavors that much like the crack pie or salted pretzel way too salty for me and i don't know jus too much for me but they have another one fruity cereal that I love but they don't have all the time what a bummmer. I also recommend the cake truffles if you want a burst of sweetness in your mouth. You can also take them home and freeze them if you like! Overall this place is awesome I love the vibe the girls are always friendly there! And they give big samples!

I did expect better. I've seen the reviews, seen the chef on tv, and even went back twice. But all three items didn't ever call me back. The crack pie made me believe I could easily quit crack. It was forgettable. The birthday cake shake was not the party I was expecting. And the compost cookie was not even as good as Panera's Kitchen sink cookie. Too bad because I really wanted to like this place as it's location is awesome and the help is great there! I'll be back at the Cosmo, and when I do, hopefully, they'll have something new for me too try.

Was super excited to try Milk bar with all the hype and after watching the Netflix special. Ordered the greatest hits which is a nice mix of options (cereal milk soft serve, crack pie, bday cake truffles, compost cookie). Ate them in that order and it definitely declined in quality as we went - by a crazy amount. Cereal milk soft serve - amazing. I thought this was kind of gimmicky but it pleasantly surprised me. The taste is more subtle than I expected and I loved it. Crack pie - I was looking forward to this the most and it met my expectations. Love the chewy texture and flavour. I didn't find it too sweet and I'm not big on sweet. It's buttery and as someone mentioned has a hint of citrus (although there's no actual citrus in it) which is odd but I really enjoyed. Bday cake truffles - getting a little disappointing. Still enjoyable, nice texture but tasting pretty artificial and not fresh. Compost cookie - huge dive in quality. Honestly it was gross. Tasted so artificial, fake sweet, not fresh, yuck. Also had a coffee which was a nice surprise - found it delicious! So definitely worth a visit but unfortunate that some of the items were a miss for me. Not sure if maybe the quality/freshness has declined as this brand has grown. Would def recommend the cereal milk soft serve if you only want to try one thing. In general this place doesn't seem to have a focus on quality ingredients which thankfully is more on trend in general and could hurt milk bars longevity.

Crack Pie. After watching Chef's Table I was obsessed with trying this Crack pie. In the documentary they had Matt Lauer saying it really was like crack and he needed more. So I finally get to the one at Cosmo in Vegas and order a piece. It's $6.50 and smaller than a McDonald's apple pie. Maybe the size of a McDonald's apple pie with a bite taken out of it. From what I've been told it's supposed to be gooey toward the center (center? At that size there's really no center!), smooth and silky. Instead I paid for a dense, chewy piece that more resembled a cliff energy bar. The flavor was good and very sugary but nothing close to what was billed in the documentary. I was really, really bummed. You see, I gave up crack a few years ago and was looking for a replacement. This ain't it. I'm wondering now if it wasn't sitting in their cooler too long and I just got a stale piece. Nonetheless I would expect more from a place like this. I was going to get a slice of Birthday Cake for my granddaughter but at $14 a slice I didn't want further disappointment and possibly become suicidal. In my opinion Crack pie is not all it's cracked up to be. I may be giving it another try in the future though. You know how junkies are.

I wanted to try the cookies here; the flavors sounded very interesting. I got the blueberry one, the Compost cookie, and the cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow one. I didn't feel like any individual ingredient really popped out when you're eating it, I guess it all blended in well all together. Maybe next time, I'll get a chance to try more off the menu.

Had this placed bookmarked and finally got to try this place. Bought a dozen of cookies. Cookies are just ok, not too impress with them. Kinda pricey, a dozen cookies set you back $28. I bought 2 of each flavor and it was just ok. Nothing stood out for me with the cookies. A slice of crack pie goes for $6 and the whole pie at $56. But omg that pie is so damn good!! Makes everything jiggly and happy at the same time. This and the soft serve I will definitely go back for. In the meantime, I will try to make my own crack pie as the recipe is posted on the web and they also sell the mix at Target. But when in Vegas, definitely a treat. The cashier was very perky and peppy. A tad bit too cheerful for that morning that I went but it's just me as I didn't sleep much the night before. Definitely go for the crack pie and the soft serve!

First time checking out the Milk Bar at the Cosmopolitan. It always has a steady line but it moves quickly. I decided to try the Crunchy Cereal shake which is one of their most popular. It's definitely on the more pricier side in regards to their offerings, but it's good and tastes great. I like how you can really crunch the cereal. This is definitely a shake you need to drink right away, in order to enjoy the crunch.

Date & Time: Monday July 31, 2017 @ 1am Dining Companions: Cousins & Husband Scene: Guys in Fitted Tee's, Shorts & Sneakers & Girls in Crop Tops, Short Denim Cut-Off's, Hermes "H" Belt, Flat Strappy Sandals Decor: Cute Pink & White Ice Cream Stand Service: Friendly, Efficient w/ Awesome Asian Manager Imbibe: Green Juice Devour: Cereal Soft-Serve Total: $20

I missed the Milk Bar Yelp event and was surprised by the low ratings when this business opened, so I had to check it out myself. I have very mixed feelings about how to rate this place because some of the reviews are nitpicky as hell (but they bring up a lot of valid points), but the product is pretty good. Worth the Strip price-hike though? Debatable. LOCATION: Inside the Cosmo, easily accessible from the parking garage. Walkup counter, no dedicated seating, Chandelier Bar has couches and Eggslut has counter seating nearby. Other locations are walkup only, so this shouldn't be an issue. But a lot of people dislike it. PRICING: Compared to NYC locations, prices are a bit higher (+75c per cookie, +$1 for Crack Pie Slice, +$1.50 soft serve, +$3 for greatest hits combo, etc.). Similarly, their Milk Quakes are $12 compared to other alcoholic shake options nearby that are $15. But the other place has larger portions and great presentation, too. SERVICE: Fine. No complaints. My order was taken by friendly staff. I waited on one of my items for a few minutes and a staff member asked what I was waiting on, noticed it had been forgotten, and made it immediately. PRODUCT: Sampled a little bit of everything with the Greatest Hits Combo ($19). There are also mixes, cookbooks, tote bags, scarves, and such available for gifting. Cereal Milk Soft Serve- other reviews say the flavor is bland and portion is small, but I could barely eat half of it. I'm not a corn flake fan but the texture was appreciated and enhanced the flavor, which had a nice pinch of saltiness to it like you really get at the bottom of a bowl. Compost Cookie- #nocrunchycookies! This had the perfect texture of soft and chewy, but not falling apart. Interesting combination of flavors but I can't really say I liked it. Maybe I'll try other cookie flavors in the future, but the NYC price is a lot more appealing. Birthday Truffles- I couldn't decide if I liked this. Nice hint of bday cake flavor but really sweet. Only ate one of the pack of three and that was enough. This might be fun for gifting though. Crack Pie- It's like pecan pie without the pecans and I like that it isn't too sweet but I'm not about to get addicted. As others have said, the slice is tiny. For the price, it should be deeper/taller. It's a nice little treat but the cardboard sleeve packaging preventing you from seeing the portion size is a bit deceptive. Birthday Cake!- Okay, full disclosure, I got the cake free through an IG promo. The 6" regularly retails for $56. The portion claims to feed 8-12, and I'd say that's accurate. It's fairly tasty and not too sweet, and I like how the crumbles add texture. The "naked" decoration style also keeps the ratio of cake to frosting more even, and the multiple layers are both pretty and help to distribute the frosting. Would I eat it again? Probably. Would I pay nearly $60 for this cake? Probably not. Unclear why the crack pie is available whole or sliced but their self-proclaimed "fan favorite" cake is not. In short, it's A-OK. It's exciting that we have a Milk Bar location on the West coast and I'm glad I tried it, but even if I happen to be at the Cosmo, it's not a must-go place for me. Even if there isn't a line.

When I first heard about Momofuku Milk Bar coming to Vegas, I was so excited to finally try it! Since Momofuku is a popular brand in NYC and I have never been to NYC, it is nice to see that I am able to try it at home! Momofuku Milk Bar is located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, and it is next to Momofuku Noodle Bar, which is opening in January. Since they had a large selection of different types of desserts, I got the cereal milk soft serve with crunch topping as well as some cookies and crack pie to take home to try! Their cereal milk soft serve with crunch topping was very interesting because it had a salty tang to it, which I didn't expect, but it was good! The items that I took home were the crack pie, blueberry and cream cookie, compost cookie, and chocolate chocolate cookie. The crack pie was quite small, but it was really good in my opinion! I did not like the blueberry and cream cookie since it taste saltier than expected and had the taste of a type of blueberry muffin that I did not like. My favorite cookie was the compost cookie since it combined a coffee tasting cookie with a bunch of crunchy toppings! The chocolate chocolate cookie was pretty good also!

After dinner we were looking for something to satisfy that sweet craving ordered- milk bar pie, cereal milk soft serve, and the compost cookie. The cereal milk soft serve has got to be my favorite, the taste brings you back to being young and waking up early on Saturday mornings for cartoons and cereal. The milk bar pie was also delicious, buttery and super rich. We couldn't finish this one because of it. The compost cookie was great, a wonderful mix of salty and sweet. Taking one bite ultimately leads you to wanting another. Until "poof!" It's all gone. If only able to get one I would recommend the cereal milk soft serve!
No place to sit down we shared a slice of the birthday cake. Wasn't too impressive and was way over priced. 15.00 a slice. Had to try it out but wasn't worth the money. Pretty disappointed.

We ordered compost cookies and milk ice cream for our after dinner deserts one night. The verdict was ordinary tasting cookies and ice cream, not worth the high prices. Basically we paid for bragging and photos of the famous Milk Bar visit. I supposed the high rent of locating the store inside The Cosmopolitan justified the high prices. One visit was enough.

I have been to the one in New York but I have never seen the birthday cake available by the slice! Because I have to try the hype and see for myself I forked over the $14 for a slice. Verdict? Taste just like a funfetti cake mix cake. But Hey I can cross it off my list! I will say the sample of the cinnaswirl soft serve was tasty and much better than the cornflake one they usually have.

As a long time Masterchef fan, I've been dying to try out the famous Milk Bar by dessert legend, Christina Tosi. Cue a long weekend trip to Vegas, offering the perfect opportunity to cross Milk Bar off my culinary bucket list. I shared a Milk Pie (formerly known as Crack Pie, but I guess that's not PC?) and Cereal Milk soft serve (with added cornflakes) with my partner. Both were fantastic. The "Milk" Pie (brown sugar and butter on an oat crust cookie) lived up to its former name, as it was so darn delicious. It offered every flavor and texture I'm looking for in a dessert. Sweet, buttery, salty, sticky, gooey, and simply delicious. Be warned that this is a very rich, sweet dessert. If I wasn't already in dessert heaven with my Milk Pie, my Cereal Milk soft serve brought me there for sure. I loved how the soft serve really did taste like cereal milk; like the sweet milk you drink after the frosted coasting on your cereal disintegrates into your milk. However, it wasn't overly sweet and the soft serve had a nice, mellow sweet flavor. The cornflakes were essential in adding a much needed textural element to compliment the creaminess of the soft serve. I wish there was a Milk Bar by me so I could always treat myself to one of Christina Tosi's fantastic creations. Not only is Milk Bar super cute and #grammable, but also outright delicious. I suppose my body...and wallet, for that matter, are happy that it requires a plane ride for me to get a treat at Milk Bar. If not, you'd find me here on the regular!

My wife and I were in LV over a month ago and stopped at Milk Bar in the Cosmo. As expected, it was quite busy but the line moved quickly. We ordered the single serving of the fruity cereal milk (basically fruity pebbles inspired) soft serve. I personally loved the flavor and the cereal topping (cornflake crunch which was an extra charge) on the edges as well. The next day, I stopped by for the birthday cake milkshake which was delicious - but super rich (I couldn't finish it! So sweet!). The birthday cake is filled with sprinkles, cake pieces, and cereal milk. I still have cravings for Milk Bar and am so happy my wife convinced me to stop by.

I had heard so much about the crack pie I knew I had to try it. I bellied up to the countered, handed over ~$10, and received this itty-bitty piece of pie. It must be the best pie ever for that price/size, right? I took a bite and...ok? I don't know what the big hoopla is over crack pie as it didn't come close to blowing me away. It was ok, but not worth it for the size/price. Try something else!

Milk Bar is located on the second floor of Cosmo, right in front of the escalators. Given that there was so much hype around their NY location, I was really excited to finally be able to try it for myself. ...I guess I'm glad I got to try it once? The cereal milk ice cream was SO SO SO SO SO overrated. Even considering "strip prices," the amount you get for the price you pay is not worth it at all. I liked that the taste of the ice cream was subtle. I do not suggest the corn flake topping; I get that people add salt to bring out the flavors of desserts -- but this was wayyy too salty. We also got a corn cookie and compost cookie. The corn cookie tasted like corn bread in cookie form, which I surprisingly really enjoyed. Compost cookie had interesting texture to it (it has potato chips in it!). In regards to the service, it was very subpar. They were quick to fulfill my order, but let's be real, you're just dispensing ice cream and handing me prepackaged cookies. The lady who took my order could not understand my order at all. I had to repeat my order several times and still she got it wrong. TL;DR This place was way overhyped. The ice cream and corn cookie weren't bad, but given the price and service, I don't think I'll be coming back.

Pretty disappointed in this place. I'd been wanting to try milk bar for a very long time. A single slice of cake here was $15. I was expecting higher prices, given we're in a casino. I was not expecting the cake to taste like it was made from a Betty Crocker box. Overall very bummed. Would be very curious to know if the cake tastes the same at other locations.

I really wanted to like this place, but it's not for me! Everything I had was a little too sweet and buttery. The crackpie soft serve was so rich and sweet I could not finish it. The crackpie itself was served cold, I didn't know that and it was too buttery, so were the cookies I had. I actually preferred the crackpie I made myself at home with the pie mix cause it was warm. I tried my friends cereal milk soft serve and it was pretty good and not as sweet.

Where are the white tablecloths? I hope this place fails. Not for the tastes of what my group had, most of which was respectable, but rather for the obscene and unwarranted price point. It's the first time I've found pricing to be offensive, even as an Apple products' loyalist. It just doesn't make sense, despite the location and not even for the overall quality. $6.50+tax and they ask for a tip for tossing you a pre-packaged microscopic crack pie, delivered to you abjectly in a cardboard box that belies the actual size of your wedge. I had a flashback to one of those trashy McDonald's apple pies that come in those flashy red plastic containers. I began to utter, "what's this?" to the cashier as she thrust it at me, but stopped when I saw the label, my eyes widening, my heart deflating. At least at McDonald's they put it on a tray and give you a place to sit and enjoy their classy dining. Not at Milk. At Milk you're supposed to stand around awkwardly amidst the mass of people jostling for either the escalator or a slutEgg, looking like a chump for having bought some egregiously priced grab-n-go miniscule. $6.50+ for this sliver that is smaller than my small Trump hands, with an embarrassing un-artsy smudge of confectioner's sugar? NO. My friends got the $12 (TWELVE!) booze shakes, and I felt sorry for them. The presentation was trash: a cheap plastic dome top, about the size of a Starbucks tall. Know where you can get a beautifully crafted booze shake 3x the size? Two shops down at Holsteins. Not coming back. I'm secure enough with myself I don't need the name-notoriety of this place to feel like I'm succeeding in life for having bought something here. As an accomplished amateur baker, my dreams for this place after the impressive marketing they did pre-opening were shot. Total implode. It's an insult to anyone who knows their way around confections or who respects the American dollar.

Klossis review - I tried the 5boro which is chocolate fudge cookie with chocolate chips and is gluten free and dairy free which is my jam! This cookie is almost paleo except for small amounts of corn starch. It's got a flourless brownie texture and taste which I absolutely loved. Calling this a cookie is just wrong so I think it's misplaced into that but if you want a flattened brownie which gives you that decadent fix - get it! They had two other gluten free and dairy free options which sound interesting with one being more of a energy bar style cookie and the other a simple oats and maple cookie which sounded meh. Any place that has great cookies for the allergy friendly and doesn't taste like cardboard is a win in my book!
The milk ice cream and cereal flakes is of course a must get. In addition, I recommend getting the birthday cookie. So good!

I could not get enough of this place! I've been to the original Milk in NYC, so I was hoping for a similar experience. I was not disappointed, the Vegas location tastes just like real thing! All the ice cream is made from cereal milk and it tastes A-MAZE-BALLS. With or without the cereal crunch toppings, this place won't let you down! Located inside the Cosmo, just up the escalator, it's in a great location next to many other food options. My only gripe is that it's a bit pricey, but so was the NYC locale.
Out of the birthday cake when I arrived. Tried the birthday cake truffle instead and was not impressed--just overly saccharine, nothing interesting about it. Over rated!

I was very disappointed in the cereal milk soft serve. There was no flavor and it wasn't good at all. I've ordered it at the NY location so I know what it's supposed to taste like. Total waste of $6. The crack pie was pretty good. I ended up dipping it in the soft serve to try and give it more flavor.

Milk Bar is fantastic!! It's full of tasty treats and morsels. I originally only went because a friend of mine asked me to pick up the Confetti Cookie mix for her. I ordered a slice of their birthday cake. The slice was large. My friend and I shared it. It was absolutely delicious. I'll be coming here again very soon. Id say this is a must visit stop if you have a sweet tooth and you're in Vegas.

Milk Bar, located in the Cosmo, fittingly right next to momofuku, is a great spot to satisfy your sweet tooth! So many options - cookies, cake, crack pie, soft serve, cake pops, milkshakes. The best thing to get here is the soft serve hands down! You can split even the smaller size into 2 flavors and the best is the cereal milk and chocolate pretzel side by side. Add the corn flake crunch - they put it on the top/sides and there's a surprise layer on the bottom too! You will not be disappointed. Also delicious as an affogato and less sweet. Cookies are great to take on the go as they are packaged and you can also get a gift box to bring back as well. Unfortunately they also taste a bit like they are packaged too. Nonetheless, the best flavors are the corn cookie and compost cookie! The rest of the treats, like the crack pie or milkshakes, are good for a one time try or a taste but probably not as repeat orders since they are really super sweet.

I'm really not a dessert person but when I tried the cereal milk soft serve I couldn't get enough of it! If you like plain ice cream or want to pick a safe bet, definitely get the cereal milk soft serve. It is pretty expensive though which is the downside, and wouldn't be a place where I can stop by everyday. And they close at 1AM which is also a plus compared to other ice cream/dessert shops.

My expectations were probably too high, since I've always been hearing how good Milk Bar is in NYC. To save money, 4 of us split a pint of Cereal Milk Soft Serve with Cereal Toppings (~$3/person). I was a bit disappointed because there wasn't anything "wow" about it. But the ice cream was good, if I remember. The cereal toppings are a must. They packed the top AND bottom AND middle of our pint with cereal. By itself, the cereal seems really salty, but it's a surprisingly perfect combination with the ice cream that made me kept going for more. The strange part is that I kept wanting to go back for more the following day and even after leaving Vegas.

I was very happy this famous dessert place in New York opened in Vegas. But after trying the ice cream, I think this place is bit overrated. The milk soft serve with crunchy cereal add-on ended up costing me $7 something. I was like ??? at the moment because I couldn't believe I paid that much just for ice cream. The price might work for NYC but definitely not sustainable here. There's no line when I visited. The soft serve was good but I think the cereal was a bit too salty. I'm not sure if I will come back.

I haven't gotten the chance to visit the one in NYC, which is more convenient, but always busy. So, I figured it was my chance to try Milk while I was on vacation with a very, very short waiting time. I just have to say everything was amazing: the cookies (I got 6 for $17, expensive I know but you have to understand 1. Your in LV 2. This is located in a hotel 3. It's Milk), the crack pie (now I know why everyone is obsessed) and the Cereal Milk soft serve with the crunchies. The only thing Negative thing I would say is that, when I was trying to figure out what I want to get, the person taking my order wasn't really any help and kinda looked at me like I was stupid.

I'm a big fan of Milk Bar in NYC, so it was fun to see a Vegas Milk Bar. They're pretty much the same but with a bit more promotional material laid out. For a midday snack and booze, my husband and I got two boozy milkshakes ($12): cereal milk and coffee white russian. They were definitely creative, and you could taste that they were spiked. I did find them a little small, but they were a snack, after all. If you're looking for a fun, unique snack on the Strip, stop by this spot. They also have amazing, unique cookies.

I was excited to try this and I'll say that the crack pie was great. We also got the cereal milk soft serve which was just ok in my opinion. It cost $6. And we added a cereal topping which I thought was stale and that cost $1.25. Like I know she's a celeb chef and it's Vegas, but it was not $7 good. I'd give it 3 1/2 stars, but I can't. So just come prepared with the idea that it's fun, but pricey w a lot of hype.

My girl was hyped up to come and try their Crack Pie. On our way there I was thinking this pie must be amazing to have a name like that. It was the only thing she ordered and when I saw it I couldn't believe how small it was, in my head I thought it would be a huge slice of pie. My girl loved the pie but when I tried it I just thought it was okay, nothing spectacular and definitely no fireworks from the experience. This is a review on the pie but in the future I would like to try their other products.
Ingrid at milk bar was the absolute most help. She was so sweet and helpful. I appreciate her so much!

I've been waiting for Milk Bar to open for a few weeks now after stumbling upon it's storefront advertisement a few weeks ago. I stopped by today after lunch to check it out. I've had Momofuku Milk Bar a few times before in NYC so the opening in Vegas is really exciting for me! Their most popular dessert is the milk and cereal - I wouldn't say it's the most spectacular dessert, it literally tastes like milk and cereal, but it's worth a try. What I keep coming back for is their cookies - compost, corn, blueberries and cream are among my favorites. So far the line is pretty empty, I don't think a lot of people know it has opened in Vegas, but I anticipate it will get busy soon.

Haven't been to the original location in NYC but decided to come here since I've been wanting to try it. My bf & I shared the milk and cereal flavored soft serve. It was super creamy and I also added the corn flakes topping as well. Overall, the ice cream was good, but definitely not good enough to warrant the price. For one small soft serve I paid almost $8!!! The corn flakes topping itself was an extra $1.50 & they didn't even give that much. It was pretty much just fried corn flake crumbles. I would prefer milk & cereal flavored ice cream from afters back home instead of this one, although this one wasn't necessarily bad, it was just way overpriced and not that great.

Good customer service the girl helping us was very happy to explain the menu. The bday cake slice I was skeptical about but tasted pretty good, has bits of cookie in it which was unique to us. Also ordered the cereal milk soft serve but that was super lackluster and I wouldn't recommend. It reminds me of a custard and it wasn't at all sweet and easy to get sick of the taste.

What I ate: Babyquake with cereal mill soft serve and crack pie Visit Date: March 2, 2019 First time? Yes. I asked the cashier if I could have the cereal milk soft serve with crack pie on top. He suggested I get a Babyquake which has crack pie blended into the soft serve and then it's topped with more crack pie pieces. It was a great suggestion! It was my first time trying both and I was pleasantly surprised. After watching Christina Tosi's Netflix special I was thinking her creations would be overly sweet, but they weren't! The soft serve was just slightly sweet, just like cereal milk (er, sugary cereal cereal milk). The crack pie had the texture of lemon bars, and the comforting feels of pumpkin pie. It was sweet, but paired well with the soft serve. I bought the corn and blueberry creamcheese cookies to take home. To be honest, I was also scared of the corn cookie, but it was so delightful and not too corny or sweet. Now I want to go to New York to visit the original location and take a workshop!

This establishment has the coolest dessert concept ever. The thought of bringing your childhood memories back by creating fruity pebble cereal milk soft serve! Delicious. They also have created a soft serve imitating their famous crack pie, tasting similar to caramel. Don't stop there, they offer so much more! Cookies: my favorite was the blueberry creme but if you're a chocolate lover go for the chocolate chocolate. If you are gluten-free or have an allergy to nuts they offer a klossie which is a cookie just for you. There are 3 to chose from; chocolate, coconut and I believe a chocolate chip. Milkshakes: the options are endless for shakes! They have birthday, Crack pie, cereal milk, coffee and chocolate malt where they add chocolate cake truffles in the shake. You want alcohol, you got it! They can turn your shake into a "fancy" milkshake. And don't forget toppings! Truffles: the truffles are more like cake pops. They come in a 3 pack and your options are bday, chocolate malt or white chocolate passion fruit. Las Vegas strip has so many dessert options but if you are in or near the Cosmopolitan I highly recommend you trying it out. If you are dining with momofuku, they also offer milk bar desserts. Don't forget to get a coffee with your treats! They have their own coffee blend which makes an amazing espresso.

I finally tried this place because both my friend and I wanted to see if it was worth becoming a regular place to visit. Unfortunately it did not live up to all the hype that I've seen online. Their soft serves were eh at best. I liked the flavor of the cereal soft serve, but its texture wasn't my favorite. I was expecting it to be smoother, and it wasn't like that at all. The texture on the cracked pie soft serve was much, much better and I liked how it tasted too. It was a little salty, but not a bad taste. I don't think I will visit this place again as I feel like the $7+ on a soft serve just isn't worth paying, especially when quality isn't the best. The stars on this review are really just for the employee that helped my friend and I. She was very friendly and patient with us and made our first time a pretty good experience.
Meh. My mom makes gooey bars better than the crack pie. And the one cookie we had (we ordered two but only got one for some reason) was like a pre-packaged cookie you'd get at a gas station.

I didn't get the chance to try Milk Bar while I was in NYC so I was excited to get the chance to try it while I was in Vegas. I got the famous cereal milk soft serve. I was told it tastes "just like the milk at the bottom of a bowl of corn flakes" but for $6 I was thinking "surely there's more to it than that?" Well, there's not. It tastes JUST like the leftover milk after you finish eating your corn flakes. Don't expect anything more. If you don't like sweet desserts - this would be an option for you since there's barely any sweetness to it. I decided to add cornflake crunch around my tiny cup of soft serve because it made it look more appealing. I mean, I asked myself what the perfect topping would be for cereal milk soft serve - obviously the cornflake crunch??? NOPE. Not only was it $1 extra but I thought it was seriously on the salty side. Yuck! I appreciate the sweet and salty combination (I love salted caramel...and dipping my fries into milkshakes) but this combo that Milk Bar put together was a no no in my book. My friend got the fruity cereal milk soft serve and I thought that had a pretty nice Fruity Pebbles milk taste. Was it $6 good though? Granted, this review is only based on the cereal milk soft serve so don't let that stop you from trying their other menu items! What's unique and exclusive to the Vegas Milk Bar is they have "Milkquakes" so maybe give those a try?

I FINALLY GOT TO TRY THEIR CEREAL MILK ICE CREAM. Sorry for the caps, I was just that excited. I tried some of their goodies (corn cookie, cake truffles) before, but since I haven't made it out to NY since before Y2K, I had not been able to try the ice cream. Until now. I love milk flavored ice cream, which my fiance finds ironic because I don't like to drink milk. Furthermore, I love the milk leftover from my cereal bowl. The fact that they put it in an ice cream makes me so happy. I got the classic cereal milk ice cream with corn flake topping. NOTE: THIS IS NOT A SUPER SWEET ICE CREAM. If you're expecting a lot of sweetness, this is not for you. I really enjoyed it. If you're into the sweeter things, they have a fruity cereal milk ice cream which tastes like the milk leftover after Froot Loops or Fruity Pebbles. I tried the sample of this one, and it was good, but I preferred the original cereal milk. I also bought a dozen cookies to take home with me. There were literally 10 corn cookies and 2 compost cookies. Those corn cookies are my favorite cookies of all time. Period. They almost taste like a sweet cornbread. I LOVE them. I do want to come back and trie the crack pie next time I come back. It's on my list!

We stopped by here after a pool party at Marquee. Prices were steep but the cakes and cookies were delicious. We got the bo they cake and 4 cookies. My favorite one was the toffee cookie. There isn't much room to sit it is more of a take out place but tis on the 2nd floor of the Cosmopolitan and there is great people watching. Wouldn't say it's the best cookie I've had but I hit the spot after a hot pool party!

Just like in NYC, you get the same quality soft serve. And unlike NYC, it's always hot in LV. David Chang you genius of a man. I'd happily slurp your leftover bowl of cereals milk. Wait a minute. Isn't this what it is?

I've heard a lot about how good their cookies are from my cookie loving friends who enjoy baking, so I was excited to run across the cookie/soft serve bar while walking around the Strip. The soft serve was very tempting, but it wasn't an option, given the fact that dinner was less than 1 hour away, but the staff here was very nice and even gave me a sample taste. The soft serve was definitely tasty but a little pricey as well. I opted to buy some cookies since I could take them with me and I got a compost cookie, cornflake-choco chip-marshmallow cookie, and the blueberry & cream cookie. Note that the cookies are cheaper if you buy 3 or more ($3 each or 3 for $8)! Compost cookie was my favorite of the 3. Sweet and salty, so many different textures and flavors all in one cookie. Yum! My wife enjoyed the cornflake-chocolate chip-marshmallow one the best. We were both lukewarm on the blueberry and cream, a little too creamy and not as flavorful as the other two in our opinion.

My sisters were not impressed with the crack pie at all . It is extremely sweet but nothing special. Taste like raw Dough. Just tasted like sugar Cookies taste better but they aren't that great either It wasn't amazing but it was dry !!!! Milkshake was good. Coffee is good to me cold brewed but some people aren't into the sour taste . Overall, a spot that doesn't hit the spot as much as you have expected

An awesome place to go find a sweet treat while in Las Vegas. Everything on the menu looks great. If I would go back again I would get the cookies and/or cake instead of the ice cream products. It seems like there is always a line but it goes pretty quickly and the product is served pretty quickly too. Its a fun place to get a treat in Las Vegas on the strip.

I'm happy that Cosmo Vegas houses all these popular food spots from around the US (Hattie B's in Nashville, Pok Pok in Portland, Eggslut in LA) as I can get easier access to these foods when I'm in town. I've always been interested in Milk Bar and I missed my chance in trying it in NYC but I'm glad to see it has it's own place at Cosmo. Milk Bar is in the same space at Momofuku but separate so you can just wlak up and get your desserts. I did a YOLO Vegas move and got the greatest hits, which included 4 of their best selling items: birthday truffles (which came in 3), crack pie slice, compost cookie, and a cereal milk soft serve ice cream. I ate the ice cream right away and ate the others slowly in the coming days. The cereal milk ice cream had a great salty and sweet flavor. I am pretty sure that Afters Ice Cream (based in Orange County in CA) copied this flavor into their traditional non-soft served based ice cream, which is just as great. I really enjoyed this ice cream with the corn flakes. I tried the other desserts little by little, and I wasn't too impressed. The crack pie was good but way too rich and buttery; I would recommend sharing a slice with 2 or even 3 people of the same taste buds. The compost cookie had more of a coffee flavor which I wasn't too much of a fan of. The birthday truffles were good, but a little too rich as well; I probably could eat half of more truffle in one sitting. Overall, I do think Milk Bar is overrated and overhyped (sorry!) but the ice cream is something I would definitely get again when I visit Cosmo Vegas.

I was too full to truly enjoy dessert after my feast at Momofuku LV, but the soft serve milk and cereal ice cream did taste like milk with corn flakes. I found it not too sweet, and satisfactory. I'd come back for the cookies and the healthier LIFE menu.

Maybe its been too long since i've had momofuku milk bar. the first time i had it was in 2010 in NYC and i fell in love with the crack pie and the cereal milk soft serve. I had raved about it to my bf and convinced him to come. We came here after we ate at the noodle bar and we were sorely disappointed. I got the breakfast cereal quake and it tasted like horolicks, reminded me of a mcd mcflurry. it was thick and similar to ice cream. after a little bit it started tasting bland and overly sweet. maybe the other flavors are better but i wouldn't get this one again. My bf tried the cereal milk soft serve and he actually didn't like it. The consistency was smooth, it was a bit sweet and the corn flakes did nothing for him. He didn't even have half before tossing it out. While i was there i got the compost cookie and im glad that it still taste as great as it did before. i do like that you can try the other various flavors such as lemon blueberry and chocolate chip marshmallow, they were good but not as great as the compost cookie. next time i'm back in vegas, i'm not sure if ill get the soft serve but i'll definitely be back for the cookies! total $40

Had to check out Milk Bar Las Vegas! Since it's inside of the Cosmopolitan, there's plenty of places to sit and enjoy their crack pie soft serve. I bought three of their cute totes to take as souvenirs. Service was great considering how busy it was. I'd go back.

I would legit drive to Vegas just to get a Cereal Milk Milkshake! (Luckily one just opened in LA, so I don't have to - but still!!) I pretty much got everything cereal milk because its SO GOOD. You get the cold, and the sweet, and the salty, and the crunchy, and it all comes together to make magic in your mouth. Definitely preferred the shake over the soft serve. Christina Tosi - girl, you crazy and I love you.

I went to visit after reading the reviews that the milk cereal was the best. I was greatly disappointed. It tasted like sour milk. It was a big let down because it looked so good. Will not be coming again.

I am 100% addicted to the cereal milk soft serve with the crunchy topping. No, really. My first taste of it in New York 2 years ago, sent a friend and I running around the big apple in the wee hours of the night taking multiple trains and walking blocks after blocks through torrential rain, just to get it almost every day we were there. Fast forward to a year later, and they opened one a bit closer to me, in my second home, Vegas. Once again, braving horrible conditions of 110 degree plus weather, and a $7 parking fee, I trucked my ass all the way to the Cosmo from Mandalay Bay and $30 later I had my cereal milk soft serve. They also have a crack pie soft serve, which my friend preferred over the cereal milk. Me, I prefer the original. You can get the soft serve in shake form, which is pretty handy, especially if you are trying to rush back to your car to avoid the parking fee after 1 hour. It's expensive, it's a small serving, and it's worth every penny. That is, if it's your thing. The crack pie, which I also love, tastes a bit stale at the Vegas location. The pie I can do without, especially since it costs something like $10 a slice (ok, more like $6). The cookies are not my favorite. While they are good, they aren't worth the price. The cakes, on the other hand, are definitely worth a try. We ordered a whole birthday cake for my hubby and it was exactly has we hoped it would be. If you like the birthday cake flavor, this is the cake for you. The service from the cashiers is hit or miss. I've had the same, disinterested one several times, and for this price and from a place this popular, I would expect friendlier service. It's borderline rude. I've also had nicer service from other employees, so I can't say it's a consistent problem. All in all, a perfect little place for the Cosmopolitan and it's uber hip and trendy crowd. Especially with Block 16 opening up soon. It fits right in.

My only complaint about Milk Bar is the prices. $4 a cookie is really steep. I read Tosi's books and even made a few of her treats at home. She does use premium ingredients. For example, the butter she uses is $8/lb at Whole Foods. She also uses Valrhona & Callebaut chocolate feves which is typically used by the finest chocolatiers @ 5-star hotels.

I watched Chef's Table and learned about Milk Bar NY. Had no idea there was one in Vegas so when I found this one right next to where we were staying I was excited. I had the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake topping and a piece of crack pie. Neither disappointed! The crack pie is so interesting - the flavor keeps changing with each bite and I never did figure out what's in it. The ice cream was wonderful. I may have to investigate their delivery.
Came here to experience the Christina Tosi enterprise. We had the crack pie, cereal milk ice cream, and a chocolate malt shake. It was all just as delicious as we hoped!

Order the crack pie to satisfy that sweet tooth. It's so delicious and addictive. Milk is located in the Cosmopolitan near Momofuku. It's a walk up dessert bar that has many choices. Didn't get to try the birthday cake, cookies or cereal milk ice cream but definitely going back and trying it when I go back.

Before any Vegas trip, I find it necessary to look to Yelp for any new, must-try foods or desserts that have arrived in Vegas. This most recent trip, Milk seemed like a must-try given that they only have three other locations (NYC, DC, and Toronto). The shop has a small footprint in the Cosmopolitan where real estate must be extremely pricey and for that reason, it's mostly a buy and go, but there's plenty of seating nearby. The menu has lots of options but breaks down pretty simple to cookies, klossies, which are also cookies, cake truffles, cakes and pies, soft serves and shakes, and lastly, buns and breads. If you look on Yelp or Instagram, the go-to is the cereal milk soft serve, which when you break it down is a vanilla soft serve and garnished with corn flakes. It's funny how something so simple can be so tasty and grow a following. If you're visiting from out of town, I suggest going with this menu staple. If you're a coffee lover, you cannot leave without trying their cereal milk affogato, which was made with their vanilla soft serve and topped off with a double espresso shot. Again, simple in its own right, but oh so tasty. If there's anything I could of changed, I would of asked if they could of added corn flakes on to the affogato. If you're with a big party, there are more items on the menu that can be shared such as the infamous Crack Pie or their cookies, but if your by yourself or with your significant other, you can't go wrong with their cereal milk soft serve. Note: Located on the second floor near Eggslut. Ambiance/Decor: N/A Food: 4/5 Service: 3/5 Price: $ Overall: 3/5 Pros: + Simple and straight forward dessert menu + Tasty soft serve concoctions + Delicious affogato + Grab and go storefront + Late hours Cons: - Staff could have been a little more friendly - A bit on the pricey side; $7 for cereal soft serve; and a reasonable $5 for the affogato

Milk Bar in Vegas! This is a small storefront in the Cosmopolitan, located next to the new Momofuku. All the standbys are here, from the cookies to the soft serve. If you've never had a corn cookie, get your ass down there asap and get one. The blueberry and cream cookie is equally amazing. Prices aren't super crazy and that cereal milk soft serve is creamy and heavenly.

This place is located in the Cosmopolitan Hotel right next to Momofuku. My friend told me about this place and I thought I'd give this a try to see what the hype was all about. This place constantly had a line but the workers move pretty quick. Being my first time here, I referred to yelp to help me decide on what Soft serve/dessert I wanted to try and it seemed like their cereal milk soft serve($6) with Frosted Flakes add-on ($1.50)seems the most popular, so I thought I'd give that a try. The soft serve wasn't the best I've had, but it definitely wasn't the worst. I expected a lot more from the soft serve but it just tasted like milk with salty Frosted Flakes. It was something I would try but I wouldn't go out of my way to get it again.

Ordered a crack pie milk shake and a side expresso. I was going to sip the espresso and follow it with the milkshake but laziness got the better of me so I just dumped it in there to form a super powerful, flavorful, milk shake. I'm sure the caffeine content was much higher than your standard coffee milkshake because I'm wired as fuck. The milk shake itself had a nice consistency to it. I couldn't put my finger on what the flavor was, never had crack pie before, but after mixing it with the expresso I could definitely taste a buttery creaminess to it that was artery clogging satisfaction. Order up.

I've always wanted to try Milk Bar and luckily one opened up on the west coast! Make sure to ask for samples of their famous soft serve since there's 3 flavors you can choose from (Cereal Milk, Fruity Cereal Milk, and Crack Pie). I unfortunately found out about the samples after we ordered the classic Cereal Milk but I actually liked the Fruity one the most. The Soft Serve really does taste like milk! I liked the texture the cornflakes added but my boyfriend didn't. It was a nice dessert but I can't justify $6 for a cup of ice cream again. We also got 3 cookies (Corn, Compost, and Cornflakes Chocolate Chip Marshmallow cookie) for $8 and a slice of Crack Pie for $6. - Corn Cookie - I loved the soft, chewy texture of the cookie but I found the smell of corn too overwhelming for me to finish the cookie ): - Compost Cookie - it's selling point is a mix of salty and sweet but I don't remember it being such a great mix. It was a delicious cookie though and has the consistency of an oatmeal cookie. - Crack Pie - This was my favorite item to eat. Soft goodness with a perfect amount of sweet filling and a crispy oat crust. My huge complaint about this though was that it's such a tiny slice for $6!! I could buy so much more with that money elsewhere. I think Milk Bar is something you gotta try once for the hype and move on with your life. It's too ridiculously priced for me and I think would be worthwhile if the dessert were half the price!

3 stars for the milk quake and crack pie that I also got. They were really sweet and a little too much for me. I must say however, that the cereal milk soft serve ice cream was freaking amazing. To some it may seem like a normal bland ice cream but I thought it was fantastic. It was light and had a good texture..wasn't too sweet so it was easy to eat. The corn flakes were salty which balanced the whole thing really well. Being a self proclaimed ice cream connoisseur, i am 100% a fan of this ice cream. And my fiance that doesn't ever eat dessert or sweets thought it was super good too.

Excited to come here & wanted to try everything but I opted for the famous crack pie, it was way smaller than I thought & wasn't fresh it was prepackaged. The cookie was good but not mind blowing. The soft serves were ok but honestly they were way TOO SWEET for our liking. My daughter did not even want to finish it because it was too sweet & that is a big deal since kids love all things sweet. All in all I think my $30 could have been spent elsewhere!

I thought this place was all hype, but it's definitely one of the few that lives up to it! We came back several times during our Vegas trip and got cereal milk with corn flakes soft serve every time. SO GOOD!!!!!!!! Not only is it coated with the corn flakes at the top but also at the bottom of the ice cream. I knocked off one star because I was able to try 3 of the cookies (blueberry, compost, & chocolate chocolate), I'm not sure if I got a bad batch or it's suppose to taste as salty as they all were. Also, please do yourself a favor & try the crack pie. You will not be disappointed.

I was so pumped to learn Milk Bar was in our resort! I ordered the milk bar pie a la mode. It was delicious! The ice cream really did taste like cereal milk! It was strange and tasty at the same time. I also ordered the strawberry lemon cake truffles. While they tasted great, they were too rich for my liking. The line was crazy long, but service was fast and organized.

The confetti cookies are unreal, so good I think everyone should try them at least once in their life. The cake truffles are so amazing also, the ice cream was alright. I wish there was one I of these closer to me so I could go every day

OMG! Soooo good! Hot and tired from walking the strip? Swing through the Cosmopolitan Hotel and stop by Milk Bar. You have to get a cereal milk soft serve. I got cereal milk with corn flakes. It was awesome! My wife had the compost cookie with hot fudge. It did not disappoint. The best part was just as we thought we were full we found additional toppings at the bottom of our cups...we just couldn't help but to eat it all. Refreshing, not just because we were hot and the ice cream was cool, but because the flavors were amazing. Next visit need to try the cookies and amazing looking cake slices.

Fun, unique desserts if a bit pricey. One night after visiting Secret Pizza we tried the B'Day Milkquake ($10) - this was the better of the items we sampled. It's their Cereal Milk soft serve with birthday cake mixers stirred in. Easily feeds two. This alone will bring me back. On a later visit, we also tried single servings of their birthday cake soft serve ($6) and while good, seemed pricey for what you got and just didn't compare to the B'Day Milkquake. Seating can be a challenge late night (they don't have their own dedicated space) and if you need a sugar fix after visiting Secret Pizza, make sure you pay attention to closing times as Milk Bar closes first.
Got the 'Compost cookie' here and it really tastes like the name. The cookie was stale and over-salted. Also very crumbly.

I have a HUGE sweet tooth, so I was looking forward to some good dessert, but unfortunately this fell far short of expectations. This review is based on the cookies and cake balls. First of all, the cookies are packaged. Based on that plus how they tasted, they definitely don't seem baked fresh. The cookies had a stale and/or freezer burnt taste. They also tasted oddly bland. I couldn't even finish it because it just wasn't enjoyable. As for the cake balls, they came out so cold that they were pretty much frozen which, again, makes me think they're not baked fresh. When I bit into it, all I tasted was pure sugar and nothing else. Also the inside is extremely dense. It doesn't even taste like cake. The texture was almost like a thick paste. Maybe that's what happens when you freeze cake and then it thaws? I really wanted to like this place considering I love dessert and I'm a fan of both David Chang and Christina Tosi, but the product does not stack up at all to the hype.

The cake is good but the frosting was a little much for my liking. Don't think it's worth $14 a slice. The boozy shakes are so worth it. They are super strong so be careful. They can be pricey but what isn't in Vegas.

Very nice location on the 2nd floor of the Cosmopolitan hotel. I was so happy to see the ad while at the Cosmo pool and even more so because I was actually contemplating paying $63 for a small cake to get shipped to me from New York. I opted for the slice of confetti cake and boy was I disappointed! $16 for a small slice of dry, crumbly cake with no flavor! I expected it to be stellar based on all the hype but maybe this was an old cake and I got a bad slice. I would not go back but glad I got to experience milk in Vegas.

Confetti Cake!!!!!!!! First, I want to make it clear that I'm not a cake person, BUT this cake is to die for. It was sooo damn good I didn't even have a moment to take a picture of it. It has magical crunchies inside every bite. It was nothing like I ever expected. 10/10 I would recommend to everyone and their mothers. It was so yummy I came back the next day to try the strawberry short cake and once again I was blown away.

I've had Milk's cookies from New York before and thought they were pretty good but I was so excited to try the soft serve ice creams. Located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, right next door to Momofoku, Milk Bar is hard not to miss with their bright signage. We came here on a Friday night and surprisingly the line was short with about 4 people ahead of us. My cousin and I both got the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch. I also got cookies to take home to my son. Honestly, the cereal milk soft serve tasted like milk that had gone bad. And, it did not mix well with the saltiness of the cornflakes. The cornflakes were much harder than an average cornflake, it was more like hard granola and it was put on the top and the bottom of the soft serve. I got tired of it real quick! After three bites, both my cousin and I threw it out. What a waste of money - for $7.50 each, we should have just shared one. It was really disappointing . . . As for the pre-packaged cookies, it's also pricey - $4 each or 6 for $22. I ended up buying 6 and a tin to store them in. The corn cookie was my fav - not too sweet and as buttery as the other flavors. My son hated all the flavors so that was also a waste of money. Totally underwhelmed - maybe it tastes better in New York, but here in Vegas its NOT worth the hype.

The gluten free birthday cake truffles are ridiculous. Stopped by to pick some up, and was able to grab a few 3 packs. Service was fast and friendly. The cake bites are honestly perfect. They're soft and cake-y without being crumbly or having that "gluten-free" taste. No mealy, pasty texture. They're perfect, and it was too easy to get them.

I went here last year in June and look forward to going back this April for my birthday. I've had lots of cookies, cereal milk soft serve, and the cereal milk latte. Personally, I love the aesthetic of this place and the theme within the food (And Miss Tosi!). The cookies last awhile so if you're visiting Vegas they'll travel home fine. The cereal milk reminds me a lot of my childhood so I love getting it whenever I'm there (gotta add the crunch!). My favorite cookie is the corn cookie, and you have to try the crack pie. It's one of my favorite desserts.

Milk Bar has really good cake and the slices are enough for two people. They were really moist and fresh. I didn't have to wait in line long it took about 5 minutes. All the employees were really nice and it's in a great location.

This is a review for their shipped cookies. We had a great friend ship some to us and unfortunately, they were some of the worst cookies I've ever had. It was so dry, unflavorful, and just straight whack give me chips ahoy over this any day (not even exaggerating). I'm sure it's better fresh and from the store but come on. If you're gonna offer them shipped, at least try and make sure they are somewhat okay.

Wow. So disappointing. I'd heard so much about the birthday cake so I decided to get a slice with my cappuccino tonight. First, the cappuccino was bad. It tasted like something they'd serve at a Denny's or TGIFridays. Next, $14 for a slice of cake?! Wtf. If it's going to cost that much, it better be the best damn cake I've ever had in my life. Sadly, it was not. The birthday cake was super average. Maybe even a bit below average.

We wanted a pick-me-up after enjoying a delicious lunch at Momofuku, so we got an affogato next door. The cereal milk soft serve pairs perfectly with the rich espresso and tasted even better when all mixed together. I would recommend getting the cereal milk flavor over the crack pie, since the latter is pretty sweet and wouldn't go as well with the espresso. It made for a delicious treat and gave us the extra caffeine boost we needed!
This place was a nice place to try but it's nothing special, especially for it's price. I probably prefer cold stone more than here.

I don't understand the hype or the line for this place. Wanted some late night dessert, and was intrigued by the concept of a $15 milkshake (like how John Travolta's character in "Pulp Fiction" wanted to taste Uma Thurman's $5 shake). These are "fancy shakes" because they have alcohol in them. Great! I like alcohol and sweets! None of the shake combos sounded like what I wanted, so I asked if they could make a peppermint bark shake with the creme de menthe and creme de cocoa they use in their fancy hot chocolates. Nope. They can't. I really don't know why this would be a problem--they have all of the ingredients right there. There was no line, so it's not like this experiment would cause a back up. So anyway, now I've got peppermint bark on my mind so I forgo the alcohol and get a peppermint bark milkquake. It was okay. Very minty and not enough chocolate for it to really seem like peppermint bark. And why are there pretzels in it?! (I specifically ordered the peppermint bark version and not the peppermint pretzel version because that doesn't sound like a good combo to me, and I was right) I also got a compost cookie because I looooove cookies with lots of stuff in them. I had it warmed up, and it was dry and crumbly, with not enough contrast between the different elements in it. That was really disappointing--especially after paying $4 for it. Didn't finish it. All I can figure is people these days must not bake themselves, or their mamas don't bake. Because I don't know why else anyone would be impressed by this.

Not sure what all the hype was about as I didn't think this place was any good. I came here as my brides maids wanted to come and check it out and I ordered the crack pie ice cream and it was okay. I didn't want to try the milk flavor or whatever as I'm not a big fan of left over milk from my cereal. Pretty pricey. I probably wouldn't come back or even recommend this place to anyone.

One of the reasons I wanted to come to Vegas was to try Milk Bar, so I was not going to leave this town without stopping here. On the last day of our trip, we made this important stop for breakfast. As soon as I saw the menu I wanted to eat one of each, but I had to compose myself and pick a few things off rather than the entire store. After a very hard decision, I went for their famous Cereal Milk Soft Serve with Crunch Cereal topping and a slice of their Crack Pie. I was already expecting great things from this place, but I was not expecting such perfect flavors. The Cereal Milk ice cream was seriously one of the yummiest Ice creams I have ever had, and because of it, I will never look at cereal and milk the same. I think the Crack Pie was really made with crack additives because it was addictive! Technically, my husband ordered the pie for him, but in reality I ate most of it. I have no idea what it's made out of, but it's flaky, sweet, and it melts in your mouth all at the same time. I am so happy I made it here and this will def be a preferred spot next time I come to Vegas.

UPDATE: I visited Milk bar again and had a better experience. It still seems too expensive but I had the crack pie soft serve with corn flake crunchies this time and it was really yummy!! I also sampled the cereal milk soft serve. It was definitely different than last time. Tasted a lot better! ---- I was really excited to try this. I have watched the chef's table episode about this place and thought it looked so good. Unfortunately it just didn't live up to the hype. The cereal milk soft serve was too cereal-y if that makes sense. I think it should be more subtle. This was the biggest disappointment. I didn't like it very much. Besides that, I DID really like the crack pie and we went back for another the next day. I'm bummed their prices are so high. $6 for a small soft serve? $6.50 for one slice of crack pie? I bake and I know these ingredients are not pricey or extremely difficult to make. The prices need to come down.
The chocolate malt cake balls are incredible and very reasonably priced. We got the cornflake cookie as well and loved it.
Aside from their crack pje, you should try their Chocolate Malt Shake. Super rich with chocolate milkshake. The bottom has a chocolate fudge that makes every sip tastes like heaven!

Not sure why this place has several bad reviews. It has offers a pretty simple, straight forward menu. Given the cookies are pre-packaged set your expectations accordingly. Ordered a chai tea latte and was pleased. Additionally, they were willing to add flavoring if it wasn't to my liking. Not terribly priced. Give it a try when looking to satisfy your sweet tooth. I suggest the corn cookie!

WHEN YOU HAVE THOSE SWEET CRAVINGS (Warning: Young adult from Central Florida in for vacation) The Cookies, Crack Pie, and Coffee all fell to my cravings- sadly since these snacks were just to top off a meal, I had no room for the (very cool and crazy looking) Milkshakes... which can be made boozy! COMPOST COOKIES- NAME SAYS IT ALL ... and I also took a Cornflake Cookie. With ingredients like Coffee, Potato Chips, or Cornflakes, the end result was actually more like a 'more complicated' Chocolate Chip Cookie. I barely (if at all) tasted those weird ingredients individually so it was a bit of a miss. The best part were the bursts of salt from the Pretzels or Cornflakes. I also enjoyed the changed texture, ore similar to a soft (but not gooey) Oatmeal Cookie. IT IS ALL IT'S 'CRACKED' UP TO BE? The Crack Pie was a decent dessert. I liked the butterscotch flavor a lot- something I don't see in many pies. But the hard texture and strange way of serving it (packaging it in a cardboard, roundish box) were curiosities. Overall, this place is a bit pricey... but I also know you're paying for Strip resort prices. Keep in mind there's no seating here- just a walk up counter.

I have read most of the owners recipes and have only attempted to make crack pies, which pales in comparison to the real thing. While the service was sub par the crack pie was delicious! Buttery, sweet, smooth and crunchy all in one bite. We also ordered the cake truffles which were amazing and I have contemplated shipping them to my house. If you're in the area looking for dessert make your way to Milk bar, they have a variety of options for every sweet tooth!

Wanted to try this place out since there was one at the cosmo and was craving ice cream!The employees were so friendly!The girl that helped me asked if I've ever tried their ice cream before I chose one and I said no,so she gave me samples of the cereal milk or fruity crunch.I liked the fruity crunch so I got that in a cup.It was really good! They put a layer of cereal on the bottom of the cup,then coated the sides with more cereal.It was just a lot for me so I ended up throwing half away I also got the chocolate chocolate cookie but I haven't had it just yet.

Stopped by this place as everyone is always talking about it. They offer samples of whatever they have so you can definitely taste before you commit. It's good but not as amazing as everyone made it seem. They do have unique flavors. And it's convenient when you crave dessert while in the Cosmo hotel.

Cracked pie 'butter' be good! I must say it is delcious. Im every bite, you can taste a hint of salty-buttery pie! I love the oat crust; it has a hint of sweetness to it. This pie is on crack, one slice will satisfy your imagination.

I usually come here to just buy the cookies. But this time I decided to try some of their other desserts. Got 6 cookies (in a tin can is $12), crack pie, and the cereal milk soft serve. My favorite cookies are the blueberry and cornflake ones. Crack pie was $6.50 and it's super small. Smaller than your McDonald's apple pie. It was very rich and I felt like I was eating a stick of butter. The cereal milk soft serve is $6 just for the ice cream and adding on cornflakes is another $0.50. It tasted like plain vanilla ice cream with buttery/salty cornflakes. Pretty pricey for just a basic cup of vanilla ice cream if you ask me. The cookies make up for these other two items. Probably will just stick to getting cookies since the other things on the menu have too much butter in them.

The hype is UNREAL! I would like to start off with saying I love cake. All kinds of cake and my kids are a big fan of shakes and ice cream. We ordered 3 items making our total a little under $40 The birthday cake shake is so plain and flat and tasteless. Also it was not picture worthy. Secondly the ice cream, glad we took samples of all and we settled on the chocolate pretzel as the other two were pretty bad, especially the cereal milk one. And lastly the cake was sold out which gave us a feeling that it was that good. We were offered a chance to wait an hour to get a slice and we agreed. About 5 minutes later they let us know they actually had a slice available. We came back to our hotel excited to enjoy our cake and wow what a disappointment. It was cold,dry, hard and just bleh in flavor. I cannot believe they charge $14+ for a single slice of cake. You'd think they would make quality dessert to have customers coming back regardless of price.

EDIT- I came back to try something new at Milk Bar the other day because maybe I'm limiting my review on just Klossies (see review below). Caroline reached out and offered me to come back to try some other treats, and I honestly couldn't resist. I tried the fruit loop soft serve w/ cornflakes and the birthday truffles. The soft serve was pretty generous, and it tasted just like the cereal milk from a bowl fruity loops. The cornflakes were a little salty and crunchy which was great with the sweet soft serve. The birthday cake truffles come refrigerated but they aren't super cold. Maybe it's because I waited a bit to try them. They're the bees knees, so if you stop by, I'd definitely try the truffles! The customer service for me was great both times I stopped by, so no complaints here. Both times, the staff were very inviting and professional, so it makes me want to come back again for them. The drive still sucks if you're going to the strip during peak hours. Don't try to navigate the strip on friday and Saturday nights or during rush hour. It'll be a bit of a while to get through the traffic. Tldr- great service, try the truffles and maybe the fruit loop soft serve if you want to treat yo self. Driving here and parking still sucks, but I guess it's just something I'll have to accept about the strip. OG REVIEW- I've always wanted to try Momofuku's Milk Bar ever since I was in New York and saw that the line was way too long to stick around. Must be something that's good there right?! Ehhh, i'm low-key disappointed... and by low-key, i'm not just low-key disappointed.. I'm straight up disappointed. I got the perfect 10 and the coco klossies. For those of you who aren't familiar with what these are, they're the vegan cookies made/endorsed by Karlie Kloss, the model. The cookies were about $3-4 a cookie, and they aren't bad but they aren't definitely worth it for the price. They cost too much for just 1 cookie. If they were maybe $2 a cookie, I'd be more inclined to make the trek to the strip, sit in traffic, navigate the Cosmo's awful parking, and buy these cookies. The cookies themselves are slightly dense and very flavorful which saves these cookies. So all in all, the klossies are great cookies but definitely not worth it for the price and the annoyance of getting my butt through the traffic/headache that is the strip. If i'm already in Cosmo, then yeah, I'll probably go back but I wouldn't go to Cosmo solely to try their treats.

Rating: 3.5 I'm a big fan of David Chang and I've been wanting to try Milk Bar ever since watching a video of Christina Tosi making her famous birthday cake. Milk Bar is located at the Cosmopolitan near the Chandelier. It's pretty awesome that a location has opened in Vegas and that it's open until 2am. Unknowingly, we ordered all of the "greatest hits" which include a compost cookie, a slice of crack pie, 3 birthday cake truffles, and cereal milk soft serve which totals to $21. In addition, we got a bottle of cereal milk. Cereal milk is so yummy and it tastes like childhood. I appreciate that it's not overpoweringly sweet. However, I feel like it's just something I can make at home and I would never think about spending another $6 to try again. Cereal milk soft serve was just as good and not too sweet. The corn flakes offered a great contrast to the creamy soft serve. Even though we only ordered 1 soft serve, the cashier gave us 2 because he thought we waited to long for our soft serve! I don't even remember waiting for more than 5-10 minutes. I've tried all the flavors of cookies the offer and blueberry and cream is by far my favorite. Yeah, I'm raving about Milk Bar, but why am I giving it only 3.5 stars? The price! It's way overpriced, which is expected since it's a touristy area, but come on. $3 of a small thin cookie? $6.50 for a tiny slice of pie? $6 for a bottle of cereal milk? Too expensive. Also, I wish they had chairs and tables so you can enjoy your desserts there. It's not really ideal trying to eat your soft serve walking through a sea of people on the strip.

A friend gifted me some Milk Bar Birthday Cake balls a few years ago and it's basically been my fave food ever since. I was hoping to stop by the NYC outpost when I was there but unfortunately didn't end up making it during that whirlwind trip. I made my friend come here after we ate next door at Momofuku, even though she was, 'too full', it didn't stop her from enjoying one of my birthday cake balls from the three pack. My friend offered up her opinion on the crack pie, which was to definitely get it as it's what they're known for. I got a single slice and it was darn good but I def favor the birthday cake balls, hands down. Those are the best dessert ever (sorry, nothing bundt cakes- you're second tho). We also tried the crack pie soft serve since we got lucky and there was no line. It tasted just like the crack pie, tho I don't know that I'd ever want to eat that much of it in one sitting. My go-to is def the birthday cake balls and I don't see that changing in the foreseeable future but I'd def be open to going back and trying more... or just ordering a few dozen of the balls.

I tried the fruity cereal milk soft serve and it was alright. It literally tasted like fruit loops and milk. It was worth trying once, but not worth a repeat visit as I would spend the same amount of money on some quality gelato instead.
Yummy icecream, i tried the cereal icecream it was cold and delicious. My husband tried the red velvet with brownies on top, he liked it a lot to the point that he finished it in a couple of minutes.

The cookies, cakes and cereal milk soft serve are to die for at this window kiosk establishment. Lines can be long and it is sometimes difficult to read the menu and specials with so many people around. But the desserts are decadent!

Stopped by to try the cereal milk and cookies. Maybe it was an off day but the texture of the cereal milk soft serve wasn't smooth but more airy like a mousse. The flavor was on point and tasted the same from nyc milk bars though. Some of the cookies also tasted dry and stale :(( Service was good though and staff offered samples.
Nom nom nom - we always stop here for treats. Cookies are just the right amount of chewy and the flavors are unique. Cake truffles are yummy, too. And the people working there are always nice.

I got this cake my daughter's birthday because she requested it because of the reputation of these cakes for being off the hook so obviously I'm very pissed because I paid $50 for a tiny ass cake that tastes like any cake that I could have gotten from the supermarket, nothing more. in fact it was a lot drier than nothing bundt cakes. Which cost less. Never again!

I was a little disappointed after finally trying this place. I got the Crack Pie and the cereal milk Soft Serve, both of which were just okay to me. I was hoping the crack pie would have me hooked as any name with "crack" in it should but... it did not live up the hype. I like when desserts aren't that sweet, so I was expecting to like these -- they weren't bad, but I wouldn't spend money on them again.

I love Milk Bar in NYC. This is the closest Milk Bar to me in the Bay Area, and it's so far!!! I fell in love with Compost Cookies about 5+ years ago when trying them in NYC. They are so delicious! I have to say while the cookies are still good, I feel like maybe the recipe has changed a little. My go to item now is a slice of the birthday cake! Ohhhhh mannn!! It is not too sweet. It is moist. Good ratio of cake to frosting. Then there's these crunchy bits scattered around. It's not cheap. Get a slice, get some milk somewhere, and get a sugar rush for sure! I also love that Milk Bar is opened late, as I always have a craving for sweets in the form of cookies and cakes at night.

I went to the new Milk in Vegas after hearing the hype and I must say it wasn't worth it at all. I got the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes and it didn't taste like anything at all. I ate the whole thing and felt like I ate a cone of air. There was zero flavor - you could hardly call that cereal milk. I also sampled the sweet potato pie soft serve, and while it had a lot of flavor, it didn't exactly taste like sweet potato pie. There was something a little off about it. The only thing it was good for was a cute photo of the ice cream in front of the neon sign. Milk is definitely all hype, overpriced, and not worth it.

Christina Tosi's creations are fun, a little whimsical and very much out of the ordinary. From her compost cookie to her crack pie, her creations are fun to try because there's just no way I would have thought to put those flavors together!
