That being said, perhaps my favorite of all the things on her menu is the cereal milkshake. It is the best ever. Ask for it with cornflakes - you won't be sorry. It is so simple - milk soaked in cereal and made into ice cream (well, it's a bit more complicated than that). If you like crunchy soft, sweet cookies, her compost cookie is a must try. I myself found it a bit too sweet but I did still enjoy it. The best time to come here is right after some grub at Momofuku. Milkbar is a great way to end a great meal. There's no seating at Milkbar, just a booth and a line - or not (if you're lucky). If you have a sweet tooth and want something fun and unexpected, try this place. You won't be sorry. If you want boozy sweets then this is also a great place for you. Their version of a White Russian blew my head off.

What can I say about Milk Bar that hasn't been said before. If you are a sweets person(yes you) then head over and go crazy. The compost cookie is the best cookie you will ever eat. Like cake? Elvis baby!
Momofuku milk bar inside the cosmo. I would stick to the crack pie. The cereal milk soft serve and milkshake just taste like plain milk.

Love me some Milk Bar. If you haven't watched the documentary about Christina Tosi on Netflix, your missing out. My husband and I always get the cereal milk ice cream with cornflakes, it will blow your mind. This will nostalgically take you back to your childhood days of drinking all the milk after eating your cereal. The crack pie, is just that, it's like crack, one bite and you want more and more. I have had the birthday cake truffles, not a fan and the birthday cake, cake I had was a tad dry for me. Which is why I'm giving it 4/5.

The aesthetic of the place is super cute and the line was not long. I got a cookie and a shake but they didn't really excite me. However, my husband really enjoyed the birthday cake shake, if you are a fan of birthday cake flavor I recommend it.

I had to try it all! I got the fruity pebble shake which was super yummy and it was so cool that they got clumps of cereal to stay crunchy in the ice cream. I got the cereal, chocolate, marshmallow cookie which I can't wait to try and duplicate. And of course I had to get to get a slice of the crack pie, which did not disappoint.

I'm a devote Milk Bar fan. Last weekend during a visit to Las Vegas I had to stop by the store twice. Both times the experience was wonderful and the treats were delicious. On Saturday night (12/1/18) my friend and I came by for dessert. When we got to the counter we were greeted by Candice who patiently helped us decide on what to order, she offered helpful suggestions. There was a line of people behind us but she treated us like we were the only customers, just as she had to the people before and after us. If I lived in Las Vegas I'd want Candice to be my friend. Thank you for adding to the great time.

It is worth a try if youre in the cosmopolitan but it is quite pricy for what you get! The cereal milk ice cream was pretty good and ive never really had ice cream like it before. I really liked how it wasnt too overpowering yet had a nice smooth flavor. The crunchy cereal is definitely a good addition to it. I also ordered the crack pie due to all the good reviews but thought it was way too sweet. Would definitely pass on the pie if you arent a huge sweets person.

I've been wanting to try this ever since our friends were raving about it, I thought it was a bit over rated and I said oh it's just another soft serve vanilla ice cream but Noooooooooo, as soon as you taste it, it's literally like eating cereal and milk! It's not too overly sweet and doesn't have any after taste! I kept eating here like 4 times a week, I didn't know I could do that, usually I get sick of too much dairy. I really am satisfied with this place! It also has so many other things, like crack pie and the birthday cake, they also have gluten free options which I loved coz I'm also gluten free! The crack pie is phenomenal, it's a buttery brown sugar crust, very yummy! It's so good! I had to come for more again for 4 days straight since we were in Vegas, also the birthday cake is this white cake with sprinkles on top! It's also not overly sweet which is good coz you really taste the cake! This is a must try for everyone and kids will love it too! Wish they had one in seattle though! Wishful thinking!

Cereal. Milk. Soft. Serve. Oh, and more dessert. Fan of the milk that Frosted Flakes leaves? Try the cereal milk. Or for Fruity Pebbles enthusiasts? Fruity cereal milk is your go to. Butterscotch lover? Crack pie is the way to go. I was honestly more excited to try out their soft serve flavors than anything else due to the high prices. $14 for a slice of a birthday cake seemed like a steep price for Funfetti but man, was that good cake. Cookies? I'd skip on this next time. Too expensive. I'll go to McDonald's.

My go-to order for this place would be the milk and cereal soft serve with added corn flakes. I tried this place once already on the grand opening day for their newly opened Los Angeles location. I was in Vegas and was in the mood for something sweet. I headed over to the Cosmopolitan and easily spotted Milk because of their bright lighted sign. The saltiness and crunchiness of the cornflakes compliment the soft serve perfectly. I would want to come more often but the price is a tad high considering that it's hard to imagine ordering the milk and cereal soft serve ($7) without the added corn flakes ($1.25). Another honorable mention would be that the workers were extremely friendly and were all smiles. Thumbs up for friendly service!

Been here twice before. Both times I got the crack pie which I would get again if I'm in the area and feel the need to indulge :) The crack pie has a nice buttery, sweet, salty taste to it though after a few bites, it gets too sweet for me so I usually save the rest to finish later. I also tried the birthday cake truffle and that was just way too sweet for me. Like it's I-can-feel-a-cavity-forming sweet. The price is steep for what you get. It's $6.50 for 1 small slice of crack pie and $6.50 for 3 truffles. But it is in the Cosmo so I can see why the prices are what they are.

Came here for an iced cereal milk latte and slice of birthday cake. A lot of photos of the menu on here don't show it, but you can get a slice of cake for $14. It also doesn't show that you can get iced lattes, but you can so that is exciting! I got a 16 oz latte which they told me has 4 shots of espresso. So just FYI. The cashiers was super friendly, which is always nice. I went right after they opened and there was no one there.

I was really looking forward to trying Milk Bar, but to my dismay, it really wasn't that great. It's not even that the prices are ridiculous or anything; the sweets just didn't live up to the hype. When we went around 1:30pm on a Sunday, there was about 10 people in line and it didn't take too long to get to the counter. They ran out of a few of the popular cookies so we ended up getting the crack pie, corn cookie, blueberry and cream cookie, birthday cake truffles, and the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch. The crack pie was way too sweet for my taste, though I enjoyed the consistency of the pie.. The blueberry and cream cookie was kind of oily, and the corn cookie was pretty good. I only had a bite of the soft serve because I was so full, but my first impression was slight disappointment and that I've had better. So all in all, I may have expected too much, but it was simply a mediocre experience.
We bought four dozens for friends and family! My favorite is the confetti cookie! Their peppermint holiday cookie was amazing as well, just slightly more sweet, but it was great!

This place has tasty items but they are extremely expensive. I totally believe you get what you paid for but this is extreme. $17 for a slice of cake with taxes. The lease at the Cosmopolitan can't be that high.

Of course whenever I go to Las Vegas (like once a year), I look up all the cool insta-worthy food places to try...LOL. This cute little place is located on the SECOND FLOOR of The Cosmopolitan Las Vegas. I had a bit of trouble locating this, but realizing the arrows on the signs I was able to find it haha. Keep in mind, this place is actually pretty small. The Milk Bar is directly right next to Momofuko which took part in developing this dessert place. I was super super anxious to taste their soft serve (that I've seen in pics on the insta from the NY location) so I could see just HOW good it really is. They serve pies, cookies, drinks (with or without coffee), and of course their soft serve ice cream. Their ice cream is actually pretty pricey starting at around $6-7. You get options for toppings such as fruity pebbles or cereal, chocolate chips, and even sprinkles. But still, pretty pricy. The amount they give you ALMOST makes up for that, but not quite all the way. My sister didn't really find the taste of the cereal soft serve appealing, but for me it was pretty dang good, but not enough to amaze me. Compared to other places I've tried, Milk Bar is definitely up in my Top 4. It's similar to MilkCow in Fremont but a more sharper/unique taste. It's simple yet so interesting and different. I'd give this place 3.8 stars, but rounded up to 4 because it was both aesthetically pleasing and appealing to my tongue.

I was super excited to try Milk Bar as I am a huge Christina Tosi fan and when I heard her talk about this place on Chefs Table it looked super good. On my recent trip to Vegas I decided to check it out and got a crack bar latte, cereal milk latte, bagel ball, and crack pie slice. The crack pie latte was atrociously sweet - after a few sips I got really sick and couldnt drink anymore and had to switch with my BF for his cereal milk latte which was also extremely sweet, but less so. Both did not taste that good and had an over powering sugary taste. Also - the only dairy option they had was whole milk which I never drink and made the latte taste extremely rich...in a bad way. The bagel ball came out really soft and kind of soggy...the bread tasted like it was steamed instead of toasted...gross. The cream cheese they used was also very salty. I finished it, but did not enjoy it. The bantem bagels from starbucks are wayyyy better. The crack pie was decadent and delicious, although very sugary. I did enjoy it a lot, but I don't think I could ever eat a full slice of it! If you are going to come here, I recommend to only get a slice of the crack pie and go somewhere else for regular food and coffee. The decor is really cute and I love their branding, but they really have to work on developing their other menu items to be on par with the other bakeries.

Don't understand all the hype and outrageous prices! Was highly disappointed, soft serve was disgusting, my children didn't even like it. And their kids, what kids would say no thanks? Got myself a slice of cake, over priced, it was dry, we will not stop here again.

Everyone loved the cake!! Excited for the milk bar pie!! Staff was super kind and helpful and line was not to bad! Excited to go back They have lattes too so I'm definitely getting one of those next time!

This is a really fun snack dessert bar inside the cosmopolitan casino next to Momofuku. We went to the Milk Bar in NYC several years ago and was excited to see it in Vegas. We got the crack pie, which was our favorite and also got the milk ice cream. I want to try the "adult" milkshakes next visit. It's definitely something different that isn't available elsewhere.

Delicious and unusual! I got the salted chocolate ice cream with corn flakes - a weird combination, but it worked well together. I wasn't a fan of the coffee milkshake - it was so mildly flavored that the coffee didn't come through, and it mostly tasted of the soft serve - fine, but not interesting, and we didn't want a full glass of it. We ended up throwing most of that away.

I had no idea Milk Bar had a Las Vegas location. I was so excited to come here and it didn't disappoint at all. What an amazing treat! We bought a lineup of all the popular items. You can't go wrong with the soft serve and cookies. Really, you can't go wrong here at all. If you've never experienced a treat from Milk Bar, then get ready for all your 8-year old dreams of sugar and desserts to be released. The customer service was awesome. Special shout out to Precious for making us feel so special.

Don't come here expecting the same light and delicate flavors and sweetness of Asian deserts (head to Suzuya for that). Milk bar is truly American in its sweetness, but done right. Cereal milk soft serve has a hint of malt. I'm a fan of malts, so this worked for me. The cornflakes are a nice touch. If you're into sprinkles, you should just get yourself a slice of birthday cake. I don't usually like birthday cakes, but I loved the birthday cake here. Some folks have mentioned that their slices were dry, but mine was just right. I enjoyed the bits of birthday cake truffle throughout the batter, the milk soak helped moisten the slice, and the frosting was actually pretty good. I'd definitely get this again along with a side of extra birthday cake truffles. This one's huge and should probably be shared. Speaking of sharing - the crack pie is also something to share. If you enjoy caramel or the inside of a pecan pie, you'll like the crack pie. If I was being super indulgent, I'd probably eat the entire slice myself. The corn cookie (warmed up) is a nice mix of sweet and savory. Not sure I'd get it again, but it was worth a try. I'll probably try the compost cookie next time. So for me, the birthday cake, birthday cake truffles, and crack pie are tops. I'd get those again with a coffee or tea anytime I'm in Vegas. If you're not afraid of sweet, enjoy the occasional treat, and don't mind Vegas prices, then you'll likely enjoy this place.

I haven't had the original location in NYC to compare but I really did enjoy the cookies at Milk Bar. I got their greatest hits combo which comes with their most famous compost cookie, a slice of crack pie, birthday truffles, and cereal milk soft serve. Pros: Cookies: After taking a bite of the Compost Cookie, I said to myself "that's a damn good cookie!!!" I was so happy with the compost cookie that I went back to grab other flavors to try out. The cookie itself is chewy and ultra rich so I recommend having a non-sweetened beverage for pairing. Crack Pie: It was a bit too sugary at first but I did enjoy the buttery and smooth filling with a little bit of saltiness lingering around. Cons Soft Serve: Tried both the cereal milk soft serve and crack pie soft serve which was way too sugary for my taste. I only had a couple of spoonfuls before I got sick of the overly sweetened taste. The corn flake crunch topping did help make the soft serve taste better by adding crunchy and salty flavors. Birthday Truffles: Was not pleased with these overpriced truffles since it tasted exactly like cookie dough but sweeter and more doughy. I was fortunate to have an unsweetened cold brew coffee next to me while I was consuming these truffles because they just stuck to my mouth.
It was okay! flavor of soft serve was interesting maybe just not my thing. Bummed to see employees serve others that order after and some of us where still waiting for our orders.

Aesthetically pleasing.. The shop is super cute and all of the workers were extremely friendly and fast with cranking out orders. We finished up dinner at Momofuku and decided to grab something sweet. I got the Crackpie Soft serve with Cornflakes and the rest of the girls got Cookies and pies, one even got the Crackpie Shake. Super messy, I kept dropping Cornflakes all over the Cosmopolitan floor but that's not their fault, it's soft serve.. it melts. The other thing is it was super salty! like after a few bites I had to toss it. I'm not sure if it was supposed to taste like that or if it were too rich for my taste buds but I couldn't finish. My friend with the shake was good after a few sips.. seemed like a waste. I did also grab a few cookies to take home and those were a big hit. All in all it was good try. I'm just not sure i'd order the same thing, or i'd split it with someone one. Worth giving it a try.

Went to Milk Bar after eating at Momofuku in Las Vegas. Was excited to after seeing in on TV and how she got started in David Chang's kitchen. We got the layered confetti cake and 3 cookies. Cookies were great but the cake was frozen and then defrosted, you could tell. Taste was okay but the moistness and freshness was not there. I so wanted to love this because of the owners story and creativeness but walked away not impressed. I'd rather go to the local Nothin' Bundt Cakes in my area as they are always fresh and moist. Or at least they have figured out how keeps things fresher if they had to freeze them. Overall just okay and not worth a return trip.

I think I had high expectations for this place due to the hype. I was really looking forward to trying their cereal ice cream. I had a sample before committing to buying and it didn't taste good. They use corn flakes when I think they should use Frosted Flakes. Usually ice cream is sweet but this one was not. The cookies I felt were good but not great, my favorite was the blueberry one. Overall, I say try this place once if you can't make it to New York to try the original.

Unique flavors and dessert options, I've never seen alcoholic milkshakes before. The fruity cereal was enjoyable and creamy but $6+ for an ice cream is expensive. Stop by if you have the time but not a must see spot.

I had it in NY and was eager to retry it. But the price really threw me off when I wanted the milk/cereal soft serve and then when you add toppings; it ends up being pricy for a simple piece of ice cream. It was still good, and corn flakes as a topping is the way to go, not sprinkles. Still, wouldn't go out of my way for it knowing this.

Had to check it out after seeing chef's table. I really don't like says very much but I have to say the cereal milk ice cream and crack pie were better than they were on the small screen. You know when you watch a food show and wish that you could taste it, well now you can. I fell in love with the cereal milk ice cream. The salty corn flakes they add to the side add a much needed break from an overbearing sugar rush. Deff brings you back to being a kid eating cereal but more refined. And for you alcoholics like me they also make a cereal milk white Russians. Just take my money

Service was fast - order in, order out. We ordered the fruity cereal milk soft serve with added cornflake crunch and a slice of crack pie. The soft serve was creamy and tasted exactly as described but wasn't overly sweet. But, the added cornflake crunch was not what I'd expected. It had a saltiness to it that didn't really mesh well with the soft serve. We ended up scraping it off. Now, the crack pie. Ohhhhh, the crack pie. I'm obsessed with it. It reminds me of a pecan pie, without the pecans, but more dense. It was rich but not heavy. You could taste the butter in every bite. My only regret was not getting another slice for the ride home. Crack pie. Just do it.

Disclaimer: this review is only for the ice cream. That being said, I gave it an extra * because I'm only reviewing a portion of their offerings. The milk bar is a walk up dessert shop in the Cosmopolitan. If you stop by at any type of popular time, there's going to be a wait. But to try such unique confections by one of TVs most beloved celebrity chefs (Christina Tosi), it would be worth it, right?? For the ice cream, not so much. Milk has three different flavors--cereal milk, chocolate pretzel, and a fruity cereal milk. I got cereal milk and chocolate pretzel with chocolate topping. A small was ~$6, it wasn't a huge amount for the price, but it would be enough for one or two people to share. Or even 20, because once I had a few bites, I went from being intrigued to really put off. The pros: The consistency is perfect. You can tell its a high quality soft serve. The staff is nice. The cons: The descriptions are 100% what you're getting. The cereal milk ice cream tastes like cereal milk. And not cookie crisp cereal milk, but some kind of cardboard healthy cereal. And the chocolate pretzel was the same--it was extra pretzelly, not enough chocolatey. Overall my biggest problem was there wasn't enough sweetness to it--it really just tasted like creamy versions of the flavors. The chocolate topping, for $1 extra, wasn't hot fudge-y and it wasn't sauce-y, it was weird and almost taffy-like. I wanted to try one of their cake or pie offerings, but they were just way too expensive for me to justify spending on dessert. Next time I'm in Vegas and have a hankering for ice cream, idk where I'll go, but I won't be visiting Milk again.

Foodie bucket list item accomplished! I've always wanted to try this, to say I have a sweet tooth is an understatement! When I got to the milk bar I wanted to try everything, I went with the sampler that came with a slice of its Crack pie, a cereal milk soft serve that was to die for, a compost cookie, and some birthday truffles. I also got a cornflakes chocolate chip cookie as well. The girl at the counter was amazingly nice, she was the bomb . com ! That cereal milk though wow!

Can't believe a Milk Bar opened in Vegas! What an exciting treat to find when browsing the Cosmo. I tried the cereal milk chai tea and it was amazing. So creamy and good! We bought a 3 pack of cookies - corn cookie, blueberry muffin, and chocolate cookies. All of them were great. This is an awesome gem in Vegas especially since the lines at all other locations I've been are very long! Try the ice cream and cookies whenever you can.

Stopped by here after getting some food at Secret Pizza. Got the 3 for $8 packaged cookies and a crack pie soft serve. The soft serve was way too sweet for me and my boyfriend's liking. The flavor isn't anything special either, just a hint of caramel with vanilla. The packaged cookies (Chocolate Chocolate, Compost cookie, Blueberry and Cream) that I took home were pretty good though. I recommend the Blueberry and Cream out of the three. This place is quite pricy for what they have, so I won't be going out of my way to come here.
Expensive?? Well, duh... you're in Vegas. Here's the deal though... nothing is better than milk bar! Period.

I was craving something sweet during my weekend Vegas trip and decided to give this place try. As a first timer, I decided to get a red velvet soft serve (just to play it safe). The worker who took my order told me that it would have a rich and creamy chocolate taste to it which it indeed did. I topped it off with sprinkles since it was such a small serving but it was enough for me since it was super sweet. Only giving it 4 stars since it was a little pricey for such a small serving (paid $8 plus tip). Hoping to try their other flavors during my next Vegas trip!

I loved the cereal milk soft serve! Like when I first heard of it I didn't know what to expect, but when I had it, it literally tasted like the milk you'd have right after you finish eating all the cereal in the bowl. Haha I was so happy because I haven't had that taste in my mouth for a while. It was the perfect amount of sweetness (not too sweet which was perfect, like I didn't want to throw it away I just kept going at it) and I bought it with the corn flakes, so the crunch added texture and made it so pleasant to eat! I'm craving this right now tbh, which is why it has taking me so long to give a review, Staff members were super informative and sweet when I was there. So at that time service was 5/5 :)

Fun flavors! I got the Fruity cereal soft serve and it tasted just like fruity pebbles. Such a nostalgic and fun flavor. It was perfectly sweet and the small portion was just the right size to split between two people. I think it was a bit pricey for soft serve (around $6 or $7, additional $0.50 for topping) but worth a try. Located in the Cosmo on the second floor food court next to Momofuku.
I'm obsessed with milk bar!!! I got the cereal milk soft serve with cereal on top, I loved it so much I wanted it again after I finished it lol.
Cereal milk soft serve is what I usually get here when I'm at the Cosmo. I enjoy every crunch of cereal on my soft serve. It's the perfect combination.
My husband and I just got back from Vegas. We loved this place. The compost cookie milk quake was very salty but the strawberry and corn milk quake is awesome. A must try while in Vegas.

Fast, friendly service. Came specifically for the birthday cake and was gravely disappointed. Smaller and LESS frosting than last year's visit. I expected a little more...Tasty but not worth $14. Maybe next time I'll try the Elvis cake...

This place is new so it's not on the directory in the cosmopolitan but you can just go up the escalator and you will spot it on the left side. It's a little stand like a food court counter. There was a small line when we got there but it went by super fast. I ordered the Fruity Soft Serve with cornflakes and my boyfriend ordered the crack pie milk quake. We also bought 3 cookies. The blueberry and cream, chocolate chocolate, and the marshmallow, cornflakes, and chocolate chip. The Fruity Soft Serve tastes exactly like your leftover milk after a bowl of Fruity Pebbles. It was so yummy to me, and it's pink - so pretty :)! While I loved the ice cream I didn't quite like the cornflakes... they were way too salty and just not very tasty, IMO. The Crack Pie Milk Quake was very sweet... almost too sweet but there are big chunks of crack pie in it and little crumbs in every other bite, which was wonderful! Hated the blueberry and cream cookie! It tasted so weird. I don't know how to explain it... just don't get it! I loved the marshmallow, cornflakes, and chocolate chip cookie. Perfect mixture of sweet and salty. It was soft and chewy. Mmmmm. I still have to try my chocolate chocolate cookie but I have a feeling it will be delicious! I think I'll go back for the Fruity soft serve with a different or no topping next time!!

Birthday truffles. BOMB. Compost cookie. Eh. Their version of a White Russian. WOO. This is like a big kids dream come true. I'm dying to go to the New York location but this will do for now. Located upstairs you'll find it next to Momofuku restaurant and I believe some kind of a juice bar. I panicked and ordered the basic things: Birthday truffles and compost cookie. I also ordered their version of a White Russian. The birthday truffles are BOMB DIGGITTTTYY. So soft and melt in your mouth. Be careful if you don't plan on eating them immediately. Because they are so soft, they can get squished!!! A big fat duh but still. Some people's children y'know?? The compost cookie though... I heard it was good but I am not the biggest fan. It's good but not omg amazing. Their version of a White Russian? Like I said before. WOOOO. Make sure you mix that baby up good before, during, and after you drink it because that alcohol SITS. And boy is it strong. I loved it but it gave me a headache. I cannot wait to go back and try more of their goodies!!

Got the birthday milkquake and it was okay cause the Birthday cake chunks at the bottom of the cup tasted good but the ice cream itself tasted flat and seemed not sweet enough. Presentation wise it looked unappetizing. For $10.83 for a regular size, I probably wouldn't order the milkquake again. The milk soft serve sample I tried reminded me of milk that's been sitting in the refrigerator for too long. Next time I come back I will probably try the cookies.

A trip to Las Vegas without a stop at Milk Bar at the Cosmopolitan is incomplete. I've always want to try award-winning pastry chef Christina Tosi's dessert place. Her creations are so fun, creative and delicious!! She is the creator of the highly addictive cereal milk ice cream, compost cookies and crack pie. The place is super popular and crazy busy day and night. I tried her signature Crack pie and the soft serve ice cream with crunch, which was on top and the bottom of the ice cream. I enjoyed the soft serve, but it was a little sweet for me (not that it stopped me from eating it all). The Crack pie, which has an pat crush with a gooey butter filling, appealed more to my palette as it was less sweet, but equally delicious. I would highly recommend checking out any or all of the sweet treats at Milk Bar. I'm already looking forward to going back in November.

The crack pie itself and the soft serve crack pie with the added corn flakes never fail to satisfy my childhood sweet tooth dessert cravings. I've been to the one in New York before so I was familiar with the menu offerings. Service was quick at this location and staff were friendly. I had the iced crack pie latte too which was also delicious. If you haven't been here, definitely this place is worth making a visit to.
He crack pie is amazing. Imagine eating a buttered piece of brown sugar cooked perfectly. It is a wonderful decadent treat!!

Fits perfectly in the Cosmopolitan! Goes along with the theme of OVERPRICED... *ahem (Eggslut) yeah except for (Holsteins) And who isn't a sucker for Cereal Milk? Shoot, looking at their menu screams all types of lust and temptations. So despite a bunch of discouraging reviews on Yelp, I said, "Nah man, it was probably hyped up, I'll give it a chance..." I mean for $7.50 for soft serve and cornflakes on top? I wasn't impressed, simply because the flavor doesn't match the value(price) And soft serve should be the easiest thing to execute. Glad I didn't get anything more expensive. But the Cake Truffle was DYNOMITE! But for $6 bucks for 3 pieces... It might just have to be a one time thing. I'm a fan of Masterchef and Christina Tosi has a great rep especially in baking... but this is HYPE. The soft serve is not the one and you'll be more satisfied grabbing a shake at Holsteins instead of here. Dining in the Cosmo can burn a hole in a wallet real fast. If you decide you wanna ignore what more people are saying, my tip would be to try and limit yourself and not go crazy and try everything. Its not the worst way to satisfy your sweet tooth, but could be pricey.

I'm not late to try this place out. I'm just late to review them. First of all, I'm not a huge fan of sweets unless it's peanut butter covered with chocolate in a dark brown paper cup and packaged in an orange wrapper. Yes, I have a weakness for Reese's. Where was I? Oh Yeah, Milk Bar. My first experience with Milk Bar was a melted soft serve, Compost cookie, Corn cookie, and the Crack Pie. I didn't think that the soft serve was bad, just expensive and melts way too quick. Their cereal milk soft serve is worth if you're a fan of cereal and milk. I also wasn't too impressed with their cookies and the Crack Pie. Crack is supposed to be addicting. I wasn't addicted and only needed one bite. I was ready to give Milk Bar 3-stars because I thought that everything I tried was just A-Ok. Then it happened. I got a chance to try their Birthday Cake and was blown away. It's hard for me to explain what makes their Birthday Cake so good. Everything from the icing to the buttery taste of the cake is simply just awesome. The cake is small and the price is massive. Take my advice and limit your feeding to just a few bites a day. You can make a whole cake last a whole week doing this. Just don't forget to keep the cake in the fridge. That's what we do when we have Milk Bar's Birthday Cake at home. Best Week Ever!!

You have to get the cereal milk soft serve with extra cereal flakes (sweet and salty?!?! yaaassss!). You will turn over in your grave with regret if you don't try this dessert at least once! I guess my love for this soft serve comes from childhood nostalgia because I've only tasted something like this in Korea when I had cereal milk as a youngin! So freaking good! I also really enjoyed the crack pie and birthday cake!!!

We were staying at the Cosmo but even if we werent, we would have made the trek to try Milk Bar after watching the Netflix special. We tried various menu items: - The BFC - it was very rich but the flavor was well balanced - The perfect 10- this cookie was a little bland but still tasty, would be good dipped in ice cream. -The gluten free cake ball truffles- FAVORITE thing we tried, very flavorful and moist -My boy friend tried the crack pie and said it was okay but did not compare to the cake balls. The next morning we went back to try the fruity cereal milk ice cream and it was very good as well. We topped it with more fruity pebbles and sprinkles and loved that they also put toppings in the bottom of the cup so there was more left when we got to the bottom :)

I ordered a piece of birthday cake - cost with tax was over $15...for dinner one slice. The dessert was entirely too sweet. It was sweet on sweet so that there was not real flavor, just sugar. I did enjoy the few crunchy crumbles in the layers but it was too little. Also, the cake was dry and fell apart making it difficult to eat with the stiff icing. Man, I have terrible luck at Vegas restaurants unless I leave the strip. Wan wah :(

I have seen Milk Bar all over my Instagram feed. They're cups are trendy, the presentation is perfect for your feed (and for feeding). I was delighted when I visited Las Vegas and saw they had a location in the Cosmopolitan. The wannabe Instagram influencer came out in me and was ecstatic to try this cereal + milk ice cream combo. I've never been one to drink the milk at the bottom of my cereal bowl so I was didn't think I was going to enjoy this treat as much as I did. The corn cereal flavor really shined. It was creamy, sweet, and crunchy. A perfect treat for a warm Las Vegas afternoon. I would love to visit Milk Bar's other locations and try more of their creations.

I literally have been wanting to try this place for years. I made their recipe for birthday cake in 2014 and have dreamt of trying their stuff since. The staff is friendly, this review is solely on the food. I got a slice of crack pie and 2 cookies. Everything was meh, not mind blowing. Nothing's baked on site so it's not as good of quality as other bakeries. I microwaved my cookies so they were less hard and stale. The crack pie was decent. Honestly, I'd prefer safeway or sprouts lol. Because while the goods are average tasting, they're quite pricy. If you're able to microwave your cookies, they'll be a lot better, if not the cookies aren't very good as is lol. I also went the following evening and tried their birthday soft serve with cornflakes. It was really sweet and fun. I really want to try their birthday cake, I wish they sold it by the slice.

This place is located inside the Cosmo, you see it right when you get off the escalator upstairs by the chandelier bar. They gave us a sample of the cereal ice cream. It def tasted like milk and cereal but I wouldnt eat it again for free. I got a slice of birthday cake. It was $13 (yikes) but enough to share with 2. It was very good and fresh. I also wanted a cookie but didnt think $4 was worth a packaged cookie. If Ima spend 4 bucks on a cookie it better be atleast hot and fresh out the oven! I wish they would expand locations though bc the birthday cake mmm...

3.5 stars. I've had five different desserts from this location. The crack pie is adequately named. I've never done crack cocaine but the addicting qualities of the crack pie make me see how someone would break in to a CVS to steal $7 from the cash register to buy a piece of this of this crack pie. Ice cream, cookies and cake slice are decent...not amazing. Get the crack pie. On my most recent trip, I purchased the $14 cake slice. Cake was ok--definitely not worth $14. I've had better cake from Wal-Mart.

I can't speak for anything else, but their coffee is FAN-Friggin-Tastic!! It's so rich. And the creamer they provide is actually, thick cream. Even my mom who usually don't like coffee said it's the best she's had. I'm definitely coming back with my Lactaid pills ready so I can try the soft serve and other goodies.

Milk Bar is located inside of the Cosmopolitan in Vegas and is found and owned by Chef Christina Tosi. Milk Bar is located on the 2nd floor of the casino and is next to Momofuku. Milk Bar is not a sit down place. There is a bench on the side, but not a full on table and seating area. There is a menu above the registers and you order, pay, and pick up your food to go eat elsewhere. There's a lot of seating on the actual floor so seating shouldn't be a problem. Depending on the time of day, Milk Bar can get crazy busy with a long line. My bf and I lucked out and showed up at a right time just because there was not a long line and after we ordered, the line grew super long. Milk Bar is more of a dessert place so don't come by thinking you can order a full on meal. Milk Bar offers coffee/espresso drinks, cookies, cakes, soft serve, milkshakes, pies, and yogurt cups. The only gluten-free and dairy-free items that they have are the Life cookies ($4.25 each) and the Life Brekkie Cups ($6.25 each). This is pretty expensive for such small portions, but then again it is Vegas. I did not think that these items were worth the price. They honestly tasted just like regular cookies and yogurt cups that you can get anywhere. The fancy shakes ($12) contain alcohol. My bf ordered the Chocolate Malt Cake Fancy Shake which comes with vodka and kahlua. He enjoyed the alcohol, but thought the drink was overall too sweet. I completely glutened myself and tried the Cereal Milk milk shake ($7.50) just because of all of the great reviews. This milk shake literally tasted like cereal milk, but for some strange reason tasted really good as a milk shake and I can see how it can be quite addicting. Overall, the staff was knowledgeable, quick, and friendly. The only thing that stood out for me was the cereal milk which I don't think I have seen this anywhere before, but other than that, the other items on the menu are pretty basic. I think Milk Bar is overpriced for the basic items that they sell.

As part of the Momofuku experience, it would be hard pressed not to stop and try some goodies from Milk! However, because I'm lactose intolerant and didn't bring any lactaid with me when I went, I have to give a review on the cookies only. First, the staff work as quickly as possible, but since they're basically a stand next to Momofuku in the Cosmopolitan, people can be rude and cut right in front of you! (Which they do!) Only so much the staff can do about these people lol. They're all really nice people though! (As are most servers in Vegas) I got three cookies, which is one of the deals. Cookies are $3 each or 3/$8. Blueberry and cream, compost cookie, and the chocolate chocolate cookie. All of these cookies were a bit dry and not really that great or even memorable. The blueberry and cream tasted like it had sour cream in it. It was weird and I wasn't too much of a fan, that I didn't even finish it. The compost cookie wasn't *bad* but it wasn't that great either. It was a little salty, a little sweet, and pretty much forgetabble. Also crumbly and did I mention dry? Finally, the chocolate chocolate, which lives up to its name. It's super rich and pretty satisfying, but again, nothing special. So for cookies, I think because they're prepackaged and not freshly made, I would just skip it. I want to come back and try some of their other goodies though like their stuffed bagels or their ice cream!
This is a very good Milk Bar from NYC. But it's very sweet for me. But cookies is very nice. There's have big menu. If's you don't know what you need just ask for recommend

I didn't think i would be a huge fan of the cereal milk soft serve but woaw did it surprise me brought me back to my childhood with that flavor and best part is you get a cornflake topping and they dont get soggy like when you would put them in ur milk soo they stayed crunchy all throughout which was awesome. Loved it!
This place is a must! Every time I'm near a Milk Bar I have to make a pit stop! You won't be disappointed! Crack pie is my favorite!
WoW! Don't get the cookies! Overpriced and terribile in taste. Subway has better cookies.

I tried Crack Pie, Cereal Milk ice cream, cheese and eggs bread. Food tastes bland, monotonous in flavor, overly sweet, and definitely overpriced. I would not eat here again. Desserts do not need to be overly complex but when they are like at Milk then they'd better be amazing. They are below average. I do not understand the hype. Any dessert at the Wicked Spoon buffet would hands down beat what Milk sells. They were nice to give us a cup of cold water which was refreshing and good!

This place is aiiiteeeee. We stayed at the Cosmo for a weekend in Vegas and our mission was to try as much foods as we could that is conveniently located in our hotel. We arrived on a Sunday afternoon and there was no line. The girls working were super sweet. They gave me complimentary birthday truffles when my boyfriend told them it was my birthday. The birthday truffles were a bit too sweet for my liking but my boyfriend absolutely loves it. He ordered the compost cookie which I highly do not recommend. Flavors were lacking and cookie isn't too soft. I ordered the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crumble, one of their popular items I was told. It tasted exactly like its name - cereal and milk lol. While decent, it isn't worth $7 and probably is something I wouldn't go out of my way to get in Vegas.

This is so much fun dessert! I got the traditional birthday cake for my birthday from my sister-in-law and trust me I was expecting a vanilla cake box type cake with some tasteless sprinkles but I was blown away by just how delicious this cake was! The whole concept of icing smeared thick around cake just to cover its imperfections is not necessary so this pastry chef is so spot on; I mean who really eats all that frosting and who wants it covering the beautiful layers of delicious cake smothered between the delicious fillings! Anyway the birthday cake truffles on top and the slightly vanilla tasting crunch from the sprinkles was the correct balance for this rich, moist vanilla birthday cake. I love Birthday cake again thanks to this place. Did I mention my sister gave me cookies here too?!?! The cookie flavors here are so much fun too. You aren't getting the traditional chocolate chip, peanut butter or oatmeal here. We are talking about fruity pebbles, corn flakes, marshmallow, coffee crunch type mixes and it's actually pretty darn good. It reminds me a little bit of the cereal bars with milk that I used to have as a kid and also reminds me of the taste of milk left over when I eat my breakfast cereal....it's just a very warm comforting fun feeling. I guess I gave it four stars because I would like the price to be a little more within range for the size of cake I got

Stopped by Milk Bar after eating at Hattie B's while at the cosmopolitan. I had heard good reviews so I definitely had to give it a try. Luckily it was Milk Bar's "birthday" so they had a deal for the milk ice cream for $1... we added on the cereal which was a good decision! The ice cream was soooo milky (go figure) and creamy and my husband said "I feel like I'm eating cereal and ice cream at the same time" haha! Which was true! I think it was good to try, but it wasn't the best ice cream I've ever had however it wasn't bad. I'd give it a try if you stumble upon it!

I was craving something sweet when I happened upon Milk Bar in Las Vegas. I was so excited as I did not know they had a location there. They have a bunch of cookies and milkshakes, but I got the Cereal milk soft serve which comes with cereal toppings. It hit the spot and I was a happy camper that day. I wish they had Milk Bar in the Bay Area, so I could try everything else on their menu !

I always enjoy Milk Bar! The soft serve is amazing. I haven't tried anything else. The cereal milk one and fruity cereal are both so delish! I like getting it with cereal and sprinkles both. I haven't tried their other dessert but next time I'll do one of the milkshakes!

Milk Bar is one of my favorite go to spots when I'm back home in NYC so I was very happy when I found that there was a full location in Las Vegas. I had my usual the first visit, cereal ice cream with corn flakes dusted on the sides, the second time around I had the cereal milk latte which was basically my two favorite food items combined. The service here was quick and easy and the young lady who took my order was quick to have my ice cream served to me before I could finish even signing my receipt, just an awesome experience with good dessert, can't wait to go back.

I've tried the cereal milk soft serve ice cream before in New York and I wasn't blown away. This time we tried the cereal milk and crack pie soft serve while visiting Vegas. The crack pie ice cream was unique and tasted really good. I recommend getting the crack pie flavor over the cereal milk.

Was excited to try this but the excitement soon waned. I purchased a slice of crack pie for like $6-7. Well if that's a slice I'd sure hate to see their version of a sliver because that's what it really was. For that price you should get a generous slice. It was okay, kinda like cold pecan pie without the pecans. I asked for it alamode but was told that wasn't an option so I purchased a small ice cream of chocolate covered pretzel and cereal milk., for another $6-7 I might add. Consistency was good but there was virtually no flavor. I tasted salt in the chocolate but really no chocolate. So I give them A for marketing and C- for their product. Great marketing can make anything look good - beware. :)

This is the closest Milk Bar as I'm gonna get and I surely made a beeline for it once I spotted the infamous signage. It's worth the chaotic trek through the strip and the Cosmopolitan. It's all expensive as F*** but who cares because the Cereal milk soft serve is where it's at without going to NY. It was tough to not load up on the cookies or a slice of cake. Staff was so ultimately cute and friendly, and right next door is Momofuku if you happen to be fan.

Disclaimer: i was so excited to come here bc i'm a huge Christina Tosi fan, and i'm totally biased but this place really is fantastic. The prices are definitely pretentious, but the food is so so great! The cereal milk soft-serve is everything it's hyped up to be, and you absolutely need that crunchy cornflake topping. We also tried the crack pie (lives up to its name for sure) and the b-day milkshake, which will bring you back to 2nd grade chuck-e-cheese birthday memories. The coffee was really great too. Overall, it's expensive af but definitely lives up to the hype.

Located inside the cosmo and right next to momofuku sits the best dessert one can have during their stay here. A very light refreshing flavor of milk cereal soft serve brings you back to your childhood. At 6 bucks for a soft serve and 1.5 bucks for their salted cornflake topping, you'll be salivating for more... so much more than I came here three days in a row. A buck fifty for one topping is bit hefty but worth trying at least once bc the salty crunchy cuts the sweetness in the soft serve just right. Their crack pie is also a must try but only once bc pies are typically too sweet for me. It's not your typical pie as it's very dense. I can't describe the flavor of crack pie well but I can see why it gets its name. Quick service and attentive. You can ask to sample their soft serve before selecting which flavor. They had a crack pie flavor soft serve but I wasn't impress at all. Too sweet and dense. It almost makes you wonder if the actual crack pie will be tasty.... and it sure was.
Cereal Milk soft serve is to die for! The cookies are pricey but worth every penny!! A must see if in Vegas!
First time trying this place just walking by. It's good but I would say it's a little pricey. I would stil try it just to taste and know.
Nasty and over priced! They served me a crack pie cold! sorry but I think ooey and gooey butter bar should be warm and gooey. No thank you.
Had the cereal milk soft serve which was good. Has a nice malt flavor to it. Also got some cookies to go but they are pre-packaged and does seem to be made onsite.

I have a serious Milkbar obsession and I always have - so take that for what it's worth with my review. Yes - this place is pricey, and that's the downside. But it's Milkbar and it's in Vegas, so honestly, pricing isn't really too out of whack if you ask me... Would I pay this much for this back home in Denver? God no... but after I paid $14 for a 12oz. can of corona at the (incredibly stupid) encore beach club earlier in the day, you really couldn't scare me off from the cost of anything... We got the cereal milk shake and the birthday cake shake. The cereal milk is exactly what it sounds like and tasted exactly as you imagine it would - delicious cornflakes in cornflake flavored ice cream. We both agreed that while we liked that the original flavor is the only one on the menu, had we been given the option to order a different cereal flavor - like cinnamon toast crunch or something more sugary (of course), we would have chosen one of those flavors. The birthday cake shake was riddled with cookie chunks and sprinkles and if you're into that kind of thing like I am, you will love it. The crack pie was great, I don't think anyone can really complain about something so great. It was a smaller than expected slice, though. The flavor was buttery and delicious and I would absolutely eat 10 of those pies if left unsupervised with them. If you like sugar and have followed Milkbar for years like me, again, you will like it. If you don't like overpaying for hyped up sugar shops, you probably won't be happy.

This place is NOT worth the hype! I ordered the b-day soft serve and was sadly disappointed. My soft serve had a weird salty flavor and tasted nothing like a bday cake. After I ate off all the sprinkles, I just threw it away which was a complete waste! It was definitely not worth $6.50! I also tried the milk and cereal soft serve and that wasn't much better. The soft serve literally tastes like milk with zero hint of sweetness. Save yourself the time and money and go elsewhere!

All I can say is yum!! I've been to Milk Bar before in New York City but I'd only tried the cereal milk soft serve before. This time I opted to try the toffee crunch soft serve which was delicious. I added rainbow sprinkles and corn flakes on top. I loved the amount of variety their menu has with cookies, cakes and soft serve. They also have cool books and cooking ingredients for purchase as well. It was my friend's birthday so we opted for a slice of bday cake to go and the staff was so nice to include two candles for the celebration and candles from the bar right next door, which is great to know for birthday celebrations. I'd highly recommend stopping by Milk Bar after trying David Chang's Momofuku restaurant next door for your dessert needs.
This place is pretty good for sweets and desserts. We got the ice cream and cupcakes. They were both just ok. The setting and ambiance is nice and so is the presentation

I used to like their cookies, but the quality and taste has declined tremendously. This is the third time in a row I've bought the cookies and it tastes stale and just doesn't taste good in general. After all the hype this bakery has gotten, the efforts aren't there anymore. There's a reason why people raved about this place when it first opened, but come on! You're going to lose your customers if your passion for baking doesn't reflect the results.

Overall: overwhelming flavors, slightly overpriced, nothing special I had heard a lot about Milk Bar, as everyone has, especially since watching MasterChef Junior with the chef Christina Tosi. I've seen many Instagram posts from the Milk Bar in NYC too, and there is overall a lot of hype, so I was excited to try it in Las Vegas. It's an adorable shop, just a window, but the neon sign grabs your attention. The menu is pretty confusing; it seems to be mostly cookies, slices of cake, soft serve, and milkshakes. I've seen people mostly get soft serve, so that's what I went for. They did offer samples which was nice. I was pretty underwhelmed with the flavor options. They had three flavors: cereal milk (corn flakes), crack pie (toffee), and chocolate pretzel (salty chocolate). All of the flavors were unique, but the crack pie was so overwhelmingly sweet and salty at the same time we did not like it at all. The cereal milk was okay but a little subtle, like corn flakes aren't a strong flavor to begin with. The chocolate pretzel was good, but the salt was a bit much, and I couldn't eat a whole cup of it. Another thing to note is that the corn flake topping on the cereal milk soft serve was $1.25 which seemed a little high for just a few corn flake crumbles around the side. All of the flavors were very creamy, but I have had so many ice cream places that I prefer that I have no desire to return here. I think it's overly hyped and there are plenty of better places to go for ice cream.

Went here New Years Day, so a wait was expected. I ordered a variety pack of treats for about $20. Evertyhing had super basic but delicious ingredients. The staff actually misplaced our order and we had to wait an additional 20 minutes. The crack pie was the best! Also had a milkshake cocktail that was meh...

Went here during labor day weekend to try the cereal milk soft serve. It was $6, but for some reason my bank statement says $6.50. I didn't catch it when he told me the total because I figured it would be just the $6. Check the amount prior to paying/leaving!! The soft serve was so gross. I can't believe all the hype on it. I took a few bites and threw it away. What a waste! My friend got the soft serve with corn flakes. She kept saying how nasty the soft serve was and how salty the cornflakes were. Aside from that experience, I've had some of the cookies before and my fave is the blueberry. Crack pie is extremely too sweet and I love sweets.

A fun place for a sweet treat on the Strip. The place has a very cute vibe and is quite tiny, squeezed into a small storefront next to Momofuku in the Cosmo. Staff is friendly and takes orders quickly. If nothing else, the flavors at Milk Bar are out of the box. There were lots of items I wanted to try, but I was most intrigued by the cereal milk soft serve and the crack pie. The cereal milk soft serve really does taste like sugar-infused milk with a starchiness that's quite unique. My slice of crack pie was gooey and very delicious. Neither item was overly sweet. Prices are high -- probably too high for the portion size. But maybe I shouldn't complain, since portion sizes are obscenely huge elsewhere. I'd be interested in coming back to try the cookies and klossies.

I got the crack pie slice and the bday cake truffles. The crack pie slice was so buttery and gooey; it was good! The bday cake truffles are another one of their signature items, I think? Those are just okay, sorta dry and too sweet. The problem I had with this place was the prices! The teeny slice of pie was $6 while the 3 little truffles were ~$7. I feel like for this prices it maybe should've a bit bigger or maybe baked fresh? I'm not sure about the pie, but the cookies and truffles were already in plastic bags so they were a bit dry looking. I think what I'm going to have to do is find a copy cat recipe for that crack pie though...

I seriously do not understand what the hype is all about. I got the super hyped milk and cereal cornflakes soft serve and it was the saltiest ice cream I have ever tasted!! and the fact that the owner is a Master Chef judge I don't know how I feel. It was so ughhh (that's my first reaction when I tasted it). It was not even really sweet at all, just all salt even when I just eat the ice cream part. It made me so dehydrated lol. Maybe I just don't have a refined enough platelet for things like this. I also bought their compost cookies which were good but also salty lol, it has coffee bits in it which I like and make it sweeter but the cookie itself was also on the salty side. I also tried the cornflakes and marshmallows which once again salty af. The chocolate cookie was also salty more than sweet so I really don't know how to feel about this place. It's either my tongue is broken or this place just full of saltttttttt Overall Taste 2/5 Service 4/5 Parking 3/5 - garage parking of the hotel Price 2/5 not worth it

I was so excited to go to Milk from all of the pictures i see on social media. I got 3 things at Milk. First since I am a cake lover I got a slice of Birthday Cake which is a vanilla rainbow cake, rainbow cake crumbs, sprinkles, vanilla frosting. The cake was moist and and the frosting did have a big vanilla taste but as far as cakes go it was a little underwhelming. Really nothing special with that slice of cake. The second thing I ordered was the Crunchy Cereal Shake which was made with milk, cornflakes, brown sugar and a pinch of salt. It did taste like cereal like I expected but all I really did was pay $9 to drink cereal, nothing special there either. The last thing I ordered which was the best thing was the Crack Pie. I can see why this is there fan favorite because it is addicting as if you were doing crack. Haha. The Crack Pie has a toasted oat crust and a gooey butter filling. So you get that crunch of the crust with that creamy gooey filling. This is the one thing you must have at Milk, but overall this place was pricey and not as exciting as it has been made out to be. BrandonFitFoodie

Food: only tried the dessert items: assortment of cookies and crack pie. Have made several of the cookies from the cookbook. Not impressed. All of this might be better if if was freshly baked. Like my own versions better. Service: it was a walk up counter. Atmospher: it was a walk up counter. Visited on 2.24.18

Wow, I cannot believe how bad this cake is. Bought 4 pieces of different types for my birthday yesterday, to share with my family. Every piece was dry, flavorless, and honestly the worst cake I have had. Should have gone to a grocery store and saved the $50

One of my favorite dessert places! The ice cream is not too sweet, it's just right. The ice cream with the fruity pebbles cereal tasted exactly like a bowl of cereal but in a ice cream form. I love the environment and it's very clean. I would definitely come here again.

LOOK AWAY. JUST SAVE YOUR MONEY. This place is NOT worth trying. $7.50 down the drain just like that. One bite in I had tears streaming down my face. My wallet was crying too. JUST KIDDING. But it was that bad. The consistency and taste was not up to par. If I were ever in New York, I would not make a stop at Milk Bar.

I really really really wanted to like this place. I made a special detour to las Vegas just to try the crack pie and ice cream. I'll confess my expectations were high after watching the Netflix documentary that featured these treats. Sadly it didn't live up to the hype. I'm not sure what happen but the the prices were high compared to the portion sizes and the deserts were nothing to write home about. Where's the love for quality that I saw in the documentary?

So I recently watched the episode showing Milk Bar on Chef's Table. I loved watching the chef's story on how she developed the crack pie! It definitely did not disappoint! The crack pie is buttery and I've not tasted a sweet treat like it before! I also tasted the Birthday Truffles and they were AMAZING! I may even consider ordering these items to be delivered to my house in Texas for a future birthday!

cute little spot in the LINQ hotel. Seems a bit pricey for a birthday coffee (regular iced coffee with sprinkles onto) 9$. I had to try it once it was a good cup of coffee, but didn't live up to the price.

I'm addicted. There are some really nice ladies there that have been so nice to us every time which makes this place even sweeter. The strawberry n corn quake is the absolute best thing. I love it. I'm addicted to Milk Bar. Please put one in my city ASAP That little girl named Precious took care of us. She remembered our names each time we returned. She deserves a raise. :)

Sorry not sorry but not worth the hype. Maybe take this with a grain of salt as I'm not the biggest fan of sweets/desert places, but even I can appreciate some good sweets when given. Unfortunately Milk Bar does not live up to the expectations and for the price you pay, I didn't see it worthwhile. There are a lot of dessert places off-the-strip that are better and way worth the price. Overall, Milk Bar is overpriced which is something to expect being on the strip. I just didn't feel like the value of the treats I got were worth the monetary value. So I did the "Greatest Hits" combo which was a little over $20 for their best treats. It came with: - compost cookie - 2.5/5. Was okay. I kept eating it but couldn't figure out if I liked it or not... yep, one of those. - slice of crack pie: 1/5 I didn't particularly like this - b'day truffles: 5/5 i really liked these! pretty good. i definitely needed a drink to counteract the sweetness of this though. this was my favorite and i'd opt to get these again if i came across it. - cereal milk soft serve: 4/5 really cool concept. actually just tastes like corn flakes with milk. not sure if i'd pay for it because it wasn't anything unique.

Eh, very overpriced for what. You get. Soft serve is decent. Consistency is fine, but not creamy luxurious. Flavor of cereal milk is as expected. Also got a cookie and the crack pie. Easy on the sugar! Mouth puckering sweetness overwhelms anything else, but what I could taste was pretty pedestrian. Crack pie slice was also small and thin, not that I would want more, but for the price... Even my kid who is an unabashed sweet tooth dessert guy didn't want another bite. Place is bright and good for pics and service is efficient, but definitely style over substance.

This place is overpriced, however the desserts are legit good. We tried a pack of cake balls (Is that the correct name lol) and a cookie and both were super tasty. I would definitely drop by here the next time I'm in Vegas.

Im soooo sad! I wanted to like this place so much. We ordered the soft serve with cereal. It was okay didnt really have taste and was slightly salty for some reason. I personally enjoyed the sweet bites i did get, but my boyfriend didnt. We also got the crack pie... i was so disappointed!!! I dont think its something to be eaten cold.... it was hard to chew, the flavor wasn't anything extremely special it just was not what i expected at all:(

This place is so stinking cute it's a small spot and I decided to get a soft serve which is what there know for, and it was good I would say it literally tasted like left over milk from the bottom of fruity pebbles or Frosted Flakes, but frozen and I made a mistake on getting chocolate chips with it definitely would recommend the cereal crunch instead it pairs way better. It was pricey though for two soft serves it was $14 so about $7 each ice cream with out the cone. It was good but not that good maybe if it was cheaper I would consider getting ice cream again but I'm not much of a cereal person to begin with so I might have to pass.

I'll start by saying that I practically worship Christina Tosi. I'm a classically trained pastry chef and have always looked forward to trying her product. The actual sweets themselves were fine, but the prices were outrageous. I would have loved for the cookies to have been fresh, but they were prepackaged and the compost cookie I so looked forward to tasted very stale. Disappointed!

I love white russians so I had to get the cereal milk white russian milkshake--bad choice! It made me sick to my stomach, it tasted so gross. I ate some of my friends' soft serve (different ones got the different flavors) and they were all good and made up for the bad milkshake.

I have wanted to try this place since a friend brought me back some cookies from this place. Now this is one of my favorite places in Vegas to get dessert or a coffee beverage. While in Vegas recently I tried the iced crack pie latte and it was like drinking liquid dessert. Definitely a must try for people with a sweet tooth! I also recently purchased a dozen cookies because I wanted to sample a variety of their flavors. All the cookies are all delicious, but my current favorites are the blueberry and cream, confetti and compost ones. Meanwhile, the service is surprisingly very quick. Even though I went on a busier weekday, the line was moving pretty quickly and I was able to place my order and purchase my items without having to wait for a long time.

While staying at the Cosmopolitan , I was trying to stop at as many restaurants as possible and have the best LV dining experience as I could. Milk Bar is right near Egg Slut & the Juice Standard (reviews below) in the Boulevard Tower. To forewarn you, the menu is pretty extensive and a little bit difficult to navigate. I wasn't sure what I wanted - and that didn't help either. The girl at the register whose name is Lissa, helped me through the ordering process. She went through each of the things they offer and told me what the most popular items were & what her personal favorites were as well. That helped me figure out my order. I knew I wanted to do the three cookies for $10 deal and I went for the chocolate chip marshmallow cookie, the confetti cookie, and the compost cookie which is supposed to be their most popular. They also had a blueberry flavor, and a corn meal - which Lissa said was her favorite. They also had a new birthday cake flavored - scented balm they were selling. Most people use it on their lips but it's concentrated enough that you can use it on your hands as well. I love birthday cake flavored/scented anything and everything so I purchased that as well for $12. To round it all off- Lissa said that her favorite thing on the menu as well as the most popular item was the birthday cake truffles. She said hands-down you need to get that. So for an additional six dollars I purchased that as well. For $28 I got three cookies, a lip - hand balm, and the birthday cake truffles which was a set of three. I have to say, I was not a big fan of the compost cookie or the chocolate chip marshmallow cookie. The lip - hand balm was good for the lips but not great anywhere else. Wasn't the best purchase. Now-in my opinion, the confetti flavored cookie was unreal. Sugar cookie with rainbow/funfetti sprinkles inside. Also, the birthday truffles were no joke! Yum status. There was not really a long line at all when we went. In fact, every time we walked by there didn't seem like a long line. However there are always a few people there which is a good sign. It's a tad on the Las Vegas pricey side, but that's what you would expect. I did get a lot for under $30. Get your sweet tooth on.
The cereal milk soft serve was soooo good!!!! It was a tad expensive, but that's Vegas for you.

This placed wowed me! The cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes is crazy good. It's just the right amount of sweetness in the soft serve mixed with the corn flakes. It was light and creamy, but not heavy. We took home 2 crack pies which was also really good. Butter the brown sugar is heaven. They're small but it's the perfect amount because they're rich. My only only con would be the prices. I know it's the cosmo, but I'm local and paying $30 for 2 soft serves and 2 pies is kind of crazy + parking. Local love would be appreciated.

Was super excited to try out Milk Bar after watching Christina Tosi's episode of Chef's Table and knew I had to stop by. We ordered a slice of crack pie and a cereal milk soft serve as a post-lunch dessert. As many others have said, everything here is expensive and in my opinion, not worth the high price-tag. The cereal milk soft serve tasted nice, wasn't too sweet, and had a lighter texture than many soft serves I've tried before but I felt that there really wasn't anything special or memorable about it- at least not enough to warrant $6 (& this is without the cereal flakes on top). Now moving on to the crack pie, I was pretty shocked with the size, this thing is SMALL. My boyfriend is honestly still appalled that we paid over $6 for this but I personally think it's a better deal than the soft serve. Yes it's small but it is really dense and filling. It has a beautiful buttery and sugary taste that I really enjoyed - I'd probably bump my rating up to 4 stars if the price of this dropped to about $4 or $5 to be honest. Overall I think Milk Bar is the type of place you visit just to say you've visited. The prices are simply too high- even if it does taste pretty good. I would only be back if I was SUPER craving crack pie or if I won a nice little jackpot downstairs (then I'd buy the entire crack pie for ~$50)

All in all, everything is overpriced. The ice cream was good and the quality was great, but I honestly wouldn't pay that much for a cup of soft serve ice cream. I got the milk cereal soft serve which basically tasted like corn flakes soaked in milk for 10 minutes, which might taste bad or good depending on your opinions on corn flakes itself. Despite the high price, I can't say I'm surprised because it is such an aesthetically pleasing food and on top of that it's located in Vegas. Overall, good quality ice cream, but would not spend money on it every time.

Three stars - Milk Bar was just "A - OKAY." I was super amped to try this place upon viewing photos of the ever popular Milk Bar on Instagram. However, the taste did not make up for the hype or all the visually appealing photos. I tried the crack pie, cereal milk soft serve and three cookies. Crack Pie - My friend made this once with a recipe she found online and it was ah-ma-zinnnnnng! Surely I thought the original must taste 10x better. Unfortunately, it was a total let down -- nothing too spectacular about it. It was essentially like I was eating a really sweet piece of butter. Cereal Milk Soft Serve - This literally just tasted like milk. If you enjoy the aftertaste of milk in your mouth, this this might be for you. I didn't enjoy this overall. But that's just my opinion. Cookies (3 for $8) - I tried the Blueberry & Cream, Compost and the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow. I enjoyed them most in the order listed. The texture of the cookie was a weird hard chewiness? The blueberry & cream was quite tasty, so I would probably get that again if I were to return.

Avoid this vile place at all costs... and it'll cost you a lot. Cookies are bagged in cellophane, and just look at all the nasty ingredients on the label. The soft serve ice cream has no taste, I tried a twist and could not distinguish one flavour from the other. This place is a perfect example of why the Cosmopolitan should not rely so heavily on celebrity chefs. And this one should be ashamed of herself. Judging by the lineups, it's a money maker, but don't waste yours!!!
Had to come here after watching Chef's Table even though it's not the same location. Crack pie was gross. Milk soft serve just tasted like....milk. Why do people eat that?

Had to try Milk Bar because of all the hype. We managed to go when it was crazy so there was a long line to wait for your cookies/sweets. I ordered the compost cookie because that's what I've heard you have to try. Overall it was just eh. Don't get me wrong if you need sugar then it will do the trick, but I would honestly rather eat my sugar in a different form. The cookie was a little chewy, and there was an unpleasant crunch from some of the nuts where I thought I would break a tooth. I don't know; I don't see the hype. I think next time I will go elsewhere to get my sugar fix.

In looking for another ice cream place in Las Vegas, we ended up here. Intrigued by the business name, we approached and saw that they serve soft serve. One of the soft serve flavours is "Cereal Milk". I asked the server what it tasted like and he said, "It's really hard to describe the taste, other than cereal milk." So I replied, "So....vanilla?" And he said "No, not vanilla. Let me give you a sample." So he gave me a sample and the rest is history. It tasted like cereal milk! I said to the server, "OMG this tastes like cereal milk", and he laughed and said "I know, hard to describe otherwise!" Now I'm not usually an ice cream eater but I had to order myself a cup of this cereal milk soft serve, which blew my mind every time I tasted it. They had other flavours too, but honestly I couldn't tell you what they were - I didn't pay attention because I was so blown away by the cereal milk flavour. I did notice that they sell the flavour mixture so you can create your own cereal milk ice cream at home. So, it's no secret that the flavour is achieved by adding corn cereal powder to ice cream, among other things I'm sure. Next time I'm in Las Vegas, with kids or otherwise, I'm totally hitting this place up again!

I've been a fan of Christina Tosi/Momofuku/Milk Bar for a while. I finally got to try it all since I'm here in Vegas, and it's everything I pretty much expected milk bar to be. I ordered the greatest hits (compost cookie, crack pie, birthday truffles, and cereal milk) The cereal milk was okay. It didn't really blow my mind. Was kind of hoping the ice cream would be more creamier. Birthday truffles were probably my favorite-- just moist birthday cake sprinkled with white chocolate. It was so creamy and addicting. and the crack pie was amazing. It's one of a kind for sure. Still haven't tried the compost cookie but so far I'm excited. The staff was extremely informative, kind, and sweet. I'm definitely a true fan!

I went to Milk Bar in NYC and I've been craving the Crack Pie ever since my last visit there. I ordered the Crack Pie ($6.50) here and it was nasty and disappointing ugh. It tasted like straight up butter so this ruined my craving boo. It was not the Crack Pie that I enjoyed eating in NYC. However, I liked the crack pie soft serve ($6) which I ordered with rainbow sprinkles (50 cents more) which was sweet! I enjoyed the Confetti, Compost, and Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmellow cookies (3 for $8) as well which were way better than the crack pie unfortunately.
The shake isn't sweet but so good like having cereal in a shake would totally recommend it

Timing is everything! Got there and no one in line. Ordered my slice of Crack pie and blueberry & cream cookie, paid, and turned around and there was a line of 7 or 8 customers. I do enjoy the crack pie & that cookie, but the price. It's just as well this is the closest location for me & I'm rarely here. Food is 3.5-4 stars, value is 2 stars.

5-Star - cereal milk soft serve 3-Star everything else. I ordered the gift box that came with: -cereal milk soft serve (cereal topping included) -slice of crack pie --on the sweet side. Was able to share this piece with 3 others, and even then I wished it came with a smaller piece. - 3 birthday cake truffles --wayyy too sweet. Skip this. -compost cookie--honestly could not understand the hype about this product. The whole thing came out to $23 or $24. Note I think if you bought each individually it would be about the same price... All in all, I am glad I tried all of the famous items on the menu, but I will come back for the soft serve only! Maybe I'll even be adventurous and try the crack pie soft serve next!

First glance of their menu and I thought this place would be great. Ice cream and other desserts based on the flavors you get after eating a bowl of cereal. I was disappointed when I got my ice cream and it tasted less like a bowl of milk from a cinnamon cereal than it did a sickly sweet bowl of sugar. I think maybe in trying to make it taste a certain way, they overdid it. Also, how do you not give a spoon for ice cream? You get a little stick like those tiny ice creams you'd get in elementary school. It's one of those places that asks you to leave a tip with your order, even though nobody has actually did anything for you yet. I HATE that. For the price and the taste, I think I'd just pass on by next time.

Move on to something better and lighter. I tried the birthday cake shake since the server told it's the most popular item they sell and it was not remotely good. The $10 price tag for the shake also didn't help its cause.

Got 6 cookies and a crack pie to go - thank goodness I was allowed to bring them on my flight home! The crack pie is basically like a chess pie but with a yummier crust I think. And their cookies are good with interesting flavors! We also tried their soft serve while we were there and I think out of the three items I liked that the most! The flavor of the milk soft serve was subtle and not overly sweet, and I loved it with the crunchy cereal bits! Overall a great solid dessert place when you are looking for some sweets!

After dining at Momofuku next door, I bought a tin of cookies to take home from here--6 for $17. I got one of each flavor: compost, confetti, chocolate chocolate, corn, cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow, and blueberry cream. A few of the cookie flavors I had tried last year in NYC. The plastic and metal tin was cute. Unfortunately, the mf TSA screener at the airport stopped, inspected, and rubbed that solution on the edges of the tin from my carry on because he thought it looked suspicious with sharp edges...SMH...OMG!!

I love the cereal milk soft serve ! Every time I go to the cosmo, I have to get it ! The cookies were ok, I'm really looking forward to trying their confetti cake. The prices are very high, but hey ... that's the cost of the strip atmosphere, right?

Although we were stuffed after feasting at Momofuku, we still hit up Milk Bar on the way out. I mean, it's ice cream. It's basically like drinking some milk...yeah...After getting to know Christina Tosi's thought process through Netflix's Chef's Table, I wholeheartedly appreciate the joy and delight she projects into her desserts. I could taste the fun in the cereal milk soft serve, I can taste the inner childishness of her affogato, and the absolute indulgence of the crack pie. It's true, there is a separate stomach for desserts @thegrandappetit

I really wanted to like this place more, but it's only okay! I had tried most of the treats at the Yelp event, but really wanted to try to soft serve and some of the other treats I had previously sampled. Tip number one: get there early! If not, try to order online. They were out of some of the treats I had my heart set on. I ended up getting the crack pie milkquake, the compost cookie and a slice of crack pie. The milkquakes are priced at $10, and is maybe around 16oz.. don't quote me on the size. It seemed pretty small for the price, but I wasn't able to finish it. The crack pie/cereal milk combo is super sweet and rich. I definitely wouldn't want it again unless it came in a mini version. The crack pie was crumbled into the soft serve in large chunks. Had it been better incorporated, it may have enhanced the taste. The compost cookie is good.. I have previously reviewed it, so I won't go into great detail. The price is a bit much though.. $3 plus tax. If you want to try the soft serve, they offer generous sample size. I tried the cereal milk soft on its own, and I wasn't inpressed. It does taste a lot like cornflake milk, which is pretty neat, just it's not my favorite combo. The crack pie is priced at $6.50 plus tax.. ouch! It's good, but not worthy of its name or price tag.
