Overall, it's a neat place to try. The best thing they have, the cake, is way overpriced. I'm not sure if I'll return. Maybe if I'm in the area?
Crack pie is the best thing ever!! Everything on the menu is good. They should have another location off the strip.

I chose the crack pie shake because it sounded like crack pipe. Being in Vegas I thought why not. Props to the clever naming. It ended up being some salty and sweet concoction that filled me with regret. I regretted it as soon as I received in, in some dingy plastic cup. For all the fanfare that came with the decor they could've at least thrown some whipped cream on it or had a plastic cup with at least "Milk" written on it.

Not a fan. It was my first time and the service wasn't very friendly as I was asking about what to try. I just felt rushed and like I was a burden to them. The ice cream was too runny for me and way over priced for what it was.

Cereal milk ice cream with cornflakes- yes! It was great! The birthday truffles not really a texture or taste I enjoyed. The compost cookie was out of this world, it has potato chips in it - wow! The crack pie was good, sorry Milk Bar my Mom has a better recipe. All said, we will be back and definitely worth a stop or two!

To be fair, I haven't tried most items on the menu. But when I come to Vegas I always make the long walk to Cosmo for their birthday cake. At first I thought it was delicious; a bit dense and on the dry side, but still good. Also pricey for what you get; 14 dollars a hit. Today I got my slice and took some bites and realised it's just plain dry. In addition to being dry, the texture felt wet and sandy at the same time. Kind of like when you're trying not to eat the rest of a piece of cake so you put it in the sink and try to destroy it by running the water on it for a second but then panic and realize you're throwing away cake and eat it despite it's new wet texture. Kind of like that. I probably won't be getting another slice anytime soon. Finally closed the book on that chapter of my life....

I turned 50 this weekend, for a milestone birthday I asked my husband for a birthday cake from Milk Bar. It's a tiny cake and cost around $60. The cake is very cute. The frosting is good, not typical sickeningly sweet frosting. The cake itself, was the driest most crumbly cake I've ever had. Such a let down. It was impossible to cut an actual slice, we served a plate of crumbs held together with frosting. My one friend said he was so glad we wasted the money on this pretty cake, we just saved him 60 bucks. I just can't express how disappointed I was with this cake.

Last time I was in Vegas this place wasn't open yet but I knew the next time I came I wanted to check it out. I had already looked at the menu online so I sort of had an idea of what I was going to get. I ended up trying the fruit cereal soft serve with crunchy cereal topping and the corn cookie. I really enjoyed the soft serve and love that they have the crunch cereal in the bottom and on the outside of the ice cream. Makes it feel like you get your money's worth. The cookie I didn't care for the flavor. It wasn't horrible but just not what I was expecting. But you can taste the butter in it. The prices are slightly high depending on what you get. However, I go into it thinking I'm OK with spending this certain amount for what I want. I will come here again to try out the other offerings.

On our latest trip to Vegas, we stayed at the Cosmo and conveniently took the elevator down to Milk Bar one afternoon. I only had one mission for this place and that was to try something with the Cereal Milk! I ended up getting Cereal Milk Soft Serve with Corn Flakes as a topping....and WOW it really does taste like Cereal Milk!! I liked it because it wasn't too sweet and the texture was light and creamy. We also tried some of the cookies that turned out to be great gifts to bring home! They are a bit inconsistent though as my sister said that sometimes when she gets the "Corn Cookie" it's not as good as when they buy the mix and bake them themselves... I did like our batch though since it was nice and soft and I personally prefer soft cookies over crispy (It was just a tad underdone though...). Overall, really enjoyed this place and can't wait to come back and try more!

So yummy! Located on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, Milk Bar has a wide selection of treats ranging from cake truffles to cookies to milk shakes. The cake truffles come in packs of three for $7.95(?) and are worth every penny. They have a slightly crisp exterior followed by OMG melt in your mouth goodness. I had the birthday cake flavor my first day and enjoyed the grasshopper chocolate flavor on my flight home. Many have raved about the crack pie and I will add on to that! I had the crack pie milkshake for lunch another day and it was amazing. Big chunks of the famous crack pie throughout the shake, like a Dairy Queen Blizzard on steroids. No need for booze in this shake, although they do offer it! There is no seating at Milk Bar, but there are numerous small tables and chairs/sofas located on the 2nd floor, especially by neighboring Egg Slut and the Chandelier Bar.
Really liked the cereal and milk ice cream. It was refreshing and delicious! I can see where the hype comes from. I would visit again if I got the chance!

I've been hearing about the amazing sweets served in this establishment in New York and Los Angeles. Since we wee near the area showing out of towners around, we thought "Why not?" Located in Cosmopolitan Hotel in between Momofoku and Eggslut, the establishment is pretty small and only has one bench for a couple of people to sit on. There is a bright pink neon sign that signals you have reached your destination. The menu is shown above the cash registers. They offer various things, from soft serves, milkshakes, prepackaged cookies, and different sweets. Thankful there was no line, we decided to try a cereal soft serve with corn flakes. After ordering and paying at the cashier, you wait by the window on the right for them to serve you your order. Orders came quick, but I would hope so considering they are basically just preparing ice cream in a cup/prepackaged desserts in the front. The soft serve was very underwhelming. Yes. It tasted like cereal milk. That was the whole point. However, for $10+? Not worth it. The portion was very small and the corn flakes tasted bland and somewhat gross. If you like them, however, you would be very thankful that probably 1/3 of the cup is filled with corn flakes in the bottom, as well as topped on the soft serve. For all the hype for this establishment, I was honestly expecting way more. Maybe I would try the prepackaged pastries and cookies if they were offered to me. However, I would not be returning. Very disappointing.

We came here after my coworker watched Chefs Table and learned about this place We came for the cereal flavor ice cream. It was good on it's own, not omg but good. (See TIP below) We got a slice of the crack pie and that REALLY lived up to it's name. Wow it was good. TIP: Put the ice cream ON the pie... and your tastebuds won't even know how to handle it. Flipping a, I want it right now.

Won like $11 from the penny slots in the Cosmo casino so decided to treat myself and my girls to a few cookies. We ended up getting all 6 flavors and a birthday cake shake. Pretty expensive for cookies. The Corn one was not impressive, but oddly enough, I really liked the birthday cake one, which I thought would be my least favorite cuz I'm not a big fan of sprinkles. The cornflake marshmallow cookie was aight. I'm kinda proud to say that I do a better version at home that's like crack and people will throw down and smack a b--ch to get the last one. Overall, average for me. For $4 a cookie, I'd expect better ingredients. If you check the label on the package, there's artificial flavors and food coloring, dextrose, you name it. There's a whole laundry list of stuff in it.

High quality, overly priced type II diabetes for sale! I'm pretty sure I could make all of these desserts if I had access to a couple of sticks of butter, a carton of eggs, an entire bag of sugar and some random leftovers from last weekends camping trip (marshmallows, corn, chocolate chips) to make a SINGLE cookie/slice of cake. Milk Bar was a yuuuge disappointment and a day of regret. The portions are very small for a high price, but trust me, you'll be thankful that it's so small. The cakes and cookies are nothing more than overly sweetened and super condensed sweets you could make yourself. You know those hydraulic press videos that everyone loves watching? I'm pretty sure that's how they make their crack cake. It was like a overly, overly, overly sweet cookie smooshed into the smallest slice of cake you'll ever have. I took a single bite and could already feel the diagnosis of atherosclerosis appearing in my near future. ALSO corn? chocolate chip? marshmallow? EXTRA EXTRA SUGAR?!?! I felt like a real food connoisseur tasting so many different "levels" in my cookie, but not in a good way. It was something I imagined my future 5 year old daughter "cooking" for me. A mushy mixture of all of her favorite foods (or maybe all of the ingredients on the lowest level of the refrigerator that she could reach). Either way, it was not something I'll be eating again! What made Milk Bar so famous? I have no idea. I'm betting money on a future study done on the relationship between Milk Bar customers and diabetes. Bring on that Metformin!

Since watching Chef's Table I have been clamoring to try Milk Bar in NY, but won't be going for a few months. I was surprised and excited to wander by this one in LV. I do not have a big sweet tooth but was intrigued by Chef Christina Tosi's innovation and passion as portrayed on Chef's Table. I decided to try the ICED CEREAL MILK LATTE and it was sooo good. The cashier confirmed it was not too sweet and she was right. It was not overly sweet but it was amazingly delicious with a slight hint of cereal milk flavor. It was so good I wanted to come back the next day for another one in a larger size.

We got the chocolate cake malt. It was an okay drink. It tasted like chocolate with chunks of like a cookie dough/chocolate chip chunks in it. The malt could've also have been more prominent. For 10$ I was expecting something special. I guess the price is just because the place is on the strip. The malt I make at home are much better than what they gave us.I would not go back.

I was last here around New Years and all i remember is Yummmy! My friend and I dropped by Milk a few times when we were last here. I remember having the bday truffles and cookies - so good! Picked up some more right before heading to the airport. =)

I didn't get any of their extravagant desserts, but they seem to be known for their soft serve which was very mediocre. I got a sample of the cereal milk flavor and it was OK. It tasted a little like malt flavor, almost bland. I ultimately ordered the crack pie flavor with corn flakes... WAYYYY too sweet. Maybe it's just a preference, but the ice cream was very light, almost fluffy. Personally, I like my soft serve to be dense and creamy.

My husband and I were waiting in line for Eggslut and needed pre-breakfast. He went to find us a snack and came back with a Momofuku chocolate cereal milk shake and cookies - yaaas! The milkshake was one of the best milkshakes I've ever had in my life. It is thin - more like melted milkshake but the flavor is outstanding. We like it so much we went back two more times over our stay! For the cookies we tried the compost cookie - awesome, chocolate chocolate - just okay, actually kinda gritty, and of course a slice of crack pie. Crack pie is kind of like a pecan pie without the pecans. It is aptly named as you will crave more as soon as you're done. Each time we went there the people working were fun and friendly and the lines were never real long. Momofuku Milk Bar was a food highlight of the trip for sure.

Over hyped and overpriced. Went on opening day..not much of a wait to order. I ordered the "Greatest Hits" combo and the strawberry-corn milkquake. Service was fast, but they did make a mistake with our order which resulted in a free sweet potato milkquake. The milkquakes (made only in Las Vegas) are supposed to be similar to a Dairy Queen blizzard. As I tried the strawberry corn milkquake, my first impression likened it to a McFlurry without an adequate spoon for eating. Milk Bar has flat wooden spatulas (larger ones are provided with the milk quake than what is on the counter). The flat spatula shape made it incredibly difficult to actually scoop the bits in the milkquake. The strawberry corn milkquake was a lot thicker consistency wise in comparison to the sweet potato milkquake we also had. Taste was so-so as I would often get a chunk of corn cereal or blob of strawberry jelly/preserve stuck in my "bubble tea sized straw). Presentation for the milkquake was also lacking. For $10, I expected something more than a clear plastic cup with a domed lid. Greatest hits combo: A nice option for those who are new to Milk Bar & want to try a little bit of everything. Presentation was lacking also as it comes in a basic brown paper bag "partially" stamped with the milk logo (see attached pics). I've had take out food presented in better packaging than this. The bday truffles were decent, but I feel like they don't match the 3 for $6 price tag (as they are very similar to a starbucks cake pop). Compost cookies were not anything special either. I know they're made up of Chocolate chips, butterscotch chips, coffee, graham cracker crust, pretzels and even potato chips...but in all honesty, the flavors were muddled together and the cookie itself was drier and smaller than expected for a $3 cookie. The crack pie was ridiculously SMALL. Upon opening the clever cardboard packaging, I was shocked to realize that I had paid $6.50 for a slice of pie smaller than my hand. Marketed as a twist on the traditional Chess pie, the Crack pie was disappointing...if served independent from it's wrapper, i would not be able to identify anything unique about it. The cereal milk soft serve is just okay, a gimmicky flavor to try if you like cereal--as it tastes like cap n crunch flavored milk. All in all, my opening day experience at Milk Bar was disappointing. Presentation, portions, and taste just don't match the hype or cost. I believe there are plenty of other better looking and better priced options for sweets in Las Vegas...don't waste your dollars or calories on this one.

I heard so much about this place, I had such high expectations... I ordered a chocolate cereal milk (milkshake) and it literally tasted like baby food, I couldn't eat it anymore... I had to throw it away. I felt like the people working there didn't know what they were doing. The place is overrated and overpriced, not worth it.

I was in literal heaven eating the birthday cake here. It was so good. We have a bag of six cookies that I will eat on the plane ride home today that I'm sure will be absolutely delicious. Can't say enough good things. And it was quick which didn't hurt.
milk ice cream tasted like milk, kinda interesting. compost cookie was just okay, i asked for it to be warmed, but it was wasn't warmed properly.

Everything about this place is amazing. The crack pie was best. It's sweet and chewy. The cereal ice cream initially tasted weird but your second and third bite was amazing. They also put cereal at the bottom of the cup which made for a nice surprise. The service was fast and easy! I couldn't be happier. I've been wanting to try this place forever.

When the elite event happened here I was home for the holidays so I missed my chance to try this place. I was walking around with my partner and saw their advertisement on the Cosmo and it reminded me to try this place. Very easy to find in the hotel. Located near eggslut. It isn't a restaurant it's more of a grab and go place. My partner and I were staring from a distance at the menu and I was greeted by a very friendly but loud Ingrid. When I said loud that's not a bad thing. She got my attention and got me into Milk bar. To start I want to say what a pleasure Ingrid was. She had a strong personality and a beautiful smile. She guided me through the menu and made great suggestions and recommendations. She even let me try a truffle or two. That was rad! I ended up getting a box of 12 cookies and a "crack pie" because I heard you had to get it. The compost cookie is THE BEST COOKIE THERE. It has a mix of like all their cookie flavors with a hint of coffee it was great. I wasn't crazy about the cornflake choc chip marshmallow cookie. However the crack pie was a little crackish. Tasted like pecan pie without pecans. A little too much powdered sugar on mine but not the worst thing to complain about. The only thing was the crack pie is small. You can't tell the size because it's in a deceptively sized box. So don't be mislead. My partner and I split it and I maybe got 2-3 bites. Again very good just not a good price point for how small. I heard things about the soft serve that it wasn't amazing so I stayed away from it because I trust my fellow elitist reviews. Biggest negative about this place is the price point. I spent about $40 on 12 cookies and one small crack pie. Honestly if I didn't have Ingrid there I prob would have put back some cookies after seeing the total but I let it go. $40 for all that is excessive. Just because you are on the strip doesn't mean the prices have to match. If your prices are lower I guarantee you would have more lines at this place and higher star rating, but hey that's what I notice after living here for years. Would I go back? That's debatable. If I saw Ingrid working would I Pop by and grab a cookie, probably. Honestly though in vegas your store should be getting business for its food not its awesome staff, not that having an awesome staff is bad thing but your food should always out shine everything if you stand behind it. Maybe a little more seating could be worked out. I know it's grab and go but seating was limited. I took mine to go, luckily I'm a local! Thank you milk bar for having us!

Might not be fair to rate this because I didn't try the cake. I had a birthday cake shipped from this store to a friend for his birthday. He had thanked me for the cake but didn't say anything about liking it. I asked him if the cake was good. He hated to tell me because he loved the gesture, but he said it was not even average. I heard the founder on How I Built This (NPR) and was so excited to send a cake from Milk Bar. I haven't tried anything from Milk Bar, sending this was my first purchase. I read great reviews so I will try it again. Would love to know if anyone else has had a disappointing experience with the shipped cakes. I planned on them being my "go to" gift for family birthdays.

I threw my ice cream in the trash. That's how much I disliked it. It just wasn't worth the calories I would ingest trying to finish it. The compost cookie was interesting, with all its various ingredients, but part of the texture was off and somewhat off-putting. Lastly, the crack pie was extremely sweet and seemed predominately butter and sugar. I liked this best, but I also felt like I was slowly killing myself with each bite. Tip: share it with someone else.

Their cereal milk soft serve is JUST AS GOOD as people say! The first bite was AMAZING. I freaking love the salty after taste. Though it does get a bit too much towards the end, that's why it's a 4 instead of 5. I recommend sharing with another person to get the best experience.

UPDATED: In regards of my review, the manager reached out to me and was extremely polite and considerate causing me to raise my star review. I will be giving this place another try because of his kind words & customer service skills. Milk bar was extremely mediocre. The regular vanilla soft serve was disgusting. The chocolate pretzel soft serve was wayyyyy to salty. The crack pie soft serve is by far the best out of all of them. The crack pie is good, but way over rated, I've had much better. The birthday cake shakes had to be the best thing our party got. The girls at the register were nice & polite, but you could tell they were trying to rush through the line because it was slightly busy. Overall it seemed extremely over priced & definitely not good. We will not be returning.

This is a great new addition to the offerings at the Cosmopolitan. They opened today at noon and while they are still figuring out their systems, they are putting out an amazing quality of treats. While I only had the crack'd boozy shake, a crack pie milkshake with liquor, I will be back during my stay. The only thing that would make the experience better would be Christina Tosi feeding us from her hands. Looking forward to all the options they are offering.

I like Milk Bar, but it's all hype and not enough bang for your buck. I believe Milk Bar originates from NYC and is a progenitor of this cereal trend along with Kith, and is a welcome addition to the Cosmopolitan. Like everything else at the Cosmopolitan, it's also overpriced. That's not to say it isn't good. Milk Bar does have some very solid items, from their cookies to their milkshakes, but I've got to say that it doesn't fulfill the craving. When you want a milkshake, you want a heavy, completely guilty item that makes you feel like you've made a terrible mistake but at least your wallet isn't hurting. Here, you'll get something that doesn't quite fulfill the craving, doesn't feel guilty, and hurts your wallet. Not exactly my ideal milkshake or dessert option. It's still definitely worth trying, and the $12 spiked milkshakes are almost fair priced even if downed in basically a minute. $3 cookies sound a bit much, but cookies are generally expensive if you're not getting some cheap grocery option. At the same time, you can get like 50 cookies from Safeway for like $5 so you should also consider that. Milk Bar will be a welcome addition, but definitely not something I'll get every day when I'm in Vegas, or even once a trip. TIP: Get a spiked milkshake because at least alcohol is always overpriced in Vegas.

Tried 4 different cookies. Too sweet, not fresh, not delicious. Lots of ingredients that seem to be there for spectacle rather than effect. Very disappointing. I really wish I hadn't spent the money, and I don't often say that. Frankly I think the celebrity chef/baker with their name on this place should be a bit embarrassed to serve these. I assume the profits outweigh the shame. The counter person was very nice.

I tried the birthday cake milkshake and all I can say is WOW. I've never had a milkshake this good before. As I was drinking the milkshake, it's like I was chewing cake the entire time and it was so delicious. Not to mention, i got a little baby size which was so cute!! I definitely recommend trying this place it is a 10/10 for me.

This is a place I was REALLY looking forward to visiting since it is finally close enough for me to get to it. We ordered the cereal milk, cereal milk soft serve, crack pie, crack pie milkshake, and a corn cookie. The cereal milk and corn cookie were definitely my favorites. The crack pie milkshake was SUPER sweet, and for that reason I didn't have a bite of the pie. The cereal milk soft serve was good, served with lots of cereal piled on top and in the bottom of the cup. I guess my only complaint is that for the price, it wasn't quite as mind blowing as I had hoped. Next time I would like to try the cake bites and will have another cereal milk and some corn cookies.

Being a MasterChef fan (where Christina Tosi is a judge), I was quite excited for Milk Bar. The menu and bookshelf set up is super cute. I ordered the Birthday Cake soft serve ice cream and it was fun and tasty! I will say I thought my friend's Cereal Milk with Cornflakes was better and more unique so I'd order that next time. I don't normally eat a lot of soft serve but I found this to be an enjoyable treat after an afternoon at Marquee Day Club!

Despite the mediocre reviews and people's disappointment over the hype of Milk Bar, I still have to praise their soft serve. People say smell and taste illicit the strongest of memories and that's probably why tasting cereal milk soft serve topped with cornflakes is so nostalgic for me. I realize it is probably one of the most overpriced soft serves in the country, but I will gladly pay $6 (+$1 cornflakes topping) for a piece of my childhood. The soft serve is thicker than typical and each spoonful literally reminds me of the bottom of a bowl of cornflakes. Outstanding. As for the other soft serves, I wasn't a big fan of the fruity [pebbles] soft serve or the crack pie version. For me, I like it pretty simple. They do offer samples for you to try should you want to taste before ordering. In terms of the cookies and pies, these definitely go into the overpriced and over hyped category. Years ago when I first tried their cookies at the original Milk Bar in NYC, the cookies were sold in display cases instead of being wrapped in cellophane. At that time, I thought the compost cookie was the best thing since sliced bread. Now, I think the cookies taste stale and mass produced. The crack pie is also no longer crack to me. It was so overtly sweet that I couldn't understand why I liked it before. However, that isn't to say I won't return for the soft serve. Yum!

CEREAL MILK ICE CREAM END OF STORY. was bummed that it was too damn cold to enjoy soft serve on my most recent trip to NYC (ok i lie my sister shamed me and was like eww don't be basic) I don't care if it's basic I love Milk Bar. This 6 dollar ice cream is so fricking good. I don't understand why all of California is obsessed with Salt and Straw -- this stuff is infinitely better. also the coffee drinks sooo good -- not a super acidic coffee which I appreciate. I tried a latte which was great strong but not bitter and an iced coffee both were fantastic my only regret was not ordering a large iced coffee for the heat.

Cereal milk soft serve topped with cornflakes FOREVA!! So let me preface my review with 'The Before'. I practically rolled myself out of Momofoku looking like Violet Beauregarde after indulging in an unbelievably incredible and massive dinner. I was SO full you guys and that is genuinely an understatement! I overestimated the allotment of stomach space I thought I saved to try Milk Bar's soft serve afterwards - when judgement time arrived I failed myself and my taste buds and sadly commenced my foodie walk of shame... past Milk Bar. *tear* FFW a couple of hours and viola - I found myself back at Milk Bar, feeling like a champ!, around 1am to claim my prize! Mind you, I was still full so I decided to split an order with my friend. As soon as it hit my lips, my god, the heavens spoke to me! That serving, even if just half, was everything in a dessert I never knew I wanted until then. I know it's a bold statement, but I think I experienced nirvana you guys, who knows? I just know that it was me, that cup of soft serve and those cornflakes for a good 10 minutes and nothing. else. mattered. Anyway, we ate at Wicked Spoon for lunch the next day and you best belie' I beelined it back to Milk Bar afterwards and ordered my OWN cereal milk soft serve w/ cornflakes... yuuum! It was just as heavenly as the first time. Bummed their only locations are NYC, DC, Toronto, Las Vegas. Here's to hoping they open one in L.A. sooner rather than later, until then, I'll just be over here daydreaming of that magical encounter.
Yummy yummy yummy! The crack pie ice cream is amazing. Highly recommend. So creamy and rich and they will give you samples of everything.

I tried 2 items here, and was blown away by both of them! Item #1: Everything bagel bomb. Preface: I don't like bagels. Why am I even ordering this....oh yeah...because my friend swears by these things... Post-consumption review: O.M.G. I LOVE bagels now. These are really as good as it gets. It's perfectly warm, doughy and the inner filling is just out of this world. All I can think about now is how I am going to get my next bagel bomb fix since I don't live in Vegas... Item #2: Cereal milk icecream Preface: I don't drink the milk in my cereal bowel after I eat the cereal. Well...I didn't like bagels originally and their bagel bomb changed my mind, maybe this will too? Post-consumption review: I did not know that I needed this in my life until now. This is just like milk in cereal. While, milk left over in my cereal bowl is not what I typically crave (ever crave), this taste is so spot on and intriguing, all I want to do is to continue tasting it and marveling at how interesting it is! Overall = eating adventures here are a total experience. ENJOY, even taste items a little outside of your comfort zone!

Heard the rave about their shakes so had to give it a try. I've only tried the Crack Pie Milk, a slice of crack pie blended into cereal milk, soft serve. It wasn't anything spectacular. It was a bit too sweet for my liking, but to be fair I don't have a super love for overly sweet things. For the price and flavor I most likely wouldn't order again. Maybe next time I'd order something else to give this place a fair shot.
Meh, it was overhyped and definitely overpriced (even for cosmo). I really wanted to like this place but it just didn't cut it.

"You have a Milk Bar in Las Vegas?!?!" says my friend. "You HAVE to get their funfetti birthday cake for the very next person you are buying a birthday cake for." Well I did. I paid $68 (tax & tip included) for their sort of itty bitty looking Funfetti birthday cake. And felt thoroughly underwhelmed. As did the 3 other people who shared the cake with me. I don't know if expectations were just too high, but the cake just tasted dry and mediocre. For an itty bitty 6"(?) cake, it felt heavy enough, but after tasting the cake, I felt like it was more of a $20 cake, not $68. The only positive to the whole experience was that the staff were super nice, and that birthday candles were included. I may go back again to see if anything else is better, but judging by the reviews of others' experiences...maybe not.

Christina Tosi! Love the feel and the cuteness of this dessert stop. Amazing selection of cookies and cakes soft serves and milk shakes. It's a lovely place and there's now an Alice in wonderland themed dining area out in front of Milk Bar and eggslut, super cute picture opportunities! Pro tip: if you don't mind the price get Milk Bar dessert after dining at Momofuku next door - saves time standing in line! The line can get really long.

I got the Cereal Milk soft serve with corn flakes. I have to say, it was really delicious. It actually tasted like the milk after I finish eating the cereal! The service was good, I got my dessert right after I paid because they took my order while I was waiting in line. I don't mind coming back here to order this again and try other flavors
I'm not too much of a dessert person, it was good. A little too sweet for my taste buds but it's good. I mainly wanted to try it because of the Chef's Table episode.

My husband knows I'm a huge Momofuku fan so I dragged him here to get "the original" compost cookie. We grabbed that, along with the cornflake cookie, the crack pie, the blueberry cookie and some other cookies I now forget the names of. All in all, the cookies were DELISH! I really really liked the cornflake cookie a lot - enough to look for the recipe online and try to replicate it. Went there twice since it was an easy walk from the Bellagio and I never had to wait -ever. I would go back again just because I love cookies in general but its something you should try out if you haven't. Try and crack pie...it won't disappoint.

I really wanted to love this place. I'd heard so much about it. NYorkers love this place and I was so happy to finally have one in Vegas. Sad to say, the cookies and the cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes were strange. Flavors were on the savory side. I don't mind savory, but the cookies were not good at all. I took a bite of the 3 Flavors- corn, compost and cornflake chocolate chip- marshmallow. All 3 were meh. I love sweets, but these are not as good as the hype. Two stars as the service was good. Informative and friendly.

CRACK PIE. CRACK PIE MILKSHAKE. CRACK PIE EVERYTHING. I never thought I could NEED a certain kind of food so desperately until I met this goddess. Besides the super friendly staff, the treats are beyond words... I don't know what to tell you. I truly don't. You just have to try it for yourself. Those of us, ie me, who aren't so lucky will have to travel state lines to ever try such a delectable so if you have a Milk Bar in your city, what is stopping you from devouring maybe 10,000 calories per bite/sip? YOLO.
I am obsessed with the blueberry and cream cookies so I had to stop in to get some. Also tried the corn cookie and compost cookies but B and C is still number one in my book.

As a resident of California I get to Las Vegas a lot more frequently than I do Brooklyn, so when I heard about Milk Bar LV opening in my favorite casino/hotel I was soooo excited! This weekend (May 13, 2017) I finally got to visit. I've been to the original Milk Bar so had some expectations. I was extremely sad the pretzel milkshake wasn't an option, so I got the B'day shake which was delicious. My friend got a cereal milk shake and she liked it better, saying mine was too sweet. So if you don't like super sweet maybe skip B'day (but again, I loved it). I also got the 3 cookies for $8 deal ($2.95 each). At the Brooklyn location I had the corn cookie and blueberries and cream cookie, both of which I thought were great. The blueberries and cream cookie was perfect but the corn cookie had an unpleasant flavor. I also got a cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie; it was okay but not my favorite due to the overly chewy texture. While I restrained myself from visiting Milk Bar twice in my 2 day trip, I wanted another B'day milkshake craaaazy bad. Next time I'll probably get the chocolate cereal milk shake. There were TONS of milkshake options. The service was fine, by the way. They were curt and got through the line because they were busy as fawk. Low reviews are just haters.

Meeeeeh! After a tasty and delectable dining experience at Scarpetta I suggested we walk right over to Milk for a post dinner treat. All 10 of us ordered something, you're welcome Milk.... Soft Serve was okay but oddly very salty and I am normally a salty cat. In fact, so were all the cookies we picked up (Double Chocolate and Compost cookies). I bought 2 Blueberry and Cream cookies but gave them away to friends so I couldn't tell you how those were but also didn't get any feedback from those I gave it to. So letdown by Milk and the $80 we spent on Soft Serve and Cookies. $80! Even the girl at the register was a little salty too. I will say that the Fruity Pebbles Soft Serve was the best because it had more dynamic flavor. Otherwise, I'm happy if we never go back. Glad we got to try it though.

I saw a review earlier calling out the affrogato here specifically, and I want to second that: in no way should the 5 stars I'm leaving be considered a general recommendation for everything here, as I haven't tried most of the menu, so I can't really comment. But, on recommendation of several previous yelp reviews, I just tried the affrogato, and it was seriously legit. It's a decent amount of soft serve, a decent amount of coffee, and they go *so* well together. The "cereal milk" flavor is very unique - it's not particularly sweet, which isn't necessarily a good thing in ice cream eaten by itself, but is just the perfect sweetness to accompany coffee. I especially like it because it's really two desserts in one: it's both perfectly-creamy high quality iced coffee (the coffee is served hot, but after melting a bit of ice cream around it, becomes refreshing iced coffee almost immediately), *and* tasty soft serve that's made better by dunking it in coffee before eating it. Highly recommended, and totally reasonably priced at $5, even if it weren't in the heart of the strip. I did try a couple sips of my my wife's cereal milk milkshake, and it was... fine. I wouldn't go out of my way to get that, and felt like $7.50 was a bit overpriced for it (that said, I personally think a rice-based cereal milk milkshake would likely be much tastier than the corn-based one they make currently. I'd come back to try that if they made one, which, to my knowledge, they don't currently.) I *would* absolutely get the affrogato again for $5, though (in fact, I just might get another one tomorrow, before we leave Las Vegas!) Edit: I did, sort of - I decided I had to try the "crack pie" affrogato, too. I told the cashier I was there yesterday and had to try the other one, she said I made a good choice, the crack pie's her favorite. It's good, but personally, I think the cereal milk is a much better affrogato (though the crack pie would probably better by itself - it's like 10 times sweeter.)

Very overpriced, honestly have had better shakes at Burger King. Nothing special about this place at all. I got a slice milk bar pie I thought it would come with ice cream and it didn't, it was like paying $6.50 for a cookie. A milkshake there runs ya $10 totally not worth it

I tried the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes and it's delicious! The corn flakes are lightly salted and they add a nice texture to the ice cream. It's a little on the expensive size though. One soft serve was $6 and to add the corn flakes was an additional $1.25. I also bought 3 cookies for $8, which I haven't tried yet.

Love ice cream? Love cereal? Love sweets in general? This is the place for you. Love a little booze with your milk shake? Even better. We came here mid-day, and it was just the right time for something sweet - and something boozy. I had the fancy birthday cake shake. It was made perfectly so the Kahlua wasn't overpowering and you had plenty of sweet birthday cake flavor. At $12, I thought it was fairly priced since I've had other boozy shakes in Vegas for $15 and over. They had other sweet treats, and I bough pumpkin pie cake truffles (only available in November). They were definitely sweet, but they came packaged so that was a little odd. I expected something freshly made. They were still plenty yummy. If you have time, or even have kids, this is a fun place to stop for some sweet treats.

Being a huge fan of Christina Tosi I was beyond excited to try Milk Bar. I was sadly disappointed. I got a slice of birthday cake, birthday cake truffles, a corn cookie and a slice of crack pie. The birthday cake was my least favorite. The icing had a weird lemon like flavor. The birthday cake truffles were sandy in texture, tasted like a birthday cake pop from Starbucks, but the chocolate replaced with sand. The corn cookie was extremely salty. Like someone replaced the sugar with salt. And the crack pie was alright. It was super sweet and hard to eat more than one bite. It tasted like pecan pie without the pecans. With all the hype and how expensive it was I was hoping for more.

This review is only for the cereal milk soft serve which I got with cornflake crunch. I've been wanting to try this for a long time now, ever since I first saw it on a NYC foodie page when they first opened. However, I think it has been way overhyped, at least for myself. :( I really didn't appreciate the flavor and actually thought it had a weird after taste. It was about $8 and I'm not sure I would get this again. I am open to trying the other options on their menu, such as the crack pie so I may come back! I'd recommend coming here or to a similar location to try it out for yourself!

Finally got to try this soft serve ice cream place that I've always been wanting to try because this place is all hype up and people just have been raving about! The staff was nice to give me samples to try all flavors, and I liked cereal milk flavor because it was not too sweet she very rich milky flavor. To be honest, the soft serve ice cream was really just mediocre and it was very pricey for a small cup as well. I ordered what's the most popular one - cereal milk soft serve ice cream with cornflakes crunch around them, it was yummy and all that, but it wasn't like oh my god! like how I would've expected it. It was just about the hype and it was definitely overrated and overpriced. But, the staff was really friendly and nice to take my order and feed me samples to try though :) this was a cutesy ice cream milk bar/ bakery shop overall!

Came here over the weekend while visiting family in Vegas. Ordered the milk bar pie (?)- formerly "crack pie," slice of birthday cake, compost cookie, and cereal milk soft serve + cereal crunch. The milk bar pie was hands down my favorite and I think is a must try! The compost cookie was prepackaged which may have been why it was a bit dry. The birthday cake was delicious, it was VERY sweet. My friends and I also enjoyed the soft serve. 10/10 stars for service! The lady working behind the counter (Saturday June 22 around 4pm) was so friendly. The other employees were all smiling and all working fast. 4/5 purely for the price. Holy cow, it's quite expensive. The above items plus 2 waters was $40. Despite this, I would definitely come back when I'm in town.

I was so surprised to see Milk Bar at the Cosmopolitan! We were there for breakfast sandwiches from Eggslut and ran right into it. Unfortunately it wasn't opened yet. We decided to come back later in the day to get our fix because it's always crowded in our neighborhood. The crack pie is so damn good! I like to eat it at room temperature. We picked up a few slices and had it as an after dinner treat later in the evening. Of course it was as good as I remembered and I wanted another slice but the guilt of how much sugar is in a slice helped me balance that lol. I'm not quite sure what they put into that pie buts is damn delicious! I can totally understand why they call it crack pie because you always want more. I would definitely recommend that one tries the crack pie and the other treats that milk bar has to offer because everything is good. Crack pie is most definitely the star of the show!

Yikes. You expect a milkshake shop to have some good flavors. Nope. Mostly cereal milk (NO ONE EVER DRANK CEREAL MILK AND THOUGHT, 'you know, the milk is the best part') and a few other flavors. They're all awful. They'll all cost you $10 and you're better off getting a McFlurry across the street, or spend a little more and go to Holstein's. I got the crack pie, my friends got three different cereal flavors, and we all tried all of them. Half of us threw them away after a few bites. I finished mine mostly out of spite and optimism. Side note, if you've been to Milk in LA (I haven't), apparently it's not the same.

Milk and cereal ice cream with corn flakes is a must try if you enjoy your milk after a bowl of cereal. It was divine. To be honest, my wife and I purchased a pail of cookies, and they weren't that great. I think you'd be ok to skip out on the cookies they sell here.

I tried this place knowing already how good their desserts are. My wife brought home a cookie and she had been dying to go back. We actually came here Before dinner this time and bought a tin of cookies. 6 for $17. We also got a slice of their crack pie and it was so good. I recommend you try that first. Next time I will try a shake or some of their soft serve concoctions. Will definitely be back. I'd give it a perfect score but it's a bit too pricey, hey, it is the strip. 4.5 stars.

I can't even remember how long it has been since I have daydreamed of sinking my teeth into the infamous Milk Bar birthday cake. I've lost count of the number of times I have considered visiting NYC just so I can try the compost cookie and crack pie. When Milk Bar opened in Vegas, I finally had my chance! The bakery is right next to Momofuku restaurant. It's just a little walk-up booth where you can order your sweets to go. We had a birthday cake delivered to our table when we were eating at Momofuku. It tasted like a really good funfetti cake. It was a little dry, and had crunchy balls throughout which added a nice texture. Overall, it wasn't the best birthday cake I have had (susiecakes is much better). I also purchased 3 cookies which were also underwhelming. They aren't fresh baked at the store, instead they are shipped in prepackaged from NYC. They tasted a little stale and artificial. I would pass on coming back here again.

I just wanna say thank you Milk Bar and Christina Tosi for opening this location lol. It's still an airplane ride away but at least its on the west coast! Every Vegas trip literally results in a daily trip for Cereal Milk froyo (don't forget the cornflakes!). And thank you for Vegas business hours so we can make it for late after dinner treats!

The Crack Pie Ice cream is TO DIE FOR!!!! Crack pie is also very delicious as well. I've been a longtime IG follower and was pumped to hear that there was a MILK in Vegas back in April. Had a local take me to the money and spent a shit ton of $ on desserts for the 5 hours drive back to California. Best cookies to order in my opinion are the compost and cornflake-chocolate-chip-marshmallow cookie. I honest feel like the cornflake is the best. If you have a craving for corn, grab the cornbread cookie. First time I had it, it hit the spot... Second time around it kind of tasted different. Hoping that that was just the heat and alcohol causing the difference. When ordering the soft serve, do yourself a got damn favor and get the crack pie with cornflakes... That shit is FIRE! OVERALL - love this damn spot & they need to come to SoCal!!

Excellent quality goods! Would highly recommend the soft serve Cereal Milk for the hot Vegas afternoons. The flavors gives you a sense of Saturday morning cartoon nostalgia. Don't be afraid to ask for a sample before ordering, staff are super friendly. Another great find!

This review is only for the cookies. I was excited for milk bar to open in the cosmo, only to find out it takes up only a small area right next to momofuku. Anyway, this review is only for the cookies. We opted to try the corn cookie, blueberry cream cookie, and compost cookie. A little Pricey for cookies, but totally worth it! I loved the corn cookie especially, it tasted a lot like corn bread. I'll be back to try the soft serve the next time I'm in Vegas

Decided to visit this place since it was so hyped by its East Coast stores and it's definitely overrated in my opinion. First of all, the line is almost always really long. You can expect to wait probably at least 15-20 minutes in line. Not sure about the prices in New York but this was probably one of the priciest ice cream places I've been to. A serving of soft-serve is $6 and the milkshakes go from $7-$9 for the basic ones ($12 for alcoholic ones). The serving size of a milkshare is about the size of a Grande cup at Starbucks so it wasn't even that much either. I got the cereal milk milkshake and I actually couldn't even finish it because of the taste. The one good thing was that it wasn't overly sweet but it started tasting worse and worse with every sip. It also felt very heavy for some reason. If you're in Vegas and you want something refreshing to drink/eat, don't come to Milk. The taste, price and line is just not worth it.

I love sugar. I love butter. I don't like when sugar and butter are overused in my desserts. The crack pie, crack pie soft serve, birthday truffles, and compost cookie had too much of the above, which was really disappointing. I threw away those desserts after 2 bites. The cereal milk soft serve with cornflakes was delicious though! Surprised by the comments about overly salty corn flakes. I also REALLY enjoyed the blueberry cream cookie. The corn cookie was yum too. I'll be back for the cereal milk soft serve and blueberry cream cookies!

I got the infamous cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch. It was good but don't see myself getting it again because of how overpriced it was. The single is $6 and $1 extra for the cornflakes (which was a bit skimpy). On a better note, they offered me a free cookie.

Even though Milk Bar has locations in New York, the Vegas location at Cosmo was my first time. I will definitely be visiting the New York City stores. I only ordered the soft serve cereal milk frozen yogurt with chocolate chips. It is reasonably priced at about $7.00 with one topping. I thought the flavor was wonderful - almost a vanilla malt flavor. The combination with the chocolate chips was perfect. As I walked around the Cosmopolitan, guests asked me where I got it. I gladly pointed upstairs and told them to be ready to love every item they were about to lay their eyes on! It all looked delicious and my next time in, I will try some of the other appetizing dessert items. So here is what you do the next time you are having a late breakfast at The Cosmopolitan. Go to Eggslut (see my review) and wait on line for about 30 minutes until you are completely starving. Get and consume your wonderful breakfast there. Then mosey on over to Milk Bar (20 feet away) and order the cereal milk flavor frozen yogurt with a few toppings. You might want to get some of their crazy pastries to enjoy later. Wait about 2-3 hours then for lunch mosey on over to In-N-Out Burger at the Linq (oh wait - that will be a future review). Anytime you have the words bar, Eggslut, In-N-Out, chocolate and crazy in a review, it must be talking about Vegas!

The first time I had cookies from here was when I visited Washington DC. I'm a California girl so when I heard there was a location opening closer to me I was all for it. My go-to order is an assortment 6 cookie tin and Cereal Milk with cornflakes. The cereal milk soft serve is the best and tastes exactly like the leftover milk from a bowl of cornflake cereal.

The Milk Bar has been a huge disappointment for me given how much I love Chang and Momofuku. At the center of the Milk Bar's menu is a sampling of crazy pies and cookies. Sometimes the flavor combinations work better than other times. But the problem with even the best of them is that they're baked somewhere else (presumably in NYC) and shipped across the nation to the various Milk Bar locations. As a result they all taste very much like 3-day old cookies baked at home. They are dense and muted in flavor, and for the price it is a huge disappointment. I tried the ice cream for the first time here as well. I tried both the Cereal Milk and Crack Pie flavors. Both were OK but nothing much to speak of. I had crushed corn flakes added to my Cereal Milk ice cream and also found its strong salted brown butter taste to be off putting. Such a shame, but I'll probably visit again next time I'm in NY to see if it's any better there.

Came here Friday around 1 a.m. and got excellent service. Yes, it was empty but the girls were also friendly besides being available. We tried the pumpkin pie cake milkshake made with their homemade cake balls and it was amazing! I love all the pictures of the dogs on their machines and the fun variety of their menu items. Don't forget to ask for recommendations, the regular employees know what to recommend!

I was so excited for Milk Bar's arrival. And, I was So disappointed. I got 3 cookies, a shake, and a soft serve ice cream. Everything was OK, but for $26 I expected to be blown away and I wasn't. There are off Strip places for way less money turning out a much better product. I wished that this location was more bakery and less walk up counter. I think when you SEE items in a bakery case... It's part of the experience. Everything here is already packaged to go or, with the frozen treats, you don't see them until you get them. Also, there is no seating anywhere. The Birthday Cake shake was tasty, but fairly small for $10. The soft serve cup is one size, but they do fill it up. I got the cereal milk flavor with the cornflake topping. It definitely tasted like it was supposed to which I enjoyed, bit the ice cream had a weird texture that was off-putting...like the cream was curdled or something. I threw it away about halfway through. Cookies was an OK size and a chewy texture, but 3 for $8?!?!? Completely overpriced. I can cross this place off my bucket list, but I won't likely be back.

we stopped by to try their milk bar pie, apple pie milk-quake & soft serve ice cream. the employee was very helpful with helping us order and the lines moved very quickly. the apple pie milk-quake was so good! we loved the apple bits in the shake and the flavor was great. the soft serve flavor we chose was the milk bar pie - it was sweet but the cornflake topping help cut the sweetness down. we also tried their milk bar pie - kinda too sweet for me.

I'm already a Milk Bar fan (been in NY and LA) so really this is just a confirmation that the crack pie could easily be my favorite dessert of all time and that it's just that . . CRACK. give me more! Cookies are quirky flavor combos but they just work . . . personal favs and the chocolate chocolate and the compost.

Customer service was amazing! We picked the crack pie affogato, horrible !!!! Let's just say I believe ice cream is for the soul, but I really had to throw it away, didn't care about my $15. Cereal milk was even worse.
Cereal Milk soft serve with extra crunch topping is sure to be a crowd pleaser. Everyone who I've turned on to this place has become hooked. The long line and wait time would bey only critique.

Ummmm what else is there to say other than EVERYTHING they make is amazing! We had birthday cake, egg and cheddar bombs, and the bagel bombs. The bombs make the absolute most perfect breakfast after a late night out too. So glad it is so close to where we live so we can grab them anytime.

I watched a show about this place, once upon a time, so I knew what to expect. The texture of the soft serve is perfection, however the cereal milk flavor messes with my brain. We ordered the a la mode, which had some sort of chess pie type of desert with the ice cream. The pie is impossible to eat with the plastic spoons that they give you and it is crazy sweet. Overall it was good. I would not repeat it just from a personal taste preference standpoint.

Opening day... first impressions... prices are rather steep for what you get... For opening day there really wasn't much wait at all, went quickly to the registers after coming off of the Cosmo escalator. To get a nice sampling I opted for the "Greatest Hits" combo and the strawberry-corn milkquake. Service was speedy despite a mistake in our order which resulted in a free sweet potato milkquake. The milkquakes are supposed to be similar to a Dairy Queen blizzard or a mcflurry. To my surprise neither was overly sweet, and taste was rather enjoyable. What missed the mark were all the leftover bits at the bottom of the milkquake. A large "boba tea straw" is provided however the chunks are too overwhelming for the straw and unfortunately no regular spoons are available, all that can be obtained is a wooden spatula type. Also the consistency between the 2 milkquakes differed greatly, one was too thick to drink with the straw and the other was super runny. As for the cereal milk soft serve, nothing too spectacular to me. I have yet to try the crack pie, bday truffles, and compost cookies from my combo. However, I don't foresee myself returning to Milk; there are other, better priced, options in VEGAS! Unfortunately.... overhyped

I had high expectations for this place because they have one in ny. I had order cereal milk ice cream and cornflakes. I do not recommend it because it made the ice cream extremely salty. And it was not worth $7, will not be coming back.

I do not understand the reviews on here. This place is all a hype. Do not waste your time and money here. Ordered red velvet ice cream that tasted like pure chocolate ice cream with red food coloring. The texture was strange, somewhat grainy. I also ordered a slice of birthday cake. This has to be the worst slice of cake that I have ever had, and the slice cost $14! I took a few bites and straight to the garbage it went. If you're looking for something sweet, district donuts is just across and much better. I will never eat from Milk nor do I recommend it to anyone.
Gabby has a beautiful smile Precious and James is great I will come here back to get that compost cookie

The cereal ice cream from here is great! The ice cream was smooth, and not too sweet. I added corn flakes which added another level of texture to the ice cream. My only problem with milk bar was that it was pretty pricey compared to other ice cream places that serve a similar product but its expected from an ice cream place in the cosmopolitan. Definately will try the ice cream with the bun next time. I'll be back, definately would recommend.

I love Christina Tosi, but I've found that most of her stuff is too sweet (even for a dessert bar). The staff here was nice enough to let my fiance and me sample the different soft serves. I found them all except the cereal milk to be way too sweet. We ordered a crunchy cereal milk shake and a chocolate shake. I liked my cereal milk shake a lot because of the corn flakes added to it. The next day we went back and replicated our order, except this time I forgot to order my shake "crunchy." The staff was nice enough to add the cornflakes in for me, which made all the difference. We also purchased three cookies (bulk discount) but were disappointed in all of them. The compost cookie had interesting coffee notes to it, but all the cookies tasted way too sweet and honestly kind of stale. We didn't have the birthday cake truffles here, but my fiance has had these shipped to me from Milk Bar in NYC and they are delicious. I would recommend that and the Crunchy Cereal Milk shake, but not much else here.

I have been following Milk Bar on Instagram for months now. Finally trying the cereal milk soft serve with corn flakes was a highlight of my trip to Vegas (yes, I really like ice cream). I also got a few cookies to bring back, cause why not?

To be quite honest, the desserts here are mediocre. My bf said this was apparently "really good" and lines were "out the door" so while dinning at momofuku, we had the option of trying Milkbar via the restaurant. We had the b'day cake truffle and crack pie. Crack pie was alright but it wasn't mind blowing. The bday truffle which is a ball of dough was just odd. Everything was way too sweet and I didn't find it to be very special.

Honestly I had their cakes and crack pie. Have not been to the actual store but was given their Birthday Cake and Crack Pie. Birthday Cake could be a little bit "too sweet" for some but to me it was more rich than sweet. The Crack PIe is the business. If you freeze it it's even better. Again very rich and flavorful and a cross between pecan pie and peanut brittle (without the nuts) but it's one of those things where the whole pie is in front of you and 10 mins later you look down and nothing is there cause your fat ass ate the whole damn thing without realizing it. It's that good imo. Will def go to the store to try other items like the Cookies and Cereal Milk.

Cereal milk soft serve! Without a doubt this was one of my favorite things I've ever had. It's exactly what I was expecting, the cereal milk flavor completely shined through in the soft serve. You HAVE to get the crunchy cereal topping with it. That crunch MAKES the dessert. It's not a sweet cereal-- it's reminiscent of corn flakes but a bit more thick and crunchy. It actually adds a hint of saltiness in the dessert. I'm a huge fan of sweet and salty desserts so this was absolutely perfect. I got cereal milk soft serve 3 times within Labor Day weekend and I wish I could get some right now. As you can guess I didn't try anything else because cereal milk soft serve is all I need! Mmmmm...

Pretty letdown at what "looked" to be an exciting new place. I saw this being constructed a few months ago, and wanted to give it a try. Place is very very small, and full of the drunken guests taking up the line asking for a million samples. Meanwhile 4 other employees just stood around doing nothing really, where they could've helped me. I got a sample of the fruity cereal, and it was pretty gross, obviously full of artificial flavoring and just left a bad after taste. Finally ordered a strawberry "Quake" shake, and a cookie. The shake was a major letdown, and flat of flavor. Couldn't eat more than 2 bites and threw away. The cookie was even worse, just garbage: NO flavor whatsoever. That was thrown away as well. Giving them 1 star for the marketing, as the signs & promotional items got me really interested. Unfortunately I just don't thing they serve a good product. I also liked them open late, but besides that, I'll clearly never return.
Just okay. We had some kind of cereal ice cream. Humphry slocomb is better!

I love to bake and love to try others creations when I can. This place left us UNDERWHELMED. The two stars are for the polite staff encountered on two occasions. We tried an array of items: Crack Pie: Tastes likes pecan pie without pecans in an oily/tasteless crust. Still do not understand the hype around this item. Bday cake slice: It is a decent hunk of cake, but $14 seemed high...but it was my bday so I went for it. I love buttercream..but not buttercream that tastes like over churned butter. The cake itself was cute to look at but it had a tough cornbread taste/texture. Compost Cookie: Truly the worst cookie we ever tasted. It is supposed to have pretzels, chocolate, potato chips and other stuff. All we tasted was a bland oily mess. Cereal Milk Soft Serve: Soft serve was yummy...this was the only one I would call a winner if I had to choose one. It does remind you of the sugary remnants of cereal in milk. Glad we tried it but would not purchase again. They serve this with their signature "cereal flakes" around the edge (beware they charge for the flakes..which they do not tell you) The flakes were not good. They tasted like flakes soaked in butter and salt. Anyone can create a fattening, butter laden dessert...but what about adding flavors instead? Milk is a whimsical and visually appealing dessert bar. That was about it. After spending around $34 for the above treats I still wanted an actual dessert. If you must get something, try the soft serve. But I suggest passing on this place.

4 stars only because they changed their cookie recipe and added eggs!!! 1.Best birthday cake milkshake 2.best customer service 3.best cookies until they changed their recipe and added eggs. (Please make some without eggs for people who like the old recipe) 4.love this milk bar. The best people ever!

Before the Milk store had opened, the CEO of the Cosmo had a cake ordered for a birthday he was celebrating at the restaurant I work at upstairs. After cutting the cake, of course I tasted a piece from what was stuck to the cardboard bottom after slicing. I was so disappointed and didn't understand the craze. I figured it was probably just because the cake had been shipped and was nowhere near as fresh as it should have been. When the store opened up a few months later, all of my coworkers and I were really excited to try everything but the majority of us were let down. The crack pie soft serve tastes like brown sugar-vanilla nothing special. We've tasted tested 6 different cookie flavors which I think is all of them, and nothing has left a lasting impression. Someone else mentioned the cookie is tough and chewy but not the chewy goodness you'd expect. I gave them one more try yesterday before work, and I regret it. The cookies were cold which leads me to believe they're made somewhere else and shipped there, and kept in the fridge until they're ready to be sold. Uhmmm no thanks. The place will be successful because it's inside a hotel and people recognize the name, but I can't imagine a free-standing store surviving here in Vegas.

After trying their cake mixes and seeing all the hype online about Milk, I thought, "this is it. I'm actually gonna be at the real Milk and taste the best sweets ever!"... It was a huge disappointment. It's just a window with only a handful of selections to choose from. I was enticed by their pumpkin ducle de leche bites, so I ordered it, not knowing it was prepackaged like a Hostess Twinkie would be. When the menu advertised that it came in set of 3, I thought they would be boxed up (assuming they were made fresh) and that I'd be able to possibly mix in a birthday cake flavor as well. The cashier told me it was 3 of the same flavor, so i settled with 3 of the pumpkin. When she quickly handed me the prepackaged plastic wrapped truffles , i was a little stunned. They were very cold and felt heavy and hard. I waited a while to have it with coffee and allow it to get to room temp/soften a bit. They softened, but I couldn't taste any dulce de leche. It was just a plain jane pumpkin dessert. It tasted alright, but nothing to write home about and not worth specifically walking to the Cosmo just for Milk. I think they're catering a bit too much to tourists on the go, rather than a fun experience for people who have made the journey to try their goods in person. Food for thought. After all, this is Vegas!

From "Mind of a Chef" to cosmos of happiness. The cereal milk frozen yogurt with corn flakes lived up to the hype portrayed on the show and is the perfect 2am snack while youre partying it up in Las Vegas. I ended up getting the sample platter and loved errrthannnggg outside of the compost cookies and birthday truffle. Crack Pie was everything and more. #nojoke I was back at 215am for seconds.

WHAT A FREAKIN LIFE CHANGING EXPERIENCE!! While my lunch at Momofuku next door left much to be desired, Momofuku's dessert concept Milk Bar was a smash hit!! I asked for samples of both their crack pie and cereal milk soft serves. The crack pie was delicious and decadent but slightly too sweet for my taste, so I opted for the cereal milk, which is probably their most well known dessert anyways. The best decision I made that entire trip, however, was getting a cereal milk affogato - cereal milk soft serve served with a shot of espresso poured over it. That pleasantly elevated the already superb cereal milk ice cream to a foodgasm worthy experience!! The bitter potency of the pulled espresso shot balanced DIVINELY with the sweet, rich, milky creaminess of the ice cream. I was so so so happy - got my coffee fix and had Milk Bar cherry popped in one! Best $5 I've ever spent!! Lastly, not sure why people are complaining about the prices here, btw. You're in Vegas, at a luxury resort on the strip, at one of the most renowned dessert joints in the US. There are plenty of things to be complaining about when it comes to Vegas (maybe the price of clubs, for starters?!); I know you party people can shell out $7 for ice cream.

So. Good. Stopped by after dinner at Block 16. I became a fan of David Chang after watching "The Mind of a Chef", and since Milk Bar is under his Momofuku brand, I had to try it. We were unsure of what we wanted, but tried to order the cereal flavored soft-serve. I think the worker could sense that we were unsure because she asked us if we wanted to sample both flavors before committing. We ended up getting an ice cream swirl of the cereal milk and crack pie flavors coated in corn flakes. Delicious. Smooth, not to sweet/heavy, and it definitely hit the spot. We got a slice of crack pie to go and it held up well in our suitcase back to the DFW area. The pie was extremely rich but not too overbearing since we split the slice. I pray that they open one up near me!

I visited Milk Bar twice during my recent stay in Vegas. The first time I got a fantastic Boozy Coffee milkshake. The guy making the drinks was informative, patient with EVERYONE in line asking "what's cereal milk" ** and he made sure it was done right. The result was a fabulous, just the right thickness, not too boozy, just the right coffee essence masterpiece. The second time I went no one seemed to know how to make the SAME milkshake I ordered before and it was dismal. Way too thin this time with no balance of flavors and really not at all worth the $12 price tag. We ordered two and they came out different, neither of them like the fantastic one I had the day before. Bad execution issues.

Milk Bar is definitely one of the most unique ice cream/dessert shops I've been to. Their class cereal milk ice cream with cornflakes threw me off. I was expecting a sweet, creamy flavor but was struck with slight sweetness overpowered by salt from the cornflakes. The ice cream takes a more salty approach than sweet. I also tried their compose cookie - one of a kind taste made with unconventional ingredients. Definitely worth a try. 3 stars because my taste buds say no but obviously Milk Bar has a huge fan base from all the 5 star reviews.

I was really bummed that I didn't get a chance to check this place out when I was visiting NYC, as this place is mentioned in pretty much every article that goes something like, "25 things you must eat before you die in NYC." So I was thrilled to find out that a location opened in Vegas, a place where I visit much more frequently than NYC. Turns out that I wasn't missing out much. I tried the cereal milk soft serve w/ cereal crunch, crack pie, compost cookie, cornflake marshmallow cookie, and corn cookie. Cereal milk soft serve was nice; it wasn't too sweet, and it indeed tasted like milk where cereal had been soaked in. But it's not something that I would crave again. Crack pie - Sadly, this pie did not live up to its name at all. It was dry on the outside, mushy on the inside, and sickeningly sweet. Just imagine what baked butter with a crap ton of sugar would taste like... Yep. All the cookies - Super dry & way too sweet. Not to mention that all of these items are overpriced. (Soft serve & crack pie were both $6 , the cookies were something like $3 each) All in all, the soft serve is worth trying once. Don't bother getting the pie or the cookies.

We walked right up after dinner. The person working was really helpful with recommendations. I had the chocolate chip cornflake cookie which were good and the birthday cake truffles which were great! It is expensive, but a fun, unique treat.

After hearing about Milk & their looong lines in New York, I was excited for it to open in Vegas at the Cosmo. It finally opened in late December & I was able to see what the "hype" was all about. We got a slice of the Crack Pie, cereal milk soft serve with cornflake toppings & crack pie soft serve with cornflake toppings as well. I spent $20 for these three items. I also was confused about the toppings & thought the cornflakes already came with the soft serve but I was wrong. However, they were nice about it & didn't charge me $2 for the two toppings ($1 per topping). I tried my crack pie soft serve first. My first bite was good with the salty cornflake topping mixed with the super sweet soft serve. But after a few bites, especially when I ate all the toppings already, it wasn't that great. It was also messy to eat since they overload the soft serve onto a mini cup so be prepared with extra napkins or wet ones. I didn't even bother finishing my soft serve since it wasn't worth it anymore. Next, I tried their crack pie. I've read reviews on yelp about how good it is; however, when I took a bite, I wasn't impressed. There was nothing extraordinary or good about it. It was cold & mushy. It didn't taste like anything, tbh. I wish I could say Milk was amazingly good & too die for. But I would be lying if I said it did. It was disappointing. Maybe the original location in New York is waaaay better than this one.

Update: I came back and ordered the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmellow cookie and of the three cookies I've tried there, it's my favorite. I took it to go and I wish I ordered a couple more. I love the texture of the cookie. It's chewy but has some crunch every now and then from the cornflake crunchies in it. And the taste isn't overly sweet which is what I liked. Get it. You can't go wrong :)

Someone left these chocolate cake truffles in the office and I decided to take one. They are round chocolate balls with brown powder surrounding it. I popped it in my mouth and my jaws dropped. It was SO good. I'm very picky with my brownies but these are easily one of the bests I've had. When you bite into it, it crumbles into little pieces. For lack of better terms, it kinda looks like dirt- but extremely delicious dirt. Another coworker of my walked into the office pantry and popped one of these babies in his mouth- his eyes lit up and jaws dropped as well, "What the hell are these?! They are SO GOOD." I was glad someone else shared the same genuine reaction. One day I decided to stop by Cosmo to pick up some for my family so they can try them- I've been telling them how amazing these chocolate cake truffles were. They were $6.49 for 3 little truffles... whatever, still worth it. But when I tried them this time they are solid hard- the brownie isn't soft and crumbly as the first time. Then I realized they take them out from the fridge as they sell them to keep them fresh. :( Okay so what I'm trying to say here is you have to try these chocolate cake truffles but when you purchase them they come straight out of the fridge so make sure you wait till the brownies are room temp before you eat them because it taste the best when they are soft. :)

Okay, so two weeks later almost all their cookies are sold out? Today they only had Chocolate Chocolate and Corn Cookies... While I knew it was wishful thinking to think they made the cookies onsite (they are all packaged), selling out confirms it. I hope they get their supply figured out. They are missing out on a lot of business.
It was ok had the milk cereal ice cream differently different than anything ice cream I have tried before.
No line no wait and think the price is slightly cheaper then the in west 4 NYC location. Always love their cereal milk soft serve with crunch.

Plastic wrapped cookies and five dollar jars of dry cereal. We tried the compost and marshmallow/whatever cookies and you really just taste sugar above the other flavorings. I am still going to try the original Milk in NYC because grabbing the cookies when they are fresh baked is probably a completely different experience.
Omg for the best service and ice cream out of the. Ix u can't beat fruity pebbles shake. Gabby and Samantha rock !!
We heard about Milk Bar from Chef's Table's recent documentary on Christina Tosi, and since then, sought to try the infamous Crack Pie and Milk & Cereal soft-serve; it was a sweet snack!

Yes, it is hyped up because of David Chang. No it is not the same as the Milk bar on the east coast in regards to sitting in and dining. It is as stated, a "bar" that serves quick desserts. Much like an expensive Starbucks, created by a 2 Star Michelin Chef... It is a very good option for dessert. Being local I've been back a few times during the day - no long lines and one Saturday night during CES and was 12 deep. Not a factor cause the staff was prepared and had the line moving pretty well. Each time that I have went, the staff was really helpful and if there was a lag in service, they apologized cause some of them were still learning how to make certain things. The Crack Pie - on point, just like the one I tried at the east coast Milk Bar. The crack pie in shake form - yeah 10 bucks but it is Vegas. Competition will cause the prices to lower a little and stabilize. (maybe) Really sweet and rich - so bring your sweet tooth or have something pretty savory beforehand. Cookies - had them all but my fav is the compost and Corn flake with choc. and marshmallow. The one I liked the least was the chocolate chocolate chip. That was a little too sweet for me but I'm sure there are people out there who like them. Birthday cake Truffle - Was ok to me but my cousin loves them. They don't have the steam buns... Yet, but I am hoping that will happen. Sad to see some of the reviews be really picky with a place that just opened up. Give it a second chance and see how they have evolved to work out their kinks. I know that some are looking for that "experience" - I get it. Then dine in at Momofuku for that. I'm glad that Momofuku and Milk Bar are here and I look forward to returning.

This was the redeeming grace of our night at the cosmopolitan after our diner at DOCG was a train wreck. We had the crack pie milk shake that tasted like a vanilla shake on steroids. So delicious. We also grabed the tin of 6 cookies to give to some friends at work. Some really interesting flavors for the cookies, I think the one that stood out the most was the corn flake cookie. Ow so good.
Crack pie yesss! Blueberry pie cookie noooo! Well that's all I had but I would go back and get a whole pie!

I really don't see what the hype is about. Overpriced for what it is and taste is pretty average. I went here around 12pm on a busy weekend and there was a line to order and everyone was excited to try it but afterwards I and 2 friends didn't find anything exceptional.

The dessert bar looks cool and are operated by nice people. They have baskets of cookies arranged in the front and a chalkboard menu. Only ordered the most recommended dessert, the birthday cake, since I make it a habit now to try the best thing before buying a lot of things (especially at $16/ slice with tax). Not a huge fan of the cake. The portion was substantial but the cake was dry and the frosting was plain. A friend complained it was too sweet. I'd have rather bought the pillsbury funfetti cake mix and made it myself for much cheaper and same taste. Don't waste money here for any hype, it's not worth the price or the calories.

MILK BAR!! Ahhhh sugary goodness I've been dreaming about since they were only open in NYC...until they came to Vegas!! Lucky for me, since I come here 2-3 times a year! Let's get on to the good stuff. GET THE ICE CREAM. Sooo so so good. I am a sucker for cereal milk and anything cereal milk flavored. I got it mixed with the birthday cake and was definitely not disappointed!! BLUEBERRY COOKIES. Super delicious and soft. They stayed pretty soft when I took them home a few days later!! The corn one is good too. I would pass on the other flavors though. SKIP THE ALCOHOLIC MILKSHAKES. They were so horrible and overpowering with the alcohol flavor. Ugggghh such a waste of $13. That's the reason why I lower it a star. Yes it's Vegas, but I couldn't taste any milkshake at all! Just vodka. Bleghhh. I always make a point to come here when I'm on the strip!

Okay so I was taken here by a friend. But once I got here I was pretty excited! I personally got a slice of the vanilla cake and 3 cookies. And while the cake was good at first I really expected better, but the cookies OMFG they were so good. So personal opinion here, but get the cookies...they are worth it!

Guys, maybe it's just me? But I'm not a fan. I don't get the hype. Besides the service, everything else ranged from underwhelming to not delicious. I'm not a fan of the cereal milk soft serve, nor was anyone else in our group of five people. The crack pie soft serve was not my jam, either. The b'day truffles taste like a Starbucks cake pop without the fake chocolate coating. Everything kinda tastes the same, and it's not a taste I want more of.
