Hands down answer was Custard Cup cold fudge. What is cold fudge? How is it different from all the other's? After listening to them raving about it and the anticipation of this so called cold fudge, we have have finally arrived at the cup. I didn't realize there were so many other flavors and I was curious what they were. My friend didn't know what they were either, frankly, it didn't matter as long as cold fudge was on the menu. Finally, custard in hand, so much hype has built up that I was now thinking it would be a letdown. I took one bite and in a few minutes I am scraping deep into the styrofoam cup. I liked that it tasted like real natural chocolate. All I can say is, I am officially hooked.

Jarling's Custard Cup is a Champaign institution. Whenever my family from out of town/state comes to visit, they have to go to Custard Cup. First, I *HIGHLY* recommend going at times when they're less busy if you don't like waiting in lines because it's a popular place. They open at Noon daily, and there's usually no line if you go between Noon-2pm (not sure about later times in the afternoon but I imagine it's not so busy on weekdays). I have also been around 8pm on weeknights and while it looks like the place is a madhouse (parking lot completely full), once we finally found a spot to park, there was only one person in line before us (because people were just hanging out at the picnic tables outside). One more pro-tip: there are THREE lines (one at each window), so go inside and pick the shortest line rather than going in the first door and thinking you have to wait in that same line. Now, let's get to the custard: I have such a hard time making a decision each time we go because there are literally SO many things I love. My favorites include: brownie fudge sundae, cold fudge milk shake, cold fudge and peanut sundae (their cold fudge is a specialty and tastes delicious), berry delightful parfait (with strawberries, raspberries, blueberries), banana split snowstorm (their version of a blizzard), and caramel apple snowstorm. They always have vanilla, chocolate, and strawberry and then they have a flavor of the week. My husband usually gets regular custard (any flavor) in a cone. Our family members have gotten a variety of different snowstorms and are never disappointed. You really can't go wrong here. Check it out!

Long wait for OK ice cream. I stood in line for 20 minutes and watched two families cut in front of everyone because they knew someone. Ended up leaving out of frustration. The new owners need to take a course on process management or hire on someone who is an expert in the subject. It is interesting how Culver's, which has equally as good custard, can get me in and out in minutes but I have to make a calendar appointment if I want to try Jarling's again.

Cold fudge shake = heaven. Seriously. I think it's my favorite cold dessert of all time. Only give it 4/5 stars because their service is SLOW. I drank an entire medium cup of coffee while waiting in line to get service. And I'm a slow coffee-drinker. The cold fudge shake is so good that it's almost worth the wait, though.
I ordered Jarlings delivery today as a treat for the office--it was delivered on time and in good order, and of course, delicious as always. I highly recommend their delivery.
Try the cappuccino with root beer! Sometimes just a snowstorm is too much so the root beer offsets the constant sweetness!

Custard Cup is a LONG-time family-favorite (I have memories of going there when I could barely walk), but today I had such shockingly abysmal treatment from a long-time employee that I felt moved to jump on yelp to say something about it. Someone in my group was having trouble deciding between two things while we were ordering, and she said "just make up your mind, because there ARE other people waiting to order" in a nasty tone. For the record, there were two other couples in the place and both had already ordered. We weren't holding anyone up, and even if we had been it wouldn't be by much... and while it's her job to make sure things move along, it should NOT come at the expense of acceptable customer service. I left the place stuck between feeling shamed by the employee and shocked at her treatment of us... not the way that loyal customers should be made to feel by any business. I doubt it will affect my future patronage, because after 20+ years of Custard Cup in my life, one bad experience won't keep me from returning while I'm visiting my former C-U 'hood. It has soured the magic for me, though, and this can no longer be one of those pristine childhood memories. Say it ain't so - what's next, Curtis Orchard??

While not the glory that is Ted Drewes, Jarling's provides an outstanding experience. The atmosphere here is friendly and welcoming. The custard also invites you to eat it. I am not normally a marshmallow or fluff fan, but the black and white with cold fudge has made me rethink my aversion. I still don't like the store-bought junk, but will get a Black and White any time I am in Champaign.

Pretty tasty. I got a single scoop of chocolate. Yeah, I know boring, right? But it was chocolate done right. Very creamy and chocolaty. My two complaints would be that the chocolate custard seemed to start melting as soon as it hit the cone, and the cone was a bit stale. .

yum.yum.yum. i am so happy when this place is open!!! i can't really comment on much of their menu because i continually go back to the peanut butter cup snowstorm. it's not just reese's peanut butter cups that you get at dq (though i do love me some dq, don't get me wrong), but in this snowstorm it's a swirl of fudge and peanuts and my oh my, soooo good. best part is i can only eat half of a junior at a time so i have some for the next day as well. can't wait to step out of my comfort zone and try their fruity flavored custard (here's looking at you lemon custard) and possibly some other snowstorm flavors.... cash only. but for this treat i don't mind stopping at the atm beforehand. now stay open all year long!

It's pretty good stuff, although a little pricey. I'm a fan of the cold fudge and tortoise sundaes. And the waffle cones- yum. I mean, it's your average local ice cream shop- a great idea for when family comes into town, or you're just not sure what to do with yourself, you want to splurge on a treat for yourself, etc.

A Champaign institution! I bring all my out-of-town relatives and friends here when they visit during the spring and summer. It's one of those things that lets you know that summer really is on its way; when Custard Cup opens up in the spring, it gives you a sense of hope that winter may, at some point, end. All the flavors and toppings are delicious. Summer evenings, it's THE place to be, and there always seems to be plenty of outdoor seating despite the crowds.
I love this place. It's a staple from college and worth a trip here everytime. It's such great custard...it makes me want to make the sucky drive down 57 right now.

I rate frozen custard places on one criterion: chocolate chips. There are innumerable ways that you can have a concrete and the superior combinations involve something-CHIP (I use the blueberry-chip as a litmus test). On the one hand, inferior custard stands will throw in a handful of actual chips, or the mini toll house chips, something like that. They do that because they do not respect us enough to think that we care. Culver's and DQ, I am talking to you (they are not even real custard stands, but sadly, that is all that most people will ever know). But if you do care, then you know that the way to -chip a concrete it to put a layer of the hard-shell chocolate topping into the middle -- the effect being that when you blend it the custard is infused with tiny little frozen shards of chocolate goodness. If the custard stand respects you and your highly developed tastes, they will serve you that way. Jarling's does that right, and earns my Champaign loyalty. That is all there is to know; the custard is good, it would have been five stars had they used fresh blueberries, but it was the first hot and humid night of the year so they get something of a pass. So glad that summer is back....

I had never had custard before Jarlings aka honestly was not living before Jarlings. I haven't tried many things on the menu because everytime I get either vanilla custard + cold fudge or the turtle sundae. Once I came 3 times in one week. The custard is so creamy!

Hmmm, not bad but I have had creamier custard. I tried the limited edition cherries jubilee with cold fudge topping. Was hoping for fresh cherry flavor since cherries are in season, but got a pepto-bismol pink concoction with strong overly sweet maraschino cherry flavor. Combined with the cold fudge it tasted like those chocolate-covered cherries you can buy in a box at the drugstore. Husband's chocolate custard with almonds on top was a much better choice. We didn't wait in line and the service was fine. I winced at the amount of styrofoam they must be contributing to landfills, but maybe it's needed to make the custard stay cold longer. I'd be happy to use paper and eat faster! Cash only, kids, or take your old-fashioned checkbook.

A Champaign staple that all the locals go to and if you attend the University of Illinois it certainly needs to be on your bucket list. The only thing you will regret about this place is not coming to it sooner! I absolutely love it from the snowstorms (their take on a blizzard) to one dips of the flavor of the week to their hot sundaes. I always try to try something new. The prices are extremely reasonable and what can be better than supporting a local business. They are not open in the winter so by the time March rolls around you are ready to have your first taste of the season. If you drive by and there are lines out the door don't turn around - the wait is worth it and not to mention will give you plenty of time to look over the menu.

Superb. I pretty much go here constantly when they're open for the season. It makes winter all the worse with no Custard Cup. I'd eat it outside in the middle of a blizzard it's that good. Snowstorms are an obvious go to here. I look forward to my favorite flavors of the week (Cold Fudge, Cake Batter, Key Lime, Mango, and the former regular Orange) but just a vanilla with Oreo or Heath is outa this world, also lemon custard with fruit cup on a hot day is perfect. Well made Chocolate Sodas here might be the best thing I've ever eaten and Green River shakes are also a favorite. Just go and keep going. There's so much menu to explore and it's all incredible.

I remember going to Jarlings with my grandparents and getting orange custard when I was 4 years old.... I go back EVERY time I'm in Champaign and the custard is just as I remembered. :D The fruit flavors are still my favorite too. CASH ONLY

Old school custard. You can't live here without trying it. In grad school, I lived a couple of blocks away, and I only went here a couple of times. What was I thinking? Skip your forgettable entrees and come here instead. Delicious!

Stopped at this local favorite while in the C-U area last week. I got a medium peanut butter and chocolate (I forget the name but its basically a blizzard) and my hubby got the same type of thing but with coffee and oreos. The mediums are a good size (I wanna say 16 oz.?), though a bit expensive at $4.95. The price seemed a bit steep only because this is a custard place and to be honest, I've had better custard. Theirs wasn't bad, it just wasn't as extraordinary as the locals we went with made it out to be. Pros: lots of outdoor seating and some minimal indoor seating, they take cash and credit, variety Cons: no bathroom which meant my 3 year old nephew had to be walked across the (fairly busy) street to pee instead of just going while we waited for the order. This left both him and dad with melted custard when they returned. Also, and this is one of my pet peeves, they charge for water. I understand that the cup costs money and all that but if I'm dropping $30 on custard then I'd like to skip the 10 cent charge for the water.

I love this place.... it is five stars. Their cold fudge is the best. Yes, it may not be real custard --- Culver's is closer to custard than Jarlings, but still Jarling's is AMAZING. My only gripe ---- since changing owners..... it was the Friday before Labor Day --- September 4, 2015..... the local pools are celebrating their last weekend of the season. It's 94 degrees out....it's going to be mid 90's all weekend long..... wow, Jarling's would really hit the spot on this super hot sunny weekend..... oh wait.... the parking lot is empty....the barricades are up. Sign in the window says, CLOSED FOR THE SEASON. Hello?!?! It's still summer!!! It's not even Labor Day..... you closed four days ago on August 31st?!?! What the hell?!??!!!!

Our family favorites: *Strawberry milkshake, specify "made with real fruit" ~~A MUST TRY!!!~~ *Lemon custard in a waffle basket with raspberry topping *Banana split snowstorm made with strawberry custard I've been going to Jarlings all my life and it's always been a staple for my family. I adore their lemon custard and I order it every time. Unfortunately, last night my lemon custard tasted different, almost bland. Out of the hundreds of times I've ordered the lemon, this is the first time I have been let down. I'm sad to say that it seems that quality standards are slipping since the change in ownership. The new POS system is nice, but it's t doesn't really save time when the order is rung up incorrectly. We ordered in the drive through, an employee came out to the car and wrote our order down on a notepad. She tried to upsell my scoop of lemon in a waffle basket w/ raspberry topping as a sundae, and I had to explain a few times that I really just want a scoop of lemon in a waffle basket with raspberry topping. Otherwise, I would gladly order a sundae. My dad's giant milkshake was written down as a regular and had to be remade. Back when the employees had to take orders by memory I honestly think it forced them to pay attention to the order and care if it was right, I've never had a problem with my order in the past. I hope our experience last night was a fluke and not the new normal, I will be so sad to see Jarlings go out of business if these small issues continue to add up.
Outstanding flavor and freshness. Drive thru moves well even with a line. Good service.

Greatest ice cream ever. If you are within 300 miles of Urbana-Champaign, take an unforgettable detour to Jarling's. You can thank me after you have swooned on two large scoops of their vanilla "custard" ice creams topped with pecans, bananas and fudge
Fun outdoor seating and the lemon custard tastes perfect for the summer! ($1.97 for a single scoop)However, the overhead menu is overwhelming and outdated in appearance.

I have nothing against this custard place. Its old school, and an institution I'm sure. It has a ton of different menu items for the frequent visitor and I am sure that its custard is really good, compared to other custard stands. However, in my humble fat opinion, custard sucks. It is just not that good of a dairy dessert. Sorry, but custard is basically soft-serv iced cream with a little zing, owing to the addition of egg and/or a little fermentation. Anyway, not my thing. I would much rather go for scoops of "regular" American-style ice cream, a la Baskin Robbins down the street or, better yet, gelato (if its fresh) at Pekara.

I remember visiting my uncle and going to Jarlings Custard Cup as a child. I'm an adult now and it was just as delicious as I remember! I got the Banana Cream Pie Snowstorm and it tasted better than a blizzard from dairy queen! My other family members got Root beer floats and they said that they tasted delicious as well.

It's a little different than having regular ice-cream, but it you're in the mood for something rich and tasty you will not be dissappointed. I happen to be a fan of the Snowstorms myself; there are tons of different varieties to choose from. Also, they have Green River Slushees which I've never found anywhere else!

My go-to ice cream place in the summer! The lines are usually long and you have to wait a while, but they have some delicious snowstorms! They also have a drive-thru, which I have never used, but that is because I like to sit out front at the tables in the parking lot. Perfect place to go with friends on a beautiful summer night for a yummy treat!

The best ice cream/custard in the world! Or, at least in the country! Jarlings Custard Cup and Papa Del's are the only two things I miss in Champaign. I've moved to CA and every time I go to visit Chicago, I have to drive down to Champaign to get this yummy yummy dessert. I love the hard shell chocolate snowstorm the best! I don't think this is on the menu. Just ask them to pour the hard shell chocolate stuff on top of the custard and blend it. It's to die for!!!! I also like the grasshopper. Just try the different snowstorms. They are all pretty damn good! I miss you Custard Cup. You should open one in the SF bay area. You'd put all the sorry ice cream creamery around here out of business!

The frozen custard here is absolutely delicious! My two favorite flavors are the strawberry and orange. Compared to dessert places in the city, Jarling's prices are cheap. I would highly recommend anyone who visits Champaign to stop by here for at least one dip (one scoop). I have tried their snowstorms as well (strawberry custard as the base, with cheesecake mixed in), which is equally tasty. The portions are generous, so sharing shouldn't be a problem. ;]
The best icecream place in town! Try the coconut, lemon custard

It's good. But there's so much hype about it that I expected more. Indoor seating would be nice on a hot summer day. The whole establishment screams of Midwest country homemade ice cream/custard/whatever.

I love Jarling's Custard. Every time I try something new, I'm never disappointed. A smooth, buttery finish with strong flavors, this place always serves the best. I usually get the coconut seasonal custard, peach cobbler snowstorm, strawberry cheesecake snowstorm, coffee/espresso snowstorm or grasshopper (mint chocolate) snowstorm. Everything here tastes divine, so don't be afraid to experiment! Also, junior cups are huge, so order in moderation.
Delicious custard with a bit of a steep price, but it's worth it for the good service and the experience overall. I've loved this place since I was a kid.

First of all, Jarling's custard cup is NOT custard. I assume it used to be custard at one time. It isn't anymore, but they've retained their name. The website clearly states that they serve "Ice Milk". "Our Product is Ice Milk. It has 30% less butterfat and cholesterol than traditional iced cream and contains no eggs." Try to make custard without eggs. Oh wait, you can't because eggs are one of the defining ingredients! If you have had real custard before, then just go to Jarling's knowing it's NOT custard, and it'll be okay. I went thinking it was custard and was disappointed. It all made sense when I found out the truth. I highly recommend the lemon flavor. We're used to lemon tasting artificial. Lemon meringue pie, lemon bars, lemonade, etc. all taste artificially sweet and like, well, lemon flavoring. That's why lemon tastes the best at Jarling's. You are used to and expect the artificial taste. The other flavors taste artificial (because the ingredients are), but they're not satisfying. Personally, I prefer natural strawberry flavor over artificial strawberry syrup. This applies to almost every flavor, except lemon! The waffle cones are generally good. The best part of going here is watching the employees create snowstorms and sundaes. You can see that they are using a freshly opened Snickers candy bar in your treat rather than scooping sitting pieces out of a bucket. TIP: If you don't want to wait in line, go on a rainy day!

Chambananites, Thank you for introducing me to this place. When I first heard about it, I was a little grossed out by the idea of "custard cup." Mainly I recall my past experience of rock-solid curd that everyone calls custard. However, I now understand that frozen custard is just a better and tastier version of ice cream. The selection of flavors is impressive and their ice cream cakes are tasty and great for parties. The biggest problems I have with the place is that they don't take credit cards and they are closed for winters. Man, I would still come to Jarling's even if it was below zero. It is that good!

- Heeaavvennlly custard - Reasonable prices/sizes - Great parking and outdoor seating - Awesome service Custard Cup is one of the staples of things to try in Champaign, IL. As a native Champurbanian, I awaited Custard Cup's re-opening with glee along with

The #1 best thing about Jarlings is the speedy, friendly service. Well, at least it was the one whole time I've been there. There were a ton of people there, but the line moved very quickly (which was good for everyone nearby--I had serious custard jones). #2 best thing is, of course, the custard. I had a 'mini' butterscotch sundae, which was *plenty* if you just want a little something. Mini my foot, really. It's a large scoop of custard. SO worth it for the meager price tag of $2.55. #3 best thing is all the fixings available.....like butter pecans or pecan pralines. Or both. I'm drooling just thinking about that. And I cannot *wait* to try a "Snickerette Snowstorm." Mmm....bad for me...

I dig this place! The fact that it's constantly packed every day of the week tells me this place must be doing something right! Tried the snowstorms, which are the Jarling's equivalent to a Dairy Queen Blizzard. Overall great ice cream, good for date nights or the "just 'cuz!" moments! They're still old school with their drive through with only one window and can only take, and make, a single order rather than build a queue of orders to help speed things along. Worth the wait in my opinion though!

I love this place. It's not the best, but it' s definitely not the worst. What's great about Jarling's is that it's always exactly the same, and that's good. Jarling's cares nothing for trends, for fashion, for progress. You will never go there and see to your dismay that it has gotten a piercing that it thought was cool but is by now completely cliched, a tattoo of something coyly cryptic, or that it prefers only bands that are so pure that they haven't yet been formed. It's Jarling's. It listens to whatever station comes in best on the AM band in the car and it hopes you brought your appetite because there's a lot of stuff to eat. It's beyond cool. It's eternal.

Boy do I loooooove Custard Cup! I'm not a big ice cream person, but this stuff is awesome! My only gripe is that they don't accept credit cards... but it's so good that the one time I forgot cash, I chose to drive around Champaign for 20 minutes looking for an ATM because I was that desperate for Custard Cup. I've only had the chocolatey-type snowstorms like butterfinger, grasshopper, reeses, etc, but I'm sure the others are just as awesome. And the place is always packed which is a good sign that the place is pretty freaking sweet. Mmmm I want some Jarlings right now!! It's way better than Cold Stone, Marble Slab & DQ combined!!

Brought my hubby here for the first time and decided to get the vanilla and orange custard. It was pretty good, but as we were finishing our cup, we smelled the waffle cones and had to get it! So we ordered the strawberry custard in a waffle cone. I could barely get a lick in before my hubby engulfed the whole thing! This was RIGHT AFTER we finished our first cup of ice cream too! Yes, it was THAT good!

An absolute five-star dessert place. Their custards are to die for! I LOVE their orange shake, mint chocolate chip snowstorm, lemon custard and nut parfaits. They have so many snowstorm options, you will definitely find a combination of your choice. They offer a different 'flavor of the week' every week. Of the ones I tried, found peach and peppermint to be super yummy!

I totally love that you get your custard and then sit out on the picnic tables. It is as close to "the good old days" as it gets anymore. I really like that you can add banana to anything too! And I've gotten my kids the Teddy Bear Custard Cup a couple of times, its cute. They love it and its pretty cheap. Its just a regular cup of custard with like 5 teddy grahams stuck in the custard and you can add banana or nuts or whatever.

Open only in warmer weather, these design-your-own custard creations are akin to Dairy Queen - but better! The wait in the long line at the stand is worth it. Choose your custard, pick candy or nuts to have blended in, and enjoy. If you're counting calories, hold out for the pumpkin pie custard, available in the fall only.
This place is a landmark in CU. Not too expensive, great variety, comforting ambiance. If you're not a local, you will still get those nostalgic feelings when you stop by here. A+

Ah, the memories. I have been coming here since the 80's. I probably have hundreds of visits here. I spent nearly all of that decade at Uni here. And I just graduated an offspring as well. No trip to CU is complete without a stop here. Heck, I used to walk here from FAR. The product has remained unchanged over the years; the custard has less fat than ice cream, and is smooth and creamy and flavorful. I've had sundaes, but love the Snowstorm. The fruit ones are my favorite. The lines are long. There are three lines, one for each window. They move slowly since everything is hand dipped. No extruders here. Marriages have been contracted in these lines. LTRs have broken up in these lines. I'll bet some lady has had her water break, but couldn't leave because she was next in line at last!! They have abundant outdoor seating and a drive-thru. Check it out--Classic and good. Always delivers.
Not too expensive, custard is good too. We got snowstorms and they were pretty standard. Sizing is great t

Pretty awesome. I've been going to this place since I was little, and it's been consistently good as far as I can remember. THE ONLY THING, is that I wish they had a cake batter flavor, it's my favorite and sometimes it's the only thing that brings me to Cold Stone. Other than that, I love Custard Cup. I usually get a cookie-dough snowstorm, cold-fudge sundae, butterscotch sundae, or strawberry custard, but you can never go wrong, seriously. I never feel like it's officially summer until this place is open!

This was my go-to study break place (when it was open) when I lived in C-U. I miss it! I never ordered anything I didn't like. The service was quick and helpful and patient considering I always stood under the enormous sign and said WHAT DO I WANT? The only downside is cash-only. But there is an ATM in the grocery store across the street, if needed.

The ice cream is great. The service is TERRIBLE!!! the people got two of our four orders wrong, but refused to remake them. They just looked at us, and kept saying "no, this is what you ordered". What happened to the customer is always right? Very frustrated with the rude service. After beging a regular, I won't be going back after numberous bad service experiences now!

Anyone that gives Jarlings Custard Cup below a 5 star rating is functionally insane, or, they were huffing spray paint in the preceding 5 hours before enjoying their tasty treats. Seriously, Jarlings is that good. To those drawing similarities between their product and ice cream? You're gastronomically challenged. Yes they are both cold and dairy based, but it ends there. Their custard is obviously so much denser and creamier than ice cream. Ice cream by process has to have a bunch of air stirred into it. The only knock on the Jarling organization is that they don't want to franchise it or distribute the secret process. Jarlings inc world wide could have an IPO greater than Google's ;)

Excellent frozen treats for hot summer nights. The menu is more than just custard. Jarlings has cups, cones, sundaes, shakes, frozen cakes, and floats (i.e. rootbeer floats and other combinations). Lemon custard really hit the spot for me. The lines can be a bit long (and one day they ran out of vanilla custard, which was a buzz kill) but it is worth the wait. Also, $10 minnimun for credit card purchases could be less than fun if you're not expecting it, but they take debit cards with credit logos without a minnimum.
tried it twice. very delicious. especially key lime custard.

I got a junior snowstorm with heath bar and cheesecake. It was so good and a large portion; you definitely don't need any bigger. The add-ins were in big chunks and tasted great, unlike the add-ins at the big chains. The custard was very creamy. I can't wait to go back!

I've never had frozen custard until I lived in Champaign. Let me just say that this stuff is amazing!! Prior to this I was a huge fan of Dairy Queen. Jarling's Custard Cup has changed me forever and I miss it greatly now that I'm back in Virginia. I'll never look at DQ the same way again.

I really like the atmosphere here. Even though I'm not from around here, its the sort of place I can feel right at home in. And its fun to people-watch everyone enjoying their cold treats on a hot summer day. And if you grow tired of the crowd, its across the street from Hessel Park, where you can find a spot out on the grass. The frozen custard itself? Nothing out of the ordinary. I mean, of course its good, its cold, creamy and sweet. But so is the ice cream from anywhere else.

Local institution (though started in Danville, where there is, or at least used to be, a location). Lines can be long, but service is pretty good. Typical items: shakes, snowstorms (like a blizzard), some specialty items. It's good, but getting more expensive every year. If ANYONE is in Quincy, IL, there is a place called Deter's that puts this to shame in quality of ingredients and price. Too bad it's 200 miles away. Luckily my parents still live there!

as a previous resident of c-u, i have not found anything in anywhere to equal the custard at jarling's! they have heavenly vanilla, lemon, chocolate, and strawberry custard you can get in sudaes, cones, waffle baskets, or their version of a concrete. most custards - like ted drewe's in st. louis - have egg in them, giving them a heavier texture. my all-time favorite is a jarling custard cup chocolate almond crackle basket - that's vanilla custard in a waffle cup, topped with hard chocolate shell with almonds, whipped cream, & a cherry. next birthday don't bake - try a jarling's illini pie. or one of their other ice cream pies. i haven't found anything anywhere to beat that!

Given how famous Jarling's is, this place doesn't need anymore 5-star reviews...AS IF! Absolutely delicious! If you're looking for a tasty, sugary treat to heaven, look no further, you've found the spot. But do beware of the largest size - unless you are Phelps or are on a "dirty bulk", you'll be consuming 3000 calories of pure sugar carbs. Get the small size and let your taste buds go to heaven.
This place has so many flavors, it puts DQ to shame. So cheap, great vintage feel, outdoor seating. Short drive off campus.

this was my first experience w/ frozen custard, which i had heard a lot about on shows on travel channel and food network. we don't have stuff like this in CA, but i guess it's big in the midwest. there aren't many flavors, but i had lemon custard on a cone. at $1.65, you can't beat the price. it was so creamy and not icey at all, which ice cream can get sometimes. i tried my brother's choc, and it was good too. my dad got the blueberry cobbler snowstorm, which was like a blizzard, and it's made w/ vanilla custard. yum!
Good custard. They can make about anything. Service is fast although it's a popular place so there is usually a line.
Who doesn't love lemon custard? So refreshing! And really great in a lemon chiffon snowstorm. The only negative is the long lines - but still worth it!
Best ice cream in Champaign! The banana chocolate chip snowstorm and the oatmeal cookie snowstorm are amazing!
It's a mom & pop ice cream place. What's not to like? They recently starting taking credit cards so I like them even more now ;-)

We decided head to Jarlings in the dark and rain, but that didn't put a damper on our custard experience. Despite the poor weather, the place was packed. The staff was great and moved the line quickly, and the custard was definitely worth the wait. They have plenty of outdoor seating (not much indoor); so I can't wait to try it out some sunny summer evening.

Fantastically amazing custard! The cold fudge sundae with vanilla custard is my favorite thing on the menu. The pumpkin pie snowstorm (seasonal) takes a close second. We just discovered they sell frozen custard cookie sandwiches which are also yummy. It seems like Jarlings is always open when we need to make a "late" night custard run around 9pm or so.

Jarlings holds a special place in our hearts. It's the best ice cream place in town. The staff are somewhat slow at times, and use their bare hands to put toppings on (which irritates me because they do this immediately after handling money), but there's just no substitute. They don't have Reese's and are fussy if you ask, so just let it go. They also don't have hot fudge and get fussy if you ask. Luckily the custard is good enough that it eclipses any grievances. When we move away someday, I know I will miss this custard sorely.

This is such a local gem. Everyone from the 217 knows this place as a symbol of their childhood. The crazy lines are part of the experience. Use it as an opportunity to observe the townies, we're interesting people. You have to pick a side though, are you going to call it Jarling's or Custard Cup? Cold fudge is their specialty, and yeah, it really is better cold.

I will freely admit that I have not lived in Champaign since 1996, but my heart still belongs to Jarlings. Their "black and white" was my all time favorite. We got friends and family hooked on their custard when they'd visit, and it's still talked about when discussions of those days come up. Worth every penny of the price, and I would make the trip back just for a black and white if I could!
I think this place is a little overrated. I honestly don't think it is as good as some described it to be. My custard was a little too soft and not creamy at all. I would rather have Culvers.

A unique treat in the CU area. The setting is quaint, the custard wonderfully creamy, and the toppings decadent...a perfect place to go with friends or on a date. I only wish it were closer to campus. I highly recommend the lemon custard.

I am not a big ice cream or frozen custard fan. I had never been to Jarlings before and I have lived in this area all my life. I started a new job and was asked if I wanted something from Jarlkings. Since they were buying I said OK I will try it. I ordered the special for simplistic sakes. I surely could not pick one thing out of all the choices they have. The special was a carmel apple snowstorm and it is fantastic. I ordered a small but I couldn't finish it so I put it in the freezer and ate it again the next day and I think I liked it a little better the second time because it was frozen more than the first if that makes any sense.

I guess it fits the midwest ok..but kinda so/so. Seems really pricey for such small servings, and I dont think I would wait in a long line again for this. Nothing out of the ordinary, not sure what the ruckus is about. Try COCOMERA...seek it out, for a real experience.
So delicious. Lemon custard with cold fudge is a favorite!
Maybe the custard is good, but this is the slowest place I have ever been in my entire life. Honestly.....awful!!!!

Goddamn I miss this place. Cold Stone Creamery has got nothing on Custard Cup. I have so many awesome memories of friends and family gathering here on hot summer days and nights. The only bummer was that it would shut down at the end of the season and we'd have to go without these delicious treats for a whole 6 months. Smart choice on their part. Because as soon as those doors opened at the beginning of each summer, the line never ended til the end of Sept.

Custard isn't really like anything I've tried before. It's rich and creamy. I got chocolate the first time I went there, and I was told by pretty much everyone that I made the wrong choice. Come here for the lemon custard. I haven't gotten into all of the other complicated choices, mainly because the lemon custard on a sugar cone is so darn good! And the prices are extremely reasonable. My one complaint, and it's a small one, is that they don't take credit cards. Oh well, guess I'll have to keep cash around for when the mood strikes!
love it. i have been comming here with the rents since i was little, so its nostolgic for me. i still get the same thing, a scoop of lemon on top of a scoop of chocolate in a waffle cone.
Amazing frozen custard. I like to stick to the basics -- vanilla or chocolate on a waffle cone. The stuff is just great.

A Champaign-Urbana institution. I've been going here since I was a kid and it's stayed consistent. Tough deciding whether to go with a Snowstorm or just some of the simple flavors in a waffle cone. The pies and ice cream sandwiches are great too.
Best place ever. Loved this place as a kid. One of the few things I miss about Champaign...haha.
simply fantastic, been here 4 days straight since they opened, the lemon custard is amazing in their banana splits. i would go EVERY DAY.
This is place is just awesome. I highly recommend the strawberry cheesecake with strawberry custard snowstorm

I might be a little biased because Jarlings comes nowhere near close to my favorite frozen custard place in Chicago (Scooters!). It still satisfies the sweet tooth and they have a pretty good variety. I've just had better frozen custard (at other locations besides my favorite).

AMAZING! delicious, awesome prices, and they give you a ton of ice cream. The atmosphere is great as well. Perfect on a warm summer night. (well perfect anytime really) I'm always sad when it closes for the winter.

Custard Cup was my friends and I's place to go in the summers! They have the best tasting Custard around! You can create your own mixture with their large variety of toppings! It kind of reminds you of a Dairy Queen but sooo much better!

The chocolate custard is pretty good. I didn't care much for the snowstorms, cause the few times I've gotten them, they've been pretty melty, and they're comparable to Blizzards, depending on what you're looking for. Student staff is friendly, but the others have are slightly standoffish. My biggest complaint is that they didn't accept cards, but I didn't dock stars for that.
Just great asian ice cream every time, taste is outstanding and the fish waffles are always fresh

following up on my previous message, I wanted to change my review to a 5 star. Not only did the owner ensure to provide a better experience for me, but the employees also made sure I was provided with exceptional all service. For a Company to show that they care about their customers' experience is rare and Somi Somi in the Henderson location is worth visiting! Thank you for the wonderful experience!

Hands down one of my go to when I want something sweet! Not only is the ice cream DELISH, but the experience was so FUN! I love watching the staff make the cones and the taiyaki! I haven't had a bad experience here yet! The staff is typically friendly and fast! I got the upside down ah bong with strawberry and guava swirl and the hubby got ube. It's so good and affordable!

Excellent ice cream and taiyaki the first time and every time! With a rotating list of 6 swirlable ice cream flavors (ube, matcha, Oreo, black sesame, guava, milk tea, and more) and perfectly cooked taiyaki with 5 filling options (Nutella - do it!, ube, custard, taro, red bean, and cheddar), I'm in heaven! I usually get a custom Upsidedown Taiyaki which is delicious ice cream in a cup topped with a Nutella-filled taiyaki, sprinkles, and a macaron wafer or strawberry. My family also orders a Box of 5 custard- or Nutella-filled Taiyaki (you can only chose one filling type for one box. They also offer a box of 3). Treat yourself! NOTES/TIPS **Plenty of parking in a shared lot within Sansone Park Plaza. **Zero lines, especially compared to their Chinatown location on Spring Mountain Rd. **Indoor and outdoor seating. Wheelchair-accessible.

First time here. Great service. Order came through quickly. Clean. The front desk guy explained the ordering system very clearly. It was really hot so I didn't get the waffle fish, just Ebi ice cream swirl in a cup. The gal preparing my order asked if I wanted toppings which is included in the price. I chose the toasted coconut and a fresh strawberry. Loved the cold creaminess and the coconut and strawberry provided a nice contrast.

We've been here a few times now, I love this place! The ice cream is super good and the Taiyaki are so delicious. The service has always been pretty quick when we've been here, even when there's quite a few people in the shop. Sometimes we even come for the ice cream and then take taiyaki home for dessert that night or a snack for the next day. We'll definitely keep coming back, if you haven't tried SomiSomi yet, give it a try!
Great location! However the service here isn't the best! Not the best customer service I had!

I absolutely cannot get enough of Somi Somi! I've been a loyal customer from way back when their only location was Chinatown, so when they opened this location closer to me, I was stoked. I'm constantly checking their Instagram every Friday to see what their weekly flavors will be. This particular week had been Thai Tea/Black Sesame swirl. I got the ahboong with custard. So divine, every time. I'm still hoping out for when they bring Hojicha... *fingers crossed*

I wasn't sure what to expect honestly, but I was in for a great surprise!! I ordered an upside down milk tea with custard. It was so delicious. We also ordered taiyaki with custard, cheese, and Nutella. The cheese was by far the winner!! I'd say it's like a fish shaped grilled cheese. I can't even rave enough about it. It was so simple but so good. I would definitely recommend this place. The stage is friendly. The place is bright and clean. Not a lot of seating so definitely good for take out.

Holy cow-worth all the hype!!!! Best dessert on the south side of LV. I don't even know what to compare it too but those little fish come things are a little crunchy, a little soft and a lot delicious. Very clean, love the vibes. Vegetarian friendly Good services, no complaints

SomiSomi is serving up delicious soft serve and waffle cones in a unique way. This has been a long time bookmark for me and it was even better than I expected. The shop is bright and welcoming with cute art on the walls. The dining room is large, but right now only offers one standing bar style area. I'd love to see them return to offering tables for dine in. Without indoor tables I can't justify returning with my toddler in the dead of summer. They have a couple of picnic tables in front for outdoor seating. The service was friendly and our sweet treats were ready after only a few minutes. There are a variety ways to enjoy these treats. You can choose soft serve in a cup, soft serve in a cone, or a cup of soft serve with a cone on top. Then you choose a soft serve flavor. They offer specials with a twist of two flavors too. Then choose a filling for the cone. Lastly, when you pick up your treat you can choose toppings like a macaron, cereal, or candy. Cones can be purchased on their own too. For my treat I went with a cup of Ube soft serve topped with a cone filled with taro. To finish it I added a macaron and Fruity Pebbles. The soft serve was very creamy and not too sweet. The Fruity Pebbles sweetened it up a bit. The macaron was tasty. My favorite part was the fish shaped cone. It was a little crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside with a lovely flavor. The taro inside was enough to add something, but didn't overpower the cone. The serving of soft serve was too much for me to finish. If I return with my husband I would share one and add a couple of cones. There are other flavors that I look forward to trying. I'm excited to return when it's cool enough to eat outside!

I loooooooooove ice cream, it's my weakness and the most important on my cheat days. I had somi in Cali a few years back when it first started so I was thrilled when it made its way here! The ice cream is so creamy and the fishy has the best crispy gooey texture to it. It's probably more dangerous for me because I live down the street, eek!! The plus side is this location is a little slower than China town so I don't have to turn myself away from long lines.

Located in the Eastern and 215 shopping center, Somi somi has taken over the old Rolled Ice cream space. We went on opening day and it was a little bit of a cluster, as you expect from opening day. But we've been there 4 times since their grand opening, a month ago, and they have definitely smoothed out the kinks and now is like a well oiled machine. Somi Somi is a Korean inspired dessert place. Their signature is the Taiyaki, which is a fish shaped pastry filled with a filling of your choice: cheddar, Nutella, custard, red bean, Taro and Oreo. Taiyakis are 2 for $3.95 or 5 for $7.95. The taiyaki are perfection. Crispy on the outside and chewy and perfect once you bite in. We chose the custard, Nutella, red bean and Oreo fillings. All were really good. The Oreo was a little dry as it's just an Oreo cookie broken in half and placed in the middle. We also ordered the Ahboong $5.95 which is soft serve with a fish cone on top. Soft serve flavors change out as they are seasonal. When we went we tried the matcha, Oreo and ube swirl. The soft serve was thick and creamy. Tasted so rich, like frozen custard. Sooo good! Mashisoyo. You can choose a filling to fill inside the Ahboong as well but we opted not to. Once your order is ready, you go to the pick up counter and can add complimentary toppings like a macaron shell, sprinkles or a fresh strawberry. So incredibly happy to have Somi Somi come down to the Henderson area. A great new and fresh addition to the sea of restaurants on Eastern. Check it out you will not be disappointed. There taiyaki is the best we've ever had.

I just recently found this delicious gem!! I luckily found it because Dairy Queen was closed and I was craving soft serve. I had no idea what I was in store for and was I ever in for a big surprise! I was especially surprised to find that they offer Red Bean TAIYAKI which is a warm fish-shaped waffle filled with choice of filling. Fillings include custard, taro, red beans and more! Red Bean Taiyaki was one of my favorite things when I lived in Japan and I've never been able to find it's equal in the USA until now. I also had the Milk Tea Swirl AH-BOONG which is their signature goldfish-shaped waffle cone stuffed with your choice of filling & soft serve. I chose the Custard filling and was so glad I did! Both of these items were super YUM! It's making my mouth water just writing this review so I think I better go back for more!!!
Perfect little ice cream portion. And love the extra waffle on top. It's cute and delicious.

My wife wanted to try this place. The place is small but really how big does it need to be. The menu has a few great selections and it is great to see the likes of red bean as an option. The smells are wonderful, the art on the wall matches. This is a great treat for the whole family. Recommend.

This is actually SomiSomi's second location in Las Vegas. Their first location being the one in Shanghai Plaza and I'll admit, if you can, come to this location instead. There isn't much difference in quality or service but the wait at this location is significantly less. While they have both soft serve and taiyaki (fish shaped waffle), I think their taiyaki is better than their soft serve. Their soft serve is good but a lot of the flavors are really subtle. They rotate their flavors though so at least there is always something new to try if that is your thing. I love their taiyakis. You can get them filled with nutella, custard, cookies and cream, taro, cheese, or red bean. My favorite is the custard and they are absolutely delicious when eaten fresh. If you haven't tried them before, you should give it a go.

Came here with the fam after a stop at Kura Sushi. They are a unique dessert spot. They serve 2 forms of a fish shaped waffle. One has a giant open mouth that can be either filled with soft serve ice cream or stuffed on top of the ice cream. The other version is filled with your choice of filling. We went with the big mouth lined with Nutella stuck on soft serve. It was delicious. The service is as fast as it can be and watching them make the waffle fish is interesting if you have never seen it. I'll spare you the details and just lost some pics. I would highly recommend this place for both families and as a date night. It's very cool, and right next to a Korean corn dog place I wanna check out next time! Stay tuned!

Surprisingly this was the first time I ever tried this place! So many people have raved about it and I can see why. People of all ages come and enjoy the unique sweet treat this place has to offer. I didn't get a picture of mine and my husband's Ah-Boong in a cup but it was yummy. I had a Nutella filled with milk and cookies and creams and my husband had a Nutella with milk tea and ube. My husband is big on cold brew so we also go a cold brew with milk tea and he loved it. We will definitely be coming back especially for the waffle fish that you can order alone. So good!

Love this new location it's really clean inside, there is no seating options inside as of now I'm not sure if there will be... there are a few tables outside. I love the soft serve ice cream here I got the Oreo flavor with Oreo crumbs and Oreo and green tea mix with captain crunch cereal
Came in a little last minute without even realizing but they had great service, a very clean place. Love the vibe definitely recommend my kids loved it

Simply delicious! Ordered the upside down ahboong nutella filled with ube soft serve. The staff recommended the ube flavored as I previously tried the milk tea and it was a bit underwhelming for me. However, the ube flavored soft serve has a good flavor (hint of coconut) and is my go-to now. I also ordered the taiyaki filled with nutella. I would definitely come back and recommend to friends and family! Hubby isn't usually a big dessert person, but he really enjoyed this.
An expected new find -- it was so good that we went twice in one week! The fish-shaped waffle on top is a delicious touch.
I love this place! The ice cream is delicious and fish with Nutella is my favorite. The staff is always friendly and professional.

This was my first time visiting this location. Somisomi has been one of my fave spots for soft serve ever since they opened their first location in Chinatown. Even on a cold day, I crave it! Service isn't much different from the Chinatown location and there was practically no wait when my sister and I arrived around 3 pm. Their soft serve is on the creamier side. I find their flavors subtle and not overly sweet, which is typically how I prefer my desserts. I love that they keep flavors on rotation so I get to try something a little different every time I visit. The taiyaki is light and crisp on the outside. Not at all cakey as I've experienced with other places that also serve it. Serving size is also huge! I'm sure I've had to share one most of the time. You can also purchase the taiyaki without the soft serve and just have the fillings in it. The custard filling is my favorite!

They say that Koi fishes are lucky but no one ever told me that they are delicious too, especially when they are made as soft waffles with fillings inside. We finally visited Somi Somi. Since Kayla, yelp's Las Vegas' community manager gave them a great review, Somi Somi was one of my must-visit sooner than later. We arrived in the afternoon when the weather was 108 degrees. The place did not have a line when we arrived and the ice cream flavors was different today than it was the previous week. I think they change the flavors periodically. We were helped immediately. Both my friend and I ordered the Thai tea and Ube swirl which was delicious. The combination of these two flavors complimented each other. There was the immediate Thai tea flavor as you first taste the ice cream then comes the subtle taste of the Ube. It was epic! I finished mine before we left the place. We decided to eat our ice cream cups inside the establishment. They did not have individual tables and chairs inside but they had a long wall table and patrons can stand next to it while enjoying their soft serve. They do have tables and chairs right outside their door. It was hot so we decided to stay inside. We picked the Nutella filled Koi fish waffle which was an added excellence to this amazing treat. I am inviting all of you to come and have one of these treats, you will get hooked!

i've been here several times and it dose not disappoint! it's clean, everyone working is very nice and friendly and the ice cream is fantastic! i try something new everytime and i have yet to find something i wouldn't get again. great place highly recommend
It's amazing I've cream. I recommend to bring your kids it's a good environment to bring kids. There is a big selection of toppings to choose from. Nice staff as well

I really love somiSomi! The soft serve is soo creamy compared to every other soft serve I've had. This time I decided to go with the cookie butter flavor with Oreo crumbs. The flavor was subtle but still delicious. The red bean paste and Nutella are my favorites to fill the fish. The dessert here is surprisingly filling. Ube is my favorite flavor of soft serve but none that I've had are overpowering. I love the option of the little macaron also. They finally do have a few barstools to sit inside now. There are also a few tables outside. It's never been crazy busy any time I've been. Service is always quick and friendly. It's located on eastern in the strip mall next to a chiropractor. The bright yellow lettering makes it easy to locate.

Location is now open and was super excited to visit. The ice cream is consistent, staff is nice, fish is usually burnt so nothing new there (unlike the spring mountain location); however, it seems like the cups got smaller but not the cost. I thought maybe my eyeglasses had issues but unfortunately it was not the case. The pics show the fishes for upside down in the cup not completely encompassing the cup in my latest experience. This part was really disappointing.
my favorite ice cream ever! love all the fun flavors and of course the presentation. this is my go to if someone tells me they want ice cream!

Yay! A new Somi Somi location! I have been to their Spring Mt location a couple of times, so happy there's a closer one now! They have soft serve with rotating flavors (everytime I go they have had at least one unique flavor!) This time they had Boysenberry/mango swirl, which I'm not sure what boysenberry should taste like, but was super fruity and sweet! I always get the custard filled taiyaki on top of the cup! If you are coming here straight after a meal, be sure to leave some room because it is fiiillling!

Im so glad i found this spot for my sweet tooth cravings! They have the most unique fish shaped waffle with filling thats to die for lol and the frozen yogurt is delish!!! The waffle cookies are freshly made as well as there waffle cones ;-) I got them filled with nutella and they were amazing! The Ube frozen yogurt went amazingly well with the waffle cone nutella filling i even was able to add a topping free of charge ( i got coco flakes) SOOO GOOD ITS A MUST TRY !!!! I will def be coming here for my desert cravings. I highly recommend it too you will love it! new local fav!
I was in town and came across this establishment. Really neat and fun place to get dessert. Different and family friendly!

Went to Somisomi in Henderson and counter asked where my mask was. So I walked out. I watched from the window four feet from her was a crowd of unmasked customers eating ice cream. Why in the hell do I need a mask for when the rest of the restaurant is unmasked. Do germs stay away from the left side of the restaurant? Idiots.

More like so yummy so yummy. SomiSomi is a growing chain of dessert-centric locations that just opened this 2nd outpost in the Las Vegas area. This one is located toward the middle of Sansone Park Place on the east side of Eastern near Richmar. If memory serves, it used to be a Rolled Ice Cream, which I predicted was due to fail because they just plain sucked. Fortunately, SomiSomi does not suck. If they offered just one of either the soft serve or the taiyaki, I would already be happy with them. Those who know/stalk me may be aware that I'm on a perpetual rant about how this hot desert doesn't seem to sustain dessert places, in particular ice cream / gelato. The milk tea / thai tea soft serve swirl (combinations will rotate, according to the menu) was delightful though, with plenty of flavor and creaminess. Free toppings can go a long way too, especially the crispy coconut flakes. The matcha powder was also nice, but be careful because wind or jostling may result in your clothing or car turning green. Just as enjoyable was their custard-filled taiyaki (which I ended up trying twice due to their free taiyaki w/ purchase grand opening promo). For their ahboong ($5.95), they serve a rounder, hollow fish; due to COVID policy, they merely invert this onto a cup of conical ice cream instead of filling the fish itself. To be clear, the taiyaki is a star because it's pretty much a fun-shaped waffle, and you can even watch them cook these waffles on their proprietary waffle iron. Crispy exterior and delightfully chewy interior (yes, I'm sure I've used that exact phrasing before, but it fits) are what you'll find with the taiyaki, as well as a sweet creamy filling of your choice. (Local dessert lovers or people who've known me will also recall that the Waffle Love food truck was amazing until it was kidnapped and gutted, then subsequently retired. Fortunately, we now we have a waffle that, while not in the same style, is also awesome in its own way.) I was silly silly to pass up on SomiSomi when I was near their location on Spring Mountain in Shanghai Plaza, but I'll be sure to avoid making that mistake in the future. Whether you're in Nevada or another state, these guys are worth going out of your way to try.

Okay so I think "fish waffles" is my new favorite swear phrase Cuz holy fish waffles this place is amazing -the cream filled waffle is one of my new favorite things. The ice cream was delicious and creamy but the waffles were really the star. Warm and soft sand just so yummy! Chef's kiss!!

It was delicious and my kids loved it. At first I thought it wouldn't be enough but it was more than enough. One suggestion tho. It was around the time the sun was about to set so it was shining directly into where the cash register is. Everyone was covering their eyes to shield their eyeballs from the sun. The inside was also quite warm due to this. Maybe some kind of window tinting or blinds would help. No one was sitting in the front part of the store where the wooden bench thing is, I imagine because it was too warm to sit there. Otherwise cute shop, great service and delicious!
This location is the only one to offer Thai tea flavor. I love it when they have it swirled with milk tea so Yummy!

With summer right around the corner, this would be a great spot to beat the heat and satisfy your sweet tooth. I ordered the Ah-boong upside down style with Nutella filling, choose the Thai tea/Oreo swirl flavor, topped it off with crushed Oreos and garnished with a strawberry. Best decision ever! Would highly recommend!
It's amazing and super delicious, they have very fun and unique flavors my personal fave is the half Thai tea half Oreo and the little fish they put out are so good!!!
Yummy! Took the kids here for some soft serve. The ice cream was soft and creamy and the fish waffles was crispy on the outside and gooey soft on the inside. Check them out if you havent.

Tried this new location tonight and really enjoyed it. Cute dÃ©cor, ultra friendly staff, and delicious soft serve ice cream! We tried the matcha & cookies n cream swirl and the mango & boysenberry swirl; both were so good. Definitely will be telling family & friends about this place!
Delicious treat and extremely friendly and helpful staff. What's more to love? Lol just go and try it you won't regret it! :)
Tasty on a warm Vegas day. Absolutely so amazing with quick service. It was my first time being there and workers were so kind and patient. The service was super timely as well.

Refreshing dessert worth the price! You can have the soft serve by itself or "ahboong" (upside-down style) with a filled-taiyaki on top. Definitely a good amount of combos to try and they're all pretty and seems good

Went on the first day of their soft opening - we were welcomed by the staff. The cashier taking our order was polite and super friendly! All of the employees are wearing mask and gloves. There was social distancing signs on the floor - to keep 6 feet apart. Everything is brand new - so no complaints about anything inside. There are a set of tables outside - if you want to eat outside. So glad they opened a Somi Somi near me- will definitely be going to this location more!
Literally the best soft serve you will ever have in your life. I can't really put into words how good this place is so just go and find out for yourself! You won't regret it.
Love this place, cool options and good options for those not too adventurous. Tasty ice cream so fresh and I had the coffee float with sesame ice cream DELICIOUS!

Found this place on Yelp while in town for soccer. Really enjoyed the cone filled with Nutella. Definitely try this place if you are looking for something different then the usual ice cream/gelato place.

What a magical treat this place is! I have had Somi Somi bookmarked for quite a while. Just a couple of locations and all far from where I live. I met a friend to try a new pizza place and Somi Somi was only two doors down so we stopped for dessert. So easy to find right off of Eastern Avenue. Somi Somi is a special Korean dessert that is known is Ah Boong. First you decide how you wish to eat your Somi Somi. I chose upside down Ah Boong. It is served in a fish shape waffle cone. Next you select a soft serve flavor. I chose Matcha. Then you choose a filling. I decided on Taro. Lastly you may also select a topping of cereal bites, coconut, strawberry etc. I have been back several times now and almost always order my dessert now with Ube soft serve, Nutella filling and a different topping each time. This is one of the most refreshing and tasty desserts I had all summer. Their soft serve is so creamy and packs plenty of flavor. The homemade waffle cone is soft and flavorful especially with Nutella. Warning, the servings are large so you can probably share one with whomever you are with. I look forward to returning again and again. I am pretty sure that I will be eating this delightful dessert in the winter too. Why not?
Novel remaking of soft serve experience. Black sesame not available at this location and out of chocolate on a busy Saturday afternoon.

Our favorite dessert spot is finally on this side of the town, we don't have to drive all the way to Chinatown anymore. Taiyaki cones are crispy on the outside, and airy on the inside. Great texture overall. You can customize the toppings as well. Great service and fast too!

Korean dessert place that serves their version of soft serve ice cream is what's the big hit here! Flavors at this location, Thai Tea (only Henderson) Oreo, Matcha, Ube and Milk Tea.. and the swirls (combo of 2 flavor) changes every week. Ice cream is either served in a cup or Taiyaki (waffle cone made in fish shaped molds) So the cool thing for me about this Korean dessert craze is the fillings that go in the cone. Some of the choices here are custard, Nutella, taro, and cheddar! During the restrictions, only Ah-boong was the only way they served it here. Soft serve in a cup, topped with a Taiyaki and additional toppings. (cereal, candy, sprinkles, plus either a mini macaron or strawberry slice) The soft serve is delicious, non dairy, Ube is my favorite, so get that purple stuff! Cold Brew Float Kinda weak.. You don't get that much much soft serve.. compared to what I saw on IG that's for sure. So just giving you heads up and saving you six bucks on that one! Service excellent, lines that are out the door and down a few stores seem to go by quick, thanks to the efficient and organized crew. Even the owner is there helping FOH. Other than the counter along the back wall, there's no place to sit inside and the walls aren't as grammable (is that a word?) like the Spring Mt location. To prevent people from lingering inside Im guessing. There's two picnic tables just outside though! Don't know if eating soft serve outside will go over well with the Vegas heat. Find this location off Eastern Ave, BJ's Restaurant is your visual cue to spot Somi Somi directly across.
Clean, fast, friendly & DELICIOUS I'm on a mission to try all their flavors & fillings!

The customer service we got was amazing! The cashier walked us through the ordering process. We got the Ahboong with Ube flavored soft serve. It was amazing! It's not too sweet and you can taste the Ube flavor. The fish waffle went well with it. It was soft and warm. I definitely will be back for more!
So yummy and really nice menu nice location first time coming here and I recommend. The service was friendly and helpful

This place is so. stinkin'. CUTE! The interior elements really add to the aesthetic of the shop, like the fish scale panels with lighting, the wall art, the light colors with tall windows, allowing for a bright and airy feel - it's just so CUTE! The menu isn't anything extensive - it's a very niche business, but they do great at what they do. You can pick some Taiyaki, which are fish-shaped waffles (not flavored, shaped, lol) that have your choice of filling. My personal favorites are the Nutella, Cheese, and Oreo, in that order. You can also do a soft-serve, with rotating flavors and swirls (combos of two flavors), depending on the day. My daughter loved the oreo flavor, and the milk/thai tea swirl was delicious! You can also throw on an open-mouth taiyaki fish, also with your choice of filling, on top of the ice cream, and unfortunately they did not have the waffle fish that acts as the ice cream cone (yet, hopefully). You can then top your ice cream off with several different topping choices (oreo crumbles, matcha, sprinkles, etc.) with a strawberry or macaron on top. I've also tried their strawberry milk, which looked so pretty in the photos. It was good, and the strawberry chunks were fresh and yummy, but probably wouldn't get again. This is a family favorite and so accessible in the plaza - we'll be coming back here for sure!
This will probably be my new favorite dessert place! I ordered a milk tea soft serve with the fish shaped waffle cone and filled it with Nutella. This combo is fire so yummy can't wait to go back

So thankful SomiSomi has finally made it to Henderson! It's located in the same plaza as Brew Tea Bar and it's just the perfect addition. This location is on par with the other locations in Nevada and California. Don't let their small menu deter you away from coming in and trying their desserts. Their taiyaki and soft served ice cream are delicious! The ice cream is so soft and decadent without being overly sweet. If you're looking for something warm I love the custard taiyaki because its chewy and a perfect way to end your meal. Customer service is quick and efficient. Overall, I love all the SomiSomi locations and I'm glad there one closer to my home.

Normally, I love SomiSomi. So much I wanted to get gift cards for whole bunch of graduates and birthdays. When I walked in, I asked if I could buy some gift cards. The person at the register said they don't do gift cards, but they have a QR code. I asked how can I give gift amount if I don't have email addresses? She responds that she is sorry and she has never done it before. She let me just walk out. This store lost some money from me. So I went down the store front to Brew Tea and bought some gift cards. Wish I could have given SomiSomi business, but nope. Just a suggestion, it's nice to have gift cards for customers to just pick up. One star less for not having gift cards and another star less for the person who didn't know how it works to purchase a e-gift card.

My daughter and I were craving for ice cream and saw this place in Yelp. We were excited for Somisomi as it was our first time here. We walked in and it smelled so good! The fragrance of the waffles filled the room and so we decided to get the 5 pc Nutella filled Taiyaki. After further examination of the menu, we also opt for the soft serve - ube and matcha. Everything was delicious. The gentleman who prepared our food was great! He was polite and helpful. The girl at the register however came off as rude and impatient. We had questions about the menu and it was obvious it was our first time here but she had this attitude like oh you don't know?! We will try this place again and hopefully we don't get that girl. She was the reason why our first experience at this establishment was not great. Our excitement slightly fizzled after we encountered her.
They will not let you order the soft serve on the cone and the only way you can get the cone is to pay $2 more to have them put it in upside down in a cup. They also did not have the cold brew float.
Loveeeee this place! The milk tea ice cream is my favorite. You can't go wrong with trying any flavor honestly! I recently tried the cold brew float with Thai tea ice cream and it's sooo good!

We've been here several times now and every time has been excellent. The soft serve is very high quality, super thick and creamy. The taiyaki is fresh, crunchy on the outside, and chewy on the inside. Absolutely delicious. The place is clean inside and service is friendly and quick. Definitely recommend!

They do not offer carry out orders. I did not want any of the soft serve products and they still would not take order over the phone even willing to pay with credit card. I was literally in the parking lot but had sleeping kids in car and did not want to leave them in car you themselves. Also it takes a few minutes to make the food and it would still be hot to eat so ordering inside was not idea.
What a fun experience not to mention tasty. Long queues shows what an experience this is . Imagine a waffle shaped as fish filled with flavor and ice team Astounding good dessert

Ugh finally one opened close to me! Normally I always go for their taiyaki and never really cared about their soft serves -- I changed that today. Got their upside down ah-boong with Oreo and another one with their Milk Tea/Thai tea combo and it was so good! One can definitely not go wrong with their taiyaki here, as well -- Nutella, custard, and taro is my fave! They had an Oreo flavor in this location which is v new to me. I dig it. Please note that this location just opened so the line is friggin' long! Despite that, customer service is great!

This place used to be my favorite soft serve place. But the portions have gotten super small. And even the pulling is not as good. Usually they take great care into making it look good. Of late. Its been lopsided, uneven and ugly. The guy behind the counter needs to be retrained.

This little center has a lot of great options for food bf dessert. To be honest it's a tough choice to choose between this and nielsons across the way, but I prefer this place and my husband prefers them and it's fine cuz we can go get our orders and meet up at the car. I got matcha with fruity pebbles toppings and custard filled fish. Really yummy and creamy. I can't wait to try more flavor combos

Love this place and so does our little ones! So yummy and so worth it for outdoor fun get away with anyone to enjoy some yummy soft serve. The employees are so helpful and sweet will be retiring again!
Pretty cool place to try. I tried a few of the different fillings in the Taiyaki. Custard was yummy.
the workers were so kind! the milk tea + strawberry soft serve was AMAZING. they were so delicious, i highly recommend this place, it's SO GOOD!!

I really enjoyed visiting this establishment for ice cream, although they were out of a few flavors at the time. Still, ice cream is creamy and delicious, and with the fresh, hot taiyaki, it's even better.

This was my first time trying SomiSomi as this new location opened up right by my house. It's amazing!! The taiyaki was so good. We tried the cheddar and custard and both were amazing. The ah-boong was also one of the best desserts I've ever had. The taiyaki waffle is so flaky on the outside but doughy and soft inside. It goes so well with the ice cream!! I can't wait to go back!!!
I mean my daughter loved it. I thought it was good but nothing super over the top. Just a typical fany ice cream place. Any time places do something different with ice cream kids go crazy over it.
Somisomi Henderson!! Thank you to come this area. I love this plaza !!! Everything is here!!! Thai tea with milk tea combination is very tasty and creamy !! Also i love custard and taro Taiyaki!!

This is the best soft ice cream. I had the strawberry soft serve in the fish waffle cone which was filled with Nutella. It was warm and rich and so good. You are offered a topping and a cookie or strawberry on the side. So yummy! Highly recommended.

The place is clean and staff are all nice and attentive. My to go to place this hot summer season. I love the upside down ahboong and yes I tried all the flavor and filling and my favorite nutella taiyaki, always had it to go to pair it with my favorite tea.
Great service and delicious soft serve! Will need to go back to try the taiyaki but I'm sure that will be good too. I got the ube matcha swirl with red bean filling, amazing!
Finally!! A franchise 1 mile away from me! The best ube ice cream plus a taiyaki with red bean filling. Always happy to go there.

A little busy on a Sunday afternoon at 3pm, it's starting to get packed right after we ordered. The place was clean, we love the interior design. The staff were nice. We like that they feature weekly swirls. The taiyaki waffles are made to order, so it was hot and fresh :) There are additional toppings on the swirl if desired. Taiyaki - sooo soft yet crispy! Milk Tea - sweet, love this milk tea! Cookies and Cream - it's ok Ube - not too sweet, just right Chocolate- just ok Real Strawberry Milk - milk and pureed strawberry?! wow!!! *Favorite: Taiyaki Waffle, Milk Tea Soft Serve, Real Strawberry Milk Parking: easy, plenty of spots outside

This is by far the greatest desert! I call it fish ice cream, my friends are like gross. Then when I take them it's all over!! I love the custard on the inside, the icee cream is just perfect, and the FISH!!!! I'm gonna leave that right there, if you don't go then there will be more for me!!! I promise you will love it!!!

SomiSomi has just opened up a shop in Henderson! Super excited to see another Chinatown business open up a second location here in our neighborhood. SomiSomi....get in my tomi tomi!! They specialize in Asian-inspired soft serve flavors and fish-shaped waffles (aka Taiyaki) with fillings. A perfect dessert, especially in this Vegas heat! Soft serve flavors: milk, matcha, milk tea, Oreo, ube, and Thai Tea. Plus, every week they offer different swirl combinations. When your order is ready, you can add toppings such as Oreo, toasted coconut, cocoa pebbles, and more, plus add a macaron or fresh strawberry. Fillings for the Taiyaki include Nutella, custard, taro, and red bean. The Oreo/Milk swirl I had was firm and creamy, but be sure to eat it up quick before it starts to melt and drip once outdoors. I was craving sweet & savory, so I also ordered two waffles filled with Custard and Cheese. I couldn't finish because, so I kept them in the box provided. The next morning I popped these cuties into my toaster and they still tasted pretty good with the rest of my egg breakfast! Location: just off of the I-215 & Eastern Ave next to one of my favorite restaurants, Pin Kaow Thai. Plenty of parking!

It was amazing experienc that I had ahboong with Ube and nutella, taiyaki flavor of redbean and the mustard in Somisomi! ILook adorable and the taste was so yummy too!! Also employees were so kind and nice:)

Fun and affordable dessert shop! We enjoyed our visit. Definitely a cute place to bring the family. We ordered upside down ah-boong with Thai tea soft serve. It was delicious! Definitely going to recommend this place to my friends.

Literally the most incredible soft serve I've ever tasted !! The servers are all super friendly, the orders come out quick & the flavors are amazing. Milk tea matcha swirl and Thai tea milk swirl are my faves and the custard is the perfect filling IMO.

Such a magical little treat! I got the milk tea soft serve and the taro filled taiyaki. Soft serve was tasteless, but the taiyaki was amazing! I'll probably stick to ordering taiyakis from here going forward. Give them a try!
Came with my wife to try a new flavor and we loved it. Remind us Japan when we've been there few years ago so we do recommend it to anyone

There's always a line here and I never understood why until I tried this place. This place is super cute. The way they make their deserts with the fish shaped taiyaki. It is filled with custard and soft serve! Place is clean and it really didn't take ther long for them to make my order. The ice cream melted fast but probably because of the Vegas heat. There's a few bar seating inside and a couple of tables outside. Will be back!

Got to try the Thai Tea flavor which is only available at this location. Sooo delicious! They are also giving out a free taiyaki when you purchase an upside down ahboong ice cream for this weekend only!

Such a cute little dessert spot for ice cream and taiyaki. You can watch the process of how the fish dessert is made. The flavor of soft serve were interesting like black sesame or Thai tea and ube. Definitely will be coming back!!
Amazing ice cream! The little fish waffles are fantastic as well i forget what they are called. Great customer service and great recommendations when you don't know what you want. Will return
It it amazing !! Best soft serve ice cream in town.My kid love the ice creams. Ube is my favorite flavor It is so creamy and not too sweet. Love this place. Thanks for open in Henderson Las Vegas

This location is just as good as the other, which a much much shorter line. They pretty much have the same flavors and concept. Employees are really nice, flavors are good, and same menu as the other location. Good seating inside and out too. Great for kids and families.

I'm in love!!! Such a cute idea... I love the fish shaped waffle cones! I had the ah-boong with ube ice cream and taro filling with some dried coconut sprinkled on top.
