Prices are a little high in my opinion for some of the things they offer, but the place seems to do really well, especially since remodeling the store. I recommend it, but try to avoid the place on a Weekend evening in the summer since the place can be packed with a line to the door.

I liked the food here. Different twists on some typically made at home sandwiches. If your on your lunch break allow yourself some time. It's friendly and seems to be family run but preparation is deliberate slow paced. Worth the wait, though. Ice cream products are good but that's not why I go there. Interior is clean but very few tables - 5,6? If it's good weather there are some places outside - otherwise plan to take out. Seats were not comfortable.
Everything here is amazing and I now will only eat macaroons as ice cream sandwiches. ORDER ONE OF EVERYTHING

This place is a nice dessert place at the boardwalk. It was super hot and humid that I needed a fix and they were happy to oblige. I only got one scoop, but the serving was more than satisfactory which is more than what I can say about most places. Absolutely no negative impressions. The place inside looks old and could use a makeover to make it more appealing for people to come in.

My family and I love this place. It is our go to icecream spot in the university area. I loved how patient they are when you are trying to decide what you want because they have so many yummy options.
We love this place! Their candy-rimmed cups are one of my kids' favorites! I love their homemade ice cream sandwiches! Yum yum!!

Ok on a quick whim for ice cream. Sandwiches are super blah and greasy. Service sucks, the young college girl working the day we went could have cared less and her attitude showed it. Nevermind the 4 other guys standing around behind the ice cream counter behind her standing around... talking...staring....akward.

Ninety's is very popular in the university area! Every time I come here there's always a huge line, but the employees work together well enough to get the customers taken care of in a VERY timely manner! Impressive. They have a little digital menu of their stuff and it makes things so much easier. I've gone multiple times and I'm even lactose intolerant, lmao

Their daily special was the bomb. They don't shy away from adding enough meat! It's hard for me to believe people go to Subway when little shops like this exist. Good location. Great staff. I'll be back.
i freaking LOVE this place! The employees are so nice. the environment is clean and everyone seems so delighted over their cute little treats!
Very nice upgrade to the store. So much more on their menu and my kids love it. Every time we go we get to enjoy the outside air and walk around the pond.

My first trip to this establishment was very pleasing. They serve Hershey's ice cream at reasonable prices and the staff was helpful and had personality. I got a double scoop cone of strawberry and chocolate and my daughter got strawberry lemonade Italian ice. We were both pleased with our selections. I also tasted the strawberry cheesecake and cinnamon roll ice cream which were both amazing. Very clean restaurant.

Great place if you love sweets! Definitely recommend the yummy buns! If you have a sweet tooth then this is the place for you. The staff is amazing and they take pride in everything they do! ... Cookie dough pops are also a favorite

Good ice cream and macarons. However, I seen personnel wipe face and scratch hair with gloves on . Plus customer service could be a bit better. Nonetheless, being sanitary is a number 1 thing for me. So if you go make sure you watch them put a new glove on.
Great ice cream shop we found during race weekend. Amazing ice cream and shakes. Will definitely go back!

Initially, when we walked in the door it was very crowded, but the line moved fast. My boyfriend and I both got macaroon ice cream sandwiches and edible cookie dough on a stick. The sandwich was perfect and he definitely agreed. I enjoyed the cookie dough, but my boyfriend did not want his. When I tasted his, it tasted like straight up salt. Maybe that batch wasn't stirred properly?

My little girl and her friends absolutely loved their Unicorn Milkshakes. The ice cream cookies take 2 hands to enjoy! This place is full of good Sugar and is out of sight. Hidden to those that are not looking .... it has been around for years and I never thought to go inside until recently ... we love it
Best ice cream I have ever had. Service is great and ice cream is amazing. Sometimes they are really busy and it make take a little until you get your ice cream, definitely worth the wait!

Yummy!!! I love cookies and cream so of course I tried that flavor which was amazing. But since I also love coffee I just had to try the coffee cookies and cream. OMG!!!! The best coffee ice cream mix I've ever had. Surely recommend this place. They didn't receive 5 stars cause their service could be better and there wasn't any tissue in the restroom. But the ice cream is delish.

I love getting there mango stuff!! It's so good!! It salty, soury, and have spices to it which I love the most! I have gotten this like twice and both times I have loved it. I also love there ice cream! My friends have gotten their different drinks/ milkshake and they have love it. I love this place. This place has never disappointed me!!

My daughter and I love coming here after some time at the park and feeding the ducks during the warmer months! The new renovations & menu is just perfect! I am yet to try something there that I do not like, and service is always fast and friendly.
Yum-e-buns!! Very friendly staff and lots of yummy treats! So creative! Check it out!!

I just walked into this establishment. I was standing in front of the order here sign and two employees were behind the counter just talking so I didn't get service I just turned around and left out but the only reason for two stars is because the menu looks really big. I have never been here but have heard such good things about the salads.

Oh my goodness!!!!! This is the best dessert place I have ever been too. So many options!! The service was superb and had so many recommendations for my first time there. Best part about it is , I work in the service industry/ hospitality and have been for the last 3 years and I KNOW how places get when people come in so close to closing time. My boyfriend and I came in 20-30 minutes before close and the staff was STILL so incredibly friendly and helpful. I would recommend this place to ANYONE! And pray they never close down.
Always friendly. Quick service. The ice cream reminds you of the old school ice cream parlors. The location is great for a for an afternoon at the boardwalk.

Good selection of sandwiches. The ice cream looked great but I didn't try it. Husband and I both had the BLT which was good. Nice crisp bacon on some kind of toasted egg bread. All very reasonable priced. The only reason for the two stars is that we both had some tummy issues about an hour or so later and that was the last thing we ate. If it wasn't for that I would give another star. I could be encouraged to give this place another go though and hope that it's a one off just because the food tasted so good.

this place is amazing! as long as you like your desserts extremely sweet and unhealthy. i usually go for the donut ice cream sandwiches and man they're impressive!!! they incorporate cereal in everything which is my favorite part about this place you can't go wrong with with some ice cream in between some macaroons either. i don't think there's anything here i wouldn't recommend 10/10
They have changed exponentially since my last visit about 7 years ago. This place is fantastic! Glazed donut filled with strawberry ice cream ,

Got the strawberry shortcake macaron sandwich and my expectations were exceeded by far. Friend got banana pudding macaron sandwich and was equally impressed. Workers were friendly and willing to help us out as new customers. Will return!

I really like this place! They really try to make your ice cream experience better! I had the "Cookie Monster" (cookies and cream ice cream with Cookie Crisp cereal and chocolate syrup) perfect to share if you're not to much into sweets.

Ninety's has you covered for ice cream! However, before their renovations, they used to have THE best sandwiches (especially the BLT) and THE best potato salad. Their new sandwich menu has much to be desired and they've limited their side options to chips. Oh how I wish they would bring back the original food menu.
This place was so delicious. We got a shake and their donut sammy (warmed donut, filled with ice cream). I just about died and went to heaven.

Best place in Charlotte for their famous macaron ice cream sandwiches. But they run out pretty fast so you gotta come early. Also this place has ice cream and other selections of small bite and drinks.

I gave this place 4 stars because I absolutely love their ice cream but the only thing is I wish the workers were more friendly. At least a smile would be nice but hey the ice cream is delicious so that won't stop me from coming back!

I was looking forward to trying their macaroon ice cream and when I got there, they ran out of the ones I wanted! I opted for a random one and I didn't think it was really worth the price. The staff was okay, the guy seemed annoyed that I couldn't decide what I wanted right off the bat, but there was no one else in line or marked what they did or didn't have! I think next time if I can, I would come earlier to try it. My boyfriend got the fruity pebble milkshake and it really did taste like fruity pebbles but it was way too sweet. It was hard to finish it but nonetheless it was good.
Love Love love, such a friendly staff and wonderful icecream options. If you're going on a weekend be prepared for a line. They do tend to get busy, especially on warm days.
Been there twice...order wrong both times and flavor of sandwiches average at best. No desire to ever go back

Y'all ninety's is a dessert lovers paradise! We went for the first time yesterday after reading tons of great reviews on yelp and seeing the cool pics of the tasty treats. It for sure lived up to the hype. The guy taking our order was super helpful and when he found out it was our first time he pulled out an iPad and walked us through the menu with pictures of all the treats. They have freshly fried donuts and stuff them with ice cream and toppings, they have cereal milkshakes, cookie dough pops and macaroon ice cream sandwiches. We both got milkshakes- I can't remember the name of mine but it was like a samoa cookie and my husband got the Reese's puff shake. It was SO GOOD!!! My shake tasted just like the samoa Girl Scout cookie. The Reese's puff one was really good as well. I wish I didn't live so far away because I'd be there at least weekly but I guess it's a good thing for my waistline
I love 90's! A little slow and sometimes the cleanliness is questionable - but there's nothing better than their App Wrap.

Unfortunate that you'll stand there waiting for service and no one will speak to you. Then another customer comes in and is immediately helped. Walked out without buying and will never visit this place again.
this place is awesome!!! the macaroon ice cream sandwiches are the bomb!!!!! kids will love this place as well as adults!!

I came here over this past weekend to get some ice cream with my boyfriend and my sister who was visiting from CT. I found it about Ninety's through Instagram and Charlotte Agenda. I have been wanting to come here since the reopening back in June. Anyway, the ice cream was good but it is definitely more of a novelty than great taste. I tried the peanut butter cookie dough pop which isn't ice cream but straight up cookie dough. It took more than the three minutes they recommend to defrost and overall it didn't taste like much. My boyfriend got one of the hot doughnuts with the ice cream inside. This was also pretty good but he commented that there wasn't enough ice cream inside. Still pretty impressive that the ice cream doesn't fully melt when the doughnut is heated! Finally, my sister got the birthday cake macaroon ice cream sandwich. This was probably the best thing we tried. It came with cake chunks and a buttercream drizzle! Overall, I think there are better ice cream spots in the Charlotte area but I'm glad we checked this place out.

Wow this place has incredible ice cream desserts. We visited with friends, which was a great way to sample a variety of treats. We ordered the salted caramel french macaron ice cream sandwich...it was amazing! I love macarons the ones Ninetys make for their ice cream sandwiches are the perfect texture! We also ordered the Brownie milkshake and one oreo milkshake. It was a unanimous decision that these were some of the best desserts we had in a long time. The texture of the ice cream was silky smooth and flavors were on point, they know what theyre doing! The location is perfect too, because afterwards we took all the kids to the playground and for a walk along the lake.

This place can be deceiving because the first thing you see on their sign is ice cream and I always thought that it was a predominantly ice cream shop. However, this place has the best sandwiches for the price in all of north Charlotte. Their potato salad is amazing and I recommend getting it with whichever tasty delight you choose. Their ice cream is good, bit we always go for sandwiches. Excellent lunch spot!

The ice cream and smoothies are delicious. The only reason I rated them so long its because they have really bad customer service. The person who "helped" me out had an attitude the whole time. He acted like he was there against his will or something. I would not go back because I didn't feel welcomed at all.

Ninety's is cool and sweet, just like their ice cream. I haven't had their sandwiches, but I dropped by for a seat on their patio & indulged in a little afternoon treat. The coconut ice cream was smooth and tasty, just like I thought it would be. The staff behind the counter was a little disenchanted...maybe he was up later pulling an all nighter? Regardless, my order of two scoop of ice cream and two bottled waters came to $6 and change. That, I can handle. If you seek a sweet treat in University City, head over to Ninety's and be sure to enjoy that spacious shared patio!

Definitely a one of a kind dessert place. They have so many different creative treats to try! I haven't tried anything that I don't like yet and you definitely get your money's worth the portions are huge! The customer service is always great as well they are so friendly and helpful! I would give this place 10 stars if I could it's my favorite dessert place and I HIGHLY recommend!!

Perfect little ice cream shop from the prices to the sandwiches. Staff is friendly and orders are made quickly. It's located on a broadwalk so it perfect for just a spot to relax. Make sure to grab one of the huge brownies for a buck and some change before leaving this place it's well worth it.
Best place ever!!!! Was totally impressed by the service and it could only be matched by the incredible taste

There's a wide variety of sandwiches to choose from. The chunky chicken melt kind of tastes like Thanksgiving, I don't know how to describe it better than that. It was just really good. The ice cream was pretty good. I've had better, but not very often. The service could have been better. The people just kind of seemed uninterested, if that makes any sense. Overall, I'll probably be back if I'm in that part of town, but I won't seek it out.

after following your instagram for a couple months i was really excited to head up there. it was a 30 minute drive so I had been waiting for an opportunity to make the trip. however, after following the instagram for so long, i was kind of disappointed. the woman working there seemed really done with everything and didn't seem like she wanted to serve us. we got the s'mores macaroon, green tea milkshake, and a cookies and cream yummee bun. the bun was amazing and the green tea milkshake was good but the s'mores macaroon was just a ton of chocolate ice cream with a couple of marshmallows thrown on the side. i was disappointed with the milkshake because the lady didn't do any of the cool side decorating that i had seen on the instagram and in the other reviews. altogether the yummy bun was delicious butthe service and other items were average, and the decorating (which is what i thought was one of the key characteristics of the store) was not good :(

This little place has poor decor and it looks outdated. BUT IT'S FOOD IS AWESOME! !! I'm a bacon, sausage, steak and cheese loving individual. BUT, I love their veggie wrap, and I would have it everyday for lunch if I could. Their wraps and sandwiches are so delicious. I have been going here for over two years, and will continue to go.

I recently tried this place and I was very impressed with how delicious their sandwiches are. I have tried the chicken salad sandwich and the reuben and they were great. Super cheap prices and fast and friendly service. BTW their smoothies are pretty good too. I will definitely stop by again.

This place has me coming back all the time. The soft serve is still delicious, and I feel like the toppings/varieties are just continuing to grow. Pick a flavor that you love and you can't go wrong. Expect long waits in the evenings. My only complaint every visit was that there was no outside menu to help me decide which delicious treat I was going to indulge in. (I would usually have to peak through the windows to make a last minute decision). But Lo behold.

If you're in the mood for a delicious, refreshing treat, then you need to try Paige's Ice Cream! This local ice cream shop has a wide variety of flavors to choose from, so there's something for everyone. The ice cream is made fresh daily and is always super creamy and flavorful. The staff at Paige's Ice Cream are always so friendly and welcoming, and they make sure you're getting exactly what you want. They offer samples of any flavor you want to try, so you can be sure you're getting exactly what you're looking for. The shop is always clean and bright, and the perfect place to cool off on a hot day. If you're looking for an amazing ice cream experience, then you need to head to Paige's Ice Cream! You won't be disappointed!

It's always ice cream o clock for me! And Page is the reason why! A family owned and operated treasure, Page is one of the oldest soft serve places in Pittsburgh. I took my parents here and they loved it! We ordered a vanilla chocolate twist topped with nuts, coffee soft serve and blueberry soft serve. They were all delicious! The best part is that it's not very sweet and heavy. The portion size is good and not overwhelming. We ordered small size with waffle cone. There has always been a queue but it's a fast moving one. Great staff as well. There is enough place in front of the store to park and chill. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

PAGE'S SZN! Page's is located under the train tracks at the light on Carson Street/ Becks Run Road. There is plenty of parking in the lot under the tracks, alongside the building, and across the alley behind the business. And the ice cream, 10/10. We shared the banana split and were sure to order it with whipped cream and nuts. A very generous portion and the soft serve is some of the best. It's not just ice cream, but a wonderful experience - family, nostalgia, summer, all of the above. Take your family, take your date, take yourself - you won't regret it.

Is it summer yet? Although I've been a Pittsburgh native my whole life, my first time at Page's was very recently! I've had a lot of delicious ice cream experiences but this one was VERY high on my list. It's in a very interesting area - one that you need to get to by car and make sure some interesting liquids don't fall from the rain tracks above on to your car. This place is always busy so parking can be a little challenging, but we were able to find some next to the mechanic next door. The long line went by very quickly as they have a really well-oiled operation going on there! After we ordered, we also didn't need to wait very long for the ice cream. There were some areas for seating but it's mostly a place to grab and go - we ate our ice cream in the car. Well, what we could finish! The sundaes were INCREDIBLE but also MASSIVE - bigger than my face!! Next time, I think my husband and I will split a sundae (but there will definitely be a battle for the last bite!) It was a tasty evening and I can't wait to go back!

This place is a well oiled machine! So clever that they have dedicated waiting zone spots. They also have the parking setup really well. As for the ice cream, wow it's so good. I got the butterfinger, which is literally pre-mixed like a butterfinger McFlurry but in much better soft serve ice cream. My wife got the blueberry and wow it was literal actual blueberry ice cream. Great spot!

We stopped by Page's for our last meal in Pittsburgh before starting the drive back to Baltimore, and I'm so glad we did. It's a traditional, old-fashioned, retro ice cream stand/burger spot. You'll probably come for the soft-serve, sundaes, or milkshakes, but don't skip the food. It's a to go or enjoy in your car place (no inside seating). We had a cheeseburger, hot dog, extra small vanilla sugar cone with chocolate dip, and another dip cone (can't remember what flavor my husband got)! They offer more than 25 soft serve flavors! They have everything from the traditional to the modern (vegan oat-based soft serve, cold brew milkshakes)! The cheeseburger was a classic - classic burger with American cheese, ketchup, mustard, onion, pickles, and mayo. The hot dog was classic too. And the soft serve really hit the spot on a hot day. This place is a classic. And I 100% enjoyed my meal and my soft serve, the service, and the retro vibes. I would absolutely come back. I might even get exactly the same thing. Is there anything better than a classic cheeseburger and chocolate-dipped soft serve sometimes!? Definitely a place I want to return to on a future trip to Pittsburgh!

This is my second time at pages and I can't wait to come back again. Not only do me and Pages dairy mart share the same name they also have amazing ice cream and so many flavors to choose from. They also have dairy free options like oat milk ice cream. This time I got butter pecan soft serve on a sugar cone. It was wonderful! They also have blueberry soft serve that looked intriguing I'll have to try that next time.

Please go here and taste some of the most creamy delicious soft serve ever. After a long hot day of work you deserve a reward a decadence. The medium is ginormous and only in the 3.50 range. It was so good I almost went back for another. Almost.

I've heard so many great things about this ice cream shop and I finally got a chance to check it out. This place is super popular, we ended up waiting in line for maybe 15-20 minutes but the ice cream is worth the wait. I got the butterscotch sundae and the ice cream was so incredibly creamy. Probably one of the best soft serves I've ever had in my life. The parking situation here is pretty bad though so be prepared if you make the drive over and try going earlier in the day to avoid a huge crowd. The ice cream here is so good though that it's worth the trip!

We stopped for an afternoon snack on a weekday. There was a line but it moved. She had blackberry soft serve. He had the apple dumpling sundae with caramel sauce. There a LOT of choices. Fun to read the historical write-ups on the south side of the building. No seating (use the car). We will find an excuse to return!!

Connect to Page's FB or IG and be sure not to miss the fresh, seasonal blueberry soft serve. It's my absolute favorite soft serve and I look forward to it every season. Blueberry is so popular that they'll only sell it in the small and medium sizes. The ice cream is more on the creamy side and Page's is generous with the toppings. The line is always wrapped around the building but moves quickly. The employees are friendly and efficient. Cash only. Parking is a nightmare but doesn't deter my visits. Happy 70th Birthday Page Dairy Mart!

When I was a kid I used to come here all the time, but it's been about 50 years and it's still here. Every time we visit the City and drive by there is a line. In the middle of a weekday, it wasn't so bad so we stopped. I had a blizzard type treat and their ice cream is the real deal, not that ice milk garbage. My husband had a milkshake and it was so thick, it was yummy. Thumbs up for continuing to run a successful business for so long.

What a wonderful little place. I heard it was a Pittsburgh "Must Do" experience and I'm glad I went. I already know how I felt about Nancy B cookies (a spot that deserves it's spot on that list twice over) and was delighted to see all the reviews about the Nancy B chocolate chip cookie sundae, so I had to get it. Do not be fooled by the pictures: this can easily serve 2 people and was not meant for 1 excited Yelper on a hot summer afternoon.

I wish I could count how many times I've been here. Can any of us though? This is one of my favorite places to take guests visiting from out of town (in season of course). The fact that the soft serve tastes as good as it did when I was a kid (if not better) is obviously the main attraction. They always have so many fun flavors and all kinds of different ice cream treats from the classics to the modern and even things you can't get anywhere else. Be prepared to wait online because it's a hugely popular spot...but well worth the wait!

I've been to Page's multiple times, and it's one of my favorite places to go in Pittsburgh for dessert at night. The custard/soft serve is to die for. The menu is huge, and I generally get something new each time I go, but there is still so much to try. I recently got the peach sundae. It was sweet, but refreshingly so because of the fruit. (I highly recommend). I also think their burgers are good for the price (under $3!), and the fries are great too! Overall, Page's Dairy Mart is a great experience for a great price!

A classic. We have somehow managed to live in Pittsburgh for 27 years, and only discovered Page's this summer. What were we thinking? The line is always long, but it always moves quickly. I stick with the classics -- dip cone, hot fudge sundae-- and I am never disappointed. Love you, Page!

During this crazy time Page Dairy Mart closed shortly after they opened this year. After a few weeks they reopened using a website where you can order and pay online! pagedairymart.net It was so easy to order and pickup. We parked at a pickup number and an employee came to see our name and brought our ice cream right to our car. We were so happy to get our favorite treat. We will definitely be back to do another pickup and I hope that they keep this option in some form when they reopen fully.

Yummy soft serve! Classic cones and a great destination spot after a bike ride! Lots of parking available, if you choose the pick up option you have to be in the parking lot at their curbside spots. When it's busy it can take up to 30 minutes for an order and you can't wait in their designated curbside pick up spots.

While there's usually a line, this ice cream is worth the wait! My go-to is the South Side shake - a milkshake with a sundae on top! They have the most extensive ice cream menu, with something for every taste. They even have some dairy-free options, too, which my husband said was delicious. If you want to avoid a line, stop by on a rainy day.

Even though it was freezing out when we came to get our ice cream, our second experience was better than the first. Music from loudspeakers kept us entertained while we waited, distanced, in the long line of masked customers. It moved relatively quickly for how labor intensive it is to make custom ice cream orders. This time the server rang us up immediately, and there is a separate area for waiting for your order. Hubby had a small raspberry sundae, and I had a small turtle sundae. It was just the right amount, and so good. We ate in our car with the heat on and plan to be back if we're in the neighborhood.

Best ice cream in Pittsburgh!! I will forever recommend Page's to anyone who asks and their wrap around line speaks for itself. Try the Nancy B's Sunday or go for a simple twist in a cone. You won't be disappointed. And now they take cards!

Best ice cream/milkshakes in the city! My fave - peanut butter milkshakes! Don't let a line scare u from trying this place...it moves quick and worth the wait! The special sundaes are amazing and a meal in itself.. love the Nancy B chocolate chip cookie sundae ( warm cookies and ice cream how can you go wrong UPDATE: must try the burnt almond tort arctic swirl ..... so good! See ne

This ice cream was good but I'm not sure if it was really worth the hype in my opinion. You can get good ice cream without standing in a 25 minute line. Definitely worth stopping if the line looks short but not really worth the huge wait.
OH. MY. GOODNESS. Page's fall menu is to die for! Had the pumpkin roll attic swirl & it was the perfect combo of fall
We fell in love with this place! Tons of flavors in soft serve ice cream and the employees were super nice. The pistachio and mango soft serve flavors were our favorites!!

I've been waiting so long to come to Page's and already knew I'd order a Nancy B's chocolate chip cookie sundae. It didn't disappoint-- tons of hot fudge, whipped cream, creamy soft serve and warm cookie pieces. I love that they have so many types of milkshakes, sundaes and arctic swirls -- I'd love to come back and try the raspberry almond torte sundae or one of their pumpkin roll arctic blasts I've heard they have in the fall!

Don't be fooled by the simple exterior, a heavenly ice cream experience awaits at Page Dairy Mart. Oftentimes the line is long and is wrapped around the building. It's worth the wait. The line usually goes pretty fast, too. The menu is extensive and practically impossible to read, so there's a QR code to scan for easy viewing. I usually just go for soft serve. There are dozens of flavors, some even have crumbles or sprinkles mixed in, something I've never seen any other ice cream place with soft serve. Sundaes are great but very large. Either come hungry or consider sharing. You can't go wrong with the Nancy B cookie sundae, or really any other choice. The seasonal flavors are pretty great, too. In the summer they mix fresh blueberries into soft serve. And in the fall there's lots of choices, from pumpkin to apple and maple options. The only complaint I have is the parking situation. It's stressful and chaotic. But if you get past that, you're golden.

I'm so glad that I found this place last year! It's a PGH classic but if you don't know about it then you're missing out. Tucked away on an unassuming street in South Side, this little dairy mart knows its way around ice cream. It's always worth the drive and usual long wait in the line. Never disappoints. I have only gone at peak hours on weekends during which times we have waited sometimes close to an hour to order. But honestly, on a nice night out, I don't mind hanging out and chatting with friends while we're waiting to order. Once you order the food comes out super quickly. The non-ice cream food is just so-so but if you're hungry for something savory to complement your dairy dessert, it'll hit that spot for sure. The ice cream. Wow. So so good. As someone who eats probably way too much ice cream, I can honestly say that this place is one of the best. No matter what you order, it will be good. The arctic freezes easily beat out the classic Blizzard from Dairy Queen. Thicker, creamier, and more flavor options. The sundaes are huge - definitely split with someone if you're not up for the task of consuming the whole thing. The soft serve is delicious and the number of topping options is really impressive. Will definitely be coming here more as the summer heats up to try the other things on the menu. Note that parking can be pretty chaotic. You kind of just have to pull in and haphazardly find a spot to park (and probably eat your ice cream). There isn't any seating outside the place and there is no inside space. It's part of the charm in my opinion but definitely can see how it could be stressful if you have kiddos with you. Make sure to be prepared to eat in the car and grab some extra napkins for any spills!

Page's is a Pittsburgh staple and a must stop for anyone visiting. If you go at night time be prepared for a very long line, but it is definitely worth the wait. They have some of the best sundaes you will ever have. My favorite is the grilled sticky buns sundae. It is vanilla ice cream with two warm sticky buns and maple syrup on top. Their chocolate chip cookie sundae is also very good. An underrated part of Page's is their food. They have one of the best cheesesteaks you will find it Pittsburgh. Their burgers are also great.

Creamy soft serve End of story ...it's so good that you can eat it plain But why when this place offers dips Cherry chocolate and yes even blueberry It's a semi soft candy shell My daughter got the medium cherry dip cone it was huge I had a yum turtle Sunday The soft serve covered with chocolate sauce caramel and pecans heaven in a cup. Menu has all sorts of Sundaes Saw people enjoying Some were eating out right huge ones We brought home ice cream sammies Chocolate cookie filled with that same dreamy vanilla This place is that good A line on a cold spring night (38 degrees ) At 9:30pm If that doesn't tell you something You order at the window This is Outside my yelping friends outside

On our recent trip to Pittsburgh, we were finally able to stop at this gem. We tend to only come during the winter when it is closed, so it was very exciting to be there when this ice cream stand was open. Not being a Pittsburgh native, we had no idea of the backstory of this place or how amazing it would be. They have an amazing variety of ice cream treats and delicious soft serve. We went twice over the weekend. The line is definitely shorter during the day, and they are cash only. We tried soft serve,, waffle sundae, a dipped cone, an Arctic Blast and a cold brew shake, loved it all.

Pittsburgh's hidden gem! I lived here for 3 year before I even heard about this place. On the far far end of South Side (toward Homestead) sits Page Dairy Mart. One might be skeptical about stopping in after seeing its location on the side of a road, under a bridge, across from a train track but trust me - it is SO worth it. Honestly, the long line that weaves through the parking lot should be a dead giveaway about how good it is. Don't let the line steer you away either! It tends to move very quickly and the ice cream is worth the wait. The ONLY downside to Page's is there isn't really a seating area so you tend to either have to stand around to enjoy your treat or eat it in your car. But again, worth it. The menu is overwhelming large (a good problem to have) with your choices of milkshakes, arctic swirls, ice cream sandwiches, so many types of cones...the list goes on. (They also have food like fries, hot dogs, etc. but back to the ice cream). You can get something so decadent and sweet like an Yinzer sundae or something so simple and classic like a soft serve cone. It's some of the best soft serve in the 'burgh. I do have a roommate that is dairy sensitive and they don't have many options for that (I think just slushies/snow cones) but, for any one else, the world is your oyster at Page's. You can choose any item off the menu or come up with your own creation. I come from a small town where little, locally run ice cream shops thrive and this place just feels like home. If you're coming to visit Pittsburgh, I would honestly recommend coming here before some of the other "Pittsburgh classics".
Loved the variety in soft serve. I can see why the line is always there, every thing was delicious. I just wish absolutely everything was posted outside so I could make sure I saw all of my choices.

If you love soft serve, this is the place to go. There's history, tradition, the beauty of neon lights, plus really wonderful ice cream. You simply must experience the blueberry soft serve which is usually a limited time offering (not sure when it runs, but they had it there last night, June 8). Page is cash only, just so you know. It's definitely worth the trip. There's a small parking lot, so you can sit and eat your ice cream, as you may need to give it your full attention. Anyway, go for the nostalgia or go for the great ice cream, either way you win!

A friend and I came here right before closing on a Thursday night. This was my first time going but I've always been curious because every time I pass by there's always a huge line! We waited in line and I tried to read the extensive menu through the window behind the counter, which was pretty difficult. My friend informed that there menu is actually online so that might be an easier way to look at the huge menu. I decided on a vanilla cone dipped in cherry. I ordered a medium and was surprised how big it was! However, the cherry coating left a little bit of a waxy taste in my mouth. The vanilla ice cream was delicious though! While I don't think think I'd try their dip cones again I'd definitely give it another go with one of their many other products. Customer service was great! Even though it was close to closing and still had a line the woman who took our order was super friendly and helpful. Also this ice stand only takes cash but there is an atm on site.

My husband had heard about this ice cream shop from a coworker, and he wanted to try it out. The shop is a small older building that is located under a bridge. It has adequate parking but little seating outside. I ordered a vanilla soft-serve ice cream with peaches on top. The ice cream tasted very rich, and the peaches were sweet. I ordered a size small, but it was the perfect size for me. The employee who served us was polite. My husband ordered a root-beer float because this business seems to make their own root beer. He enjoyed his float. Prices were reasonable. We would feel happy to be return customers in the future.

I've driven past here several times and have seen it with literally 100 people wrapped around the side, so it has to be good, right? Yes. My first experience having something from here was on my special day. I had requested an ice cream cake for my birthday and my friend Jash was all like no it's going to melt in the sun. We compromised and had it indoors instead of at the picnic. I said I wanted a Dairy Queen cake and he decided to order from here instead. I was so mad, like, it was my birthday and should get what I wanted. Either way, he got me one from here and boy was I surprised. It was so much better than Dairy Queen (still love you), but it was richer, creamier, and did not leave me disappointed. Will absolutely return here again. Jash, if you're reading this, please buy me another cake.
We love to stop at Page's. They have a huge selection, and prices are good. Staff is always very friendly. It's a Pittsburgh tradition!!

Page's is good! Such a big selection of ice cream/desserts! The line can get long, and it's a little confusing after you order as they just shout out orders to the crowd. Overall though, would definitely recommend! (cash only!)

I really wanted to like this nostalgic place, but the service was terrible. The line (we had been forewarned) was long but quick. We got to the window and my partner ordered a medium cake batter shake. I ordered a Yintzer sundae and we stepped away to wait. The male who took my order called me back over and said they were no longer serving the Yintzer. I asked if they had anything similar and he said the chocolate chip cookie sundae was "basically the same thing, but with a chocolate chip cookie instead of a blonde brownie". No biggie-I ordered it. When we picked up our order at the window, the sundae had chocolate sauce instead of caramel. I told him I didn't care for chocolate, and that I thought it was supposed to be like the Yintzer? He said yes, you CAN get caramel sauce, but it's a special request. Huh? I asked for a Yintzer-like sundae, you affirm one exists then play semantics? He offered to remake it, but I declined and asked for a simple cone with sprinkles. He returned (several minutes later) with a plain cone. I asked again if he could put sprinkles on it? He did, begrudgingly. If I wanted to pull teeth, I'd have gone to dental school. Pass this "gem" up-it's a cubic zirconia. 2 stars because the cake batter shake tasted just like cake batter and the building is pretty cool.

If I had not been so busy shoveling blondies covered in butterscotch and the most decadent soft serve I've tasted, I would've gotten a photo. Though there were limits with supply chain issues (no dairy free or caramel the day we went) the line moved fast and the staff were quick and offered options. Next time we're in PGH were heading back!

The new oat-based vegan soft serve is amazing (better than the previously offered silk brand dairy free soft serve) ! It's creamy, soft, and moderately sweet. For people have problems with lactose, this is heaven! I will miss Page Dairy Mart when I leave Pittsburgh!
Always a family favorite. We don't mind the wait in the long line for kind service and great ice cream.

I've been coming to Page's my entire life and have to say its a staple to Pittsburgh culture. It's always been a special treat that never disappoints whether you are coming from a ball game at PNC Park or a night out on town. While they have your staples like chocolate and vanilla soft serve, Arctic swirls (a blizzard), and sundaes don't be afraid to try something a little out of the ordinary. Anytime after 6-7pm the line wraps around the building, but don't be discouraged as the line moves fast! The workers move as fast as they can to get you the ice cream you ordered. One of the best ice cream places in town by FAR! Way better than the chain restaurants like Dairy Queen and the likes. Just a tip: While it is cash only there is an ATM on the side of the building.

Don't let the line fool you, 15 minute wait for fantastic ice cream treats is worth it!! All the kids working there feed the line quickly and deliciously! Grilled food is fantastic also. Thank you Pages!!!

Every visit to Pittsburgh must include a Page stop. Bring cash as they don't take credit cards. Menu is so extensive that it is impossible to choose! But the swirl is always a good bet. Very thick and rich and easy to individualize with multiple base flavors and every add-in you can imagine. Their cheesecake chunks are so much better than cheesecake add-ins anywhere else. They are actual pieces of real cheesecake! Sundaes are enormous!

This place is all about the vibe, and I think most people get that. There are a lot of factors about Page Dairy Mart that, taken on their own, could raise some eyebrows. But I love the fact that it's right under an abandoned bridge. I love the menu that's too big to be contained by a chalkboard, so it's sprawled across the walls and off onto the side of the shack. I love peering into the dilapidated storefront across the street that once sold designer fashion articles, but I guess we'll never know for sure. I love that fact that you have to inhale your soft-serve on the side of a busy thoroughfare before it melts. And if it does melt, it joins the donations of previous costumers on the asphalt around the mart. I don't love the fact that it's difficult to find legitimate parking, but hey, it did spark thoughtful conversations about "What is legitimate parking, anyways?" and "Is this safe?" and "Are we sure this is the right place?" Ice cream 10/10. Also, every time I've gone here, I've gotten a cheeseburger for some reason. It's legit too, or maybe I was just really hungry.

If you're looking for a sweet spot that truly captures the heart of what Pittsburgh is, look no further than Page Dairy Mart. Is there a long line? Don't worry. It goes fast, and besides, you'll need the extra time to decide... There's just about any ice cream treat you can dream up (and more). To start, there are a zillion flavors of soft-serve, from Pistachio to Toasted Coconut. Just try to think up a topping or Arctic Swirl mix-in that they don't offer! There are even several sprinkle varieties to choose from. We can't not talk about their incredible lineup of unique Pittsburgh-inspired sundaes and seasonal treats. Page Diary Mart features local baked goodies too--like blondie brownies and cookies from Nancy B's and the famous Burnt Almond Torte from Prantl's. This is the REAL Pittsburgh: a legendary sweet treat tradition. You can keep your fancypants lavender and green tea flavors, your rolled ice cream novelty... take me to the ice cream joint by the river with the neon signs and the 900 flavors and the oversized servings I can share with my favorite people.

Thought this place was excellent. Have driven by many times and was didn't know if the line meant that it was understaffed or what? So I gave it a shot and was impressed! The staff was friendly and kept the line moving. The servings are generous and the choices are numerous. Definitely can see why there was a line. I'm not a soft serve fan and loved the place. I got a small and was thought WOW that's humongous! Definitely a repeater!

This place is busy every time I go! Before I moved to Pittsburgh, I remember going on an air bnb date with my partner, driving by this place and seeing the line. "WOAH, what's going on there?!" "That's Page's Dairy Mart-- I'll take you there next time you visit!" Little did I realize, they completely close down in the winter. It became a goal of mine to go there after a good date night. Yesterday, after seeing a $5 Monday movie at the south side works cinema, we went to Pages. We've been a few times together now, and I think on it fondly. They have a classic soft serve, very tasty, with almost every flavor I could imagine wanting. I become overwhelmed at the menu. I find that going with a peanut butter sundae with whipped cream, a chocolate dip cone, or a butterfinger shake is always good. Parking can be a bit sticky... but it does have its own lot. Order at the front and then pay CASH ONLY when you pick up. Make sure to lick at your treat as you read the history of Page's Dairy Mart, which can be found on the wall opposite of the ordering window.

After stopping here on several occasions, I've yet to figure out the hype. It must be rooted in the tradition and memories this place invokes for a lot of Pittsburghers. All local soft serve establishments run together for me, and this one is no exception. You'll get a good basic cone, a standard milkshake, or a decent banana boat, but it's otherwise nothing to write home about. I still don't understand their system either as different cashiers shift in and out of the 4 windows. Some people pay when ordering, some when the items are ready to be picked up (cash only mind you). There is always general confusion about who's order belongs to whom as they are typically busy. It's a Pittsburgh staple though, and worth the annual visit.

WOW, what a delicious, historical ice cream spot! This has been on my bucket list for a long time because all of the locals recommend this place for ice cream. There is usually a REALLY long line during the summer, wrapped around the little building. Luckily, I went there around 3 PM on Saturday and there was barely a line. I got the coffee soft serve with their crunch topping which is basically oreo crumbles. There are SO many soft serve flavors, about 20! They don't only sell soft serve. My boyfriend got the "yinzer sundae" which I wish I got. It had blondies, caramel, whipped cream, and all of the deliciousness you could imagine in one bowl! There are also milkshakes, smoothies, cookies, brownies, and other scrumptious sweet treats. I think they are well known for the smooth, rich cream they use! Also, there is a huge timeline of their history and they date back to the 1800s! You can't beat that!

If you want the smoothest soft serve ice cream ever, then Page's is the place. It is located under an outrageously large and high concrete train trestle at the corner of Becks Run aka the blue belt and Carson. Its a cool spot especially on a warm night. I decided to try a Heath bar swirl which is actually like a blizzard and not a swirl. I got a small but would have preferred half the amount I got. I also would have preferred half the amount of Heath bar. Next time I will ask for half the amount they normally put in. The vanilla ice cream was very good, and had the smoothest texture of any ice cream I've ever had. I really liked it.
THE BEST ICE CREAM IN THE BURGH! So many ice cream options... and let's not forget pup cups!
One of my favorite spots in the summer. Great variety to choose from. It's cash only so make sure to bring enough cash.

Yeah, I get the hype now. My first visit was above average, everything was delicious, but I left debating if the 25 minute line was really worth it or not. After craving some elevated soft serve, we made a trip back, and again, and again, and again. Each time trying something different. I get the hype now, this place is legit. They have a ton of different flavored soft serves, all of them are extremely well executed! Their sundaes are enormous and can easily be shared between 2-3 people. While the line may appear long, it does move quickly. Cash only with an ATM on site. The one thing I do wish they did is call out orders via a numbering system. They have designated spots for those who have ordered to wait by and hear their orders being called out, but you have to be paying attention to hear your order called, and know who ordered before/after you, as oftentimes people will get the same things, especially if they're running their seasonal menu. There's been a few times where a customer and I will be in a silent standoff debating if the Nancy B Cookie Sundae was theirs or mine. Would be much easier if they gave you a number which they called out, rather than calling out the order details. Either way, we can't wait for Page Diary Mart to reopen for 2022!
Best ice cream ever. Cash only. Long lines weekend nights. Limited parking. Get the Nancy B cookie sundae you won't regret it!

Page's is a Pittsburgh ICON. I've been eating their ice cream since before I could walk or talk. The creamy cones are synonymous with summer in Pittsburgh. During the summer, you can expect to wait to get your dessert from Page's, but it's always worth it. They have such a huge selection to choose from, most using their thick soft serve as a starting point. Personally, I find it refreshing from time to time to order just a vanilla soft serve cone. Get back to basics and really enjoy the extra cream that they stir into their mix. I do recommend the dirt sundae. It was my go-to growing up. What's better than finding a rock hard gummy worm nestled into your crunched up Oreo's?? Aside from ice cream, Page's also serves a small menu of hot food. I can remember stopping by during the day with my gramma to get a 35 cent cheeseburger. They are always made fresh on their grill inside next to the banana split station (odd combo, I know.) I was ALWAYs tempted to get the nacho's because you can see them from the ordering window, but always had stage fright going up to that little window. Page's has been around for decades, and it's clear that it will be around for decades longer. If you're looking for an authentic Pittsburgh experience, it always ends with a cone from Page's!
My favorite place to go for ice cream in Pittsburgh! So many different options of flavors and speciality items.

The line is WORTH IT every time. Always. Even though it's cash only, they have a helpful ATM right there in case you are short a couple bucks. Every option on the menu is affordable! The Nancy B's sundae with twist is easily the closest thing to heaven here on earth. I highly recommend trying it at least once. Honestly, I've never tried anything else....yet.

This is a nice drive-in ice cream mart which has a wide variety of items including cones, shakes, sundaes, ... It is at a busy intersection and parking can be tricky and it can be crowded. The crowded times speak to its popularity though. With many places to choose for ice cream in Pittsburgh, I come to Page because it serves a wickedly good toasted coconut ice cream. Well worth the trip even if you have to wait.

The lines are always superrrrrrrrrr long, but well worth the wait. Chocolate chip cookie sundae is to die for! Somehow the keep the cookie super soft, moist, and still warm like it was fresh out of the over. Many windows so line moves rather quickly. Cash only which sucks, but for a few there is an atm onsite

Page's has become my family's go-to ice cream. My favorite is the birthday cake which contains ACTUAL BIRTHDAY CAKE. If you're feeling sassy, ask them to dip it in peanuts. There's always a line and parking can be dicey so bring your bike or compact car! It can also be a pain to get out of this place when there's traffic.

OMG the works sundae was delicious and put me in a sugar coma (just kidding). First off the vanilla ice cream is so rich and creamy it's good all by itself, then you add the yinzer sundae with the burnt almond torte sundae and you have the best of both worlds and an explosion in your mouth. My daughter got the cookie sundae and she said that was delicious to, I don't think you can get something that you don't like from this place.

Page Dairy Mart is a very nice place. They have a great selection of flavors. As the seasons change, so do their flavors. We tried the apple butter soft serve. Very good! My son had the pumpkin roll. It was served with a small piece of pumpkin roll on it. Everyone seemed to be wearing big smiles as they left with their ice cream.

Always a line, but so worth it. Over a dozen flavors of soft serve. They even have one made from oat milk so you can bring your lactose intolerant friends. A small cone here is what most places consider to be a medium. Yes, it's worth the wait in line. Besides, you are going to need the extra time to consider all the different options of soft serve flavors and sundaes.
Page's ice cream is so good! They have many different concoctions to try! The couple in front of me were ordering cheese steak hoagies. I'll try this on a visit with a sundae for dessert.

While dying from the Pittsburgh July sun, me and a couple friends made our way for our first visit to Page's (I've heard glowing reviews about this place)! I came on July 4th/Independence day! It was open regular hours. Quite a lot of people were here too so there was a bit of a line. SOFT SERVE (~$2.50ea for small) MANGO: My mango loving ice cream friend got this. Unfortunately, didn't really taste like mango, bummer... TOASTED COCONUT: I loved this one so much!!! The creamy ice cream with the toasted coconut flakes were bombbbbbbb. PISTACHIO: Very tasty! Tastes like pistachio if that's what you like! I wanna come back and try everything. Maybe the cookie dough artic swirl? Or strawberry shortcake sundae? Or a hot dog?!

Great selection of goodies! The hardest part is deciding what to get from the vast variety offered. Just had a pecan pumpkin arctic swirl-deliciousness is a cup! Fresh pumpkin, pecans and vanilla wafers all blended together. It was So good I forgot to take a picture.

Literally the best place in Pittsburgh to get ice cream. They have something for everyone, including multiple soft serve flavors, sundaes, banana splits, cookie sundaes ft. Nancy B's cookies, scooter crunch topping, shakes, and so much more! Be prepared to wait in line. It moves quickly, but there is normally a wait. FYI- this place is cash only (I'm almost positive), so bring some cash with you. I honestly can't sing Page's praises enough... if you've never been... make sure you stop here this summer!
Favorite ice cream in the Burgh! I would eat it year round if I could. Key Lime Pie! Can't wait till the warmer weather.

love pages so much. It's always busy, but the line usually goes pretty fast and gives you enough time to decide what you want haha. I think it's very fair pricing, but it's cash only. I believe there is an ATM on site

The ice cream is delicious! I've tried a few different sundaes, both good. Of course I've had the cookie sundae which is delicious but too much for me to eat. I think it's perfect to share with someone. The ice cream is smooth and creamy. This coupled with the warm cookies and hot fudge is just perfect. They seem to have endless options for ice cream flavors, sundaes, snow cones, etc. I'm sure everyone can find something they like here. CASH ONLY but there is an ATM on the side of the building.

The best soft serve ice cream around hands down. My favorite is the peanut butter sundae. On my most recent visit I tried the pumpkin ice cream. It was really good but Im going back to my peanut butter sundae next time. They have MANY flavors to choose from. They do have social distance guidelines in place waiting in line, however, after you order and pay everyone is bulked in one spot to pick up their ice cream. It would be nice if there was a better system for that but hopefully they won't have to worry about this next year!
Ice Cream!! Oh Yeah!! This is one of my favorite places to go. Everything is so delicious. Favorite pick :. Chocolate Peanut Nut Butter Milkshake. Need I say more.... it's the best!!!!

If I were to compare Page Dairy Mart to a book, I'd compare its S'mores Arctic Swirl to The Hazel Wood by Melissa Albert. Every taste is filled with smoky, enticing flavors of marshmallow, graham cracker, and chocolate. Page's is a Pittsburgh icon with its tucked-away location and infamous lines of ice cream lovers. But Page's isn't just for ice cream! You can order an entire meal as well, but I tend to just go for the ice cream because if you order appropriately, then that's a whole meal! My favorites at Page's include the S'mores arctic swirl and the Burnt Almond Raspberry Torte sundae. Honestly, it's really difficult to make me change my order! Pro Tip: Bring cash and a few small bills to tip! Extra Pro Tip: After you order, step away from the window to the side because they'll keep taking orders, and keep an eye out for the individual that took your order.

How is it possible that I have never reviewed Page's (how any proper Pittsburgher refers to this spot)? It's a Pittsburgh institution and most definitely the first place I think to take an out-of-owner when it comes to Pittsburgh ice cream spots. The soft serve is delicious, but what really makes this place is the collaborations with fellow Pittsburgh small businesses like Nancy B's chocolate chip cookies, local cinnamon buns, blondies (try the Yinzer sundae!) and banana bread. Look for the "Made in Pittsburgh" marker on the little banner ads they have hanging on the windows while you wait in line, and those would be the go-to items in my opinion. I can honestly say I've never had a bad item here. The Nancy B's (best chocolate chip cookie in the city) and Yinzer are two favorites, but one day they were out of both toward the end of the season and I got the cinnamon bun sundae which was surprisingly light with crunchy pastry pieces. The seasonal soft-serve flavors are also a big favorite; try the blueberry (a very fast melter so get eating quick), during summer, and pumpkin and apple during fall. They were briefly accepting cards via online ordering/curbside pickup earlier during Covid but are back to cash only, so bring your cash unless you want to pay an onsite ATM fee, and be prepared for some long lines and challenging parking during peak summer evening or weekend hours. It's worth it.

Is it good? Yes. Is it worth standing in line 30 minutes for? Debatable. Also, social distancing signs present but not observed. People, on top of people. This was my first Page Dairy Mart experience. Parking, tricky. Line, long. Mind you, this was a Sunday evening around 730PM. If I return, it will be mid-day. Unfortunately, I think You'll always run into a long line here. Our ice cream was pretty good. I had the "Yinzer Sundae" and my fiancÃ© had the "Hot cookie Sundae" both were very good, and a little under $7 each. If I had to choose, I would to with the Yinzer Sundae because they use a blonde brownie from pastries al a carte, which is one of my favorite bakeries! They also had a puppy bone to throw in to my four legged babies dessert.

A hidden gem for sure! My friend always raved about Pages and I'm glad I finally got to try it. I got the chocolate chip cookie sundae. The soft serve ice cream is so creamy and smooooth. The chocolate chip cookie is warmed before being added to your Sunday. OMG, mouthgasm!!! I didn't realize how popular it was until I got there and there was a line of probably 25-30 people on a Sunday night! Line goes by relatively quickly and the staff are really nice despite being slammed. Parking can get tricky when it's crowded but people are in a out often so you can find one in a few minutes if you don't at first. Also remember it's *cash only* but there's an ATM around the corner. Can't wait to come back and try something else!

Omg! Where do I begin with this wonderfully sweet cold heavenly treat. Page Dairy Mart's ice cream is great by itself but they support local businesses to create mind blowing sundaes. Like Nancy B's chocolate chip cookie sundae. Or even better the burnt Almond Torte sundae which simply was the greatest ice cream creation that I've ever had in my life. Seriously, Page Dairy Mart is my new favorite and worth the 40 minute drive.

I visited this place last night on a bike ride, which allowed me to feel less guilty about my small chocolate-dipped cone. I wouldn't call myself a huge fan of soft serve ice cream in general, but the stuff they serve here is so incredibly smooth and creamy! I've been here twice before, and one of these times, I ordered the chocolate chip cookie sundae, which was incredible! The warmth of the cookie and hot fudge, and the coolness of the ice cream was pure bliss. While there last night, I saw a sign in the window advertising a cinnamon roll sundae--guess I know what I'm getting next time! EDIT: Tried the cinnamon roll sundae, and was given a stale cinnamon roll. Also, they didn't have maple syrup the day I ordered it, and it tasted weird with butterscotch syrup. I'll be sticking to the cookie and brownie sundaes from now on. 4.5 stars.

I want to focus on ordering their fast food items and Sundays, which might not have been covered by other reviews. I wanted to get a quick dinner there in addition to some ice cream being that it was a hot day. I ordered a cheeseburger with tomato, lettuce and onions and the Yinzer Sunday. After I ordered the food she asked me if I wanted the Sunday with the hot food and I told her I would get that separate. I am not sure how many orders they get for food because this took quite a while. When I finally got it I was pretty impressed with the burger though. It was nicely cooked and had good bread. The fries were a bit limp and not crisp like they should be, but I was o.k. with that. I went back to get the Yinzer sunday because it is one of my favorites. Vanilla ice cream with a blondie brownie, caramel syrup, wipped cream and nuts on top. It is quite lovely and more than one person can typically handle. Drawbacks to Page: The location of this place is a disaster that always happens. This is because it is right at the corner of where 2 busy roads meet(West Carson and Becks Run Road). You pull in off of Carson and no one knows where to go when they are leaving. There is no set way of doing things. When you leave, where do you go? If you try to go back the way you came onto Carson there is traffic stopped at the light blocking your path and other traffic coming in the next lane. You can circle around onto Becks Run Road, but you will have to wait for traffic to stop moving coming from Becks, which takes forever, or they will be stopped at the light on the other side of the corner and you will have to wait for that also. Either way it makes for a very akward visit. And this is when it is not so busy, if it is busy expect more confusion and utter chaos. If you are a patient person than ignore what I have just said and go there all the time.

Pure Americana right here! Some of the best soft serve ice cream in all of Pittsburgh! There menu is so vast, you could probably order something different every day of the summer! Personal favorites include South Side Shakes, Arctic Swirls, and the Nancy B's Cookie Sundae (If you don't know about Nancy B's cookies in Homestead, then make sure you add it to your list of delicious places to visit!). Prepare to wait in long lines here, but trust me....it's worth it. Also a cash only establishment....there is an ATM on site for those of us like me who never carry cash!
This place is a Pittsbrgh tradition! You have to stop at pages Dairy and get some ice cream in the summer months!

There's no better place for ice cream and decadent treats in Pittsburgh. The menu is huge and makes it difficult to choose from. Their ice cream cakes are great also! Be prepared for the long line which moves at a decent pace.

Have been wanting to trying this place for a while! Came on a Thursday night and there was a pretty long line, but it moves quickly. Luckily we found a parking spot. I got the Nancy B Chocolate Fudge Sundae! Wow, was it huge! The chocolate chip cookie was nice and warm and they did not skimp on the fudge. I truly enjoyed every bite! They have so many options to choose from, so I know I will definitely be back. My friend got an arctic swirl and enjoyed it as well. Their portions are huge, so come hungry! Overall, a great place to satisfy your sweet tooth craving! Prices are super reasonable as well!
Best soft serve around. Just look at the line of people. The prices are reasonable as well.

Such an awesome place to grab a satisfying cone of ice cream on a summer afternoon! Great to spend time with friends, lines can get very very long, some times can be difficult to find parking as well. I wouldn't say the ice cream is gourmet, but it's very delicious nonetheless. My friend ordered coconut caramel cookie, and it tasted like a Girl Scout cookie samosa in ice cream form. It was a unique flavor and I hope to go back to try what else they have, which by the way is an enormous list!

Fun spot to get soft serve ice cream! We beat the long line but I always see a line here. I got the toasted coconut soft serve on a sugar cone - so yummy! They had bits of toasted coconut. Serving size is large. I got a small cone and went into a delightful food coma after

Good ice cream bad line sometimes when everyone has the same idea but it moves quickly. Good scenery too eye farkin every car parked at that light waiting to go while you eat your twist come. I get a soft serve dip when I'm here it's the stuff

First time here. On a chilly Mid March Saturday night, the place was packed. If you love big soft serve sundaes with all the fixings, this is the place to come, just be careful getting in and out of the lot.
You owe it to yourself to get a treat from this stand. Super cool location under the bridge, bring cash and your sweet tooth as they have a lot of options!

Page dairy mart is delightful! There are SOOO many options that its a little overwhelming on the first visit. The menu seems to be spread out, so take a minute to soak the options in. There were a lot of people when I went, but the line moved super fast. There is also a ton of parking, so turn down the intersecting road and find a relaxed spot under the bridge. A friend recommended the snowstorm to me, so I am recommending it to yelp! I got an oreo cheesecake snowstorm and it was divine!
still amazing. got the cheesecake soft serve with the cookie crumble on the outside. my sister got the coconut ice cream dipped in chocolate, both loved ours.

Major fail. If this place is supposed to be a great representation of Pittsburgh's offerings... Pittsburgh is in trouble. :( It was a hot night. So of course we wanted ice cream. Dude... the soft serve was just a melted mess!! It was more like a gross milkshake cuz it was so liquidy. But it also tasted like hell. I ordered a coffee arctic w heath bar candy. How dare she claim that it's like a blizzard!?! This thing was nowhere near a blizzard! I could mix ingredients better at home. And w better flavor. Then... the kid ordered the mango soft serve. The server said, "we dont have mango." We had to point it out to her on the menu. They dont offer samples. She said, its "probably" good. Um... no... it was not good at all. It was so disgusting that my kid couldnt even eat it. And we NEVER throw away ice cream!! Tip to the business: if your soft serve is a hot melted mess... dont open your doors until you fix your refrigeration problem.

Dairy Queen at the other end of Carson st. is waaaaay better & The lines if any are never too bad. Y'all people that wait in that long azz line every night for mediocre ice cream, lined up like sheep that wraps around the building are just stupid......

Decided to stop by Page Dairy Mart for the first time ever last night after a Riverhounds game and WOW am I glad we did - it completely lives up to the hype! We arrived and parked in their unassuming parking lot and got in (the very long) line. It was pushing 10pm and we were nervous about whether or not we'd be served before they closed. Amazingly, he incredible staff in PDM served every customer until the line was over. They were SO gracious and kind and they deserved every tip on the planet for being so awesome, in spite of the late night and the long long that remained at 10! By the time we reached the front of the line I decided to try the famous chocolate chip cookie sundae with pecans. When I say this was the best ice cream treat I've had in SUCH a long time, I mean it - an incredible warm cookie, delicious custard-y ice cream, hot fudge, and salty nuts? It was every bit as delicious as I hoped for, and again, the staff put their all into making great quality products despite the lateness of the evening. I'm so impressed and truly cannot wait to return. My husband (who enjoyed an enormous soft serve cone) said "it's a good thing we don't live closer, otherwise we'd be there every day." He's right - but that doesn't mean we won't be back as soon as possible!

This place has such great ice cream. The menu is big enough that I can try something new every time I come. Be careful if you have a nut allergy- but it is nice that all the flavors are soft serve so there is no cross contamination from the scoops. My friends and I keep coming back here! I'll miss it when I graduate from Pitt.
Such an iconic and classic place! Love the dairy free options! Everything I have ever had here has been delicious!

Page's is the best. As a dairy lover, I also happen to be lactose intolerant, and so most of my dairy outings are spent wondering if it was worth it. Whenever I hit up Page's, the answer is always, without any hesitation, yes. It was very worth it. Get your soft serve dipped, get it with a freshly warm cookie or brownie, and if you can't decide, get a little bit of everything (really, it's an option). Don't want ice cream? Get a burger! But, actually, get ice cream. Why would you not want ice cream? The line moves fast, the people are awesome, and the ice cream makes it all worth it.
Such a fun vibe with a million options and can't beat prices ! No place to sit if that's what you're looking for
This place is awesome! The line may sometimes be long, but you'll be at the front before you know it. Everyone that works there is so polite, especially the Manager!

I don't know how I lived in Pittsburgh for five years without trying this place. But I finally did and my life has been CHANGED! I love ice cream and this place is just the best! I love that they have so many flavors of soft serve - I think that sets them apart from many other places. They also have so many unique sundaes and other ice cream treats that I can't wait to try! I do wish they had bicycle parking - my husband and I rode their bikes down there and it started raining once we were there. There was nowhere to lock up our bikes, otherwise we would have just taken an uber home and come back for them later.

Do chaufeering for local company. Many times while going to allegheny county west Mifflin airport (private ) client stops for treat. B4 they're whisked away to a foreign land or accross the great USA...... It's a burg thing ya know.

This is always our go-to ice cream place. My kids and I have been coming for years! Lines can get a little hectic, but it's worth the chaos. They have everything from flavored soft serve, to tropical snow, to milkshakes, to sundaes, to Arctic swirls (blizzards). Not to mention their other hot food, such as their fries and burgers, plus straight-from-the-barrel root beer, all make for a pretty satisfying treat on a warm summer night.

I have to go back to this place! It's a gem hiding in an old gas station. I had the cinnamon roll Sunday and it was just big and amazing. I mean for $4.25 it was big. I mean it's like the size of something from the Cheesecake Factory but with a price from the 90s. They have a massive selection and it's hard to pick. If everything is as good as what I had today I can't wait to try something different every time I go back from now on. This place is a must try.
I remember that as a kid they used to give milkshake tickets when you hit a homerun for North Baldwin Still great service still great ice cream iconic location.

You really cannot go wrong here! No matter when you arrive, there will probably be a wait so be prepared. However, it is so worth it! They serve about 20 flavors of the best soft serve ice cream! Their milkshakes are incredible. Plus they have sooo many toppings! If you want something different than the usual cone/milkshake, try one of their creations! Think Nancy B cookie sundaes, yummm. I know this sounds crazy but their ice cream is so rich & creamy, it doesn't melt right away which is amazing! Cash only which is the only downfall. I really feel this would speed up the line, but hey whatever they are doing seems to work! ATM on site. Don't forget your dogs pup cup :)

I have been looking forward to returning to Page Dairy Mart since I've been seeing it get rave reviews on different sites. I finally got that opportunity. The first thing I must stress is that they serve soft serve ice cream. They do not have any hard ice cream you would find in stores or at different vendors. I'm usually a fan of the latter but in this case I will make an exception. Page dairy mart carries your traditional vanilla, chocolate, and twist varieties but they have a number of different flavors they can make them in. A few of these flavors include black cherry, butter pecan, birthday cake (made with real cake) and peanut butter (again made with real peanut butter). In addition to cones they carry the usual fare which include milkshakes, arctic swirls, slushes, floats, etc. However, there number one selling item is their sundaes. Their sundaes come in several different sizes which if you end up with a medium will be about 3 scoops of ice cream and they will add things like brownies, cake, cinnamon bun or even a cookie. One of the two top selling sundaes is the "Yinzer" which is made with a brownie, chocolate chip Heath bar, vanilla ice cream, topped with hot caramel and whipped cream. The other is the cookie sundae which is made with a large warmed chocolate peanut butter chip cookie that comes from Nancy B's further down in Homestead, vanilla ice cream, and topped with your choice. When I went to order I learned that Nancy B's is closed this week due to vacation so they did not stock that flavor. However they came out with a brand new flavor called burnt almond cake sundae. The burnt almond cake comes from Grandview bakery on Mt. Washington where I have often frequented and have been very pleased with their baked goods. It has a custard filling and they thought to put a small amount of raspberry glaze on it to give it just a touch of flavor. Although normally served as medium I asked if they could make it into a smaller size which they did. I was aware how huge these portions are. You really get more bang for your buck here! I was grateful and believe me this was just like eating a burnt almond torte. It was so good!! Page Dairy Mart has been a long standing ice cream stand which is easy to overlook when driving to either Homestead or the Southside. Located on E Carson St at the corner of Becks Run Road near Carrick it is probably the best soft serve ice cream you can find in the city. Open seasonally. A must return!

I haven't been to Pages since I was a kid! And it's as good as I remember it. If you like soft serve then they will have a flavor you will love. I really wanted to get a chocolate chip Sundae. They make it with Nancy B's cookies (the best chocolate chip cookie I've ever had) Their Sundae's are huge!! Under $5. Decided to just get a small Sunday with a cookie on the side! Peanut butter soft serve with hot fudge and a chocolate chip cookie on the side. PERFECT!!!!!

One of my favorite places to get ice cream in the summer! They make their own soft serve flavors, a pretty large list of options, which are different from your typical chocolate, vanilla, or twist. Not only does the ice cream have the unique delicious flavor, but they add more flavoring by mixing in chocolate chips, brownie pieces, coconut flakes, etc. depending on which flavor you order. It's made to order, so your ice cream is freshly made by the employees. They also make delicious sundaes that include all your favorite toppings. Just like the classic Dairy Queen restaurants, there is no seating. So make sure you grab napkins before climbing back into your car. It's a fantastic place to go with friends and family, there's something for everyone
So good ive lived here for years and I've never been shame on me. If you're a cookie lover like me then the cookie sundae is a must

Massive menu with a lot of great options and huge portions. I am a fan of the Cookie Sundae (soft serve, hot fudge, fresh warm chocolate chip cookies, whipped cream and nuts) or the Blondie Sundae (same deal as previous, but blondies instead of cookies). My son is a big fan of the dip cones - soft serve dipped in a flavored sauce that forms a hard shell. He often orders based on color - with blueberry and cherry being his favorites. And if the massive amount of ice cream options aren't enough, PDM also has surprisingly good food options. The line can get long and parking is limited, but fortunately the employees really keep things moving. Page Dairy Mart is a Pittsburgh classic and one of my favorite places for ice cream in the city.

This place is such a Pittsburgh gem!! The best ice cream I've ever had. Their menu is HUGE and everything is so so good. This is a must if you are visiting Pittsburgh or live here and haven't ever been.
