Cute 'little' ice cream stand on the side of the road. They have so many options. Really delicious soft serve, quick service, friendly, and such a fun atmosphere. They have dairy free options, and lots of great mix in choices. We will definitely be back! *they are cash ONLY

Anytime I am in Pittsburgh I have to stop at Page Dairy Mart. I love this place! The ice cream is so creamy and has a smooth taste. It's also not so sweet that you feel sick after eating it (looking at you Dairy Queen). Page Dairy Mart is located under a rail road trestle in an industrial area in the South Side close to Hays. Its a cool place for an ice cream shop. When we visited in the early evening it was very crowded with a diverse group of ice cream aficionados all enjoying their desserts (they also serve savory food like cheese burgers). I had a South Side Shake (milkshake with a sundae on top -- I chose a peanut butter base with hot fudge topping) and the others in my party had a Yinzer Sundae and a cookie dough Arctic Swirl. I wish they had a Page Dairy Mart in Vegas!

Have I really never reviewed Page's?! Page's is my absolute favorite ice cream in Pittsburgh. It's a soft serve shop - so if you prefer hard scoop this is not your place! They do tons of speciality items and make soft serve in a great variety of flavors. My favorite is their mint chocolate chip - I think it's so refreshing in the summer. The blueberry is very good too! They are cash only. I wish they would always do curbside pre-orders like they did during the heart of the quarantine.

Page Dairy Mart is not near anything and you will specifically only come to this area for Page. The parking lot is not so big and parts of it are awkward and under a bridge but no worries you will always be able to find a spot. I have never been to page when the line is not super long. Daytime, nighttime, weekday, weekend, rain or shine. Always long! But fear not again, the line moves super quick. But, you know the saying if the line is long the place must be good, well the saying is true. Page is amazingly delicious and worth the line. They have what feels like a million things on their menu. Ice cream, soft serve, shakes, shaved iced, slushies , sundaes, arctic swirls, ice cream sandwiches, and so much more. For the soft serve they don't just have the traditional vanilla, chocolate, and twist. Page has almost 30 soft serve flavors. Some of my favs are the pistachio and birthday cake. My go to order is normally a small cherry dipped vanilla soft serve in a cone. I know I know, not the most interesting order but I just can't resist the classics. They have the best vanilla soft serve out of anywhere I have been. Page is cheap and is in no way stingy with the portions. Some major pieces of advice/things to know ***cash only!!! (They do have an atm with a fee) ***If you have never been here before look at the menu online or once you get there, just go to the front of the line to get one of the paper menus they have by the window ***there is no seating, so be prepared to stand on the sidewalk or sit in your car to enjoy your treats The only bad thing I can say about this place and something I wish they would change is that they take your order, you wait to the side, they give you your treats, and then you pay. So you are holding your cone trying to get your money out and then trying to shove your change back in your purse or pocket all while leaning over the next person who is trying to order. It's awkward and not efficient in my opinion. Please just take my order, let me pay, then hand me my tasty treats. Thank you! Other than that Page is delicious and I will be back and back again. Maybe just stay open through the winter so I can keep eating cherry dipped cones.
Friendly atmosphere and delicious ice cream. The customer service is always outstanding.

Probably the greatest ice cream spot- definitely in Pittsburgh, maybe the US? The atmosphere is what makes Page stand out - the location tucked under a rail bridge, the excessive signage, the old fashioned building and lights, the lines wrapping around the parking lot. The ice cream selection is immense and can be a bit hit or miss, but generally delicious. Special flavors are usually winners. The fresh blueberry soft serve is soooo good! I've never had anything like it before and was blown away by how fresh it was! If you're feeling decadent, the specialty sundaes are intense and delicious. The cinnamon roll one is my favorite.

Paige Dairy Mart will blow you away. The ice cream is really out of this world and totally worth the hype. Be sure to bring cash when you visit! I always opt for an arctic swirl and my all-time favorite has been the pumpkin pie. In the fall they make a delicious pumpkin ice cream and it has me looking forward to fall already! The banana bread arctic swirl is also a favorite because it contains real banana bread!! I have had many other delicious arctic swirls and never met one that I didn't like. My boyfriend also really enjoys their coffee soft serve. It is made with coffee from Big Dog Coffee in the southside. I love that Paige Dairy Mart uses local ingredients in their recipes!

I'm definitely a minority, because I didn't find the ice cream to be particularly amazing. Plus the workers were so rushed that despite requesting a twist on my cinnamon bun sundae, I was given plain vanilla and realized it too late. The description says it comes with 2 cinnamon buns, but I received two halves of the outermost roll, so less than 1. Portions are still enormous but not worth the $4.50 or so, considering I could just pay for a cinnamon bun separately (it's good they sell pastries as well). I'll go back to try the interesting soft-serve flavors though.

Wow! Incredible quality for a little ice cream stand. Typical cones, sundaes, and milkshakes. But a menu of burgers, fries, nachos, etc. and items like the raspberry toasted almond tort sundae really set this place a part from competitors. Worth the trip.

This is hands down, the best ice cream place in Pittsburgh. It is legendary. The lines are well worth the wait, but honestly, it moves pretty fast. It is CASH ONLY so remember to keep that in mind. There is an atm on site though. My favorite is the pistachio soft serve with crunchies on top. Also every single sunday they have on the menu there is to die for! I seriously can't say enough good things about this place. Go now to find out for yourself.

Over-hyped. I thought that Page's tasted like an average soft-serve ice cream shop. I was also surprised about the lack of flavors that they offered, there was no cookies and cream or sorbets. I ordered a small Chocolate Chip ice cream with rainbow sprinkles and my boyfriend ordered the Strawberry Shortcake sundae. My Chocolate Chip ice cream tasted identical to Breyer's boxed ice cream from the grocery store. I may have ordered the wrong item but because it is soft-serve ice cream they don't offer samples. My boyfriend had the Strawberry Shortcake sundae which had 3 pieces of cake on the bottom, 2 scoops of vanilla ice cream, strawberry syrup, strawberries (not fresh), almonds and whipped cream. It was huge and they didn't allow him to swap flavors or make any adjustments. Maybe my expectations of Page's were too high, but when I had heard about this ice cream shop whose line wrapped down the street I knew I had to check this place out. When I went on a Friday night there was no line and the ice cream was sub-par.

Pros: this place has really great ice cream. They have a wide selection of different flavors and preparations that basically anything you'd want from traditional ice cream is covered here. There's nothing particularly fancy about it, but this place just has really good ice cream. Cons: it's under an overpass, near some train tracks (so often it's loud), difficult to get to unless you drive there, doesn't really have outdoor seating since it's just situated in a parking lot, and is cash only. Also there's a line usually but that's to be expected. If you can get there and have cash on hand (and some patience) great ice cream can be yours.

Awesome ice cream with extremely reasonable prices. There are tons of options and the workers are always so friendly and will be accommodating with whatever you order. Cash only, but they do have an ATM. Not very many places to sit there and eat so you have to eat in your car or just wander around the property.
This is one of our favorite ice cream places in Pittsburgh! Everything is delicious! EVERYTHING!!!! Only downside is that they only accept cash, oh and they aren't open year round!

Looks like this is the place to go to for soft serve ice cream! The location and environment are definitely unique, and the parking situation might be a bit difficult if a lot of people are there, but it's worth the wait. We tried the toasted coconut and birthday cake, and suffice to say both were amazing. Soft and smooth texture, deep flavors with real coconut flakes or cake batter, all in a nice tall cone. Can't wait to go back and try some other flavors or maybe their shaved ice.

Tasty local establishment, featuring extensive menu of novelty ice cream treats! They partner with other local bakeries and pastry shops to create new novelties, such as a burnt almond torte sundae. Great for fun concoctions and decadent milkshakes, but also a go-to for basic staples (its my favorite vanilla cone!). Cash only! Usually will have a long line but they are EFFICIENT! and you won't have to wait more than 10 minutes before you can order,even with the line winding around the lot! Parking is limited, first come first served, with no real parking rules, but with such quick service, parking opens up quickly.

Really wanted to like our trip, and might give it another try, today was probably their first really busy evening. Went with our kids and right out of the window our cones were melting all over our legs, sprinkles cascading on our shoes. We dug in anyway, and the kids liked the ice cream, but it was too frustrating to eat as an adult. I expected to feel satisfied but it was a miss for me this time.
As an ice cream lover, I loved it. So many fun options to choose from at a reasonable price. The location is also kind of quirky. I will certainly return.

Page's Dairy Mart is a Pittsburgh classic. It sits in somewhat of an odd location slightly outside Southside, but it is worth the drive. Page's has a massive selection of ice cream, desserts, and even food such as burgers or fries (although I believe most people go for the ice cream only!) My usual go-to is any of the arctic swirls, which are similar to blizzards that you get at Dairy Queen, except they're better. If you're looking for something larger to split, I recommend their cookie sundae; it is delicious. The best part about Page's besides the quality? The price! Everything you can get there is very reasonablly priced, and the portions are generous. The sad part is that they are only open early spring to mid fall.. there are times where I crave it on a cold day.

PAGE'S HAS THE BEST SOFT SERVE IN THE STATE!!!! They offer a dairy free oat milk ice cream option, which is absolutely incredible. I got an arctic swirl made with the pistachio oat milk ice cream and cookie dough and it was phenomenal. The prices are great, especially compared to other ice cream joints around the city. The business gives off the perfect nostalgic feeling as you are surrounded with historical information of the business site and the history of the surrounding neighborhoods. Page's is the best local business and I would recommend it to anyone who is passing through Pittsburgh, or anyone who lives here and has not yet had the pleasure of trying their ice cream.

Just started coming here about 6 months ago, and wow I cannot believe I didn't come here sooner! I am in love with their ice cream here. Workers are always friendly. Tips are encouraged for the workers too, so keep that in mind when you get some ice cream. The prices are cheap too. My only complaint would be how long the line can get, but it seems to move relatively quickly and they never seem understaffed.

Came here at 9pm on a Sunday and the line was insane! But it moves fairly quickly so don't let that scare you away. So many options to pick from, Sundaes are top notch but then again everything from here looks like it is! We ordered the cookie sundae and the strawberry shortcake sundae , they were massive and a great price! ***this is a cash only establishment with an atm off to the side!

Best ice cream in Pittsburgh IMO. So many unique options. Soft serve, frozen lemonade, milkshakes, sundaes, Arctic swirls, banana splits, smoothies..endless options. You can include cookies from the best ( Nancy b's ) or grilled stickies from eat n Park, two other Pittsburgh classics. The line will most likely be long, but it will move. You can make it a full course by getting one of their burgers and curly fries. Pure greasy delicious goodness

Let me start with the positives. This shop has a great vibe to it, and the family seems passionate about it. The young employees always bust their behinds, running in such a small space so fluently, tackling the long lines. They also have an endless menu board of various food and treats. The prices are reasonable. Now for the reason for two stars. The ice cream is absolutely terrible. I have had three very different items off the menu, over a three year period, desperately trying to figure out the hype and find something good. I'm sorry, but everything was downright awful. The third, and final attempt, I had such high hopes, but despite how great my sundae looked, half of it ended up in the trash. My bf also tossed his. Not only was it tasteless and disappointing (even the brownie and cookie were terrible), 3/3 times I've been there, it upset my stomach. Mind you, I eat ice cream almost every single day, and have been to over 30 shops, and never had a problem. In fact, my bf, myself, and even my dog all had audibly gurgling stomachs soon after consumption. I'm sorry, but the hype is just unreal to me. This ranks 33 of 33 places I've gotten ice cream. I believe the hype is pure nostalgia from people that grew up going there, addicted to the memories and passing tradition on, not because it's actually fantastic. There are reasons to love it, but if you're going to an ice cream shop for the ice cream, you may be greatly disappointed. (If you care about covid, I drove past twice a week, and there was never any social distancing last year/giant crowds all bundled together in line, and not many customers wore masks. It's as if a pandemic wasn't going on)

This is your classic ice cream shop and one of the best in the Burgh! Even though it is only soft serve (all homemade with plenty of flavors) don't let that stop you from visiting. The menu is extensive with every kind of sundae and Arctic swirl combo you could imagine. The cookie crumb arctic swirl with Nancy B's chocolate chip cookies is one of my favorites. Also their fall menu with pumpkin ice cream is amazing! I highly recommend the pumpkin roll arctic swirl topped with a homemade pumpkin roll. The parking here is a bit tricky (gravel lot under a bridge) and no seating (outdoor counter only) but absolutely worth the stop and wait (can be long lines on the weekends).

It doesn't get much more Pittsburgh classic than Page's! I fondly remember driving past Page's on the drive into Bloomfield to see my grandparents, into Oakland to return back to Pitt, into the South Side to go shopping with friends...the list goes on and on. Now that I am no longer a Pittsburgh resident, I think back to those memories and when I do drive past Page's during trips home, I know a stop is in order. During my most recent visit this past weekend, my also out-of-towner sister and current Pittsburgh resident parents all embarked on that Page's trip, because truly, who turns down ice cream?! It was an unseasonably warm March weekend, so many people had the same idea as us, but the long line went by really quickly, and luckily, all our ice cream choices were still well-stocked. My favorite thing at Page's is the number of soft serve options, so I had to go with that. I was so happy to see birthday cake soft serve on the menu, so I jumped on that in a cake cone. For just shy of $3, you get a perfectly sized portion that hits your sweet tooth but doesn't make you feel totally gross for indulging. The birthday cake also wasn't sickeningly sweet, as I've had in other desserts, and it was chockfull of sprinkles. This was definitely one of the best soft serves I've had in a long time! My sister and mom loved their toasted coconut soft serve, and my dad was a big fan of his black raspberry dish as well. Page's is always a crowd pleaser, and we love being able to try something new every time. While I do have a soft spot for the soft serve, the sundaes are second to none as well, and should definitely be considered during any visit! Thank you for allowing me to reminisce on my childhood memories and for being a constant during my visits back to ever-changing Pittsburgh - can't wait to visit again!

This place tho.... If I could give it more than 5 stars I would. This place is located underneath a over pass and what it feels like the older area of Pittsburgh. We were actually at Keystone Raceway park for a car show and after that we decided to visit Pittsburgh for the rest of the afternoon. For lunch we went to a Chinese buffet that was just ok. We were looking for a ice cream place and this place came up on my Yelp app and having high ratings. From our location we were at, to Page Dairy Mart, it was about a 20 min drive. I was ok with the drive because we wanted to see and taste the best of what they have to offer. After getting there, there is a few stalls in the front of the place and a small lot in the back. I opt to park in the front because i took the track car to the car show. When we first got there, there was maybe about 3-4 people in front of us, but when we got in line and a few minutes later, the line was wrapping around the building. We got there just in time! Now for my order, I got the brownie hot fudge sundae and Dan got the warm chocolate cookie sundae. I must say BOTH looked and tasted amazing but the Brownie one was a tad bit better. Both are advertised as made from scratch from a local popular bakery and yes it is. I can tell from a scratch brownie / cookie to a box cookie. The soft serve ice cream was also one of the best I have tasted. The price also was amazing for the amount and quality you get. Their menu was extensive but I just went with whats popular and it always seems to work. Also what made me happy was they had Shave Ice. Its a Hawaii thing. I was thinking of getting it but I think i'll just save something like that when I go back home to visit. Other then that, if your looking for Ice cream / soft serve and is in Pittsburg, take a visit to Page Dairy Mart.

We stopped here for our sweet treat after dinner before heading back to our hotel, and the place was BUMPIN'. There was already a line snaking around the building by the time we parked, and we waited about twice as long here as at Primanti Brothers. No worries though; it moved quickly enough and everyone was in a pleasant mood. Our kiddo got birthday cake in a cup with mini M&Ms; one of us got a pistachio cone with rainbow sprinkles and the other got their celebrated chocolate chip sundae. The ice cream here is delicious: super thick and creamy and the perfect soft serve consistency. The pistachio had a bit of a chemical aftertaste, but that's how it sometimes goes with that flavor at these sorts of joints. The sundae was a bit too overwhelming for us, but it was good. Prices are fair. Page's is a charming (and obviously) popular spot, and what we liked most about it was that it seemed to attract characters from all walks of life, which is kind of rare to witness these days. Everyone was just wanting a frozen treat on a hot Memorial Day and it was kind of nice to be reminded that Americans of different races and classes can all enjoy the same thing without any vitriol. We'd definitely recommend this joint and might even come back later this week.

I've seen this place on many Pittsburgh tv shows and I've always wanted to stop. There always seems to be a big line. We went on a Saturday night and found a decent line, but they keep the line moving quickly. The prices were very fair, less than DQ. The servings were huge! My wife ordered a hot fudge sundae with warm Nancy B cookies (Nancy B's are amazing!!). I ordered a medium blizzard style treat with Nancy B cookies mixed in and on top. Both came rather quickly and were enormous. So big that neither of us were able to finish them. They were so darn good. They have a ton of variety to choose from as well. Huge menu, decent prices, lots to choose from and all delicious.

This is one of many hidden gems here in the Burgh. Check it out, freaky good ice cream, better blizzards than Dairy Queen, shakes that would have Ronald McDonald spinning in his grave if he were dead. I love Page's dairy mart, and look forward to opening day every spring, then go at least every week on those warm summer nights and have a cone or my favorite, peanut butter chocolate ice cream with butterfingers and reeses peanut butter cups running through it. Then I go run for two hours to burn it off, but it's worth it. Why four stars? Bad intersection (Carson and Beck's Run) and parking can be a motherbucket. You're still sitting there reading this? GO TO PAGE'S NOW!

Best ice cream in Pittsburgh! I love every single thing I've ever gotten here. I especially recommend the Raspberry Almond Torte Sundae and the Yinzer sundae... YUM! Support your local family-owned businesses!
This is a great place to stop for desert after a great dinner night out with the family or friends I would also recommend this place for a sandwich it's awesome and family owned

This place is such a gem under an overpass. I drive past Page Dairy Mart every day after work and there is always a long line at 3:30 in the afternoon, even in a downpour of rain. I finally stopped one day and it was so good... it's now going to become a bad habit. I went simple - swirl soft serve ice cream on a cake coke. So yummy and nostalgic. They have tons of flavors and dips though, so I hope to try out more in the future. Maybe I'll even try one of the many sundaes they advertise! There is no inside- you order from a window. They don't accept cash but there is an ATM around the corner of the building. The menu is pretty extensive so make sure you're studying all the options while you're waiting in line! The parking situation is decent- there are a lot of spots that surround Page's.
The chocolate chip cookie sunday made with Nancy B's cookies will blow you away! Awesome selection. Quality ice cream. Average prices.

This ice cream shoppe is definitely the best around. Their service is quick and efficient, and the quality of their ice cream is higher than any I have visited. Their cone size while being the standard contains more ice cream then is common and the flavor and quality of the ice cream is better than most. Besides ice cream they also have malts, shakes, ice cream sandwiches and many more things to enjoy. I hope you check it out because they're really very good. Their location may not seem ideal, but the position of nearly under the bridge offers shade on hot days while also not being dropped rusty water on. Next time you're in Pittsburgh, be sure to get a treat there.

Have to say this ice cream joint is great! This has been my 2nd visit since yesterday, 2 days in a row! Was born here but raised in the DMV & sad there isn't a cool ice cream joint in the DMV! Their ice cream is soft, full of flavor, reasonably priced & great for all members of the family. I will definitely come back when I visit Pgh again!

Ok, ok, ok, ok, I know, I know, that was naughty. But it was oh sooooooooooooooooooo Good! We split a medium turtle sundae. It is just your average soft serve ice cream. What makes them truly fabulous is the whole package. The turtle had the most wonderful slightly warm toasted salted pecans and plenty of them. The sundae was perfectly put together such that I was able to have toppings in every bite. The medium size was plenty big enough for us to split and feel satisfied with our naughtiness. You can park under the overpass which is actually super cool looking and oddly urban romantic. Prices are exactly where you want them, family spending friendly. I love this place!

This is a cool little ice cream stand that has apparently been in this location for quite some time. Their advertising reach is not very far, but if you get close to them you will see and be inundated by the colorful myriad of amusing bandit signs that are posted. What caught my eye? The orange sign that looked like it belonged to a construction company that said, "Ice Cream in 500 ft." Points for originality and tenacity. For my first visit, I ordered the following: Apple Dumpling Sundae Vanilla Ice Cream with chocolate sauce The associates were nice and quick and I enjoyed my apply dumpling sundae. It wasn't too sweet and had really good apple and cinnamon flavor. I really liked the dichotomy and juxtaposition of the hot of the apples against the cold of the ice cream. A true testament to their popularity is the fact that they still have patrons awaiting their fare when it is 50 degrees outside. I want to try so much more of what they have to offer.

This place is great! I got a chocolate brownie sundae that was big enough for two. The serving size is generous for around $5.00 with tax, lots of everything except for the brownies themselves. A little more brownie in the bottom would have been nice, but it was still very good and I will be back!!

It's hotter than blazes outside so naturally I needed to try the ice cream place that everyone raves about. I was told by many people to try the chocolate chip cookie sundae so that's what I did. And wow! First off it's huge. Definitely was not expecting that. I knew right away that I would not be able to finish it all at once. Second, it was less than $7 which is awesome in my book especially because it's too big to eat in one sitting. Third, it tasted like heaven. I know how busy this place can get so I tried to go closer to opening time and there was still a line. Will definitely be back and can't wait to try more things!

This ice cream shop is outstanding. Truly. Old school Americana, the kind of place I love. From the appearance to the ice cream itself. Went at night, so as to take in the glow of the signage and neon. There was a big line - perhaps 40 minutes or so - but well worth it in the end. Highly recommended if you find yourself near Pittsburgh. I really don't think you could go wrong with anything you order here.

It's funny I was trying to go to a brusters for some afternoon ice cream but had the wrong address so ended up here! I got an arctic swirl with cookie dough, Reese's cup and Oreo (what I get everywhere I go lol). It was perfect! Ice cream was very tasty. The service was so friendly! I'll definitely come back here soon!

Page's...A Love Poem Oh Page's, How I love thee... With your swirled frozen peaks And sundaes covered in rainbow jimmies, Leaves me smiling, cheek to cheek. Page's has been a regular family outing as far back as I can remember and clearly the popularity doesn't stop with just my family. From opening day to closing you will find people willing to line up around the block to get their ice cream fix. No other ice cream location in Pittsburgh even comes close to rivaling this outstanding soft serve experience. Our usual order consists of the basics: swirled soft serve (cup or cone) dipped in crunches or jimmies. Not only do they have soft serve but also a wide variety of insane sundae creations and other novelties. And don't forget about the shaved ice - which comes in basically ever flavor you could imagine. Visiting Page's isn't just about ice cream, it's about making a pilgrimage to quite possibly the city's signature ice cream experience.

Great be cream parlor at the end of Carson.. line gets a lil long but it's worth the wait.. typical ice cream in many varieties that's pretty good.. many flavors and varieties including Nancy b cookies.. great location in south side

This is by far my favorite spot to visit when I come back home to Pittsburgh! This place has been a family favorite since I've been little and clearly my family is not the only one. From opening to closing day, there usually is a line, but the ice cream is amazing and worth it. I usually get a soft serve cone with the crunch topping. It's simple and phenomenal ! The food is also good too with the burger being my go to. Every time I go home, I make it a point to come back here !
I've been coming here for YEARS. Literally the best ice cream in the world. That's all.

The quintessential Pittsburgh ice cream destination! Don't let the long line and parking deter you. The menu is overflowing with options and everything is delicious! Prices are amazing and portions are generous. They only accept cash and have an ATM on-site you can use.

Bummer!! We love their ice cream, probably our favorite in the area, but we were horrified at the blatant disregard for healthy and safe standards during Covid-19. Less than half of the customers in line had masks on, and no one stayed 6' apart. People were sticking their unmasked faces into the opening to shout their orders, so I fear for the employees. We will stay away until things clear up or management insists on masks and social distancing.

Stopped by yesterday for the first time this season and Page's continues to serve the best ice cream in Pittsburgh. Everything on the menu is so good and you can't just get one item. I got a 32oz hot fudge shake along with a rocky road arctic swirl. Both were excellent and I would recommend them to anyone. If you go on the weekend and late in the day, be prepared to wait for a bit. It's worth it though!

I'll go ahead and declare that Page Dairy Mart has the best soft serve ice cream in Pittsburgh. I stop by regularly during the summer only to stymie myself with the eternal debate- cone, Arctic Swirl, or sundae? I grew up on Page's dipped soft serve cones. To me, no other ice cream shop's dipped chocolate cone tastes as good as Page's. It doesn't have that off-putting artificial flavor that is common with a chocolate dip. The cone sizes are ridiculous. For me, their small is the perfect size. If you want to go crazy, go medium or large, or if you're in the mood just a little treat, go for the extra small or kid size. Their Arctic Swirls are wonderful. My current favorite is the Burnt Almond Cake flavor which has actual chunks of locally-made burnt almond cake mixed in. Amazing cake and ice cream together, all in one convenient package. How can you go wrong? The best part about their Arctic Swirls is that they identify their mix-ins that are locally made- this way, you know that you are getting a wonderful, fresh mix-in as opposed to the odd, artificial mix-ins that you typically receive at something like a Dairy Queen. When I'm looking to replace a meal with ice cream (as I did tonight), I order one of Page's outrageously large specialty sundaes. The Nancy B's chocolate chip cookie sundae is the best in my eyes. Tons of ice cream, gigantic pieces of a delicious chocolate chip cookie, hot fudge, whip cream, and nuts; it's truly a masterpiece. My summer (and your summer) is not complete without having at least one. The Yinzer sundae (with a locally made Blondie) is the next best choice. I will say that while these sundaes are great, the brownie sundae is rather middling. I'd like to see the mass-produced brownies they use now swapped out for something from a local bakery to take it to the next level. More importantly, though, I would love to see these specialty sundaes offered in a small size as well as the regular size (so I can enjoy one after dinner instead of having one for dinner...). Parking can be difficult during busy times, and there's usually a line, but that's all a part of the experience and charm of a popular and well-known ice cream shop. The staff is made up of younger kids, and they are always friendly and willing to help. Honestly, I always make sure to have some cash on me just in case I'm in the mood to stop by Page's. It's worth the drive!

I am SO hooked on this ice cream! I had the blueberry soft serve a few years ago with a friend, and loved it! I hadn't been back until a few weeks ago when I was bike riding on the trail nearby. Over the train tracks I spotted the Page's ice cream cone sign. I couldn't figure out how to get off the trail and over to the ice cream shop until I saw a man cross the railroad tracks eating an ice cream cone. Apparently other people had the same idea as I did. I left my boyfriend with the bikes and ran across the tracks and over to Page's. I got him a blueberry soft serve and I tried the toasted coconut. OMG the toasted coconut is unreal. It tastes like a toasted coconut donut. I am obsessed. When I posted photos, I got so many responses asking if I got the dairy free. I didn't even realize they had that! When we went yesterday, I ordered the dairy free (oat based) made into toasted coconut and dipped in chocolate (shoutout to Angie C. for the suggestion). My boyfriend tried the raspberry cheesecake arctic swirl and my brother tried the warm Nancy B's chocolate chip cookie sundae. Everything was great (and huge portions). The warm cookie sundae was enough for 2-3 people to share. The dairy free ice cream I got was perfect. This is absolutely my new ice cream order. We waited in line for about 20 minutes, and when we left the line was much longer. Side note- they do accept credit cards now. This place is worth the wait!

This place came highly recommended to us as a local gem but we were warned that the place always has a wrap around line with no parking to be found! Well, we drove by and there was no line!!!!!!! We slammed on the brakes and took the chance that fate had allowed us and man it didn't disappoint! We spent a long time reading all the history on the back of the building while enjoying the incredibly delicious ice cream!!! The staff was incredible! Let us take our time figuring out what we wanted and they were very understanding when the 5 year old changed his mind right as we paid! Thank you! Most importantly is they use the 90s/2000s McDonalds water cup as the cups for their freezes and they bring back all the childhood nostalgia

I've been coming to Page's since I was a kid and at 25 I still get that "YAY ICE CREAM!" feeling when I go here. Their soft serve ice cream is great and their Hawaiian Ice/Slushes come in several different flavors. The dips on their ice cream cones are very good and very popular as well. However, my favorite thing to get their is their Artic Swirls which also come in distinct and fun flavors (I really enjoy the Banana Cream Pie). Did I mention the great prices and friendly staff? This place has been a staple of the South Hills and it never fails to attract a large crowd of people. You can't go wrong with Page's!

Hubby and I have taken to driving up Carson street to get to the Southside in order to avoid that HORRENDOUS traffic in Squirrel Hill. We drove by Page Dairy Mart a few times and each time he would casually mention that he would like to go there someday. Well, we did. I wish I could comment on one of the DELICIOUS looking Sundaes, but I'm watching what I eat soooo... frozen yogurt it was. What I can say is that the yogurt was smooth and creamy and I LOVE that they have a ton of flavors they can "mix into" the yogurt so you can get almost any flavor you want. Hubby had a cone of regular soft serve ice cream and said it was really yummy. He also had an order of cheese sticks and said they were just o.k., so we will probably stick to ice cream/frozen yogurt from this place. The kids working were fast and friendly so we left them a nice tip. As someone who worked her way through college working at a frozen yogurt shop I can say -- TIP YOUR SERVERS, even if just your change -- they will greatly appreciate it. :-)
The best ice cream in the burgh!!! My husband and daughter love the simple cones and I always get the brownie sundae.. the brownie is always soft and warm and perfect.

It's open for spring! Was pretty chilly out tonight but that didn't stop us from waiting in line for what we have been waiting for all winter!! Tonight I tried the cinnamon bun sundae topped with Carmel and nuts!! Yum, no matter what you get you'll love it !!!

Great little spot to get some interesting ice cream choices. I got a sundae with blonde brownie, caramel, Heath and vanilla. It was so good! My husband got the warm cinnamon roll sundae and it was great too! We want to try some other things next time. We are out of town and this place is not like any we have in Georgia.
Always a crowd and a crowd-pleaser. What more needs to be said besides, YUMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
This is definitely a Pittsburgh staple! The ice cream is delicious. They're always adding new items and flavors to their menu which is co

Was my second time here and wasn't dissapointed! The first time I came here I had a strawberry shortcake sundae and today I had an XS sundae with strawberries and bananas. I really liked both sundaes I tried. My boyfriend got an XS chocolate sundae with fudge, his sister got a fudge brownie sundae, and her friend got a blue raspberry dipped vanilla cone. Everyone liked what they got! The only thing is I ordered a hot dog also and the actual hot dog tasted yummy but the bun was kind of weird. Other than that, it's a must go to if you're in Pittsburgh!

If you're in pittsburgh, this is a must stop for ice cream. Personally, I get a Southside shake almost every time. It's a milkshake & a sundae. Pretty cool, right? I've had their version of a DQ Blizzard (what they call them, I can't remember right now, sorry) but it was delicious. I got it with chocolate ice cream and Reese's cups. The possibilities are endless, seriously. My bf has had their chocolate chip sundae & the brownie sundae. Their cookies and brownies are both amazing and soft and tasty. They have food also, which I haven't had the opportunity to try at this point but I have heard good things. The prices are more than reasonable. The parking is ample but it's sporadic, kinda just park where ya can, no designated spaces etc. the other down side is that there is ALWAYS a line. Unless it's raining etc. The line gets insanely long but it's almost always worth the wait !

We have lived around town since we were little. The staff at Page's are always amazing. We went last night and waited for a little while but did not feel long at all. One of the staff made the ice cream and was about to hand it to me. They noticed a bug landed on the treat on top and completely remade my order. I would completely recommend.

When you want soft-serve ice cream in Pittsburgh, this is where to go! In addition to the usual vanilla and chocolate you'd find at most places, Page's has a slew of other flavors like orange, mint chocolate chip, amaretto, pumpkin, and many more! You really can't go wrong with any soft serve flavor. It seems that these flavors rotate depending on the season as well; for instance, pumpkin only appears on the menu in the fall. I tend to stick to the simple small cone, but they have a huge variety of sundaes and other ways to enjoy the many soft serve flavors. Not to mention, they have a few savory food items too, which I have yet to try. The lines are long, but don't let that stop you because the wait is worth it. Oh, and it's cash only, but they have an atm to the side of the building!

Can you believe I used to live in the southside and never once went to Page's? I know, it's blasphemy. Luckily, I made up for lost time by visiting TWICE in two days when I was in the neighborhood recently. The shop itself gets zero points for ambiance. It's in an odd location at a busy intersection, with limited seating and parking. Well, I should strike that last part...there is parking, but it's a little bit of a chaotic free-for-all (especially behind the building) and can be hard to navigate when it's crowded (when I was there, I watched a BMW back into a telephone pole trying to leave....talk about an expensive ice cream cone!) As others have mentioned, the lines get crazy long (it was literally 40 degrees and windy the two times I went, but it was still insanely busy), but they move fast. Soft serve ice cream is their thing and they have about a gazillion flavors served up in a gazillion different ways....definitely scout out the menu beforehand to avoid indecision paralysis when it's your turn to order! I got the strawberry shortcake sundae on my first visit and then went with a parfait the next time. Note that although they have a zillion different options, your ability to customize is somewhat limited. I had wanted to get a parfait with peanut butter ice cream, but the only thing they let me choose in the parfait was the topping (they forced me to get vanilla, so that's kind of a buzzkill). The portions here are comically large....easily enough for two people and should probably be served with a complimentary side of insulin. But friends, I tell you, it is worth the calories and ensuing sugar coma! The strawberry sundae in particular is divine...soft pound cake nestled underneath 673 lbs of vanilla ice cream, smothered in sweet strawberries....mmmmmm! My hubby got the cookie sundae, and it was a beautiful amalgamation of warm cookies, hot fudge, and ice cream (I'm drooling just thinking about it!) The parfait I had during my second visit was also good, but it wasn't particularly better than parfaits I've had elsewhere. Stick with their specialty sundaes, kids...I think that's what truly sets Page's apart from other ice cream joints. Cash only. See ya next time I'm in the southside!

I think 3 years is long enough to write an update. This is our go to spot which is great because we live 5 min away. Even when we venture off to new dessert and ice cream places, we end up comparing quality, quantity and price to Pages. Cash only. Tons of dessert and very reasonable prices. Parking lot is small and oddly shaped, but somehow it always works out and you can find spot. There is usually a line at the window but it's Well worth it A few of my favs: cinnamon bun sundae, brownie sundae, banana split ect

The best in the Burg. Peanut butter is my favorite, but Amaretto is a close second. Amaretto taste like maraschino cherry meets almond torte! Peanut butter is made with the real stuff! So many options for you to ponder over while you wait in-line. You may change your mind a few times while you wait!

This place is a GEM! Only open during 'ice cream season' but why would you want ice cream in the winter anyway? Lines are always long but there's plenty of friendly staff inside to get your order and build your dessert masterpiece in a few minutes. Do yourself a flavor (see what I did there?) and skip the Dairy Queen or Baskin Robins and go to Pages... You'll be a fan for life...!
Best ice cream in Pittsburgh! Amazing owner and top notch employees! Definitely 5/5 stars!
Page dairy mart has the best ice cream! My family and I love getting ice cream from here.
Absolutely perfect dessert spot! Fun location! Amazing choices! Best soft serve I have ever had! I will be coming back every single time I come to Pittsburgh!

This is hands down one of the best icecream shops in Pittsburgh. I tried the Yinzer Sundae last summer and thought about it the entire year, waiting for the new season. There's almost always a line but Page's is always staffed very well that the line goes quick. Something about this place puts everyone in a good mood. Never a bad experience!

I've been going to Page's since I was very young. Every time I go I am always just as impressed. Any time friends visit from out of town I be sure to take them to this Pittsburgh staple!! I usually get the same thing every time I go but tonight I decided to try something new with the Hot Apple Dumpling Sundae, it was amazing! It put me right in the fall mood. They have their full fall menu items up now so definitely try it out before they close for the season.

Page's is a Pittsburgh staple. Best soft-serve ice cream out there. I especially love their blueberry soft-serve and pumpkin soft-serve in the fall. The cash-only aspect is a bit inconvenient, but it's worth a stop at the ATM

Craving some homemade ice cream? Maybe some shaved ice? Nachos or a hamburger? Page Dairy Mart has it all covered! Homemade blueberry ice cream is delicious! With pieces of blueberries in it. Not too sweet but completely enjoyable! Coconut shaved ice is just what you need on a hot sticky day! The place is a small restaurant for take out only. People wrap around the building on most days. If you taste this ice cream you will understand why. It has so much fun foods too! Hot dogs, nachos, hamburgers and steak sandwiches. All at a great reasonable price too! This is a great little gem and has been in business since 1951! You come here once, you will be back again, and again, and again...

This place is a little gem! Hidden just down E Carson, past all the shops and busy streets there is a tiny little unassuming building on a large corner lot. I've never been a fan of soft serve or gone out of my way for it, but this place will make you do just that. Not to mention the fresh squeezed lemonade made to order (yes, they squeeze the lemons right into your cup.) Burgers and fries are also made to order, so be prepared for a short wait while you prepare mentally for the heaven you're about to consume. I'm not a fan of their fries (they tasted like they were made in old grease) but wow that cheeseburger. I have a small appetite and can't usually finish most things - so when I ordered my burger and fries I let the bf know he was expected to finish it for me. Little did we know he wouldn't get any of that delicious burger, because the second I took the first bite the rest magically disappeared. Oh! They also have old fashioned dip cones which are one of my favs. Definitely recommended.

Page's is one of my favorite places to go for ice cream in Pittsburgh. It is a pretty cheap place to go for the amount of ice cream that they give. I'm a big fan of soft serve ice cream so if you are too then definitely check this place out. Their cookie sundae and yinzer sundae are to die for and can easily be shared among 2 or 3 people. The only thing that I wish they would would do is give out samples of the ice cream flavors and take credit/debit cards. They are known for their ice cream but they also have food (burgers, hot dogs, nachos etc) I personally never tried it. But I'm sure it's good as well!

Best place close to the city for a Dippy cone! I grew up in small town that hosted a Whippy Dip! Every time I see this type of privately run ice cream shop it reminds me of home and lazy summer days with my girlfriends. Riding bikes to the local pool, playing at the beach on lakeside, or causing a ruckus at the Whippy Dip! Oh, sooo serious summer romances... flirting with boys while throwing ice from our slushies was a regular occurrence. Finally, a warm spring day on the books and the only place I want to go is The Page. The location is so weird! Under this huge bridge away from any greenery or picnic tables next to a low end used car dealer. I suggest grabbing your food and heading elsewhere. There is always some sort of line and it gets worse on the weekend. These guys and gals are pros when it comes to ice cream and will recite all the flavors with speed that you might miss them. It's kind of like the Cheese steak place in Philly. Know your order when you get to the counter, pay, and move OVER! They have so many flavors of ice cream! The menu is extensive, you can get anything here, brgrs, fries, hot fudge brownie sundae, or a banana split! I will be back all summer!

So I have never been here... and I have lived in Pittsburgh a few times in my life. Now that I live a hop, skip and a jump away from this fabulous little place, we finally made it there and I have now been there twice. This is for one reason... it is scrumptious. They have so many soft serve flavors, arctic swirls, dippy cones, Southside shakes, milkshakes, you name it really. There is something here for everyone! The inside of the stand looks clean too which is a huge plus for me. The kids that work there are also very nice. A+!

This place isn't very good. I ordered a sundae and asked for a flavored ice cream but was told they could only do chocolate or vanilla because of "how they mix it". It's a sundae so no mixing is involved so I don't understand that. Then when I got it, it was missing half the toppings that were listed in the description. Definitely not as good as people claim. Won't be going back.
If you are in Pittsburgh you MUST go here! Lines are long but they move fast. Delicious ice cream.

Wow. Everything we have tried has been amazing. So many flavors. We were in line for only 10 minutes. There were about 20 to 25 people in front of us. Well worth the wait. The portions are huge too. Great value for the money.

Everyone waits for Page's to open in the Spring and is sad when it closes for the winter. It's a small establishment with no seating, but there is always a line at the order windows. Page's is a Pittsburgh landmark. My family has been going for 20 years but it's been around for many many years. Page's serves hamburgers, icecream cones, sundaes, shakes, pretty much anything you can do with ice cream . . . and it's all good. One of my favorite's is a sundae made with a Nancy B's cookie. (Please tell me that you know what a Nancy B cookie is!) but sometimes I order just a simple twist. People hang out in the parking lot and eat there ice cream. They bring their kids and dogs and everyone is chatty and happy. It's a fun place to be.
Never be turned off by the line! It is worth the wait, which is never that bad and goes by fairly quickly. My favorite thing to get there is an arctic blast with cookie dough!

Dude... the Cookie sundae Hidden between the Waterfront and Southside in a pretty random area, it's pretty easy to miss this place. Surrounded by hills and located under a bridge. The only other thing nearby is a car place. But this is Pittsburgh, it seems to me that some of the best things in the city are hidden. Ice cream is soft serve and is your pretty standard good ice cream: creamy, soft, cold, with authentic flavors. It's delicious. But honestly, good ice cream can be found in many places in Pittsburgh. So what makes this place stand out from all the other ice cream places in Pittsburgh is the fact that they have delicious sundaes. My favorite is the cookie sundae, which has fresh-out-of-the-oven-melt-in-your-mouth cookies on top of a mountain of ice cream and hot fudge. They use Nancy B's bakery cookies. Yum. The menu is HUGE. So no, I haven't tried everything. Also, I've found love in the cookie sundae, so I may just stick to that. Place is cash-only.

This is by far my favorite ice cream shop is Pittsburgh. There is such a variety to choose from and it is GOOD! A strawberry sundae with whipped cream (fresh, from a whipped cream machine!!!) and nuts is my personal favorite. The freckled lemonade is also a must-try! This place has become a summer tradition for my family and we have never been disappointed. They make smaller sized cones for my kids and will make any custom requests that we have. Parking can be a challenge, but we always find a way! There is only one bench seat along the side and there are milk crates in the back that can double as seats. I think the lack of seating is actually good because people don't linger as long and it keeps the traffic flowing. It is cash only, but an ATM is located at the side of the building.

What a nice find for ice cream! I visited with my wife and parents on Sunday and was happily surprised to see they had fall seasonal flavors. The pumpkin roll arctic twist was amazing and came with a slice of pumpkin roll on top. I can't wait to visit again soon!

If you're looking for soft serve - this is the place to go! I only have 3 things to review, but I feel confident in a 5 star rating for the ice cream and 0 stars for the food.. My go to is the standard twist in a cake cone with scooter crunch topping. The ice cream is smooth and rich and the scooter crunch topping takes it to the next level. Classic! My husband ordered the chocolate chip cookie sundae and it was delicious but a little over the top for me. It came with vanilla ice cream, a warm Nancy B chocolate chip cookie, and hot fudge. If you have a sweet tooth and a big appetite I say go for it. On my last trip I tried the blueberry cheesecake arctic swirl. If the cheesecake part doesn't spark your interest, just get the blueberry soft serve. Worth it. Skip the food - my friend ordered french fries and they were raw. Don't be deterred by the line, it moves quickly

I love Pages! Cute little ice cream shop on the corner that reminds me of a drive in theater concession stand. Perfect place to hit up on a hot day for some ice cream or a slush. They also have burgers, French fries and all that kind of good stuff! The staff at Pages is always friendly. They have a nice selection of soft serve ice cream, more then just your chocolate and vanilla. The cake batter is a MUST try. I am looking forward to my next visit!

Page Dairy Mart--truly a Pittsburgh summer staple for me. Don't let the location under a bridge scare you off, they have some delicious ice cream!! The prices are great too. Beware, it's cash only but they do have an ATM on site. You really can't go wrong with any Arctic Swirl. My personal favorite is the cookie dough Arctic Swirl. Most use vanilla soft serve, but you can upgrade to any flavor, which I highly recommend. Their birthday cake soft serve is amazing! It has sprinkles and cake pieces in it (though mostly sprinkles). If you have a bigger appetite, the cookie sundae is a crowd favorite. Just come here. It's ice cream. You won't regret it

Page Dairy Mart is about as Pittsburgh as you can get. Located off the established portion of East Carson, this shack is gritty and located underneath some train tracks. It's not a pretty location, but if you love the Pittsburgh's industrial charm, you'll be right at home here. With the typical American snack bar choices, the mart's signature for their sundaes. The Nancy B's Chocolate Chip Cookie sundae is godsent. Warm cookie from a great local bakery, hot fudge, nuts, whip cream, and the best homemade ice cream (arguably) in the area. It may have been my favorite sundae ever. The ice cream here also has a historical significance, as the Page family has been producing dairy products since the 1800s. The mart never left it's original location. On the backside of the premise, you can read up on the history of Pittsburgh dairy and ice cream. This place really is perfect, I love everything about it. It's so genuinely American, and native to Pittsburgh. The ice cream is made from generations and generations of love and passion for the dessert. I can't wait to come back to this place. 5 stars well earned.

Holy moly Page's is awesome. Like the absolute best soft serve ever. EVER. They have a ridiculous amount of flavors and toppings and different sundaes. They might have the biggest selection of soft serve options I've seen. I've been to the trendy soft serve places in a few major cities and they don't have NOTHIN' on Pages. I've been consistently getting the butterscotch sundae ever since I tried it on my third visit, but have tried a few other options as well. I also now get the crunchies as a topping. At first the crunchies seemed to be all of the leftover toppings swept into a cup and poured onto my ice cream, but now I understand that that mixture is a perfect mix of crunch, salt, and sweet for any type of ice cream concoction you could order. The location is weird and under a bridge on the outskirts of south side, but DO NOT LET THAT DISCOURAGE YOU. There always seems to be some parking and although there's only one bench to sit on, standing around eating soft serve makes me strangely happy.

Came here the other night around 9pm, It was a rainy day so there wasn't a huge line but normally late night the line is so long! I ordered the yinzer sundae! Let me tell you It was SOOOO good. I've never had soft serve this good! Wow! I can't wait to come back all summer and try more things!

I filmed my music video to a song called ICE CREAM ROAD here. This place will always be a place that's important to me in Pittsburgh. Beyond that, it's just a awesome family owned Ice Cream Parlor. If there's a type of ice cream or sundae or frozen dairy concoction you love they got it. From blend ins to banana splits and hot fudge sundaes and flavored soft serve. Speaking of, you can combine flavors which I just learned of and blended peanut butter and banana, it tasted exactly how I had hoped. This place gets ridiculously busy on a hot day so be ready to stand in line for a half hour if its one of those days. While you stand in line copy and paste the info below into YouTube HITTofMCM - ICE CREAN ROAD You can listen to introspective raps in front of the same place and road the video was made while they blend your soft serve.

Great ice cream. I used to come here all the time when I lived closer. The ice cream is great and the food is pretty good as well. Just your typical burgers, chicken fingers and other fast food but still decent tasting.

The best ice cream in Pittsburgh! I've had so many different sundaes over the years. I recommend asking for vanilla with hot fudge and marshmallow sauce with graham crackers for a S'mores sundae. It is not posted in their window anymore but they will do it! With the traffic from Liberty Tunnel closures rerouting past here, you should TOTALLY make a stop. It'll be the best part of your commute.

Awwww yeeeeeeah. Just went to this place for the first time and it was awesome. I had driven past it many times and my curiosity was piqued by the many signs all over the building with delicious-looking ice cream on them. So naturally I was super pumped to go to celebrate a friend's birthday. We pulled up and found parking right by the building, and then only had to wait in line a few minutes before placing our order. They have about 15 different flavors of soft serve, a whole bunch of different dips, different cones to choose from (pretzel, waffle, cake). They also have a whole bunch of delicious looking sundaes and Arctic blasts, and tons of other options. I went with a cone of the birthday cake soft serve dipped in chocolate. It was fantastic - the soft serve has a great smooth texture and the dip was on point. They also put a plastic sleeve on the cone to catch drips, which totally saved my clothes. My husband got the Yinzer Sundae, which had a blondie, vanilla ice cream, milk chocolate, white chocolate, caramel sauce and whipped cream. YUM. The employees were polite and very efficient keeping the line moving. The place has a fun laid back, retro atmosphere. Can't wait to come back!

It's ok if you like soft serve and enormous amounts of it. I am not a huge soft serve fan and I find the flavour of Paige's very bland. So I t tastes like cold sweet and that's about it. The atmosphere is great and it's worth a trip come here once just for that. I don't think it is worth a second trip though.
A south side summer staple. Say that 4 times as fast. One can expect to find a family atmosphere here and who doesn't like soft serve.

Best ice cream place in the 412 without a doubt!! Being from Homestead I grew up on Nancy B chocolate chip cookies. And Paige's Nancy B cookie sundae is like heaven on earth It's worth the long line wait they usually have every night

Came here while in the city; it had the best reviews for ice cream and honestly the pictures looked so cool. We navigated here on a Saturday night and there was a huge line. It moved relatively quickly though, took about 25 mins to order. Was this the best ice cream I've ever had? Nope. Was nothing special honestly. The place is cool and very photogenic. They serve up good portion sizes (I don't know if it's cause it's American or if they're actually big portions) but I wasn't a huge fan honestly. I ordered a small sundae that came with almost no fudge and maybe 3 peanuts worth of peanut topping lol. My SO did order a medium twist cone though and it was disgustingly massive. Overall, my opinion of this place is to come here once, take some pictures and be done with it.. there's much better ice cream elsewhere.
Lines may be long, even during social distancing but it's nice to have a place where we can respectfully gather and cool off with something delicious!

I've been coming to page's since I was about 5, literally. I love it. It's a local favorite for sure and for many reasons. 1) the history behind page's... Literally if you walk behind page's there are old photos of what the building used to look like and some south side history :P. 2) their ice cream is incredibleeee. They have a ton of unique flavors and combinations. My favorite item on the menu is their strawberry sundae with twist ice cream, with an Esther's chocolate covered pretzel on the side. Pure heaven. 3) their food is amazing as well. I love their south side hot dog! It's unique and amazing.. Toast bun, grilled dog and chilli sauce.. So good. Their fries are awesome as well. I also adore their lemonade, both regular and freckled. Keep in mind they are cash only though!

Absolutely amazing ice cream place with super reasonable prices! The chocolate chip cookie sundaes are game changing. They actually heat the cookies up in an oven before putting them on your ice cream. Portion sizes are huge. This place is totally worth visiting!
The blueberry soft serve was so good! I'm a little grateful this isn't super close to me because I would have no restraint!! Glad we checked this out- we will be back FOR SURE!

You want the best? Here it is! I lived across town for a while and still detoured to pages to satisfy the ol sweet tooth. The brownie Sunday and malt milkshakes are my go to treats You go there on a hot summer night and the line can be across the lot into the lot for the car dealership. Amazingly the people there keep things rocking and rolling. Around back is little history of the Baldwin necks run area.

Ice cream heaven. So many flavors of soft serve and all of them are so good, you will swear that there's some sort of illegal substance hidden in there. The sundaes are gigantic and will send you into a sugar coma but you will be too blissed out to care. Even though I live on the other side of town now, we still drive here once every few weeks. Heck, I'd probably still drive here even if I moved out of the city. But I won't move away, and at least 10% of the reason is so I can easily go to Page Dairy Mart. Seriously, just go. Waiting in that long line is worth it.

I've been coming to Page's my entire adult life. It's always been a special occasion treat that never disappoints. While they have your staples like chocolate and vanilla soft serve, Arctic swirls (their version of a blizzard), sprinkles, sundaes and such don't be afraid to try something a little out of the ordinary like the Southside Shake. Live a little! While it is cash only there is an ATM on the side of the building. The ice cream is dirt cheap and always excellent. You may have driven by, seen the line and decided not to stop. Rest assured that the line moves very quickly. These kids are hauling a** to get you in and out, so toss them a buck or two. I worked in an ice cream shop when I was a young woman, and it's harder work than you think. Be sure to stop by later in the season for the pumpkin pie arctic swirl. It's one of my favorite things about early fall.

I had heard about this soft serve ice cream place as a Southside staple awhile ago, so when I found myself driving by I decided to check it out. Parking is limited and we waited about 10 minutes in line. I could have used another 10 minutes to decide what I wanted to order! There are sooooo many options. I ordered an Arctic Swirl with vanilla ice cream and locally made chocolate chip cookies from Nancy B mixed it. My friend got a soft serve mint chocolate chip cone. The prices were average. It's really the selection of choices that left the greatest impression. There is something for everyone with classic choices to one of a kind choices (Belgium waffles pieces anyone?) I can see why this place is still going strong a half of century later. p.s. I didn't take a photo because the photo just didn't do the dessert justice.

This was the first time my boyfriend and I tried this. We have lived in Pittsburgh our whole lives and have heard good reviews. The menu had plenty of options and looked awesome. I was torn between the chocolate chip sundae and the chocolate dip cone. I decided to get the dip cone but they said they had no chocolate left. This was at 7pm. I then asked for the sundae and they also had no chocolate chip cookies left. Whaaat!? Ugh. So I got a regular vanilla brownie sundae. The sundae was mostly vanilla and had one small brownie and very little chocolate syrup. I asked to add cherries which tasted different to me as well. I can sadly say I was disappointed in my Visit here and am truly not a picky eater. I wish they had possibly put a sign on the window that they were out of these ingredients before people ordered. My boyfriend did say he enjoyed his dirt sundae though. I don't think I will be returning unfortunately.
Came here during a lunch break from work with coworker also doing in office training and I enjoyed the ice cream so much. Good quality tasting product and staff quick n friendly will be back soon.

Such a huge selection-hard to make a decision because it is ALL good!!! Love that they partner with other local businesses to source items for their menus like Nancy B's and Pastries ala carte. Is highly recommend trying Page's!!!

This place speaks for itself, with lines extending to the main road. A few friends have mentioned this place to me recently and I can now appreciate why. They have soft serve ice cream in a variety of classic decadent flavors, but I'd really recommend taking it a step further and adding Nancy Bs warm chocolate chip cookies to the mix.... especially if you appreciate MEGA chunks of candy in your ice cream. You'll need a car to get here and there isn't really anywhere to sit to enjoy your treat, but it's certainly worth the drive over and there are plenty of new friends to mingle and chat with on line at this delightful joint in Southside.

Amazing. This place is cheap and the proportions are HUGE. It's definitely best to split a sundae because there so big. Unfortunately they don't have a seating area and the parking lot sucks but definitely worth it. The line was super long when i went on a Tuesday night but it went by pretty quickly. Wish I had know about this place sooner! It's great.

I love Page's! It's a Pittsburgh staple that gives the summer months a sweeter taste! I went to Page's last week and it was delicious as always! This time I thought to treat my puppy to a small cup of vanilla ice cream. I asked the lady at the counter for a small to-go cup of vanilla ice cream for my puppy! When I got home and went to give my dog the cup I saw a milkbone topper that she had placed in his ice cream! It was a perfect added touch that will keep us coming back! Thank you!

My favorite ice cream place in Pittsburgh... they have over a dozen varieties of soft serve... caramel, coconut, peach, pineapple, peanut butter... and I can never decide which to get. They're all yummy. I've never tried the food, but who cares, it's all about the soft serve!

Page's is the best ice cream place I have ever been to! Their ice cream is creamy and full of flavor and their artic swirls are filled with all the good stuff, no more digging at the bottom to find the goods! They use Nancy B's decadent cookies, which shows you they care about the quality of what goes in their ice cream! There is usually a line to wait in, no matter what the weather is, because everyone wants a piece of Page's! The only small, teeny tiny issue I have is the location, while there is much history behind it (Refer to windows for newspaper articles), it is dangerous to pull in and out of on the corner of Carson and Becks Run. I got in a horrible accident by someone who hit me coming out of Fagel Street, which is right behind the dairy mart, so just be careful pulling in and out of Page's. Other than that, this place is sure to melt your taste buds! And it is wallet friendly too! Just bring the cash, no cards accepted (atm on location) and make sure you get there before they close for winter!!

They have a huge selection of yummy treats! I had the strawberry shortcake and added bananas on it. They were more than willing to customize my order and it was amazing! I would recommend it highly to anyone!!

Page's is a must have summer spot! Once you go once, I guarantee you'll go back! There ice cream is so good and there's so many different options to pick from! You could pick something different each time you go there, and still never run out of options. Not only do they have ice cream they also have food items such as hot dogs, burgers, nachos, etc. They get super busy on evenings and the line can be pretty long, but it moves quickly and it's part of the fun. They don't accept any cards, only cash...there is an atm outside of the building. The prices are so reasonable also! I love page's!

Page's has been one of those places that has become a family tradition. My parents can't drive past without stopping and sometimes drive 40 minutes just to go. Since I was a kid I've always gotten the dirt sundae (oreo cookies and gummy worms) and always feel like a kid again when I get one.

LOVE page's, been coming here since i was a kid, same GREAT ice cream, shakes, etc, even BETTER burgers, dogs & fries, prices so low it's almost shocking, if you're in the south hills & want QUALITY soft serve this is the place, & believe me, it's worth the wait when the line is long, always has been

Great menu of choices and friendly staff. Funky location with poor parking and long lines. Prices were reasonable and it is cash only so be prepared for that. We received our ice cream first before we paid.

100% Pittsburgh treasure! The Carmel sauce is the secret winner but also the burgers and rib eye sandwich! .......The soft serve is a totally different object! That's The Godfather! It tastes like 1955 all over!!

Love Pages! The ice cream is well worth the line! I love that they incorporate other local treats into their menu and think it is great to see everyone supporting each other. It is always so sad to see them close and I look forward to them opening! I love the Nancy B cookie sundae!

This is my favorite local ice cream shop in Pittsburgh. They value the customer, it tastes delicious, and they can even make it your way. They are quick, even when the line is wrapping around the store. The artic swirls are amazing, and they get creative and make new sundaes/shakes every year. Love this place and I'll always support them!

I don't love ice cream, I'm more of a salty snack girl, but this place is a dream come true. They just came out with their yearly blueberry soft serve magic. The signs on E Carson leading up to Page's tease me to stop in daily on my work commute but I couldn't pass up the blueberry and it did not disappoint! There is something about the friendly neighborhood ice cream joint that opens and closes with the seasons. Page's is a must try at least once a year, even if you don't love ice cream!

This is the best ice cream place in Pittsburgh!!! They have many flavors, many mix ins, sprinkles, dips, multiple sundae options and snow cones. The variety is endless! The line is usually long, but goes quickly and is well worth the wait... Every time. This place is consistently great!
Great ice-cream at a reasonable price. I love their chocolate banana milkshake.
Quite possibly the best ice cream places outside of Sarris in Pittsburgh. That is all.

I grew up in Baldwin, so as a kid, the family and I would always frequent this place often. The Best ice cream around!!! I have to agree the arctic swirl is the best around!!! I suggest you try the chocolate covered pretzel!!! YUMM-O!!!! Good prices and fantastic people working there!!!
Whoever doesn't give Page a 5 has no soul. It's childhood everyday March-October. I love the pretzel cones, but everything is good.

Have driven by this establishment many times when I lived in Pittsburgh and in my visits, but I never pulled over to sample the goods. That is until today and it was really good! Don't be swayed by the lines. The staff is really efficient and move quickly. Prices are reasonable and portions are huge. Although I was really impressed by the different flavors of soft serve and that they are all homemade, I saw the sign for the apple dumpling sundae so I opted for that instead. My aunt went with a classic chocolate shake. The sundae is massive and the ice cream was so good, some of the best vanilla that I've had. Only critique is that the core part of the dessert were canned and were too sweet and sugary(- a star) Even though I don't opt for anything vanilla in life, I think I might squeeze in one more scoop on this trip!

Located beyond the crowded streets of South Side, Page Dairy Mart has been serving soft serve ice cream for over sixty years. The shop is open seasonally and the spring opening is a cause to celebrate, signaling the end of winter and beginning of warmer temperatures. The menu and ice cream possibilities are seemingly endless, from basic ice cream cones to the behemoth South Side Shake: a combination milkshake with a separate sundae on top. Although I've yet to make a dent in the full menu, I recommend going for a classic on your first trip: a vanilla cone covered with jimmies. While the ice cream is tasty (more so than similar chain ice cream shops throughout the city), the main appeal is the offbeat location and the celebratory camaraderie of the crowded parking lot during those long summer nights. Note: The shop is cash only, although there is an ATM located on the side of the building.

The best soft serve I have ever had. Some flavors are better than others. Of the mint chocolate chip, toasted coconut, and pistachio that I tried last night (what can I say, I was hungry) the toasted coconut was the best. It has real pieces of toasted coconut. A very good value for your money. Don't expect to find any seating here.
Love pages!!!! The grasshopper is awesome, a great spot in the summer to take the baseball/softball teams. The staff is so friendly and pretty quick service considering it was PACKED.
Best soft serve in Pittsburgh. Especially when blueberries are in season!

Page Dairy Mart (or simply PDM, as my friends and I call it) is nothing short of wonderful. Cheap prices for giant, delicious ice cream treats. What more could you ask for? It's a tiny little place (window service only) on a random corner underneath an overpass. But don't let the appearance and location fool you; you will not leave disappointed. A personal favorite of mine is the chocolate chip cookie sundae. It's made with one of Nancy B's chocolate cookies (hands down one of the best cookies in existence--in college I worked for a coffee shop that sold these, and we would literally rejoice when one broke in half because that meant we couldn't sell it and would get to eat it). Anyway, the cookie is warmed up and served atop vanilla soft-serve ice cream with hot fudge and whipped cream. I think most people usually assume that all soft serve ice cream is basically the same, but Page will prove you wrong. It reaches a whole new level of creamy deliciousness. It's cash-only and there is usually a line, but it moves quickly and the service is friendly. You won't be disappointed by this iconic summer favorite.

I LOVE Page Dairy Mart (PDM for short). Every spring for the 6 years that I lived in Pittsburgh we would count down the days until PDM opened. PDM has seen me at my best and my worst. I've paid Mr. Page in coin change I found on the floor of my car for a brownie sundae. I've gone twice in one day. I've waited in lines way longer than I care to admit just for a sweet, sweet brownie sundae. These people are NICE, good people. One fateful day my roommate and I decided to swing down to PDM for a sweet treat. Little did I know I would face one of my life's greatest humiliations to date. After enjoying our ice cream, we went to get in the car to drive home and it would NOT start. It just wasn't happening. We called AAA, we laughed a little bit, but as our wait grew longer and longer my dairy induced emergency grew more and more dire. I struggled, could I really ask them to use their restroom? How totally embarrassing. Y'all, I've seen the inside of PDM and it's just as incredible as you'd ever imagine. Thank you, kind high school boy, for letting me into your ice cream shop and into your heart. They may have made fun of me later, but in the moment they were super gracious and wonderful. PDM will always hold a special place in my heart. Go! And if your car won't start, don't fear. They'll take care of you.

Considering my absolute love for sweets - and more specifically, ice cream - it just doesn't make sense that it took me nearly 6 years of living in Pittsburgh to go to Page Dairy Mart. The only bad thing is that it's too close to where we live, so I can expect my sugar intake to go through the roof now. As you walk up, it's easy to be overwhelmed by the signage and menu, as they seem to have everything that you could ever imagine. In fact, you might just be better off walking up and ordering whatever you want without looking at the menu. Odds are, they'll just smile and run off to make it. I mean, if they have toasted coconut soft serve ice cream, what don't they have, right? The people that work there are all really pleasant and the ice cream is excellent! It is cash only, so that might be a downside if you're just randomly stopping by for the first time, but it's one place where the long lines are truly warranted in this town. Don't worry, though, usually the line isn't actually long at all. They take your order quickly at Page and your order will actually be up impressively fast for the amount of people ordering thanks to Page Dairy Mart's army of ice cream servers on staff. That "line" of people will disappear as quickly as a new one appears. A night hasn't gone by since our first visit that my wife and I haven't wanted to go back. Only our conscious willpower has kept us away, and there aren't a lot of places that have left me feeling that way, so kudos to Page Dairy Mart and their staff! Heck, it's snowing today, and I'm probably going to go!
Despite the location under the railroad tracks, this ice cream rocks. I love the endless options. The wait isn't too long even if the line is long. Yummmmmmmm.
