The milkshake was delicious and the customer service was awesome! Very friendly group in there and explained all the items for us newbies.
The employees were the sweetest people! And the shakes were bomb asf 10/10 recommend.

Wow! Wowzers! Great Scott! Great Googoo Moogoo! Holy moly! Holy S@!#, Are you kidding me right now!? Hopscotch is absolutely incredible. The service, the baked goods (especially the cinnamon roll bread pudding), and the food (especially the Caprese Sandwich) are just unbelievable. Honestly, the only thing I can think of that would be better than the combination of those two things I mentioned would be like...free ice cream and never having to clean your apartment again. Do yourself a favor once in your pathetic life and go to Hopscotch Bakery. I don't have photos because when I was eating these things nothing else existed in the world at that moment.
Beautiful & cozy Cafe The pastries are yummy All the staff are so sweet, definitely would visit again

Hopscotch bakery is such a delightful place to go when you need some pick-me-up goodies. I have tried their cupcakes, flourless chocolate cake (not pictured), and lemon bars! By far, I think their sliced chocolate cake is the BEST chocolate cake I have ever had in my life; I don't understand how the cake can be so soft and light when it is flourless. Their coffee is also fantastic. I would love to know what kind of coffee grounds they use, so I can make some at home! Their whole cake is also delicious and gorgeous. I attached a picture of a cake order that I placed a couple of months ago for my boss. I think I paid extra for the fancy cake decor, but it is definitely worth the money if you are getting a cake for a special occasion (or if you are extra like me haha). The bakery also has coffee beans/tea leaves, stationery goods, fresh flowers (sometimes), and other home goods such as candles for sale. The vibe is so cozy and bright that it brightens up my day every time I visit. However, parking is very small and limited.

This place is ok but don't go early - staff is slow and most items don't get put out until after 9 or later. Definitely overpriced and everything looks better than it tastes. Lots of better options nearby.

Very tucked away, but special place. I came here with a friend to have macaroons, tea, breakfast sandwich, and tomato soup. I felt like every other sentence I said while eating my breakfast sandwich is "this is so good". Very flavorful. Very cute place with some cute gifts throughout the store. A bit on the pricey side for a cafe, but I knew that going into it. Nice vibe on the inside, too. Overall lovely experience!

A great little place to escape the chilly Illinois weather! I stopped in here for coffee with a friend one day, had never tried this spot but have heard good things (and really wanna check out The Literary as well!) I was just looking for a cup of warmth and maybe a couple of sweet treats. We went in and it was so cute and intimate, a little bar near the window, some tables in the corner to work at, and a nice comfy couch with a gorgeous coffee table in the middle of the space. The walls were lined with various jams, cocktail mixes, teas, and coffees you could buy to try. A great little area to peruse while waiting for your coffee and food. I ended up ordering the Salted Orange Mocha and my friend got a Plain Black Coffee, I paired my yummy mocha with a decadent ooey-gooey salted caramel brownie and a flakey buttery classic croissant. The brownie was so rich and the salted caramel balanced it out nicely so the chocolate wasn't too overpowering. The croissant was very buttery and had a nice crisp flakey outside. The inside was fluffy and had those beautiful croissant layers you look for. My mocha really shocked me, surprisingly I don't typically like chocolate and orange together but I do love trying new things. The orange in this is super soft and doesn't have quite the punch I thought it would, it dances over your tongue and gets enveloped by the mocha. It's a very subtle concoction and I would definitely order it again! Overall this was a great coffee spot and it wasn't too crowded when we went in the afternoon. I think it may be a little overlooked with all the coffee shops on campus and downtown Champaign, I definitely think Hopscotch needs more recognition especially with all their cool coffee creations. I can't wait to go back and see what else they have to offer! * * * Check out my Instagram thatfoodiewithglasses

Really great little place for some baked goods. We had the macarons, a scone, cupcake, and lemon bar. I also had one of the lattes, which was really good. There is enough seating inside or outside as long as it's not too busy.

I don't know why I keep coming here. It's expensive and not the best coffee or bakery. The chocolate chip cookie was severely lacking in chocolate chips. The coffee is bland. The only thing really going for it is it's in the neighborhood and has some vegan selections.

I want to start by saying Hopscotch has delicious food and drinks and is always keeping the menu fresh which is great for a repeat customer such as myself. However I recently had a really poor experience here, of course on the day I finally bring my fiancÃ© to visit for his birthday. We arrived about an hour before closing and ordered sandwiches, bread pudding, and drinks. They didn't have their signature drinks updated which was definitely a bummer, but we chose off the regular menu instead. My drink was good but my fiancÃ© ended up with the wrong drink. The bread pudding was served to us ice cold. I don't know if that's a normal thing, but I've had a lot of bread pudding at different places, and it's ALWAYS served warm and soft, so that was very off putting. I asked if they could please heat them up, which they did, but when we got them back they were still ice cold in the middle so we ended up bringing them home to reheat ourselves. We were waiting for our sandwiches for a while and were then told they were out of one that we ordered. No big deal, so we got a panini instead (which was very delicious). After waiting a bit longer, we finally got our sandwiches and my egg sandwich was cold in the middle. At this point, I just gave up and tried to eat around the cold parts. Soon after we began eating, an employee let us know that they were closing and began cleaning up our plates. I was clearly still eating so it was very uncomfortable to be rushed out after waiting and trying to salvage cold food. We paid more than $50 for a meal that was of extremely subpar quality. It also felt like we were a bother to some of the staff members when we asked for a box so we could finish our meal after being swept out. I've only ever ordered out from Hopscotch and probably will in the future if I happen to return. Really disappointed because this bakery is one of my favorites in the area, and this was truly one of the worst dining experiences I've had.

If you're looking for the best croissants in town, look no further! They have a great selection of bakery items and savory treats. The quiches are also very creamy and delicious. Finally, the homemade caramel and chocolate sauces make the lattes unforgettable.

Women owned, women run, badass babe bakery. Everything is amazing and I'm very impressed with how well they've handled the shelter in place order during this pandemic. They have a very easy to use website (hopscotchcurbside.com) with everything they're making. They've also started adding grocery items for people to pick up so you don't even have to go to a busy grocery store and risk getting sick. I have a ton of respect for Kaya and her team and I haven't had a pastry or beverage from Hopscotch I didn't love. I'm particularly obsessed with the sunshine cookies. They're the perfect citrus cookie (also vegan and gluten free).
Bright environment. Friendly workers. Amazing sweets and pastries. What more could you ask for??

I tried to love it. I really did. So much so I tried it 4 times. Their cupcakes and cake slices are so dry. Each and every time. The frosting is so heavy! But this could be a personal preference. The frosting is very thick and taste like pure butter. Savory items are okay. Both items were bland and plain. Again, I tried to love it but I just can't. You can't go wrong with their croissants. Haven't tried their coffee. Three stars for friendly staff, great location, and super cute store. We need more of these please!
Hopscotch is the champagne of bakeries and cafes. You will not lack for delicious croissants in Champaign.

I saw hopscotch at farmer's market last year and bought lavender honeycomb and baby cake from their stall. I liked the honeycomb but did not like baby cake. Now, after a year, I thought of trying it again as I found it located inside art mart. I bought walnut caramel bar, brownie, champagne baby cake and gooey butter cake. I wanted to try a few before writing a review. My review of each item is as follow: Walnut caramel bar(2/5): it was not overly sweet, which I liked. Had good amount of walnut. But, the overall taste was not that good. Brownie(3/5): again not too sweet, was more on bitter side. Liked the caramel on top. Overall, good. Champagne baby cake(2/5): too sweet, was not moist, felt heavy. Gooey butter cake(1/5): extremely sweet. And that's the only thing I could taste. I couldn't eat it more than one bite.

We stayed at the air bnb above this bakery and just had to try it. It's in a charming neighborhood in Champaign just a block off of Prospect Ave and across the street from Southside Elementary School. There's a small parking lot and plenty of street parking available. Inside you will find an adorable bakery and cafe. We went in around 9am on a Friday and the place was ours. There's seating available if you would like to enjoy your treats in house. We ordered carry out to share with some friends and family. 2 cinnamon rolls, 2 tomato and herb quiche, 2 bagels and cream cheese. I split a quiche and one of the jug ge cinnamon rolls with my husband. They were both well made and the cinnamon roll was delicious! I wish they had a few more savory breakfast items but their traffic might be lighter on weekdays..? They had some baked desserts that looked amazing and some unique drinks you won't find just anywhere like a brown sugar and fig latte. I also noticed hand made marshmallows! They sell specialty food items and gifts as well. This place is really cute and seems to have a little bit of everything. No matter who you are and what you're looking for Hopscotch has something for everyone. Stop in and check it out for yourself!

Ordered an 6 inch lemons berry mix birthday cake. It was just ok, sort of dry and ingredients aren't as fresh. The candle was $1 and it was so tiny that I thought it was a joke. At a price close to $50 I expected more.

I've been a fan of Hopscotch since they opened, and continue to support them during lockdown and curbside-only pickup, but think customers should be aware that they're not quite ready to handle more than a very few customers at a time. I've had several experiences in the last few weeks where my orders were wrong or seriously delayed behind others who arrived and ordered after me, so be prepared. And the mask/distancing of patrons standing outside is very variable- you take your chances.
Very very nice coffee shop to hang out at and good coffee. Cons, highly over priced and limited parking.

The best treats in town! My favorite are the various caramels and single serve cakes. I have gifted the bourbon vanilla extract which Kaya makes/ages herself and the recipient could not have been happier! Some of her marshmallows have been used in drink specials at flying machine coffee and really made the (already awesome) drinks supreme. I can't say enough good things about Kaya and this lovely budding business!

Firstly, I have to say that Hopscotch does a great job in their cake decoration! Unfortunately, the cakes don't taste nearly as good as how they look. I bought Hopscotch's berry buttercream 6'' vanilla cake for a birthday party. The cake cost $40 and was quite small but well-decorated, so I expected it to taste great and impress the other guests. I even hyped it up at the party, so people were expecting some great cake... Sadly, the cake was very disappointing. The buttercream was bland and tasteless, and the cake was dry and stale (like old pound cake). I have to say that even the generic cake from Meijer tastes better. I was pretty embarrassed to say the least... If all you want is a cake that looks pretty in a picture, then by all means come to Hopscotch. But, whatever you do, don't count on their cakes tasting any good!

Thanks to their online ordering option I was able to order a few breakfast items this morning and then swing by to pick them up, which was very convenient. Ordered the pear bostock, a cinnamon roll, a ham and cheese croissant, and an egg in a croissant. Glad to see them still open and able to serve customers safely and conveniently during COVID.
Really enjoyed an iced rose cardamom latte w/ oat milk. There was more seating than I expected as it is attached/open to a bike shop, Seems to get super busy with students studying, Enjoyed our stop,

I really like their order ahead service. A lot of business have a cutoff the night before and this doesn't work well for me as I'm more of a spur of the moment eater. So the fact that I can order something for 10 minutes later is fantastic. The food has been great and I like their coffee as well!

We ordered a custom cake for a family celebration. It was beautiful and tasted great. The cake here is not overwhelmingly sweet like you get at a grocery store, but it has intense flavors, which we prefer. The 8 inch cake easily served 13 with some leftovers. My one recommendation is that the business set it up so that you receive an automated email confirmation when you submit an order online. The shop is really nice too if you want to sit and enjoy a coffee.

I just went to their new location at the intersection of John St. & Pine St. I think today was their official opening. I have been walking past it long enough and was interested to try it. Simply said, it blew me away! Service was amazing with a sea of smiling and helpful faces. The food and drinks were out of this world. And, the prices were reasonable. Easily my new favorite place in town.

The absolute worst customer service. I tried to make a phone order and apparently because she was "too busy," she felt my order must not have been important. The lady on the phone was snarky and rude. Told me to go to their website, and the website said to call for what's available." It's clear they don't want you to call them. Absolute worst service I've ever received. Plenty of other local bakeries that would take my business. I am just astonished by the lack of professionalism and the horrid customer service. WILL NEVER RECOMMEND OR RETURN.

It was my first time trying Hopscotch this past week. I got a ham and Swiss croissant and cinnamon roll with a matcha latte. The croissant was delicious and flaky and the cinnamon roll had to be one of the best I've had. There's a great selection of other bakery items too. Everything is reasonably priced and the atmosphere is really chill. The person taking my order was also super nice and welcoming. This will definitely turn into a regular stop for me.

We just moved into the neighborhood and have mixed feelings about living close to this gem... Obviously, we're stoked because their drinks and food are so delicious... but we've been treating ourselves a little too much with the help of their convenient online app - we're gonna be broke and chubby in no time. I guess it's fine as long as we're happy, right? My favorite drink is the London fog, and really, you can't go wrong with any of their pastries. Our favorite, though, are their macarons! Our realtor bought us a box of them after we closed on our house and thus were pleasantly introduced to Hopscotch. Now we're hooked!

Located in the middle of a quiet neighborhood. Not a lot of parking (3-4 spots?) but there is street parking available. I was surprised by the wide range of baked goods they offered. They also had cakes along the wall that were beautifully decorated. We ordered an iced coffee and the bread pudding. The bread pudding was very moist and coffee was good. Overall, very nice decor and atmosphere.
Hopscotch bakery is the most aesthetically pleasing bakery in C-U. Incredible pastries, quiche, cakes, etc! Amazing service and quality coffee. Love the gifts that support local businesses.

We've purchased caramel sauce, cupcakes, marshmallows in flavors like passion fruit, lavender honeycomb, and pistachio shortbread from her farmer's market booth over the last year--all were amazing. I ordered cupcakes for a going away party from the online site, which has one of the best ordering interfaces I've seen. They were delicious AND ready ahead of schedule. The citrus tarts from the case at Art Mart tasted like the ones we had in Paris, creamy not rubbery and the perfect combination of tart and sweet. Can't wait to try the cannelÃ©s!

Oh how I wanted to LOVE Hopscotch. The interior is darling and some of the artistry done with frosting is magnificent. For my birthday, I heavily hinted to my husband that I would really, really love to have one of their works of art as my cake, and he delivered. The cake he brought home was pretty, although not exactly what he has asked for (roses instead of peonies but really not a big deal), but the flavor was what we were excited about; vanilla blackberry. We eagerly cut into the cake (after letting it sit out for two hours as instructed) to find that on sight, it resembled very stale soda bread. It was incredibly dense and heavy - and really tough to cut (sawing was required). Still, we remained hopeful, but on first bite we struggled to chew the cake that was tough, dry, and not even a little sweet (and I prefer my desserts on the unsweetened side). There was no taste of vanilla or blackberry, and there was a definite smell and taste of frostbite or perhaps just something very artificial. Neither of us could finish our pieces, and the rest of the cake was tragically trashed. The worst part of this was not that my birthday cake was a total dud, but rather watching my husband's face fall as he realized what a disappointment this cake was. I am quite pregnant and not able to partake in some more typical celebratory indulgences, so he had hoped to get me an epic cake to make up for it. I hope others don't have this experience, but also hope that the bakers at Hopscotch can work to prevent any future disasters. All the pretty icing in the world won't help a cake that's too tough to chew.
Amazing cake. Great bakery! Thank you for making a magical birthday!! Terrific bakery. Wide selection of baked goods. Super helpful staff.

A colleague brought a beautiful cake from here to celebrate a milestone in my life. The cake was absolutely beautiful and equally as tasty. The sweetness was perfect, not too overwhelming. Also super moist. The buttercream was heavenly. I can't say enough nice things about this cake. I've also tried your cupcakes and they are also great. The tastiest cake in this town for sure, maybe even the tastiest I've had.

I want to love this place, but they've given me too many reasons not to. Their drinks are truly sub-par. No, I'd rather not spend $4.50 on a lukewarm hot cocoa that has only a faint hint of chocolate flavor, or $5.00 on a dry brownie. The customer service is lacking as well, usually they just stare at you and wait for you to talk, without asking how they can help you, so it's quite an awkward experience.

I highly enjoy the creativity that goes into the food and drink items, the decor of the shop, and the variety of things available to try on a regular basis. I also love supporting a local owner. Most of what my family has bought has ranged from very good to excellent. For example, the gluten-free options are outstanding, including the brown sugar oat cupcakes and the carrot cupcakes. The egg-free chocolate cookie is very rich with a distinct chocolate flavor and wonderful texture. I can also attest to the quiche and have tried at least two flavors. Her bread puddings are also terrific. There are some items that aren't a runaway success but am not opting to list those. Instead, here's a handful of reasons why it's not a 5-star review for me: 1) The espresso-based drinks are not always very hot. Temperature is crucial to a really good espresso drink, especially if you are going to spend $5 or more on it. 2) The attitudes of the employees are not always stellar. The last two times I have picked up items from Hopscotch to go, each young woman behind the counter who rang me up were coolly polite at best. There wasn't service with a smile or any kind of cheerfulness, even when I would try to engage about the items. I felt as if I was inconveniencing each of them being there. The first time it happened, I chalked it up to the person having a bad day. But the second time, with a different person, I had someone else with me who also thought it was a stiff transaction for being such a homey place. This might seem like a small thing but for me, this makes the difference of being a regular versus going only once every few months. 3) During peak times, it would be an improvement if there were more than one person behind the counter, e.g. one person making hot drinks and another person helping those in line who are picking out baked goods. Tip: don't go here in a hurry. All in all, a great place to go when you have time, and you want to try locally-made delicious treats or pick up a unique gift for a loved one. It's also conveniently located in the center of town.

I submitted a wedding inquiry with Hopscotch at the beginning of May and received a response relatively quickly from the owner, Kaya Tate. After looking over the website and weighing my options, I sent Kaya a response letting her know that I would like to secure an order and schedule a tasting. I paid my deposit on May 31st. One June 24th, I asked her in an email about the tasting, as I had not heard from her since I paid my deposit. She didn't answer me until July 15th and her response was that she would get with me to set up an appointment once her shop was finally open. Her shop opened in July and I eagerly waited for a call. On August 26th I had to email her again to see if we could finally set up a tasting appointment. She didn't answer until September 5th to ask what flavors I was interested in and said that there wouldn't be an appointment, but simply a tasting box that I would pick up from the store. It was implied that we would have a physical meeting and that I would have the opportunity to try the cupcakes and pick my favorites, but now I only had the choice to pick three cupcakes for a tasting box and hope that they were good. I planned on getting three flavors of cupcakes for my wedding reception and so only choosing three to try was very limiting. By September 20th, I still hadn't heard anything from Kaya, so I went to the shop to see if I could get any further with her in person. At this point, my wedding was about two months away and I couldn't afford to wait around several weeks between emails anymore. I asked the woman at the counter about the tasting box that Kaya had mentioned and she told me that they don't do tasting boxes and that I would have to purchase the cupcakes that I wanted to try. I put a deposit down and was purchasing 144 cupcakes for my event already, now my taste testing appointment turned taste test box with three options had been downgraded again to buying the cupcakes that I wanted to taste individually? I told her which flavors that I wanted to try and gave her my phone number so that she could call me when the flavors that I wanted to try were available in the case for sale in the shop. I left and called my fiancÃ© to discuss the situation, who then called Hopscotch to speak to Kaya herself. She was told that Kaya was busy and that "they only opened about 7 weeks ago." Shortly after their phone call, I received an email from Kaya stating that there would be a taste test box with my three flavors ready on September 27th. I arrived to pick up the box and when I opened it, there were only two cupcakes inside. I asked the woman behind the counter where the third cupcake was and her response was that they were out of strawberries and that there was nothing that they could do. I asked if I could go to the store and buy her some strawberries and explained that my wedding was less than a month and a half away and that we had started this process clear back in May. I then asked to speak to Kaya. I was told that she was busy in the back and that she couldn't come speak with me. I left the box of two cupcakes and said that I would email Kaya. I then emailed Kaya requesting my deposit back, as we had spent four months getting nowhere. Less than five minutes after I sent that email, she had already refunded my deposit, which was the fastest correspondence that I had gotten out of Kaya since we spoke in May. There was no further communication, she was just as done with me as I was with her. The deposit has now made it into my bank account, leaving me less than a month to find and coordinate with another bakery for my wedding. This place is adorable and their treats are tasty, but they are not capable of handling a wedding or any other large event. If they can't make three cupcakes in four whole months, they are certainly not capable of making 144 cupcakes for one day's event.

A gem in Champaign! This space is so lovely, and I was surprised to see that they sell cute stationary in addition to amazing baked goods. It's not a huge space, and I personally wouldn't come here to study and chill for a long time. However, I would stop by to have a latte and share a dessert with a friend. I just wish they stayed open later! Came for $1 macaron Wednesdays and was not disappointed. Also ordered the mini Oreo cheesecake, which was rich and delicious.
Delicious baked goods with a variety of options! Artistically designed and so delicious. Fresh peach lavender coffee cake went great with a drip cup of coffee for my afternoon pick me up.

I'm 7 months pregnant, so this place opening in my neighborhood is pretty much the worst best thing to ever happen to me. There is some sort of chocolate salted caramel bar that will restore your faith in humanity. Lattes are stellar, made with homemade syrups and high quality espresso. Large ice cubes are also a nice touch. Scones are also killer.

Vanilla bean cheesecake was decadent and yummy but did not have a hint of vanilla bean flavor. The crust was also rock hard and literally impossible to put my fork through. I really don't understand the point of having such a rock solid crust. Chocolate chip cookie sandwich was soft and tasty. Salted caramel coconut macaroon was delicious (I love caramel and coconut) but was sorely lacking in salt. Salted caramel brownie was very fudgey and decadent! The champagne cupcake was very pretty but bland, did not taste like anything special. Wish they had more cupcake choices. My friends really liked the peanut butter chocolate cake and the birthday macaron. I feel like I tried a good variety of things and wasn't exactly amazed, especially at these prices, but I didn't hate it either. It's essentially just a cute place to take good Instagram pictures and eat something sweet. Service was mediocre, cold and unfriendly. I don't expect people to be in my face with joy and excitement but such a harsh demeanor isn't really necessary. The women who work here definitely aren't giving customers the best experience.
Such a cute little spot, really amazing coffee and probably the best bakery in our area

Hopscotch continues to shine, especially in light of the ongoing pandemic. They've added numerous delicious new items, continue to excel at established favorites, and retain the same bright, welcoming, and safe service.

Decided to try them again! Well I didn't think it could get much worse but it definitely did. Decided to get some French macaroons, a cupcake, and a croissant. The macaroon was the worst texture. You can tell they have no clue what they are doing when it comes to them. The cupcake was dry and crumbly with little to no flavor. My croissant was BURNT! Terrible experience and customer service. Will not be back.
Environment is pretty neat. Online order process is easy and they make your cake very quickly. Cake looks beautiful however the taste doesn't live up to the aesthetics. Price is little high as well.

Hopscotch is THE BEST. The cakes are delicious, unique and utterly gorgeous. I have been known to eat the butterscotch and mint chocolate sauces directly from the jar. My boyfriend has developed a severe marshmallow addiction. Hopscotch is my go-to for special occasions and for everyday indulgences.

Kaya will be making my wedding desserts next March. As research (tough, right?), my fiancÃ© and I have tried many of her goodies at various markets. I love that she uses all natural ingredients. Taste is never sacrificed though as these are some of the yummiest desserts I've ever tasted. I love her caramels, cookie boxes, and peanut brittle. The salted caramel chocolate cake was great, too. Communication is easy with Kaya via whatever method you prefer. Her website is easy to navigate and she has a strong presence on social media. Check Hopscotch out. You won't regret it.

Where do I even start? I met Kaya and her husband at the Urbana Farmers Market and they were amazing and friendly. I probably had a million questions as I normally do and wanted to try everything. I started out by trying the cupcakes and I was blown away. Her stand immediately became a must stop every weekend. I believe there was one weekend they were off and my farmers market experience was just not the same. Now I'm not a professional Yelp reviewer, but I can say her baby cakes are amazing. If you tell Kaya some of your tastes, she tries her best to give you recommendations and/or make stuff for you. Also, you MUST try the marshmallows. They are to die for and you will never, or should never buy them from the store again. If I only had one suggestion it would be, in the holidays make smaller ones to put in hot cocoa. Actually, I take that back because I should just do a giant cup of hot cocoa so my marshmallow can fit. Keep doing what you are doing! I get that some people might not care about Kaya's views on life, but as a customer, I like to take my money to someone with a conscience. Which is why I take my business to Hopscotch. Thanks to Hopscotch and many of the amazing local shops, my husband and I fell in love with Urbana/Champaign and look forward to moving back there again some day!

I bought a cake pre artmart location and it was phenomenal, I told everyone and anyone about how amazing the cake was. I recently got one for my children's birthday and it didn't taste as fresh and had so much filling in between the layers it was not much of a cake. It also didn't look as appealing as other cakes I have seen of hers. I asked for something simple but it looked like a cake from Schnuck's. For the price I paid I was not impressed or a happy customer the second time. Its very sad the quality has declined with such amazing ingredients and talent.

Many Gluten free, vegan options for pastries. The succulent cupcake was very pretty but mild in flavor - which would be good with tea. They also have a very interesting Coffee menu with new combos of coffee I've never heard of.

I've never really had a good experience with Hopscotch in the past, so decided to give it another go after winning a gift card from a game night. However I do like the idea and the location and it's nice to have a bakery in town like this. First thing to know though is the staff is generally rude and if you have questions - lord help you because they'll either act like you're dumb or act like their life is ruined by you asking anything. Second thing to know : DO NOT ORDER COFFEE. Just don't - it tastes sour .. somehow. Just go somewhere else.. Third: do not get bakery items such as cakes or muffins- will 100% always be dry I recommend the lemon bar or bread pudding when it's available. The ambiance is really cute but I think that's what draws people. They also sell fun little things like notebooks, stickers and even kitchen supplies which are great for gifts. Their website is also user friendly right now due to Covid, but remember you cannot go in and browse. Overall it was exactly as expected. Mediocre quality and a cute aesthetic.

Cute place but expensive. The cookies we purchased were not worth the cost. Also, there were kids trying to do headstands on the couch who kicked a glass bottle of fancy candy onto the floor while we were looking at them. Luckily, it didn't break, but we picked it up (Mom was too busy shopping) and it was irritating and we left without buying anything else. Barista/Cashier didn't speak or acknowledge anything. Not a very welcoming atmosphere.

Tried croissants, scones, cinnamon rolls, pain au chocolat, "breakfast cakes" and all are amazing. I agree with the reviewer who said that they have the best croissants in town by far- crispy outside, tender and chewy inside. The order ahead service worked great.

I would highly recommend this bakery! We moved to Champaign about a year ago and recently discovered it. Their sweets and drinks are delicious. After trying their lemon berry cupcake we decided to order the 10'' cake version for our small, backyard wedding. We were a little worried about not seeing the cake/it not being an actual wedding cake but it was AMAZING. It was beautiful and delicious and so reasonably priced. We will continue to support them!

We love Hopscotch!! While we have tried many items, our favorites would have to be her chocolate cake (so moist and tasty!) and her marshmallows. Last summer we tried strawberry marshmallows which were divine! We would love to try the infamous salted caramel marshmallows, but haven't had the chance yet. Ordering is very easy online, and Kaya is quick to respond and answer your questions. She is kind and really makes an effort to connect with her customers. Not only are her treats delicious, but also gorgeous! After a recent cake purchase for Mother's Day, my mom referred to her as an "artist" and got inspired to create some of her own lampwork beads based off of the color combinations Kaya uses to decorate her cakes. Can't say enough great things about Hopscotch!!

I love the interior and the owner is super nice, and the cakes look gorgeous, but I had the cupcakes twice and they were pretty dry both times. I wish they had a better selection to choose from. We were there quite a bit when they first opened, but their prices and limited selection (maybe I am going the wrong days?), and prettier to the eye but meh to the taste cupcakes/other pastries prevents me from going regularly. I was really looking forward to coming here regularly, but i am not surprised by the mixed reviews on the cakes here. I dare not order a custom cake here because their cupcakes aren't that great. Some of their things are pretty good though. Overall I expect more, but the desserts don't always live up to the hype. Mixed bag. 2.5 stars ish

This neighborhood cafe has all the ambiance you want for a cup of coffee and a their yummy cinnamon rolls. It's one place I can go by myself and feel peaceful. Their bakery it's look wonderful although I have not sample much. Love supporting this place.

Tucked away in a neighborhood is this bakery and store (milk eggs and such. We shared a blackberry rosemary pastry it was moist fresh tasting. If we hadn't filled up with apple fritters at Curtis Orchard we would carry out. Best to just enjoy good drip coffee.

I ordered 3 different bakery items and a drink. Because everything was so over priced I thought they charged me for all of it. I asked if they had butter for them. They told me yes, but, didn't include any in my order. Upon leaving I realized that they only heard me order two things. My supposed to be hot drink was tiny for $5 and only luke warm. I gave them 4 stars because, despite all this, the bakery items that I did receive were very tasty.

Kaya makes the most beautiful and delectable desserts! She uses natural and seasonal ingredients, which guarantees a fresh, full-flavored taste in all of her treats. I *love* Hopscotch's mini-cakes, lemon bars, and chocolate anythings. Hopscotch Bakery + Market's response to the Covid-19 crisis has been unmatched. From the beginning, they met the needs of our C-U community and have had their staff + our health and wellbeing at the forefront of their minds. They also have an amazing donation program to give baked goods to essential workers! So awesome! I highly recommend Hopscotch to anyone looking for desserts for a wedding or other special event - or for a sweet treat for yourself and your loved ones! You will love to work with this team!

Drove to Champaign from Bloomington to try these beautiful treats. Did not disappoint :) Atmosphere 5: very cute shop inside and out Service 5: very nice helpful girl at the counter that gave us awesome suggestions Desserts 5: I got the vegan pumpkin cookie. It was very moist and the right amount of sweet, I would get again. My mom got the macaroon. She said it was the best she had ever had. Very buttery. My brother got the pistachio shortbread. He said it was flaky goodness! Overall worth the drive!!

They have the best croissants in the entire city, hands down. Art Mart is a distant second. Even Hopscotch's butter croissant is amazing; as good as one would find in France. I actually think this place has stepped up its game even more since Covid.

I came here every week overall I enjoyed the environment and service every time but I had a bad experience today. I feel like I'm not respected by the barista/cashier - Jesse (that's what she told me not sure if she made it up). I'd like some milk for my dripped coffee but she did not seem like to help me with it. She was reluctant to get me the milk but instead trying to have me used the cream on the table. That is not something I need and when I insist on getting the milk, she took the milk out from the fridge with a lot of aversion on her face. I feel like being discriminated as she treats other caucasian customers with a MUCH MORE friendly manner. I feel like your store needs an ethical training especially for Jesse.

Whenever we crave sweets, there is nothing more satisfying than Hopscotch! She is always so friendly in helping us pick out out treats (we can never leave with just one treat!). We ordered a Tiramisu cake for my wife's birthday--best cake ever!! Not only is everything super aesthetically pleasing, but also you can taste the choicest ingredients used for everything. Thank you Hopscotch for being so awesome!!

Updating my review from 1 to 4 stars. Tonight I tried the chocolate chip cookie, the caraway shortbread, and a honey miso latte. I didn't like the chocolate chip cookie but my partner did; it was chewy which he's a fan of. The caraway shortbread was GREAT. The shortbread was so good-- a little salty, subtly sweet, and had a great texture. The honey miso latte was good! I appreciated that the shortbread was labeled as "caraway shortbread" so I knew I was getting something herbaceous and unique. The service could be better by which I mean the people could be more talkative and a little less "moody but cute Tumblr chick". There was no effort to build rapport but I'll assume they were just incredibly focused on cutting marshmallows. I will be back!
The staff is so friendly and there is a wide variety of treats for vegan and gluten free customers.

I was very impressed with the cake I ordered from Kaya Tate at Hopscotch for the Mother's Day holiday. Kaya has a very creative approach to pastry cooking, and I love her design aesthetic and presentation. I would highly recommend Kaya's services for a wedding, holiday or other special occasion. Her small business recently moved into a new space on John Street in Champaign, and I'm excited to see Hopscotch continue to grow in the future.

Stopped in today for lavender-rose macarons and a lemon bar. The macarons were delicious, and the lemon bar is the only one I've gotten in a bakery that tasted as good as homemade ones. Everything in the cases looked delicious and well-presented. Will definitely return.

I have been following along on their Instagram for months and couldn't have been more excited to try Hopscotch. Although you sadly can't go inside right now they have done their best to make it a pleasant experience even while waiting outside. With both online and in-person order options they have made getting fresh baked goods during these crazy times a breeze. The employee I interacted with during my visit was kind and very friendly, happy to give me her recommendations when I asked and was super patient while I figured out what I wanted. I got the Plum and Pistachio Croissant and a Honey Miso Latte. Both were amazing! It is definitely on the pricey side but for handmade quality products you definitely get what you pay for. Overall such a pleasant experience and I will definitely be going back!

Such a great little bakery. Highly recommended. Their baked goods are terrific. We've gotten cupcakes (so good), cookies (huge!) and more over the long, long pandemic. They're very safe, providing online ordering, outdoor pickup, and curbside. They've also got great coffee drinks (try the oatmilk latte with honey; it's delicious) and they're always so friendly when you pick your order up. They also offer a really cool service to support our healthcare workers too: Buy a Nurse a Cookie. You can pay just a little over two bucks and change for a nurse to get one of their delicious cookies. So cool! They've got a little parking lot but if it's packed you may need to do street parking. They're in a quiet, residential neighborhood, though, so you don't need to worry about parking on a busy street. They've also got outdoor seating too.

Headed into Hopscotch today on a friend's recommendation, and this place is way too cute! From the awesome crafts you can buy from local talent to the desserts that look too cute to eat, I was overwhelmed with beauty when I stepped in! I can't wait to order treats for my Madison family next time I'm in town!

I have been enjoying Hopscotch baked goods since their Art Mart days and have had plenty of great experiences. Unfortunately, the order this review is based on will be our last from this bakery due both to the quality of the cake and the awful customer service I experienced. I placed a custom order of a cake and 3 dozen cupcakes for my dad's 50th birthday party in May, which they estimated would feed around 60 people. This order cost $230, for price reference. At the end of the night we had all but 7 cupcakes and 1 slice of cake left due to the fact that the cake was almost inedible. The cake was supposed to be camouflage - I'm not sure if the bakery was confused on the coloring or if they were just too busy to care (I was told on two occasions that they had several wedding orders they were working on as well), but what we ended up with was three of the ugliest shades of green swirled together on the cake, and two shades of green dotted onto the cupcakes. My dad did not even know it was supposed to be camoflage and likely wouldn't have known it tied into the theme at all if I hadn't purchased duck toppers for it. The cake was dense, very dry and reminded me more of week-old muffins or scones than chocolate cake. I had requested 3 flavors of cupcakes but only received two (lemon and some variation of vanilla, we believe) - neither had much, if any, flavor. What was supposed to be buttercream icing was completely void of flavor and the texture was far too fluffy - I'm talking airy, flavorless goop - and ugly goop, at that. I tried a cupcake first and asked several close friends to taste as well, thinking my palate might have just been confused that night. The consensus was much the same - the cake was dry, had likely been either overcooked and/or frozen for too long and not properly thawed, and neither the cake nor the icing had any flavor at all. I was so embarrassed we just skipped dessert all together and I boxed up the cake to return to the bakery. I placed 4 calls to the bakery that next week. I believe all were answered by the same woman at the front counter, who relayed 3 separate stories about why the owner had not been in contact with me (not in today, has been on vacation, isn't in until this afternoon) but she insisted the owner would receive the message and call me back. She never did. To this day I have not received a phone call or apology. I happened to be reviewing my bank account and saw a full refund for my order a week after my first call to the bakery. While I am thankful for the refund, it just doesn't excuse the awful service and terrible quality of the cake. We have thankfully found a fantastic baker in Effingham to use instead for our upcoming wedding and wedding festivities, as Hopscotch was going to be our bakery of choice. If you are considering Hopscotch and are looking for good quality, tasty baked goods, I would sincerely suggest you keep looking.

This is a great bakery when it comes to their baked goods. Unfortunately, their service leaves a lot to be desired. One usually comes to places like this to relax, but the two ladies behind the counter were apathetic at best and did not care how they packaged the goods before giving them to the customer. This experience takes away so much from the food.

I've been to this bakery many times and I am always satisfied with my order. I really like the aesthetic of the location, however it could use some more parking. I really enjoy the carrot cake and peanut cookies as well as the scones.

Hopscotch is a small local bakery. Every day they feature different baked goods and have a selection of cake and seasonal beverages. The food tastes great but the opening time doesn't make sense. They open later in the morning and close at 5:30. This is the reason for the 4 stars...beyond that the food is great.

The good: Their cheesecake is phenomenal. Everything else looks wonderful as well, but I love their cheesecake. The bad: The service could be better. Not bad but not great either. Whenever I get there and there is a line, I dread it as I know I will be in it for quite some time. Odds are someone is going to order a cake right in front of you and it's a time consumer and the process needs to be improved. Also, odds are against you if you want to grab a slice of something and get a spot inside to eat. Hopscotch has quickly grown a fan base and it stays pretty packed inside.

This is my favorite place in the whole dang town. It's a little pricey, but I love their cold brew and their cool selection of bakery items. I can compare it to cool coffee shops I've seen in places like San Francisco or NYC or even london, it has a neat atmosphere and the decorations and drinks change seasonally. I think it's a special place in town we have so I support it any chance I get. I would rather spend my coffee money there over Starbucks or any other chain.

This place is AMAZING. It is a hidden little gem in Champaign. There are always so many options to choose from. My husband and my favorite 3 are the salted caramel brownie, the lemon bar, and the ooey gooey cake. You must stop by every Wednesday for $1 macarons. Very pleased with the gluten free cake they made for my husband's PhD ceremony. No one could tell it was GF! So delicious. You won't be sorry that you stopped here!

I am in love with the cake from here! She made my sister's wedding cake that was absolutely gorgeous and delicious and now I can stop by to get occasional cupcakes! So amazing. Just had a blackberry lime cupcake that was so fresh and beautiful. Can't wait to go again with girlfriends.

We went in there before Christmas in hopes of finding a new type of bakery for this area. There seems to be a trend in town of cranky people working in bakeries. The lady at the counter seemed to be inconvenienced by our questions about the products. She didn't even know the types of cakes that were behind the counter. Secondly, we inquired about the "party room". Literally it's just a long table within the seating area for guests. They lost our business because they do not provide this service on weekends or after 530. The chocolate chip cookie was delicious the first time we came. The second time it was not the sane experience. The cupcakes were dry and flavorless. The chocolate cupcakes had a strong coffee flavor so the kids were turned off. They are very cute however. Hopefully the customer service will improve along with the products' consistency.

I was excited by the photos and so glad to see a new bakery choice in Champaign. I've tried several of the smaller items from the case to taste test for larger occasions. I have to say - I'm not particularly impressed. It pains me to say that because I really tried. The most lasting impression was a small cheesecake I tried a few weeks ago. The batch was so underdone that the bottom was soupy, which in turn made the crust (and the cake) inedible. When I went back a few days later, I mentioned it while pursuing the case to try something new. The woman behind the counter said she knew the batch was underdone. But no refund offer, replacement, or even an apology. Just an, "We know." I left with a bottle of wine and some cheese instead. There are other places to go for bakery items so maybe I'll try again after they've been settled for awhile.
Aesthetically pleasing bakery with some unique flavor combinations, but it lacks in the taste and quality department.
I was so excited about this place but the customer service was meh. We weren't greeted by the cashier and she seemed like she didn't want to be there. The chai latte was okay.

One of the best little hidden treasures in Champaign! I have never had anything I didn't like here. The drinks are all really good, and the treats, oh man the treats! They always have a great variety to choose from and if you have a sweet tooth then this is the place for you. The shop also has some really great little unique items, whether for gifts or just yourself. I've never had a bad experience here, the girls are all so sweet and helpful! Anytime anyone comes to town to visit I make sure to bring them to Hopscotch for a goodie! This business is just one great example of why you should support local businesses.

Although the shop itself and baked goods are very aesthetically pleasing, I'm sad to say I was disappointed. I paid $7 for their specialty drinks (I do have to pay extra for dairy free milk, to be fair) and it has been lukewarm on 2 separate occasions. It is also freezing in the building. Myself and everyone around me are wearing their winter coats. I rarely bring up complaints, but asked an employee if there was something that could be done and was pretty much brushed off. I thought seeing everyone wear their winter coats inside should have been a sufficient hint itself. For $7, I was hoping to escape the cold to settle in a cozy shop & warm up with a latte, but that is just not the experience you will get here. I also do not recommend going there to study or work. There is not much seating and I don't get the vibe that they want you to stay long. It's more for grabbing a treat, enjoying it, and then leaving.
Best coffee shop in the area. They have the best* pastries and coffee. Service is hit or miss though.
Very cute shop! Great coffee, delicious baked goods, and a bright and cheerful atmosphere.

I'm sorry but went to buy a fondant cake today and they didn't have any. Bought 12 macaroons only to find when I got home they were so dried out they crumbled. I know sometimes that just happens, but to pay $24. and have this happen stings. Had great Lavender lemonaid, and the person who took care of us was nice. Cute shop.

I followed Hopscotch's buzz before ever tasting its baked goods. When we first moved to CU in 1993, there was only one upscale bakery in town and we longed for more and different. Now, we have a few to choose from, but more and different is always good. Hopscotch is a new take on the upscale bakery, a hipster one, with a particular decor style that is at once vintage and subdued with a modern twist. Think de-colorsatured roses, flattened, or cakes barely iced with embedded contrasting grit. I like this aesthetic -- it seems fresh and understated to me. I first tasted Hopscotch's products after purchasing them at a local arts pop-up. I bought a brownie and some kind of brown sugar butter bar. The brownie was truly phenomenal if you like fudge (rather than cake) style brownies, and I love them. The chocolate was so dark and dense it was like having my tongue immersed in a deep chocolate groove. The brownie had a soft, chewy bite and wasn't overly sweet. The other bar had good taste: brown sugar meets browned butter, but it was dry and crumbly. When Hopscotch opened in the new Art Mart space, I tried another brownie, and it was as good as the first. So, high marks on consistency. I recently went back and tried a strawberry baby cake for me and a white chocolate brownie for my son. I loved the baby cake itself as well as the fresh strawberry compote on top. The cake was moist and tender, the compote had great strawberry flavor. Neither was overly sweet. I did not like the disc of heavy buttercream frosting that sat on top of these. It had the texture of refrigerated butter and did not eat well with the more tender components. Although I suppose my standard for all such strawberry cakes is the enchanting cassata, a softer frosting would move this baby cake toward perfection. My son did not like the white chocolate brownie, although he loves both brownies and white chocolate. He thought the brownie was greasy and salty. It had moved from a fudgy texture to a fatty one without enough flour to support a good bite. Embedded in the bar were bits of white chocolate, which he said was the only positive note. Given Hopscotch's stiff prices ($8 for a baby cake, $4 for a brownie), one expects products to be truly exceptional, without any missteps. I believe there's real quality here and that products are sometimes worth the price. Hopscotch uses carefully sourced, superior ingredients; good technique; and a refined aesthetic. There's a great deal of potential here, but all of the products are not quite yet perfected. And, to be fair, I haven't yet tried many of Hopscotch's other products, although the case is full of tempting options (full sized cakes, meringues, and more). I will also add that I had one encounter with the owner (Kaya Tate) that disappointed me. When her new website went up, she asked followers on Facebook for feedback. I provided some, much of it positive, especially about the website's look & feel and navigation. However, I also said that I thought the landing page should open with something about the deliciousness of the products rather than ethics, originality, etc. The Hopscotch owner wrote back to defend her choices. I replied that I understood why she'd made those choices -- I get how important food ethics and authenticity (localism, etc.) are to the hipster culinary scene -- but stood by my point that what I want first in a bakery is tasty products. How the products get that way can follow. The owner replied again to defend her choices. To me, this was a misstep in a customer interaction. She had every right to disagree with my feedback, but she should have simply thanked me and moved on. Despite this rather sour interaction, I am rooting for Hopscotch.

I love what's happening in this historic building. They have the spot looking very nice, and the treats I have had are nothing short of fucking amazing. Super nice and knowledgeable folks. I really enjoy their drip coffee. I'd love the option of walking out with a 16oz instead of the smallish size offered, but hey, whatever! The damn salted Caramel Brownie I left with last visit still has me whistling zippadee do dah like mug.

Very nice unisex bathroom with a urinal as well as a toilet. It has bright pink walls and low lighting which adds a lot to it's atmosphere. They also have a very inspiring Frida Painting about being yourself which fits the atmosphere of the place. Also a very interesting design choice is that there are several dozen reflective ornaments above the toilet which really caused me to ponder my place in the universe while defecating. My only complaint is that there was specks of poop coating the bowl of the toilet. With proper maintenance this would be 5 out of 5 stars.
Very cute interior but very bad, overpriced cupcake. Wish them the best of luck, but there were clearly some ingredients missing from the batter.

We ordered some cheesecakes from here for a wedding. They weren't good at all about getting back to us when we called which was frustrating. They also didn't cut the cakes which made them hard to prepare and set out the day-of. They were beautiful and delicious but it probably wasn't worth all the hassle.

I really wanted to like Hopscotch. The decor and ambiance is lovely, and I really like how you can purchase pieces from local artists and creators. However, the treats are rather lacking. I ordered a butterscotch cookie and a chocolate cupcake with strawberry frosting. For the quality, they are very overpriced. The chocolate cupcake, although pretty, was very lacking in any "chocolate" flavor, and honestly tasted similar to one from Schnucks. The frosting was okay. The cookie was better, but a little bit too tough. My jaw hurt after chewing. In addition, the customer service left something to be desired. The people at the counter seemed quite cool, almost judgmental. I hope Hopscotch will be able to improve their treats and cheer up a bit. Until then, I'll probably look somewhere else for coffee and dessert.

The shop itself is quaint. A bit pricey, but it's fine. My main issue is for anyone looking to order a cake or pastries for an event. I had been in contact with the owner, Kaya, since June/July for a wedding cake for May (I like to be prepared). Communication was minimal on her part. She'd email me once every week or two weeks. At first she seemed open to customization and personalization for the cake, then pulled every excuse in the book to avoid working with me (she could do it on a tiered cake, we didn't want a tiered cake, well then she just couldn't do it). My main issue is that i don't like their buttercream. I've seen some reviews stating it as heavenly. This might be true, as it's pretty close to eating a slab of whipped butter; it will definitely get you closer to death. She wouldn't make a shortening based icing. I then asked for their cream cheese icing (it's pretty tasty) and she then sent me an email that they updated their website with available flavors and she looked forward to working with me. This was in October. We had been working with each other for months. And on the new website, guess which icing WASNT an option anymore? Cream cheese. Unless you are a friend or want exactly what she'll make for you, don't expect a lot of great customer service. I don't know if she's just got too much on her plate or what, but she definitely needs to work on communication skills or hire someone else to organize custom orders.
Sweetest little neighborhood bakery!! Everything at hopscotch is so special. I pick up brownies and lemon bars every time I host a dinner!

I'm so happy this place opened nearby. The Matcha is well made and the girls at the counter are helpful with customer who's there for the first time. Looking forward to going back to try other items on the menu

Visited here with a friend today- it was our first time trying matcha as a flavor and had heard great things so we were excited to try it out! The store had a very cute aesthetic- amazing decorations inside, very clean and a good amount of seating The individuals working the register were all very kind and allowed me to sample to matcha and toasted matcha flavor! I ordered a matcha and ube swirl cone and my friend ordered the Maiko special. Both came out quick and aesthetically were very pleasing A tip for anyone wanting to try something new: a few of the toppings in the Maiko special (jelly, mochi, etc) are not sweet/have no distinct flavor so keep this in mind!! I would recommend this location to others :)

Such a cute place! I love the ambiance and decor. Unfortunately I already bought a sweet drink in the area so I didn't get any ice cream here however the strawberry sandwich I ordered was yummy. I took a star off because it was super pricey and the bread was a little hard like it was left out too long. $4 for half a crust less sandwich with 1.5 strawberries and cream - it should've been made fresh.

This is a cute little spot in a shopping center off providence road. I wanted to check it out after seeing photos of the maiko special. I had no clue what the ingredients included were but I wanted to try it. Typically at a place like this, I stick with soft serve but I forced myself to venture out. The soft serve was great and the rest of it was good but for me it felt like there was too much going on. I think I'm the future I will stick to my usual choice of soft serve. They had some toast options too which looked pretty good.

Swung in to try their Black Sesame flavor... Got the Matcha Green Tea & Black Sesame Swirl Soft Serve Cone. As expected, it was SO Good!! Think I liked this combo even more than the Green Tea & Ube Swirl? Anyway, just wanted to quickly drop more 5 stars...and a picture!

I've met my matcha. This place is amazing. Lots of selections from lattes, teas, espresso based drinks, and even soft serve. It's a little on the pricy side ($6-$7) per drink, but definitely worth it in my opinion

Came here to try out everything matcha! I got their maiko special. I am not too familiar with Japanese desserts, so didn't appreciate the cereal cornflakes and the particular beans or the syrup. The ice cream, however, was on point. I got some black sesame inside (I tried it alone, and it was too strong for me). Overall, matcha flavor was on point, but $10 was a lot for this cup. If I came again, I'd just get a drink or ice cream alone.

This place was featured on yelp and not too far for me so I just had to try it. It's a small cafÃ© located in the Arboretum shopping area. There is plenty of shared parking. The place is clean and they have good customer service. I decided to try the yuca (seasonal flavor) and Matcha swirl based on the staffs recommendations. I found the Matcha to be very tasty and a very strong flavor it would probably taste really good with the vanilla in a swirl. They have a variety of other treats offered besides the frozen yogurt. Now so sell a variation of beverages. They sell merchandise as well. I would like to come back and try some different flavors and treats. Hope you enjoy!

INTRO: A unique Asian cafe that specializes in matcha desserts, Matcha Cafe Maiko is prepared to bring some matcha into your life. I can guarantee that this special experience will make you say "I love matcha so matcha!" after finishing your first dessert. I normally get their matcha soft serve, but you also can't go wrong with their other desserts and drinks on their menu. DESSERT 1: Golden Shogun ($9.50) - This is the ultimate flex move. A soft-serve flavor of your choice (matcha, hojicha, seasonal) topped off with a 24k edible gold sheet in a waffle cone will make you feel like a millionaire. The matcha flavor is present, but it's definitely not one of the strongest I've tasted. I've made stronger matcha milkshakes at home. WORTH IT? YES, it's worth it for the experience and whenever you're in town (Overall 7/10)

YUM! I've been wanting to check this spot out for some months now. When I happened to be on this side of town for a work meeting I had to stop in. The shop is super cute inside. They have real plants all over and huge table for a large groups, that's great for pics lol. There's some smaller tables and seats by the window. Very nicely decorated and situated inside! The ladies working behind the counter were all friendly and helpful. They answered a few of my questions and suggested a some things too, which I appreciated. I ordered the ube matcha latte and the matcha cream puffs! They were both sooooooo yummy!!! I can't wait to try some other menu items the next time I'm in the area. I definitely recommend checking this spot out.

Probably the most decent matcha you can get in North Carolina. I get half sugar so the bitterness of the matcha comes through. I could taste the kinako but couldn't really taste the kuromitsu in this drink. Would recommend just getting their regular matcha drinks instead so you don't waste your money on this drink which was basically the same thing.
Cute and cozy atmosphere. The lattes were delicious! Hung out here with a friend for several hours and we both enjoyed it very much

As a big fan of green tea ice cream, this is a must place to check out. I like their cute design inside of the cafe. Their green tea ice cream is so good, not too sweet and very authentic. You can try before you order. Tried their signature matches parfait and it was so good. Each ingredient was all good and after you mix it, you can totally enjoy the mixed flavor of them. I also tried their hot matcha kinako latte and hojicha latte. Specially I like their hojicha latte as it is very unique roasted tea taste. The owner lady was very kind so she explained every question we asked. Definitely we will go back for caffeinated teas other than coffee!

I didn't rush to try this place since I don't like matcha, but we had lunch in the area so we decided to stop by. They have so much more than just matcha. They had us sample all their ice cream flavors and I loved hojicha and black sesame. It was the first time I've seen either of these in Charlotte. We decided to get the Maiko Special with a vanilla hojicha ice cream swirl. Overall, I loved it. It had a matcha cake in it that I actually liked. It also had a special matcha ice cream in it which I really didn't like, but was able to avoid. They use the same waffle cones as Jeni's which I love. I tried some of my friends black sesame waffle cone which was great. Warning: the hojicha and matcha products have caffeine in them. It makes sense if you think about it but I forgot since I was just eating dessert and it kept me up half the night (I don't drink caffeine). The decor is really well done. The service is incredibly friendly. I will be back (but will probably stick to black sesame next time to avoid the caffeine)!

Very cute cafe and who knew, you can have a shop with a varied selection focused on one flavor?! The shop is brightly lit on the inside and had cute little tables inside and out for dining in. The menu had so many options from matcha tea, to tea lattes, matcha latte floats, soft serve ice cream, pastries, etc. We ordered a matcha latte float with black sesame soft serve and a matcha lemonade float with matcha soft serve. The matcha flavors were very distinct, not weak at all. I really enjoyed my black sesame soft serve ice cream, it was creamy and nutty, surprisingly wonderful! COVID precautions: Staff wore face coverings and requires patrons as well. Hand sanitizer was provided as well. We came during the slow hours of evening so I'm unsure about socially distancing precautions. They have little signs on their tables that when they're busy, you have a certain time limit dining in until a staff asks you to leave for them to disinfect, I assume to get people in and out the establishment and prevent longtime exposure. The inside of the shop is cute, the decor cute enough for an IG photo op. I will be back to try more matcha options the next time I'm in Charlotte!

Not a big fan of Matcha, but I have to give this place a five star . A very nice, beautiful, cute, fancy little place. Clean, bright, friendly atmosphere. Never wanna try matcha until come to this place and give myself a shot, not bad not bad but matcha still not my things tho...but again this place so welcoming, so instagrammable, matcha lover out there, this is all about matcha...this is your place, come and try this out....they have good selection of matcha...

It was pricey for a snack, but everything tasted excellent! I got the Maiko Special with matcha and ube soft serve. Couldn't really taste the ube, but the cornflakes and red beans really added something extra to it. My mother got the matcha lemon float and enjoyed it as well.

This place is great! It's on the outskirt of Charlotte, so I would stop by if I'm in the area. Maybe that's a good thing or else this place would take all of my money. If you love Matcha as much as I do I'm sure you will love this place. I wouldn't recommend getting the specIal they have because it is not worth. It's a mess. However; everytime I get the soft served matcha ice cream, I am never disappointed! They have vanilla too but I wouldn't spend money on it. Stick with matcha and you can even get the roasted matcha (hojicha) with it (pic of it on the right!) The place is nice. Very instagramable. The service is fast. Go try this place out! You won't regret it.

First time here, tried the cream hojicha tea, not very good, definitely an acquired taste. Then second time tried the maiko special and dang, it's good. Ingredient is quality here, you can taste the difference. Even utensils they use compostable. Decor inside is very cute. Only complaint is the items can be kind of expensive.

This has got to be the tastiest and also the most instagrammable little cafe I've ever been to! When you first walk in you notice that the cafe is on the smaller side but the decor is very inviting. I tried the Maiko Special which was a very unique dessert. If you're not a fan of very sweet desserts, this is perfect for you. The dessert was made up of your choice of soft serve, matcha cake, red beans, corn flakes, agar jelly, black honey, and mochi. I chose the matcha and black sesame swirl soft serve. Their menu was extensive so I can't wait to go back and try more items!

If you love matcha you would surely enjoy this place! I would recommend getting the matcha ice cream in a cone. To be honest the prices are very high, but then again the quality of the matcha is very good. The range is from 5.50 to 8. If you don't like matcha you wouldn't like this place, but they do have vanilla ice cream as an option as well! The interior of the shop is so beautiful so I would reccommend to come try it out at least once! They also have samples too to taste if you want to see how dank the matcha is. Just make sure to ask!

Very cute cafe. It gives me all the cozy hangout feels. The soft serve flavors tastes like what they are described as. The Ube and hojicha flavors were amazing. It was a tough decision as to what to get my first time coming here. Everything sounded so tasty. The Ube latte mixture was homemade. I asked and they boil down the Ube root. It was very creamy and rich tasting. The matcha latte was good as well. They do have a loyalty program as well.
Not a fan, but my friend that brought me here absolutely loved it so yeah, he had a frappe. He couldn't stop talking how great it was.

So glad that Charlotte finally have a place for matcha ice cream!!! Love it so much that I have been here twice already since they opened. Great place and the staffs are friendly. Soft serve tasted good with huge tea flavor, vanilla is also great, not much vanilla flavor but more like milk flavor. A little on the pricey side but pretty sure I will be a regular here.
Grace staff, delicious Matcha and a great place to meet a friend and relax. The aesthetic of the overall shop is overall a vibe.
I was expecting this to be more of a drink, but still enjoyed it as a desert- next time I will get without the beans. Sn:They do have plenty of drink options as well.

So, I gotta say the place was almost perfectly as expected. If not a little different. Having lived in Japan in the past there's a soft spot on my heart for soft serve (see what I did there?). Specifically the parfaits with a concoction of toppings. So naturally that's what I got first. The price was high! For the special parfait it's $7.80. Which I suppose I totally understand when you consider the quality of ingredients here. Most specifically in the case of the real matcha ice cream. They also hand make their own waffle cones. And free samples aplenty - definitely try out that earthy hojicha soft serve. Apparently I didn't have enough because I decided to opt for a soft serve cone at $5.50 with a swirl of hojicha and matcha. It was good stuff, ain't gonna lie. The consistency of the ice cream was certainly unique, all the while it wasn't unpalatably cold. Some dark magic is at work here! The aesthetic of the shop is on point here. They staffed primarily with teenagers who definitely fit the bill for touting the place regularly on social media. And the managers/owners are incredibly friendly and fun with both the employees and the customers. The walls and floors are a bright white and something about the lighting in here makes every picture POP when people post it. (More magic at work here...or by design??) The menu is delightfully simple once you get the hang of it. Amazing they can offer so much from so few base ingredients. They even have Japanese on the menus; I thought that was cool stuff. I will probably stop by again a little ways out in the future for that sinful indulgence and in hopes of seeing more of the non-frozen sweets on offer.
Kinda love it, I had the cream puff and the matcha maiko I didn't finish either as the portions were large. Strong green tea flavor so if you get ube and green tea the green tea will win.
This is the place to be if you love matcha!! So many options to choose from. The cafe is super cute and staff is very friendly! Can't wait to go back.

Omg, I didn't know I needed this in my life, but I do. Totally worth the drive across town. The soft serve is just like the matcha ice cream we got in Japan. I personally prefer the hochicha flavor, and I can't wait for a cheat day so I can try their other products.

I drove 15 minutes out of my way to come here as I've visited this chain in Seattle. Was craving a matcha soft serve bad and this hit the spot. The quality of the matcha is always 100% and the mochi is delicious (though I hate paying 50 cents for 1 mochi). Service was excellent. There were 2 women who were manning the front and it wasn't busy at all at around 2PM on Saturday. I loved that parking was easy and right in front of the store. The cashier area has a plastic glass pane to protect against airborne transmissions. Overall I'd come back here again.
Yummy matcha ice cream. The red bean pastry was delish also. I wish the cost was a bit lower though.

Yum and Yum!!! Coming from CA I was so excited to see a place like this!!! Always got my matcha ice cream fix when I went home. Now I can get it locally. Wish they had the black sesame, but they rotate flavors so it will come back. Met the owner and she is so nice. Support her business, so we can have matcha ice cream for years to come. Friendly staff too!

Just pay attention if you are paying cash. As much as it so easy to pay with a card....I tend to pay cash and TIP with cash for servers. I order a matcha and mochi sundae (cup No waffle) and paid cash = 7.95 Unfortunately the change never given to me at the register and as I sat in their shop on a slow Sunday evening. I even gave them a chance by going up to the counter to ask for receipt and change. She said they gave me change from the $20. I don't remember giving them tip (and I tip good) from the change I receive back. I don't even have change to prove they gave me my change back!!! Seriously!!! I love Unique businesses like maiko matcha, but I don't think I will go back because they don't watch their "customer's back".

So happy that this place opened up in Charlotte. The inside is very cute and quaint. I felt like I was walking into a Japanese/Korean cafe and makes me miss the cafe culture in those places so much. I recently visited a Virginia location and had the Matcha ice cream patbingsu. Was a little disappointed that they didn't have it. But the very friendly worker told me they will start rolling out other menu items in the spring and summer. So pretty excited for that! Oh and for some reason didn't realize that this cafe offers a stronger matcha flavor. I will definitely go for that next time. Since mine wasn't that strong in matcha flavor. But that's definitely a personal preference. Overall great experience and will drive the 30 minutes to get there again.

Me and my friend drove an hour to get here, but the food was 100% worth it. We bought ice cream there, and got some more treats to go and eat later. I definitely recommend their soft serve ice cream, I got the matcha/black sesame soft serve with the black honey and adzuki beans at the bottom of the cone.
Best matcha cafe! Its aesthetics are glorious. The service phenomenal. The food!!! Leaves you speechless

I love this cafe with delicious drinks, ice cream and pastry, cute decors and welcoming staff members. I love their matcha ice cream and matcha frappe with cheese cream! The baked goodies are really yummy too. I have tried their matcha tiramisu, matcha creme puffs, matcha creme bun, madeleines, etc. I love all of them as they are very unique and not too sweet.

Words and pictures can not express how amazing Matcha Cafe Maiko is, but I will try to articulate it anyway. Tl;Dr If I could, I'd give them ten stars. They are truly a unique and aritisan cafe that takes pride in their craft. You would be a fool to not go here. Let's break it down: The digs: Located in a shopping complex off Providence Rd near the Arboretum with plenty of parking. The decor is beautifully done. Clean and simple lines with a calming color scheme. The furniture is fun and modern and doesn't look cheap or kitschy. The people: I'm not positive, but I'm fairly certain that the owners were there when we ordered. They love what they do and are so kind, helpful, and informative. I really do wish them the most success with this endeavor. The menu: As the name suggests, they specialize in matcha everything. They have a mix of cold and hot drink/snack options. However, I'll make things easy for you. GET THE MAIKO SPECIAL! It's your choice of soft serve flavors with all sorts of layered goodies; almost like an elevated parfait. I recommend the hojicha soft serve, which is roasted matcha. It has a wonderful complex and nutty flavor. As for all of those goodies, they include but are not limited to mochi, cornflakes, chiffon cake pieces, and red bean paste. The combination of textures and flavors are phenomenal. And oh by the way, everything is made in house. I mean you really can't beat that.

I have pretty mixed feelings about Matcha Cafe because i've had some items that were pretty hit or miss. I did not enjoy the new Shokupan or the Maiko special, however I really do enjoyed their soft serve ice creams and hot drink selection. The matcha soft serve is my favorite item on the menu (surprise surprise).
